He said to him: From where do you … this … He said to him: My father my teacher told … me and my father my teacher … from Rav.

Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: That which we said … moved his feet he returns to the beginning, we only said … where he is unaccustomed to reciting … supplications after his prayer. However, … he is accustomed to reciting supplications after his prayer, … he … return to the … service,

Some say, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: That which we said … did not … move his feet, he … return to the … service, we only said … where he is accustomed to reciting … supplications after his prayer. However, … he is unaccustomed to reciting supplications after his prayer, he must return to the beginning of the prayer,

Rabbi Eliezer says: One whose prayer is fixed, his prayer is not supplication. … What is … fixed … Rabbi Ya’akov bar Idi said … Rabbi Oshaya said: … anyone for whom his prayer is like a burden upon him, … The Rabbis say: … anyone who does not recite … in the language of supplication, … Rabba and Rav Yosef both said: … anyone unable to introduce … element,
Rabbi Zeira said: I could introduce … element … I am afraid that perhaps I will … confused.

Abaye bar Avin and Rabbi Ḥanina bar Avin, both said: … anyone who does not … pray with the reddening of the sun, … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It is a mitzva to pray with the reddening of the sun. And Rabbi Zeira said: What is the verse … “Let them fear You with the sun and before the moon, generation after generation” … in the West, … they cursed one who prays with the reddening of the sun … What is the reason? Perhaps, … confused about the hour

Rabbi Yehoshua says: One who is walking in a place of danger, recites a brief prayer…at parashat ha’ibur. … What is … parashat ha’ibur? Rav Ḥisda said … Mar Ukva said: … Even at a time when You are as filled with anger [evra], towards them, as a pregnant woman [ubara], may all of their needs be before You. Some say … Rav Ḥisda said … Mar Ukva said: Even when they violate [ovrim] the commandments of the Torah, may all of their needs be before You.

The Sages taught: One who walks in a place where there are groups of wild beasts and robbers recites an abbreviated prayer. Which is an abbreviated prayer? Rabbi Eliezer says, “Carry out Your will in the heavens above, and give peace of mind to those who fear You below, and perform that which is good in Your eyes. Blessed are You, Lord, Who listens to prayer.”
Rabbi Yehoshua says … Hear the cry of Your nation, Israel, and quickly fulfill their request. Blessed are You, Lord, Who listens to prayer.
Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok says … Hear the shout of Your nation, Israel, and quickly fulfill their request. Blessed are You, Lord, Who listens to prayer.

Aḥerim say … The needs of Your nation, Israel, are many and their intelligence is limited, … may it be Your will, Lord our God, to provide each and every one with his necessary sustenance, and to each and every body all that it lacks. Blessed are You, Lord, Who listens to prayer.
Rav Huna said: The halakha … is in accordance with … Aḥerim.

Elijah … said to Rav Yehuda brother of Rav Sala Ḥasida: Do not get angry and you will not sin. Do not get drunk and you will not sin. And when you set out on a journey, consult with your Creator, and … set out. The Gemara asks: What is the meaning of: Consult with your Creator, and then set out? Rabbi Ya’akov said … Rav Ḥisda said: That is the traveler’s prayer. And Rabbi Ya’akov said … Rav Ḥisda said: … anyone who sets out on a journey must recite the traveler’s prayer

What is … the traveler’s prayer? … May it be Your will, Lord my God, to lead me to peace, direct my steps to peace, and guide me to peace, and rescue me from the hands of any enemy or ambush along the way, and send blessing to the work of my hands, and let me find grace, kindness, and compassion in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see me. Blessed are You, Lord, Who hears prayer.
Abaye said: At all times
a person should associate himself with the congregation … How should he say … May it be Your will, Lord our God, that You lead us to peace, etc.,

When does one pray? Rabbi Ya’akov said … Rav Ḥisda said: From when one sets out on his journey, … How long … Rabbi Ya’akov said … Rav Ḥisda said: At least a parasang. How does he recite … Rav Ḥisda said: … standing … Rav Sheshet said: Even walking

Rav Ḥisda and Rav Sheshet were walking along the path, Rav Ḥisda stood and recited … Rav Sheshet asked his servant: What is Rav Ḥisda doing … said to him: He is standing and praying. … said to … Stand me up as well and I will pray. … From being good, do not be called wicked.

What is … Grant us understanding and the brief prayer … Grant us understanding is required to recite the first three … and the last three … and when he reaches his home, he need not pray again. … the brief prayer, … need recite neither the first three … nor the last three … However, when he reaches his home, he must pray again.
The halakha is: Grant us understanding, … standing. The brief prayer, … whether … standing or whether … walking.

One who was riding on a donkey … The Sages taught … One who was riding on a donkey and the time for prayer arrived, if he has someone to hold … the donkey, he should dismount and pray. If not, he should sit in his place … and pray. Rabbi … says: In any case, … he should sit in his place … and pray, as his mind will not be calm.
Rava, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, said: … halakha … is in accordance with … Rabbi
The Sages taught … A blind person and one who is unable to approximate the directions … may focus his heart towards his Father in Heaven, as it is stated: “And they shall pray to the Lord”

One who was standing … in the Diaspora should focus his heart toward Eretz Yisrael, as it is stated: “And they shall pray to You by way of their land … One who was standing in Eretz Yisrael should focus his heart toward Jerusalem, as it is stated: “And they shall pray to the Lord by way of the city that You have chosen” … One who was standing in Jerusalem should focus his heart toward the Temple, as it is stated: “And they shall pray toward this house” … One who was standing in the Temple should focus his heart toward the Holy of Holies, as it is stated: “And they shall pray toward this place” … One who was standing in the Holy of Holies should focus his heart toward the seat of the ark-cover [kapporet], … One who was standing behind the seat of the ark-cover should visualize himself as if standing before the ark-cover … Consequently, … standing … in the East turns to face west, … in the West turns to face east. … in the South turns to face north, … in the North turns to face south; Consequently, all of … Israel focus … focusing their hearts toward one place,
Rabbi Avin, and some say Rabbi Avina, said: What verse … this? “Your neck is like the Tower of David, built with turrets [talpiyyot], … hill … tel] toward which all mouths … piyyot] turn,
When Shmuel’s father and Levi wanted to set out on a journey … they would pray early … When, … the time to recite Shema would arrive, they recited it.

In accordance with whose … In accordance with this tanna, as it was taught … One who rose early to set out on … path … they bring him a shofar and he sounds … a lulav and he takes it … a megilla, … and he reads it … and when the time comes to recite Shema, he recites … one who rose early to sit in a wagon or in a boat prays, and when the time comes to recite Shema, he recites it.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, says: In either case, … recite Shema and … pray … so that he will juxtapose redemption and prayer.
Regarding what do they disagree? … This Sage, … holds … prayer … standing is preferable. … This Sage, … holds … juxtaposition of redemption and prayer is preferable,
Mareimar and Mar Zutra would gather ten … on … Shabbat of the festival and pray, and set out to deliver their lecture [pirka].

Rav Ashi would pray with the congregation individually … seated, … when he would come to his house, he would pray again … standing … The Sages said to him: The Master should do as Mareimar and Mar Zutra … He said to them: It is burdensome to me … said to him: The Master should do as Shmuel’s father and Levi … He said to them: I have not seen Sages older than us do that,

MISHNA: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says: The additional prayer is only … in a city where there is a quorum of ten [ḥever ir]. The Rabbis say: … with a ḥever ir or without a ḥever ir. Rabbi Yehuda says … in his name, … Any place where there is a ḥever ir, an individual is … exempt from … the additional prayer.
GEMARA: … Rabbi Yehuda’s … is … the first tanna. … There is … between them: … an individual who is not in … a ḥever ir. … first tanna holds … individual is exempt … And Rabbi Yehuda holds … obligated

Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana said … Ḥiyya bar Rav said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, who said … in the name of … Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya. Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin said to him: You have spoken well, as … Shmuel said: In all my days I have never prayed the additional prayer as an individual

in Neharde’a, … except for the day when the king’s army [pulmusa] came to the city, and the Sages were preoccupied and did not pray … and I prayed as an individual, and I was an individual … not … in a prayer quorum.

Rabbi Ḥanina Kara, … sat before Rabbi Yannai, and he sat and he said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda who said … in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya. … said to him: Go and read your verses outside, … as the halakha is not in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda who said … in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: I saw Rabbi Yannai, who prayed and then prayed again. … Rabbi Yirmeya said to … Rabbi Zeira: … Perhaps initially he did not focus his mind … and ultimately he focused his mind, … said to him: Look at who the great man is who is testifying about him.
although there were thirteen synagogues in Tiberias, Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi would only pray between the columns where they studied,

It was stated: Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi in the name of Rabbeinu, … said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda who said … in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya. … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba prayed and … prayed again. Rav Zeira said to him: Why did the Master do this? If you say because the Master did not focus his mind … didn’t Rabbi Eliezer say: One must always evaluate himself … If he is able to focus his heart … he should pray, but if not, … he should not pray. … Rather, … my Master did not mention the New Moon

Wasn’t it taught … One who erred and did not mention the New Moon in the evening prayer, we do not require him to return … because he can recite it in the morning prayer. … in the morning prayer, we do not require him to return … because he can recite it in the additional prayer. … in the additional prayer, we do not require him to return … because he can recite it in the afternoon prayer?
said to him: Wasn’t it stated about that … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: They taught … in a communal

How long should one wait between … prayer and … prayer? Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda … One said … so that his mind will be in a pleading … [titḥonen], … One … said: … so that his mind will be in a beseeching … [titḥolel],

The one who said: So that his mind will be in a pleading … [titḥonen], as it is written: “And I pleaded [va’etḥanan] before the Lord” … And the one who said: So that his mind will be in a beseeching … [titḥolel] as it is written: “And Moses besought [vayeḥal] the Lord”
Rav Anan said … Rav said: One who erred and did not mention the New Moon in the evening prayer, we do not require him to return … because the court only sanctifies the new month by day,
Ameimar said: Rav’s statement is reasonable in a full month, … But in a short month … we require him to return
Rav Ashi said to Ameimar: Since Rav states a reason … what … is … to me … short, and what … is … to me … full? Rather, there is no difference.

MISHNA: One … only stand … from … gravity … the early … pious … would wait one hour, … and … pray, so that they would focus their hearts toward their Father in Heaven. … even … the king greets him, he should not respond to him; and even if a snake is wrapped on his heel, he should not interrupt
GEMARA: … From where are these matters … as the verse states: “And she felt bitterness of soul,
From what … Perhaps Hannah is different, as … heart was extremely embittered,
Rather, Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said, … from here, … “But as for me, by Your abundant loving-kindness I will enter Your house, at Your Holy Temple I will bow in reverence for You”

From what … Perhaps David is different, as he would excessively afflict himself in prayer … Rather, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, … from here, … bow to the Lord in the beauty of holiness [behadrat kodesh]” … Do not read: In the beauty of [behadrat] … Rather … In trembling of [beḥerdat]

From what … Perhaps, actually I would say to you … Specifically, “in the beauty,” … as … of Rav Yehuda who would adorn himself and then pray. … Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said … from here, … “Serve the Lord in fear and rejoice with trembling”
What is … rejoice with trembling? Rav Adda bar Mattana said … Rabba said: … where there is rejoicing, there should be trembling.
Abaye was sitting before … Rabba, … saw that he was excessively joyful. He said … It is written: Rejoice with trembling,
said to him: … I am donning phylacteries
Rabbi Yirmeya was sitting before Rabbi Zeira. He saw that Rabbi Yirmeya was excessively joyful. He said to him: It is written: “In all sorrow there is profit”
said to him: … I am donning phylacteries.
Mar, son of Ravina, made a wedding … for his son … he saw the Sages, who were excessively joyous.
He brought a valuable cup worth four hundred zuz and broke it before them and they became sad.
Rav Ashi made a wedding … for his son … he saw the Sages, who were excessively joyous. He brought a cup of … white glass and broke it before them, and they became sad.

The Sages said to Rav Hamnuna Zuti at the wedding … of Mar, son of Ravina: Let the Master sing for us. … he said to them, … Woe unto us, for we shall die, woe unto us, for we shall die. They said to him: What shall we respond after you? … He said to them, … Where is Torah and where is mitzva that protect us?

Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: One is forbidden to fill his mouth with mirth in this world, … as it is stated: … “then will our mouths fill with laughter and our lips with song” … When … “they will say among nations, the Lord has done great things with these” … They said about Reish Lakish that throughout his life he did not fill his mouth with laughter in this world once he heard this … from his teacher, Rabbi Yoḥanan.
the Sages taught: One … neither stand … from … judgment nor … from … matter of halakha, … Rather … from … a … conclusive halakha
And … What is an example … conclusive halakha?

Abaye said: … like this … of Rabbi Zeira, … Rabbi Zeira said: The daughters of Israel were stringent with themselves; … that even if they see a drop of blood corresponding to … a mustard … she sits seven clean … for it.
Rava said: … like this … of Rav Hoshaya, as Rav Hoshaya said: A person may employ artifice … upon … his grain and bring it into … in its chaff so that his animal will eat … and … is exempt … tithes.
And if you wish, say … like this … of Rav Huna, … Rav Huna said … Rabbi Zeira said: One who lets blood from a consecrated animal … benefit … is prohibited. … one misuses
the Sages acted in accordance with … our mishna … Rav Ashi acted in accordance with … the baraita

the Sages taught: One may neither stand to pray from … sorrow nor from … laziness, nor from … laughter, nor from … conversation, nor from … frivolity, nor from … purposeless matters. Rather, … from … the joy of a mitzva.

Similarly, a person should neither take leave of another from … conversation, nor from … laughter, nor from … frivolity, nor from … purposeless matters. Rather, … from … matter of halakha. As we found in … the early prophets, that they would conclude their talks with words of praise and consolation.
And so Mari, the grandson of Rav Huna, son of Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba, taught in a baraita: One should only take leave of another from … matter of halakha, so that, consequently, he will remember him;

As … that Rav Kahana accompanied Rav Shimi bar Ashi from … Pum Nahara to the palm grove … Babylonia. When he arrived there, … said to … Master, what is meant by that which people say: These palm trees … Babylonia have been … Adam the first … until now?

said to him: You reminded me of something that Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, … as Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: What is … that which is written: “In a land through which no man has passed and where no person [adam] has settled” … since it is … no … has passed, how … have settled … Rather, … to teach … every land … which Adam the first … decreed that it would be settled was settled, and every land … which … decreed that it would not be settled was not settled.
Rav Mordekhai accompanied … Rav Shimi bar Ashi, … from … Hagronya to Bei Keifei; and some say … to Bei Dura.
the Sages taught … One who prays must focus his heart toward Heaven. Abba Shaul says: An indication of … matter … direct their hearts, Your ear will listen”

it was taught … Rabbi Yehuda said: This was the custom of Rabbi Akiva, when he would pray with the congregation he would shorten … and go up, due to … encumbrance on the congregation … But when he prayed by himself … a person would leave … in one corner … and … find him … in another corner. And why … so much? Because of his bows and prostrations.
Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said: One should always pray in a house with windows, as it is stated … there were open windows
might have … that one could pray … throughout the entire day; it has already been articulated by Daniel, … “And three times
I might have thought that this … began … when he came to … exile; it was stated: … as he had done before.”
might have … that one may pray … any direction he wishes; the verse states: … “facing Jerusalem.”
might have … that one may include all … at one time; it has already been articulated by David … as it is written: “Evening and morning and noon,
I might have … that one may make his voice heard in his … prayer; it has already been articulated by Hannah … as it is stated: … and her voice could not be heard”

might have … that one should request his own needs first, and afterwards recite prayers … it has already been articulated by Solomon … it is stated: “To hear the song and the prayer … song is prayer … prayer is … request … does not speak matters of request after … emet veyatziv … But after the … prayer … even the equivalent of the order of the confession of Yom Kippur, … recite

was also stated … Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said … Rav said: Although … said … one requests his … needs in … Who listens to prayer, … If he comes … and recite … after … his … prayer, even … the equivalent of the order of the confession of Yom Kippur, … recite

Rav Hamnuna said: How many significant … can be derived from these verses … of Hannah? … From … here: “And Hannah spoke in her heart,” … one who prays must focus his heart … from … here: “Only her lips moved,” … one who prays must enunciate … with his lips, … From … here: “And her voice could not be heard,” … one is forbidden to raise his voice in his … prayer … From … here: “So Eli thought her to be drunk,” … a drunk person is forbidden to pray.
“And Eli said to her: How long will you remain drunk? … Rabbi Elazar said: From here … one who sees in another

an unseemly matter, he must reprimand him, … “And Hannah answered and she said no, my master, … Ulla, and some say Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said … she said to him, … With regard to this matter, you are not a master, and the Divine Spirit does not rest upon you, as you … suspect me of this.

Some say … She said to him, … Aren’t you a master? Aren’t the Divine Presence and Divine Spirit with you that you judged me to be guilty, and you did not judge me to be innocent? Didn’t you know that I am a woman of distressed spirit?
“I have drunk neither wine nor liquor,” Rabbi Elazar said: From here … that one who is suspected of something of which he is not … must inform

“Do not take your maidservant as a wicked woman [bat beliya’al] … Rabbi Elazar said: From here … that when a drunk person prays it is as if he engaged in idol worship … it is written here … as a bat beliya’al”; … it is written there, … “Benei beliya’al have gone out from your midst … Just as there, … idol worship, so too here, … idol worship.

“And Eli answered and said: May you go in peace” … Rabbi Elazar said: From here … that one who suspects another of something that he has not … he must appease him. Moreover, … must bless him, … as it is stated: “And may the God of Israel grant your request

“And she swore an oath and said, Lord of Hosts [Tzeva’ot] … Rabbi Elazar said: From the day that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created His world, there was no person who called the Holy One, Blessed be He, Lord of Hosts until Hannah came and called Him Lord of Hosts.
Hannah said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, … of all of the hosts and hosts … that You created in Your world, is it difficult in Your eyes to grant me one son?

a parable: To what is this similar? … a flesh and blood king who made a feast for his servants. A poor person came and stood at the door. He said to them: Give me one slice … And they paid him no attention. He pushed and entered before the king. He said to him: My lord, the King, from this entire feast that you have prepared, is it so difficult in your eyes to give me a single slice

“if you will look upon [im ra’o tireh],” Rabbi Elazar said: Hannah said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, if You will look upon [ra’o … fine, and if not, … You will see … tireh

I will go and seclude myself … before Elkana, my husband. Since I secluded myself, they will force me to drink the sota water … and … You will not make Your Torah false [pelaster], … says: … she shall be acquitted and she shall conceive”

works out well … to the one who said … If she were barren, she will be remembered … well. But … to the one who said … if she had … given birth with pain, … gives birth with ease, … daughters, … gives birth to sons, … black … gives birth to fair … short, … gives birth to tall, … what can be said?

As it was taught … “Then she shall be acquitted and she shall conceive” teaches that if she was barren, she will be remembered … the statement of Rabbi Yishmael. Rabbi Akiva said to him: If so, all barren women will go and seclude themselves … and any … who did not … sin … will be remembered … Rather, … teaches … if she has … given birth with pain, … gives birth with ease, … short … gives birth to tall … black … gives birth to fair … one … gives birth to two
what … Im ra’o tireh? The Torah spoke in the language of men,
“The affliction of Your maidservant … not forget Your maidservant and will give Your maidservant”

Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: Why … these three maidservants [amatot] … Hannah said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, You have created three crucibles … death in a woman, … some say: … three accelerants of death … They are … a menstruating woman, … ḥalla … and lighting … candles. Have I ever violated one of them?
“And You will grant Your servant an offspring of men.”

What is … “an offspring of men”? Rav said: … a man among men, … And Shmuel said: … an offspring who will anoint two men … And who were they? Saul and David. And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … an offspring who … the equivalent of two … men. And who were they? Moses and Aaron. As it is stated: “Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among those who call His name” … And the Rabbis say: “An offspring of men”: … an offspring who would be inconspicuous among men,
When Rav Dimi came … he said … neither too tall nor too short; neither too small nor too fat; neither too white nor too red; neither too smart nor too stupid.
I am the woman who stood here with you … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: From here … that it is forbidden to sit within four cubits of … praying

“for this youth I prayed” … Rabbi Elazar said: Samuel was … taught halakha in the presence of his teacher. … as it is stated: “And they slaughtered the cow and they brought the youth to Eli” … Because they slaughtered the cow, … they brought the youth to Eli?

Rather, … Eli said to … Call a priest; he will come and slaughter … Samuel saw them looking for a priest to slaughter … He said to them: Why do you … to look for a priest to slaughter … Slaughter … by a non-priest is valid. They brought him before Eli … said to him: How do you know this? … said to him: Is it written … And the priest shall slaughter … It is written: “And the priests shall offer,” … from … receiving … and onward is it a mitzva … priests … From here … slaughter by a non-priest is acceptable

said to … You have spoken well … nevertheless, you are … issued a halakhic ruling in the presence of your teacher, and anyone who issues a halakhic ruling in the presence of his teacher, … is liable for death … Hannah came and shouted before him: “I am the woman who stood here with you … He said to her: Let me punish him, and I will pray … will grant you … greater than … She said to him: “For this youth I prayed”

“And Hannah spoke on her heart.” … Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra: … concerning matters of her heart. She said before Him: Master of the Universe, … all … You created in a woman, You have not created one in vain. … eyes to see, ears to hear, a nose to smell, a mouth to speak, hands with which to perform labor, feet with which to walk, breasts with which to nurse. … these breasts that You placed upon my heart, to what … not … to nurse with them? Grant me a son and I will nurse with them.

Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra: Anyone who sits … fast on Shabbat, … they tear up … his sentence of seventy years; … Nevertheless, they then hold him accountable … the halakha of delight of Shabbat
What is his remedy … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: He must sit … fast … for the fast
And Rabbi Elazar said: Hannah spoke impertinently toward … on High. As it is stated: “And she prayed onto the Lord,” … teaches that she spoke impertinently toward on High.

And … Rabbi Elazar said … Elijah spoke impertinently toward … on High … as it is stated: … and You have turned their hearts backward” … Rabbi Shmuel bar Rabbi Yitzḥak said: From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, ultimately conceded to Elijah
As it is written … those with whom I have dealt in wickedness”
Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: Had it not been for these three verses, the legs of the enemies of Israel, … would have collapsed, as

One … it is written: “Those whom I have dealt in wickedness.” And one … it is written: “Behold, like clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in My hand, house of Israel” … And one … it is written: … and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and I will give you a heart of flesh”
Rav Pappa said … from here: “And I will place My spirit within you and I will cause you to walk in My statutes,
And Rabbi Elazar said: Moses … spoke impertinently toward … on High, as it is stated … “And Moses prayed to the Lord … Do not read to [el] the Lord, … onto [al] the Lord,
As … of the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov would … read alef as ayin and ayin as alef
the school of Rabbi Yannai, … say … from here, … “And Di Zahav”

What is … and Di Zahav? … the school of Rabbi Yannai said that Moses said the following before the Holy One, Blessed be He, … Master of the Universe, because of the gold and silver that you lavished upon Israel … until they said enough [dai]; … that caused … to make the … Calf.
the school of Rabbi Yannai said: A lion does not roar … over a basket of straw … but … over a basket of meat,
Rabbi Oshaya said: … comparable to a person who had a lean, but large-limbed cow. … he fed it lupines, … and … was kicking him. He said to … Who caused you … kicking me if not the lupines I fed you?

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … comparable to a person who had a son; he bathed him and anointed him … fed him and gave him drink, and hung a purse … around his neck. … brought … to the entrance of a brothel. What could the son do to avoid sinning?

Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Huna, said … Rav Sheshet said: That is what people say … Filling his stomach is a type of sin, as it is stated: “When they were fed and became full they were sated, and their hearts were lifted and they have forgotten Me” … Rav Naḥman said: … from here: “And your heart is lifted and you forget the Lord” … And the Rabbis say … from here: “And they will have eaten and been sated and fattened, and they will turn

And if you wish, say … from here: “And Jeshurun grew fat and kicked” … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yonatan said: From where … the Holy One, Blessed be He, ultimately conceded to Moses … As it is stated: “And I gave them an abundance of silver and gold, which they used for the Ba’al”

“And the Lord said to Moses: Go and descend, … What is … “go and descend”? Rabbi Elazar said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses: Moses, descend from your greatness. Isn’t it only for the sake of Israel, … that I granted you prominence; and now that Israel has sinned, why do I … you? … Immediately, Moses’ strength waned and he was powerless to speak … And once … said … “Leave Me be, that I may destroy them” … Moses said … this matter is dependent upon me. Immediately Moses stood and was strengthened in prayer, and asked … mercy

wheat flour, … Rav Yehuda said … Who creates fruit of the ground, and Rav Naḥman said … By Whose word all things came to be.

about the rest,

Granted, according to the one who said … burned by the heat … that is … that it was taught … lenient with regard to demai, … those … uncertainty … that are exempt … Those … certainty … one is obligated … However, according to the one who said … dates … of the wind, … Those … certainty … one is obligated? They are ownerless,

With what are we dealing here? … made them … a pile of threshed grain, … As Rabbi Yitzḥak said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov: … gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and … corners, … made them into a pile of threshed grain, … they were rendered … tithes.

Granted, according to the one who said … dispute … in … where their blessings are identical, it … well. However, according to the one who says … they disagree in … where their blessings are not identical, … about what do they disagree? … Rabbi Yirmeya said: … precedes

As Rav Yosef, and some say Rabbi Yitzḥak, said: Each … precedes … in this verse, … takes precedence … in terms of blessing as well, as it is stated: “A land of wheat and barley, vines, figs and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey”
disagrees … of Rabbi Ḥanan. As Rabbi Ḥanan said: The entire verse was stated for … measures

Wheat … as we learned … One who enters a house afflicted … with his clothes … on his shoulders, and his sandals and his rings are in his hands, … he and they, … immediately … ritually impure. … he was dressed in his clothes, and his sandals were on his feet and his rings on his fingers, he immediately becomes ritually impure … but they, … remain pure until he stays … long enough to eat half a loaf … wheat bread, … and not … barley bread, … reclining and eating … with a relish,

vines … the quantity of a quarter log of wine for a Nazirite … Figs … a dried fig-bulk, … for carrying out on Shabbat … Pomegranates … as we learned … All … utensils belonging to … homeowners

said to him: This, … is … second to … land, … and this, … fifth to … land. … said to him … Who will give us iron legs that we may serve you

asked Ben Zoma: Why did … say … items that come due to the meal during the meal, neither require a blessing before … them nor after … them? He said to them: Because bread exempts them. … If so, bread should also exempt wine. … Wine is different,
as it causes a blessing itself.

said to them: … it was stated … The halakha is not in accordance with … Rabbi Mona. wine came before them during the meal, each and every … recites a blessing … for himself. … after the meal, one recites a blessing on behalf of them all. And he, … says … over the incense … mugmar … although they only bring the incense … after the meal.

were sitting … and each and every … they reclined, yes, … they did not recline, no. according to that version … Rav said: This … was only taught … bread that … requires reclining … However, wine does not require reclining; the first clause … is difficult.

wine came before them during the meal, … They asked Ben Zoma: Why did … say: … wine came before them during the meal, each and every … recites a blessing … for himself; … after the meal, one recites a blessing on behalf of them all? He said to them: … because … the throat is not available.
