Rabbi Abbahu ate … until … a fly would slip from his forehead. And Rav Ami and Rav Asi would eat … until their hair fell out. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish would eat them until he became confused. And … Rabbi Yoḥanan would tell the household of the Nasi … and Rabbi Yehuda Nesia would send the authorities after him and they would take him to his house.

When Rav Dimi came … he said: King Yannai had a city on the King’s Mountain, from which they would take six-hundred thousand bowls of sardines for those cutting figs … trees … from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve.

when Rav Dimi came … he said: King Yannai had a tree on the King’s Mountain from which they would remove forty se’a of pigeons from three broods each month. When Rabbi Yitzḥak came … he said: There was a city in Eretz Yisrael named Gufnit, in which there were eighty pairs of brothers who were priests, married to eighty pairs of sisters, who were all from priestly … And … The Sages checked from Sura to Neharde’a, and with the exception of the daughters of Rav Ḥisda, who were married to Rami bar Ḥama and … Mar Ukva bar Ḥama, they could not find … And, … although they, … were … a priest, they, … were not priests.
Rav said: Any meal in which there is no salt is not … a meal. Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Any meal in which there is no … gravy … is not … a meal.

MISHNA: One who ate … grapes and figs and pomegranates, recites … three blessings … the statement of Rabban Gamliel. And the Rabbis say: … one blessing abridged from … three … Rabbi Akiva says: … even … one ate boiled vegetables, but it is his … sustenance, he recites … three blessings … One who drinks water … his thirst recites: By whose word all things came to be. Rabbi Tarfon says: … Who creates the many forms of life and their needs.

GEMARA: … What is the reason … of Rabban Gamliel? … As it is written … “A land of wheat and barley, … and it is written: “A land in which you will eat bread without scarcity” … and it is written: “And you will eat and be satisfied and then you shall bless the Lord your God
And … the Rabbis … “A land … concluded … that matter, … And … Rabban Gamliel as well, … “land” conclude … that matter? Rather, that … is necessary … to exclude one who chews … wheat

Rabbi Ya’akov bar Idi said … Rabbi Ḥanina said: Anything that is from the five species … at the start, one recites over it: Who creates the various kinds of nourishment, and at the end, one blessing abridged from … three

Rabba bar Mari said … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Anything that is from the seven species … at the start, one recites over it: Who creates fruit of the tree, and afterward and at the end, one blessing abridged from … three

Abaye said to Rav Dimi: What is the … one blessing abridged from … three … Over fruits of a tree one recites:
For the tree and the fruit of the tree,
and for the produce of the field,
and for the desirable, good and spacious land that you gave as a heritage to our ancestors
that they might eat of its fruit and be satisfied with its goodness.
Have compassion, Lord our God,
upon Israel Your people and upon Jerusalem Your city,
and upon Your Temple and upon Your altar.
May You rebuild Jerusalem, Your holy city, swiftly in our time, 
and may You bring us back there rejoicing in it
as You are good and do good to all.
five species … For the nourishment and sustenance and for the produce of the field, and he concludes: For the land and for the nourishment.
conclusion, with what does he conclude … When Rav Dimi came … he said: Rav … conclude … on the New Moon: Blessed…Who sanctifies Israel and the New Moons. … What … here?
Rav Ḥisda said: For the land and for its fruits. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: For the land and for the fruits. Rav Amram said: They do not disagree; … this … for us, … and this … them,

Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak strongly objects: They, … eat and we, … recite a blessing? … Rather, reverse … Rav Ḥisda said: For the land and for the fruits, and Rabbi Yoḥanan said: For the land and for its fruits.

Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said in the name of Rabbeinu, … Over the egg and types of meat [kupra], at the start, one recites: By Whose word all things came to be, and at the end: Who creates the many forms of life. However, … vegetables, no, … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Even … vegetables … but … water, no, … And Rav Pappa said: Even … water
Mar Zutra acted in accordance with … Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avdimi … Rav Shimi bar Ashi acted in accordance with … Rabbi Yitzḥak … And a mnemonic … One like two, and two like one.
Rav Ashi said: At times when I remember, I act in accordance with … all of them

We learned … Anything that requires a blessing thereafter requires a blessing beforehand; and there are … that require a blessing beforehand and do not require a blessing thereafter. … granted, according to Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi’s … excludes vegetables … according to Rabbi Yitzḥak’s … excludes water … However, according to Rav Pappa’s opinion, what does it exclude?
to exclude mitzvot,
And for the residents of the West, … who, after they remove their phylacteries, recite: Who has made us holy through His mitzvot and commanded us to keep His laws, what … come to exclude?
to exclude … fragrances.

Rabbi Yannai said … Rabbi … said: Anything that is an egg’s equivalent … an egg is superior to it. … when Ravin came … he said: A lightly cooked egg is better than six log of fine flour. … when Rav Dimi came … he said: A lightly cooked egg is better than six … roasted … four, … cooked … Anything that is an egg’s equivalent, an egg is superior to it except for meat.

Rabbi Akiva says: Even … one ate boiled vegetables, but it is his … sustenance, he recites … three blessings … And is there a … where in its boiled … it is … sustenance? Rav Ashi said: This was taught … a cabbage stalk,

the Sages taught … spleen is beneficial for the teeth and harmful for the intestines. Leeks, … are harmful for the teeth and beneficial for the intestines. … all raw vegetables … pale. … anything small … impedes growth, and any living creature … restores the soul. And anything close to the soul restores the soul. Cabbage … for nourishment and beets for healing. Woe unto the house through which the turnip passes,
The Master said … The spleen is beneficial for the teeth and harmful for the intestines. … What is its remedy? … One should chew it, … and throw it away.
Leeks are harmful for the teeth and beneficial for the intestines. … What is its remedy? … One should boil them and swallow them
All raw vegetables … pale. Rabbi Yitzḥak said: … to the first meal after bloodletting,

And Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Anyone who eats vegetables before four hours … it is forbidden to speak with him. … What is the reason? … because the smell … And … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: It is forbidden to eat raw vegetables before four hours

Ameimar, Mar Zutra, and Rav Ashi were sitting. They brought raw vegetables before them before four hours … Ameimar and Rav Ashi ate and Mar Zutra did not eat. They said to him: What is your thinking … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Anyone who eats vegetables before four hours … it is forbidden to speak with him because of the smell? Aren’t we eating and you are … speaking with us?
He said to them: I hold in accordance with the other … Rabbi Yitzḥak, as Rabbi Yitzḥak said … It is forbidden to eat raw vegetables before four hours
Anything small impedes growth. Rav Ḥisda said: … even to a small goat, … a zuz. … And we only said … to … has not … one fourth … But … it has … one fourth … we need not
And any living creature … restores the soul. Rav Pappa said: … even small fish … among the reeds,

Anything close to the soul restores the soul. Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: … neck, … Rava said to his servant: When you bring me a piece of meat, make an effort to bring me … from the place of the blessing,

Cabbage for nourishment and beets for healing. … cabbage … for nourishment and not for healing? Wasn’t it taught … Six things cure the ill … of his disease and their cure is an … cure, and these are: Cabbage, beets, chamomile water, honey, stomach, heret, and liver. … Rather, say: Cabbage is even for sustenance
Woe unto the house through which the turnip passes, … Is that so? Didn’t Rava say to his servant: When you see a turnip in the market, do not ask me with what will you eat your bread today?
Abaye said: … without meat. And Rava said: Without wine. It was stated … Rav said: … without meat. And Shmuel said: Without wood, … And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Without wine.

Rava said to Rav Pappa: Farmer … we break … with meat and wine. You, who do not have a lot of wine, with what do you break its … said to him: With wood. As that … Rav Pappa’s wife … After she cooked … she would break it with eighty pieces … from a palm tree.

the Sages taught … A small salted fish sometimes kills, … seven … seventeen … and twenty-seven … And some say: Twenty-three. And we only said this when it is roasted and not roasted … but … roasted well, we need not … And when it is not roasted well, we only said this when one does not drink beer thereafter; however, … one drinks beer thereafter, we need not
drinks water … his thirst. … What does … to exclude? Rav Idi bar Avin said: … to exclude one
who was choked by a piece of meat

Rabbi Tarfon says: … Who creates the many forms of life and their needs. Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye, and some say to Rav Yosef: What is the halakha … He said to him: Go out and observe what the people are doing

MISHNA: … Three … who ate as one are required to form a zimmun … one ate doubtfully tithed produce [demai], and first tithe from which its teruma was … taken, … second tithe, and consecrated food that were redeemed … and … the waiter … who ate … an olive-bulk … and the Samaritan [Kuti] … to obligate … in a zimmun.

one who ate untithed produce [tevel], and first tithe from which its teruma was not separated, and second tithe, and consecrated food that were not redeemed, and the waiter who did not eat an olive-bulk, and the gentile … to obligate … in a zimmun. Women, slaves, and minors do not obligate … in a zimmun. How much … to obligate … in a zimmun? An olive-bulk … Rabbi Yehuda says: An egg-bulk

GEMARA: … From where are these matters … , … Rav Asi said: As the verse states: “Praise God with me, and we will exalt His name together” … Rabbi Abbahu said: … from … here: “When I call the Name of the Lord, give … praise to our God”

Rav Ḥanan bar Abba said: From where … that one who answers amen should not raise his voice louder than the one reciting the blessing? As it is stated: “Praise God with me, and we will exalt His Name together”;

Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said: From where … that the translator … is not permitted to raise his voice louder than the reader? As it is stated: “Moses spoke, and God responded in a voice” … there is no need for the verse to state: In a voice. … what … did the verse state: In a voice? In Moses’ voice,

This was also taught … The translator is not permitted to raise his voice louder than the reader. … and if the translator cannot raise his voice to match … the reader, the reader should lower his voice and read.

It was stated: Two who ate as one … Rav and Rabbi Yoḥanan disagreed: One said: If they wanted to join together, they may form a zimmun. The other said: … if they wanted to join together, they may not form a zimmun.
we learned … Three who ate as one are required to join together … Three, yes, … two, no,
there, … obligatory … here, … optional
Come and hear: Three who ate as one are required to join together … and may not disperse … three, yes, … two, no,
It is different there, … from the outset, they established themselves as … obligated
Come and hear, … A waiter who was serving two people eats with them, although they did not give him permission … was serving three … he may not eat with them unless they gave him permission
It is different there,
because from the outset, they prefer to establish … as an obligation

Come and hear: Women form a zimmun for themselves and slaves form a zimmun for themselves; … women, slaves, and minors, … if they wish to form a zimmun … they may not form a zimmun. But aren’t one hundred women considered the equivalent of two men, in that they cannot constitute a prayer quorum? And yet, the baraita teaches that women form a zimmun for themselves and Canaanite slaves form a zimmun for themselves. Apparently, like women, two men can form a zimmun on their own.
There it is different because, … there are … minds,
If so, say the latter clause … Women and slaves, if they wish to form a zimmun, they may not form a zimmun. Why not? Aren’t … minds,
it is different there, … due to promiscuity.

Conclude that Rav … said: If they wanted to join together, they may not form a zimmun. As Rav Dimi bar Yosef said … Rav said: Three … who ate as one and one of them went out to the marketplace, they call him and include him in the zimmun. The reason is because they call him; … if they do not call him, no,
It is different there, … from the outset, they established themselves as … obligated

Rather, conclude that Rabbi Yoḥanan is the one who said: If they wanted to join together, they may not form a zimmun, as Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Two … who ate as one, one fulfills his obligation … with the … blessing of the other.
And we discussed it … What is he teaching us? We … learned this … One who heard … and did not respond, … he fulfilled … And Rabbi Zeira said: … there is no blessing of zimmun among them. … conclude

Rava bar Rav Huna said to … Rav Huna: Didn’t the Sages who came from the West, … say that … if they wanted to join together, they may form a zimmun? What, is it not that they heard … from Rabbi Yoḥanan, … No, … that they heard … from Rav before he … descended to Babylonia.

the matter … itself: Rav Dimi bar Yosef said … Rav said: Three … who ate as one and one of them went out to the marketplace, they call him and include him in the zimmun, … Abaye said: This is … that they call him and he responds,
Mar Zutra said: We only said … with regard to … three; but, with regard to … ten, … until … comes
Rav Ashi strongly objects to this: On the contrary, the opposite is more reasonable. Nine … appear like ten, … Two … do not appear like three,

And the halakha is in accordance with … Mar Zutra. What is the reason? Because in a zimmun of ten they need to mention the Name of Heaven, and it is not proper conduct to invoke the Name of Heaven with fewer than ten people present.

Abaye said … we have a tradition: Two … who ate as one, it is a mitzva … to separate … This was also taught … Two … who ate as one, it is a mitzva … to separate … In what … are these matters stated? … when both … are learned people [soferim] … However, … one of them was a learned person and the other an ignoramus, the learned person recites the blessing … the ignoramus thereby fulfills

Rava said: This is a statement that I said and it was stated in the name of Rabbi Zeira in accordance with my … Three … who ate as one … one interrupts … to … two … but two do not interrupt … to … one
And … not … Didn’t Rav Pappa interrupt … to … Abba Mar, his son, … and one … Rav Pappa is different, as … acted beyond the letter of the law.

Yehuda bar Mareimar, Mar bar Rav Ashi and Rav Aḥa of Difti ate bread together. None among them was greater than the other … recite the blessing on their behalf. They sat down and raised a dilemma: That which we learned … Three … who ate as one are required to join together … that apply only when there is a great man … but where they are on a par with each other, … separating … blessings is preferable?

each person recited the blessing for himself. … they came before Mareimar … said to them: … you fulfilled your … blessing … you did not fulfill … zimmun. And if you say: Let us go back and form a zimmun, there is no retroactive zimmun.
One who came and found them reciting the … blessing, what does he say after them … Rav Zevid said … Blessed … and blessed … Rav Pappa said: He answers amen.

do not disagree. This is … where he found them saying: Let us bless; and that is … where he found them saying: Blessed be. … Where he found them saying: Let us bless, he says: Blessed … and blessed … where he found them saying: Blessed be, he answers amen.
One … taught: One who answers amen after his … blessings, it is praiseworthy. Another … taught: It is reprehensible.
not difficult. This, … is in … Who builds Jerusalem; this, … is in other blessings.

Abaye would answer … aloud … so the workers would hear and stand … as … Who is good and does good, is not … by Torah law, … Rav Ashi, … answer … in a whisper, so that … would not relate to … Who is good and does good, with contempt.

Rabbi Zeira took ill. Rabbi Abbahu went to visit him and resolved: If the little man with the scorched legs, … is cured, I will make a festival, … for the Sages. … was cured and … made a feast for all the Sages. When it came time to break … said to Rabbi Zeira: Master, … break … for us. … said to him: Doesn’t the Master hold … that … of Rabbi Yoḥanan, … said: The host breaks … broke … for them.
When … came to recite the blessing, … said to … Master, recite … on our behalf. … said to him: Doesn’t the Master hold … that … of Rabbi Huna of Babylonia, … said: He who breaks … recites
And in accordance with whose … does … hold

that Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: The host breaks bread and a guest recites … The host breaks … so that he will break … generously, … and the guest recites … so that he may bless the host
What is … blesses … May it be Your will that the master of the house shall not suffer shame in this world, nor humiliation in the World-to-Come.

Rabbi … added to it elements … And may he be very successful with all his possessions, 
and may his possessions and our possessions be successful and near the city, 
and may Satan control neither his deeds nor our deeds, 
and may no thought of sin, iniquity, or transgression stand before him or before us 
from now and for evermore.
Until where … the zimmun blessing
Rav Naḥman says: … until: Let us bless. Rav Sheshet says … until … Who feeds

Let us say … is parallel to a … between the tanna’im. As one … taught: Grace after Meals … two and three … and another … taught: Grace after Meals … three and four … assumed that everyone … Who is good and does good, … is not … by Torah law. What … Is it not that they disagree about this: The one who said … two and three … holds that the zimmun blessing extends until … Who feeds … Who feeds … And the one who said … three and four … holds … until: Let us bless,
No; Rav Naḥman explains in accordance with his reasoning and Rav Sheshet explains in accordance with his reasoning.

Rav Naḥman explains in accordance with his reasoning; everyone … until Let us bless. … the one who said … three and four … well. And the one who said … two and three … said to you: Here we are dealing with the blessing recited by laborers, as the Master said … he begins with … Who feeds … and includes … Who builds Jerusalem, in … the blessing of the land.

Rav Sheshet explains in accordance with his reasoning; everyone … until … Who feeds … the one who said … two and three … well; and the one who said … three and four … holds … Who is good and does good, is … by Torah law.
Rav Yosef said: Know … Who is good and does good, is not … by Torah law, as laborers … eliminate it.

Rav Yitzḥak bar Shmuel bar Marta said … in the name of Rav: Know … Who is good and does good, is not … by Torah law, … begins … with: Blessed, but does not conclude reciting it with: Blessed. … as it was taught … All blessings, … begins … them with: Blessed, and concludes … them with: Blessed, except for blessings over fruit, blessings over mitzvot, a blessing that is juxtaposed to another … and the final blessing after Shema. There are among these … those that … begins … with: Blessed, but does not conclude reciting it with: Blessed;

and there are among these … that … concludes … with: Blessed, but does not begin … with: Blessed. … Who is good and does good, … begins … with: Blessed, but does not conclude … with: Blessed. … by inference that it is an independent blessing.

And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: Know … Who is good and does good, is not … by Torah law, as it is eliminated in the house of the mourner, as it was taught … What do they say in the house of the mourner? Blessed…Who is good and does good. Rabbi Akiva says: Blessed…the true Judge.
Who is good and does good, yes, … the true Judge, no, … Rather, say: Who is good and does good, … as well.

Mar Zutra happened … to Rav Ashi’s home … incident of … befell … began … and recited:
Who is good and does good, 
God of truth, the true Judge,
Who judges with righteousness, takes away with justice,
and is the ruler of His world to do in it as He wills,
as all His ways are just,
that all is His and we are His people and His servants,
and in everything we are obligated to thank Him and bless Him,
Who repairs the breaches in Israel,
He will repair this breach in Israel for life.

To where does he return … Rav Zevid in the name of Abaye said: He returns to the beginning … And the Rabbis say: He returns to the place that he stopped. And the halakha is: He returns to the place that he stopped,

The Exilarch said to Rav Sheshet: Although you are elderly Sages, the Persians are more expert than you with regard to the required … meals. … when there are two divans … the greater … reclines first and the … second to him … above him, … When there are three … the greatest … reclines … the one second to him … above him, and the one third to him … below
said to … If … wishes to speak with … he must straighten up and sit and … speak to him. … answered: The Persians are different, as they signal … with … gestures,
the first waters. … from where do they begin? … said to him: They begin from the greatest.
should the greatest … sit and keep his hands clean … everyone has washed … said to him: They bring him his table [takka] immediately,
the final waters. … from where do they begin? … said to him: They begin with the least significant
should the greatest … sit with dirty hands until everyone washes … said to him: They do not remove the table from before him until the water reaches him;

Rav Sheshet said: … I know a baraita, as it was taught: What is the order of reclining? When there are two divans … the greater … reclines first, and the … second to him … below him. When there are three divans, the greatest … reclines first, … the one second to him … above him, and the one third to him … below … The first waters … they begin with the greatest … The final waters; when they are five … they begin with the greatest … When they are … one hundred, they begin … with the least significant … until they reach the five greatest … they return and begin with the greatest … And to the place that the final waters return the blessing also reverts,
This … supports … Rav, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ashi said … Rav said: Whoever washes his hands first at the end … is designated to … the blessing

Rav and Rabbi Ḥiyya were seated at a meal before Rabbi … Rabbi … said to Rav: Stand, wash your hands. … saw that … was trembling … said to him: Son of noblemen, he is saying to you to review Grace after Meals,
The Sages taught: … one shows deference neither on roads nor on bridges,
nor with … dirty hands,

Ravin and Abaye were traveling along the road … Ravin’s donkey preceded Abaye’s and … did not say … Let the Master go … said … since this one of the Sages, … ascended from the West, … he has become arrogant. When they reached the door of the synagogue, … said to … Let the Master enter … said to him: Until now was I not Master? … said to him: Rabbi Yoḥanan said the following: One only defers … at a doorway that has a mezuza,
that has a mezuza, yes, … that does not have a mezuza, no, … If so, a synagogue or study hall that has no mezuza, … too, does one not defer … Rather, say … at a doorway … of … a mezuza,
Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav: Those reclining … may not eat anything until the one breaking bread has tasted … Rav Safra sat and said: … taste, was stated
What difference does … make … one must say … in the … language … by his teacher

The Sages taught: Two people … from a single dish must wait for each other, … three, … they need not wait … the one who breaks bread extends his hand … first, … if he wishes to defer to his teacher or to one who is greater … he has permission

Rabba bar bar Ḥana engaged in … for his son’s … in the house of Rav Shmuel bar Rav Ketina. He arrived early and sat and taught his son … The one who breaks bread may not break … until amen has ended from the mouths of those responding. Rav Ḥisda said: … from the mouths of the majority of those responding.
Rami bar Ḥama said to him: What is different … the majority … That … the blessing has not yet concluded. … the minority … as well, the blessing has not yet concluded.
said to him: Because I say … anyone who answers … amen … excessive … is merely mistaken.
the Sages taught: One should not respond … an abbreviated [ḥatufa] amen, … and a truncated [ketufa] amen, … and an orphaned [yetoma] amen, … one should not … discharge a blessing from his mouth.

Ben Azzai says: Anyone who recites an orphaned amen, his children will be orphaned; … abbreviated … his days will be abbreviated … a truncated … his days will be truncated. One who extends his amen, they will extend his days and years for him.

Rav and Shmuel were sitting at a meal … Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya arrived and was hurrying and eating. Rav said to him: What is your thinking? … to join together with us … We have already eaten … our … Shmuel said to … if they brought me truffles or a young pigeon for Abba, … wouldn’t we eat it?

Rav’s students were seated at a meal … Rav Aḥa entered. … said: A great man has come who can recite the blessing on our behalf. … said to them: Do you think that the greatest recites the blessing? … the main … of the meal recites the blessing. … The halakha … is that the greatest … recites the blessing, even if he arrived at the end

one ate doubtfully tithed produce [demai], … But … is not fit for his … because, if he wants, he could declare all of his property ownerless [hefker] and he would be a pauper, … fit for his … As we learned … One may feed the impoverished demai and … soldiers [akhsania], … demai. And Rav Huna said: It was taught … Beit Shammai say: One may not feed the impoverished and soldiers demai.

first tithe from which its teruma was … taken, … It is obvious … It was only necessary … in … preceded … on the stalks, and he separated the teruma of the tithes … did not separate the teruma gedola. … And … in accordance with … Rabbi Abbahu, as Rabbi Abbahu said … Reish Lakish said: First tithe … preceded … on the stalks is exempt from teruma gedola, as it is stated: “And you shall set apart from it a gift for the Lord, even a tenth part of the tithe” … teaches … a tenth part of the tithe, … and not teruma gedola and the teruma of the tithe.
Rav Pappa said to Abaye: If so, even if … preceded … in a pile, … said to him: With regard to your … the verse stated:
“From all of that is given to you, you shall set apart … And what did you see … This, … has become grain, and that, … did not … become grain.

second tithe and consecrated food that were redeemed, … It is obvious … With what are we dealing here? … a case … where one gave … the principal, … but he did not give … the fifth … and … teaches us … the fifth does not invalidate
The waiter who ate … an olive-bulk … It is obvious. … Lest you say that the waiter … did not establish … teaches us
a Samaritan [Kuti] may be included in a zimmun. … Why? … let him be merely an am ha’aretz, … and it was taught … An am ha’aretz may not be included in a zimmun.

Abaye said: … Kuti who is a ḥaver, … Rava said: Even if you say … a Kuti … am ha’aretz, and here … am ha’aretz … the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Meir, as it was taught … Who is an am ha’aretz? Anyone who does not eat non-sacred food in … ritual purity. … the statement of Rabbi Meir. And the Rabbis say: … anyone who does not appropriately tithe his produce. And these Kutim tithe … appropriately, as they are scrupulous with regard to that which is written in the Torah, as the Master said: Any mitzva that the Kutim embraced … they are … more exacting in its … than Jews.

The Sages taught: Who is an am ha’aretz? One who does not recite Shema in the evening and morning. This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer. Rabbi Yehoshua says: … one who does not don phylacteries. Ben Azzai says: … one who does not have ritual fringes on his garment. Rabbi Natan says: … one who does not have a mezuza on his doorway. Rabbi Natan bar Yosef says: … one who has children but … does not raise them to … Torah study. Aḥerim say: Even if one read the Bible and studied Mishna and did not serve Torah scholars … that is an am ha’aretz. Rav Huna said: The halakha is in accordance with … Aḥerim.

Rami bar Ḥama did not include Rav Menashya bar Taḥlifa, who studied Sifra, Sifrei, and halakhot, in a zimmun … When Rami bar Ḥama passed away, Rava said: Rami bar Ḥama died only because he did not include Rabbi Menashya bar Taḥlifa in a zimmun. … Was it not taught … Aḥerim say: Even if one read the Bible and studied mishna and did not serve Torah scholars, that is an am ha’aretz? … Rav Menashya bar Taḥlifa is different, as he served the Sages. And it was Rami bar Ḥama who was not precise … after him … Another version … who hears halakhot from the mouths of Sages and studies them is considered a Torah scholar.
one who ate untithed produce and … tithe etc. … It is obvious … It was only necessary … untithed produce by rabbinic law, … What are the circumstances? … in an unperforated flowerpot,
first tithe … It is obvious. … It was only necessary … where … preceded … in a pile. Lest you say as Rav Pappa said to Abaye, … teaches us as … responded

second tithe … It is obvious? … It was only necessary … where they were redeemed, but not redeemed properly, i.e., second tithe that was redeemed with an unminted coin [asimon], … And the Torah says: “And bind up [vetzarta] the money in your hand” … money that has a form [tzura] … upon it. Consecrated property; … where he redeemed it … for land instead of money, and the Torah states: “He will give the money and it will be assured to him”
a waiter who ate less than an olive-bulk … It is obvious. … Since the first clause … taught … an olive-bulk, the latter clause taught … less than an olive-bulk.

a gentile is not included in a zimmun. … It is obvious. … With what are we dealing here? … with … a convert who was circumcised but … not … immerse … as Rabbi Zeira said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One is never … a proselyte until he is circumcised and immerses … As long as he did not immerse … he is a gentile.
women, slaves, and minors are not included in a zimmun. Rabbi Yosei said: A minor lying in a cradle is included in a zimmun.
Didn’t we learn … that women, slaves, and minors are not included in a zimmun?
stated … in accordance with … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Although a minor lying in a cradle is not included in a zimmun, one may make him an adjunct to … ten

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Nine … and a slave join together … raises an objection: … incident involving Rabbi Eliezer, who entered a synagogue and did not find … ten, and he liberated his slave and he completed the … ten. … freed … yes, … did not free … no, … two were required … freed one and fulfilled his obligation with … one,

How did he do that? Didn’t Rav Yehuda say: Anyone who frees his … slave violates a positive mitzva, as it is stated … they will serve as bondsmen for you forever” … a mitzva is different. … It is a mitzva that comes through a transgression, … A mitzva … the many is different,

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: One should always rise early … to the synagogue in order to have the privilege and be counted among the first ten … as even if one hundred … arrive after him, he receives the reward of them all, … Does it enter your mind … the reward of them all? … Rather, … say: He receives a reward equivalent to … them all.

Rav Huna said: Nine plus an ark … join … Rav Naḥman said to him: Is an ark a man, … Rather, Rav Huna said: Nine who appear like ten may join together. … Some said this … when they are gathered. And some said this … when they are scattered,

Rav Ami said: Two … and Shabbat join … Rav Naḥman said to him: Is Shabbat a person, … Rather, Rav Ami said: Two Torah scholars who hone each other’s … in halakhic … join together … Rav Ḥisda pointed … For example, me and Rav Sheshet. … Rav Sheshet pointed: For example, me and Rav Ḥisda.

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: A mature minor, … is included in a zimmun. That … was also taught … A minor who grew two … hairs, … is included in a zimmun; and one who did not grow two hairs is not included in a zimmun. And one is not exacting with regard to a minor. … This … itself is difficult. You said that … who grew two hairs, yes, … one who did not grow … no, … and then it taught that one is not exacting with regard to a minor. What … to include? Is it not
to include a mature minor?
The halakha is not in accordance with all of these statements. Rather, … in accordance with this … that Rav Naḥman said: A minor who knows to Whom one recites a blessing is included in a zimmun.

Abaye and Rava, … were seated before Rabba. Rabba said to them: To whom does one recite blessings? They said to him: To … the All-Merciful. … And where does the All-Merciful reside? Rava pointed to the ceiling. Abaye went outside and pointed toward the heaven. Rabba said to them: You will both become Sages. It is as the popular saying goes: A cucumber can be recognized from its blossoming

Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav: … nine ate grain and one ate vegetables, they join … Rabbi Zeira said: I raised a dilemma before Rav Yehuda: What is … eight … What is … seven … He said to me: There is no difference. I certainly had no dilemma with regard to six, … Rabbi Yirmeya said to him: You did well that you had no dilemma … There, … what is the reason … Because there is a majority … Here, too, there is a majority. … held: We require an obvious majority.

King Yannai and the queen ate bread together. And since … executed the Sages, there was no one to recite the … blessing on their behalf. He said to his wife: Who will provide us … a man to recite the blessing on our behalf? She said to him: Swear to me that if I bring you … a man, you will not harass him. He swore, … she brought her brother, Shimon ben Shataḥ. She sat him between … and hers. … said to him: Do you see how much honor I am according you? He responded: … not you who honors me; rather, the Torah honors me, as it is written: “Extol her and she will exalt you; she will bring you to honor when you embrace her” … said to … You see that he does not accept authority.

They gave … a cup … over which to recite … He said: How shall I recite the blessing? … Blessed is He from Whom Yannai and his companions have eaten? … He drank that cup … They gave him another cup, and he recited the … blessing.

Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said): That which Shimon ben Shataḥ did, … he did on his own, … as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said as follows: One … cannot fulfill the obligation of others … until he eats an olive-bulk of grain.
raises an objection … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: One who entered and reclined together … even if he only dipped with them … in … brine … and ate with them only a single dry fig, he joins them.
he joins them, but … satisfy the obligation of the many unless he has eaten an olive-bulk of grain.
was also stated: Rav Ḥana bar Yehuda said in the name of Rava: Even if he only

dipped with them … in brine and ate with them only a single dry fig, he joins them. And to satisfy the obligation of the many, he does not satisfy … until he eats an olive-bulk of grain. Rabbi Ḥana bar Yehuda said in the name of Rava … the halakha is: … ate a vegetable leaf and drank a cup of wine, he joins … to satisfy … he does not satisfy … until he eats an olive-bulk of grain.

Rav Naḥman said: 
Moses instituted for Israel the … blessing of: Who feeds … when the manna descended for them … Joshua instituted the blessing of the land when they entered Eretz Yisrael.
David and Solomon instituted the … Who builds Jerusalem, … David instituted “…on Israel Your people and on Jerusalem Your city…” … and Solomon instituted “…on the great and Holy Temple…” … They instituted … Who is good and does good, at Yavne in reference to the slain … of … Beitar … As Rav Mattana said: On the same day that the slain of Beitar were brought to burial, they instituted … Who is good and does good, at Yavne. Who is good, … did not decompose … and does good, … that they were … brought to burial.

the Sages taught … the order of Grace after Meals is as follows: The first blessing is the blessing of: Who feeds … the second is the blessing of the land; the third is: Who builds Jerusalem; and the fourth is: Who is good and does good. On Shabbat one begins … with consolation and ends with consolation and mentions the sanctity of the day … in the middle. Rabbi Eliezer says: If one wishes to recite … the blessing of consolation: … he recites it … in the blessing of the land, he recites it … in the blessing instituted by the Sages at Yavne, … he recites it … And the Rabbis say: He may only recite … in … the blessing of consolation.
The … Rabbis is … the first tanna. … The difference between … after the fact.

The Sages taught … From where … Grace after Meals is from the Torah? As it is stated: “And you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless … And you shall bless, that is the blessing of: Who feeds … The Lord, your God, that is the zimmun blessing … For the land, that is the blessing of the land; good, that is … Who builds Jerusalem, and it also says: “This good mountain and Lebanon” … That He gave you, that is: Who is good and does good. … I only have … after … From where … before … You said … an a fortiori inference: When one is satisfied, he … recite a blessing … when he is hungry, all the more so

Rabbi … says: It is not necessary … “And you shall eat and be satisfied, and you shall bless,” that is the blessing of: Who feeds … however, the zimmun blessing is derived … “Praise God with me … For the land, that is the blessing of the land. Good, that is … Who builds Jerusalem, and it also says: This good mountain and Lebanon. They instituted … Who is good and does good, at Yavne … I only have … after … From where … before … The verse states: That he gave you. … from … gave it to you,

Rabbi Yitzḥak says: … is not necessary, as it says: “And He will bless your bread and your water” … do not read: And He will bless [uveirakh], rather: And you will bless [uvareikh]. And when is it called bread? Before it is eaten.

Rabbi Natan says: … is not necessary, as it says … “As soon you come into the city, find him right away, before he goes up to the high place to eat; for the people will not eat until he comes, because he will bless the sacrifice; and afterwards all those who are invited will eat;

Why … so expansively … It is because women are chatterers. And Shmuel said … in order to gaze upon Saul’s beauty … as it is written … he was taller than the people from the shoulders up” … Rabbi Yoḥanan said … one sovereignty does not overlap with its counterpart, even … hairbreadth.

I only have … Grace after Meals. From where … the blessing of the Torah … Rabbi Yishmael said: … an a fortiori inference … Over … temporal life, one recites a blessing, all the more so … eternal life. Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Naḥmani, … student of Rabbi Yishmael, says in the name of Rabbi Yishmael: This … is not necessary, … as it states: “For the good land that He gave [natan] you,” and below, … it says: “And I will give [ve’etna] you the stone tablets, and the Torah and the mitzva,

Rabbi Meir says: From where … just as one recites a blessing over the good … he recites a blessing over the bad? The verse states: “That the Lord, your God gave you.” … your Judge, in whatever judgment that He judges you, whether it is a positive measure of goodness or a measure of calamity.

Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: … is not necessary, as it says: … Tova, that is Torah, as it says: “For I have given you good [tov] teachings, … hatova, that is the building of Jerusalem, as it says: “This good mountain [hatov] and Lebanon.”

It was taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: Anyone who did not say: A desirable, good, and spacious land in the blessing of the land, and … the royal house of David in … Who builds Jerusalem, did not fulfill his obligation. Naḥum the Elder says: One must mention the covenant … in … Rabbi Yosei says: One must mention the Torah in … Pelimu, … says: He must … covenant … preceding … Torah, as this, … was given … with three covenants,
and that, … was given with thirteen covenants,

Rabbi Abba says: One must mention thanks … at the beginning and the end … And one who decreases … may not decrease … to fewer than one, and … anyone decreases … to fewer than one, it is reprehensible.

Anyone who concludes the blessing of the land: Who bequeaths lands and … the blessing: Who builds Jerusalem, … Who redeems Israel, is an ignoramus, … And anyone who does not mention covenant and Torah in the blessing of the land and the royal house of David in … Who builds Jerusalem, did not fulfill his obligation.

This … supports … Rabbi Il’a, as Rabbi Il’a said … Rabbi Ya’akov bar Aḥa said in the name of Rabbeinu, … Anyone who did not mention covenant and Torah in the blessing of the land and the royal house of David in … Who builds Jerusalem, did not fulfill his obligation.

Abba Yosei ben Dostai and the Rabbis disagreed … One said: Who is good and does good, requires … sovereignty, and one said: It does not require … sovereignty. … The one who said that it requires … sovereignty holds that … by the Sages, … The one who said that it does not require … sovereignty holds that … is by Torah law.

what … does he conclude … the building of Jerusalem? Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says: … Who redeems Israel. … Who redeems Israel, yes, … The building of Jerusalem, no, … Rather, say … or even … Who redeems Israel.

Rabba bar Rav Huna happened … to the house of the Exilarch. … he opened with one … and concluded with two … Rav Ḥisda said … great fortitude to conclude with two … Wasn’t it taught … Rabbi … says: One may not conclude with two

the matter itself: Rabbi … says: One may not conclude with two … Levi, … raised an objection to … Rabbi … For the land and for the food. … The land that produces food. … For the land and for the fruit. … The land that produces fruit.
Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons. … Who sanctifies Israel, who sanctify the seasons. Who sanctifies Israel and the New Moon. … Who sanctifies Israel, who sanctify the New Moons.
Who sanctifies Shabbat, Israel, and the seasons. … Except for that
What is different … Here, … for one … there, … two … each one is distinct
And what is the reason that one does not conclude … with two … Because … One does not perform mitzvot in bundles;
What … about it?

Rav Sheshet said: … he opened with: Have compassion on Your people, Israel, … he concludes with: Who redeems Israel; … he opened with: Have compassion on Jerusalem, he concludes with: Who builds Jerusalem. Rav Naḥman said: Even if he opened with: Have compassion on Israel, he concludes with: Who builds Jerusalem, because it is stated: “The Lord builds Jerusalem; He gathers in the exiles of Israel” … When does God build Jerusalem? When He gathers in the exiles of Israel.

Rabbi Zeira said to Rav Ḥisda: Let the Master come and teach … He responded: I have not … learned Grace after Meals, and I will teach Mishna? He responded: What is this? … He said to him: I happened … to the house of the Exilarch and recited Grace after Meals, and Rav Sheshet stiffened his neck over me like a snake, … And why … I did not mention covenant, Torah, or sovereignty … And why did you not mention … in accordance with … Rav Ḥananel … Rav said, as Rav Ḥananel said … Rav said: If one does not mention covenant, Torah or sovereignty … he … fulfilled … Covenant does not apply to women; Torah and sovereignty apply neither to women nor to slaves. … And you abandoned all of these tanna’im and amora’im … and followed Rav?

Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … Who is good and does good, requires … sovereignty. … What is he teaching us … any blessing that does not contain mention of … sovereignty is not … blessing, didn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan already say that … once? Rabbi Zeira said: … is saying that … requires two … sovereignty, one for itself and one for … Who builds Jerusalem.

If so, … it should require three … one of its own, one for … Who builds Jerusalem, and one for the blessing of the land, … Rather, … the blessing of the land, what is the reason … not … Because it is a blessing juxtaposed to another … Who builds Jerusalem, should also not require … as it is a blessing juxtaposed to another

The same is true even … Who builds Jerusalem, … does not require … since he mentioned the royal house of David … it would not be proper … he did not mention God’s sovereignty … Rav Pappa said: … requires two … sovereignty besides its own;

Rabbi Zeira sat behind Rav Giddel … and Rav Giddel sat before Rav Huna, and he sat and he said: One who erred and did not mention … for Shabbat … says … Blessed…Who gave Shabbatot for rest to His people Israel with love, as a sign and a covenant; Blessed…Who sanctifies the Shabbat. … said to him: Who said … Rav.

Again … sat and said: One who erred and did not mention … for Festivals … says: “Blessed…Who gave Festivals to His people Israel for joy and for commemoration; Blessed…Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons.” … said to him: Who said … Rav.

Again … sat and said: If one erred and did not mention the New Moon, he says: “Blessed…Who gave the New Moon to His people Israel for commemoration. … I do not know whether he mentioned joy in … or whether he did not mention joy, whether he concluded this … or if he did not conclude it … and whether … is his or whether it is his teacher
Giddel bar Manyumi was standing before Rav Naḥman, Rav Naḥman erred
and he returned to the beginning … said to … Why did the master act in that manner? He said: As Rabbi Sheila said … Rav said: If one erred, he returns to the beginning.

Didn’t Rav Huna say … Rav said: If one erred, he recites: Blessed…Who gave? … said to him: Wasn’t it stated about this … Rabbi Menashya bar Taḥlifa said … Rav said: They only taught that … he did not … begin … Who is good and does good; however, … he … began … Who is good and does good, he must return to the beginning

Rav Idi bar Avin said … Rav Amram said … Rav Naḥman said … Shmuel said: If one erred and did not mention the … New Moon in his … prayer, we require him to return … in Grace after Meals, we do not require him to return

Rav Avin said to Rav Amram … What is the difference between … prayer and Grace after Meals? He said to him: That … was also difficult for me and I asked Rav Naḥman … it, and he said to me: I did not hear … from Mar Shmuel … but let us see … prayer, which is an obligation, we require him to return … Grace after Meals, which … if he wants … he eats and if he wants … he does not eat, we do not require him to return

If so, on Shabbatot and Festivals, … when it is not possible to refrain from eating, … too, if he erred … he must return … He said: Yes. As Rabbi Sheila said … Rav said: If one erred, he returns to the beginning … Didn’t Rav Huna say … Rav said: If one erred, he recites: Blessed…Who gave? … Wasn’t it stated about this: They only taught that … he did not … begin … Who is good and does good; however, … he … began … Who is good and does good, he must return to the beginning
How much … to obligate … in a zimmun?

Is that to say that Rabbi Meir considers an olive-bulk significant and Rabbi Yehuda considers an egg-bulk significant? Didn’t we hear them … the opposite … As we learned … And similarly, one who left Jerusalem and remembered that there was consecrated meat in his hand, … if he passed … Scopus, … he burns … at the site … he … and if … not … he must return to burn it before the Temple with the wood of the arrangement
How much … them to return? Rabbi Meir says: … for an egg-bulk of this, … and that, … And Rabbi Yehuda says: … for an olive-bulk of this and that.

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The opinions are reversed … Abaye said: Actually do not reverse … Here, … they disagree with regard to … verses. Rabbi Meir holds: “And you shall eat,” that is eating; “and be satisfied,” that is drinking … eating … an olive-bulk. And Rabbi Yehuda holds: “And you shall eat and be satisfied,” … eating that includes satisfaction. And what is … an egg-bulk.

there, … they disagree … with regard to logical reasoning. Rabbi Meir holds: … return … is analogous to its ritual impurity, and just as its … ritual impurity is … egg-bulk, so too, … return it is … egg-bulk. And Rabbi Yehuda holds: … return … is analogous to its prohibition, and just as its prohibition is … olive-bulk, so too, … return it is … olive-bulk.
MISHNA: … How does one recite the zimmun? In … three … says: Let us bless … In … three … and him, … says: Bless
In … ten … says: Let us bless our God. In … ten … and him, … says: Bless … both … ten and in … one hundred thousand.

In … one hundred … says: Let us bless the Lord our God. In … one hundred … and him, … says: Bless … In … one thousand … says: Let us bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel. In … one thousand … and him, he says: Bless … In … ten thousand … says: Let us bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs, for the food that we have eaten. In … ten thousand … and him, … says: Bless
just as he recites the blessing, so too … recite in response: Blessed be the Lord our God, the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs, for the food that we have eaten.

Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: According to the size of the crowd, they recite the blessing, as it is stated: “Bless you God in full assemblies, even the Lord, you who are from the fountain of Israel” … Rabbi Akiva said … What do we find in the synagogue? Both … many and … few, … says: Bless [barekhu] the Lord. Rabbi Yishmael said … Bless the Lord the blessed One.
GEMARA: Shmuel said: One should never exclude himself from the collective.
we learned … In … three … and him, … says: Bless
Say
even … Bless; nevertheless: Let us bless, is preferable as Rav Adda bar Ahava said … they said in the school of Rav: We learned: … six to ten … divide

Granted, if you say: Let us bless is preferable, that is why … divide … However, if you say: Bless is preferable, why … divide … Rather, mustn’t one conclude from this: Let us bless is preferable … conclude from this

That was also taught … Both … he said: Bless, and … he said: Let us bless, we do not reprimand him for … so; and the punctilious reprimand him for … so. And … from … one’s blessings it is obvious whether or not he is a Torah scholar. How so? … Rabbi … says: … and by Whose goodness … he is a Torah scholar. … and from Whose goodness … he is an ignoramus,

Abaye said to Rav Dimi: Isn’t it written … And from Your blessing may Your servant’s house be blessed forever” … In … request it is different, … In … request, too, is it not written … “Open your mouth wide, that I will fill it” … That … is written with regard to matters of Torah,

it was taught … Rabbi … says: … And by His goodness we live, he is a Torah scholar. … they live, he is a fool, … of Neharbela taught the opposite. … The halakha is not in accordance with … of Neharbela.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … Let us bless the One Whose food we have eaten, he is a Torah scholar. … to Him from Whose food we have eaten, he is an ignoramus,

Rabbi Aḥa the son of Rava … said to Rav Ashi: Don’t we say … To He Who performed all of these miracles for our ancestors and for us, … said to him: There, … it is self-evident … Who performs miracles? The Holy One, blessed be He.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said … Blessed be the One from Whose food we have eaten, he is a Torah scholar. … For the food we have eaten, he is an ignoramus,

Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua said: We only said … with regard to … three, where there is no … God’s name. In … ten, however, where there is … God’s name, it is self-evident … as we learned … Just as he recites the blessing, so too … recite in response: Blessed be the Lord our God, the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs, for the food that we have eaten.

both … ten and in … one hundred thousand. … The … itself is difficult. … you said: … both … ten and in … one hundred thousand; consequently, … are the same. … it is then taught: In … one hundred … says; in … one thousand … says; in … ten thousand … says.

Rav Yosef said: … not difficult, … This is … Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, and that is … Rabbi Akiva. As we learned … Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: According to the size of the crowd, they recite the blessing, as it is stated: “Bless you God in full assemblies,

Rabbi Akiva said … What do we find in the synagogue? … And Rabbi Akiva, what does he do with that verse … Rabbi Yosei HaGelili? … He needs it to … that which was taught … Rabbi Meir says: From where … that even fetuses in their mother’s womb recited … song at the … Sea? As it is stated … “In assemblies, bless God, the Lord, from the source of Israel,” … And … the other … He derives … from … the source

Rava said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Akiva. … Ravina and Rav Ḥama bar Buzi happened … to … the house of the Exilarch. … Rav Ḥama rose and was seeking … one hundred … Ravina said to him: You need not … Rava declared the following: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Akiva

Rava said: When we would eat bread at the house of the Exilarch, we would recite the … blessing in groups of three. … Let them recite the blessing in groups of ten. … the Exilarch would hear and become angry … Why could they not satisfy their obligation with the Exilarch’s blessing? … Since everyone is making noise, they do not hear

Rabba Tosefa’a said: These three … who break bread together and one of them went ahead and recited … on his own … they, … fulfill … with his … zimmun; he, … does not fulfill … with … their zimmun because there is no retroactive zimmun,

Rabbi Yishmael said … Bless the Lord the blessed One. Rafram bar Pappa happened … to the synagogue of Abei Givar when he rose to read from the … scroll and recited: Bless the Lord, and was silent, and did not recite: The blessed One. … everyone … cried out: Bless the Lord the blessed One. Rava said … You black pot, … why are you … in this … dispute? … Furthermore, standard practice is in accordance with … Rabbi Yishmael.
MISHNA: Three … who ate as one are not permitted to divide … And the same … four … and the same … five. … six, up to … ten … may divide … And … ten may not divide … until there are twenty
Two groups that were eating in one house, when some … can see each other, they may combine to … zimmun. And if not, these recite a zimmun for themselves and those recite a zimmun for themselves.
One does not recite a blessing over wine until he adds water to it, … the statement of Rabbi Eliezer. … And the Rabbis say: … recites a blessing over it.
GEMARA: … What does this … teach us? We … learned this once: Three … who ate as one are required to form a zimmun.
This teaches us that … which Rabbi Abba said … Shmuel said: Three … who sat to eat as one, and they have not yet begun to eat, … they are not permitted to divide

another version: Rabbi Abba said … Shmuel said … this is what … teaches: Three … who sat to eat as one, even though … each and every one … eats from his own loaf, they … are not permitted to divide. Alternatively, … that … of Rav Huna, as Rav Huna said: Three … who came from three … groups … are not permitted to divide.
Rav Ḥisda said: And that … came from three groups of three people
Rava … said:
We only said … where those … did not include them in the zimmun in their … place, but in a case where they included them in the zimmun in their … place, their … zimmun has left them.

Rava said: From where do I … say this … As we learned … A … bed, half of which was stolen or half of which was lost, or it was divided by brothers … partners, it is ritually pure. … if they restored it … it is susceptible to ritual impurity from here on.
From here on, yes, … retroactively, no, … Apparently, once they divided it, the ritual impurity left it. … Here, too, once they included them in the zimmun, their … left them
two groups … It was taught: If there is a … waiter among them, … the waiter joins them

One does not recite a blessing over wine … the Sages taught … Over wine, until he added water to it, one does not recite: Who creates fruit of the vine; rather, … Who creates fruit of the tree, … one … washes his hands with it. Once he added water to it, … one recites over it: Who creates fruit of the vine, and one does not … wash his hands with it, … the statement of Rabbi Eliezer. The Rabbis say: In either case, … one recites over it: Who creates fruit of the vine, and one may not … wash his hands from it.
In accordance with whose … is that … which Shmuel said: A person may perform all his needs with bread? … In accordance with whose … in accordance with … Rabbi Eliezer,

Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Ḥanina said: The Rabbis agree with Rabbi Eliezer with regard to a cup of blessing, … that one does not recite a blessing over it until he adds water to it. What is the reason? Rav Oshaya said: We require … a mitzva be … in the best
And according to the Rabbis, for what is … fit? Rabbi Zeira said: … for koraiytei,

The Sages taught: Four things were said with regard to bread: One may not place raw meat on bread … and one may not pass a full cup … over bread … and one may not throw bread; and one may not prop up a dish with … bread.

Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi ate bread together when they brought dates and pomegranates before them. Mar Zutra took … and threw a portion before Rav Ashi. … said to him: … the Master not hold with that which was taught … One may not throw food? … That was taught with regard to bread, … Wasn’t it taught … Just as one may not throw bread, so too one may not throw … foods? … said to him: Wasn’t … taught … Although one may not throw bread, he may throw … foods?
Rather, … not difficult, … This … a … item that becomes disgusting … that … a … item that does not become disgusting

the Sages taught: One may draw wine through pipes before a bride and groom … throw roasted grain and nuts before them in the summer, but not in the rainy season, … But one may not throw cakes, neither in the summer nor in the rainy season.
Rav Yehuda said: If one forgot and put food … in his mouth without … a blessing, he moves them to one side … and recites the blessing.
It was taught … one … He swallows them. It was taught … another … He spits them out. Another … taught: He moves them

not difficult, … This … in which it was taught: He swallows them … to liquids, … This … in which it was taught: He spits them out, … a … item that does not become disgusting … This … in which it was taught: He moves them … a … item that becomes disgusting,

It cannot enter your mind … As it was taught here in the mishna, … Beit Shammai say: … candle, … Meals … spices, … havdala. And Beit Hillel say: … candle, spices, … Meals, and havdala. And do Beit Shammai hold … Grace after Meals requires a cup … Didn’t we learn … Wine came before … after the meal; if only that cup … is there, Beit Shammai say: One recites a blessing over the wine and recites a blessing over the food, … thereafter. Wasn’t it taught … If he has only one cup … there are not two … but … more than one.

Beit Shammai say:

let it render the liquids that are within … ritually impure? … Here we are dealing with a vessel … the outside of which has been rendered ritually impure by liquids … the inside … is pure and the outside is impure. Beit Shammai say: One sweeps the … house … and he washes his hands … thereafter. And Beit Hillel say: One washes his hands and sweeps the house thereafter.

With regard to what do they disagree? … Beit Hillel hold: One is forbidden to use … a waiter … am ha’aretz. … And Beit Shammai hold: One is permitted to use … an attendant … am ha’aretz.

the Sages taught: One who was walking outside the city … and saw a child with a torch in his hand, he … check after his … If … is a Jew, he may recite a blessing … but if … is a gentile, he may not recite a blessing

“The baker saw … from where did … know … Rabbi Elazar said: … teaches that each … was shown his dream and the interpretation of the other’s dream.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who awakened … and a … verse happens into his mouth, it is a minor prophecy

Rabbi Yoḥanan also said: Three dreams are fulfilled: A dream of the morning, a dream that one’s fellow dreamed about him, and a dream that is interpreted within a dream. And some say that a dream that is repeated … as it is stated: “And for that the dream was doubled

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yonatan said: A person is shown … only the thoughts of his heart … as it is stated: “As for you, O king, your thoughts came upon your bed, … And if you wish, say … from here, … “And that you may know the thoughts of your … Rava said: Know … for one is neither shown a golden palm tree nor an elephant … the eye of a needle

emperor said to Rabbi Yehoshua, son of Rabbi Ḥananya: You … say that you are extremely wise. … tell me what I will see in my dream. … said to him: You will see the Persians capture you, and enslave you, and force you to herd unclean animals with a golden staff. He thought the entire day … and that night he saw … King Shapur … said to Shmuel: You … say that you are extremely wise. … tell me what I will see in my dream. Shmuel said to him: You will see the Romans come and take you into captivity … to grind date pits in mills of gold. He thought the entire day … and that night he saw

Bar Haddaya was an interpreter of dreams. … one who gave him a fee, he would interpret … favorably, and … one who did not give him a fee, he would interpret … unfavorably. … Abaye and Rava saw an … dream … Abaye gave him money … while Rava did not give him … They said to him: … “Your ox shall be slain before your eyes … was read to us in our dream. He … to Rava he said: Your business will be lost and you will derive no pleasure from eating because of the … sadness of your heart. To Abaye he said: Your business will profit and you will be unable to eat due to the joy in your heart.

They said to him: … “You shall beget sons and daughters, but they shall not be yours; for they shall go into captivity” … was read to us … to Rava he said its … adverse … To Abaye he said: Your sons and daughters will be numerous, and your daughters will be married to outsiders and it will seem to you as if they were taken in captivity.

The verse: “Your sons and your daughters shall be given unto another people” … was read to us … To Abaye he said: Your sons and daughters will be numerous. You say, … your relatives and … says … her relatives and she will impose … upon you and they will be given … to her relatives, which is like another nation … To Rava he said: Your wife will die and your sons and daughters will come into the hands of another woman. As Rava said … Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said … Rav said: What is … that which is written … “Your sons and your daughters shall be given unto another people”? This … the father’s wife,

“Go your way, eat your bread with joy, … was read to us in our dream. To Abaye he said: Your business will profit and you will eat and drink and read the verse out of the joy of your heart. To Rava he said: Your business will be lost, you will slaughter but not eat, you will drink … read … to allay your fears.
“You shall carry much seed out into the field, … was read to us … To Abaye he said from the beginning … To Rava he said from the end
“You shall have olive trees throughout all your borders, … was read to us … to Abaye he said from the beginning … To Rava he said from the end

“All the peoples of the earth shall see … was read to us … To Abaye he said: Your name will become well-known as head of the yeshiva, and you will be feared by all. To Rava he said: The king’s treasury was broken … and you will be apprehended as a thief, and everyone will draw an a fortiori inference from you: … the next day, the king’s treasury was burglarized, and they came and apprehended Rava.
said to him: We saw lettuce on the mouth of the barrels. To Abaye he said: Your business will double like lettuce … To Rava he said: Your work will be bitter like … lettuce

They said to him: We saw meat on the mouth of barrels. To Abaye he said: Your wine will be sweet and everyone will come to buy meat and wine from you. To Rava he said: Your wine will spoil, and everyone will go to buy meat in order to eat with it,
They said to him: We saw a barrel hanging from a palm tree. To Abaye he said: Your business will rise like a palm tree. To Rava he said: Your work will be sweet like dates

They said to him: We saw a pomegranate taking root on the mouth of barrels. To Abaye he said: Your business will increase in value like a pomegranate. To Rava he said: Your work will go sour like a pomegranate.

They said to him: We saw a barrel fall into a pit. To Abaye he said: Your merchandise will be in demand as … says: Bread falls in a pit and is not found. … To Rava he said: Your merchandise will be ruined and you will throw it … into a pit.

They said to him: We saw a donkey foal standing near our heads, braying. To Abaye he said: You will be a king, … head of the yeshiva, and an interpreter will stand near you … To Rava he said: … peter ḥamor, first-born donkey, erased from your phylacteries. … said to him: I myself saw it and it is there. … said to him: … vav of … peter ḥamor is certainly erased from your phylacteries.

Ultimately, Rava went to … alone. … said to him: I saw the outer door … fall. … said to him: Your wife will die, … said to him: I saw my front and back teeth fall out. He said to him: Your sons and daughters will die. … said to him: I saw two doves that were flying. He said to him: You will divorce two women. … said to him: I saw two turnip heads [gargelidei]. He said to him: You will receive two blows with a club … That same day Rava went and sat in the study hall the entire day. He discovered these two blind people who were fighting with each other. Rava went to separate them and they struck Rava two … they raised … to strike him an additional blow, he said: … enough for me, I … saw two.

Ultimately, Rava came and gave him, … a fee. And … said to him: I saw my … fall. … said to him: You will acquire property without limits. … said to him: I saw Abaye’s house [appadna] fall and its dust covered me. … said to him: Abaye will die and his yeshiva will come to you. … said to him: I saw my house fall, and everyone came and took the bricks. He said to him: Your teachings will be disseminated throughout the world. … said to him: I saw that my head split and my brain fell out. He said to him: A feather will fall out of the pillow … said to him: The Egyptian hallel, … was read to me in a dream. He said to him: Miracles will be performed for you.

was going with … on a ship; … said: Why am I … with a person for whom miracles will be performed, … As … was climbing … a book fell from him. Rava found … and saw: All dreams follow the mouth, written therein. He said … Scoundrel. It was … on you, and you caused me so much suffering. I forgive you for everything except for the daughter … Rav Ḥisda, … May it be … will that this man be delivered into the hands of a kingdom that has no compassion on him.

said … What will I do? We learned … that the curse of a Sage, … baseless, comes … And all the more so … Rava, as he cursed … justifiably. He said … I will get up and go into exile, … the Master said: Exile atones for transgression.

He arose and exiled himself to the seat of the Roman … He went and sat by the entrance, … the keeper of the king’s wardrobe … The wardrobe guard dreamed a dream. … said to … I saw in the dream that a needle pierced my finger. … said to him: Give me a zuz. He did not give him … so … said nothing to him. … said to him: I saw a worm that fell … my two fingers, … said to him: Give me a zuz. He did not give him … so … said nothing to him. … said to him: I saw that a worm fell … entire hand, … said to him: A worm fell … all the silk … They heard … in the king’s palace and they brought the wardrobe keeper and were … executing him. He said to them: Why me? Bring the one who knew and did not say … They brought … and said to him: Because of your zuz, ruin

the king’s silk … They tied two cedar … with a rope, and tied one of his legs to one cedar and one of his legs to … cedar, and they released the rope until his head split open. Each … went … and stood in its place and … split and fell … in two.
Ben Dama, son of Rabbi Yishmael’s sister, asked … Rabbi Yishmael: I saw … my two cheeks fell off. … said to him: Two Roman battalions spoke ill of you, and they died.

Bar Kappara said to Rabbi … I saw … my nose fell off. … He said to him: … anger [ḥaron af] … has been removed from you. … said to him: I saw … my two hands were cut off. … said to him: … you will not require the labor of your hands, … said to him: I saw my two legs were cut off. … said: You are riding a horse. … I saw that … to me … in … Adar I will die … I will not see Nisan. He said to him: You will die in glory [adruta] and you will not be brought to temptation [nissayon].

A certain heretic said to Rabbi Yishmael: I saw … that I was irrigating olives with … oil. … He said to him: … you had relations with your mother, … said to Rabbi Yishmael: I saw that I was plucking a star. He said to him: You kidnapped an Israelite man, … said to him: I saw that I swallowed a star. He said to him: You sold the Israelite man … and spent the money … said to him: I saw my eyes kissing one another. He said to him: You had relations with your sister, … said to him: I saw myself kissing the moon. He said to him: You slept with an Israelite woman, … He said to him: I saw that I was treading in the shade of a myrtle tree. He said to him: You slept with a betrothed young woman, … He said to him: I saw that the shade was above me, and … was below me. He said to him: Your bed is upside-down, … He said to him: I saw ravens circling my bed. He said to him: Your wife committed adultery with many men. He said to him: I saw doves circling around my bed. He said to him: You defiled many women. He said to him: I saw that I was holding two doves and … were flying. He said to him: You married two women and dismissed them … without a divorce.

He said to him: I saw myself peeling eggs. He said to him: You stripped dead people, … said to him: Everything … is true, with the exception of this one, … which is not true. Meanwhile, this woman came and said to him: This cloak that you are wearing … to such-and-such a man, who died and whom you stripped

He said to … I saw that they said to me … Your father left you property in Cappadocia. … said to him: Do you have property in Cappadocia? … said to him: No. Did your father … go to Cappadocia? … said to him: No. … said to him: If so, … Kappa … beam; deka … ten. Go look at the tenth beam … that it is full of coins. He went and found that it was full of coins.

Rabbi Ḥanina said: One who sees a well in a dream sees peace, as it is said: “And Isaac’s servants dug in the valley and found there a well of living water” … Rabbi Natan says: … he has found Torah, … As it is stated … “For whoever finds me finds life” … and it is written here: “A well of living water,” … Rava said: … actual life.

Rabbi Ḥanan said: There are three … peace: A river, a bird and a pot. … A river, as it is written: “I will extend peace to her like a river” … a bird, as it is written: “As birds hovering, so will the Lord of hosts protect Jerusalem” … a pot, as it is written: “Lord, You will establish [tishpot] peace for us” … And Rabbi Ḥanina said: We learned … with regard to a pot that does not have meat in it, … “Yea, they chop them in pieces, as that which is in the pot, and as flesh within the cauldron”

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: … one who sees a river in a dream … rise early … recite: “I will extend peace to her like a river,” before a different verse, … can precede it … “For distress will come in like a river” … One who sees a bird in a dream … rise early and recite: “As birds hovering, so will the Lord of hosts protect Jerusalem,” before a different verse, … can precede it … “As a bird that wanders from her nest, … One who sees a pot in a dream … rise early and recite: “Lord, You will establish peace for us,” before a different verse, … can precede it … “Set on the pot, set it on”

one who sees grapes in a dream … rise early and recite: … like grapes in the wilderness” … before a different verse, … can precede it … “Their grapes are grapes of gall, … One who sees a mountain in a dream … rise early and recite: “How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger … before a different verse, … can precede it … “For the mountains will I take up a weeping and wailing”

One who sees a shofar in a dream … rise early and recite: “And it shall come to pass in that day, that a great shofar shall be sounded; … before a different verse, … can precede it … “Blow you the horn [shofar] in Giva”

One who sees a dog in a dream … rise early and recite: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog whet his tongue” … before a different verse, … can precede it … “Yea, the dogs are greedy” … One who sees a lion in a dream … rise early and recite: “The lion has roared, who will not fear? … before a different verse, … can precede it … “A lion is gone up from his thicket,

One who sees a shave in a dream … rise early and recite: “And he shaved himself, and changed his raiment” … before a different verse, … can precede it … “If I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak” … One who sees a well in a dream … rise early and recite: “A well of living waters” … before a different verse, … can precede it … “As a cistern wells with her waters, … One who sees a reed in a dream … rise early and recite: “A bruised reed shall he not break” … before a different verse, … can precede it … “Now, behold, you trust upon the staff of this bruised reed”

The Sages teach: One who sees a reed [kaneh] in a dream should expect wisdom, as it is stated: “Get [kene] wisdom” … reeds [kanim] should expect understanding, as it said: “Yea, with all your acquisitions [kinyanekha] acquire understanding” … Rabbi Zeira said: Pumpkin [kara], heart of palm [kura], wax [kira], and reed [kanya], are all advantageous when one dreams … It was taught … A pumpkin is only shown … to one who fears Heaven with all his might, … [delu’im]
One who sees an ox in a dream, … rise early and recite: “His firstling bullock, majesty is his” … before a different verse, … can precede it … “And if an ox gore a man”

The Sages taught … Five matters are said … the ox. … he ate from its flesh will become wealthy. … gored him will have sons … who gore … in … Torah. … it bit him, suffering is coming to him. … it kicked him will be required to travel a great distance in the future. … he was riding it, … rise to greatness.
Wasn’t it taught … he was riding it, … die? … not difficult. This, … that he was riding the ox, while this, … that the ox was riding him.

One who sees a donkey in a dream should anticipate salvation, as it is said: “Behold, your king comes unto you; he is triumphant, and victorious, lowly, and riding upon a donkey” … One who sees a cat in a dream in a place where … they call it shunra, a nice song [shira na’a] will be composed for him. … shinra, it is a sign that he will undergo a change for the worse [shinui ra]. One who sees grapes in a dream … white … whether … in their season or not in their season, it is a good … black … in their season, it is a good … not in their season, it is a bad … One who sees a white horse in a dream, … whether … walking or running, it is a good … for him. … red … walking, it is a good … running, it is a bad

One who sees Ishmael in a dream, … his prayer … heard, … specifically … Ishmael, son of Abraham, … not … a random Arab. One who sees a camel [gamal] in a dream, … death was decreed upon him from heaven but he was spared. Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: What verse … “I will go down with you into Egypt; and I will also surely bring you up again [gam alo]” ( … ), … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: … from here, … “The Lord also [gam] has put away your sin; you shall not die”

One who sees Pinehas in a dream, … that a miracle will be performed on his behalf, … One who sees an elephant [pil] in a dream … miracles [pelaot] will be performed for him. … elephants … miracles upon miracles will be performed for him.
Was it not taught … All species of animals are good … in a dream, with the exception of an elephant and a monkey? … not difficult.

This … it saddled, while this … is not saddled. One who sees … Huna in a dream, … a miracle will be performed for him, … Ḥanina, Ḥananya, or Yoḥanan, … many miracles will be performed for him, … a eulogy in a dream, … the heavens had mercy upon him, and spared him … this only applies … written

One who answers … May His great name be blessed … is assured that he is one … the World-to-Come. One … reciting Shema … is worthy of having the Divine Presence rest upon him, but his generation is unworthy,

One who … don phylacteries in a dream should anticipate greatness, as it is stated: “And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you; … And it was taught … Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: That the Name of the Lord is called upon you, refers to phylacteries of the head, … One who … pray in a dream, … an auspicious omen. … This only applies … had not … finished

One who … he had relations with his mother [em] in a dream, he should anticipate … understanding, as it is stated: “Yea if [im] you call for understanding” … One who … had relations with a betrothed young woman … he should anticipate Torah, as it is stated: “Moses commanded us Torah, an inheritance [morasha] of the congregation of Jacob” … Do not read … morasha; rather, … me’orasa, betrothed. One who … had relations with his sister in a dream, should anticipate wisdom, as it is stated: “Say unto wisdom: You are my sister” … One who … he had relations with a married woman in a dream is assured that he is one … the World-to-Come. … This only applies … he did not know her and was not thinking about her that evening;

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said: One who sees wheat in a dream has seen peace, as it is stated: “He makes your borders peace; He gives you in plenty the fat of wheat” … one who sees barley [se’orim] in a dream … his iniquities are taken away, as it is stated: “And your iniquity is taken away [vesar avonekh], and your sin expiated” … Rabbi Zeira said: I did not ascend from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael until I saw barley in my dream.

One who sees a vine laden … in a dream, … his wife will not miscarry, as it is stated: “Your wife shall be as a fruitful vine, … a … vine branch … should anticipate the Messiah, as it is stated: “Binding his foal unto the vine and his donkey’s colt unto the vine branch”
