One who sees a fig tree in a dream, … his Torah is preserved within him, as it is stated: “One who keeps the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof” … One who sees pomegranates in a dream, … small, his business will flourish like the seeds of … pomegranate, … large, his business will increase like a pomegranate. … slices of pomegranates … if he is a Torah scholar, he should anticipate Torah, as it is stated: “I would cause you to drink of spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate” … And if … is an ignoramus, he should anticipate mitzvot, … “Your temples are like a split pomegranate” … What is … “Your temples [rakatekh]”? Even the most ignorant [reikanin] among you, … are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate.

One who sees olives in a dream, … small, … his business will flourish, increase and be durable like olives. … this applies only … fruit … but, … trees, … he will have many children, as it is stated: “Your children like olive plants, … Some say that one who sees an olive tree in a dream, … a good reputation will spread for him, as it is stated: … a leafy olive tree, fair with goodly fruit” … One who sees olive oil in a dream should anticipate the light of Torah, as it is stated: “That they bring unto you pure olive oil … One who sees palm trees [temarim] in a dream … his transgressions have ceased, as it is stated: “Your iniquity is finished, O daughter of Zion”

Rav Yosef says: One who sees a goat in a dream, … his year will be blessed; … goats, his years will be blessed, as it is stated: “And there will be goats’ milk enough for your food, … One who sees myrtle in a dream, … his property will be successful. And if he does not … property, … he will receive an inheritance. Ulla said, and some say it was taught in a baraita: This … where he saw … on their stem. One who sees a citron [etrog] in a dream … he is honored [hadur] before his Creator, as it is stated … “The fruit of goodly trees [hadar], branches of palm trees” … One who sees a palm branch [lulav] in a dream, … he has but one heart for his Father in heaven.

One who sees a goose in a dream should anticipate wisdom, as it is stated: “Wisdoms cry aloud in the streets, … he has relations with … will become head of the yeshiva. Rav Ashi said: I saw … had relations with it … and I ascended to greatness

One who sees a rooster in a dream … a male child. … roosters should expect male children. … a hen [tarnegolet] should anticipate a beautiful garden and … rejoice [tarbitza na’a vegila], … One who sees eggs in a dream, … his request is pending, … broke, … his request … granted, … The same is true of nuts, and the same is true of cucumbers, and the same is true of all glass vessels, and the same is true of anything similarly fragile

One … he entered a city, … his desires will be fulfilled, as it is stated: “And He led them unto their desired haven” … One who shaves his head in a dream, it is a good omen for him, … shaved his head and his beard … for him and his entire family.
One who sits in a small boat … a good reputation will spread for him. … in a large boat … a good reputation will spread for him and his entire family. … this only applies … the boat was floating high
One who defecates … it is a good omen for him, as it is stated: “He that is bent down shall speedily be loosed; … this only applies … he does not wipe

One who climbs up to the roof in a dream, … he will ascend to greatness. … he climbed … down, … will descend from … greatness he … Abaye and Rava both said: Once one ascended … he ascended, … One who rips his clothing in a dream, … rip up his sentence. One who stands naked in Babylonia in a dream, … he stands free of transgression. … in Eretz Yisrael, … naked without mitzvot. One … he was apprehended … by a soldier [sardeyot], … protection was provided him … he is wearing a neck chain [kolar], … they have increased his level of protection. … this only applies … in a neck chain; if … simply … a noose, it does not
One who enters a marsh in a dream, … he will become head of a yeshiva, … a forest … will be made head of … the advanced students [kalla],

Rav Pappa and Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, … saw a dream: Rav Pappa, … that he entered a marsh … was appointed head of a yeshiva. Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, … that he entered a forest … was appointed head of the advanced students. Some say that both of them … they entered a marsh, … Rav Pappa, … that a drum hung … was appointed head of the yeshiva, … Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, … did not … that a drum hung around … was … appointed head of the advanced students. Rav Ashi said: I … I entered a marsh and hung a drum and beat it,
tanna … before Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak taught: One who lets blood in a dream, … his transgressions have been forgiven,
Was it not taught … his transgressions are enumerated before him? … What … enumerated? … enumerated to be forgiven.

tanna … before Rav Sheshet taught: One who sees a snake in a dream, … his livelihood is accessible to him … bit him … will double. … he killed … he will lose his livelihood. Rav Sheshet said to … all the more so his livelihood will double. … But that is not so. Rav Sheshet saw a snake in his dream and killed it,

tanna … before Rabbi Yoḥanan taught: One who sees any kind of drink in a dream it is … good … except for wine, … there is … who drinks it … and it is … good … for him, and there is … who drinks it … and it is … bad … for him. … There is … who drinks … and it is … good … for him, as it is stated: “And wine that makes glad the heart of man” … and there is … who drinks it … and it is … bad … for him, as it is stated: “Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish and wine unto the bitter in soul”
Rabbi Yoḥanan said to the tanna: … teach … a Torah scholar, … always … good … as it is stated: “Come, eat of my bread and drink of the wine which I have mingled”

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who awakened … a verse … falls into his mouth, … a minor prophecy. The Sages taught: There are three kings … One who sees David in a dream should expect piety; … Solomon should expect wisdom; … Ahab should be concerned about calamity.

three books of Prophets … One who sees the book of Kings should anticipate greatness, … Ezekiel should anticipate wisdom, … Isaiah should anticipate consolation; … Jeremiah should be concerned about calamity,
three great … Writings … One who sees the book of Psalms should anticipate piety; … Proverbs should anticipate wisdom; … Job should be concerned about calamity.

There are … three minor … Writings … One who sees Song of Songs in a dream should anticipate piety, … Ecclesiastes should anticipate wisdom; … Lamentations should be concerned about calamity; … one who sees the scroll of Esther, … a miracle will be performed on his behalf.
There are three Sages … One who sees Rabbi … in a dream should anticipate wisdom; … Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya should anticipate wealth, … Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha should be concerned about calamity,
three Torah scholars … One who sees Ben Azzai in a dream should anticipate piety; … Ben Zoma should anticipate wisdom; … Aḥer, … should be concerned about calamity,

All types of animals are auspicious … for a dream except for an elephant, a monkey and a long-tailed ape. … Didn’t the Master say: A miracle will be performed for one who sees an elephant in a dream? … not difficult. This … where it is saddled, … this … where it is not saddled.

All types of metal … are auspicious … for a dream, except for a hoe, a chisel, and an axe, … this applies … when they are seen on their handles. … All kinds of fruit are auspicious … for a dream except for unripe dates. All kinds of vegetables are auspicious … for a dream except for turnip heads. … Didn’t Rav say: I did not become wealthy until I saw turnip heads … When Rav saw … he saw them on their stems; … all kinds of colors are auspicious … for a dream, except for sky-blue [tekhelet]. All kinds of birds are auspicious … except for an eagle-owl, and an owl, and a kurferai,
The body, the body, microcosm, ease, … comfort … mnemonics

Three … enter the body … the body does not benefit from them: Cherries, bad dates, and unripe dates. … Three … do not enter the body … the body benefits from them, and they are: Washing, anointing, and usage [tashmish], … Three … are microcosms of the World-to-Come, and they are: Sabbath, the sun and usage.
Usage of what … If you say … conjugal relations, doesn’t that weaken … Rather, … usage of his orifices,
Three … ease one’s mind, and they are: Voice, sight, and smell, … Three … give a person comfort, and they are: A beautiful abode, a beautiful wife, and beautiful vessels.

five, six, and ten are mnemonics … five … one-sixtieth … They are: Fire, honey, Shabbat, sleep, and a dream. … fire … one-sixtieth of … Gehenna; honey is one-sixtieth of manna; Shabbat is one-sixtieth of the World-to-Come; sleep is one-sixtieth of death; … a dream is one-sixtieth of prophecy.

Six matters are good omens for the sick: Sneezing, sweating, diarrhea, a seminal emission, sleep, and a dream. … Sneezing, as it is written: “His sneezes flash forth light” … Sweat, as it is written: “In the sweat of your face shall you eat bread” … Diarrhea, as it is written: “He that is bent down shall speedily be loosed; and he shall not go down dying into the pit” … A seminal emission, as it is written: “That he might see his seed, prolong his days” … Sleep, as it is written: “I should have slept; then had I been at rest” … A dream, as it is written: “Wherefore You recover me [vataḥalimeni], and make me to live”

Six matters cure a sick person from his illness, and their cure is … cure. They are: Cabbage, beets, dried foley, … the stomach, the placenta, and the diaphragm … Some say … small fish … Furthermore, small fish cause one’s entire body to flourish and become healthy.

there are ten matters that … relapse of his illness, and his illness is … severe, and they are: … ox meat, … fatty meat … roasted meat, … poultry, … a roasted egg, shaving, … cress, … milk, … cheese, and … bathhouse. And some say … nuts, and some say even … cucumbers.

taught … school of Rabbi Yishmael: Why are they called cucumbers [kishu’im]? Because they are as harmful [kashim] to the body as swords. … Is that really so? Is it not written: “And the Lord said unto her: Two nations [goyim] are in your womb” … Do not read … goyim, rather … gayim, proud ones. And Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: … these … Antoninus and Rabbi … whose tables, … never lacked for radish, lettuce or cucumbers, neither in summer nor in the rainy season.
not difficult. This … to large ones, … this … to small ones.

the Sages taught: … a corpse in his house, … peace in his house. … ate and drank in the house, it is good omen for the house. … removed vessels from the house, … is a bad omen for the house, … Rav Pappa explained … with regard to a shoe and a sandal, … Everything … a corpse takes … good … except a shoe and a sandal; everything that a corpse gives … good … except dust and mustard,

a place from which idolatry was eradicated … the Sages taught … One who sees … Mercury [Markulis] recites: Blessed…who has shown patience to those who violate His will, … a place from which idolatry was eradicated should recite: Blessed…Who eradicated idolatry from our land. And just as it was eradicated from this place, so too may it be eradicated from all places of Israel, and restore the hearts of their worshippers to worship You. Outside of Eretz … one need not recite: And restore the hearts of their worshippers to worship You, since it is predominantly populated by gentiles. Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Even outside of Eretz … one is required to recite that … because … will convert, as it is stated: “For then will I turn to the peoples a pure language,

Rav Hamnuna taught: One who sees the wicked Babylonia must recite five blessings. … One who saw … Babylonia, recites: Blessed…Who destroyed the wicked Babylonia.
One who saw … Nebuchadnezzar’s house, recites: Blessed…Who destroyed the house of wicked Nebuchadnezzar.
One who saw the lion’s den … or the furnace … were thrown … recites: Blessed…Who performed miracles for our ancestors in this place.
One who saw Mercury, recites: Blessed…Who has shown patience to those who violate His will.
One who saw a place from which earth is taken, … recites: Blessed…Who speaks and acts, decrees and fulfills.

when Rava would see donkeys carrying earth … he would slap their backs with his hand and say … Run, righteous ones, and fulfill the will of your Master. When Mar, son of Ravina, would arrive in Babylonia he would take earth in his kerchief and throw it outside, to fulfill that which is said: “And I will sweep it with the broom of destruction” … Rav Ashi said: I never heard the … Rav Hamnuna, … However, based on my independent reasoning, I recited all of the blessings.

Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said: … Babylonia was cursed, its neighbors were cursed … Samaria was cursed, its neighbors were blessed. … Babylonia was cursed its neighbors were cursed … as it is written: “I will also make it a possession for the bittern, … and pools of water” … Samaria was cursed, … its neighbors were blessed, as it is written: “Therefore I will make Samaria a heap in the field, a place for the planting of vineyards”
And Rav Hamnuna said: One who sees multitudes of Israel, … recites: Blessed…Who knows all secrets. … multitudes of gentiles recites: “Your mother shall be sore ashamed,

The Sages taught … One who sees multitudes of Israel recites: Blessed…Who knows all secrets. … whose minds are unlike each other and whose faces are unlike each other, … Ben Zoma once saw a multitude [okhlosa] of Israel … on a stair on the Temple Mount. … recited: Blessed…Who knows all secrets and Blessed…Who created all these to serve me.

he would say: How much effort did Adam the first … exert before he found bread to eat: … plowed, sowed, reaped, sheaved, threshed, winnowed … separated … ground … sifted, kneaded, and baked and … thereafter he ate. And I, … wake up and find all of these prepared for me. … how much effort did Adam the first … exert before he found a garment to wear? … sheared, laundered, combed, spun and wove, and … thereafter he found a garment to wear. And I, … wake up and find all of these prepared for me. … all nations, … diligently come to the entrance of my home, and I wake up and find all of these before me.

would say: A good guest, what does he say? How much effort did the host expend on my behalf, how much meat did … bring before me. How much wine did he bring before me. How many loaves [geluskaot] did he bring before me. All the … that he expended, he expended only for me. However, a bad guest, what does he say? What effort did the host expend? I ate … one … bread, I ate … one piece of meat … I drank … one cup … All the effort that the home owner expended he only expended on behalf of his wife and children.
With regard to a good guest, what does he say? “Remember that you magnify his work, whereof men have sung” … With regard to a bad guest it is written: “Men do therefore fear him;

“And the man in the days of Saul was old, and came among men” … Rava, and some say Rav Zevid, and some say Rav Oshaya, said: This … Yishai, father of David, who … went out with multitudes, and entered with multitudes, and taught Torah with multitudes. Ulla said: We hold there is no multitude in Babylonia. … taught: A multitude is no fewer than six hundred thousand

The Sages taught: One who sees the Sages of Israel recites: Blessed…Who has shared of His wisdom with those who revere Him. … Sages of the nations of the world recites: Blessed…Who has given of His wisdom to flesh and blood. One who sees kings of Israel recites: Blessed…Who has shared of His glory with those who revere Him. … kings of the … nations of the world recites: Blessed…Who has given of His glory to flesh and blood.

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One should always strive to run toward kings of Israel … And not only … toward kings of Israel, but also toward kings of the nations of the world, so that if he will be privileged … he will distinguish between the kings of Israel and the kings of the nations of the world.

Rav Sheshet was blind. Everyone was going to greet the king and Rav Sheshet stood up and went along with them. This heretic found him … said to him: … jugs … to the river, where do the broken … go? … said to him: Come see that I know more than you … The first troop passed, … when the noise grew louder, this heretic said to him: The king is coming. Rav Sheshet said to him: … is not coming. The second troop passed, … when the noise grew louder, this heretic said to him: Now the king is coming. Rav Sheshet said to him: The king is not coming. The third … passed, … when there was silence, Rav Sheshet said to him: Certainly now the king is coming.

When the king came, Rav Sheshet began to bless him. The heretic … said to him: Do you bless someone you do not see? … And what ultimately happened to this heretic? Some say … his friends gouged out his eyes, and some say … Rav Sheshet fixed his gaze upon him, and … became a pile of bones.

Rabbi Sheila … a man who had relations with a gentile woman be flogged. … went to inform the king and said: There is one man among the Jews who renders judgment without the king’s authority [harmana]. … sent a messenger [peristaka] for … When … came, they said to him: Why did you … flogging for this man? He said to them: … he had relations with a female donkey. … they said to him: Do you have witnesses … He replied: Yes, … Elijah the prophet came … appeared as a person and testified. They said to … If so, he is liable for the death penalty; … He replied: Since the day we were exiled from our land we do not have the authority to execute, … you, do with him as you wish.

As … considered the sentence, … “Yours, O Lord, is the greatness, power, … They asked him: What did you say? He told them: This is what I said: Blessed is the Merciful One who grants kingdom on earth … microcosm of the kingdom in heaven, and granted you dominion and love of justice. They said to him: … honor of royalty is so dear to you. They gave him a staff … said to him: Judge.

As he was leaving, that man said to … Does God perform such miracles for liars? He replied: Scoundrel! Aren’t … called donkeys? As it is written: “Whose flesh is as the flesh of donkeys” … saw that he was going to tell … that he called them donkeys. He said: … a pursuer. … And the Torah said: If one comes to kill you, kill him first. He struck him with the staff and killed him.

said: Since a miracle was performed on my behalf with this verse … I will interpret it homiletically: Yours, O Lord, is the greatness; that is the act of creation, and so it says: “Who does great things past finding out” … And the power; that is the exodus from Egypt, as it is stated: “And Israel saw the great work … Egyptians” … And the glory; that is the sun and the moon that stood still for Joshua, as it is stated: “And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, … And the triumph; that is the downfall of Rome, and so it says … “Their lifeblood is dashed against My garments … And the majesty; this is the war of the valleys of Arnon, as it is stated: “Wherefore it is said in the book of the Wars of the Lord: Vahev in Sufa, … For all that is in the heaven and in the earth is Yours; this is the war of Sisera, as it is stated: “They fought from heaven, the stars in their courses … Yours is the kingdom, O Lord; this is the war of Amalek, and so it says: … The hand upon the throne of the Lord: … And you are exalted; this is the war of Gog and Magog, and so it says: “I am against you, O Gog, the chief prince of Meshekh and Tubal” … As head above all; Rav Ḥanan bar Rava said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … even … one responsible for distributing water, is appointed by heaven.

The Sages taught: One who sees the houses of Israel inhabited … recites: Blessed…Who establishes the border of the widow. … in ruins he recites: Blessed…the true Judge. … the houses of the nations of the world inhabited recites: “The Lord will destroy the house of the proud, … And … in ruins he recites: “God of vengeance, Lord, God of vengeance, shine forth”

Ulla and Rav Ḥisda were once walking along the road when they came upon the doorway of the house of Rav Ḥana bar Ḥanilai. Rav Ḥisda groaned and sighed. Ulla asked him: Why are you sighing? Didn’t Rav say: Sighing breaks half of one’s body? As it is stated: “Sigh, therefore, you son of man; with the breaking of your loins” … And Rabbi Yoḥanan said … even … entire body, as it is stated: “And it shall be, when they say unto you: Why are you sighing? That you shall say: Because of the tidings, for it comes; and every heart shall melt,

said to … How can I not sigh? … this house where there were sixty cooks during the day and sixty cooks at night who would cook for anyone in need, and … never removed his hand from his pocket … thought: Perhaps a well-born poor person … come and … until he put his hand in his pocket … would be embarrassed. Moreover, … four doors open in … four directions, and anyone who entered hungry left satiated. And they would scatter wheat and barley outside during years of drought … anyone who was embarrassed to take … during the day could come and take … at night. Now … has fallen in ruins, … I not sigh?

said to … Rabbi Yoḥanan said as follows: From the day that the Temple was destroyed a decree was issued upon the houses of the righteous that they would be destroyed, as it is stated: “In mine ears said the Lord of hosts: Of a truth many houses shall be desolate, even great and fair, without inhabitant” … And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … future, … the Holy One, Blessed be He, will restore them to their … inhabited state, as it is stated: “A Song of Ascents of David. They who trust in the Lord are as Mount Zion, … just as in the future the Holy One, Blessed be He, will restore Mount Zion to its inhabited state, so too, in the future the Holy One, Blessed be He, will restore the houses of the righteous to their inhabited state, … Seeing that he was still not satisfied, … said to him: It is enough for a servant to be like his master.

The Sages taught … One who sees graves of Israel recites: 
Blessed…Who formed you in judgment,
and Who nourished you in judgment,
and Who sustained you in judgment,
and collected … in judgment,
and in the future will raise you … in judgment. … Mar, son of Ravina, concludes … in the name of Rav Naḥman:
And Who knows the number of you all,
and Who in the future will restore you to life and sustain you.
Blessed…Who revives the dead. … graves of gentiles recites: “Your mother shall be sore ashamed,

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: One who sees his friend after thirty days … recites: Blessed…Who has given us life, sustained us and brought us to this time. … after twelve months recites: Blessed…Who revives the dead. … Rav said: A dead person is only forgotten from the heart after twelve months … as it is stated: “I am forgotten as a dead man out of mind; I am like a lost vessel”

Rav Pappa and Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, were once walking along the road when they met Rav Ḥanina the son of Rav Ika. They said to him: When we saw you we recited two blessings over … you: Blessed…Who has shared of His wisdom to those who revere Him, … Who has given us life … He said to them: I too, once I saw you, considered you in my eyes as … six hundred thousand … house of Israel, and I recited three blessings over you. I recited those two … Blessed…Who knows all secrets, … They said to him: Are you all that clever? They fixed their gaze upon him and he died.

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: One who sees spotted people recites: Blessed…Who makes creatures different. … raises a challenge: One who saw a person with … black skin, a person with … red skin, a person with … white skin [lavkan], an … tall and thin person, a dwarf, or one with warts [darnikos] recites: Blessed…Who makes creatures different. … an amputee, a blind person, a flat-headed person, a lame person, one afflicted with boils, or spotted people recites: Blessed…the true Judge,
not difficult. This, … from … in his mother’s womb, … this, … after he was born. … is also precise … it taught … similar to an amputee, … conclude from this.

The Sages taught: One who sees an elephant, a monkey, or a vulture … recites: Blessed…Who makes creatures different. One who saw beautiful … creatures … beautiful trees recites: Blessed…Who has such things in His world.

over zikin, … What are zikin? Shmuel said: A comet. Shmuel also said: The paths of the sky are as clear to me as the paths … Neharde’a, except for comets, that I do not know what they are. And we learn … that a comet does not pass … Orion … and if it does pass Orion, the world will be destroyed. … Don’t we see that … pass … The aura … passes … and it appears as though … passes. Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said … vilon, … rips and furls and the light of … firmament is seen, … Rav Ashi said … a star that is uprooted from one side of Orion, and another … from the other side … sees it and gets startled … and appears as if it is passing.

Shmuel raised a contradiction … it is written: “Who makes Ursa Major, Orion, and Pleiades, … And … it is written: “He Who makes Pleiades and Orion” … So how … Were it not for Orion’s heat, the universe could not exist because of the cold of Pleiades; … were it not for the cold of Pleiades, the universe could not exist because of the heat of Orion.

And we learned … if the tail of … Scorpio … not … in the River of Fire, anyone stung by a scorpion would not survive. And that is what the All-Merciful said to Job … “Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the bands of Orion?”
What is Pleiades [Kima]? … Shmuel said: … approximately a hundred [keme’a] stars … some say that … concentrated and some say that … dispersed.

What is Ursa Major [Ash]? Rav Yehuda said: … Yota. … What is Yota? … some say … tail of Aries, while others say … the head of Taurus. … And it stands to reason in accordance with the … one who said … tail of Aries, as it is written: “Or can you guide Ursa … with her sons?” … apparently it was incomplete and … appears

as if it was appended … And … that … follows … is saying … Give me … my children, … When the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to bring a flood into the world, He took two stars from Pleiades and brought the flood upon the world. And … when He wished to fill … He took two stars from Ursa Major and filled
And return it, … A pit cannot be filled by its own earth; … Alternatively, … a prosecutor cannot become an advocate;

Then … created two other … stars … “There is nothing new under the sun” … Rav Naḥman said: … future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will restore … to … as it is stated: “Or can you guide [tanḥem] Ursa … with her sons?”

And … over zeva’ot … What … zeva’ot? Rav Ketina said: An earthquake. … Rav Ketina was once walking along the road when he came to the entrance of the house of a necromancer and an earthquake rumbled. He said: Does this necromancer know what is this earthquake? … raised his voice … Ketina, Ketina, why would I not know? … when the Holy One, Blessed be He, remembers His children who are suffering among the nations of the world, He sheds two tears into the great sea. The sound … is heard from one end of the earth to the other. And that is an earthquake.

Rav Ketina said: The necromancer is a liar and his statements are lies. If so, it would necessitate an earthquake … earthquake, … That is not so, … causes an earthquake … earthquake; and the fact … did not admit that … so that everyone would not mistakenly follow him.

Rav Ketina also stated his own … claps His hands … as it is stated: “I will also smite My hands together and I will satisfy My fury; … Rabbi Natan says: … sighs … as it is stated: … and I will satisfy My fury upon them, and I will be eased” … And the Rabbis say: … kicks the firmament, … as it is stated: … He cries out like those who tread grapes, against all the inhabitants of the earth” … Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: … forces His feet beneath the throne of glory … as it is stated: “The heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool”

also … over thunder … What … thunder? Shmuel said: … clouds … in the curvature … as it is stated: “The voice of Your thunder was in the whirlwind; the lightning lighted up the world; the earth trembled and shook” … And the Rabbis say: … clouds pouring water into one another, as it is stated: “At the sound of His giving a multitude of waters in the heavens” … Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: … a powerful lightning bolt that flashes in the cloud and shatters the hailstones. Rav Ashi said: … clouds are hollow, and … the wind comes and blows across their mouths, … wind blowing in the mouth of a jug. … And it stands to reason in accordance with … Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov; as lightning flashes, the clouds rumble, and the rain comes.

also … that over wind … What are … winds? Abaye said: … gale force winds. Abaye said: We learned … that there are no gale force winds at night. … Don’t we see that there are … This … begins … during the day. And Abaye said: We learned … that a gale force wind does not last two hours, to fulfill that which is stated: “Trouble shall not rise up a second time” … Don’t we see that it does last … it … stops in between.

also … over lightning one recites: Blessed…Whose strength and power fill the world. … What is … lightning? Rava said: … bright light. And Rava said: A single … lightning, white lightning, green lightning, clouds that rise in the western corner and come from the southern corner, and two clouds that rise with one facing the other are all … trouble.
What practical difference … pray for God’s mercy, … this only applies … at night. In the morning, however, they are insignificant.

Rabbi Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said: Morning clouds … have no substance, as it is written: “For your goodness is as a morning cloud, … Rav Pappa said to Abaye: But … people say … If there is rain when people open their doors … donkey-driver, fold your sack and go to sleep, … not difficult, … this, … covered with thick clouds, … this … covered with flimsy clouds

Rabbi Alexandri said … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Thunder was created only … straighten the crookedness of the heart, as it is stated: “And God has so made it, that men should fear before Him” … And Rabbi Alexandri said … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: One who sees a rainbow in a cloud must fall upon his face, as it is stated: “As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud … And when I saw it, I fell upon my face” … in the West, … they would curse … because it appears as one who is bowing to the rainbow. … blessing … however, … one certainly recites a blessing. What … does one recite? Blessed…Who remembers the covenant … It was taught in a baraita … Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says … Who is faithful to His covenant and fulfills His word. Rav Pappa said: Therefore we will say them both … Blessed…Who remembers the covenant and is faithful to His covenant and fulfills His word.

over mountains and hills … Is that to say that all those that we mentioned until now, … are not acts of creation? … is it not … written: “He makes lightning for the rain” … Abaye said: Combine … teach that … Rava said: There, … one recites two … Blessed…Whose power fills the world, and: Author of creation. Here, … one … Author of creation, … need not … Whose power fills the world.

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: One who sees the firmament in its purity recites: Blessed…Author of creation. … When … Abaye said: When rain … all night and in the morning a northern wind blows, exposing the heavens.

And … disagree with Rafram bar Pappa … Rav Ḥisda said, as Rafram bar Pappa said … Rav Ḥisda said: Since the day the Temple was destroyed the firmament has not been seen in its purity, as it is said: “I clothe the heavens with blackness and I make sackcloth their covering”

The Sages taught: One who sees the sun in … its cycle, the moon in its might, the planets in their orbit, or the signs of the zodiac … in their order recites: Blessed…Author of creation. … And when is it … Abaye said: Every twenty-eight years … cycle … returns … and the Nisan, … equinox, … falls within … Saturn on the night of the third and eve of the fourth
Rabbi Yehuda said: One who sees the great sea … recites: … How much … intermittently? Rami bar Abba said … Rav Yitzḥak said: Thirty days.

And Rami bar Abba said … Rav Yitzḥak said: One who sees the Euphrates River near the bridge of Babylonia recites: Blessed…Author of creation. … And now that the Persians have rerouted … from Beit Shavor upriver. … Rav Yosef said: … from Ihi Dekira upriver. And Rami bar Abba said: One who sees the Tigris on the bridge of Shabistana recites: Blessed…Author of creation.
What is … Ḥidekel [ … Rav Ashi said: … its waters are sharp [ḥadin] and light [kalin] … What is … Perat … because its waters are fruitful [parin] and multiply [ravin];

Rava said: The inhabitants … Meḥoza are sharp because they drink the water of the Tigris; they are red because they engage in … relations in the daytime; and their eyes move … because they live in dark houses.

over rain … And over rain … one … recite the blessing: Who is good and does good? Didn’t Rabbi Abbahu say, and some say it was taught in a baraita: From when does one recite the blessing on rain? From when the groom went out to meet the bride.

What blessing does one recite? Rav Yehuda said: … We thank You for each and every drop that You have made fall for us. And Rav Yoḥanan concludes … as follows: If our mouths were as full of song as the sea…we could not sufficiently praise You O Lord our God, … until: Shall bow … Blessed are You, O Lord, … abundant thanksgivings

Abundant thanksgivings, and not: All thanksgivings? … Rava said: … say: The God of thanksgivings. Rav Pappa said: Therefore, we will recite them both: Abundant thanksgivings, and: The God of thanksgivings.
However, it is … difficult, … not difficult. This, … where one heard … This, … where one saw
One heard … that is … good tidings. And we learned … that upon … good tidings one recites: Who is good and does good.

Rather, … This, … and that, … and … not difficult. This, … refers to … where a little … fell, … that, … where a lot … fell. And if you wish, say … this and that … where a lot … fell, and … not difficult. This, … refers to … where one owns land, … that, … refers to … where one does not own land,

One who owns land recites: Who is good and does good? Didn’t we learn … One who built a new house or purchased new vessels recites: Blessed…Who has given us life…and brought us to this time. … to him and others … he recites: Who is good and does good?

not difficult. This, … refers to … where one … in partnership … that, … refers to … where one … does not have a partnership. And … was taught … The gist of the matter is, for … is … his, he recites: Blessed…Who has given us life and sustained us; for … belongs to him and to another … he recites: Who is good and does good.

And in every case where others are not with him, one does not recite: Who is good and does good? Wasn’t it taught … If they told him that his wife gave birth to a male, he recites: Who is good and does good? … There too, his wife is with him, as she is also happy that a male

Come and hear … father died and he is his heir, initially recites: Blessed…the true Judge, … and ultimately, … he recites: Blessed…Who is good and does good. … There, too, … where he has brothers who inherit along with him.

Come and hear … a change in … wine … one need not recite the blessing: … a change in place, one must recite a … blessing … And Rabbi Yosef bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Although … said that … a change in … wine one need not recite a … blessing … he does recite: Blessed…Who is good and does good. … There, too, … members of the group are drinking with him.

built a new house or purchased new vessels … Rav Huna said: They only taught … he does not … have something similar, … However, if he … has something similar he need not recite a blessing, … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even … one … has something similar … he must recite a blessing
by inference that if he purchases … and then purchases … everyone agrees that he is not required to recite a blessing,

Some say … Rav Huna said: They only taught … if he did not purchase … and purchased … However, if he purchased … and purchased … again, he need not recite a blessing. And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even if one purchased … and purchased … again, he must recite a blessing. … by inference that if one … has … and … purchased … everyone agrees that he must recite a blessing.

raises an objection … built a new house and does not … own a similar … or purchased new vessels and does not … own similar … must recite a blessing. … he … owns a similar … he need not recite a blessing, … the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda, … says: In either case, he must recite a blessing.

Granted, according to the first version … Rav Huna … in accordance with … Rabbi Meir, and … Rabbi Yoḥanan … in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda. However, according to the latter version … granted, Rav Huna … in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, but in accordance with whose … did Rabbi Yoḥanan state … is neither in accordance with … Rabbi Meir nor in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda.

Rabbi Yoḥanan … said to you: The same is true according to Rabbi Yehuda’s … one has purchased … and purchased … again, he must recite a blessing. … that they … disagreed with regard to … where he … owned … and he purchased … to convey the far-reaching nature of Rabbi Meir’s … ; even … one purchased … while owning a … he need not recite a blessing; all the more so … he purchased … and then purchased … again, he need not recite a blessing.

And … let them disagree with regard to … where one purchased … and … purchased … again, … one need not recite a blessing, in order to convey the far-reaching nature of Rabbi Yehuda’s … the strength of leniency is preferable.
One recites a blessing for the bad

What are the circumstances? … In a case where a dam was breached … onto one’s land, despite … that this will … be beneficial for him, for his land will be covered with sediment … which will enhance … it is … bad at present.
for the good
What are the circumstances? … In a case where one found a lost object, despite … that it is … bad for him … if the king heard about it, he would … take it from him. … it is favorable at present.
One whose wife was pregnant and he said: May it be … will that … will give birth … it is a vain prayer.

Is a prayer … ineffective? Rav Yosef raises an objection … “And afterwards she bore a daughter, and called her name Dina” … What is … Afterwards? … Rav said: After Leah passed judgment on herself and said: Twelve tribes are destined to descend from Jacob, six came from me and four from the maidservants, that is ten, … if this … is male, my sister … will not … be … of one the maidservants; immediately … was transformed into a daughter, as it is stated: And she called her name Dina; … One does not mention miraculous acts

And if you wish, say … story of Leah … was within forty days … As it was taught … the first three days … one should pray that … not putrefy, … From the third … until the fortieth, one should pray that it will be male. From the fortieth … until three months, one should pray that it will not be … flat fish, … From the third month until the sixth, one should pray that it will not be stillborn. … from the sixth … until the ninth, one should pray that it will be emerge safely.

Is prayer effective … Didn’t Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rav Ami, say: … man emits seed first, … gives birth to a female; … woman emits seed first, she gives birth to a male, as it is stated: “When a woman emitted seed and bore a male” … With what are we dealing here? … with a case where they both emit seed simultaneously.
One who was walking along the way

The Sages taught: There was an incident involving Hillel the Elder, who was coming on the road when he heard a scream in the city. He said: I am certain that … is not … from my house. And of him, the verse says: “He shall not be afraid of evil tidings; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the Lord” … Rava said: Any way that you interpret this verse, … It … interpreted from beginning to end … it … interpreted from end to beginning. … It … interpreted from beginning to end: Why is it that: He shall not be afraid of evil tidings? … his heart is steadfast, trusting in the Lord. … And it … interpreted from end to beginning: … heart is steadfast, trusting in the Lord … shall not be afraid of evil tidings.

This student was once walking after Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, in the marketplace of Zion. … saw that … was afraid. He said to him: You are a sinner, as it is written: “The transgressors in Zion are afraid, … replied: And is it not written: “Happy is the man that fears always” … said to him: That … is written with regard to matters of Torah,

Yehuda bar Natan was coming and going after Rav Hamnuna. … sighed; … said to him: Do you wish to bring suffering upon yourself; as it is stated: “For that which I did fear is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of has overtaken me” … Is it not said: “Happy is the man who fears always”? … That … is written with regard to matters of Torah.
We learned … One who enters a large city

The Sages taught … Upon his entrance … what does he recite? 
May it be Your will, O Lord my God, that You bring me into this city to peace. … he entered … he recites: I thank You, O Lord my God … that You brought me into this city to peace. … seeks to leave … he recites: May it be Your will, O Lord my God and God of my ancestors, that You take me out of this city to peace. … he left, he recites: I give thanks before You, O Lord my God, that You took me out of this city to peace; 
and just as You took me out to peace, 
so too lead me to peace, support me to peace, direct my steps to peace, 
and rescue me from the hand of any enemy or … lying in ambush along the way.
Rav Mattana said: This was taught only with regard to a city where … are not tried and executed, … However, in a city where … are tried and executed, … do not apply,
Some say … Rav Mattana said … Even in a city where … are tried and executed … as sometimes he may not encounter a person who will plead in his favor.

The Sages taught: One who enters a … bathhouse, … says: 
May it be Your will, O Lord my God, that you save me from this and similar … and do not let ruin or iniquity befall me, 
and if ruin or iniquity does befall me, let my death be atonement for all of my transgressions.
Abaye said: One should not say: … so as not to open his mouth to Satan … As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said and as it was taught … in the name of Rabbi Yosei: One should never open his mouth to Satan

Rav Yosef said: What is the verse … As it is written: “We should have almost been as Sodom, we should have been like unto Gomorrah” … what did … reply to them? “Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom;
When he emerges … what does he say? Rav Aḥa said: I give thanks to You, Lord, that You saved me from the fire.

Rabbi Abbahu entered a bathhouse when the bathhouse … collapsed beneath him and a miracle transpired on his behalf. He stood on a pillar and saved one hundred and one men with one arm. … He said: This is … of Rav Aḥa,

As Rav Aḥa said: One who enters to let blood says: 
May it be Your will, O Lord my God, 
that this enterprise be for healing and that You should heal me. 
As You are a faithful God of healing and Your healing is truth. 
Because it is not the way of people to heal, but they have become accustomed.
Abaye … said: One should not say this, as … taught … the school of Rabbi Yishmael … “And shall cause him to be thoroughly healed” … from here … that permission is granted to a doctor to heal.
When one stands … what does he say? Rav Aḥa said: … Blessed…Who heals without payment.

One who enters a bathroom says … Be honored, honorable holy ones, servants of … on High, 
give honor to the God of Israel, 
leave me until I enter and do my will and come … to you. 
Abaye said: A person should not say this, lest they abandon him and go. Rather he should say: 
Guard me, guard me, 
help me, help me, 
support me, support me, 
wait for me, wait for me until I enter and come out, as this is the way of man. 
Upon exiting, one says: 
Blessed…Who formed man in wisdom, 
and created in him many orifices and cavities. 
It is revealed and known before the throne of Your glory 
that were one of them to be ruptured or blocked, it would be impossible to survive and stand before You.

what … conclude … Rav said: … Healer of the sick. Shmuel said: Abba, … has rendered everyone sick. Rather, … Healer of all flesh. Rav Sheshet said: … Who performs wondrous deeds. Rav Pappa said: Therefore, let us say them both: Healer of all flesh, Who performs wondrous deeds.

One who enters to sleep on his bed recites … from Shema Yisrael to VeHaya Im Shamoa. Then he recites: 
Blessed…Who makes the bands of sleep fall upon my eyes and slumber upon my eyelids, 
and illuminates the pupil of the eye. 
May it be Your will, O Lord my God, 
that You make me lie down in peace and give me my portion in Your Torah, 
accustom me to mitzvot and do not accustom me to transgression, 
lead me not into error, nor into iniquity, nor into temptation nor into disgrace. 
May the good inclination have dominion over me 
and may the evil inclination not have dominion over me. 
Save me from an evil mishap and evil diseases. 
Let neither bad dreams nor troubling thoughts disturb me. 
May my bed be flawless before You, … Enlighten my eyes … lest I sleep … death, … Blessed are You, O Lord, Who gives light to the whole world in His glory.

When one awakens, he recites: 
My God, the soul You have placed within me is pure. 
You formed it within me, 
You breathed it into me, 
and You guard it while it is within me. 
One day You will take it from me and restore it within me in the time to come. 
As long as the soul is within me, I thank You, 
O Lord my God and God of my ancestors, Master of all worlds, Lord of all souls. 
Blessed are You, O Lord, who restores souls to lifeless bodies.

Upon hearing the sound of the rooster, one should recite: Blessed…Who gave the heart [sekhvi] understanding to distinguish between day and night. 
Upon opening his eyes, one should recite: Blessed…Who gives sight to the blind. 
Upon sitting up straight, one should recite: Blessed…Who sets captives free. 
Upon dressing, one should recite: Blessed…Who clothes the naked, … Upon standing up straight, one should recite: Blessed…Who raises those bowed down. 
Upon descending … to the ground, one should recite: Blessed…Who spreads the earth above the waters, … Upon walking, one should recite: Blessed…Who makes firm the steps of man. 
Upon putting on his shoes, one should recite: Blessed…Who has provided me with all I need, … Upon putting on his belt, one should recite: Blessed…Who girds Israel with strength. 
Upon spreading a shawl upon his head, one should recite: Blessed…Who crowns Israel with glory.

Upon wrapping himself in ritual fringes, one should recite: Blessed…Who has made us holy through His commandments and has commanded us to wrap ourselves in … ritual fringes. 
Upon donning his phylacteries on his arm, one should recite: Blessed…Who has made us holy through His commandments and has commanded us to don phylacteries. … on his head one should recite: Blessed…Who has made us holy through His commandments and has commanded us with regard to the mitzva of phylacteries. 
Upon … washing his hands: Blessed…Who has made us holy through His commandments and has commanded us with regard to the washing of the hands. 
Upon washing his face, one recites: Blessed…Who removes the bands of sleep from my eyes and slumber from my eyelids. 
And may it be Your will, O Lord my God, to accustom me in Your Torah, 
attach me to Your mitzvot, and lead me not into transgression, 
nor into error, nor into iniquity, nor into temptation nor into disgrace. 
Bend my … inclination to be subservient to You, 
and distance me from an evil person and an evil acquaintance. 
Help me attach myself to the good inclination and to a good friend in Your world. 
Grant me, today and every day, grace, loving-kindness, and compassion in Your eyes and the eyes of all who see me, 
and bestow loving-kindness upon me. 
Blessed are You, O Lord, Who bestows loving-kindness on His people, Israel.

One is obligated to recite a blessing … What … One is obligated to recite a blessing for the bad just as for the good? If we say … just as one recites a blessing for a positive event … Who is good and does good, so too one recites a blessing for a calamity … Who is good and does good, didn’t we learn … over good tidings one recites: Who is good and does good, … over bad tidings one recites: Blessed…the true Judge? … Rava said: … was only necessary … to accept … with … joy

Rav Aḥa said in the name of Rabbi Levi: What … verse … “I will sing of loving-kindness and justice; unto You, O Lord, will I sing praises” … If … loving-kindness, I will sing, and if … justice, I will sing.

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said: … from here, … “In God, I will praise His word; in the Lord, I will praise His word” … In God, I will praise His word; that is … attribute of benevolence, … In the Lord, I will praise His word; that is the attribute of suffering;
Rabbi Tanḥum said: … from here, … “I will lift up the cup of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord” … “I found trouble and sorrow, but I called upon the name of the Lord”
And the Rabbis said: … from here, … “The Lord has given and the Lord has taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord”
Rav Huna said … Rav said … Rabbi Meir said; and so it was taught … in the name of Rabbi Akiva: One must always accustom oneself to say: Everything that God does, He does for the best.

Like this … when Rabbi Akiva was walking along the road and came to a certain city, he inquired about lodging and they did not give him … He said: Everything that God does, He does for the best. He went and slept in a field, and he had with him a rooster, a donkey and a candle. A … wind came and extinguished the candle; a cat came and ate the rooster; and a lion came and ate the donkey. He said: Everything that God does, He does for the best. That night, an army came and took the city into captivity. … He said to them: Didn’t I tell you? Everything that God does,
He does for the best.

And Rav Huna said … Rav said in the name of Rabbi Meir: One’s words should always be few before the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is stated: “Be not rash with your mouth and let not your heart be hasty to utter a word before God; for God is in heaven, and you upon earth. Therefore, let your words be few”

Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda interpreted homiletically: What is the meaning of that which is written: “Then the Lord God formed [vayyitzer] man” … with a double yod? … the Holy One, Blessed be He, created two inclinations; one a good inclination and one an evil inclination.

Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak strongly objects to this: If that is so, … an animal, with regard to whom vayyitzer is not written … not have an inclination? Don’t we see that it causes damage and bites and kicks? Rather, … in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, as Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said: … woe unto me from my Creator [yotzri] and woe unto me from my inclination [yitzri].

Alternatively, … in accordance with … Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar, as Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, created two faces [du partzufin] on Adam the first … as it is stated: “You have formed me [tzartani] behind and before”
“And the tzela which the Lord, God, … He made
Rav and Shmuel … One said: … face. … And one said: … tail,

Granted, … to the one who said … face; that is … it is written: “You have formed me [tzartani] behind and before.” However, … to the one who said … tail, what is … “You have formed me [tzartani] behind and before”? … in accordance with … Rabbi Ami, as Rabbi Ami said: Behind … the act of creation; and before … for punishment.

Granted, … behind, … in the act of creation, … he was not created until … Shabbat eve; however, before, … for punishment, … what punishment … If you say … for punishment … the snake, wasn’t it taught … Rabbi … says: In … honor, one begins with the greatest; in cursing, one begins with the least significant.

In … honor, one begins with the greatest, as it is written: “And Moses said unto Aaron, and Elazar and Itamar, his remaining sons: Take … in cursing, one begins with the least significant, … first … snake was cursed, then Eve was cursed, and ultimately Adam … was cursed.
Rather, … the punishment of the flood, as it is written: “And He blotted out every living substance which was upon the face of the ground, both man and cattle, … began with man, then the animals,
Granted, according to the one who said … face … that is … it is written vayyitzer, … However, according to the one who said … tail, … what is … vayyitzer
in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, as Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said: … Woe unto me from my Creator and woe unto me from my inclination.

Granted, according to the one who said … face, that is … it is written: “Male and female, He created them” … However, according to the one who said … tail, what is … “Male and female, He created them”? … Rabbi Abbahu. … Rabbi Abbahu raised a contradiction … it is written: “Male and female, He created them,” and … it is written: “For in the image of God He made man” … How, then, … At first, the thought entered … to create two, and ultimately, only one was … created.

Granted, according to the one who said … face, that is … it is written: … and closed up the place with flesh in its place” … However, according to the one who said … tail, what is … “And closed up the place with flesh in its place”? Rabbi Yirmeya said, and some say Rav Zevid … and some say Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak … It was necessary … only with regard to the place of the incision.
Granted, according to the one … tail, that is … it is written: “And … built … However, according to the one who said … face … what is … “And He built”?

in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya, as Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya interpreted homiletically: What is … that which is written: “And the Lord God built the tzela”? … teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, braided Eve’s … and … brought her to Adam, as in the coastal towns, they call braiding … building.

Alternatively, … And He built, … Rav Ḥisda said, and some say that it is taught in a baraita: … teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, built Eve like the structure of a storehouse. Just as a storehouse is … narrow on top and wide on the bottom, in order to hold produce … so too a woman … narrow on top and wide on the bottom, in order to hold the fetus.

“And brought her unto the man” … Rabbi Yirmeya ben Elazar said: … teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, was Adam the first … best man. From here, the Torah taught that it is a desired mode of behavior for a greater individual to seek out a lesser individual to … serve as his best man. … and should not feel badly

And according to the one who said … face … which one of them walked in front? Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: It is reasonable … that the man walked in front, as it is taught … A man should not walk behind a woman on a path, … even if it is his wife. … happens upon him along a bridge, he should … move her to … sides … And anyone who walks behind a woman in a river … has no portion in the World-to-Come.

The Sages taught: One who counts money for a woman from his hand to her hand in order to look upon her, even if he has accumulated Torah and good deeds like Moses our teacher, he will not be absolved from the punishment of Gehenna, as it is stated: “Hand to hand, the evil man shall not go unpunished” … he will not be absolved from the punishment of Gehenna,
Rav Naḥman said: … Manoah, was an ignoramus, as it is written: “And Manoah…went after his wife”

Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak strongly objects to this: If that is so … with regard to Elkana, … as it is written: “And Elkana walked after his wife,” … with regard to … Elisha, as it is written: “And he arose and followed her” … Does … mean … literally walked after her? Rather, … he followed her words and advice. Here, too, … followed … words and followed her advice,

Rav Ashi said: And according to what Rav Naḥman said, … Manoah was an ignoramus; he did not even … read … in school, as it is stated: “Rebecca arose, and her damsels, and they rode upon the camels, and followed the man” … not … before the man.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … behind a lion and not behind a woman, … behind a woman and not behind idolatry, … behind idolatry and not behind a synagogue when the congregation is praying,

And we only said … in a case where he is not carrying something, and if he is carrying something, this does not apply, … And we only said … in a case where there is no other entrance … and if there is another entrance, this does not apply. And we only said … in a case where he is not riding a donkey, and if he is riding a donkey, this does not apply. And we only said … in a case where he is not donning phylacteries, but if he is donning phylacteries, this does not apply.

Rav said: The evil inclination is like a fly and it sits between the two entrances of the heart, as it is stated: “Dead flies make the ointment of the perfumer fetid and putrid” … And Shmuel said: … is like a type of wheat, as it is stated: “Transgression [ḥatat] couches at the door”

The Sages taught … A person has two kidneys; one advises him to … good and one advises him to … evil. And it stands to reason … good is to his right and … evil is to his left, as it is written: “A wise man’s understanding is at his right hand, but a fool’s understanding is at his left”
the Sages taught … The kidneys advise, the heart understands, the tongue shapes … mouth completes … esophagus takes in and lets out all kinds of food, … trachea produces the voice,

lungs draw all kinds of liquids, … liver becomes angry, … gall … injects a drop … into … allays … spleen laughs, … maw grinds … stomach … sleep, … nose awakens. … the … sleep … awaken, … the … awakens … sleep, … would gradually deteriorate. It was taught: If both … sleep or both awaken, … immediately dies.

it was taught … Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: The good inclination rules the righteous, as it is stated: “And my heart is dead within me” … evil inclination rules the wicked, as it is stated: “Transgression speaks to the wicked, there is no fear of God before his eyes” … Middling people are ruled by both … as it is stated: “Because He stands at the right hand of the needy, to save him from them that rule his soul”
Rabba said: … like us … middling. Abaye, … said to him: … the Master … does not leave … any creature to live.

And Rava said: The world was created only for … the full-fledged wicked or the full-fledged righteous; … Rava said: One should know of himself whether or not he is completely righteous, … Rav said: The world was created only for … Ahab ben Omri and for Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa. … Ahab ben Omri, this world … and … Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa, the World-to-Come

“And you shall love the Lord your God … it was taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: If it is stated: “With all your soul,” why does it state: “With all your might”? … if it stated: “With all your might,” why does it state: “With all your soul”? Rather, … if one’s body is dearer to him than his property, therefore it is stated: “With all your soul”; … And if one’s money is dearer to him than his body, therefore it is stated: “With all your might”; … Rabbi Akiva says: “With all your soul” … Even if … takes your soul.

The Sages taught: One time, … the evil empire … decreed that Israel may not engage in … Torah. Pappos ben Yehuda came and found Rabbi Akiva, who was convening assemblies in public and engaging in Torah … said to him: Akiva, are you not afraid of the empire?

answered him: I will relate a parable. To what can this be compared? … a fox walking along a riverbank when he sees fish gathering … from place to place. … said to them: From what are you fleeing? 
They said to him: … from the nets that people cast upon us. 
He said to them: Do you wish to come up onto dry land, and we will reside together just as my ancestors resided with your ancestors? … said to him: You are the one of whom they say, he is the cleverest of animals? You are not clever; you are a fool. If we are afraid in … our … habitat … life, … in a habitat … death, all the more so. … So too, we … now that we sit and engage in Torah … about which it is written: “For that is your life, and the length of your days” … to this extent; if we proceed to … idle from its … all the more so

said: Not a few days passed until they seized Rabbi Akiva and incarcerated him in prison, and seized Pappos ben Yehuda and incarcerated him alongside him. … said to him: Pappos, who brought you here? … replied: Happy are you, Rabbi Akiva, for you were arrested on … Torah … Woe unto Pappos who was seized on … idle matters.

When they took Rabbi Akiva out to be executed, it was time for the recitation of Shema. And they were raking his flesh with iron combs, and he was … accepting upon himself the yoke of Heaven. His students said to him: Our teacher, even now, … He said to them: All my days I have been troubled by the verse: With all your soul, … Even if God takes your soul. I said … When will the … be afforded me to fulfill this … Now that it has been afforded me, shall I not fulfill it? He prolonged … One, until his soul left … One. A voice descended … and said: Happy are you, Rabbi Akiva, that your soul left … as … One.

The ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: This is Torah and this its reward? … “From death, by Your hand, O Lord, from death … said … to … “Whose portion is in this life.” … a Divine Voice emerged and said: Happy are you, Rabbi Akiva, as you are destined for life in the World-to-Come,

one may not act irreverently opposite the Eastern Gate, which is aligned with the Holy of Holies. … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: They only said … from … Scopus [Tzofim] and within, and … one can see … It is also stated: Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, said: Rabbi Yoḥanan said the following: They only said … Scopus and within, … one can see, and when there is no fence … and when the Divine Presence is resting

the Sages taught: One who defecates in Judea should not defecate … east and west, … rather … facing north and south. But in the Galilee … one should only defecate … east and west. Rabbi Yosei permits … as Rabbi Yosei was wont to say: They only prohibited … one can see … where there is no fence, and when the Divine Presence is resting … And the Rabbis prohibit
Rabbis, … is … first … tanna, … between them is … the sides,

It was taught … another … One who defecates in Judea should not defecate … east and west; rather, … north and south. And in the Galilee, … north and south is prohibited, … east and west is permitted. And Rabbi Yosei permitted … as Rabbi Yosei was wont to say: They only prohibited … one can see … Rabbi Yehuda says: When the Temple is standing, it is prohibited, … when the Temple is not standing, it is permitted. … Rabbi Akiva prohibits … anywhere
Rabbi Akiva’s … is identical to … the first, … tanna, … between them … outside of Eretz … ,

Rabba’s … the bricks were placed east and west … Abaye went … placed them north and south, … Rabba entered … fixed them. He said: Who is the one that is upsetting me? I hold in accordance with … Rabbi Akiva, … said: It is prohibited everywhere.

It was taught … Rabbi Akiva said: I once entered the bathroom after … Rabbi Yehoshua, and I learned three things from … his … I learned that one should not defecate … east and west, but rather … north and south; I learned that one should not uncover himself … standing, but … sitting, … and I learned that one should not wipe with his right … but with his left. Ben Azzai, … said to him: You were impertinent to your teacher to that extent … He replied: It is Torah, and I must learn.

we learned … Ben Azzai said: I once entered a bathroom after Rabbi Akiva, and I learned three things from … his … I learned that one should not defecate … east and west, but rather … north and south; I learned that one should not uncover himself … standing, but … sitting; and I learned that one should not wipe with his right … but with his left. Rabbi Yehuda said to him: You were impertinent to your teacher to that extent? He replied: It is Torah, and I must learn.

Rav Kahana entered and lay beneath Rav’s bed. He heard … chatting and laughing … and seeing to his needs, … said to … The mouth … Abba, … is like … has never eaten a cooked dish, … said to him: Kahana, you are here? Leave, as … is an undesirable mode of behavior. … said to him: It is Torah, and I must learn.

Why must one not wipe … with his right … but with his left? Rava said: Because the Torah was given with the right … as it is stated: “At His right hand was a fiery law unto them” … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: Because … is close to the mouth, … And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Because one ties the phylacteries … with … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: Because one points to the … notes of the Torah with
parallel to a tannaitic … Rabbi Eliezer says: … because he eats with it. Rabbi Yehoshua says: Because he writes with it. Rabbi Akiva says: Because he points to the notes of the Torah with it.

Rabbi Tanḥum bar Ḥanilai said: Anyone who is modest in the bathroom will be saved from three things: From snakes, from scorpions and from demons. And some say … even his dreams will be settling for him.

There was a particular bathroom in … Tiberias, where, when two would enter it, even during the day, they would be harmed … Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi would each enter alone, they were not harmed. The Sages said to them: Aren’t you afraid? … said to them: We have learned … tradition … bathroom … modesty and silence. The tradition … suffering … silence and prayer.
Abaye’s mother raised a lamb to accompany him to the bathroom. … raised a goat for him. … A goat … interchanged with a goat-demon.

Before Rava became the head of the yeshiva, … the daughter of Rav Ḥisda, would rattle a nut in a copper vessel for him. … After … preside … she constructed a window for him, … and placed her hand upon his head.

Ulla said: Behind a fence, one … may defecate immediately. In a valley … sufficiently so that if he passes wind, no one will hear him. Isi bar Natan taught as follows: Behind a fence … sufficiently so that if he passes wind another does not hear him, and in a valley, … sufficiently so that no one can see him.
raises an objection … exit from the entrance of the olive press, defecate behind the fence, and are ritually pure.
With regard to … ritual purity, they were lenient.
Come and hear … How far … distance themselves, and … will … pure? … so far that he … sees him. … who eat in purity are different, as the Sages were lenient with them.
Rav Ashi said: What is … So long as another does not see him, which … Isi bar Natan said? Sufficient that another person cannot see his nakedness, although he does see him.

There was a particular eulogizer who went … in the presence of Rav Naḥman. … he said: This … was modest in his ways. Rav Naḥman said to him: Did you go to the bathroom with him and know whether or not he was modest? As we learned … One can only describe as modest one who is modest … in the bathroom,
And what difference … to Rav Naḥman, … Because it was taught … Just as the deceased are punished, so too are the eulogizers and those who answer after them.
The Sages taught … Who is a modest person? One who defecates at night where he defecates during the day,

Is that so? Didn’t Rav Yehuda say … Rav said: One must always accustom himself … in the morning and at night, … so that he will not need to distance himself? Moreover, during the day, Rava would go up to a mil … and at night he would tell his servant: Clear a place for me in the city street. And so too, Rabbi Zeira told his servant: See who is behind the study hall, as I need to defecate. … Rather, … say … In the manner that one defecates during the day,
Rav Ashi said: Even if you say … Where he defecates during the day, … was only necessary in … a corner,
the matter itself. Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: One must always accustom himself … in the morning and … at night so that he will not need to distance himself.

That … was also taught … Ben Azzai said: Rise early … and go … evening and go … so that you will not … distance yourself. … Touch … and … sit; do not sit and … touch, for anyone who sits and … touches, even if sorcery is performed in … Aspamia, … will come upon him.

And if one forgets and sits and then touches, what is his remedy? When … stands, … recite the following … Not for me, not for me, neither taḥim nor taḥtim, … neither these nor from these, neither the sorcery of a sorcerer nor the sorcery of a sorceress.

it was taught … Ben Azzai says: On all beds, lie, except for the ground. On all seats, sit, except for a beam, … Shmuel said: Sleeping at dawn is … as forging [istema] … to iron. A … movement at dawn … as forging … to iron.

Bar Kappara would sell sayings for dinars; … If you are hungry, eat; … if you are thirsty, drink; while the pot is still boiling, pour it … When the horn is sounded in Rome, … son of a fig seller, sell your father’s figs,

Abaye said to the Sages: When you enter the paths … Meḥoza in order to go out … in a field, look neither to one side nor to the other, as perhaps women are sitting there and it is improper to look at them.

Rav Safra once entered a bathroom, … Rabbi Abba came along. … coughed next to the door. … said to him: Enter, master. When he came out, Rabbi Abba said to him: Until now, you never entered Seir, … and … you … learned the … Seir? Didn’t we learn … There was a fire … and a bathroom of honor. held that it was dangerous … As it was taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel says: A column … that is held back … causes dropsy [hidrokan]. A stream [silon] … that is held back causes jaundice.

and he said to kill you; and you spared you”

and said to the angel that destroyed the many [rav] people: … Rabbi Elazar said … the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the angel: Take for me a great one [rav] from among them, who is worthy of defraying several … debts. … at that moment Avishai ben Tzeruya, who was equivalent to the majority of the Sanhedrin, died.

said to Rava: I … say the following: Let us say, be stringent here, … and be stringent here,

might … all of the blessings there will have … a single … praise, … the verse teaches: “That is exalted above all blessing and praise”; for every blessing, a … praise is offered.

interpreted from beginning to end: It is time to work for the Lord; what is the reason? Because they have made void Your Torah, … interpreted from end to beginning … They have made void Your Torah; what is the reason? Because it is time to work for the Lord.

it was taught … Hillel the Elder says: At the time of gathering, … disseminate … At the time of dissemination, gather, … And if you see a generation for whom Torah is beloved, disseminate, as it is stated: “There is who scatters, and yet increases” … if you see a generation for whom Torah is not beloved, gather; … as it is stated: “It is time to work for the Lord; they have made void Your Torah.”
bar Kappara taught: … declined, jump and purchase from it; and where there is no man, there be a man; … Abaye said: Infer from this … where there is a man, there do not be a man.
obvious? … This … is only necessary … where … two who are equal.

Bar Kappara taught: A person should always teach his child a clean and simple craft. … What … Rav Ḥisda said: Cutting precious stones.
were taught … Rabbi … says: One should never have too many friends in his house, … as it is stated: “There are friends that one has to his own hurt”

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … his sustenance flies [meofefet] to him like a bird, as it is stated: “And precious silver [toafot] unto you.”

Rabbi Tavi said in the name of Rabbi Yoshiya: Anyone who is lax in his … matters of Torah will … lack the strength to stand on a day of adversity, as it is stated: “If you faint in the day of adversity, your strength is small indeed” … Rav Ami bar Mattana said … Shmuel said: And even … a single … as it is stated: If you faint; … in any case,
Rav Safra said: Rabbi Abbahu would relate: When Ḥanina, son of Rabbi Yehoshua’s brother, went to the Diaspora, … he would intercalate years and establish months outside of Eretz

sent two Torah scholars after him, Rabbi Yosei ben Keifar and the grandson of Zekharya ben Kevutal. When … saw them, he asked them: Why did you come? He said to them: Why is it that … I … impure, you … pure; … I prohibit … you permit … They said to him: … because you intercalate the years and establish the months outside of Eretz

He said to them: Didn’t … Akiva ben Yosef … intercalate years and establish months outside of Eretz … They replied to him: Leave … Rabbi Akiva, as, … he did not leave behind anyone … as he in Eretz Yisrael. … said to them: I also did not leave behind anyone … as me in Eretz Yisrael. They said to him: The kids who you left behind have grown into goats with horns; … And they sent us to you, and this is what they said to us: Go and tell him in our name: If he obeys, fine; and if … not … he will be ostracized.

And … tell our brethren in exile: If they obey … fine; and if … not … They should climb a mountain; Aḥiya, … will build an altar, Ḥananya, … will play the lute, and all will … heresy and say that they have no portion in the God of Israel.
immediately the entire nation burst into tears, saying: God forbid. We do have a portion in the God of Israel.
Why … to that extent … Because it is stated: “For out of Zion shall go forth the Torah, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem”

Granted, … pure and … impure; … stringently. But … he … impure and they … pure, what are … Was it not taught … If a Sage … impure, his colleague is not permitted … pure; … prohibited … his colleague may not permit … They held … so that people would not be drawn after him;

The Sages taught: When our Rabbis, … entered the vineyard, … in Yavne, Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Yosei, Rabbi Neḥemya, and Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, were there … They all began … in honor of … hosts, … and they taught.

Rabbi Yehuda, head of the speakers in every place, opened … in honor of Torah, and taught: … “Now Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, … Isn’t this an a fortiori inference? Just as the Torah says … the ark of God, which was only twelve mil from the camp: “Every seeker of God went out unto the Tent of Meeting”; all the more so … Torah scholars, … go from city to city and country to country to study Torah,

“And the Lord spoke unto Moses, face to face” … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses: Moses, you and I will show cheerful faces in … halakha … Some say … the Holy One, Blessed be He, told Moses: Just as I showed you a cheerful face, so too you will show Israel a cheerful face and restore the tent to its place

“And he would return into the camp; … Rabbi Abbahu said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, told Moses: Now, … The Master, … is angry and … student, … angry, and what will happen to Israel? … If you restore the tent to its place, fine; and if not, Joshua bin-Nun, your student, … serve … in your place.

And that is what is written: “And he would return into the camp; … Rava said: Nevertheless, … the statement … was not uttered for naught. … “But his minister, Joshua bin-Nun, a young man, departed not out of the Tent.”

And Rabbi Yehuda again began … in honor of Torah and taught: … “Keep silence [hasket] and hear, Israel; this day you have become a people … Was the Torah given to Israel on that day? Wasn’t that day at the end of forty years … Rather, … to teach that each and every day the Torah is as dear to those who study it, as … on the day it was given from Mount Sinai.
Rabbi Tanḥum, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya, of the village of Akko, said: Know … as one who recites Shema, morning and evening, … does not recite it one evening, it is as if he never recited Shema.

hasket … Form [asu] many groups [kitot] and study Torah, for the Torah is only acquired … in a group. … in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina; as Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: What is … that which is written: “A sword is upon the boasters [habaddim], and they shall become fools [noalu]” … A sword upon the enemies of Torah scholars, … who sit alone [bad bevad] and study Torah. And furthermore, … grow foolish, as it is written here, noalu, and elsewhere it is written … “For that we have done foolishly [noalnu]” … And furthermore, they sin … as … it is stated: … and for that we have sinned.”
If you wish, say … from here: “The princes of Tzoan are become fools [noalu]”

an alternative … “Keep silence [hasket] and hear, Israel”; break [kattetu] yourselves over words of the Torah. … in accordance with … Reish Lakish, as Reish Lakish said: From where … that matters of Torah are only retained by one who kills himself over it? As it is stated: “This is the Torah: When one dies in a tent”

alternative explanation … “Keep silence [hasket] and hear, Israel”; … be silent [has] … then … analyze [kattet] … in accordance with … Rava, as Rava said: One must always study Torah … and … then analyze

In the school of Rabbi Yannai they said: What is … that which is written: “For the churning of milk brings forth curd, and the wringing of the nose [af] brings forth blood, so the forcing of wrath [appayim] brings forth strife”
in whom do you find the cream of Torah? With one who spits out the milk that he nursed from his mother’s breasts over it;

And the wringing of the nose brings forth blood, any student whose rabbi is angry [af] with him the first time and he is silent … will merit … to distinguish between blood that is ritually impure and blood that is ritually pure.

And the forcing of wrath [appayim] brings forth strife; any student whose rabbi is angry with him for the first and second times, … and he is silent, merits to distinguish between monetary cases, … and capital cases, … As we learned … Rabbi Yishmael says: One who seeks to become wise should engage in monetary laws, as there is no greater discipline in Torah, as they are like a flowing well

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said: What is … that which is written: “If you have done foolishly in lifting up yourself, or if you have planned devices [zamota], lay your hand over your mouth” … Anyone who abases himself over matters of Torah, … will ultimately be exalted.
