Rabbi Neḥemya began … in honor of the hosts and taught: What is … that which is written: “And Saul said unto the Kenites: Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites lest I destroy you with them, for you showed kindness to all the Children of Israel when they came up out of Egypt” … Isn’t this an a fortiori inference: Just as Jethro, … only befriended Moses for his own honor, … in this way … all the more so … one who hosts a Torah scholar in his home, providing him with food and drink and availing him of his possessions,

Rabbi Yosei began … in honor of the hosts, and taught: … “You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother; you shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you were a stranger in his land” … Isn’t this an a fortiori inference: Just as the Egyptians, who only befriended Israel, … for their own benefit, … as it is stated: “And if you know any able men among them, then make them rulers over my cattle” … this way, all the more so … one who hosts a Torah scholar in his home, providing him with food and drink and availing him of his possessions

Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, began … in honor of the hosts, and taught: … “The Lord has blessed the house of Oved-edom…because of the ark of God” … Isn’t this an a fortiori inference: Just as in reward for honoring the ark, which neither ate nor drank, but before which … swept and sprinkled … this way … all the more so … one who hosts a Torah scholar in his home, providing him with food and drink and availing him of his possessions

as it is stated: … sons…Peulletai the eighth,” and … it is written: “For God blessed him” … “All these were of the sons of Oved-edom; they and their sons and their brethren, able men in strength for the service; sixty-two of Oved-edom”

from … Rabba and Rav Yosef, as Rav Yosef … Sinai, … and Rabba … one who uproots mountains, … The moment arrived when they were needed; … They sent … there, … Which takes precedence, Sinai or one who uproots mountains? all those years that Rabba presided, … did not even call a bloodletter to his home.

if the threshold was ten … high and four … wide, it is an independent domain, … This supports … Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi, as Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said that Rabbi Meir used to say: Any place that you find two domains, … and … they are … one domain, … in a case … a pillar … ten … high and four … wide … in the private domain, … it is prohibited … to … shoulders upon it … a decree … due to a … mound … in the public domain.

if they started, they need not stop. Let us say that this will be a conclusive refutation of … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Once the time of the afternoon prayer has arrived, it is prohibited for a person to taste anything before he recites the afternoon prayer.

Is that so? And Rava bar Meḥasseya said … Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said … Rav said: A person should never distinguish … his sons … among … sons … As, due to the weight of two sela of fine wool [meilat] that Jacob gave to Joseph, beyond what … the rest of his sons, … his brothers became jealous of him and the matter unfolded and our forefathers descended to Egypt.

And Rava bar Meḥasseya said that Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said Rav said: A person should always seek and dwell in a city whose settling … recent … as due to the fact that its settling is recent its sins are few, … As it is stated … “Behold, here is this city that is close to run away to and it is small” … What is … close? If you say: That it is close … and … small, … Didn’t they see it? Rather, … because its settling was close, … its sins were few. Rabbi Avin said: What is the verse … As it is written: “I will escape there please [na]” … numerological value … nun alef … fifty-one, while Sodom … fifty-two … And … tranquil
twenty-six … “Twelve years they served Chedorlaomer and thirteen years they rebelled, and in the fourteenth year

And Rava bar Meḥasseya said … Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said … Rav said … Any city whose roofs are higher than the synagogue … ultimately be destroyed … which is stated: “To uplift the house of our God and restore its ruins” … And this applies only to the height of the houses … However, … the poles [kashkushei] and the towers [abrurei] … we have no … with it. Rav Ashi said: I caused … Mata Meḥasseya to not be destroyed … Wasn’t … destroyed? … It was not destroyed because of that sin;

And Rava bar Meḥasseya said … Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said … Rav said: … under … Ishmael and not under … a stranger, … under a stranger and not under a Ḥabar, … under a Ḥabar and not under a Torah scholar, … under a Torah scholar and not under an orphan or a widow,

And Rava bar Meḥasseya said … Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said … Rav said: … any … illness and not … intestinal illness. … any pain, … and not heart pain; any … ache and not a headache; any evil and not an evil wife.

And Rava bar Meḥasseya said … Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said … Rav said: A fast is effective to … a … dream like fire … chaff. Rav Ḥisda said: And … on that day … And Rav Yosef said: … even on Shabbat.

Rav Yehoshua, son of Rav Idi, happened … to the house of Rav Ashi. They prepared a third-born calf, … for him. They said to him: Let the Master taste something. He said to them: I am sitting … a fast. They said to him: And does the Master not hold … this … Rav Yehuda, as Rav Yehuda said: A person can borrow his fast … and repay it … He said to them: It is a fast for a dream. And Rava bar Meḥasseya said … Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said … Rav said: A fast is effective to … a … dream like fire … chaff. And Rav Ḥisda said … on that day … And Rav Yosef said … even on Shabbat.

if they … began … they need not stop … they stop to recite Shema. … Didn’t … first clause … teach … the latter clause … we came to … matters of Torah. … As it was taught … Torah scholars, who were engaged in the … Torah, stop … for Shema, and they do not stop for prayer. a dilemma was raised … What is … a karmelit … Abaye said: That … is … that … Rava said: … It, … itself is … a … decree. And will we arise and issue … decree to … decree?

we learned … The tailor may not go out … his needle adjacent to nightfall … lest he forget … and go out … Is it not … stuck in his clothing? … No, … where he is holding … in his hand,

Rav Yosef said: … not difficult. … this … is … Rabbi Meir; that, … is … Rabbi Yehuda.

Abaye said to … Say … you heard … Rabbi Meir … with regard to an object that is not … its … manner. … with regard to a matter that is … its … manner, did you hear … he … As, if you do not say so, … a layman [hedyot … who carved out a … kav … piece of wood on Shabbat, … Rabbi Meir also does not deem him liable
Rather, Rav Hamnuna said: … not difficult, … Here, … to a zav who … two sightings … there, … to a zav who … three sightings.

may not shake his clothes … A dilemma was raised … one may not shake his clothes … during the day … lest he kill … is … Rabbi Eliezer? it was taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says … One may not kill a louse on Shabbat, … the statement of Beit Shammai; and Beit Hillel permit

And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar would also say in the name of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: One may not make matches [meshaddekhin] for the children, to betroth … and … not … the child and teach him … a … book or to teach him a trade, and … may not comfort mourners … and … may not visit the sick on Shabbat, … the statement of Beit Shammai, … And Beit Hillel permit
The Sages taught … One who enters to visit a sick person … says: It is … Shabbat … to cry out … and healing is soon to come. And Rabbi Meir says … is capable … compassion.

one may not read … by candlelight … Rabba said: … even … two statures … high, and even … two plow handles, and even … ten houses one atop the other. … One may not read, but … two, … well … Wasn’t it taught … neither one nor two … Rabbi Elazar said: … not difficult, … here, … in one matter … There, … in two … matters. … Rav Huna said: And with regard to a bonfire, … even … ten people, it is prohibited

raises an objection … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: The schoolchildren would organize the sections and read … by candlelight. … If you wish, say … the beginning of the sections. placing incense and sulfur … what is the reason Beit Shammai permitted … there, … was placed on the ground, … A tub … and a … lamp; and a pot … and a spit [shapud] … what is the reason Beit Shammai permitted … where he declares … ownerless.

who is … who taught this … that the Sages taught: A woman may not fill up a pot with pounded wheat and lupines, … and place them in the oven … Shabbat eve at nightfall. And if she placed them … at the conclusion of Shabbat they are forbidden for a … time … sufficient for them to be prepared, … Similarly, … A baker may not fill a barrel of water and place it in the oven on Shabbat eve at nightfall … and if he did so, … at the conclusion of Shabbat it is forbidden for … time … sufficient for it to be prepared … Let us say … is … Beit Shammai and not … Beit Hillel. … Even if you say … Beit Hillel, … a decree … lest … stoke … coals

If so, … incense and sulfur, … should also issue a decree … There, … he will not stoke them, as if he stokes them smoke will rise into … and that is damaging for them. … bundles of flax, … should also issue a decree. … There, since wind is damaging for them, he does not expose them, … wool … in the … kettle, … should also issue a decree. Shmuel said: … to a pot that is removed … Let us be concerned lest he stir … to … removed … and sealed with clay

And now … the Master said … a decree … lest he stoke the coals; … this pot of raw meat, it is permitted to place it in an oven … Shabbat eve at nightfall. What is the reason … Since it is not fit for … the night, … he diverts his thoughts from it and will not come to stoke the coals. And … cooked meat; it is permitted … cooked and not … cooked is prohibited, … And if he threw a raw bone into … well

And now that the Master said … anything for which wind is damaging one does not expose, … meat of a kid … is sealed with clay, … well … of a ram … barḥa … and … not sealed with clay, it is prohibited … of a kid and … not sealed with clay, … of a ram and … sealed, … Rav Ashi permitted … and Rav Yirmeya from Difti prohibited … And … to … Rav Ashi, who permitted … wasn’t it taught … one may not roast meat, an onion, and an egg … unless … sufficient time for them to be roasted while it is still day? … There, … of a ram and … not sealed with clay.

Others say … of a kid, whether … sealed … whether … not sealed, … well … of a ram, … sealed, … well … too … Where they disagreed … in … a ram and … not sealed. Rav Ashi permitted … and Rav Yirmeya from Difti prohibited … And … to … Rav Ashi, who permitted … wasn’t it taught … one may only roast meat, an onion, and an egg … if … sufficient time for them to be roasted while it is still day? … There, … to … meat … on the coals. … Ravina said: … that raw gourd, … well … since the wind is damaging for it, it is considered like the meat of a kid.

Beit Shammai say: One may only sell … to a gentile … The Sages taught … Beit Shammai say: A person may not sell his object to a gentile, and lend … him, and loan him … and give him … as a gift … unless … sufficient time for him, … to reach his house … And Beit Hillel say: … for him to reach a house adjacent to the wall … Rabbi Akiva says: … sufficient time for him to exit the entrance of … house. … Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said: That is the statement of Rabbi Akiva; that is the statement of Beit Hillel. Rabbi Akiva came only to explain the statement of Beit Hillel.

The Sages taught … Beit Shammai say: A person may not sell his leaven to a gentile … unless he knows that … will be finished before Passover. And Beit Hillel say: As long as it is permitted … to eat … it is … permitted for him to sell it … And Rabbi Yehuda says:
Babylonian kutaḥ, … all kinds of kutaḥ, it is prohibited to sell … thirty days before Passover.
The Sages taught … One may, … put food before the dog in the courtyard … lifted it and exited … not attend to him

On a similar note, … One may place food before the gentile in the courtyard … lifted it and exited, one need not attend to him. … Why do I need this as well? This … is the same as that … Lest you say … this … is incumbent upon … And … this … is not incumbent upon … teaches us

The Sages taught … A person may not rent his utensils to a gentile on Shabbat eve, … on the fourth and on the fifth … it is permitted. On a similar note, one may not send letters in the hand of a gentile on Shabbat eve. … on the fourth and on the fifth … it is permitted. … they said about Rabbi Yosei the priest, and some say … about Rabbi Yosei the Ḥasid, that … his handwriting was never found in the hand of a gentile,

The Sages taught … One may not send a letter in the hand of a gentile … Shabbat eve unless he stipulates a set sum of money for him. … Beit Shammai say: … for … to reach his house … And Beit Hillel say: … for him to reach the house adjacent to the wall

Didn’t he stipulate a set … Rav Sheshet said, … is saying as follows: And if he did not stipulate a set … Beit Shammai say: … for … to reach his house … And Beit Hillel say: … for him to reach the house adjacent to the wall

Didn’t you say in the first clause … one may not send … not difficult, … this, … where the house of the mail carrier [bei doar] is permanently located in the city. And this, … where the house of the mail carrier is not permanently located in the city.

The Sages taught: One may not set sail on a ship fewer than three days before Shabbat, … In what case is this … said? … for a voluntary matter; however, … for a matter … mitzva, … well … And, … he … stipulate with … on the condition that he rests, … and … does not rest. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: He need not … And … from Tyre to Sidon, … is permitted even on Shabbat eve.

The Sages taught … One may not lay siege to cities of gentiles fewer than three days before Shabbat, … And if they … began … they need not stop … And so Shammai would say: … until it falls” … even on Shabbat.

Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: … was accustomed … It was taught … Rabbi Tzadok said: This was the custom of the house of Rabban Gamliel: They would give white clothes to the … launderer three days before Shabbat, and … colored … even on Shabbat eve. … And from their statement we learned that white … are more difficult to launder than colored ones,

Abaye gave this dyed garment to the launderer. … said to … How much do you want … to … it? … said to … Same as for a white … said to him: … as the Sages already preceded you, … Abaye said: One who gives clothing to the launderer, he should give … him by measure and he should take … from him by measure. … that … if it is longer, … caused him a loss … he stretched … And if it is shorter, he … caused him a loss … he shrunk it.

these, … and those, … agree … one may load … What is different about all … where Beit Shammai issued a decree … them, and what is different about the beams of the olive press and the circular wine press that … did not issue a decree … Those … where if he performed them on Shabbat he is rendered liable … a sin-offering, Beit Shammai issued a decree … them … Shabbat eve at nightfall. … the beams of the olive press and the circular wine press, … if he performed them on Shabbat he is not rendered liable … a sin-offering, … did not issue a decree.

Who is the tanna … anything that comes on its own, … well … Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: It is … Rabbi Yishmael, as we learned … the garlic and the unripe … and the stalks … that he crushed while it was still day, Rabbi Yishmael says: He may … finish after it gets dark, … And Rabbi Akiva says:

He may not finish. And … Rabbi Elazar said: … is … Rabbi Elazar … As we learned … honeycombs that he crushed on Shabbat eve and … came out on its own … it is prohibited to eat … And Rabbi Elazar permits

And Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina, what is the reason he did not say … Rabbi Elazar? … said to you … there, … it is food from the beginning and it is food at the end, … here, … from the beginning … food and now … liquid, … And Rabbi Elazar … said to you … We heard … Rabbi Elazar permitted olives and grapes as well. As when Rav Hoshaya from Neharde’a came, he came and brought a baraita with him, … Olives and grapes that he crushed from Shabbat eve and … seeped out on their own, … are prohibited. Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon permit … Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Ḥanina did not know … baraita.

And Rabbi Elazar, what is the reason he did not say … Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina, … said to you: Wasn’t it stated … Rava bar Ḥanina said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … to … lack grinding, … where they disagreed … lacking … pounding; and these … are also considered as … lacking grinding. … Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina issued a … ruling in accordance with … Rabbi Yishmael,

Oil of olive pressers and mats of olive pressers, … Rav prohibited … And Shmuel permitted … those mats … on a ship. Rav prohibited … and Shmuel permitted … Rav Naḥman said: A goat … for its milk, and a ewe … for shearing its … and a chicken … for its egg, and oxen … for plowing, … as well as dates used for commerce; … Rav prohibited … And Shmuel said: They are permitted, … they disagree in the dispute of … Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon

this student who issued a ruling in … Ḥarta De’argiz … in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon, … Rav Hamnuna excommunicated him. … Don’t we hold … in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon? … This … was in the place of Rav … should not have done this; … these two students: One would rescue … with one vessel and one would rescue with four and five vessels, … And they disagree with regard to the … dispute of Rabba bar Zavda and Rav Huna

MISHNA: … One may only roast meat, an onion, or an egg if … sufficient … so that they could be roasted while it is still day. One may only place … bread in the oven … at nightfall, and … a cake on the coals, if … enough that … surface … will form a crust while it is still day. Rabbi Eliezer says: … that its bottom … should harden, … one may, … lower the Paschal lamb … at nightfall, … And one may, … kindle the fire in the bonfire of the Chamber of the Hearth
And, … in the outlying areas, … time for the fire to take hold in most of … Rabbi Yehuda says: With … coals, … any amount

GEMARA: … And how much … Rabbi Elazar said … Rav said: So that they will be roasted while it is still day like the food of ben Drosai, … It was also stated … Rav Asi said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Anything that is … like the food of ben Drosai … no … has … cooking of gentiles. … It was taught … Ḥananya says: … anything that is … like the food of ben Drosai, it is permitted to keep it on the stove … and even though … is not swept … and … are not covered with ashes.

one may only place bread … A dilemma was raised before them: … bottom … is … that … close to the oven, or perhaps is it the bottom that is close to the fire? Come … hear … Rabbi Eliezer says … So that its surface that is stuck to the oven will form a crust.

one may lower the Paschal lamb … at nightfall. … What is the reason … Because the people of the group … are vigilant … And if that was not so, … not … Didn’t the Master say: … a kid, whether … sealed … whether … not sealed, … well … there, … was cut … here, … is not cut

And one may light the fire … From where are these matters … derived? Rav Huna said, … “You shall kindle no fire in all of your habitations … “In all of your habitations,” … you may not kindle fire, but you may kindle fire … in the bonfire of the Chamber of the Hearth, … Rav Ḥisda objects: If so, … also … even on Shabbat … Rather, Rav Ḥisda said, … When the verse came, it came to permit … limbs and fats … priests are vigilant

in the outlying areas … for … to take hold … What is … most of it? Rav said: Most of each and every one … And Shmuel said: … sufficiently … so that they will not say … Bring … branches, … and we will place … beneath … Rav Ḥiyya taught … to support Shmuel, … to the point that the flame will ascend on its own and not that the flame will ascend due to something else.

a single branch … Rav said: Most of the thickness … Others say … Most of the circumference … Rav Pappa said: … therefore, we require most of its thickness … and we require most of its circumference … parallel to the … tanna’im, … Rabbi Ḥiyya said: … the wood will be ruined to the extent … the work of a craftsman. And Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: So that the fire will take hold from both sides … And even though there is no proof for the matter, … an allusion to the matter … the fire consumed both of its ends and the midst of it is burned. Is it fit for any work?”

“And the hearth [aḥ] was burning before him” … What is … aḥ … Rav said … willow branch … aḥvana]. And Shmuel said: … wood that was lit with aḥvana, … this … who said to … Who wants aḥvana? And he was found … willow,

Rav Huna said: Reeds … do not require … most … he tied them … most … need … seeds … do not require … most … he placed them in woven baskets [ḥotalot], most … need … Rav Ḥisda strongly objects … On the contrary, the opposite makes sense, … reeds are scattered … they are bundled, they are not scattered, … seeds are scattered. … he placed them in woven baskets, they are not scattered. It was also stated
Rav Kahana said: Reeds that one tied them … require … most … one did not tie them … they do not require … most … seeds require … most … he placed them in woven baskets, they do not require … most
Rav Yosef taught … Four bonfires do not require … most … of pitch, and of sulfur, and of … cheese, and of fatty … it was taught in a baraita … of straw and … of rakings … also

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Babylonian wood does not require … most … Rav Yosef … objects: What is that … If you say … slivers … now … a wick, Ulla said … one who lights … must light most of what emerges … is it necessary … slivers … Rather, Rav Yosef said: … the branch of … cedar … Rami bar Abba said: … hyssop … zaza

MISHNA: With what may one light … and with what may one not light … neither with cedar bast [lekhesh], nor with uncombed flax [ḥosen], nor with raw silk [kalakh], nor with willow bast [petilat ha’idan], nor with desert weed [petilat hamidbar], nor with green … that is on … surface of the water. … neither with pitch [zefet], nor with wax [sha’ava], nor with castor oil [shemen kik], nor with burnt oil [shemen sereifa], nor with … a sheep’s tail [alya], nor with tallow [ḥelev]. Naḥum the Mede says: One may light with boiled tallow. And the Rabbis say: Both … boiled and … not boiled, one may not light with them.
GEMARA: … lekhesh … branch of the cedar … cedar mere wood? … the woolly … that is

one may not … with ḥosen. Rav Yosef said: … tow, … of … flax. Abaye said to him: Isn’t it written: “And the ḥason shall be as tow” … By inference, ḥosen is not tow. Rather, Abaye said: … flax whose … was crushed … not … combed.
And … one may not … with kalakh. Shmuel said: I asked all seafarers, and they said to me … name … is kulka. Rav Yitzḥak bar Ze’ira said: … the cocoon of the silkworm [gushkera].

Ravin and Abaye were sitting before Rabbana Neḥemya, brother of the Exilarch. … saw that … was wearing metaksa, … Ravin said to Abaye: This is … kalakh that we learned … said to him: We call it shira peranda.

raises an objection … The shira’im, the kalakh, and the sirikin, … require ritual fringes. … a conclusive refutation … Ravin … a conclusive refutation. If you wish, say … shira … distinct … and shira peranda is … distinct

And … one may not … with petilat ha’idan. … willow, … Ravin and Abaye were walking in the valley of Tamrurita. They saw these willow … Ravin said to Abaye: This is … idan that we learned … said to him: … this is mere wood. … peeled … and showed him the wool- … between … Nor with desert silk [petilat hamidbar]. … the mullein
And … one may not … green … that is on … What is this … If you say … moss found on standing water, … brittle … Rather, Rav Pappa said: … the moss … on ships,
It was taught … added to … of wool and hair … And our tanna … wool shrinks … hair is scorched.

And … not … zefet … zefet … pitch, … sha’ava … wax. It was taught … Until this point, … disqualification … wicks, … from this point on … disqualification … oils. … Obviously, … It was necessary … wax, lest you say … also unfit for use … for wicks, … Therefore, it teaches us
Rami bar Avin said: Tar [itran] … by-product of pitch. … wax … by-product of honey.
What … practical difference … to buying and selling.

The Sages taught … all of those … which they said … one may not light … with them on Shabbat; however, one may … them … to make a bonfire. … both to warm himself opposite it and to utilize its light, … both on the ground and on a stove. They prohibited … them only to make a wick for an oil lamp.

And … one may not … with kik oil. … What is kik oil? Shmuel said: I asked all the seafarers, and they said to me … there is a bird in the cities on the sea … and kik is its name. … Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rav Yehuda, said: … cotton oil. Reish Lakish said: … castor plant [kikayon] of Jonah. Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: I have seen … castor plant of Jonah, and it is similar to the ricinus tree and it grows in swamps, and they place it at the entrance of shops … and they produce oil from its seeds, and all the sick people of the West, … rest … its branches.

Rabba said: … wicks … which the Sages said one may not light with them on Shabbat, … Because the fire flickers on them. … oils with which the Sages said … one may not light … Because they are not drawn … by the wick.

Abaye raised a dilemma before Rabba: … oils with which the Sages said one may not light on Shabbat, what … add to them any amount of oil … and light … Do we issue a decree lest one come to light … in their natural form, … Or … not … said to him: One may not light … What is the reason … because … one may not light

objection … One who wrapped a material with which one may light around a material with which one may not light, may not light with … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: In the … house of … father, they would wrap a wick … around a nut, and … light. In any case, it is teaching … one may light.

said to him: Before you raise an objection to my … from … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, support it from … first tanna, … not difficult, … an action is great, … Nevertheless, the difficulty … Is he not … to light … No, … to float … If … floating … what is the reason … first tanna … entire … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and … incomplete, and it teaches the following: One who wrapped a material with which one may light around a material with which one may not light, may not light with it. In what … this statement said? … to light … However, … to float … it is permitted, … that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: In the … house of … father, they would wrap a wick … around a nut.

Is that so? Didn’t Rav Beruna say … Rav said: … molten fat … fish innards that dissolved … a person may place any amount of oil … into it and light. … These, … are drawn by the wick … in their natural state, and those, … are not drawn in their natural state. … the Sages issued a decree … molten fat due to unmolten fat and … dissolved fish innards due to undissolved fish innards; … Let them also issue a decree … molten fat and … fish innards to which he added oil due to molten fat and dissolved fish innards to which he did not add … oil. … That … itself is … a decree. And … we arise and issue … decree … of … decree?

Rami bar Ḥama taught … wicks and oils, which the Sages said one may not light with them on Shabbat, one may not light … in the Temple … because it is stated … to cause a lamp to burn continually” … taught that … and he … said its … so that the flame ascends of itself … and not that it ascends by means of something else,
We learned … They would unravel the … tattered trousers of … priests and their belts … and from … light … The Celebration of Drawing Water is different,
Come … hear … Rabba bar Mattana taught: Priestly garments that were tattered, they would unravel them … from which they would make wicks for the Temple. Is this not … diverse kinds, … No, … linen

Rav Huna said: … wicks and oils with which the Sages said … one may not light … on Shabbat, one may not light … with them on Hanukkah … both … on Shabbat and … during the week. Rava said: What is the reason … Rav Huna’s … He holds … becomes extinguished, … one is bound … And utilizing the light … is permitted … And Rav Ḥisda said: … one may light with them … during the week, but not on Shabbat. He holds

one is not bound … to it. … it is permitted to use its light. … Rabbi Zeira said … Rav Mattana said, and others say … Rabbi Zeira said … Rav said: The wicks and oils with which the Sages said one may not light on Shabbat, one may, … light with them on Hanukkah, both during the week and on Shabbat. Rabbi Yirmeya said: What is Rav’s reason? He holds … it is extinguished, one is not bound … to it … and it is prohibited to use its light.

the Sages said this … before Abaye in the name of Rabbi Yirmeya and he did not accept it, … when Ravin came … the Sages said … before Abaye in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan, and he accepted it. … said … Had I merited, I would have learned this halakha from the outset. … Didn’t he … learn it … The practical difference … knowledge … youth,

And … is extinguished one is not bound … to it? … raises a contradiction … The mitzva … is from sunset until traffic in the marketplace ceases. Does that not … that if … is extinguished, he … rekindle it … No, … That if one did not … light … he … light … Alternatively, … its measure.
until traffic in the marketplace ceases … Until when … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Until … traffic of … Tadmor [tarmoda’ei] ceases.

The Sages taught … The … mitzva of Hanukkah … a light … a person, … and his household. And the mehadrin, … a light for each and every one … And the mehadrin min hamehadrin, … Beit Shammai say: … the first day one kindles eight … there on, gradually decreases … And Beit Hillel say: … the first day one kindles one … there on, gradually increases

Ulla said: … two amora’im in the West, … disagreed … this … Rabbi Yosei bar Avin and Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida. One said … the reason … Beit Shammai’s … corresponds to the incoming days, … The reason … Beit Hillel’s … corresponds to the outgoing days. … And one said … the reason … Beit Shammai’s … corresponds to the bulls of the festival … The reason … Beit Hillel’s … One elevates … in … sanctity and one does not downgrade.

Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: There were two Elders in Sidon, … one … acted … Beit Shammai, and one … acted in accordance with … Beit Hillel. … One gave a reason for his actions: … corresponds to the bulls of the Festival. And one gave a reason for his actions: … One elevates … in … sanctity and one does not downgrade.

The Sages taught … It is a mitzva to place the Hanukkah lamp at the entrance to one’s house on the outside, … If he lived upstairs, he places it at the window adjacent to the public domain. And in a time of danger, … he places it on the table and … sufficient … his
Rava said: … must … another light … in order to use its light, … And if there is a bonfire, he need not … if he is an important person, … even though there is a bonfire, he must … another light.

What is Hanukkah, … The Sages taught … On the twenty-fifth of Kislev, the days of Hanukkah are eight. One may not eulogize on them and one may not fast on them. … When the Greeks entered the Sanctuary they defiled all the oils that were in the Sanctuary … And when the Hasmonean monarchy overcame … and emerged victorious over them, they searched and found only one cruse of oil that was placed with the seal of the High Priest, … And there was … there to light … only one day. A miracle occurred and they lit … from it eight days. The next year … instituted … and made them holidays with … hallel and … thanksgiving

We learned there … a spark that emerges from under a hammer, and went out … and caused damage, … liable. … a camel that is laden with flax and … passed … the public domain, and its flax entered into a store, and caught fire from the storekeeper’s lamp, and set fire to the building, the camel owner is liable. … storekeeper placed his lamp outside … the storekeeper is liable,

Rabbi Yehuda says: … by the … Hanukkah lamp … he is not liable, … Ravina said in the name of Rabba: That is to say … mitzva to place … Hanukkah lamp within ten … As if it should enter your mind … above ten handbreadths, … Let … say to … You should have placed … above … of a camel and its rider, … And perhaps … if you burden … excessively, he will come to refrain from … mitzva
Rav Kahana said … Rav Natan bar Manyumi taught in the name … Rabbi Tanḥum:

A Hanukkah lamp that one placed above twenty cubits is invalid, just as … sukka … and just as an alleyway … And … Rav Kahana said … Rav Natan bar Manyumi taught in the name … Rav Tanḥum: What … that is written … and the pit was empty, there was no water in it” … By inference from that which is stated: And the pit was empty, don’t I know that there was no water in it? Rather, why does the verse say: There was no water in it? … there was no water in it, but there were snakes and scorpions in it.

Rabba said: It is a mitzva to place the Hanukkah lamp within the handbreadth adjacent to the entrance. … And where, … does he place it? … Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said: On … right … Rav Shmuel from Difti said: On … left. And the halakha is … on the left so that the Hanukkah lamp will be on the left and the mezuza on the right.

Rav Yehuda said … Rav Asi said … Rav said: It is prohibited to count money opposite a Hanukkah light. … When I said this … before Shmuel, he said to me: Does the Hanukkah light have sanctity … Rav Yosef strongly objected to this … does the blood … have sanctity? As it was taught … He shall spill … and cover … With that which he spilled, he shall cover. … not cover it with his foot. … that mitzvot will not be contemptible to him. Here too, … mitzvot will not be contemptible to him.

they raised a dilemma before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: What … using decorations of a sukka all seven … He said to them: They … said … it is prohibited to count money opposite the Hanukkah light, … Rav Yosef … Master … Abraham! He makes … which was taught dependent upon … which was not taught. As, … sukka, … was taught … Hanukkah … was not taught … As it was taught … one who roofed … in accordance with its halakhic … and decorated it with colorful curtains and sheets, and hung in it … nuts, peaches, almonds, and pomegranates, and grape branches [parkilei], and wreaths of stalks … wines, oils, and … flour, it is prohibited to use them until the conclusion of the last day of the Festival. And, if … he stipulated with regard to them … everything is according to his stipulation, … Rather, Rav Yosef said: … the paradigm of them all is blood.

It was stated … Rav said: One may not light from … lamp to … lamp. And Shmuel said: One may light … Rav said: One may not untie ritual fringes from … garment … to … garment. And Shmuel said: One may untie … from one garment … to … garment. … Rav said: The halakha is not in accordance … Rabbi Shimon in … dragging, … Shmuel said … halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon in … dragging.

Abaye said: … all … matters of the Master, … he conducted himself in accordance with … Rav, except these three where he conducted himself in accordance with … Shmuel. … One may light from … lamp to … lamp, and one may untie … from garment to garment, and the halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon in … dragging. As it was taught … Rabbi Shimon says: A person may drag a bed, chair, and bench … as long as he does not intend to make a furrow

One of the Sages sat before Rav Adda bar Ahava, and he sat and said: The reason … Rav, … due to contempt for the mitzva. … said to … Do not listen to him, … the reason … Rav’s … due to … that he … weakens the mitzva. … What is the … between them? … between them … where he lights … from lamp to lamp, … one who said … is due to contempt for the mitzva, … from lamp to lamp he may … light … one who said … is because he weakens the mitzva, … from lamp to lamp is also prohibited,
Rav Avya raised an objection … A sela of

He said to him: Ask, my son, ask. … Why are the eyes of the residents of Tadmor bleary [terutot]? … said to him: My son, you have asked a significant question. … because they live among the sands

went, waited one hour, returned, and said: Who here is Hillel, who here is Hillel? … he, … wrapped himself and went out to greet him. He said to him: My son, what do you seek? He said to him: I have a question to ask. He said to him: Ask, my son, ask. … Why do Africans have wide feet? … said to him: You have asked a significant question. … because they live in marshlands

said to him: I have many … questions to ask, but I am afraid lest you get angry. … wrapped himself and sat before him, … he said to him: All of … questions that you have to ask, ask … said to him: Are you Hillel whom they call … Nasi of Israel? He said to him: Yes. He said to him: If … is you, … may there not be many like you in Israel. … said to him: My son, for what … said to him: Because I lost four hundred zuz because of you. … said to him: Be vigilant of your spirit … Hillel is worthy of having you lose four hundred zuz and … four hundred zuz on his account, and Hillel will not get upset.

The Sages taught: … an incident involving one gentile who came before Shammai. … said to Shammai: How many Torahs do you have? He said to him: Two, the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. … said to him: … the Written … I believe you, but … the Oral … I do not believe you. Convert me on condition that you will teach me … Written Torah. … scolded him and cast him out with reprimand. … came before Hillel, … converted him … On the first day, he … said to him: Alef, bet, gimmel, dalet. The next day he reversed … said to him: But yesterday you did not tell me that. … said to him: … Didn’t you rely on me? … also rely on me … of the Oral

another incident involving one gentile who came before Shammai … said to … Convert me on condition that you teach me the entire Torah while I am standing on one foot. … pushed him … with the builder’s cubit in his hand. … came before Hillel. He converted him … said to him: … which is hateful to you do not do to another; that is the entire Torah, and the rest is its interpretation. Go study.

another incident involving one gentile who was passing behind the study hall … heard the voice of a teacher who was … saying … “And these are the garments which they shall make: A breastplate, and an efod, … The gentile said: These … for whom are they … said to him: For the High Priest. The gentile said to himself: I will go and convert so that they will install me as High Priest. He came before Shammai … said to him: Convert me on condition that you install me … pushed him with the builder’s cubit in his hand. He came before Hillel; he converted him.

said to him, … Is it not … only one who knows the protocols [takhsisei] … is appointed king? Go … learn the royal protocols … He went and read … When he reached … “And the common man that draws near shall be put to death” … said to … With regard to whom is the verse speaking? … said to him: Even with regard to David, king of Israel. The convert reasoned an a fortiori inference himself: If the Jewish people are called God’s children, and due to the love that God loved them he called them: “Israel is My son, My firstborn” … it is written about them: And the common man that draws near shall be put to death; a mere convert who came … with … his staff and traveling bag, all the more so

came before Shammai … told him … Am I at all worthy to be High Priest? Is it not written in the Torah: And the common man that draws near shall be put to death? He came before Hillel … said to him: Hillel the patient, may blessings rest upon your head as you brought me under the wings of the Divine Presence. … Eventually, the three … gathered together … one place, … they said: Shammai’s impatience sought to drive us from the world; Hillel’s patience brought us beneath the wings of the Divine Presence.

Reish Lakish said: What … that which is written: “And the faith of your times shall be a strength of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge, … Faith; that is the order of Zera’im, Seeds, … Your times; that is the order of Moed, Festival, … Strength; that is the order of Nashim, Women. Salvations; that is the order of Nezikin, Damages, … Wisdom; that is the order of Kodashim, Consecrated Items. And knowledge; that is the order of Teharot, Purity, … And even … “the fear of the Lord is his treasure,”

Rava said: … when a person is brought to judgment … they say to him … you conduct business faithfully? … you designate times for Torah … you engage in procreation? Did you await salvation? Did you engage … wisdom … one matter from another? And, nevertheless, … if the fear of the Lord is his treasure, yes, … if not, no, … a parable … A person who said to his emissary: Bring a kor of wheat up to the attic for me … went and brought it up for him. He said to the emissary: … you mix a kav of ḥomton, … into it for me? He said to him: No. He said to him: … preferable had you not brought it up.
taught … the school … Rabbi Yishmael: A person … may, … mix a kav of ḥomton into a kor of grain and need not be concerned
Rabba bar Rav Huna said: Any person who has Torah in him but does not have

fear of Heaven … like a treasurer [gizbar] to whom they gave keys to the inner doors … but they did not give keys … outer … With what … will he enter? … Rabbi Yannai … proclaim: Woe unto … who does not have a courtyard, and who makes a fence for the courtyard, … Rav Yehuda said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, only created His world so that people would fear before Him, … it is stated: “And God has so made it that men should fear before Him”

Rabbi Simon and Rabbi Elazar were sitting. Rabbi Ya’akov bar Aḥa passed and went … One said to the other: Let us stand before him as he is a man who fears sin. The other said to him … Let us stand before him, as he is a man of Torah … He said … I said to you that he is a man who fears sin, and you said me … he is a man of Torah

Conclude that Rabbi Elazar is … one who said … because he is a man who fears sin, … As Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: The Holy One, Blessed be He, has in His world only fear of Heaven alone, as it is stated: “And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you, but to fear … ( … And it is written: “And unto man He said: Behold [hen], the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom; … as in the Greek language they call one hen. … conclude

Rav Ulla taught: What … that which is written: “Be not overmuch wicked” … overmuch one should not be wicked; a little, one should be wicked? Rather, … One who ate … garlic and its odor spreads, … he again eat … garlic so that its odor will spread

Rava bar Rav Ulla taught: What … that which is written: “For there are no pangs [ḥartzubot] at their death and their body is sound” … The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: Is it not enough for wicked people that they are not anxious [ḥared] or sad [atzuv], … of the day of … death, but … their heart is as unyielding for them as … hall … And that is … Rabba said: What is … that which is written: “This is the way of them that are foolish … wicked know that their path … to … death, … they have fat on their kidneys … Lest you say that it is … forgotten from them; … the verse states: “And of those who after them speak approvingly, Selah”

spare the lamp, … Rabbi Yosei: In accordance with whose … does he hold … If he holds in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, … even in … those … he should also deem … liable. And if he holds in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon, … a wick he should also deem … exempt. Ulla said: Actually, … holds in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda. However, Rabbi Yosei holds … he dismantles in order to rebuild in the same place, … it is considered … dismantling, … in order to build elsewhere it is not considered … dismantling.

Rabba said to him: … After all, all labors … we derive them from … and there it was … dismantling in order to build elsewhere. … said to … there, … it is different. Since it is written: “At the commandment of the Lord they encamped” … it was tantamount to demolishing in order to build in the same place.

And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Actually, … holds in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon. And … what is different … a wick, … as Rav Hamnuna said, and some say, Rav Adda bar Ahava … Here, we are dealing with a wick that one must singe … as, in that … even Rabbi Shimon agrees … as, … he prepares a vessel … Rava said: … also precise … as it was taught … because he makes … charcoal … and it was not taught because charcoal was made … Conclude from it
MISHNA: … For three transgressions women … die during childbirth: For … that they are not careful in … a menstruating woman, … in … ḥalla … and in lighting … lamp.

GEMARA: … menstruation, what is the reason … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: She sinned with … the chambers of her womb; therefore, she is afflicted in the chambers of her womb. … Granted, … menstruation; … ḥalla and in kindling the Shabbat lights, what is there to say? … in accordance with that which that Galilean taught before Rav Ḥisda. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: I placed a quarter [revi’it] … of blood in you … about matters of … blood … I warned you.

I called you first, … and I warned you about matters of the first: … The soul that I have placed in you is called ner: … I warned you about matters of the … lamp. If you fulfill these … fine, and if not, then I will take your soul.

And, … what is different during childbirth? … Rava said: … the ox fell, sharpen the knife … Abaye said: … the maidservant’s insolence abounds, she will be struck by a single blow … Rav Ḥisda said: Leave the drunk, as … falls on his own. … Mar Ukva said: The shepherd is crippled, and the goats are running, … next to the gate, … words, and inside the pen … account. … Rav Pappa said: At the entrance to the stores, … brothers and loved ones abound. … at the gate of disgrace, … no brothers and no loved ones;

And where … men examined? … Reish Lakish said: When they are crossing a bridge. … a bridge and at no other … say: … like a bridge, … Rav would not cross … in a ferry in which a gentile sat. He said … Perhaps a judgment will be reckoned with him, and I will be caught together with him … Shmuel would only cross in a ferry if there was a gentile in it. He said: Satan does not have dominion over two nations.

Rabbi Yannai would examine … and cross. … Rabbi Yannai … in accordance with his reasoning … he said: A person should never stand in a place of danger saying that they … will perform a miracle for him, lest … they do not perform a miracle for him. And, … if they do perform a miracle for him, they will deduct it from his merits. Rabbi Ḥanin said: What is the verse … “I am not worthy of all the mercies, and of all the truth, … Rabbi Zeira would not go out … among the palm trees on a day when there was a southern wind

Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rav Yehuda, said: A person should always pray that he will not become ill, as if he becomes ill they say to him: Bring … virtue and exempt yourself. … Mar Ukva said: What is the verse … if the fallen falls mimenu” … Mimenu, from him proof must be brought. … The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: … If the fallen falls from it? This … was destined to fall … from the six days of Creation, … As, … he did not … fall, the verse calls him fallen. Nevertheless, … merit is engendered by means of … innocent and guilt by means of … guilty.

The Sages taught: One who became ill and tended toward death, they say to him: Confess, as all those executed … confess. … a person goes out to the marketplace … he should consider himself as someone who has been handed over to a soldier [seradiyot]. … his head hurt, he should consider it as if they placed him in a chain [kolar] … he climbed into bed and fell ill, he should consider himself as if they took him up to the gallows to be judged, as … anyone who goes up to the gallows to be judged, if he has great advocates [peraklitin], he is spared, and if not, he is not spared.

And … these are a person’s advocates: Repentance and good deeds. … And even … nine hundred ninety-nine asserting his guilt and … one … innocence, he is spared, … it is stated: “If there be for him an angel, an advocate, one among a thousand, to vouch for a man’s uprightness; then He is gracious unto him, and says: Deliver him from going down to the pit, … Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says: Even … nine hundred ninety-nine … within that same angel accusing … and one … his innocence, he is spared, as it stated: “An advocate, one among a thousand.”

The Sages taught … For three transgressions women die in childbirth [yoledot]. Rabbi Elazar … says … women die … young [yeladot]. … Rabbi Aḥa says … for the sin of laundering their children’s feces … on Shabbat. And some say: Because they call the Holy Ark … ark.

we learned … Rabbi Yishmael ben Elazar says: On account of two sins, ignoramuses [amei ha’aretz] die … Because they call the Holy Ark … ark, and because they call the synagogue the house of the people. It was taught … Rabbi Yosei says: Three crucibles … death were created in the woman, and some say: Three accelerants of death. … Menstruation, ḥalla, and lighting the Shabbat lights. … one … in accordance with … Rabbi Elazar, … And … one, … in accordance with … the Rabbis,
it was taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel says: The halakhot of consecrated items, terumot, and tithes are themselves … essence of Torah
and they were given, … to ignoramuses

It was taught … Rabbi Natan says: Due to the sin of vows … a person’s wife dies. … as it is stated: “If you have not the wherewithal to pay, why should He take away your bed from under you?” … Rabbi … says: Due to the sin of vows … children die when they are young, as it is stated: … Suffer not your mouth to bring your flesh into guilt, neither say you before the messenger that it was an error; wherefore should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?” … What is the work of a person’s hands? You must say … a person’s sons and daughters.

the Sages taught … For the sin of vows, one’s children die, … the statement of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: For the sin of dereliction in … Torah. … Granted, according to … the one who said … due to the sin of vows, as we stated … However, according to the … the one who said … due to sin of dereliction in … Torah, what is the verse … As it is written: “In vain have I smitten your children; they received no morality” … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: According to the one who said … because of the sin of vows, it can also … from here: In vain have I smitten your children; on matters of vanity, … After all, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi is Rabbi, and … Rabbi said … because of the sin of vows. … After he heard it from Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon,

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Yosei disagree. One said … due to the sin of … mezuza … And one said … due to the sin of dereliction in … Torah. According to the one who said … because of the sin of … mezuza, … a verse is interpreted homiletically … preceding it and not … before the one preceding it. … And according to the one who said … the sin of dereliction in … Torah, … a verse is interpreted homiletically … preceding it, as well as … before the one preceding it.

Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda … disagreed about this. One said: … due to the sin of mezuza, and one said … due to the sin of … ritual fringes. … Granted, … to … the one who said … due to the sin of mezuza, … as it is written: “And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your house, … and it says thereafter: “ … hat your days may be multiplied, and the days of your children.” However, according to the one who said … because of the sin of ritual fringes, what is the reason? … Rav Kahana said, and some say … Sheila Mari: … as is written: “Also in your corners is found the blood of the souls of the innocent poor” … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: According to the one who said … because of the sin of mezuza, it is also … from here, as it is written … “You did not find them breaking in; … because they made entrances like a … breach

Reish Lakish said: Anyone who is vigilant in … ritual fringes merits … two thousand eight hundred servants will serve him … As it is stated: “Thus says the Lord of hosts: In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold, out of all the languages of the nations, shall even take hold of the corner of the garment of him that is a Jew, saying: We will go with you,

a mnemonic … Hate, ḥalla, teruma, stolen, judgment, oath, pouring, uncovering, and vulgarity. It was taught … Rabbi Neḥemya says: Due to the sin of gratuitous hatred … great discord within a person’s home, and his wife miscarries, and his sons and daughters die when they are young. Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said: Due to the sin … ḥalla … no blessing takes effect on the … gathered … and a curse spreads to the prices … and they plant seeds and others eat … as it is stated: “I also will do this unto you: I will appoint terror [behala] over you, even consumption and fever, that shall make the eyes to fail and the soul to languish; and you shall sow your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it” … Do not read … behala; rather, … beḥalla. … And if they give … they are blessed, as it is stated: “And the first of your dough you shall give unto the priest to cause a blessing to rest on your house”

Due to the sin of abrogation of terumot and tithes, the heavens are prevented from pouring down dew and rain, and expense prevails, and profit is lost, and people pursue their livelihood but do not attain … as it is stated: “Drought and heat consume the snow waters; so does the netherworld those that have sinned” … What is the inference? … The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught … Due to … things that I commanded you during the summer, … and you did not do … the snow waters will be robbed from you during the rainy season. And if … give … they are blessed, as it is stated: “Bring you the whole tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in My house, and try Me now with this, says the Lord of Hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall be more than sufficiency [ad bli dai]” … What … More than sufficiency [ad bli dai]? Rami bar Rav said … Rav said: … that your lips will be worn out [yivlu], … from saying enough [dai].

Due to the sin of robbery, locusts emerge, and famine prevails, and people eat the flesh of their sons and daughters, … it is stated: “Hear this word, you cows of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria, that oppress the poor, that crush the needy, … Rava said: … like those women of … Meḥoza,

who eat and do nothing … And it is written: “I have smitten you with blight and mildew; the multitude of your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees has the palmerworm devoured” … And it is written: “That which the palmerworm has left the locust has eaten; and that which the locust has left the cankerworm has eaten; and that which the cankerworm has left the caterpillar has eaten” … And it is written: “And one snatches on the right hand, and is hungry; and he eats on the left hand, and is not satisfied; they eat every man the flesh of his own arm [besar zero’o]” … Do not read … The flesh of his own arm [besar zero’o]; rather, the flesh of his own offspring [besar zaro].

due to the sin of delay of justice, … and … distortion of justice, … and … miscarriage of justice … and … dereliction in … Torah, violence and looting abound … and pestilence and famine come, and people eat and are not sated, and they eat their bread … by weight. As it is written: “And I will bring a sword upon you, that shall execute the vengeance of the covenant; … And covenant means nothing other than Torah, as it is stated: “If My covenant be not with day and night, … And it is written … “When I break your staff of bread, ten women shall bake … And it is written: “Even because they rejected My ordinances,

Due to the sin of an oath … in vain and a false oath, and desecration of … name, and desecration of Shabbat, wild beasts abound … and … animals cease … and human beings decrease … and the roads become desolate, as it is stated: “And if in spite of these [be’eleh] things you will not be corrected unto Me, … Do not read of these [be’eleh]; rather, … oath [be’ala]. And it is written … “And I will send the beast of the field among you, … And it is written with regard to a false oath: “And you shall not swear by My name falsely, so that you desecrate [veḥillalta] the name of your God: … And it is written with regard to desecrating the name of God: “And you shall not desecrate [teḥallelu] My Holy Name” … And it is written with regard to desecrating Shabbat: “Every one that desecrates it [meḥaleleha] shall surely be put to death” … And derive … desecration [ḥillul] of Shabbat from desecration [ḥillul] of a false oath.

Due to the sin of bloodshed, the Holy Temple is destroyed, and the Divine Presence leaves Israel, as it says: “So you shall not pollute … And you shall not defile the land which you inhabit, in the midst of which I dwell; … you defile … you will not inhabit it, and I will not dwell in it.

Due to the sin of prohibited sexual relations, and idol worship, and … lie fallow … the Sabbatical and Jubilee Years, exile comes to the world and they exile … and others come and settle in their place. As it is stated … “For all these abominations have the men of the land done, … And it is written: “And the land was defiled, therefore I did visit the iniquity thereof upon it, … And it is written: “That the land expel not you also, when you defile it,
And with regard to idol worship it is written: “And I will cast your carcasses … And it is written: “And I will bring your sanctuaries unto desolation, … “And you will I scatter among the nations,

With regard to … the Sabbatical and Jubilee Years it is written: “Then shall the land be paid her Sabbaths, as long as it lies desolate, and you are in your enemies’ land; … And it is written: “As long as it lies desolate it shall have rest; … (

Due to the sin of vulgar speech, troubles abound, and harsh decrees are renewed, and the youth among the enemies of Israel, … die, … orphans and widows cry out … and are not answered, as it is stated: “Therefore the Lord shall have no joy in their young men, neither shall He have compassion on their fatherless and widows; for everyone is ungodly and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks wantonness. For all this His anger is not turned away, but His hand is stretched out still”

What … But His hand is stretched out still? Rabbi Ḥanan bar Rava said: Everybody knows why the bride enters the wedding canopy. … Nevertheless, anyone who speaks vulgarly … even if they, … sealed for him a decree of seventy years of good … , they will reverse it to bad … Rabba bar Sheila said … Rav Ḥisda said: Anyone who speaks vulgarly, they deepen Gehenna for him, as it is stated: “The mouth that speaks perversity is a deep pit … ” … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: Even … who hears … and is silent … as it is stated: “He that is abhorred of the Lord shall fall therein,”

Rav Oshaya said: Anyone who … himself to … a sin, wounds and bruises emerge on him, as it is stated: “Sharp wounds for one devoted to evil … And not only that, but … is sentenced to … edema [hidrokan], as it is stated: So do stripes that reach the inward parts. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: A sign … committed … hidrokan,
The Sages taught … There are three types of hidrokan: … for sin … thick; and … of hunger is swollen … and … by witchcraft … thin,

Shmuel HaKatan fell ill with … He said: Master of the Universe, who will draw lots, … He was cured. Abaye … fell ill with … Rava … said … I know about Naḥmani, … that … starves himself … Rava fell ill with … But Rava … he … said: More have been killed … chamber pot … than those swollen … starvation. … Rava is different because the Sages compel him … against his will while he
the Sages taught … there are four signs: A sign of sin is hidrokan, a sign of gratuitous hatred is jaundice, a sign of arrogance is poverty, … a sign of slander is askara.
The Sages taught: Askara comes to the world

for … tithes. Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, says: … slander. Rava said, and some say … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi … What is the verse … “But the king shall rejoice in God; every one that swears by Him shall glory; for the mouth of them that speak lies shall be stopped”

A dilemma was raised before … Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, say … for slander, or perhaps he said … also for slander? Come … hear … When our Sages entered the vineyard in Yavne, Rabbi Yehuda, and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Shimon were there, and a question was asked before them … this plague … Why does it begin in the intestines and end in the mouth? Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Ila’i, … the head of the speakers in every place, responded and said: Even though the kidneys advise, and the heart understands, and the tongue shapes … the mouth completes … Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, responded and said: … because one eats with it non-kosher things. … Does it enter your mind … non-kosher food? … Rather, … for eating … that were not … prepared, … Rabbi Shimon responded and said: … for the sin of dereliction in … Torah.

They said to him: Women will prove … they cause their husbands to be idle … Gentiles will prove … they cause Israel to be idle … Children will prove … they cause their fathers to be idle … School children will prove

There … in accordance with … Rabbi Guryon, … Rabbi Guryon said, and some say … Rav Yosef, son of Rabbi Shemaya, … At a time when … righteous people in the generation, … righteous are seized … for … the generation. If there are no righteous people in the generation, school children, … are seized for … the generation … Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Ze’iri said, and some say … Rabbi Shimon ben Nezira said: What is the verse … “If you know not, you fairest among women, go your way forth by the footsteps of the flock … ” ( … And we say … lambs that are taken as collateral [hamemushkanin], … in place of the shepherds. … conclude from it … said … also … slander, … conclude from it.

And why did they call him head of the speakers in every place? … when Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon were sitting, and Yehuda, son of converts, sat beside them. Rabbi Yehuda opened and said: How pleasant are the actions of this nation, … they established marketplaces, established bridges, … established bathhouses. Rabbi Yosei was silent. Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai responded and said: Everything that they established, they established only for their own purposes. They established marketplaces, to place prostitutes in them; bathhouses, to pamper themselves; … bridges, to collect taxes from … them. Yehuda, son of converts, went and related their statements … and … they were heard by the monarchy. They … said: Yehuda, who elevated … shall be elevated … Yosei, who remained silent, shall be exiled … to … Tzippori … And Shimon, who denounced … shall be killed.

and his son, … went … hid in the study hall. Every day … wife would bring them bread and a jug of water and they would eat. When the decree intensified, … said to his son: Women are easily impressionable … lest … torture her and she reveal our … They went and they hid in a cave. A miracle occurred … a carob … was created for them as well as a spring of water. They would remove their clothes and sit … in sand up to their necks … They would study … all day … At the time of prayer, they would dress, cover themselves, and pray, and they would again remove their clothes afterward so that they would not become tattered. They sat in the cave for twelve years. Elijah … came and stood at the entrance to the cave … said: Who will inform bar Yoḥai that … emperor died and his decree has been abrogated?

They emerged … saw people who were plowing and sowing. … said: … abandon eternal life … and engage in temporal life … every place that … directed their eyes was immediately burned. A Divine Voice emerged and said to them: … you emerge … to destroy My world? Return to your cave. They again went … sat … for twelve months. They said: The judgment of the wicked in Gehenna lasts … twelve months. … A Divine Voice emerged and said … Emerge from your cave. They emerged. Everywhere that Rabbi Elazar would strike, Rabbi Shimon would heal. … said to … My son, you and I suffice for the … world,

As the sun was setting on Shabbat eve, they saw an elderly man who was holding two bundles of myrtle branches and running at twilight. They said to him: Why do you have these? He said to them: In honor of Shabbat. … And let one suffice. … One … corresponding to: “Remember … and … corresponding to: “Observe … said to his son: See how beloved the mitzvot are to Israel. Their minds were … at ease

Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir, … son-in-law … heard and went out to … him. He brought him into the bathhouse and … tending to his flesh. He saw that … had cracks in … his body. He was crying, and the tears fell from his eyes and caused … pain. … said to … Woe is me, that I have seen you like this. … said to him: Happy are you that you have seen me like this, as had you not seen me like this, you would not have found in me this … as … At first, when Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai would raise a difficulty, Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir would respond … twelve answers. Ultimately, when Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir would raise a difficulty … Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai would respond … twenty-four answers.
