That was also taught … A donkey may go out … with its saddlecloth when it was tied to … from Shabbat eve, and … not … with the saddle, even though it was tied to … from Shabbat eve. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: … even … with its saddle when it was tied to … from Shabbat eve, provided that he does not tie … strap … and provided that he does not pass a strap under … tail,

Rav Asi bar Natan raised a dilemma before Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav Ashi: What is … placing a saddlecloth on a donkey on Shabbat … said to him: It is permitted. … said to him: What is the difference between this and a saddle … remained silent

He, … raised an objection … A saddle that is on a donkey … he may not move it with his hand … rather, he walks … back and forth in the courtyard, and … falls on its own. Now … to removing … you said no, … from placing … necessary?

Rabbi Zeira said to … Leave … he agrees with his teacher. As Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said … Rav said: One may hang a basket … around … an animal on Shabbat, and … a fortiori … , … a saddlecloth … Just as there, … which is … for … pleasure, is permitted … here, … which is … suffering … all the more so

Shmuel said: A saddlecloth is permitted; … a basket … is prohibited. Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef went and said the halakha of Rav before Shmuel. … said to him: If Abba, … said that, he knows nothing at all about matters of Shabbat.

When Rabbi Zeira ascended … he found Rabbi Binyamin bar Yefet who sat and said to him in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: One may place a saddlecloth on a donkey on Shabbat. … said to him: … well, and Aryokh explained … likewise in Babylonia.
Who is Aryokh? … Shmuel. Didn’t Rav also say … Rather, he heard … conclude: However, one may not hang a basket … on Shabbat. … well … and Aryokh explained … likewise in Babylonia.
In any case, everyone agrees that a saddlecloth is permitted. … How is … different from a saddle, … It is different there, as it is possible for … to fall on its own.
Rav Pappa said: … Here, … to warm … There, … to cool … to warm … it … discomfort … to cool … does not … discomfort … And that is … that people say: A donkey, even in the … season of Tammuz, is cold.

raises an objection … A horse may neither go out … with a fox’s tail … nor with … red wool that is … between its eyes … Neither may a zav go out with his pouch … nor goats with a pouch that is on their udders … nor a cow with the muzzle that is on its mouth, nor foals with baskets … that are around their mouths into the public domain. And an animal … neither … with … shoes that are on its feet, nor with an amulet … even if … has proven effective. And this is a stricture … to animals beyond … to people,

However, … may go out with a bandage that is on a wound, and with splints that are on a broken bone … and with the afterbirth hanging … And one may plug the bell … from … neck … and … may walk with it in the courtyard,

In any case, it is taught … Nor foals with baskets … that are around their mouths into the public domain. … into the public domain … not … however, in a courtyard, … well … What? Is it not … to large … for … pleasure?
No … to small … and … to … discomfort. … This is also precise … as it teaches
similar to … an amulet … learn from it

The Master said: Nor … with an amulet … even if … proved effective. … Didn’t we learn … not … with an amulet that has not proved effective? … proved effective, … well … Here too … that has not proved effective.

Doesn’t … teach: Even if … proved effective? … proved effective for a person, and did not prove effective for an animal. … Is there … proved effective for a person and is not effective for an animal? … Yes, … aids a person, who is under … an … angel [mazal]; … it does not aid an animal, which is not under … an … angel.
If so, … what … And this is a stricture … to animals beyond … to people? … Do you hold … this … is referring to an amulet? It is referring to a shoe;

Come … hear … One may smear … oil and scrape … for a person, and one may not smear … oil and scrape … for an animal. Is it not … where there is a wound, and … and … due to … discomfort … No, … where the wound has … ceased … due to … pleasure

Come … hear … an animal … congestion … blood … one may not stand it in water so that it will cool … a person … congestion … blood … one … stand him in water so that he will cool … Ulla said: … a decree … due to the crushing of herbs
If so, … also … a person. … a person, it appears as … to cool
If so … an animal as well … it appears as … to cool … , … An animal … not … cool
Do we … issue a decree for an animal? Wasn’t it taught … were standing beyond the … limit, … he may call … and it will come … And we do not issue a decree … lest he come to bring it
And Ravina said: … where … limit was subsumed within … limit

Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: … crushing herbs is itself … the tanna’im. As it was taught … an animal that ate vetch, … one may not run it … in the courtyard to loosen … Rabbi Oshaya deems … permitted. … Rava taught: … halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Oshaya.
The Master said: Neither may a zav go out with his pouch, … nor goats with the pouch that is on their udders. … Wasn’t it taught … Goats may go out with the pouch that is on their udders?
Rav Yehuda said: … not difficult. This … that is … tightly … That … that is not tightly

Rav Yosef said: Have you removed the tanna’im from the world? … the tanna’im … as we learned … She-goats may go out … bound. Rabbi Yosei Rabbi Yosei prohibits … with all … these … except for the ewes that are kevunot. Rabbi Yehuda says: Goats may go out … bound to dry … However, … not … to … milk,
And if you wish, say … this … and that … in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, and … not difficult. Here, … to dry … There, … to … the milk
It was taught … Rabbi Yehuda said: … an incident involving the goats … a house in Antioch whose udders were … large … And they made pouches for them so that their udders would not get scratched.

Sages taught: … an incident where one … wife died, and she left … a son to nurse … and he did not have … the wages of a wet-nurse. And a miracle was performed on his behalf, and he developed breasts like the two breasts of a woman, and he nursed his son.

Rav Yosef said: Come and see how great this person is that a miracle … that … was performed on his behalf. Abaye said to him: On the contrary, how dishonorable is this person that the order of creation was altered on his behalf.

Rav Yehuda … said: Come and see how difficult … a person’s sustenance. … that the order of creation had to be altered on … behalf, … Rav Naḥman said: Know … as miracles are … performed … however, … not … food was … created

The Sages taught: … an incident involving one man who married a one-armed woman, and he did not realize … until the day that she died. Rav said: Come and see how modest this woman was that her husband did not realize … about her. Rabbi Ḥiyya said to him: That is … conduct … her, … Rather, … How modest was this man that he did not recognize … in his wife.

Rams may go out levuvin. … What is … levuvin? Rav Huna said: Tied [tutri] … From where … be inferred that this … levuvin is a term of closeness? As it is written: “You have drawn me near [libavtini], my sister my bride”

Ulla said: … hide that one ties over the hearts … so that wolves will not attack them … wolves attack rams … do not attack ewes? … Because … walk at the head of the flock. … wolves attack the head of the flock … not the rear of the flock? Rather, … because they are plump … Are there no plump … among the ewes? And furthermore, do … know … between these, … those, … Rather, … because they raise their noses and walk while looking

Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said … hide that one ties under their male … so that they will not mount the females. And from where … Because the latter clause states: Ewes may go out sheḥuzot. What is … sheḥuzot? … that they fasten [she’oḥazin] their tails … so that the males may mount them … the first clause … so that the males will not mount the females, and the latter clause … so that the males will mount them.
From where … be inferred that this … sheḥuzot is a term of exposure? … As it is written … “And behold there met him a woman
with the attire of a harlot [shit zona] and wily of heart”

Ewes may go out kevulot. … What is … kevulot? … that they bind their tails down … so that the males will not mount them. … From where … be inferred that this … kavul is a term … does not produce fruit? As it is written, … “What cities are these which you have given me, my brother? And he called them the land of Kavul to this day”

What is … the land of Kavul? Rav Huna said: That the people … there were bound [mekhubalin] … silver and gold. Rava said to him: If so, is that what is written: … and they pleased him not” … were bound in silver and gold … were not pleasing in his eyes? … said to him: Yes … Since … were wealthy and delicate, they did not perform labor.

Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: It was a sandy [ḥomton] expanse … And why was it called Kavul? … because the leg sinks into it up to the ankle [kavla]. And people say … Land … bound [mekhabela] … that does not produce fruit

kevunot. … What is … kevunot? … that they covered [mekhabnin] … to … fine wool. … As we learned … a leprous sore … se’et … is like … white wool. … What is white wool? Rav Beivai bar Abaye said: Like the clean wool of a newborn … which they cover … to … fine wool.
And the she-goats may go out … bound. … It was stated … Rav said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, and Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei.
And there are … who teach this halakha independent … Rav said: … to dry … it is permitted, and not … to … the milk. And Shmuel said: Both this and that are prohibited.

And there are … who taught … with regard to this … Goats may go out … bound to dry … but not to … the milk. In the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira they said: That is the halakha, … but who … cast lots … which … to dry … and which … to … the milk? And since one cannot distinguish … Both this and that are prohibited. Shmuel said, and some say Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira. … When Ravin came … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The halakha is in accordance with … the … first tanna
MISHNA: And with what may … not go out … A camel may not go out with a saddlecloth, nor … akud or ragul … And likewise, … all other animals
one may not tie camels one to the other and pull … However, he … place the ropes … in his hand and pull … provided that he does not intertwine

GEMARA: It was taught … A camel may not go out with a saddlecloth tied to its tail … However, it may go out with a saddlecloth tied to … its tail and its hump, … Rabba bar Rav Huna said: A … camel may go out with a saddlecloth tied to its afterbirth.

not … akud or ragul. Rav Yehuda said: Akud … the … foreleg and hind leg are bound together, similar to … Isaac, son of Abraham, … Ragul … that one may not bend … the foreleg onto the upper foreleg and tie it.

raises an objection … Akud … two forelegs and two hind legs are bound together. Ragul … that one may not bend … the foreleg onto the upper foreleg and tie it. … holds in accordance with this tanna, as it was taught … Akud … foreleg and hind leg or … two forelegs and two hind legs are bound together. Ragul … that one may not bend … the foreleg onto the upper foreleg and tie it.
And … are still not the same. Granted, the first clause, … and the last clause, … well. … the middle clause is difficult.

Rather, … stated … in accordance with this tanna, … Akud … foreleg and hind leg are bound together, similar to … Isaac, son of Abraham. Ragul … that one may not bend … the foreleg onto the upper foreleg and tie it.
And one may not tie camels … What is the reason … Rav Ashi said: Because he appears like one going to the market [ḥinga]

However, he … place the … Rav Ashi said: This … was taught … only with regard to … diverse kinds. … Diverse kinds of what? If you say … of … diverse kinds of man … Didn’t we learn … A person is permitted to plow and to pull … with all
Rather, … diverse kinds of ropes. … However, … wasn’t it taught … One who attaches … with a single stitch … it is not … a connection
Actually, … diverse kinds of ropes, and … is saying as follows: Provided that he does not intertwine … and tie
Shmuel said … provided that a handbreadth of the rope does not hang below his hand … Didn’t … of the school of Shmuel teach … two handbreadths
Abaye said: Now that Shmuel said one handbreadth, and … of the school of Shmuel taught two handbreadths … Shmuel came to teach us the practical halakha.
Wasn’t it taught … provided that he raises … one handbreadth from the ground? … When this … was taught, … with regard to the … rope between

MISHNA: … A donkey may neither go out with the saddlecloth when it is not tied to … nor with a bell even if it is plugged … nor with a ladder that is around its neck, nor with a strap that is around its leg.
And the roosters may not go out with strings and not with a strap on their feet, … And the rams may not go out with a … wagon under their tails,

And ewes may not go out ḥanunot, nor may a calf go out with a gimon, nor may a cow … with the skin of a hedgehog [kupar], nor with a strap between its horns. … Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya’s cow would go out … with a strap between its horns, contrary to the will of the Sages.
GEMARA: … What is the reason? As we stated
not … with a bell even if it is plugged … that … appears like one going to the market,
Nor with a ladder that is around its neck. Rav Huna said: … device … the jaw. For what … do … to … For … in which … has a wound … so that it does not chafe it again
Nor with a strap that is around its leg. … does … to … strides.
And the roosters may not go out with strings. … He does so to … a sign … so that they will not be confused
Nor with a strap … does … to … so that they will not break vessels. … Rams may not go out with a … wagon … in order that their tails will not be injured.

And ewes may not go out ḥanunot. … Rav Aḥa bar Ulla sat before Rav Ḥisda and he sat and he said: From when they shear … they soak a … swatch … in oil and place it on … forehead so that it will not catch cold … Rav Ḥisda said to him: If so, you turned … Mar Ukva.

Rather, Rav Pappa bar Shmuel sat before Rav Ḥisda, and he sat and he said: At the time that … crouches to give birth, … soak two swatches … in oil, and place one on … forehead and the other on its womb so that it will be warmed. … Rav Naḥman said to him: If so, you turned … Yalta,

Rather, Rav Huna said: There is a certain tree in the cities … sea … and ḥanun is its name. … bring a wood chip … and place it in … nose so that it will sneeze and the worms on its head will fall. … If so, … rams … Since the rams butt … with each other, … fall in any event. Shimon the Nazirite said: … chip of a broom tree
Granted, … Rav Huna … that is … teaches … ḥanunot. However, according to … the … Sages, what is … ḥanunot? … Because we do something to … we have mercy on them;

And a calf may not go out … with a gimon. … What is … A calf with a gimon? Rav Huna said … A small yoke … Rabbi Elazar said: From where … inferred that this … gimon is a term of bending? As it is written: “Is it to bow down his head like a bulrush [agmon]”
And a cow … not … with the skin of a hedgehog … that … does … to … so that creeping animals will not suckle from it.

And not with a strap that is between its horns. … If … to … Rav, whether … as an ornament or whether … to secure … it is prohibited … If … to … Shmuel, … as an ornament, it is prohibited; … to secure … it is permitted.
cow of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya … Did … have … one cow? Didn’t Rav say, and some say … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya would tithe from his herds 12,000 calves each and every year?
It was taught … was not his; rather, … his neighbor’s. And because he did not protest her … was called by his name

Rav, and Rabbi Ḥanina, and Rabbi Yoḥanan, and Rav Ḥaviva taught … Throughout the order of Moed, wherever this pair … exchange Rabbi Yoḥanan and insert Rabbi Yonatan … Anyone who … the capability to … protest … the members of his household and did not protest, … apprehended for … the members of his household … the people of his town, … apprehended for … the people of his town. … the whole world, … he … apprehended for … the whole world.

Rav Pappa said: And … of the household of the Exilarch were apprehended … for … the whole world. … As … that which Rabbi Ḥanina said: What is … that which is written: “The Lord will enter into judgment with the Elders of His people and its princes … If the princes sinned
what did the Elders, … sin? Rather, say: … with the Elders because they did not protest … the princes.

Rav Yehuda was sitting before Shmuel … this woman came … cried before … and … paid no attention to her. … said to … Doesn’t the Master hold … “Whoever stops his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard” … said to him: Big-toothed one, your superior … will be … in cold water. The superior of your superior will be … in hot water. Mar Ukva, who sits as president of the court,

As it is written: “House of David, so says the Lord: Execute judgment in the morning, and deliver him that is robbed out of the hand of the oppressor, lest My fury go forth like fire, and burn so that none can quench it because of the evil of your doings”

Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Simon: Let the Master reprimand … the house of the Exilarch, … said to him: They will not accept … from me. … said to him: Let my master reprimand them even if they do not accept

As Rabbi Aḥa, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: Never did … a good attribute emerge from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and He … retracted it … evil, except … this matter, as it is written: “And the Lord said to him: Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and set a mark [tav] upon the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry on account of all the abominations that are done in her midst”

The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to … Gabriel: Go and inscribe a tav of ink on the foreheads of the righteous … so that the angels of destruction will not have dominion over them. And … a tav of blood on the foreheads of the wicked … so that the angels of destruction will have dominion over them

The attribute of justice said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, how are these different from those? He said to … These are full-fledged righteous … and those are full-fledged wicked … said to Him: Master of the Universe … it was in … hands … to protest … and they did not protest.

He said to … It is revealed and known before Me that … had they protested the … they would not have accepted … from them. … said before Him: Master of the Universe, if it is revealed before You … is it revealed to them?

And that is … that which is written: “Slay utterly old and young, both maid, and little children, and women; but come not near any man upon whom is the mark; and begin at My Sanctuary” … And it is written … “Then they began with the elderly men who were before the house.” Rav Yosef taught: Read not: My Sanctuary [mikdashi], rather: Those sanctified to Me [mekudashai]. These are people who observed the whole Torah in its entirety from alef through tav. And immediately: “And, behold, six men came from the way of the higher gate, which lies toward the north, and every man with his weapon of destruction in his hand; and one man among them was clothed in linen, with a writer’s inkwell by his side; and they went in and stood beside the bronze altar”

Was there a bronze altar … The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them: Begin from the place where they recite songs … before Me … And who are the six men … Rav Ḥisda said: Fury, Wrath, and Rage, and Destroyer, and Breaker, and Annihilator,

And what is different … tav, … Rav said: Tav … tiḥye, you shall live, … Tav … tamut, you shall die, … And Shmuel said: … merit of the Patriarchs has ceased … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … that … the merit of the Patriarchs … will have mercy

And Reish Lakish said: … tav … the last … of the seal of the Holy One, Blessed be He, … Rabbi Ḥanina said: The seal of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is truth [emet], … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said: … these are people who observed the entire Torah from alef through tav.

From when did the merit of the Patriarchs cease? Rav said: From the days of … Hosea, son of Beeri, as it is stated: … I will uncover her lewdness in the sight of her lovers, and none shall deliver her out of My hand”

And Shmuel said … since the days of Hazael, as it is stated: “And Hazael, king of Aram, oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz” … And it is written … “And the Lord was gracious to them, and had compassion on them, and turned toward them because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and would not destroy them; neither has He till now cast them away from His presence”

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: … since the days of Elijah … , as it is stated: “And it came to pass at the time of the evening sacrifice, that Elijah the Prophet came near and said, Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known this day that you are God in Israel, and that I am Your servant, and that I have done all these things at Your word”

And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … since the days of Hezekiah, as it is stated: “For the increase of the realm and for peace without end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice; from now and forever the zeal of the Lord of hosts performs this”
Rav Ami said: There is no death without sin; … And there is no suffering without iniquity.

There is no death without sin, as it is written: “The soul that sins, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son; the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him” … there is no suffering without iniquity, as it is written: “Then I will punish their transgression with the rod and their iniquity with strokes”

raises an objection … The ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, why did You penalize Adam, the first man, with … death … He said to them: I gave him a simple mitzva, and he violated it. They said to Him: Didn’t Moses and Aaron, who observed the whole Torah in its entirety, … die? … said to them, … there is one event to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good

stated … in accordance with this tanna, as it was taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said: Even Moses and Aaron died due to their sin, as it is stated: … Because you did not believe in Me … Had you believed in Me … your time would not … have come to leave the world.

raises an objection … Four … died due to … the serpent, … And they are: Benjamin, son of Jacob; Amram, father of Moses; Yishai, father of David; and Kilab, son of David. And all of them … tradition, except for Yishai, father of David, with regard to whom there is an explicit verse … as it is written: “And Absalom placed Amasa in charge of the army in place of Joab, and Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra the Israelite, who had taken to himself Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, the mother of Joab”

And was … the daughter of Nahash? Wasn’t she the daughter of Yishai, as it is written: … and their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. … Rather, … the daughter of one who died on account of … the serpent [naḥash],

Who … If you say … tanna … the ministering angels … as weren’t there … Moses and Aaron … Rather, it must be Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, … Learn from it … there is death without sin and there is suffering without iniquity, and … conclusive refutation … of Rav Ami. … conclusive refutation.

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yonatan said: Anyone who says that Reuben sinned … is nothing other than mistaken, as it is stated: … Now the sons of Jacob were twelve” … teaches that, … all … were equal … How … do I establish … “And he lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine”? … This … teaches that … rearranged his father’s bed … And the verse ascribes to him … as if he had … lain with

It was taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: This righteous person, … was saved from that sin … and that action did not come to … him? Is it possible … his descendants are destined to stand on Mount Eival and say: “Cursed be he that lies with his father’s wife; … and this sin will come to … him? … How … do I establish … “And he lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine”? … He protested the affront to his mother. He said: If my mother’s sister … was a rival to my mother, will my mother’s sister’s concubine be a rival to my mother? He … stood and rearranged her bed

Aḥerim say: He rearranged two beds, one of the Divine Presence and one of his father. And that is … that which is written: … then you did defile it; he went up to my bed [yetzu’i]” … Do not read it as yetzu’i, … rather, read it as yetzu’ai, my beds,

parallel to … tanna’im. … “Unstable [paḥaz] as water, you shall not excel.” … Rabbi Eliezer says … You were impulsive [pazta], you were liable [ḥavta], and you acted contemptuously [zalta]. Rabbi Yehoshua says … You trampled the law [pasata al dat], you sinned [ḥatata], … you were promiscuous [zanita]. Rabban Gamliel says: … You prayed [pilalta], you trembled … [ḥalta], … your prayer shone forth [zarḥa].

Rabban Gamliel said: We still need … the Modaite, … Rabbi Elazar HaModa’i said: Reverse … the word … and … interpret it homiletically: You shook [zizata], you recoiled … hirtata]; … the sin flew [parḥa] from you. … Rava said, and some say … Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said: … You remembered [zakharta] the punishment … you made yourself gravely ill [ḥalita] … you … withdrew [peirashta] from sinning.
mnemonic: Reuben, the sons of Eli, the sons of Samuel, David, Solomon, and Josiah.

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yonatan said: Anyone who says that the sons of Eli sinned is nothing other than mistaken, as it is written: “And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Pinehas, were there priests of the Lord”

holds in accordance with … Rav, as Rav said: Pinehas did not sin. … juxtaposes Hophni to Pinehas; just as Pinehas did not sin, so too Hophni did not sin. … How, … do I establish … how they lay with the women … Since … delayed … the bird-offerings … not to go to their husbands … the verse ascribes to … as if they had lain with them.

the matter itself … Rav said: Pinehas did not sin, as it is stated: “And Ahijah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod’s brother, the son of Pinehas, the son of Eli, was the Lord’s priest … Is it possible that sin came to … hand and, … the verse traces the lineage … to him?

Wasn’t it was already stated … “The Lord will cut off from the man that does this, him that is awake and him that answers from the tents of Jacob, or any to present an offering to the Lord of hosts” … If … an Israelite, he will not have … one who is … awake among the Sages, or … one among … disciples who can answer … And if he is a priest, he will not have a son who will present a meal-offering. … conclude from it that Pinehas did not sin.
However, isn’t it written: “And how they lay [yishkevun] … is written … yishkeven
Isn’t it written … “No, my sons [banai]; for it is not a good report … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: It is written … my son [beni]
Isn’t it written: “You make … to transgress [ma’avirim] … Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said: … is written … You cause … to transgress [ma’aviram]
Isn’t it written: … scoundrels; … Since Pinehas should have protested Hophni’s … but he did not protest, the verse ascribes to him … as if he … had sinned.
Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yonatan said: Anyone who says

that the sons of Samuel sinned is nothing other than mistaken, as it is stated: “And it came to pass, when Samuel was old … And his sons walked not in his ways … In his ways they did not walk, … they did not sin either.

However, how … do I establish … “And they sought after unjust gain,” … that they did not conduct … in accordance with the actions of their father. As Samuel the righteous would travel to all places … Israel … and … judgment in their towns, as it is stated: “And he went from year to year in circuit from Beth-El, and Gilgal, and Mitzpa, and judged Israel … And, … they did not do so … Rather, they sat in their … cities in order to enhance the fees … by their attendants and scribes.

parallel to … tanna’im. … “And they sought after unjust gain.” Rabbi Meir says: … they vocally demanded their portions … Rabbi Yehuda says: They imposed … homeowners … merchandise … Rabbi Akiva says: They took an extra basket of tithes, … by force. However, how … do I establish … “Why have you despised the word of the Lord, to do that which is evil … sought to do … but did not do

“Uriah the Hittite you have smitten with the sword,” … that you could have judged him before the Sanhedrin … and you did not judge … “And his wife you have taken to be your wife”; … you have … marriage with her,

your servant. every judgment that he issued from the age of eight, … until … eighteen, … returned … And lest you say … he took from this … and gave to that … the verse states: … with all his might [me’odo], … that he gave … from his own

MISHNA: With what … a woman go out … and with what … she not go out?
A woman may neither go out with strings of wool, nor with strings of flax, nor with strips … in … her head. And … may not immerse … with them … until she loosens them.
And, … neither … with … totefet, nor with sarvitin that are not sewn … nor with a kavul into the public domain.
And, … neither … with a city of gold … nor with a katla … nor with nose rings, nor with a ring that has no seal on it, nor with a needle that is not perforated,
And if she … went out … she is not liable … a sin-offering.

Rather, Rav Yosef said, this is the reason that Rav Huna … Because a woman does not strangle herself

Rabbi Yehuda says: … of wool and … of hair do not interpose … because the water reaches through them.

Abaye said to him: … halakha … by inference … disagree

it was stated … Rav Naḥman said … Shmuel said: The Rabbis agree with Rabbi Yehuda with regard to strands of hair.

not … with … totefet. … What is a totefet? Rav Yosef said: A packet of spices

not … a kavul. Rabbi Yannai said: This kavul, I do not know what it is. Is it the seal of a slave, … which we learned … but a cap of wool … well … Or, perhaps we learned … a cap of wool … and all the more so … the seal of a slave

bridal crowns … not … to

a bell that is around his neck, why … not … lest it be severed and he come to carry it. … a bell on his clothes too, let us be concerned lest it be severed and he come to carry it.

a garter is pure. Rav Yehuda said: Garter; that is a bracelet

with regard to … corpse are also free. of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: For what … did Israel in that generation require atonement? Because

with a woolen cap or with a wig to the courtyard. Rav said: … all … which the Sages prohibited going out into the public domain … it is … prohibited to go out with … into the courtyard … with the exception of a woolen cap and a wig.

with a cloth that is in her ear. Rami bar Yeḥezkel taught: And that is … where … is tied to her ear

the … girls may go out with strings. … Shmuel’s father did not allow his daughters to go out with strings, and did not allow them to lie next to each other, and he made ritual baths for them in the days of Nisan and mats … in the days of Tishrei.

may fasten … on a stone, … Didn’t you say in the first clause … may fasten, … Abaye said: … the latter clause … we have arrived at … a coin,

loketamin are pure. … What are loketamin? Rabbi Abbahu said: … donkey … on the shoulders, … Rava bar Pappa said: … stilts … Rava bar Rav Huna said: They are masks [peramei].

why specifically … boys … Even girls … as well. … why specifically … young … Even adults … as well.

the first day, let him carve … a little, and recite: “And an angel of the Lord appeared to him … On the following day, let him carve … a little … and recite: “And Moses said: I will turn aside now, and see … On the following day, let him carve … a little … and recite: “And the Lord saw that he turned aside to see

Abaye said: He is liable. … Rava said … he is exempt because … did not intend … prohibited severing. … Abaye said … he is liable because he intended … standard … of cutting.

Rava said: From where do I … say this … As it was taught … a stricture … Shabbat … than … other mitzvot, and a stricture … other mitzvot … than … Shabbat. … A stricture … Shabbat … than … other mitzvot … that, … Shabbat, one who performed two … in … one lapse of awareness, is liable … for each and every one, which is not … in other mitzvot. … And a stricture … other mitzvot … than … Shabbat … that, … other mitzvot, … unwittingly without intent is liable, which is not … with … Shabbat.

The Master said … A stricture … Shabbat … than … other mitzvot … that, … Shabbat, one who performed two … in … one lapse of awareness, is liable … for each and every one, which is not … with … other mitzvot. … What are the circumstances? If you say that he … performed … reaping and grinding … the corresponding … other mitzvot … he ate forbidden fat and blood. … Here … is liable to … two … and here … is liable to … two … Rather, what are the circumstances … other mitzvot where he is liable to … only one … where … ate forbidden fat and … forbidden fat … The corresponding … Shabbat … one performed … reaping and … reaping … Here … is liable to … one … and here … is liable to … one

Actually, … where … performed … reaping and grinding. And what … Which is not … with … other mitzvot? … idolatry, … in accordance with … Rabbi Ami, as Rabbi Ami said: One who sacrificed … and burned … and poured … one lapse of awareness is liable to … only one

In what … did you establish … in … idolatry? … state the latter … A stricture … other mitzvot … that, … other mitzvot, … unwittingly without intent is liable, which is not … with … Shabbat. … That … unwittingly without intent with … idolatry, what are the circumstances? If you say … where he thought … it was a synagogue and bowed to it, … his heart was … toward Heaven, … Rather, … where he saw a statue [andarta] … and bowed to it. What are the circumstances? If … in which … he accepted … upon himself as a god, he … intentionally … And if he did not accept … upon himself as a god … it is meaningless

Rather, … due to love … and due to fear … This … well according to … Abaye, who said: … is liable … However, according to … Rava, who said: … is exempt … what can be said? … Rather, … where one says … is permitted. … Which is not … with … Shabbat, … who … is completely exempt.
Rava raised a dilemma before Rav Naḥman only whether to deem him liable to … one or whether to deem him liable to … two … However, … to exempt him completely … not

Rather, … not … first … with … idolatry, and the latter … with … other mitzvot? And what are the circumstances … Unwitting without intent, with … other mitzvot? … where … thought … was … fat, and ate it, … That is not … with … Shabbat, where … is exempt, as … intended to cut … detached … and … severed … attached … exempt. And … Abaye … what are the circumstances … Unwitting without intent, … where … he thought it was spittle and swallowed it … That is not … with … Shabbat, … exempt, … one who intended to lift … detached … and … severed … attached … he is exempt. However, … intended to cut … detached … and … severed … attached … is liable

was stated. … one who intended to throw … two … and … he threw … four … Rava said: … exempt. Abaye said: … liable. … Rava said: … exempt, as he does not intend … a throw … four … Abaye said: … liable, as he intends … a standard throw, … one who thought … the private domain … and, … it was found … the public domain, Rava said: … exempt. And Abaye said: … liable. … Rava said: … exempt, … he does not intend … a prohibited throw. … And Abaye said: … liable, as he intends … a standard throw.

And it is necessary … As, had … taught us … the first, … in that … Rava said … as he does not intend … prohibited severing. … However, … one who intended to throw … two … and he threw … four … as … cannot be thrown four … without … two cubits. … say … agrees with Abaye, … And, had … taught us … this … in that … Rava says … as he does not intend … a throw of four … However, … one who thought … the private domain, and … it was found … the public domain where the individual intends … a throw … four … say … agrees with Abaye … it is necessary

We learned … The primary categories of labor are forty-less-one, and we discussed it … Why do I need … tally … And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … that if one performed all of … in … one lapse of awareness … he is liable for each and every one. Granted, … to Abaye, who said that in a … like that … he is liable, you find that … he was aware that the prohibition of Shabbat … and he was aware … labors were prohibited, and was mistaken with regard to measures. … However, according to Rava, who said … he is exempt … what … do you find that … Shabbat, … intentional, and, … prohibited labors, … unwitting?

well if he holds in accordance with … Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said: Once he was unwitting with regard to … karet, even though he … prohibition … intentionally, … you find … when he was aware that … Shabbat … prohibition, … However, if he holds in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, … said: … until he was unwitting with regard to … prohibition and karet, … to what … He was aware … Shabbat boundaries, in accordance with … Rabbi Akiva,

MISHNA: … primary categories of labor … forty-less-one. … One who sows, and one who plows, and one who reaps, and one who gathers … and one who threshes, … and one who winnows … one who selects … one who grinds, and one who sifts … and one who kneads … and one who bakes.

One who shears wool, … one who whitens it, and one who combs … it, and one who dyes it, and one who spins … and one who stretches … and one who constructs two meshes, … and one who weaves two threads, and one who severs two threads … one who ties … and one who unties … and one who sews two stitches … one who tears … in order to sew two stitches.
One who traps a deer, … one who slaughters it, and one who flays it, … one who salts its … and one who tans its hide, and one who smooths it, … and one who cuts it

One who writes two letters and one who erases in order to write two letters. One who builds … and one who dismantles … one who extinguishes … and one who kindles … One who strikes … with a hammer … one who carries out … from domain to domain. … these are primary categories of labor, … forty-less-one.
GEMARA: … Why do I need … tally? Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … that if he performed all of … in … one lapse of awareness, … he is liable for each and every one.

One who sows, and one who plows. … Since, after all, … plowing, one plows first … let … teach … one who plows, and afterward let him teach one who sows. … tanna … based … in Eretz Yisrael, where … sow first and then plow.

is taught … One who sows, and one who prunes … and one who plants, and one who bends … and one who grafts … all … one … labor, … What is … teaching us? … This teaches us … one who … performs numerous prohibited labors … single … of labor, … is liable to … only one … Rabbi Aḥa said … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ashi said … Rabbi Ami said: One who prunes is liable for … planting. And one who plants, and one who bends, and one who grafts is liable for … sowing. … for sowing, yes, … for planting, no, … not … say … even for sowing,

Rav Kahana said: … prunes … and needs the wood … is liable to … two … One … due to … reaping, … one … due to … planting, … Rav Yosef said: One who reaps alfalfa is liable to … two … One due to reaping, … and one due to planting, … Abaye said: One who cuts beet leaves is liable to … two … One due to reaping and one due to sowing.

One who plows. … taught … One who plows, and one who digs, and one who makes a furrow … all … one … labor. Rav Sheshet said: One who had a mound … and removed it in the house, … is liable due to … building, … In the field, he is liable due to … plowing. … Rava said: One who had a hole and filled it, in the house he is liable due to … building. In the field, he is liable due to … plowing.

Rabbi Abba said: One who digs a hole on Shabbat and … only … needs its dirt is exempt for … And even according to Rabbi Yehuda, … said … labor that is not necessary for its own sake, … is liable for it; … applies only … constructive. … this … destructive,

And … One who reaps. It was taught … One who reaps, … one who picks … and one who harvests … and one who collects … and one who gathers … all … one … labor, … Rav Pappa said: One who threw a clod … at a palm tree and severed dates is liable to … two … One due to severing, … and one for extracting, … Rav Ashi said: … that is not the … manner of severing, and that is not the … manner of extracting,
And … One who gathers. Rava said: One who gathers salt from salt pools is liable due to … gathering, … Abaye said: … gathering … only to … that grows from the ground.
And … One who threshes. … taught … One who threshes, and one who beats … and one who strikes … all … one … labor.

And … One who winnows, and one who selects, and one who grinds, and one who sifts. … winnowing is the same as … selecting, … is the same as … sifting. … Abaye and Rava, who both said … Any manner … that was … in the Tabernacle,

even though there is … that is similar to it, … enumerated it. … And let him enumerate … pounding as well, … Abaye said: … as paupers eat their bread without pounding … Rava said … Who is … this … It is Rabbi … said: … primary categories of labor are forty-less-one, … And had … enumerated pounding, there would be forty … And let him take out one of these, … and insert pounding, … Rather, … is clear, according to … Abaye.

The Sages taught … If there were … types of food before him, … one selects and eats, selects and puts … And one may not select, and if one did select, he is liable to … a sin-offering. … What is … saying? … Ulla said: It is saying as follows: One selects and eats … for … that day, … And … selects and puts … for … that day. And one may not select … the next day. And if one did select … he is liable to … a sin-offering. Rav Ḥisda strongly objects to this … And is it permitted to bake for that day, and is it permitted to cook for that day?

Rather, Rav Ḥisda said … One selects and eats less than the measure … selects and puts … less than that measure. And one may not select the measure … and if one did select … he is liable to … a sin-offering. Rav Yosef strongly objects to this … And is it permitted to bake less than the measure for liability … Rather, Rav Yosef said: One selects and eats by hand, selects and put … by hand. … with a basket [kanon] or with a plate, … one may not select … And if he did select, he is exempt … However, it is prohibited. And one may not select with a sieve or with a sifter. And if he did select … he is liable to … a sin-offering.

Rav Hamnuna strongly objects to this: Does … teach anything … a basket or a plate? … Rather, Rav Hamnuna said: One selects and eats … food from the waste, … selects and puts … food from the waste. … one may not select waste from food, and if he did select … he is liable to … a sin-offering. … Abaye strongly objects to this: Does … teach anything … food from waste? … Rather, Abaye said: One selects and eats … immediate … one selects and puts … immediate … one may not select for … that same day. And if he did select, he is considered like one who selects for storage, and he is liable to … a sin-offering. … the Sages stated … before Rava. He said to them: Naḥmani, … spoke well.

there were two types of foods before him, and he selected and ate … and selected and put … Rav Ashi taught: … exempt. Rav Yirmeya from Difti taught: … liable. Rav Ashi taught: … exempt. … Wasn’t it taught … he is liable? … not difficult: This, … by … a basket or a plate, … that, … by … a sieve or a sifter,

when Rav Dimi came … he said: It was the Shabbat … Rav Beivai … and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi happened … He placed before them a basket of fruits … And I do not know whether … because he holds … is prohibited … food from waste … or whether … because he intended to … generosity to
Ḥizkiya said: One who selects lupines from their waste … is liable … Let us say, … Ḥizkiya holds … food from waste is prohibited. … Lupines are different,
as they are boiled seven times. And, if one does not remove them … rot. … it is considered like … waste from food.

And one who grinds. Rav Pappa said: One who chops beets … is liable due to … grinding, … Rav Menashe said: One who chops wood chips … is liable due to … grinding. Rav Ashi said: If … is particular … with regard to the measurement, … liable due to … cutting.
And one who kneads and one who bakes. Rav Pappa said: Our tanna left … cooking … spices … which was … in the Tabernacle, and included … baking, … Our tanna cited the sequence … bread,

Rav Aḥa bar Rav Avira said: One who places a peg into an oven … is liable for … cooking. … obvious. … Lest you say … he intends to strengthen the utensil, … he teaches us that … is softened … and … afterward it is hardened. Rabba bar Rav Huna said: One who boils pitch is liable for … cooking. … obvious. … Lest you say … since it proceeds to harden … say … not considered … he teaches us

Rava said: One who … crafted an … barrel … is liable to … seven sin-offerings: … an oven is liable for eight sin-offerings, … Abaye said: One who … crafts a receptacle … is liable to … eleven sin-offerings. … And if he sews the mouth … he is liable to … thirteen sin-offerings

One who shears wool, and one who whitens it, … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who … spins wool … on the back of … animal on Shabbat is liable to … three sin-offerings: One due to shearing, … and one due to combing … and one due to spinning. Rav Kahana said: This is not … manner of shearing, and this is not … manner of combing, and this is not … manner of spinning. … And … not … Wasn’t it taught … in the name … Rabbi Neḥemya … they washed … on the goats, and they spun … on the goats … Apparently, spinning on the back of an animal is considered … spinning. … Extraordinary wisdom is different.

The Sages taught … One who … plucks … the wing … and who snips … and who pulls out … is liable to … three sin-offerings. And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said … plucks … is liable due to … shearing. … snips … is liable due to cutting. … pulls out … is liable due to smoothing.

One who ties and one who unties. … Where was … tying in the Tabernacle? Rava said: They tied … tents … to the pegs. … tying? That was tying … in order to untie … Rather, Abaye said: As the weavers of curtains … when a thread would rip, they would tie it. Rava said to him: You have resolved … tying; however, … untying, what can be said? … And if you say that … if one found two threads … tied next to each other, he untied one and … tied; now, before a king of flesh and blood one would not do so, … before the King of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He, … one do so? Rather, Rava said, and some say … Rav Elai … The trappers of ḥilazon, … tie and untie
And one who sews two stitches. … That does not endure; … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: That … where, … he tied them.
One who tears in order to sew two stitches. … Was there tearing in … the Tabernacle? … Rabba and Rabbi Zeira who both said
As, when a curtain had a worm … in it, they would tear … and … sew it

Rav Zutra bar Toviya said … Rav said: One who tightens the thread of a stitch on Shabbat is liable to … a sin-offering. … And one who learns … one matter from a magosh, … is liable to … death … And one who knows how to calculate astronomical seasons and … constellations, and does not do so, one may not speak with him

magosh, Rav and Shmuel … One said … sorcerers, while the other said … heretics. … Conclude that Rav … who said … heretics, as Rav Zutra bar Toviya said … Rav … One who learns one matter from the magosh is liable to … death … As, if it should enter your mind … sorcerers, wasn’t it written: … you shall not learn to do … but you … learn to understand and to teach … conclude

Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of bar Kappara: Anyone who knows how to calculate astronomical seasons and … constellations and does not do so, the verse says about him: “They do not take notice of the work of God, and they do not see His handiwork” … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: From where … that … a mitzva … upon a person to calculate astronomical seasons and … constellations? As it was stated: “And you shall guard and perform, for it is your wisdom and understanding in the eyes of the nations” … What wisdom and understanding … that is in the eyes of the nations, … You must say: This is the calculation of astronomical seasons and … constellations,

One who traps a deer … The Sages taught … One who traps a ḥilazon and breaks its … is liable to … only one … Rabbi Yehuda says: He is liable to … two, … as Rabbi Yehuda would say: The breaking of a ḥilazon is included … threshing, … said to him: Breaking … is not included … threshing. Rava said: What is the rationale … of the Rabbis? They hold: Threshing … only to … that grows … the ground. … let him be liable for taking a life as well. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … where he broke its … dead.

Rava said: Even … say that he broke it … alive, … is acting unawares with regard to taking a life. … Didn’t Abaye and Rava both say … Rabbi Shimon, … agrees … in … Cut off its head and will it not die, … Here it is different, as the longer … lives, the better … for … so that its dye will become clear.
And one who slaughters … one who slaughters … due to what … liable? Rav said: … due to dyeing, … And Shmuel said: … due to taking a life.

due to dyeing, yes, … due to taking a life, no, … say: … due to dyeing as well. … Rav said: I will say something … with regard to the statement I said, … later generations will not come and laugh at me: In what … is dyeing … desired … for him? It is desired that the area of the slaughter will be inundated … blood, so that people will see it … and come to purchase … from him.

And one who salts it and one who tans it. … salting is the same as … tanning, … Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish both said: Remove one of them and replace … drafting. … Rabba bar Rav Huna said: One who salts meat … is liable due to … tanning. Rava said: There is no tanning … food. … Rav Ashi said: And even Rabba bar Rav Huna said … only when he needs to … a trip … However, to … the house, a person does not render his food … wood.

And one who smooths it and one who cuts it. Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina said: One who rubs … between the pillars on Shabbat, … is liable due to … smoothing. Rav Ḥiyya bar Abba said: Rav Ashi told me three statements in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: One who planes the tops of posts on Shabbat … is liable due to … cutting, … One who spreads a bandage … on Shabbat is liable due to … smoothing. And one who chisels a stone on Shabbat is liable due to … striking … with a hammer, … Rabbi Shimon ben Kisma said … Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: One who engraves a figure onto an … vessel and one who blows … a glass vessel is liable due to … striking … with a hammer. Rav Yehuda said: One who removes … threads from a cloak is liable due to … striking … with a hammer. And that applies … if he is particular about them

And one who writes two letters. The Sages taught: One who wrote one large letter, and in its space there is … to write two, is exempt, … one who erased … large letter, and in its space there is … to write two, is liable. Rav Menaḥem, son of Rabbi Yosei, said: And that is a … stricture with regard to erasing than with regard to writing.

One who builds and one who dismantles; one who extinguishes and one who kindles; and one who strikes … with a hammer. … Rabba and Rabbi Zeira who both stated … any … that contains … completion of work is liable for … striking … with a hammer.

These are the primary categories of labor. … these, … to exclude … Rabbi Eliezer, … renders one liable for … a subcategory … together with a primary category … less-one, … to exclude … Rabbi Yehuda. As it was taught … Rabbi Yehuda … lining up … and beating … They said to him: Lining up … subsumed under … stretching … Beating is subsumed under … weaving.

MISHNA: And they stated an additional principle … Anything fit to store, … and … store … like it, and one carried it out … on Shabbat, he is liable to … a sin-offering for … And anything not fit to store and … not store … like it, … and one carried it out on Shabbat, only the one who stores it is liable.

GEMARA: … Anything fit to store, … What does it … to exclude? … Rav Pappa said: … to exclude the blood of a menstruating woman. Mar Ukva said: … to exclude the wood of a tree designated for idolatry [ashera]. … The one who said … blood of a menstruating woman … all the more so … the wood of an ashera … the one who said … the wood of an ashera … the blood of a menstruating woman … as one stores it … to the cat. … And the other, … since … weakens … one does not store it.
Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: … these … are not in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon, as, if … Rabbi Shimon, didn’t he say: … only stated all these … measures … with regard to those who store them?
And anything not fit to store,

Rabbi Elazar said: This … not in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, as it was taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar stated a principle: Anything that is not fit to be stored and … not … store … like it, but it was deemed fit … by this … and he stored it, and another … came and carried out … that … is rendered liable by the thought of this

MISHNA: … One who carries out straw … equivalent to a cow’s mouthful … etza … equivalent to a camel’s mouthful. … ears of grain … equivalent to a lamb’s mouthful. … grass … equivalent to a goat’s mouthful, … garlic leaves and onion leaves, … moist … equivalent to a dried fig-bulk. … dry, … equivalent to a goat’s mouthful. And none … join … with one another … because they are not equal in their measures.

GEMARA: … What is etza … Rav Yehuda said: … straw of types of legumes. When Rav Dimi came … he said: … one who carries out … straw equivalent to a cow’s mouthful for a camel, … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … liable. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: … exempt. In the evening, Rabbi Yoḥanan said that; … in the morning, he reversed … Rav Yosef said: He did well to reverse … since … is not suitable for a camel. … Abaye said to … On the contrary, … original … is reasonable, as it is suitable for a cow.

Rather, when Ravin … came … he … said: … one who carries out … equivalent to a cow’s mouthful of straw for a camel, everyone agrees that he is liable. Where they disagree … in … carries … etza, … equivalent to a cow’s mouthful for … a cow.

And the opposite was stated … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … exempt. Reish Lakish said: … liable. … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … exempt … eating under duress, … is not considered eating. Reish Lakish said: … is liable … eating under duress is considered eating.
an ear of grain … equivalent to a lamb’s mouthful. … Wasn’t it taught … equivalent to a dried fig-bulk? … This, … and that, … are one, … measure.

garlic leaves and onion leaves, … moist, … equivalent to a dried fig-bulk. … dry, … equivalent to a goat’s mouthful. And none … join … with one another … because they are not equal in their measures. Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: … do not join together … among them … more stringent … However, … join together … among them … more lenient,

And do any … that are not equal in their measures join together? … Didn’t we learn … The garment … three by three … And the sack … four by four … And the … hide … five by five, … mat … six by six. And … was taught about … The garment and the sack, the sack and the hide, … the hide and the mat join together with one another. And Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason … Because … are fit to become ritually impure … a seat … The reason … because they are fit to become ritually impure … a seat. However, … is … not fit to become ritually impure … a seat, no,
Rava said:
Here too, … suited … sample

MISHNA: One who carries out … foods … equivalent to … dried fig-bulk … is liable. And … join together with one another … because they are equal in their measures. … without their shells, and their seeds, and their stems, and their bran, … and their coarse bran … Rabbi Yehuda says: … except for the shells of lentils, … they are cooked … with them.

GEMARA: … And do the bran and coarse bran … not join together? Didn’t we learn … five-quarters … flour and … more obligates … ḥalla? … them, … and their bran, and their coarse bran. … Abaye said: … since a pauper eats his loaf … from dough mixed with bran.

Rabbi Yehuda says: Except for the shells of lentils … they are cooked … with them. … lentils, yes, … beans, no, … Wasn’t it taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: Except for the shells of beans and lentils? … not difficult: This … to new, … That … to old … Why do … old … not … Rabbi Abbahu said: Because … look like flies in the dish;

MISHNA: One who carries out … wine … equivalent to … diluted in a cup. … milk … equivalent to … swallowed … honey … equivalent … to place on a sore … oil … equivalent … to spread on a small limb. … water … equivalent … to rub … an eye bandage. And … all other liquids … a quarter … And … all waste water … a quarter … Rabbi Shimon says: … all … a quarter … And all these measures were only stated with regard to those who store them.

GEMARA: It was taught … equivalent to … diluted … a significant cup … And what is … significant cup … a cup of blessing. … Rav Naḥman said … Rabba bar Avuh said: A cup of blessing must have a quarter … a quarter … in it, so that one will dilute it … and … will contain a quarter
Rava said: We too

learned … One who carries out … wine … equivalent to … diluted … a cup. And it was taught with regard to … equivalent to … diluted … a significant cup … And it was taught in the latter … And … all other liquids … a quarter … And Rava … his … reasoning, … Rava said: Any wine that does not hold one … three … water is not wine.

Abaye said: … two … responses with regard to … matter. One, as we learned … Diluted wine, … two parts water and one … wine from the wine of the Sharon. … And furthermore: … water is in the jug and … joins together

Rava said to him: That which you said that … two parts water and one … wine, from the wine of the Sharon, … Wine of the Sharon … unique … is weak, … Alternatively, there … for … appearance … however, for … of taste, more … is necessary. And that which you said: … water is in the jug and … joins together … With regard to … Shabbat, we require an object that is significant, and this … is also significant.

taught … congealed … an olive-bulk; … the statement of Rabbi Natan. Rav Yosef said: Rabbi Natan and Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said the same thing. Rabbi Natan’s … that which we … stated. And … Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, … as it was taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: Six matters are among the leniencies of Beit Shammai and among the stringencies of Beit Hillel. … the blood of a carcass. Beit Shammai deem … ritually pure, … and Beit Hillel deem … ritually impure. Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said: Even when Beit Hillel deemed … impure, they deemed impure only … blood that contains a quarter … since it can congeal and constitute an olive-bulk.

Abaye said: Perhaps that is not … Rabbi Natan said … a quarter … is required only here, with regard to wine, … is liquid; however, with regard to blood, which is viscous, … olive-bulk … a quarter … is not required. … Alternatively, Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said that … olive-bulk, a quarter … is sufficient only there, with regard to blood, … viscous; however, wine, … is liquid, … olive-bulk, more … quarter … And, … when he carries out less than an olive-bulk … let him be liable.

milk … equivalent to … swallowed [kedei gemia] … A dilemma was raised before … Kedei gemia … or kedei gemia … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: … Give me to swallow [hagmi’ini … please, a little water from your jug”
A … dilemma … was raised before
garinin … or garinin … Rava bar Ulla said: … “And it shall be subtracted [venigra … from your valuation”
A dilemma was raised before … omemot … or omemot … Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said: … “The cedars in the garden of God could not hide it [amamuhu
A dilemma was raised before … did we learn … me’amtzin … or me’amtzin … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … “And closes [ve’otzem … his eyes from seeing evil”

the Sages taught: … the milk of an animal … equivalent to … swallowed … a woman’s milk and the white of an egg … equivalent … to place on … an eye bandage … on the wound. … eye bandage … sufficiently … to rub … with water. Rav Ashi raised a dilemma: … equivalent to … rubbed … or … equivalent to … held and rubbed? … let it stand

our Sages taught: There are five dreads, … dread … the weak … over … mighty: The dread of the mafgia, … over the lion; the dread of the mosquito over the elephant; the dread of the gecko over the scorpion; the dread of the swallow over the eagle; the dread of the kilbit, … over a whale. kufta, … kuf vetiv, … livnei, … livnei benei, … hutza … ḥatzitza, … ḥatzba because it hews [ḥotzev] water from the river. … kuza, … kazeh, … shutita, … shetuta, … meshikhla, … mashei kula, … mashkhilta, … mashya kalta, … asita, … ḥasirta, … bukhna, … bo ve’akkena,

oil … equivalent … to spread on a small limb. water … equivalent … to rub … an eye bandage. Abaye said: Now, since, … any substance that is … common and uncommon … the Sages, … followed the common … as a leniency, … common and … common … the Sages, … followed the common … to a stringency,

blue eye shadow … equivalent … to paint one eye blue. … glue … equivalent … to place on the top of a board … tar and sulfur … equivalent … to make a … hole … wax … equivalent … to place on the opening of a small hole … crushed earthenware … equivalent … to … make … an opening for … a gold refiners’ crucible. paper … equivalent … to write a tax receipt. … taught … How much … a tax receipt? … two letters … of a tax receipt, … And the … raises a contradiction: One who carries out blank paper; if it has … equivalent … to write two letters, he is liable, and … not, he is exempt. … Rav Sheshet said: What … two letters … Two letters of a tax receipt. raises an objection: One who carries out paper … erased or a … note … repaid, if there is in its white … equivalent … to write two letters, or … the entire paper is equivalent … to wrap around a small jar of perfume, he is liable; and if not, … he is exempt. … Granted, according to Rav Sheshet, … said: What … two letters … two letters of a tax receipt, … well. The Sages taught: One who carries out a promissory note … before he repaid … is liable; … once he repaid it, he is exempt. Rabbi Yehuda says: Even once he repaid … he is liable … because he needs it. … What … the … between their … Rav Yosef said: There is … between their … is prohibited to keep a repaid … note … The Rabbis hold: It is prohibited to keep a repaid … note … And Rabbi Yehuda holds: It is permitted to keep a repaid … note

Abaye said: Everyone agrees … it is prohibited to keep a repaid … note … and here … admits that he wrote a … note, … ratify it … first tanna holds: … admits that he wrote a … note, … ratify it … And Rabbi Yehuda holds: … admits that he wrote a … note, … need not ratify it … And what … Before he repaid … and once he repaid it?
Until … debtor says: I repaid … I did not repay

Rava said: Everyone agrees … admits that he wrote a … note, … must ratify it … And here, … one writes a receipt … they disagree. … first tanna holds: One writes a receipt … And Rabbi Yehuda holds: One does not write a receipt. … Rav Ashi said: … because he needs … to show … to a second creditor, as he says to him: Look, I am a man who repays

hide … equivalent … Rava raised a dilemma before Rav Naḥman: … one who carries out … hide, how much … He said to him, … as we learned … hide … equivalent … to make an amulet. … tans … how much … He said to him: … no different, … to tan it, how much … He said to him: … no different.

And the measure … one who weaves two threads … double the full … distance between the forefinger and the middle finger. And … no … difference between … tanned … and … not tanned? He raised an objection to him … One who carries out herbs … soaked … equivalent … to dye a sample … a stopper for the shuttle … While … herbs that were not soaked, we learned … nutshells, and pomegranate peels, … safflower, and madder, … equivalent … to dye a small cloth … opening of a woman’s … net. … But wasn’t it stated with regard to that … Rav Naḥman said … Rabba bar Avuh said: Because a person does not … trouble to soak herbs … to dye a sample for … shuttle

And … seeds of garden … before one sowed them, we learned … seeds of garden … less than a dried fig-bulk. And the Rabbis say: … equivalent … to fertilize a leek. … Wasn’t it stated with regard to that … Rav Pappa says … this, … where … is … sown; … that, … where it is not … sown, because a person does not … trouble to carry out … one … for sowing?

And … clay before one kneads it, it was taught … And the Rabbis agree with Rabbi Shimon with regard to one who carries out waste water to the public domain, that the measure … a quarter … And we discussed … For what … is waste water fit? Ḥifa … that is salted, and not treated with flour, and not treated with gallnuts. And how much is the … As we learned … hide … equivalent … to make an amulet. In any case, it was taught … equivalent … to wrap around a small weight. And Abaye said: A quarter of a quarter … Pumbedita. … There, … wet hide

And didn’t we learn … The garment … three by three … imparted by treading? And the sack … four by four … And the … hide … five by five, … mat … six by six. … both … imparted by treading and … imparted by a corpse. And it was taught … with regard to … the garment and the sack and the hide; like … measure for ritual impurity, so too is … measure for carrying out … That … kortovela,

parchment … equivalent … to write … shortest portion … And … raised a contradiction … parchment and dokhsostos … equivalent … to write a mezuza on it. … What … mezuza … mezuza … in the phylacteries. … And are the phylacteries called mezuza? … Yes, as it was taught … The straps of the phylacteries, … with the phylacteries, render the hands ritually impure … are on their own, they do not render the hands ritually impure. And from the fact that the latter clause … teaches: … parchment … equivalent … to write … shortest portion … phylacteries, which is … Shema Yisrael, by inference, in the first … we are dealing with a mezuza itself. … this is what it teaches: … parchment and dokhsostos, how much is the … them … dokhsostos … equivalent … to write a mezuza on it. … parchment … equivalent … to write on it … shortest passage that is in the phylacteries, which is Shema Yisrael.

Rav said: Dokhsostos … as parchment: Just … one may write … phylacteries on parchment, so too, one may write … phylacteries on dokhsostos. … we learned … parchment … equivalent … to write … shortest portion … phylacteries, which is … Shema Yisrael. … Parchment, yes, … Dokhsostos, no, … to … mitzva, … Come … hear … a halakha … to Moses from Sinai … phylacteries … on parchment, and a mezuza … on dokhsostos. … parchment, … on the side … flesh; … dokhsostos, … on the side … hair. … to … mitzva.

And wasn’t it taught … deviated … it is invalid, … to … mezuza, … But was it not taught … If one deviated in this, … and that, … it is invalid? … Both this and that … mezuza, and this … is … where one … wrote it … parchment, on the side … hair; or, alternatively, … dokhsostos, on the side … flesh. And, if you wish, say … one deviated in this and that is … a tannaitic … as it was taught … If one deviated in this and that it is invalid. Rabbi Aḥa deems it valid in the name of Rabbi Aḥai bar Ḥanina, and some say in the name of Rabbi Ya’akov, son of Rabbi Ḥanina. Rav Pappa said: Rav said … of the tanna from the school … Menashe. As it was taught in the school of Menashe: If one wrote it on paper or on a cloth it is invalid. … on parchment or on a hide that was treated with gallnuts [gevil] or on dokhsostos it is valid.

If he wrote it; … what? If you say … mezuza, do we write a mezuza … parchment? Rather, isn’t … phylacteries? … And according to your reasoning, do we write phylacteries … gevil? Just as on dokhsostos, one may write a mezuza, so too, on parchment, one may write a mezuza,
ink … equivalent … to write

And didn’t Rava … say: … within three handbreadths … to … the Rabbis, must come to rest atop some … not difficult. Here, … one who throws … here, … one who passes

Abaye said: Even … a karmelit … However, … a large beam, no, … And Rava said: Even … a large beam, … And Rava follows his … reasoning … as Rava said: … domain … Shabbat is like … domain … bills of divorce.

blue eye shadow … equivalent … to paint one eye blue. … one eye? … do not paint … blue. wax … equivalent … to place on the opening of a small hole … taught … Enough to place on the opening of a small hole … wine.

lime … equivalent … to spread … taught … equivalent … to spread on the finger … the smallest of girls, … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said … daughters of Israel who reached … maturity, but had not … reached the age … They would smear daughters of the poor with lime; they would smear daughters of the wealthy with fine flour; they would smear daughters of kings with shemen hamor, as it was stated: … six months with shemen hamor” … What is shemen hamor? Rav Beivai had a daughter. He smeared her … limb by limb … he received four hundred zuz … for her … There was a certain gentile in … neighborhood. And if it should enter your mind that … the temple and the area beneath the temple, both … this, … and … that, … dissolved lime. Rav Kahana strongly objected to this: And does a person turn his money … a loss [anparot]? … Rather, Rav Kahana said: … markings … as we learned … there were markings on the hin … to here, … for … an ox, … to here, … for … a ram, … to here, … for … a sheep, … And if you wish, say … What is andifa? … the forehead … And … a certain Galilean who happened to … Babylonia, to whom they said: Stand … teach us … Act of the Divine Chariot [Ma’aseh Merkava]. He said to them: I will teach it to you as Rabbi Neḥemya taught … to his colleague. MISHNA: … earth … equivalent to the seal of large sacks; … the statement of Rabbi Akiva. … And the Rabbis say: … equivalent to the seal of letters. … manure and fine sand … equivalent … to fertilize … stalk of cabbage; … the statement of Rabbi Akiva. And the Rabbis say: … equivalent … to fertilize a leek, … coarse sand … equivalent … to place on a full spoon of plaster. … a reed … equivalent … to make a quill. a reed … equivalent … to make a quill. … taught … a quill that reaches to the joints of one’s fingers. Rav Ashi raised a dilemma: … the upper joint … or the lower joint? … let it stand

And if … was thick … taught … Beaten … in oil and placed in a stew pot. Mar, son of Ravina, said to his son: Have you heard what an egg … easily is?
