He said to him … Rav Sheshet said as follows: … the egg of a chicken. And what … they call it an egg … easily? … the Sages estimated … there is no egg easier to cook than the egg of a chicken. … And what is different … All measures of … Shabbat … a dried fig-bulk, and here … like an egg … He said to him … Rav Naḥman said as follows: … a dried fig-bulk from an egg … easily,

MISHNA: … a bone … equivalent … to make a spoon. Rabbi Yehuda says: … equivalent … to make from it a key. … glass … equivalent … to scrape … the top of a bobbin, … a pebble or a stone … equivalent … to throw at a bird … Rabbi Elazar bar Ya’akov says: Equivalent … to throw at an animal,

GEMARA: … Is that to say that the measure of Rabbi Yehuda is greater? Don’t we maintain that the measure of the Rabbis is greater? Ulla said: … the teeth of a key. … the Sages taught … The teeth of a key are ritually pure, … one affixed them to a key, they … ritually impure … And … of a lock, even though one attached them to the door and affixed them with nails, are ritually pure, as anything attached to the ground has … as the ground
glass … equivalent … to scrape … taught … glass … equivalent … to cut two threads at once,

a pebble or a stone … equivalent … to throw at a bird … Rabbi Elazar … Rabbi Ya’akov said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: And that is … that … feels it. And how much is the measure … It was taught … Rabbi Elazar ben Ya’akov says: A weight of ten zuz.

Zunin entered the study hall … said to … My teachers, … stones … the bathroom, how much is their measure? They said to him: … An olive-bulk, a nut-bulk, and an egg-bulk. He said to them: And will he take scales [turtani] into … They were counted and the Sages concluded … a handful … It was taught … Rabbi Yosei says … an olive-bulk, a nut-bulk, and an egg-bulk. Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi Yosei, says in the name of his father: … a handful

Our Sages taught … with regard to Shabbat: Three sharpened stones may be taken into the bathroom. And what is their measure? Rabbi Meir says: A nut-bulk; Rabbi Yehuda says: An egg-bulk. Rafram bar Pappa said … Rav Ḥisda said: Like … dispute here, so too, … is a dispute … with regard to … a citron. … There, … a mishna … here … a baraita, … Rather, … Like … dispute … a citron, so too, … is a dispute here.

Rav Yehuda said: However, … not … the payis … What is … payis? Rabbi Zeira said: … clods of Babylonian earth, … Rava said: It is prohibited to manipulate … with a stone on Shabbat … in the manner … one manipulates … on weekdays. Mar Zutra strongly objected to this: … endanger himself … in an unusual manner … Rabbi Yannai said: If … a fixed place for a bathroom, … a handful … If … not … an average size … of a small mortar … for … spices. Rav Sheshet said: If … has an indication on it … one is permitted

raises an objection: … Ten things bring a person to … hemorrhoids and they are: One who eats the leaves of bulrushes, grape leaves, tendrils of grapevines, the palate and tongue of an animal, … without salt, the spine of a fish, a salty fish that is not fully cooked, and one who drinks wine dregs, and one who cleans himself with lime and clay, … and one who cleans himself with a stone with which another … has cleaned himself. And some say: One who suspends himself in the bathroom as well. … not difficult. Here, … to … moist. Here, … to … dry. And if you wish, say … here, … one side, … here, … to both sides, … And if you wish, say … this, … to one’s own … this, … another
Abaye said to Rav Yosef: … rain fell on … and … were obscured? … said to him: If indication on them is apparent, … it is permitted,
Rabba bar Rav Sheila raised a dilemma before Rav

Ḥisda: What is … to taking … up with him to the roof … He said to him: … great is human dignity as it overrides a prohibition in the Torah. … Mareimar sat and stated this halakha. Ravina raised an objection to … Mareimar … Rabbi Eliezer says: A person may take a … chip from … before him to … his teeth … And the Rabbis say one may take … only from the animal’s trough, … How can you compare? There, a person determines … place for … meal. … Here, does a person determine … place for a bathroom?

Rav Huna said: It is prohibited to defecate in a plowed field on Shabbat. … What is the reason … If you say … due to … treads … even on weekdays. Rather, … due to … grasses … Didn’t Reish Lakish say … it is permitted to wipe with a stone upon which grasses have grown … And … one who … detaches … from it on Shabbat is liable to … a sin-offering. Rather, … lest he take … from … high … and throw it to … low … And … be liable due to that … Rabba … as Rabba said: … had a hole and filled it, in the house, he is liable due to … building; in the field, he is liable due to plowing.

the matter itself, Reish Lakish said: It is permitted to wipe with a stone upon which grasses have grown. And one who detaches … from it … on Shabbat is liable to … a sin-offering. Rav Pappi said: Learn from that … Reish Lakish … it is permitted to carry this perforated flowerpot … Rav Kahana strongly objects to this: If they said … for a purpose, will they say … for no purpose? Abaye said: Since … a perforated pot has come to our hands, let us say something with regard to it: … it … placed on the ground and one … placed it on top of pegs … he is liable for … detaching. … it … placed on pegs and one placed it on the ground, he is liable for … planting.

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It is prohibited to wipe with an earthenware shard on Shabbat. … What is the reason … If you say … due to … danger … also on weekdays. Rather, … due to … witchcraft. … also not … on weekdays. Rather, … lest … remove hairs … an unintentional act, … Rav Natan bar Oshaya said to … A great man said something, let us say a reason for it, … It is not necessary … prohibited on a weekday … However, with regard to Shabbat … since … has the status of a utensil … well … he teaches us

Rava taught … due to the removal of hairs, and he … a difficulty … that … Rabbi Yoḥanan … that … Rabbi Yoḥanan … Did Rabbi Yoḥanan say it is forbidden to wipe with an earthenware shard on Shabbat? Apparently, … an unintentional act is prohibited. Didn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan state … The halakha … in accordance with an unattributed mishna? And we learned … A nazirite, … may wash … and separate … however, he may not comb … Rather, it is clearly in accordance with … Rav Natan bar Oshaya.

What … witchcraft … as that … Rav Ḥisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna were going on a boat. A certain matron [matronita] said to them: Let me sit with you, and they did not let her sit. She said something, … stopped the boat. They said something, … freed it. She said to them: What will I do to you,
as you do not clean … with an earthenware shard, and you do not kill lice on your garments, and you do not pull out a vegetable and eat it … the bundle that was tied by the gardener?

Rav Huna said to his son Rabba: What is the reason that you are not … found … before Rav Ḥisda, whose halakhot are incisive? … said to him: … what … should I go to him? When I go to him, he sits me down … in mundane matters … he said to me: One who enters a bathroom should not sit down immediately and should not exert … excessively … the rectum rests upon three teeth, … lest the teeth of … rectum dislocate … and he come to danger. … said … He is dealing with … human life, and you say … with mundane matters? … all the more so go before him.

Rav Huna said: … has before him a stone and an earthenware … wipes with the stone and does not wipe with the earthenware … And Rav Ḥisda said: He wipes with the earthenware … and does not wipe with the stone, … raises an objection … If one had before him a stone and an earthenware … he wipes with the earthenware … and does not wipe with the stone. … conclusive refutation … Rav Huna. Rafram bar Pappa explained it before Rav Ḥisda in accordance … of Rav Huna: … the … rims of vessels,

There were before him a stone and grasses. … Rav Ḥisda and Rav Hamnuna. One said: He wipes with the stone and does not wipe with the grasses; and one said: He wipes with the grasses and does not wipe with the stone. … raises an objection … One who wipes with something flammable, his lower teeth, … fall out. … not difficult: This, … to moist … that, … to dry

one who needs to defecate and does not do so, … Rav Ḥisda and Ravina. One said: An evil spirit dominates him; and one said: An odor of filth dominates him. It was taught … in accordance with the one who said … an odor of filth dominates him, as it was taught: One who needs to defecate and eats is comparable to an oven that was heated on top of its ashes; and that is the onset of an odor of filth.

One who needed to defecate and is unable to do so, Rav Ḥisda said: He should stand and sit, stand and sit. Rav Ḥanan from Neharde’a said: He should move to the sides … Rav Hamnuna said: He should manipulate with a stone in that place. And the Rabbis said: He should divert his thoughts … Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi: All the more so that when he diverts his thoughts he will not … defecate. … said to him: He should divert his thoughts from other matters, … Rav Yirmeya from Difti said: I saw a certain Arab who stood and sat, stood and sat, until … poured … like a pot.
The Sages taught … One who wishes to enter … a regular meal … should pace … four cubits ten times, and some say, ten cubits four times, … and defecate, and enter, and sit in his place.

MISHNA: … earthenware … equivalent … to place between one pillar and another … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Meir says: … equivalent … to stoke a fire with it. Rabbi Yosei says: … equivalent … to hold a quarter … in it. Rabbi Meir said: Although there is no proof for the matter, … allusion to … and there shall not be found among its pieces a shard to rake fire on the hearth” … Rabbi Yosei said to him: … proof from there? … “And to extract water from the cistern,”

GEMARA: A dilemma was raised before … the measure … Rabbi Meir greater, or … the measure … Rabbi Yosei greater? … It is reasonable … the measure … Rabbi Yosei is greater; however, … verse … the measure … Rabbi Meir is greater. As, if it enters your mind … the measure … Rabbi Yosei … is greater, … curse him … a small vessel … and then curse him … a larger vessel … Abaye said: The mishna is also … to stoke the fire of a large conflagration.

Rabbi Yosei said to him: … proof from there? … Rabbi Yosei spoke well to Rabbi Meir. And … Rabbi Meir … is stated … There is no need. … There is no need … an item … significant to people, … shall not be found, but even an item … insignificant to people, … shall not be found.

MISHNA: Rabbi Akiva said: From where … that idolatry, e.g., … , transmits impurity … by carrying … , just as … menstruating woman … As it is stated: “ … , … , you will cast them away as you would a menstruating woman [dava], you will tell it, get out” … Just as a menstruating woman transmits impurity … by carrying, so too, idolatry transmits impurity … by carrying.
GEMARA: … We learned … there: One whose house was adjacent to … idolatry, … and … fell, it is prohibited to rebuild it … What should one do? He moves four cubits into his own … and builds

belonged to him and to the … idolatry, … is calculated as half and half … Its stones and its wood and its dust … transmit impurity like creeping animals, … as it is stated: … you shall utterly detest it [shaketz teshaketzenu] … Rabbi Akiva says: … like a menstruating woman, as it is stated: “You will cast them away as you would a menstruating woman [dava]” … Just as a menstruating woman transmits impurity … by carrying, … so too, idolatry transmits impurity … by carrying. Rabba said … the verse said: “You will cast them away”: Make them foreign to you like a stranger. … “You will tell it, get out” … no … say to it, come in.

And … Rabba said: With regard to … by carrying, everyone agrees … transmits impurity, as it is juxtaposed to a menstruating woman … Where they argue, … with regard to … a very heavy stone. … Rabbi Akiva holds … like … menstruating woman … just as a menstruating woman transmits impurity via a very heavy stone, so too, idolatry transmits impurity via a very heavy stone. And the Rabbis hold … like … a creeping animal; just as a creeping animal does not transmit impurity via a very heavy stone, so too, idolatry does not transmit impurity via a very heavy stone.

And … to Rabbi Akiva, … for what halakha was it juxtaposed to a creeping animal? … to its accessories, … And according to the Rabbis, for what halakha was it juxtaposed to a menstruating woman? To … carrying. And … let the Torah juxtapose it to an … carcass, … Yes, it is indeed so. … However, … Just as a menstruating woman … not … limbs, … so too, idolatry does not … limbs, … But that which Rav Ḥama bar Guria raised as a dilemma: Does idolatry have … limbs or does it not … limbs? Resolve … from this, as according to … the Rabbis, it does not … limbs. … Rav Ḥama bar Guria raised the dilemma in accordance with … Rabbi Akiva

And … Rabbi Elazar said: With regard to a very heavy stone, everyone agrees … does not transmit impurity … Where they disagree … with regard to … carrying. Rabbi Akiva holds … like … a menstruating woman: Just as a menstruating woman transmits impurity through carrying, so too, idolatry transmits impurity through carrying. And the Rabbis hold … like … a creeping animal: Just as a creeping animal does not transmit impurity through carrying, so too, idolatry does not transmit impurity through carrying. … And … Rabbi Akiva’s … to what halakha was … juxtaposed to a creeping animal? … to … its accessories … And … the Rabbis, … to what halakha was … juxtaposed to a menstruating woman? … Just as a menstruating woman does not … through … limbs, so too, idolatry does not … through … limbs.

And … Rabbi Akiva, … to what halakha was … juxtaposed to a menstruating woman? … carrying, let it be juxtaposed to an … carcass … Yes, it is indeed so. However, … Just as a menstruating woman does not … through … limbs, … so too, an idol does not … through … limbs, … But that which Rav Ḥama bar Guria raised as a dilemma: Does idolatry have … limbs or does it not … through its limbs; resolve … from this, as according to both the Rabbis and Rabbi Akiva, it does not … through limbs. … Rav Ḥama bar Guria taught in accordance with … Rabba and raised the dilemma in accordance with … Rabbi Akiva.

raises an objection … idolatry … like … a creeping animal, and … its accessories … like … a creeping animal. Rabbi Akiva says: … idolatry … like … a menstruating woman, and … its accessories … like … a creeping animal. Granted, … to … Rabbi Elazar, … well. However, … to … Rabba, it is difficult. … Rabba … said to you: Is … stronger than … mishna … which taught: Its wood and stones and dirt transmit impurity like a creeping animal? … we established: What … like a creeping animal? … that it does not transmit impurity by means of a very heavy stone. Here too, … it does not transmit impurity via a very heavy stone.

raises an objection … A gentile man and a gentile woman, … idolatry and its accessories, … They … and not their movement, … Rabbi Akiva says: … they and their movement … Granted, … to … Rabbi Elazar, … well; however, … to … Rabba, it is difficult. Rabba … said to you: And according to your reasoning, … a gentile man and a gentile woman as well, … they … and their movement … not … Wasn’t it taught … “Speak to the children of Israel … the children of Israel become impure through … emission of a zav, and gentiles do not become impure through … emission of a zav? But … decreed that they should be … like a zav for all their … matters.

Rather, Rabba explains … in accordance with his reasoning: A gentile man and a gentile woman … they and their movement and their very heavy stone. … idolatry … it and its movement but not its very heavy stone. Rabbi Akiva says: Idolatry … it and its movement and its very heavy stone. And Rabbi Elazar explains … in accordance with his reasoning … A gentile man and a gentile woman … they and their movement and their very heavy stone. Idolatry … it and not its movement. And Rabbi Akiva says: Idolatry … it and its movement.

Rav Ashi strongly objects to … what … they … Rather, Rav Ashi said, this is what … is saying: … a gentile man and a gentile woman, whether they moved others or others moved them, … are ritually impure. … Idolatry that moved others, … ritually pure; … others who moved it are ritually impure. … its accessories, whether they moved others or others moved them, … ritually pure. Rabbi Akiva says: A gentile man and a gentile woman and idolatry, whether they moved others or others moved them, … are ritually impure. Its accessories, whether they moved others or others moved them, … ritually pure.

idolatry, granted, … where others moved it … found. However, … moved others, … can it be found? … Rami, son of Rav Yeiva, said, … as we learned … the zav … on … pan of a … scale, and food and drinks … on … second pan, … the zav tipped … are ritually impure

tipped the scales, they … ritually pure. … In accordance with whose … is that which was taught … All impure items that move … pure, … except for movement by a zav, which has no counterpart in the whole Torah in its entirety? Let us say … not in accordance with … Rabbi Akiva, as if … in accordance with … Rabbi Akiva, there is also … idolatry. … Even … you say … Rabbi Akiva, teach: Zav and everything similar to it.

Rav Ḥama bar Guria raised a dilemma: Does idolatry have … limbs or does it not … through limbs? … where a common … person can restore it … do not raise the dilemma, as … considered to be attached … where you … raise the dilemma … where a common … person cannot restore it … What … since a common … person cannot restore it, … considered broken? Or perhaps … it is not lacking … And some raise this dilemma in … direction … where a common … person cannot restore it … do not raise the dilemma, as … considered to be broken. When you … raise the dilemma … where a common … person can restore it … What … since a common … person can restore it, … considered attached? Or perhaps … at present, it is in pieces and permitted? … let it stand

Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami raised a dilemma: What … idolatry … less than an olive-bulk? Rav Yosef strongly objected to this: … to what … If you say … to the matter of the prohibition … let it only be … Zevuv, the Baal of Ekron, … as it was taught … “And they made Baal Berit into their god” … this is … Zevuv, the Baal of Ekron. … teaches that each and every … made an image of his god and placed it in his pocket. When he remembered it, he removed it from his pocket and embraced and kissed it. … Rather, … What … to the matter of impurity? … Since … is juxtaposed to a creeping animal, just as a creeping animal … a lentil-bulk, so too, idolatry … a lentil-bulk. Or perhaps … is juxtaposed to a corpse, … just as a corpse … when … an olive-bulk, so too, idolatry … when … an olive-bulk.

Rav Avya said, and some say … Rabba bar Ulla … Come … hear … that … was taught … Idolatry … less than an olive-bulk has no impurity at all, as it is stated: … and cast its powder upon the graves of the common people” … Just as a corpse … an olive-bulk, so too, idolatry … an olive-bulk.

And … the Rabbis, … to what halakha was … juxtaposed to a creeping animal? … it does not transmit impurity through carrying. … to a menstruating woman … limbs. … to a corpse … does not transmit impurity when … a lentil-bulk. … say … to … a stringency. … to what halakha did the Torah juxtapose … to a creeping animal? … to … transmits impurity when … a lentil-bulk. … to a menstruating woman … to … transmits impurity via a very heavy stone; … the Torah juxtaposed … to a corpse to … transmits impurity … by a tent, … The impurity of idolatry is by rabbinic law. And … a leniency and a stringency, we juxtapose … lenient … we do not juxtapose to … the stringent
MISHNA: … From where … that the ship is ritually pure, … As it is stated: “The way of a ship in the midst of the sea”

GEMARA: … obvious. … a ship is in the midst of the sea. … this … teaches us … like … the sea. Just as the sea is ritually pure … so too, a boat is ritually pure … It was taught … Ḥananya says: … is derived from … a sack, … Just as a sack, … is carried … full and empty, so too, any … is carried … full and empty … to exclude a ship, … is not carried … full and empty,

What is … between … There is … between them … a ship made from earthenware … the one who said … “A ship in the midst of the sea,” this … also in the midst of the sea. … according to the one who said … sack, … those … that are written … together with sack … If it is carried … full and empty, yes, … not … no, … However, an earthenware ship … even though it is not carried … full and empty.

Alternatively, … Jordan ship, … According to the one who said … “A ship in the midst of the sea,” this is also a ship in the midst of the sea. … According to the one who said … carried full and empty, this is also carried … full and empty, … As Rabbi Ḥanina ben Akavya said: For what … they say that a Jordan ship can become impure? Because they load it on dry land … and … lower it into the water. … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: One should never prevent himself from … the study hall for even one moment, as this mishna … was taught for several years in the study hall, but its reason was not revealed until Rabbi Ḥanina ben Akavya came and explained it.

Rabbi Yonatan said: One should never prevent himself from … the study hall or from … matters of Torah, even at the moment of death, as it is stated: “This is the Torah: A person who dies in a tent” … even at the moment of death, one should engage in … Torah. Reish Lakish said: Matters of Torah only endure in a person who kills himself over … as it is stated: “This is the Torah: A person who dies in a tent,” … Rava said:

And … to Ḥananya, … carrying by oxen considered carrying? … Yes, … we learned … there are three … wagons: … like a chair, … ritually impure … treading. … like a bed … ritually impure … impurity … a corpse. … of stone, … ritually pure … from any … And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: And if … there is … receptacle for pomegranates, … impure with impurity … a corpse.
there are three … chests: A chest that opens from the side, … ritually impure … impurity … treading … from the top … with impurity … a corpse. And … that comes … size, … ritually pure … from any

The Sages taught … treading, an earthenware vessel is ritually pure. … Rabbi Yosei says: … even … a ship. … What is … saying? Rav Zevid said … is saying the following: … treading, an earthenware vessel is ritually pure; however, … touches … impure. And an earthenware ship … impure … in accordance with … Ḥananya. Rabbi Yosei says: Even a boat is ritually pure, in accordance with … tanna … our … Rav Pappa strongly objects to this … what … even … Rather, Rav Pappa said … is saying the following: … treading, an earthenware vessel is ritually pure, and … its contact … it is impure. And … a wooden vessel … both its … treading and its contact … impure. And a Jordan ship is ritually pure in accordance with … tanna … our … Rabbi Yosei says: Even the boat is impure … in accordance with … Ḥananya.

And from where do we … treading, an earthenware vessel is ritually pure? Ḥizkiya said: … as the verse states: “And whoever touches his bed … juxtaposes his bed to himself. Just as he has … purification … in a ritual bath, so too, his bed … has … purification in a ritual bath.

the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught … shall be for her like the bed of her menstrual period” … juxtaposes her bed to herself: Just as she has … purification in a ritual bath, so too, her bed … has … purification in a ritual bath. … to the exclusion of an earthenware vessel, which does not have … purification in a ritual bath. Rabbi Ila strongly objects … From where … a … mat … from … a corpse?

And it is … an … inference: … If small … pitchers … pure … to … a zav, … become ritually impure from … a corpse; is it not logical that a … mat, … impurity from a zav, will … ritually impure from … a corpse? And why … Isn’t it … it does not have … purification in a ritual bath? Rabbi Ḥanina said to him: There, … it is different because there is … in … of its kind,

said to … May the all-Merciful save us from this opinion. … On the contrary, may the all-Merciful save us from your opinion. And what is the reason … two verses are written. … it is written: “And whoever touches his bed … And … it is written: “Every bed on which the zav lies shall be impure; … How … these … there is … in … of its kind, even though it … does not have purification in a ritual bath, … there is no … in … of its kind, … juxtaposes his bed to himself.

Rava said: … treading, an earthenware vessel is ritually pure … from here, … “And any open vessel that does not have a sealed cover on it … there is a sealed cover on it, it is pure. Are we not dealing … where one designated … for … his wife, … menstruating woman? And … the Torah states … ritually pure?

MISHNA: … From where … that … a garden bed that is six by six handbreadths, that one may plant five … seeds in it? … four … on … the four sides of the garden bed and one in the middle. … as it is stated: “For as the earth brings forth its growth, and as a garden causes its seeds to grow, … Its seed, … is not stated; rather, its seeds,

GEMARA: … From where is it inferred … Rav Yehuda said … “For as the earth brings forth its growth” … “brings forth” … one … “its vegetation” … one, … that … two. “Its seeds,” … two, … that … four. “Cause to grow” is one … five
And the Sages … an accepted … that five … in … six- … do not draw sustenance from one another.

And from where do we … that … the Sages … an accepted … is a … matter, … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: What … which is written: “You shall not cross your neighbor’s border, which they of the old times have set … you shall not cross the border that the early … set, … What … The early … set? Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yonatan said: What is … which was written: “These are the sons of Seir the Horite who inhabit the land, … And is everyone … inhabitants of the heavens, … Rather, … that they were experts in the settlement of the land, as they would say: This … full … of a rod … for olive … this full … of a rod … for grapes, this full … of a rod … for figs. And … Horites [ḥori] … they smelled [heriḥu] the earth … And … Hivites [ḥivi] … Rav Pappa said: … they would taste the earth like a snake [ḥivya] … Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said … Horites [ḥori] … they became free [benei ḥorin] of their possessions

Rav Asi said: … garden bed … internal … is six … excluding … its boundaries, … That was also taught … The internal … of a garden bed is six … How much … its boundaries? … as we learned … Rabbi Yehuda says: … width … is like the width of a foot. … Rabbi Zeira said, and some say … Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa … said: What is the reason … Rabbi Yehuda? As it is written: “And you water it with your foot like a garden of herbs” … just as … foot is a handbreadth … so too, the boundary … is also a handbreadth

Rav said: … a garden bed … we learned this … in a desolate area … isn’t there space … the corners, … The school … Rav taught in the name of Rav: … where one fills … corners … And let him plant on the outside and not fill up the inside,

a decree lest one will fill the corners … And … should merely be … a triangular [rosh tor] … vegetables. Didn’t we learn … a triangular … vegetables was protruding into another field, it is permitted; … because the end of the field is distinguishable. … There is no … triangular plot in a garden bed.
And Shmuel said: … we learned this … a garden bed among garden beds, … Don’t the seeds become intermingled with one another? … where one inclines … row to here, … and … row to here,

Ulla said: They raise a dilemma in the West, … What … one opened a single furrow across its entirety? … Rav Sheshet said: … intermingling … comes and nullifies the row. … Rav Asi said: Its intermingling does not disqualify the row. Ravina raised an objection to … Rav Ashi … One who plants two rows of cucumbers … two rows of gourds … two rows of Egyptian beans, it is permitted … one row of cucumbers and one row of gourds and one row of Egyptian beans, it is prohibited … Here, it is different because there are branches

Rav Kahana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who wishes to fill his entire garden with vegetables … make a garden bed … six by six … and make five circles inside it … and fills its corners … whatever … he wants.

Aren’t there … between … The school of Rabbi Yannai say … where one leaves … in between … barren … Rav Ashi said: … If … were planted lengthwise, he plants … widthwise; … widthwise, he plants … lengthwise. Ravina raised an objection to … Rav Ashi: … the work … of a vegetable … a vegetable … six handbreadths. And one views them
as a … board. … like a … board, it is permitted; … when that is not … prohibited. … to introduce a different leniency. … to permit a triangular plot that protrudes from it

MISHNA: … From where … that … discharges semen … on the third day … is ritually impure, … as it is stated … prepare yourselves for three days, … From where … that one may wash the circumcision on the third day, … it occurs on Shabbat? As it is stated: “And it came to pass on the third day when they were in pain” … From where … that one ties a scarlet strip … to the head of … scapegoat … As it is stated: “If your sins be like scarlet, they will become white like snow” … From where … that smearing … is like drinking … on Yom Kippur? Although there is no proof for this, there is an allusion to it, as it is stated: “And it comes into his inward parts like water and like oil into his bones”

GEMARA: … The first clause … is not in accordance with … Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya. The latter clause … is in accordance with … Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya. As, if … in accordance with … Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, we heard him … ritually pure. … He who does not establish … tanna’im, … teaches … the first clause: … ritually pure, and establishes the entire … in accordance with … Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya. And he who establishes … tanna’im, … first clause … the Rabbis, and the latter clause is … Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

the Sages taught … discharges semen … on the third day is ritually pure; … the statement of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya. Rabbi Yishmael says: … Sometimes there are four … periods … Sometimes there are five … periods … Sometimes there are six … periods … Rabbi Akiva says: … always five … periods. And if … part of the first period passed, she is given part of the sixth period

spices … equivalent … to season an easily … egg. The … raises a contradiction … Spices, … two or three … prohibitions, … of a single species … or … of three … species, are prohibited, and they join together with each other … And Ḥizkiya said:

They taught … in … sweet types, because they are fit … to sweeten … pot. … The reason … that they are suitable to sweeten the … pot … However, … that is not so, … do not … Here, too, … they are suitable to sweeten

nutshells, pomegranate peels, safflower and madder, … equivalent … to dye a small garment … And … raised a contradiction … One who carries out herbs … soaked … equivalent … to dye a sample … for the shuttle … Wasn’t it stated with regard to that … Rav Naḥman said … Rabba bar Avuh said: … because a person does not … trouble to soak herbs … to dye a sample for … shuttle

urine. … taught … urine that is up to forty days old. … natron, … taught … Alexandrian natron … and not … natron … Anpantrin, … borit … Rav Yehuda said: That is sand. … Wasn’t it taught … Borit and sand? … Rather, what is borit? … sulphur.

The Gemara raises an objection … They added … ornithogalum and wormwood, and borit, and aloe. And if it would enter your mind … sulphur, is there sulphur … of the Sabbatical year? Didn’t we learn … this is the principle: Anything that has a root … is … the Sabbatical year, and … that does not have a root is not … the Sabbatical year. Rather, what … borit? … aloe. … Wasn’t it taught … And borit and aloe? … Rather, … two types … aloe.

cimolian earth … Rav Yehuda said: … pull out stick in [shelof dotz]. … eshlag … Shmuel said: I asked all of the seafarers … and they told me … it is called shonana, and … found in the shell of the pearl, and is removed using an iron skewer.

MISHNA: … pepper … any amount. … tar … any amount. … kinds of perfumes and … kinds of metals … any amount. … stones of the altar or earth of the altar, … mekek … scrolls, and mekek … their coverings, … any amount. That … store them … to bury them, … Rabbi Yehuda says: Even one who carries out accessories of idolatry … any amount, as it is stated: “And there shall cleave nothing of the proscribed items to your hand”

GEMARA: … For what … is any amount of pepper suited? … For … mouth odor. For what … is any amount of tar suited? … headache. … any amount … kinds of perfumes … The Sages taught … one who carries out … a foul odor … any amount. … fine … oil … any amount. … purple dye … any amount. … a virgin rosebud … one
kinds of metals … any amount. … For what … is any amount of metal suited, … It was taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Because … is fit to make a small nail.

The Sages taught … one who … says: … upon me … iron … Aḥerim say: He must … no less than a cubit by a cubit … For what … is … suited? Rav Yosef said: For a raven impediment. … And some say … Aḥerim say: He must … no less than … a raven impediment. And how much … Rav Yosef said: A cubit by a cubit. … copper must … no less than … a ma’a of silver. It was taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: One must … no less than … a small copper hook. … For what … is … suited? Abaye said: They … it … scrape the wicks … and clean … lamps

mekek … scrolls, and … mekek … coverings, … Rabbi Yehuda said: … mekek … scrolls, … tekhakh … silk, and … ila … grapes, and … pe … figs, and … ha … pomegranates, all … danger … A certain student was sitting before Rabbi Yoḥanan … was eating figs. … said to … My teacher, are there thorns in figs? … said to him: The pe killed that

MISHNA: One who carries out a merchant’s basket, even if there are many types … in it, is obligated … only one sin-offering, … garden seeds … less than a fig-bulk. Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: … five

cucumber seeds … two … squash seeds … two … seeds of Egyptian beans … two. … a live kosher locust … any amount. … dead … a fig-bulk. … tzipporet keramim, whether dead or alive, … any amount; … one stores them for medicinal purposes … Rabbi Yehuda says: Even one who carries out a live non-kosher locust … any amount, … people store … for a child … to play with it.

GEMARA: … And … raised a contradiction … compost and fine sand … equivalent … to fertilize a cabbage stalk; … the statement of Rabbi Akiva. And the Rabbis say: Equivalent … to fertilize a … leek. … Rav Pappa said: This … was … planted … That … was not … planted, because a person does not … trouble to carry out a single seed for planting.

cucumber … seeds, the Sages taught: One who carries out … pits … if … to plant, … two … If … to eat, … enough to fill a pig’s mouth. And how much is enough to fill a pig’s mouth? One … If … to burn … equivalent … to cook an easily … egg. If … to count, … two … Aḥerim say … five … The Sages taught: One who carries out two hairs from a horse’s tail … from a cow’s tail … is liable, since people store them to … traps. … stiff hair of a pig … one … palm fronds … two … palm vines,

tzipporet keramim, whether dead or alive, … any amount. … What is tzipporet keramim? Rav said: … palya biari. Abaye said: And … found in a palm tree that … one vine, and it is used … for wisdom. … eats its right half, … casts its left half into a copper tube, and seals it with sixty seals, and hangs it on his left arm. And … mnemonic … you … “A wise heart to his right and a foolish heart to his left” … And one … grows wise as much as he wants, and studies as much as he wants, and … eats the other half, as if … not … his learning … be forgotten.

Rabbi Yehuda says: Even one who carries out … And … first tanna holds … not … What is the reason … perhaps … will eat it. … If so, … also … kosher locust, … as … that Rav Kahana stood before Rav and passed a … kosher locust near his mouth. … said to … Put it down, … people will not … say: He is eating it and violating … of “You shall not make yourselves detestable” … Rather, … perhaps it will die and he will eat it. And Rabbi Yehuda, … If … dies, … child will eulogize it

MISHNA: One who stores … for sowing, or as a sample, or for medicinal purposes and carried it out on Shabbat is liable … any amount. … And any … person is only liable … if … its measure … and then brought it back in, … he is only liable if … its measure

GEMARA: … Why does … teach: One who stores … Let … teach: One who carries out … for planting, or as a sample, or for medicinal purposes is liable … any amount. … Abaye said: With what we are dealing here? … where one stored it … and forgot why he stored it, and now he carries it out … no … purpose.
Lest you say … intention is … nullified, … teaches us … anyone who performs … performs … with the original … in mind.

Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: Rabbi Meir deemed liable one who carried out even a single wheat … sowing … obvious. We learned … any amount. … Lest you say … any amount … to exclude … a dried fig- … and actually … only liable if there is … an olive-bulk … teaches us … Rav Yitzḥak the son … Rav Yehuda strongly objects to this: But now, … one who planned to carry out … his entire house … so too, is he only liable when he carries it out … There, … his intention is … irrelevant by … all … people,

And any … person is only liable … if … its measure … The mishna … not in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, as it was taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar stated a principle: Anything that is not fit to be stored, and … not … store … like it, but it was deemed fit … by this … and he stored it, and another … came and carried out … that … is rendered liable by the thought of this

Rava said … Rav Naḥman said: … one carried out … dried fig-bulk … for eating, and … reconsidered … for sowing; … alternatively, … for sowing and reconsidered … for eating, he is liable. … obvious. … Go here … there is a measure … and go here … there is a measure … Lest you say … we require … lifting and placing … with a single, … intention, and that is not … teaches us

Rava raised a dilemma: … one who carried out half a dried fig- … sowing, … and expanded … and … reconsidered … for … for eating, what … If you say … there, … he is liable … go here … there is a measure … and go here … there is a measure … here, … since at the time that he carried it out there was not a measure … eating, … he … not liable. Or, perhaps, … had … silent and had no intention with regard to … he … liable … intention … sowing, … now too, he is liable

And if you say … had … silent and had no intention with regard to … he … liable … intention … sowing, now too, he … liable, … he carried out … of a dried fig-bulk for … eating, and … shriveled … and he reconsidered … for … sowing, … what … Here, certainly had … silent and had no intention with regard to … the original intention he is not liable … or perhaps we follow … present and he is liable. And if you say … we follow … present, and he is liable, … one carried out a dried fig-bulk … for … eating, and it shriveled … and then it expanded … what … Is there disqualification with regard to … Shabbat? … Or, … there is no disqualification with regard to … Shabbat. … let them stand

Rava raised a dilemma before Rav Naḥman: … one threw an olive-bulk of teruma into an impure house, what … to what … If … with regard to Shabbat, … we require … a dried fig-bulk, … if … to ritual impurity, … we require … food … an egg-bulk, … Actually, … with regard to Shabbat. And … where there is less than an egg-bulk of food … and this … completes … to an egg-bulk. … What … from … that … joins together … with regard to ritual impurity … he is also liable with regard to Shabbat? Or perhaps, all matters … Shabbat require a dried fig-bulk … said to him: We … learned … Abba Shaul says: … the two loaves … and the showbread … is a dried fig-bulk. … And why … Let us say: From … with regard to the matter of

leaving … an olive-bulk, … with regard to Shabbat, … also … an olive-bulk. … How can you make that comparison? There, … from … that he took it beyond the courtyard wall it was disqualified … leaving. … Shabbat, he is only liable when he takes it into the public domain, … Here, … Shabbat and … impurity … come simultaneously.

and then brought it back in, he is only liable … its measure … obvious. … Abaye said: With what are we dealing here? … where he threw it into the storehouse and its place is … discernible … Lest you say … because its location is discernible … maintains its original status, … teaches us … from … that he threw it into the storehouse, … he nullified

MISHNA: One who carries out food … and placed it on the threshold … whether he then carried it out … or another person carried it out, he is exempt because he did not perform his prohibited labor … all at once. … placed a basket that is full of fruit on the outer threshold, … even though most of … fruit … outside … exempt until he carries out the entire basket.

GEMARA: … What … this threshold … If you say … a threshold … the public domain, … exempt? Didn’t he carry out … from the private domain to the public domain? Rather, … a threshold … the private domain, … Whether he then carried it out … or another person carried it out, he is exempt? … Didn’t he carry out … from the private domain to the public domain?

Rather, … a threshold … a karmelit. And … teaches us the following: The reason … that … came to rest in a karmelit. However, … did not come to rest in a karmelit, he is liable … the mishna … not in accordance with … ben Azzai, as it was taught … One who carries out … from a store, … to a plaza, … via a colonnade, … is liable … And ben Azzai … exempt

placed a basket that is full of fruit … Ḥizkiya said: They only taught … with regard to a basket full of cucumbers and gourds, … However, … full of mustard … he is liable … Apparently, he holds that the fusion … vessel is not considered fusion. … And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even … full of mustard … he is exempt. Apparently, he holds that the fusion … vessel is considered fusion.

Rabbi Zeira said: … the mishna … not precisely … Ḥizkiya, and … not precisely … Rabbi Yoḥanan. … not precisely … Ḥizkiya, as … taught: Until he carries out the entire basket. … The reason … the entire basket. However, … all the fruit, he is exempt. Apparently, … holds … fusion … vessel is considered fusion. … not precisely … Rabbi Yoḥanan, as … taught: Even though most of … fruit … outside. … The reason … most of the fruit … However, … all … fruit … even though … the basket … bound inside, he is liable. Apparently, … holds … the fusion … vessel is not considered fusion.

However, … difficult. … Ḥizkiya resolves … with his reasoning, and Rabbi Yoḥanan resolves … with his reasoning. … Ḥizkiya resolves … to his reasoning. … Until he carries out the entire basket; in what … is this statement said? … a basket full of cucumbers and gourds. However, … full of mustard … he becomes as one who carried out the entire basket, and he is liable … Rabbi Yoḥanan resolves … to his reasoning: … Even though most of … fruit … outside, … and … not only … most … fruit, but even … all the fruit … exempt, until he carries out the entire basket.

The Gemara raises an objection … One who carries out the merchant’s basket … and placed it on the outer threshold … even though most of … types … outside, he is exempt until he carries out the entire basket. It … enter your mind … of bundles … is difficult … to … Ḥizkiya, … Ḥizkiya … said to you: With what are we dealing here? With stalks [urnasei].

Rav Beivai bar Abaye … raised an objection … One who steals a purse on Shabbat is liable … because he was already liable for theft … before he came to … the prohibition … Shabbat … was dragging … and exiting … he is exempt … as … The prohibition of theft and the prohibition of Shabbat … all at once. … And if it enters your mind … fusion … vessel is considered fusion, … the prohibition of theft precedes the prohibition of Shabbat.
If … where he carried it out by way of its mouth, indeed that is so, … with what are we dealing here? … where he carried it out by … underside … Isn’t there the area of the seam?

for if he wishes, he can tear … and take … to … metal strips. … And since … has laces … that he carry it out so … its mouth … untie … and remove … And … laces … bound inside … does not have laces. And if you wish, say … it has … and … wound around

And, so too, Rava said: They only taught … with regard to … a basket full of cucumbers and gourds. However, … full of mustard … he is liable. Apparently, … holds: fusion … vessel is not considered fusion. Abaye said: Even … full of mustard … he is exempt. Apparently, … holds: Fusion … vessel is considered fusion. … Abaye … assumed the opinion of Rava, … Rava assumed the opinion of Abaye. And a contradiction is raised … Abaye … Abaye; and a contradiction is raised … Rava … Rava.

As it was stated … one who carries out fruit into the public domain. Abaye said: … in … hand, he is liable … in a vessel, … he is exempt. And Rava said: … in … hand, he is exempt … in a vessel, he is liable.

Reverse … in his hand, he is liable. … Didn’t we learn … the homeowner extended his hand into the public domain, and … the poor person took … from … or the poor person placed … into … carried … into … both are exempt. … There, … above three … Here, … below three

MISHNA: One who carries out … whether … in his right … or in his left … in his lap or on his shoulders, he is liable. … as … carrying … by the sons of Kehat … in an … backhanded … with his foot, … with his mouth, … with his elbow, with his ear, … with his hair, … with his belt [punda] whose opening … downward, … between his belt and his cloak, … with the hem of his cloak, … with his shoe, … with his sandal, he is exempt … he did not carry … out in a manner … of those who carry.

GEMARA: Rabbi Elazar said: One who carries out a load … above ten handbreadths, … he is liable, as … carrying … by the sons of Kehat. … And from where do we … carrying … by the sons of Kehat … For it is written … surrounds the Tabernacle, and the altar, … juxtaposes … altar to the Tabernacle. … just as the Tabernacle … ten cubits … so too, … altar … ten cubits high.

And from where do we … the Tabernacle itself … As it is written: … the length of a board shall be ten cubits” … And it is written … “And he spread the tent over the Tabernacle, … And Rav said: Moses, our teacher, spread it … From here you … derive that the height of the Levites was ten cubits. … And … learned … every burden that is carried with poles, one-third … is above … and two-thirds are below … It is found, … that … was very high,

And if you wish, say … the Ark … as the Master said: … Ark … nine … and the Ark-cover … handbreadth, for … ten. And … learned … every burden that is carried with poles, one-third … is above … and two-thirds are below … It is found, … that … stood ten … above … And let us derive … from Moses, … Perhaps Moses … different … the Master said: The Divine Presence only rests upon … wise, mighty, wealthy, and tall.

Rav said in the name of Rabbi Ḥiyya: One who carries out a burden on his head on Shabbat is liable … a sin-offering, as the people of Hotzal do so. … And … the people of Hotzal … the majority of the world? … Rather, if … was stated, it was stated as follows. Rav said in the name of Rabbi Ḥiyya: … a resident of Hotzal carried out a burden on his head on Shabbat he is liable, as the people of his city do so. … let his intention be … irrelevant by … all … people. … Rather, if … was stated, it was stated as follows. One who carries out a burden on his head is exempt.
And if you say … the people of Hotzal do so … their intention is … irrelevant by … all … people.

MISHNA: One who intends to carry out … before him, and … came … behind him, is exempt. … behind him and it came … before him, he is liable. In truth they said: A woman who girded herself in a … sinar … whether … before her or behind her, … she is liable, as it is common … to be reversed. Rabbi Yehuda says: Even those … who receive notes [pittakin],

GEMARA: … What is different … before him and it came … behind him … exempt? … his intention was not realized. … behind him, and it came … before him, … also … his intention was not realized. Rabbi Elazar said: … is disjointed, … He who taught this … did not teach that … Rava said: And what difficulty … Perhaps … before him, and it came … behind him, this is the reason that he is exempt: He intended to … outstanding protection, … and … he managed … reduced protection. … behind him, and it came … before him, this is the reason he is liable: He intended to … reduced protection, and … he managed … outstanding protection.

Rather, what is the difficulty … inference … the mishna … difficult. One who intends to carry out … before him, and … came … behind him, is exempt. … behind him, and … came … behind him, is liable. Say … latter clause … behind him, and it came … before him, is … where … liable. … behind him, and … came … behind him, is exempt. … Rabbi Elazar said: … is disjointed. He who taught this … did not teach that

Rav Ashi said: What difficulty … Perhaps … is stating … not necessary, … It was not necessary … behind him, and it came … behind him, is liable. … because his intention was realized. However, it was necessary for … even … behind him, and it came … before him, … It would have entered your mind to say: Since his intention was not realized, he should not be liable. … teaches us: … he intended to … reduced protection, and … he managed … outstanding protection, … liable.

And … behind him, and it came … behind him, is … tanna’im, as it was taught … One who carried out coins in his money belt, and its opening was … up, is liable … its opening … down, Rabbi Yehuda deems … liable, and the Rabbis deem … exempt. Rabbi Yehuda said to … Do you not agree … behind him, and it came … behind him, that he is liable? … And they said to him: And do you not agree … one … in a backhanded manner or with his foot is exempt?

Rabbi Yehuda said: I said one thing … and they said one thing … I did not find a response to their statement, and they did not find a response to my statement. From … that he said to them: Do you not agree … Can it not be inferred that the Sages deem … exempt … And according to your reasoning, … that … said to … Do you not agree … be inferred … Rabbi Yehuda deems … liable, … Wasn’t it taught … in a backhanded manner … his foot, everyone agrees … exempt?

Rather, … behind him, and … came … behind him, everyone agrees … liable. … in a backhanded manner … his foot, everyone agrees … exempt. Where they disagree … in his money belt with its opening … down. … Master, … likens it to … behind him and … came … behind him, … and … Master, … liken it … in a backhanded manner … his foot,
In truth they said: A woman who … It was taught … every … In truth, that is the … halakha. … Rabbi Yehuda says … even those who receive notes, … We learned … Because the royal scribes do this,

MISHNA: One who carries a … mass out to the public domain … is liable. … two carried it out … they are exempt … one … is unable to carry it out … and … two … carried it out, they are liable. And Rabbi Shimon deems … exempt

GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said … Rav said, and some say … Abaye said … and some say … it was taught in a baraita: … this … is capable … and that … is capable … Rabbi Meir deems … liable, and Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon deem … exempt. … this … is incapable and that … is incapable … Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Meir deem … liable, and Rabbi Shimon deems … exempt. … this … is capable, … that … is incapable, … everyone agrees … liable.

That was also taught … One who carries a … mass out to the public domain … is liable. … two carried it out … Rabbi Meir deems … liable, and Rabbi Yehuda says: If one is incapable of carrying it out, and two carried it out, they are liable. And if not, … they are exempt. And Rabbi Shimon deems … exempt … From where are these matters … as our Sages taught … by performing it, … one who performs … in its entirety … and not one who performs part of it. How so? … two … were holding a pitchfork and gathering … a shuttle and weaving … a quill and writing, … a reed and carrying it out to the public domain, … might … they are liable, … the verse states: “By performing it.” One who performs … in its entirety … and not one who performs … part of it.

a round cake of figs, … and they carried … out to the public domain, … a beam and carried … out to the public domain, Rabbi Yehuda says: If one … is incapable of carrying it out … and two … carried it out, they are liable. And if not, … they are exempt. Rabbi Shimon says: Even if … is incapable of carrying it out … and two … carried it out, they are exempt. It is … that … it is stated: “By performing it” … An individual who performs … is liable, two … who perform … are exempt.

With regard to what do they disagree? … over … this verse: “And if one person among the common people sins unwittingly by performing it, … Rabbi Shimon holds: Three exclusionary … are written … A person who sins, one who sins, … by performing it he sins. … One … to exclude … this … lifts … and that … places it … And one … to exclude … this … is capable … and that … is … capable, … And one … to exclude … this … is incapable … and that … is incapable

And Rabbi Yehuda … One … to exclude … this … lifts … and that person places … And one … to exclude … this … is capable … and that … is … capable. And one … to exclude … an individual who performed … in accordance with the ruling of a court. … And Rabbi Shimon … an individual who performed … in accordance with the ruling of a court is liable

And … Rabbi Meir, … Is it written … A person who sins, one who sins, … by performing it he sins? … two exclusionary … are written, … one … to exclude … this … lifts … and that … places … and one … to exclude … individual who performed … in accordance with the ruling of a court.

the Master said: … this … is capable, … this … is incapable, … everyone agrees … he is liable. … Which of them is liable? Rav Ḥisda said: The one who is capable … as if … the one who is incapable … what is he doing … Rav Hamnuna said to … as he is assisting him. … said to him: … assists … is insubstantial.

Rav Zevid said in the name of Rava: We, too, also learned … was sitting on a bed, and … four garments beneath the … legs of the bed, they are … ritually impure. … because … is incapable of standing on three … And Rabbi Shimon deems … ritually pure, … if he was riding on an animal, and there were four garments beneath the legs of the animal, they are … ritually pure because … is capable of standing on three … And why … Aren’t … assisting each other … Is it not because we say: … that assists … insubstantial?

Rav Yehuda of Diskarta said: Actually, I will say to you … that assists is substantial. However, … is different here, … lifted … completely. … And since it sometimes lifts this … and sometimes lifts that … it should … a zav who turns over. Didn’t we learn … a zav who was lying on five benches or on five money belts, … along their length, they are impure. … across their width, they are ritually pure … he slept … there is uncertainty … he turned over on them. … are impure.
Rather, is it not … because we say: … that assists … insubstantial? … Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava: We, too, also learned

Rabbi Yosei says: … the horse, … renders … impure by means of … front legs. … the donkey, … by means of … hind legs. … a horse rests … on its front legs, and … donkey … on its hind legs. But why … Don’t … assist each other? Is … not because we say … one who assists is insubstantial? Rav Ashi said: We, too, also learned … Rabbi Eliezer says: … one of his feet was on a vessel, and one of his feet was on the floor, … one of his feet was on a stone, and one of his feet was on the floor, … we see, if the vessel was removed or the stone was removed, … he would … be capable of standing on one foot … his service is valid. And if … not … his service is invalid.

And why, … Don’t … assist each other? Isn’t … because we say: One who assists is insubstantial? Ravina said: We, too, also learned … he received … in his right … and his left … assisted … his service is valid. And why … Aren’t … assisting each other? Isn’t … because we say: One who assists is insubstantial? … from this

The Master said … this … is capable … and that … is capable … Rabbi Meir deems … liable. A dilemma was raised … Do we require … measure … for this … measure … for that … or perhaps one measure … for them all? Rav Ḥisda and Rav Hamnuna … One said: … measure … for this … measure … for that … And one said: One measure … for them all. Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava: We, too, also learned … was sitting on a bed, and … four garments beneath the … legs of the bed, they are … ritually impure because … is incapable of standing on three … And why … Let them require a measure of … a zav for this … and a measure … of a zav for that … Is it not because we say … one measure … for them all?

Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: We, too, also learned … a deer that entered the house, and one … locked … before it … one is liable … two … locked … they are exempt. … one is incapable of locking … and two … locked … they are liable. And why … Let them require a measure of trapping for this … and a measure … trapping for that … Is it not because we say … one measure … for them all? Ravina said: We, too, also learned … partners who stole … and slaughtered … they are obligated … And why … Let them require a measure of slaughtering for this … and a measure … slaughtering for that … Is it not because we say … one measure … for them all?

And Rav Ashi said: We, too, also learned … Two … who carried out a weaver’s reed … are liable. And why … Let them require a measure of carrying for this … and a measure … carrying for that … Is it not because we say … one measure … for them all? Rav Aḥa, son … Rava, said to Rav Ashi: … perhaps … has a … to cook an easily-cooked egg for this … and an easily-cooked egg for that … If so, let … teach us … an ordinary reed. What is different … weaver’s … And perhaps it has a … to weave a cloth for this … and to weave a cloth for that … Rather, … cannot be learned from this
taught before Rav Naḥman: Two … who carried out a weaver’s reed … are exempt, and Rabbi Shimon deems … liable. … Toward where … Rather, say … They are liable, and Rabbi Shimon deems … exempt.

MISHNA: One who carries out foods less than the measure … in a vessel … is exempt, even for … the vessel, because the vessel is secondary to … living … on a bed is exempt, even for … the bed, because the bed is secondary to … a corpse on a bed is liable. And similarly, … an olive-bulk of a corpse, or an olive-bulk of an animal carcass, or a lentil-bulk of a creeping animal, … is liable. And Rabbi Shimon deems … exempt.

GEMARA: The Sages taught … One who carries out the measure … foods in a vessel … is liable for … the food and exempt for … the vessel. And if that vessel was needed by him … he is liable even for … the vessel. … conclude from it … eats two olive-bulks of forbidden fat in … one lapse of awareness is liable … two … Rav Sheshet said: With what are we dealing here? … where
