Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Not all enclosures are identical. … Rav Yosef said … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: … halakha … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel … Abaye said to him: … halakha … by inference … disagree, … said to him: What difference is there to you … learn the lesson, … it be … a song?

The Sages taught … One who traps a deer … blind … sleeping is liable. … a lame, old, … sick … is exempt. Abaye said to Rav Yosef: What is different … these … and what is different … those … These, … are likely to run away … these, … are not likely to run away … Wasn’t it taught … sick … is liable … Rav Sheshet said: … not difficult. This … sick due to a fever, … that … sick with fatigue

The Sages taught … One who traps locusts, cicadas, hornets, or mosquitoes on Shabbat is liable. … the statement of Rabbi Meir. And the Rabbis say: … any … whose species is … trapped … liable, and … any … whose species is … not trapped … exempt. It was taught … another … One who traps locusts when there is dew is exempt. … when it is hot, he is liable. Elazar ben Mehavai says: If … were swarming, one is exempt … A dilemma was raised before them: … Elazar ben Mehavai apply to the first clause … apply to the latter … Come and hear … One who traps locusts when there is dew is exempt; … when it is hot is liable. Elazar ben Mehavai says: Even when it is hot, if they were swarming, one is exempt.

MISHNA: … a deer entered a house … and one locked … before it, he is liable … two … locked … they are exempt, … one … is incapable of locking … and two … locked it, they are liable … And Rabbi Shimon deems them exempt
GEMARA: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said … Shmuel said: One who traps a lion on Shabbat is not liable … unless he traps it in its cage,

MISHNA: … one person sat in the entrance … but did not fill … a second … sat and filled it, the second … is liable … the first person sat in the doorway and filled it, and a second person came and sat next to him, the first person is liable and the second is exempt even if the first person stood and went … To what is this … similar? To one who locks his house to secure it, and it turns out a deer … is … secured inside it.

GEMARA: Rabbi Abba said … Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said … Rav said: … a bird flew under the flaps of one’s clothing … , he may sit and secure it until dark … . Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak raised an objection … : … the first person sat in the doorway and filled it, and a second person came and sat next to him, the first person is liable and the second is exempt, even if the first person stood and went. What, does this not … , … exempt … , … it is prohibited … : No, … exempt and … permitted … : So too, it is reasonable … from … was taught in the latter clause … : To what is this … similar? To one who locks his house to secure it, and it turns out a deer … is … secured inside it. By inference, … exempt and … permitted, … . … : … , learn from it … .

Some say … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: We too learned … Even if the first person stood and went, the first … is liable and the second is exempt. What, does this not … exempt, and it is permitted? … No, … exempt and … prohibited. … from … that it is taught in the latter clause … To what is this … similar? To one who locks his house to secure it and it turns out a deer … is … secured inside it. By inference, … exempt and … permitted, … learn from it

Shmuel said: … all exempt … of Shabbat, … exempt … prohibited … with the exception of these three … exempt and … permitted … One is this … And from what … exempt and … permitted? From … was taught in the latter clause … To what is this … similar? To one who locks his house to secure it and it turns out a deer … is … secured inside. 
And another … One who drains an abscess … on Shabbat, if … to create a … opening in it, he is liable. … if … to drain fluid from it, he is exempt. And from what … exempt and … permitted? As we learned … A hand needle … to remove a thorn. … And another … One who traps a snake on Shabbat, if … deals with it so that it will not bite him … he is exempt. … if … for medicinal … he is liable. And from what … exempt and … permitted? As we learned … One may overturn a bowl on top of a lamp … so that … will not take hold … the ceiling beam; and … on top of a child’s feces … and on top of a scorpion so it will not bite,

MISHNA: … the eight creeping animals mentioned in the Torah, one who traps them or wounds them … is liable. … other abominations and crawling things, one who wounds them is exempt. One who traps them for … need is liable; … for no … need is exempt. … animals or birds that are in his possession, … one who traps them is exempt; and, … one who wounds them is liable.

GEMARA: … From … that it is taught … One who wounds them is liable, by inference they have skins. … Who is … tanna … Shmuel said: It is Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, as we learned … Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says: The eight creeping animals … have skins. … Rabba bar Rav Huna said … Rav … Even if you say … Rabbis, the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri only with regard to the matter … impurity, as it is written … “Those are for you the impure … to include the … skins of … as their flesh … However, with regard to … Shabbat, even the Rabbis concede

And, with regard to Shabbat, they do not disagree? Wasn’t … taught … One who traps one of the eight creeping animals mentioned in the Torah … one who wounds them is liable; … the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri. And the Rabbis say: … skin is … only

enumerated by the Sages … On the contrary, those that the Sages enumerated … do not have skins. And Abaye said: This is what … is saying: Only those that the Sages did not enumerate have skin discrete from … flesh. Rava said to him: Doesn’t … say … That those enumerated by the Sages … Rather, Rava said: This is what … is saying: Only the skin of those … enumerated by the Sages transmits impurity like flesh. … by inference that Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri … not enumerated by the Sages also transmit impurity? Isn’t … taught, … Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says: … eight creeping animals have skin … does not transmit impurity? Rav Adda bar Mattana said … resolve … this way: And the Rabbis say: With regard to impurity, those … enumerated by … Sages do not have skin.

But still, … they do not disagree with regard to the matter of Shabbat? Wasn’t it taught … One who traps one of the eight creeping animals mentioned in the Torah … is liable, … one who wounds them, if they are creeping animals that have skins? And what is … an irreversible wound? … the blood collects … even if it does not emerge. Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says: … eight creeping animals have skins.

Rav Ashi said: Who is … first tanna? … Rabbi Yehuda, who follows the texture … as we learned … Rabbi Yehuda says: … the lizard … the same … as the weasel … However, the Rabbis, who disagree with Rabbi Yoḥanan with regard to impurity, concede with regard to Shabbat … If so, the … the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, … It should … the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan … and those who disagree with him, … teach: The statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and those who disagree with him.

Levi raised a dilemma before Rabbi … From where … that a wound is … irreversible? … as it is written: “Can a Cushite change his skin, or a leopard its spots [ḥavarburotav]?” … What … ḥavarburotav … If you say that they are spotted marks … that … Or a leopard its spots, should … Or a leopard its colors. Rather, … similar to … a Cushite: Just like the skin of a Cushite will not change … so too a wound … does not reverse.

And … other abominations … one kills them … liable. … Who is … tanna … Rabbi Yirmeya said: It is … Rabbi Eliezer, as it was taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: One who kills lice on Shabbat is akin to one who kills a camel on Shabbat. … Rav Yosef strongly objects to this: … the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Eliezer only with regard to lice, … do not procreate. However, … other abominations and crawling things that procreate, they do not disagree

And … they both derived … from … ram … Rabbi Eliezer holds … like rams. Just as rams have their lives taken … so too, … any animal whose life is taken, … And the Rabbis … hold … like rams. Just as rams procreate, so too, … any … that procreates. … Abaye said to … And lice do not procreate? Didn’t the Master say: The Holy One, Blessed be He, sits and sustains … from the horns of wild oxen to the eggs of lice? … There is a species … that is called lice eggs,

And wasn’t it taught … Tefuyei, … and lice eggs? … There is a species … called lice eggs. … And … a flea, which procreates … and nevertheless, it was taught … one who traps a flea on Shabbat, Rabbi Eliezer deems him liable and Rabbi Yehoshua deems him exempt. Rav Ashi said: Are you raising a contradiction between trapping … killing? Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua disagree only … that … Sage, … holds … one is liable … a species that is not typically trapped; and … Sage, … holds … exempt … However, with regard to killing, even Rabbi Yehoshua concedes
one who traps … for … need is liable, … Who is … tanna … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: It is Rabbi Shimon, who said … a … labor … not for its own sake, one is exempt.

Some taught … to this: … one who drains an abscess … on Shabbat, if … to create an opening for it … is liable; if … to remove pus from it he is exempt. … Who is … tanna … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: It is Rabbi Shimon, who said … a … labor … not for its own sake, one is exempt.

Some teach the statement of … to this: … one who traps a snake on Shabbat, if … engages … its … so it does not bite him, he is exempt; if … for medicinal … he is liable. … Who is … tanna … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: It is Rabbi Shimon, who said … a … labor … not for its own sake, one is exempt.

Shmuel said: … one who removes a fish from the sea, when … has dried up the size of a sela, … liable. … Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said: … as long as … between its fins. Rav Ashi said: Do not say … it actually dried. Rather, … even if … that mucus has formed,

Mar bar Hamdurei said … Shmuel said: One who reached his hand into the innards of an animal … and detached a fetus that was in its womb is liable. … What is the reason … Rava said: Bar Hamdurei explained … to me. Didn’t Rav Sheshet say: One … detaches hops … from the shrubs and thorns … is liable for uprooting an object from its … growth? Here, too, … one is liable for uprooting an object from its … growth. Abaye said: One who detached

a mushroom from the handle of a pitcher … is liable for uprooting an object from its … growth. Rav Oshaya raised an objection … One who detaches … from a perforated flowerpot is liable, and … an imperforate … is exempt. … There, … that is not … grows. … here, … that is … it grows.

an animal or a bird … Rav Huna said: One may write phylacteries on … skin of a kosher bird. Rav Yosef said: What is he teaching us … that … has skin, we … learned … One who wounds … is liable. … Abaye said to him: He is teaching us many things, for if … from the mishna, I would have said … Since … has many holes … not … he teaches us as they say in the West, … Any hole over which ink passes … is not … a hole

Rabbi Zeira raised an objection … by its wings … must prepare … the skin … And if it should enter your mind … is skin, how does the verse include it … Abaye said: … it is skin, and … the Torah includes it

Some say … Rabbi Zeira said: We, too, have also learned … “By its wings,” … to include the skin. Granted, if you say … is skin, that is … the verse needs to … include it. … However, if you say … is not skin, why is a verse necessary to include it? … Abaye said to him: … Actually, I … say to you … it is not skin and, … it must be … it might have entered your mind to say … since there are many holes in it, … repulsive … teaches us

Mar, son … Ravina, raised a dilemma before Rav Naḥman bar Yitzhak: What is … writing phylacteries on the skin of a kosher fish? … said to him: If Elijah comes and says. … What does … If Elijah comes and says, … If you say … whether … has skin or whether it does not have skin … we see that it has skin. And furthermore, we learned … Fish bones and skin protect … under a tent … corpse. … Rather, if Elijah comes and says whether its foul smell has ceased from it or whether its foul smell has not ceased from it.

Shmuel and Karna were sitting on the bank of the Malka River. They saw that the water was rising and was murky. … said to Karna: A great man is coming from the West, … and his intestines are aching, and the water is rising to greet him. Go sniff … his container, … went … found Rav, … He said to him: From where … that one may write phylacteries only on the hide of a kosher animal? … said to him … as it is written: … so that God’s Torah will be in your mouth” … from those … that are permitted … in your mouth, … From where … that … blood is red? … as it is stated: “And the Moabites saw the water from afar, red like blood”

From where … that circumcision is … in that place? … It is stated here, … his foreskin [orlato] … and it is stated there, … thereof as forbidden [orlato]; … Just as there … is an item that bears fruit, here, too, … an item that bears fruit. … Say … one’s heart, as it is written: “And you shall circumcise the foreskin of [orlat] your heart” … Say … one’s ear, as it is written: “Behold, their ear is dull [areila] … One derives … complete … orlato from … complete … orlato; and one does not derive … complete … orlato from … incomplete … orlat,
said to him: What is your name? … Karna. … said to him: May it be the will … that a horn [karna] will emerge in his eyes.

Ultimately, … brought him into his house. He fed him barley bread and small fried fish, and gave him beer to drink, and he did not show him the lavatory so he would suffer from diarrhea. … Rav cursed … and said: Whoever causes me suffering, let his children not survive. … and so it was

tanna’im. … From where … that circumcision … in that place? … stated here, … orlato. And … stated there, … orlato. Just as there … is an item that bears fruit, here too, … an item that bears fruit; … the statement of Rabbi Yoshiya. Rabbi Natan says: … is not necessary … as it says: “And an uncircumcised man who does not circumcise the flesh of his foreskin [orlato], … place that distinguishes between a male and a female.

The Sages taught: One may write phylacteries on the hide of a kosher domesticated animal, and on the hide of a kosher non-domesticated animal, and on the hides of their … carcasses [neveilot], and … of animals with a condition that will cause them to die within twelve months [tereifot]. And one may wrap … with the hair of these … and sew … with their sinews; … a halakha … to Moses from Sinai that … phylacteries may be wrapped with the hair of these … and sewn with their sinews. But one may not write on the hide of a non-kosher animal, or on the hide of a non-kosher undomesticated animal, and it goes without saying … on their skins … neveilot … tereifot. And one may not wrap … with the hair … nor may one sew … with their sinews.

And this question was asked by a Boethusian to Rabbi Yehoshua HaGarsi: From where … that one may not write phylacteries on the hide of a non-kosher animal? … as it is written: … So that God’s Torah will be in your mouth.” … an item that is permitted … in one’s mouth, … If … so … on the skin of neveilot and tereifot … one … not write … He said to him: I will tell you a parable. To what is this similar? To two people who were sentenced to death by the king. One was killed … king … and one was killed … executioner [ispaklitor]. Which one is … praiseworthy? You … say: … that … king … killed. … then … should be eaten, … He said to him: The Torah said: “Do not eat any neveila” … and you say they should be eaten? … said to him: Well put [kalos].
MISHNA: One may not make brine [hilmei] on Shabbat,

but one may make salt water and dip one’s bread in it, and place it in cooked food. Rabbi Yosei said: But isn’t it … brine, whether … a large quantity or whether … a small quantity? And this is … salt water that is permitted: … one places oil initially into the water or into the salt.

GEMARA: … What is … saying … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: This is what he is saying: One may not prepare a large quantity of salt water, … on Shabbat, but one may prepare a small quantity of salt water.

Rabbi Yosei said: But isn’t it … brine whether … a large quantity or a small quantity? A dilemma was raised before … Rabbi Yosei … to prohibit … to permit … Rav Yehuda said: … to permit … from … is not teaching: Rabbi Yosei prohibits. Rabba said to him: From … that it is taught in the latter … And this is … salt water that is permitted, by inference, Rabbi Yosei … to prohibit … Rather, Rabba said: … to prohibit … And similarly, Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … to prohibit.

That was also taught … One may not prepare a large quantity of salt water to add to the pickled … that are inside a … earthenware shard … gistera] … However, one may prepare a small quantity of salt water and eat his bread with it and add it to cooked food. Rabbi Yosei said: Is it because this is a large quantity and this is a small quantity … this is prohibited and this is permitted? … will … say: A large … labor is prohibited … a small … labor is permitted. Rather, … they are both prohibited. And this is … salt water that is permitted: One may place oil and salt … or oil and water … and … provided one does not place water and salt … ab initio
Strong, radish, and citron are a mnemonic

Rabbi Yehuda bar Ḥaviva taught: One may not prepare strong salt water … What is strong salt water? Rabba and Rav Yosef bar Abba both said: Any … in which an egg can float. … And how much … Abaye said: Two-thirds salt and one-third water.

For what … prepared? Rabbi Abbahu said: … for fish brine [muraisa]. … Rabbi Yehuda bar Ḥaviva taught … One may not salt a radish or an egg on Shabbat … Rav Ḥizkiya said in the name of Abaye: … a radish is prohibited, and … an egg is permitted. Rav Naḥman said: Initially, I would salt radishes … I said: I am ruining it … as Shmuel said: Sharpness is good … radishes; … once I heard this, that when Ulla came … he said … in the West, … they salt many piles … do not salt … I certainly dip
Rabbi Yehuda bar Ḥaviva taught … a citron, a radish, and an egg, if it were not for their outer peel, … they would never emerge from the intestines,

When Rav Dimi came … he said: No person has ever drowned in the Sea of Sodom, … Rav Yosef said: Sodom is overturned and … statement is backward. … it is a man who does not drown … a plank sinks? Abaye said to him: He is saying … It is not necessary: It is not necessary … a plank … does not sink in any … water in the world. But even a man, who drowns in other … water in the world, does not drown in the Sea of Sodom. … What are … practical consequences … of this … Ravin was walking after Rabbi Yirmeya on the shore of the Sea of Sodom. … said to … What is … to wash oneself with this water on Shabbat, … said to him: … well

what … close and open … said to him: That … I did not hear … a similar case, … I did hear. As Rabbi Zeira said, sometimes he said it in the name … Rav Mattana and sometimes he said it in the name of Mar Ukva, and they both said … in the name … Shmuel’s father and … Levi: One … said: … wine inside the eye … is prohibited … on the eye, … is permitted. And one … said: Bland saliva, … even … on the eye … is prohibited

Conclude that Shmuel’s father is the one who said … wine inside the eye is prohibited … on the eye is permitted, from … that Shmuel said: A person may soak his bread in wine and place it on his eye on Shabbat. … he heard this … whom? … not that he heard it from his father? … And according to your reasoning, that … which Shmuel said: It is prohibited … bland saliva even on the eye … he heard this … whom? If we say that he heard it from his father, then Levi, … did … not say … one … Rather, one … heard from his father, and one … he heard one from Levi, and we do not know which … from his father … which … from Levi.

Mar Ukva said … Shmuel said: One may soak eye salves from Shabbat eve and place … on his eyes on Shabbat, and … need not be concerned … Bar Liva’ei was standing before Mar Ukva … He saw … who was opening and closing … said to him: Master Shmuel certainly did not permit … all of this. Rabbi Yannai sent … to Mar Ukva: Can the master send us some of Master Shmuel’s eye salves? … sent him … I will send … to you … you do not say I am miserly, but … this is what Shmuel said: … better a drop of cold … morning and washing the hands and feet with hot water … evening than all the eye salves in the world. … That was also taught … Rabbi Mona said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda: Better a drop of cold … morning and washing the hands and feet … evening than all the eye salves in the world.

he would say … A hand … eye should be severed … A hand … nose should be severed. A hand … mouth should be severed. A hand … ear should be severed. A hand … wound should be severed. A hand … member should be severed, … A hand … anus should be severed, … A hand

into a barrel … should be severed … A hand … causes blindness. A hand … causes deafness. A hand … causes polyps [polypus]. It was taught … Rabbi Natan says: She is a liberated … , this … and she refuses … until one washes his hands three times. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … eye shadow … causes … the Daughter of the King to pass, and it stops tears and causes eyelashes to grow. That was also taught … Rabbi Yosei says: Eye shadow causes the Daughter of the King to pass, and stops tears and causes eyelashes to grow.

And Mar Ukva said … Shmuel said: Leaves … contain no element of healing, … Rav Yosef said: Coriander contains no element of healing.
Rav Sheshet said: Hops contain no element of healing.
Rav Yosef said: Even for me, … coriander is harmful. … Rav Sheshet said: Arugula even for me, … is beneficial.
And Mar Ukva … said … Shmuel said: All types of hops may … except for teruza,

Rav Ḥisda said: Melon juice, … may be … The juice of pipuim, … may not be … Ze’iri’s wife made … for Ḥiyya bar Ashi and he did not consume … She said to him: I made it for your Rabbi, … and he ate … and you do not eat … Ze’iri … his own reasoning … as Ze’iri said: One may place clear wine and clear water into a strainer … on Shabbat without concern. Apparently, since … are drunk … one is doing nothing … Here, too, since … is consumed this way … one is doing nothing

And Mar Ukva … said: One whose hand or foot was wounded may immerse it in wine … and he need not be concerned … A dilemma was raised before … vinegar, what … Rav Hillel said to Rav Ashi: When we were in Rav Kahana’s house they said … vinegar is not … Rava said: And these people from Meḥoza, since they are delicate, even wine heals them.

Ravina happened … to the house of Rav Ashi. He saw that a donkey stepped on the back of … foot, and … sat and immersed … in vinegar … said to … Does … Master not hold … that … Rav Hillel stated, … vinegar … not … He said to him: The back of the hand and the back of the foot are different

Some say … saw that … immersed … in wine. … said to him: Does … Master not hold … that … Rava said: These people from Meḥoza, since they are delicate, even wine heals them? And … Master is also delicate. … said to him: The back of the hand and the back of the foot are different, as Rav Adda bar Mattana said … Rav said: … the back of the hand or the back of the foot is like a fatal wound, and one may desecrate Shabbat for it.

The Sages taught … one may bathe in … waters of Gerar, in the waters of Ḥamatan, in the waters of Asya, and in the waters of Tiberias; however, … not … in the Great Sea, … nor in water … soaked, nor in the Sea of Sodom,

And … raises a contradiction … One may bathe in the waters of Tiberias … and in the Great Sea; but … not … in water … was soaked, nor in the Sea of Sodom. … difficult … the Great Sea, … the Great Sea.

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … not difficult, … this … Rabbi Meir, … That … Rabbi Yehuda, … As we learned … All seas … like a ritual bath [mikve], as it is stated: … and the gathering together of the waters [mikve] He called seas” … the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda says: … the Great Sea … like a ritual bath, and … states seas only … there are many seas in
Rabbi Yosei says: All seas purify … when … flowing. … And … is invalid for … zavim and lepers and for sanctifying purification water … with it. … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak strongly objects to this

Say that they disagree … with regard to impurity and purity, … with regard to Shabbat did you hear … Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: … not difficult. This … where one remained … That … one did not remain

And how did you establish … last … one did not remain … If … one did not remain … even in water … soaked, as it was taught … One may bathe … in the waters of Tiberias, and in water … soaked, and in the Sodom Sea, and … even though one has wounds on his head … In what … is this statement said? … where one did not remain … However, … one remained … prohibited.

Rather, … the Great Sea … the Great Sea … not difficult. … This … to … pure water in it, … That … to … polluted water in it, … And … water … soaked … water … soaked, … also not difficult. … This … where one remained … That … one did not remain

MISHNA: One may not eat eizoveyon on Shabbat because healthy people do not eat it, … However, one may eat … yo’ezer and may drink abuvro’e. … all … food … may be eaten by a person … for medicinal … And one may drink … drinks except for water from palm trees and a kos ikarin because they are … jaundice. … However, one may drink palm tree water … in order … his thirst, and one may smear ikarin oil … for non-medical purposes.

GEMARA: Rav Yosef said: … hyssop … abarta bar hamag … eizoveyon … abarta bar hing. Ulla said: … white sage. … Ulla happened … to the house of Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda. They brought white sage before him. He said: This is the hyssop that is written in the Torah. Rav Pappi said: … shumeshuk. Rav Yirmeya of Difti said: In accordance with … Rav Pappi it is reasonable, as we learned … The mitzva of hyssop … three branches each with three stems, and shumeshuk is … that is found with that … For what purpose do … eat it? … for … intestinal worms. And with what is it eaten? … with seven black dates. From what do … come into being … from … barley flour from a vessel that held … for forty days

However, one may eat … yo’ezer … What is yo’ezer? … potnak … For what is it eaten? … to … liver worms. With what is it eaten? … seven white dates. From what do … come into being … From … raw meat with water on an empty … and from … fatty meat on an empty … and from … ox meat on an empty … and from … nuts on an empty … and from eating fenugreek shoots on an empty … and drinking water thereafter.

And if … not … he should swallow white cress. And if … not … he should sit in fast, and take fatty meat and place it on coals and suck … bone and swallow vinegar. And some say: … not … vinegar because it is harmful to the liver. And if … let … take the sawdust that was scraped … of a thorn bush from top to bottom, and not from bottom to top, … perhaps … will come out through his mouth. And let … boil … in beer at twilight and the next day close his nostrils and drink … And when he defecates, he should defecate on the trunk of a palm tree.

And one may drink abuvro’e … What is abuvro’e? … ḥumtareya. … What is ḥumtareya? … the lonely staff. … For what … is it used? … for … exposed … And if … not … let … take five roses and five cups of beer and cook them together until there is a quarter … and … drink

Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami’s mother made … for a certain man … one rose and one cup of beer … she boiled … She gave it to him to drink, and lit the oven, and swept out the coals, and placed a brick inside it … And something … like a green leaf emerged,

Rav Avya said: … a quarter … of milk from a white goat. Rav Huna bar Yehuda said: Let … bring a sweet citron and make a hole in it, and fill it with honey, and place it among burning coals, and eat it. Rabbi Ḥanina said: Urine that is forty days old … A very small cupful … a hornet … A quarter … a scorpion … Half a log … exposed … A log is even effective … witchcraft. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … [anigron] … and … [avangar] … and balsam are effective for both … exposed … and … for witchcraft.

One who swallowed a snake should be fed hops in salt, and … run … three mil. … Rav Shimi bar Ashi saw a person who swallowed a snake, … appeared … as a horseman. … fed him hops with salt and made him run in front of him for three mil, and … came out of him in pieces. Some say … Rav Shimi bar Ashi … swallowed a snake, … Elijah came … appeared to … as a horseman. He fed him hops with salt and made him run in front of him for three mil, and … came out of him in pieces. One who was bitten by a snake should have the fetus of a white donkey brought … , and it should be torn open and placed on … And this applies … not … condition that will cause it to die within twelve months … tereifa]. … a certain

“And she went, and she came, and she collected in the field … Rabbi Elazar said: … that she went and came, went and came, until she found suitable people with whom to walk. … “And Boaz said to his youth who was standing over the harvesters: To whom does this young woman belong?” … And was it Boaz’s habit to inquire about a young woman? Rabbi Elazar said: He saw in her a matter of wisdom … she collected two stalks, … she did not collect three stalks.

It was taught in a baraita: He saw a matter of modesty in her … upright … standing, … fallen … sitting; … but cling to my maidens” … And was it Boaz’s habit to cling to women? Rabbi Elazar said: Since he saw “And Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and Ruth clung to her” … he said: It is permitted to cling to

“And Boaz said to her at mealtime: Come here [halom] … Rabbi Elazar … said … he hinted to her … In the future the kingdom of David will come from you, as it is written with regard to it, … “Here,” as it is stated: “And King David came and sat before God and said: Who am I, Lord, God, and who is my family that You have brought me to here [halom]?” … “And dip your bread in vinegar” … Rabbi Elazar said: From here … that vinegar … good … in hot weather.

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … he hinted to her: A son will come from you in the future whose actions will be … sharp as vinegar, and who is he? … Manasseh. “And she sat beside the harvesters.” Rabbi Elazar said with regard to this: Beside the harvesters, and not among the harvesters. He hinted to her that the kingdom of David will be divided in the future

“And he gave her roasted grain and she ate”; … Rabbi Elazar said: “And she ate” … in the days of David; “And she was satiated” … in the days of Solomon; “And she left some over” … in the days of Hezekiah. And some say … “And she ate,” … in the days of David and Solomon; “And she was satiated,” … in the days of Hezekiah; “And she left some over” … in the days of Rabbi … As the Master said: Rabbi … horsekeeper [ahuriyarei] was richer than the king … It was taught in a baraita: “And she ate,” in this world; “and she was satiated,” in the days of the Messiah; “and she left some over,” in the future,

and under his honor He will burn a burning like a burning fire” … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: “And under his honor,” but not his actual honor. … Rabbi Yoḥanan … his own reasoning, … called his clothing my honor,

Rabbi Elazar said: “And under his honor” … in place of his actual honor. … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said: Under his honor … similar to the burning of the sons of Aaron. Just as there, … the soul burned while … body … intact, so too here, … the soul burned while … body … intact.
Rabbi Aḥa bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

From where … that changing clothes … As it is stated: “And he will remove his garments and will don other garments, … The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: The Torah taught you etiquette. The clothes in which one prepared food for his master, one does not … to pour his master wine.

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It is disgraceful for a Torah scholar to go out to the marketplace in patched shoes. … Didn’t Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina go out … Rabbi Aḥa, son of Rav Naḥman, said: … if there is a patch upon a patch.

And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: A Torah scholar on whose clothes a fat stain is found is liable … death … as it is stated: “All those who hate me love death” … Do not read: Those who hate me [mesanai]. Rather, … Those who cause me to be hated [masniai]. … Ravina said: … a bloodstain [revad] was stated … They did not disagree … that … to an overgarment … that … to an undergarment,
And … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: That which is written: “As My servant Isaiah went naked and barefoot … naked … tattered clothing, and barefoot … with patched shoes.

We learned … there: A fat stain on … saddle interposes, i.e., … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: … as an Italian issar … And … on clothing on one side, it does not interpose, … on both sides it interposes. Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Yishmael: It interposes even on one side.

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish raised a dilemma before Rabbi Ḥanina: … saddle … on just one side, or … on both sides? … said to him: That, I did not hear … I heard … similar to it. As we learned … Rabbi Yosei says: … builders [banna’in] … on one side, and that of an ignoramus, … on both sides. And … saddle cannot be more important than the garment of an am ha’aretz.

Who … builders … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: These are Torah scholars, who are engaged in building the world all of their days. And … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Who is a Torah scholar … that one … return a lost object to him based on visual identification, … That is one who makes sure his upper undergarment is turned inward … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Who is a Torah scholar who … appointed … leader of the community? This is one who is asked … matters of halakha on any topic and he … answer, and even … tractate Kalla,

And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Who is the Torah scholar for whom the inhabitants of his city are commanded to perform his labor for him? This is one who sets his own matters aside and engages in matters of Heaven. … And that applies only to exerting themselves … his bread, … And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Who is … a Torah scholar? Anyone who is asked … halakha with regard to any topic and … state it. … What are the practical consequences … to appoint him a leader of the community. If … in a single tractate, … in his place; if … in all of his learning, … as the head of the yeshiva.

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: These … the clothes of the bath attendants [ulairin] that come from a country overseas, … Is that to say that these are white garments? Didn’t Rabbi Yannai say to his sons: My sons, do not bury me in white garments nor in black garments. … white, lest I not be acquitted … and I will be … like a groom among mourners. … black, lest I be acquitted … and I will be … like a mourner among grooms. Rather, … in the clothes of the bath attendants who come from a country overseas, … Apparently, these … are red. … not difficult, … that … to overgarments; … that … to undergarments.

Rabbi Yishmael says: One may fold … “The burnt-offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat, … taught, with regard to the fats of Shabbat, that … are offered on Yom Kippur, … might … even … from Yom Kippur … on Shabbat; … the verse states “on its Shabbat” … the statement of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says … “The burnt-offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat,” … that … fats of Shabbat are offered on a Festival … I might … even … on Yom Kippur … the verse states “on its Shabbat”

When you … will find … say that, in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Yishmael, vows and free-will offerings are offered on a Festival. … And the verse is needed to … Yom Kippur … according to Rabbi Akiva vows and free-will offerings are not brought on a Festival, and … the verse is needed to permit … on a Festival … Rabbi Zeira said:

When I was in Babylonia, I said … that which was taught … Yom Kippur occurred … Shabbat eve, they would not sound … and … at the conclusion of Shabbat, they would not recite havdala … a statement … all. When I went … I found Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, who sat and said: … is … Rabbi Akiva, … As, if … Rabbi Yishmael, then, since … said … fats from Shabbat are offered on Yom Kippur, let them sound … so that … will know … the fats from Shabbat are offered on Yom Kippur … And I said to him: … priests are vigilant

Mar Kashisha, … son … Rav Ḥisda, said to Rav Ashi: Do we say … priests are vigilant … Didn’t we learn in … three … to stop the people from work, … three … to demarcate between sacred and profane? … As Abaye said … for the rest of the people in Jerusalem, so too here, … for the rest of the people in Jerusalem

Let them sound … so that they will know that trimming the vegetables, … is permitted from the … afternoon and onward. … Rav Yosef said: … because a rabbinic prohibition [shevut] is not overridden … to permit
And Rav Sheisha, son … Rav Idi, said: The Sages permitted … an immediate rabbinic prohibition, … They did not permit … a … remote rabbinic prohibition,

And … they permit … an immediate rabbinic prohibition? Didn’t we learn … a Festival occurs on Shabbat eve, one sounds … but one does not recite havdala … the conclusion of Shabbat, one recites havdala … but one does not sound … And why … Let them sound … so that … will know that slaughtering is permitted immediately … Rather, it is clear … in accordance with … Rav Yosef,

Rabbi Zeira said … Rav Huna said, and some say Rabbi Abba said … Rav Huna said: … Yom Kippur occurs on Shabbat, trimming vegetables is prohibited. Rav Mana said: It was taught … From where … on Yom Kippur that occurs on Shabbat trimming vegetables is prohibited? The verse states: “A solemn rest [shabbaton], … rabbinic prohibition … for what … If you say … labor, isn’t it written … you shall not perform any labor” … Rather, does … trimming vegetables, … learn from it

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … Yom Kippur occurs on Shabbat, trimming vegetables is permitted. … raised an objection … From where … on Yom Kippur that occurs on Shabbat trimming vegetables is prohibited? The verse states: “A solemn rest [shabbaton], … rabbinic prohibition … for what … If you say … labor, isn’t it written … you shall not perform any labor” … Rather, is it not … trimming vegetables, … No, … actually … to labor. … violates … a positive mitzva and a prohibition.
It was taught … in accordance with … Rabbi Yoḥanan: … Yom Kippur occurs on Shabbat,

trimming vegetables is permitted. And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … Yom Kippur occurs on … weekday, one may crack nuts and remove pomegranate seeds from … afternoon and onward, … due to anxiety, … Rav Yehuda’s house would trim cabbage. … Rabba’s house would scrub gourds. Once … saw … they were doing … early, … he said to them: A letter came from the West, … in the name … Rabbi Yoḥanan, … prohibited.
