GEMARA: It was stated … written in … translation or in any … language. Rav Huna said: One may not rescue them from the fire … And Rav Ḥisda said: One may rescue them from the fire … According to the one who said … may be read, everybody agrees … one may rescue … Where they argue … according to the one who said that they may not be read. Rav Huna said: One may not rescue … as they may not be read. … Rav Ḥisda said: One may rescue … due to disgrace to sacred writings … We learned … all sacred writings, one may rescue them from the fire … whether they are read … or whether they are not read … even if they are written in any … language. What, is it not … “That they are read” … Prophets, and … “That they are not read” … Writings? Even though these are … written in any … language, which may not be read, it is taught that one may save them. … a conclusive refutation of … Rav Huna.

Rav Huna … said to you: And … you understand … Say the latter clause … require burial. … now, … we rescue them … is it necessary … burial? Rather, … Rav Huna reconciles … in accordance with his reasoning, and Rav Ḥisda reconciles … in accordance with his reasoning. Rav Huna reconciles … in accordance with his reasoning: Whether they are read … Prophets, and whether they are not read … Writings. In what … is … statement said? It is … where they are written in the holy tongue, but … in any … language, … not rescued … and even so, they require burial. Rav Ḥisda reconciles … in accordance with his reasoning: Whether they are read … Prophets, and whether they are not read … Writings, even if they are written in any language … also rescued. And this is what … is saying: And even the decayed … require burial.

raises an objection … they were written in … translation … any language … they are rescued from the fire … conclusive refutation … Rav Huna, … Rav Huna … said to you: This tanna holds … may be read, … Come … hear … were written … Coptic, … Median; Ivrit, … Eilamitic; … Greek are rescued from the fire … even though they may not be read. … conclusive refutation … Rav Huna, … Rav Huna … said to you: This is … tanna’im, as it was taught … they were written in … translation or in any language … one may rescue them from the fire … Rabbi Yosei says: One may not rescue them from the fire.

Rabbi Yosei said: … an incident involving … father, Ḥalafta, who went to the esteemed Rabban Gamliel … Tiberias, where he found him sitting at the table of Yoḥanan HaNazuf and in his hand … a translation of the book of Job, and he was reading … it. … said to … I remember Rabban Gamliel, your father’s father, who was standing on top of a step on the Temple Mount. And they brought before him a translation of the book of Job, and he said to the builder: Bury this … under the course of bricks. … ordered that it … and he buried it. Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says … they overturned a large bowl of mortar on it. Rabbi … said: … two responses to this … One, from where would they get mortar on the Temple Mount? … And furthermore, is it permitted to … destroy … with one’s hands? Rather, … they leave them in a neglected place, … and they decay on their own. … Who are … tanna’im

If we say … first tanna … Rabbi Yosei, … and perhaps they are disagreeing about this: This Master, … holds … may be read; and this Master, … holds … they may not be read, … Rather, … Rabbi Yosei … the … tanna, … about … Coptic.

The Sages taught … The blessings … and the amulets, even though there are the letters of the Name … in them … matters that … in the Torah … are not rescued from the fire; rather, they burn in their place, they and the names … From here … said: Writers of blessings … like burners of Torah … an incident involving one who was writing … in Sidon. They came and informed Rabbi Yishmael … and Rabbi Yishmael went to examine him … When … was ascending the ladder … sensed his … took a bundle [tomos] of blessings, and submerged it in a basin of water … And in these words Rabbi Yishmael said to him: … punishment … the latter … greater than … the former.

The Exilarch raised a dilemma before Rabba bar Rav Huna: … were written in … arsenic, or red paint, in gum, or in iron sulfate, … in the holy tongue, … one rescue them from the fire … or does one not rescue … dilemma is raised according to the one who said … one rescues … dilemma is raised according to the one who said … one does not rescue … dilemma is raised according to the one who said … one does not rescue … that applies … where … are written in … translation and in any … language; however, here, where they are written in the holy tongue, one rescues … Or perhaps even according to the one who said … one rescues … that applies … where … are written in ink that endures; however, here, since … does not endure, … not … said to him: One does not rescue them. … Didn’t Rav Hamnuna teach … that one saves them. … said to him: If it was taught … it was taught, … What … was taught … Rav Ashi said, as it was taught … The only … between … books … and the Megilla … is that … books are written in any language … and the Megilla … if it is written in Assyrian script, … on a … scroll, and in ink.

Rav Huna bar Ḥaluv raised a dilemma before Rav Naḥman: … a Torah scroll in which there is not … to compile … eighty-five … letters … as in the portion of: “And when the Ark traveled” … does one rescue it from the fire … or does one not rescue … said to him: And raise a dilemma … the portion of: “And when the Ark traveled,” itself, … where the portion of: “And when the Ark traveled,” is incomplete, it is not a dilemma for me, as since it contains names … even though there are not eighty-five letters in it, it is rescued. … where it is a dilemma for me is … a Torah scroll in which there is not … to compile … what … said to him: It is not rescued.

raised an objection to his … translation that was written … the Bible, and … the Bible that was written … translation, and … Hebrew script, one rescues … from the fire … And, needless to say, … translation that are in … Ezra, and that are in … Daniel, and that are in the Torah. What are the … translation in the Torah? … Yegar Sahaduta, … and … even though there are not eighty-five letters in it. … when that … was taught, … to complete

A dilemma was raised before … these eighty-five letters … are juxtaposed, or … scattered? Rav Huna said: … juxtaposed. Rav Ḥisda said: Even … scattered. … raises an objection … a Torah scroll that is worn, if there is … to compile … eighty-five … letters as in the portion of: “And when the Ark traveled,” one rescues … and if not one does not rescue … conclusive refutation … Rav Huna. Rav Ḥisda interpreted … according to … of Rav Huna: … in … words.
the Sages taught … “And when the Ark traveled and Moses proclaimed: … And The Holy One, Blessed be He, made signs … for this portion, above and below, … to say
that this is not its place, … Rabbi … says: It is not for that … Rather, … because … is considered a book unto itself.
According to whose … that … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman said … Rabbi Yonatan said, … she carved its seven pillars” … these are the seven books of the Torah? According to whose … according to … Rabbi

Who is … tanna who disagrees with Rabbi … It is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. As it was taught … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: In the future, this portion will be uprooted from here, … and will be written in its … place. And why was it written here, … in order to demarcate between the first punishment and the second punishment. What is the second punishment … “And the people complained … the first punishment? … “And they traveled from the mountain of God [mehar Hashem] … and Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: That they turned from after God [me’aḥarei Hashem] … And … where is … place … Rav Ashi said: In … flags,

A dilemma was raised before … the blank folios … of a Torah scroll, … one rescue them from the fire … or … one not rescue them from the fire? Come … hear … a Torah scroll that is worn, if there is … in it to compile eighty-five … letters as in the portion of: “And when the Ark traveled,” one rescues … and if not one does not rescue … why … Derive … due to its blank folios. The Gemara … worn is different,

Come … hear … a Torah scroll that was erased, if there is … in it to compile eighty-five … letters as in the portion of: “And when the Ark traveled,” one rescues … and if not, one does not rescue … And why … Derive … due to its blank folios, … the place of the writing … it is not a dilemma for me, as it is sacred due to … writing. … writing is gone, its sanctity is gone. When it is a dilemma for me is … above and below, that are between … section and … section, that are between … page and … page, that are at the beginning of the scroll, … that are at the end of the scroll. … Derive … due to that … where … was cut and thrown

Come … hear … the blank folios … above and below, that are between … section and … section, that are between … page and … page, that are at the beginning of the scroll, … that are at the end of the scroll render the hands … ritually impure. … perhaps … part of the Torah scroll, it is different,

come … hear … the blank folios and the … scrolls of heretics, one does not rescue them from the fire; rather, they burn in their place, they and the names … What, … not … blank folios … a Torah scroll? … No, … blank folios … the scrolls of heretics. … Now, … the scrolls of heretics themselves, one does not rescue … necessary … blank folios? … this is what it is saying: And the scrolls of heretics are like blank folios.

the matter itself. … the blank folios and the … scrolls of … heretics, one does not rescue them from the fire. Rabbi Yosei says: During the week, one cuts the names … therein and buries them, and burns the rest. Rabbi Tarfon said … I will bury my sons … that if … come into my possession I will burn them and the names … therein. As even … a person is pursuing him … to kill him, and a snake is hurrying to bite him, one enters a house of idolatry and does not enter the houses of these … that these … are aware … and … deny … whereas these … are not aware, and … deny … And with regard to the … the verse says: “And behind the door and the doorpost you place your memory”

Rabbi Yishmael said: … a fortiori … Just as to make peace between a husband and his wife, … Torah says: My name that was written in sanctity shall be erased in the water … these, … who impose jealousy, and hatred, and conflict between the Jewish people and their Father in Heaven, all the more so … And with regard to … David said: “For I hate those who hate You, God, and I fight those who rise against You. I hate them with the utmost hatred, they have become enemies to me” … And just as they, … are not rescued from the fire, neither are they rescued from a rockslide, nor from water, nor from … matter that destroys them.

Yosef bar Ḥanin raised a dilemma before Rabbi Abbahu: … these books of the house of Abidan, … one rescue them from the fire or … one not rescue … yes and no, and … uncertain to him. Rav would not go to the house of Abidan … and all the more so … to the house of Nitzrefei, … Shmuel, to the house of Nitzrefei he did not go, … to the house of Abidan he did go. … said to Rava: Why did you not come to the house of Abidan? … said to them: There is a certain palm tree on the road, and … difficult for me. … We will uproot it. … its place … difficult for me. Mar bar Yosef said: I am … of them, … and I do not fear them. … one time he went … they sought to endanger his … Rabbi Meir would call … wicked folio [aven gilyon]; Rabbi Yoḥanan … sinful folio [avon gilyon].
Imma Shalom, … wife … Rabbi Eliezer, was Rabban Gamliel’s sister. There was … philosopher [pilosofa] in their neighborhood

who disseminated … the reputation that he does not accept bribes. They wanted to mock him … She … gave him a golden lamp, and … came before him, … She said to … I want to share … of my father’s estate. He said to them: Divide … said to him: It is written in our … In a situation … son, the daughter does not inherit. … said to him: Since the day you were exiled from your land, the Torah of Moses was taken away and the avon gilyon was given … It is written in … A son and a daughter shall inherit alike.

The next day … brought … a Libyan donkey. … He said to them: I proceeded to the end … avon gilayon, and it is written: I, … did not come to subtract from the Torah of Moses, and I did not come to add to the Torah of Moses. And it is written there: In a situation … son, the daughter does not inherit. She said to him: May your light shine like a lamp, … Rabban Gamliel said to him: The donkey came and kicked the lamp,

And why … one not read … Due to suspension … in the study hall. Rav said: They only taught … during the hours of … the study hall; but … not during the hours of … the study hall, one may read … And Shmuel said: Even … not the hours of … the study hall one may not read … Is that so? Wasn’t Neharde’a Shmuel’s place … and in Neharde’a they concluded … regular weekly discourse with Writings on Shabbat afternoon. Rather, if … was stated … it was stated as follows: Rav said: It was only taught … in a place … study hall … but not in a place … a study hall, one may read

And Shmuel said: Whether it is in the place of the study hall or it is not the place of the study hall, one may not read … when it is during the hours of … the study hall; … when it is not during the hours of … the study hall, one may read. And Shmuel follows his … reasoning … in Neharde’a they … conclude their … Writings on Shabbat afternoon.

Rav Ashi said: Actually, … as we stated initially, and Shmuel said … in accordance with … Rabbi Neḥemya. As it was taught … Although … said … sacred writings … may not be read … one may study … them and teach them … one requires a verse … he brings … and looks in it. Rabbi Neḥemya said: Why did they say … sacred writings are not read on … So that … will say: Sacred writings may not be read, all the more so … ordinary documents,

MISHNA: One may rescue the casing … scroll … with the Torah scroll, and the casing of phylacteries along with the phylacteries, even if they have money inside them. And to where may one rescue them? Into an alley that is closed, … Ben Beteira says: Even into an open

GEMARA: … the Sages taught … the fourteenth … occurs on Shabbat, … one flays the Paschal … up to the breast … the statement of Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka. And the Rabbis say: One flays it in its entirety. … Granted, according to … Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, … Since it has … been used for its divine purpose … But according to the Rabbis, what is the reason … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The verse states, “All that the Lord has made is for His sake” … And here, what … for His sake is there … Rav Yosef said: … that … will not putrefy. Rava said: … that the sacred sacrifices will not be left … like … animal carcass

What is … between them? … There is … between them when … is laid on a golden table. … Alternatively, … a day with a … northern wind. … And what does Rabbi Yishamel, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, do with the … that the Lord has made is for His sake”? … as … not … to remove the sacrificial parts … before removing the hide … What is the reason … Rav Huna, son of Rav Natan, said: Because of … hairs,

Rav Ḥisda said … Mar Ukva said: How did the members of the group respond to Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka? This is what they said to him: If one may save … casing of a … scroll along with the … scroll, … may one not strip the Paschal … of its skin? … Are they comparable? There, … moving … here, … prohibited labor … Rav Ashi said: They are disagreeing with regard to two … They disagree with regard to moving … and they disagree with regard to the labor … And this is what they said to him: If one may rescue … casing of the Torah scroll along with the Torah scroll, … we not move … hide … together with the flesh

Are they comparable? There, … is a base for a permitted object, … here, … is a base for a prohibited object, … Rather, this is what they said to him: If one may save … casing of the Torah scroll along with the scroll, even if there is money inside it, … may one not move … hide together with … flesh? … Are they comparable? There, … becomes a base for a prohibited object and a permitted object; … here, … it is entirely a base for a prohibited object. Rather, this is what they said to him: If one may bring a casing that has money inside it from outside … to save a Torah scroll in it, … may one not move … hide together with the flesh?

And from where … this … itself? … If you say … from … that … where … in it one does not throw it … bring … along with it; is it comparable? There, … in the meantime the fire might catch … here, … in the meantime he could have thrown it away. Rather, Mar bar Rav Ashi said: Actually, … as we said initially. … And … what was difficult for you, … here, … moving … here, … labor … where one does not need the hide
But Abaye and Rava both said: Rabbi Shimon concedes in … cut off its head and will it not die, … that one flays it strip by strip,

And to where may one rescue them? … What are the circumstances … open, … what are the circumstances … not open? Rav Ḥisda said: … three walls and two posts … is an alley that is not open; … three walls and one post is an alley that is open. And they both, … in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, as we learned … preparation of an alley … Beit Shammai say … a post … and a beam … And Beit Hillel say: Either a post or a beam … Rabbi Eliezer says: … two posts

Rabba said to him: Did you call … three walls and one post open? … And furthermore, according to the Rabbis, … let us rescue food and drinks … there … Rather, Rabba said: … two walls and two posts … is an alley that is not open. … two walls and one post, it is an alley that is open.

And both of them … in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda. As it was taught … Furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said: One who has two houses … on two sides of the public domain, … he may … place a … post from here, … And … an … post from here, … Or, … a beam … from here, … And … a beam … from here, … carry … and place … in … between … said to him: One may not establish an eiruv in the public domain in that
Abaye said to … to your … too, … to the … Rabbis … us … save food and drinks … there.

Rather, Rav Ashi said: … Three walls and one post is an alley that is closed; three walls without a post … is an open alley. And even according to Rabbi Eliezer, who said we need two posts, … those words … to … food and drinks, but for … a Torah scroll, one post is sufficient.

MISHNA: One may rescue food for three meals … that is suitable for a person for a person; … that is suitable for an animal for an animal. How so? … a fire ignited on Friday night … one may rescue food for three meals. … in the morning, … one may … rescue food for two meals. … in … afternoon, … food for one meal. Rabbi Yosei says: One may always rescue food for three meals,

GEMARA: … Now, since one is exerting … permitted … let us rescue more. … Rava said: Since a person is agitated about his property, if you permit him … he will come to extinguish … Abaye said to him: Rather, that which was taught … one’s barrel broke atop one’s roof … he may bring a vessel and place it under … and … provided that he does not bring another vessel … to catch … another vessel and attach … There, what decree … Here, too, … a decree … lest one bring … vessel through the public domain,

the matter itself: … one’s barrel broke atop one’s roof … he may bring a vessel and place it under … and … provided that he does not bring another vessel … catch … another vessel and attach … guests happen … to him … he … bring another vessel and catch … he … bring another vessel and attach … And one may not catch … and then invite … rather, … invite … and afterward catch … And one may not employ artifice in this … In the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda, they said: … employ artifice.

Let us say … disagree in the dispute … Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, as it was taught … it and its offspring that fell into a pit … Rabbi Eliezer says: One may raise the first in order to slaughter it, and … slaughter it; and … the second one, one may provide it sustenance in its place … so that it will not die. Rabbi Yehoshua says: One may raise the first in order to slaughter it, and … not slaughter it, and one may employ artifice … and raise the second. If he … desires, he slaughters this … if he … desires, he slaughters that

From what … Perhaps Rabbi Eliezer only stated … there, … where it is possible … feeding … however, here, … where it is impossible to … feeding … no, … And … Rabbi Yehoshua only said there … because there is … suffering of living beings, but here, where there is no … suffering of living beings, … not

The Sages taught … one rescued … fine bread … he may not … rescue coarse bread [hadra’a], … coarse bread, … rescue fine bread. And one may rescue … on Yom Kippur for … Shabbat; however, … not … on Shabbat for … Yom Kippur. And, needless to say, … on Shabbat for … a Festival, and … not … on Shabbat for … the next Shabbat.

the Sages taught: … one forgot bread in the oven and … the day … was sanctified, he may rescue … food … three meals … And, one may say to others: Come and rescue … for yourselves. And when one removes … he may not remove … with a baker’s paddle, but … with a knife. … Is that so? Didn’t the school of Rabbi Yishmael teach … you shall not perform any labor” … excludes blowing the shofar and removing bread, which is a skill and not a labor, … as much as it is possible to alter … one alters,

Rav Ḥisda said: A person should always rise early … to … expenditures for Shabbat, as it is written … “And it shall be on the sixth day, and they will prepare that which they have brought” … immediately … Rabbi Abba said: On Shabbat a person is obligated to break … over two loaves … as it is written: … double the bread,

Rav Ashi said: I saw that Rav Kahana took two … and broke one, … He said … it is written: … collected … Rabbi Zeira would break … his entire meal. Ravina said to Rav Ashi: Doesn’t that appear like gluttony? … said to him: Since … every … day he does not do … and now he is doing … it does not appear like gluttony. Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, when the bread from the eiruv would happen … to them, they would begin … it. … said … Since one mitzva was performed with it, let an additional mitzva be performed with it.

How so? … a fire ignited … the Sages taught … How many meals is a person obligated to eat on Shabbat? Three. Rabbi Ḥidka says: Four. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: And both of them derived … from one verse: “And Moses said: Eat it today, for today is Shabbat for God, today you will not find it in the field” … Rabbi Ḥidka holds: These three … today … besides the evening … And the Rabbis hold … include the evening … We learned … fire ignited on Shabbat evening

one rescues food for three meals. What, is this not … he has not … eaten … No, … one … ate … morning, one may … rescue food for two meals. What, is it not … has not … eaten … No, … one has … eaten … in … afternoon, … food for one meal. What, is it not … has not … eaten … No, … one has … eaten.

From … it is taught in the latter clause … Rabbi Yosei says: One may always rescue food for three meals, by inference, … first tanna holds … three … Rather, it is clear … mishna is not in accordance with … Rabbi Ḥidka.

And that which we learned … One who has … food for two meals … may not take … from the charity plate … food for fourteen … may not take … from the … fund. … whose … neither … the Rabbis nor … Rabbi Ḥidka. If … the Rabbis, … they are fifteen … If … Rabbi Ḥidka, they are sixteen … Actually, … the Rabbis, … we say to him: That which you want to eat at the conclusion of Shabbat, … eat … on Shabbat.

Let us say … this … is … the Rabbis and not … Rabbi Ḥidka. … Even if you say … Rabbi Ḥidka, … as we … say to him: That which you want to eat on Shabbat eve, … eat at night … And do we have a person sit … fast all day on Shabbat eve? … Rather, … whose … this … It is … Rabbi Akiva, … said: Make your Shabbat … a weekday and do not be beholden to … beings.

And that which we learned … One gives no less … to a poor person who is traveling from place to place than a loaf … a pundeyon, … four se’a for a sela. … he sleeps … one gives him money for sleeping; and if he spends Shabbat … one gives him food for three meals. Let us say … the Rabbis and not … Rabbi Ḥidka. … Actually, … Rabbi Ḥidka. … where there is … meal … with him, for we say to him: This … that you have with you, eat it. … And when he goes, does he go … We … him a meal … accompany … What … money for sleeping? Rav Pappa said: … a bed and cushions.

The Sages taught … bowls from which one ate in the evening … he may rinse them … to eat from them in the morning. … morning, he may rinse them to eat from them in the afternoon. … in the afternoon, he may rinse them to eat from them in the afternoon. … from the afternoon onward, one may no longer rinse them … However, … cups, and ladles, and flasks, … one rinses them all day long because there is no fixed … for drinking,

Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of bar Kappara: Anyone who fulfills … three meals on Shabbat is rescued from three punishments: From the pangs of the Messiah, … and from the judgment of Gehenna, and from the war of Gog and Magog. … from the pangs of Messiah … It is written here, … day: … And it is written there, … “Behold, I am sending you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the … day … from the judgment of Gehenna … It is written here, … day, … And it is written there, … “That day will be a day of wrath, … from the war of Gog and Magog … It is written here, … day. And it is written there, … on the day that Gog arrives

Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei: … anyone who delights in the Shabbat, … gives him a boundless portion, … as it is stated: … Then you shall delight in the Lord and I will cause you to ride on the heights of the world, and to feast

on the inheritance of Jacob your father, … Not that of Abraham, about whom it is written, “Rise, walk through the land through its length … And not that of Isaac, about whom it is written, … because I will give all of these lands to you and your offspring” … Rather, that of Jacob, about whom it is written, … and you will spread out to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south,

Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: … is rescued from the oppression of exile. … It is written here, … “And I will cause you to ride on the heights [bamotei] of the world” … and it is written there: … and you will trample their high places [bamoteimo]” … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: … anyone who delights in the Shabbat, … grants him his heart’s desires, … it is stated: “And you shall delight in God and He will grant you your heart’s desires” … This delight … I do not know what it is. When it says: “And you shall call the Shabbat delight,” … must say: It is the delight of Shabbat. … With what does one delight … Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav: With a dish of beets, and large fish, and heads of garlic. Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi … Rav said: Even … a small item and one prepared it in deference to Shabbat, it is … delight. … What is … Rav Pappa said: Small fried fish.

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … anyone who observes Shabbat in accordance with its halakhot, even … worships idolatry as … the generation of Enosh, … forgives him … as it is stated: “Fortunate is the man [enosh] who does this … from desecrating it [meḥallelo], … Do not read … From desecrating it [meḥallelo], but rather: He is forgiven [maḥul lo].

Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: Had the Jewish people … observed … first Shabbat … no nation or tongue would have … ruled them, as it is stated: “And it happened on the seventh day, some people went out from the nation to collect … And it is written after … “And Amalek came … Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: If only the Jewish people would keep two Shabbatot in accordance with their halakhot, … immediately redeemed, … it is stated: “So said God to the eunuchs who will keep My Shabbatot” … and it is written after … “And I will bring them to My holy mountain

Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be among those who eat three meals on Shabbat. … Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be among those who complete hallel every day. … Is that so? Didn’t the Master say: One who reads hallel every day is … one who curses and blasphemes … When we say … the verses of praise [pesukei dezimra],

Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be among those who pray … with the reddening of the sun, … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It is a mitzva to pray with the reddening of the sun. Rabbi Zeira said: What verse … “They will fear You with the sun and before the moon, generation upon generation”

And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be among those who die from intestinal disease, as the Master said: Most righteous people die of intestinal disease. … And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be among those who die on the path to … a mitzva. And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be among those who accept Shabbat in Tiberias, … and among those who see Shabbat out in Tzippori, … And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be among those who seat … in the study hall, … and not among those who cause … to stand in the study hall,

And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be among the collectors of charity and not the distributors of charity. … And Rabbi Yosei said: May my portion be with one whom … suspect … and there is no … him. Rav Pappa said: They suspected me, and there was no … me.

Rabbi Yosei said: I engaged in relations five times, and I planted five cedars in Eretz Yisrael. And who are … Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Ḥalafta, son of Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Avtilas, son of Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Menaḥem, son of Rabbi Yosei. … Isn’t there Vardimas, … Vardimas is the same as Menaḥem. And why did they call him Vardimas? … his face was as … a rose [vered]. … Is that to say … Rabbi Yosei did not fulfill the mitzva of … conjugal rights, … Rather, say … I engaged in relations five times and I did so again,
Rabbi Yosei said … In all my days, I did not call my wife, my wife, nor my ox, my ox. Rather, … my wife, my home, … and my ox, my field,

Rabbi Yosei said: In all my days, … I never looked at my circumcision. … Is that so? Didn’t they say to Rabbi … Why did they call you our holy Rabbi? He said to them: … in all my days I never looked at my circumcision. … In … Rabbi … another matter … was … in him, as he did not insert his hand below his belt … And Rabbi Yosei said: In all my days, the walls of my house never saw the seams of my robe

And Rabbi Yosei said: In all my days I never violated the words of my friends. I know about myself that I am not a priest, … if my friends say to me: Go up to the platform … I go up. And Rabbi Yosei said: In all my days I never said something and then retreated

Rav Naḥman said: May I receive … because I fulfilled … three meals on Shabbat … Rav Yehuda said: May I receive … because I fulfilled … consideration … prayer. Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said: May I receive … I never walked four cubits with my head uncovered. Rav Sheshet said: May I receive … because I fulfilled the mitzva of phylacteries … And Rav Naḥman said: May I receive … because I fulfilled the mitzva of ritual fringes

Rav Yosef said to Rav Yosef, son of Rabba: In what … was your father, … especially vigilant? … said to him: … in … ritual fringes. … One day he was climbing the stairs … string … was severed, and he would not descend until he placed … on … And Abaye said: May I receive … when I see a young Torah scholar who has completed a tractate … he

I make a feast for the Sages. Rava said: May I receive … because when a young Torah scholar comes before me for judgment, I do not put my head on the pillow until I seek … his merits … Mar bar Rav Ashi said: I am disqualified to … judgment of a young Torah scholar. What is the reason … because … is as beloved to me as my … self, and a person does not find fault in himself.

Rabbi Ḥanina would wrap himself … and stand at nightfall on Shabbat eve, … say: Come and we will go out to greet Shabbat the queen. Rabbi Yannai put on his garment on Shabbat eve and said: Enter, O bride. Enter, O bride. … Rabba bar Rav Huna happened … to the house of Rabba bar Rav Naḥman. They brought … him three se’a of oiled biscuits. … said to them: Did you know I was coming … They said to him: Are you … important to us than

Rabbi Abba bought thirteen plain staters [astirei peshitei] … of meat from thirteen butchers … And he would place … at the door hinge … And … said to … Hurry and prepare it, hurry and prepare it. … Rabbi Abbahu would sit on an ivory chair [takhteka] and fan the fire … Rav Anan would don a … black garment … as the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: … garments in which he cooked a pot … for his master, one should not dilute a cup of wine for his Master.

Rav Safra … roast the head … Rava salted … shibuta … Rav Huna kindled lamps … Rav Pappa spun the wicks … Rav Ḥisda cut the beets … Rabba and Rav Yosef cut wood. Rabbi Zeira prepared thin sticks … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak … load … on his shoulder and enter, load … on his shoulder and exit. He said: If Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi happened to … me, would I not load … on my shoulder before them? … And some say … Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi … load … on their shoulders and enter, load … on their shoulders and exit. They said: If Rabbi Yoḥanan happened … to … us, would we not load … on our shoulders before him?

Yosef who cherishes Shabbat: There was a gentile in his neighborhood whose property was extremely plentiful. The astrologers said to … all his property: Yosef who cherishes Shabbat will consume it. … went and sold all of his property, … he bought a pearl, … placed it in his hat. When he was crossing a river … a ferry, the wind blew … and cast it into the water, … a fish swallowed it. … was … removed … it was brought … nightfall on Shabbat eve. … said: Who buys … like this? … said to … Go bring it to Yosef who cherishes Shabbat, as he regularly purchases … They brought it to him … he purchased it. He ripped … found a pearl inside it. He sold it for thirteen vessels filled with golden dinars … This elderly man … encountered him and said: One who lends … Shabbat, Shabbat repays him.

Rabbi … raised a dilemma before Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei: … the wealthy of Eretz Yisrael, by what … do they merit … said to him: Because they tithe, as it is stated: “A tithe you shall tithe [asser te’asser] … Take a tithe [asser] so that you will become wealthy [titasher]. … the wealthy of Babylonia, … by what … do they merit … said to him: Because they honor the Torah

the wealthy of other countries, … by what … do they merit … said to him: Because they honor Shabbat, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said: One time I was hosted at … a homeowner in Laodicea and … brought before him a table of gold … sixteen people to carry it, and … sixteen chains of silver attached to it, and … bowls and cups and pitchers and flasks attached to it, and … all sorts of food, and delicacies, and fragrant spices on it. And when they placed it … they … say: “The earth and all that fills it is God’s, … And when they removed it they … say: “The heavens are God’s heavens, but the earth He gave to mankind” … I said to him: My son, what did you … merit this? He said to me: I was a slaughterer, and … from every animal … fine, I would say: This will be for Shabbat. I said to him: Happy are you that you merited … and blessed is God, Who has afforded you this merit.

emperor said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya: Why does the fragrance of a cooked Shabbat dish diffuse? … said to him: We have a certain spice called dill [shevet], which we place in … and its fragrance diffuses. … said to him: Give us … of it. … said to him: For anyone who observes Shabbat, … is effective, and for one who does not observe Shabbat, it is not effective.

The Exilarch said to Rav Hamnuna: What … which is written, “The holy one of God is honored” … said to him: That is Yom Kippur, when there is no eating or drinking, … Torah said: Honor it with a clean garment. … “And you shall honor it,” Rav said: To … make … earlier … And Shmuel said: To … make … later, … The sons of Rav Pappa bar Abba said to Rav Pappa: … like us, for whom meat and wine is found … every day, in what … can we change it … said to them: If you are accustomed to … early, make it later … if you are accustomed to making it late, make it earlier … In the summer, Rav Sheshet would seat the Sages … where the sun would reach; in the winter, he would seat the Sages … where the shade would reach. … so … they would stand quickly … Rabbi Zeira
would seek pairs of Sages … said to them: Please do not desecrate

Rava said, and some say … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi … Even an individual who prays on Shabbat evening must recite … were finished [vaykhullu]” … as Rav Hamnuna said: Anyone who prays on Shabbat evening and recites … vaykhullu, the verse ascribed him … as if he became a partner with the Holy One, Blessed be He, in the act of Creation. As it is stated: … were finished [vaykhullu].” Do not read … Were finished [vaykhullu]; rather, … They finished [vaykhallu]. … Rabbi Elazar said: From where … that speech is like action? As it is stated: “By the word of God the heavens were made,

Rav Ḥisda said … Mar Ukva said: One who prays on Shabbat evening and recites vaykhullu, the two ministering angels who accompany the person … place their hands on his head and say to him: “And your iniquity has passed, and your sin has been atoned” … It was taught … Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says: Two ministering angels accompany a person on Shabbat evening from the synagogue to his home, one good … and one evil … And when … reaches his home and finds a lamp burning and a table set and his bed made, the good angel says: May it be … will that it shall be like this for another Shabbat. And the evil angel answers against his will: Amen. And if … not … the evil angel says: May it be … will that it shall be so for another Shabbat, and the good angel answers against his will: Amen.

Rabbi Elazar said: A person should always set his table on Shabbat eve … even if he only needs … an olive-bulk … And Rabbi Ḥanina said: A person should always set his table at the conclusion of Shabbat, … even if he only needs … an olive-bulk … Hot water after Shabbat … remedy [melugma], warm bread at the conclusion of Shabbat … remedy. … They would prepare for Rabbi Abbahu at the conclusion of Shabbat a third-born calf, … he would eat … kidney from it. When his son Avimi grew up, … said to … Why do you waste so much? Let us leave a kidney over from Shabbat eve, … they left … and a lion came and ate it.

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said … anyone who answers: Amen, may His great name be blessed, … with all his might, … rip his sentence, as it is stated: “When punishments are annulled in Israel, when the people offer themselves, bless the Lord” … What is the reason for when punishments are annulled? Because … blessed God. … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even … one has within him a trace of idolatry, … he is forgiven. It is written here, … “When punishments [pera’ot] are annulled.” And it is written there, … that … was wild [paru’a], … Reish Lakish said: One who answers amen with all his strength, they open the gates of the Garden of Eden before him, as it is stated: “Open the gates, and a righteous nation shall come who keeps the faith” … Do not read: Who keeps [shomer] the faith [emunim], but rather: Who say [she’omerim] amen. What … amen? Rabbi Ḥanina said: … God, faithful King [El Melekh ne’eman].

Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel, said in the name of Rav: Fire is only found in a place where there is desecration of Shabbat, as it is stated: “And if you do not heed Me to sanctify the day of Shabbat, and to refrain from carrying burdens … and I will light a fire in its gates and it will consume the palaces of Jerusalem and it will not be extinguished” … What … And it will not be extinguished? Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: … at a time when people are not found to extinguish it. Abaye said: Jerusalem was destroyed only because people desecrated the Shabbat in it, as it is stated: “And from My Shabbatot they averted their eyes, and I was profaned among them”

Rabbi Abbahu said: Jerusalem was destroyed only because … omitted recitation of Shema morning and evening, as it is stated: “Woe to those who rise early in the morning and pursue the drink … And it is written … “And their drinking parties have lyre and lute, drum and flute and wine, and they do not look upon the actions of God, … And it is written … “Therefore My nation is being exiled for its ignorance;

Rav Hamnuna said: Jerusalem was destroyed only because schoolchildren there were interrupted … as it is stated: … pour it onto the infants in the street … What is the reason that … poured? … because infants are outside … Ulla said: Jerusalem was destroyed only because people had no shame before each other, as it is stated: “They acted shamefully; they have performed abominations, yet they neither were ashamed … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Jerusalem was destroyed only because … small and … great … were equated. … as it is stated: “And the common people were like the priest, … And it is written afterward: “The land shall be utterly desolate

Rav Amram, son … Rabbi Shimon bar Abba, said … Rabbi Shimon bar Abba said … Rabbi Ḥanina said: Jerusalem was destroyed only because the people did not rebuke one another, as it is stated: “Her ministers were like stags that found no pasture, … Just as this stag … its head toward the other’s tail … so too, the Jewish people in that generation lowered their faces to the ground and did not rebuke one another. 
Rabbi Yehuda said: Jerusalem was destroyed only because they disparaged the Torah scholars in it, as it is stated: “And they mocked the messengers of God and disdained His words and taunted His prophets, until the wrath of God arose against His people, until it could not be healed” … What … Until it could not be healed? Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: … anyone who disparages Torah scholars cannot be healed from his wound.

Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: What … which is written: “Do not touch My anointed ones and do My prophets no harm” … “Do not touch My anointed ones,” these are the schoolchildren, … “and do not harm My prophets,” these are Torah scholars. Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia: The world only exists because of the breath, … of schoolchildren. Rav Pappa said to Abaye: My … and yours, what … said to him: The breath … which is … sin, is not similar to the breath … which is not … sin. And Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia: One may not interrupt schoolchildren … even in order to build the Temple. And Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yehuda Nesia: I have received from my ancestors, and some say … from your ancestors as follows: Any city in which there are no schoolchildren … destroy it. Ravina said: … it desolate.

And Rava said: Jerusalem was destroyed only because there were no more trustworthy people there, as it is stated: “Roam about the streets of Jerusalem and see, and search its plazas, if you can find a person, who acts justly, who seeks integrity, that I should forgive it” … Is that so? Didn’t Rav Ketina say: Even at the time of Jerusalem’s failure, trustworthy people did not cease there, as it is stated: “For a man will grab his brother of his father’s house and say: You have a garment. Come be a chief over us … Things that people use to cover up like a garment, … are in your hands … “And let this ruin be under your care,”

Matters … that people do not ascertain unless they misunderstand them are in your hands; … be a chief over us. … “He will rise [yissa] on that day, saying, I will not be a ruler … The term rise [yissa] means nothing other than an oath, as it says: “Do not raise [tissa] the name of the Lord … I will not be a ruler, … I will not be one of those who close themselves up in the study hall, … while in my house there is no bread and no garment, for I have neither Bible nor Mishna nor Gemara in my hands. … And from what … Perhaps it is different … as had he told them: I studied … they would have said to him: Tell us … he could have … said he learned and forgot. … what … I will not be a ruler? … not … at all. … not difficult. Here, … with regard to matters of Torah; … here, … with regard to … business.

MISHNA: One may rescue a basket full of loaves … even if there is … one hundred meals in it. And … a round … of dried figs, … and … a barrel … of wine. And one may … say to others: Come and rescue for yourselves. And if … clever, they make a calculation with him after Shabbat

To where may one rescue … to a courtyard … eiruv … Ben Beteira says: … even to … where an eiruv … not … And one may carry there all the utensils, and put on all … that he can wear, and one may wrap all … that he can wrap … Rabbi Yosei says: … eighteen garments … one may again put on … and carry … out. And he may say to others: Come and rescue with me.

GEMARA: … Wasn’t it taught in the first clause, … three meals and no more? Rav Huna said: … not difficult. This … when one comes to rescue … that … one comes to collect … When one comes to rescue, he may rescue everything; when one comes to collect, he may collect food for only three meals. … Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said … Rav said: Both this and that … where one comes to collect, and … not difficult. This … to the same courtyard; that, … to a different courtyard. Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, raised a dilemma: … one spread his cloak … and collected and placed … and collected and placed … what … considered as one who comes to rescue or … like one who comes to collect?

from that which Rava said: Rav Sheizvi misled Rav Ḥisda, and … taught … provided that one does not bring a vessel that holds more than three meals. Conclude from … like one who comes to rescue, and … well … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said to Rava: What is the error … said to him, as it is taught: Provided that he does not bring another vessel … catch … another vessel and attach … it is another vessel that one may not … but in that … vessel, one may rescue as much as he wants,

And … a round … of dried figs … What is … a calculation doing … Aren’t they acquiring … from ownerless … Rav Ḥisda said: They taught an attribute of piety here. … Rava said: … pious … take payment … Shabbat? Rather, Rava said: Here, we are dealing with one who is Heaven-fearing … And … uncomfortable for him to benefit from … others, and it is also uncomfortable for him to exert … for free. And this is what … is saying: And if they are clever and know that in a situation of this kind it is not … payment for Shabbat … they … make a calculation with him after Shabbat.

And to where may one rescue … What is different here, … that it is taught … for yourselves, and what is different here, … that it is taught … with me? … With regard to food, it taught: For yourselves, because only food for three meals is suited for him, … However, with regard to … garments, it is taught: With me, because it is suited for him … all day,

The Sages taught … may wear … take … out … and remove … and return … and wear … and take … out and remove … And … even … all day long; … the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yosei says: … eighteen garments, and these are … eighteen garments: A cloak [miktoren], a cape [unkali], … and a … belt … a wide linen garment [kalbus], and a robe … a robe … and a kerchief … and two straps, … and two shoes, and two socks [anpilaot], and two … boots [pargod], and a belt around one’s loins … and a hat on one’s head, and a scarf around one’s neck.

one may establish a barrier … Is that to say that the Rabbis hold … indirect extinguishing is permitted … and Rabbi Yosei holds … indirect extinguishing is prohibited? raises a contradiction between … the Rabbis … the Rabbis; and … raises a contradiction between … Rabbi Yosei … Rabbi Yosei. tanna … before Rava bar Rav Huna taught … One who kills snakes and scorpions on Shabbat, the spirit of … pious is not pleased with him. … said to him: And … those pious, the spirit of the Sages is not pleased with them, … And … disagrees … Rav Huna, … Rav Huna saw a person killing a hornet … said to him: Have you finished killing all

said to him: … like those from your father’s house,

the Master said: In what … is … statement, … said? … does not know him; however, … knows him, it is prohibited. … However, … Rabban Gamliel … knows him … Abaye said: … not … in … presence, … Rava said: Even if you say … in his presence, … a lamp for one is a lamp for one hundred;

holds:
an object whose … function … for a prohibited … for the purpose … itself … permitted.

a reed or a shuttle [karkar] … The Sages taught … an unripe fig that one buried in straw … and … a cake that one buried in coals … if part of it is exposed, it is permitted to move it … And if not, … it is prohibited to move it

an … hand needle … to extract … with it. Rava, son of Rabba, sent … to Rav Yosef: Let our teacher teach us: … needle whose eye or point was removed, what is its

aligning the … infant … Rav Naḥman prohibits … and Rav Sheshet permits … Rav Naḥman says: From where do I say … As we learned in a mishna: One may not make

poles is as we learned … There were thin, smooth poles … and … one places … on his shoulder and on the shoulder of another, and suspends … and flays … Rabbi Elazar said: … the fourteenth … that occurred on Shabbat, … one places

a mortar … that which we said … Rabba said: From what … Perhaps, actually I … say to you … were taught after permission … utensils … rods … what is the reason … due to concern … decay. In that brief … it will not decay. … poles, … it is possible … in accordance with … Rabbi Elazar.

the thick end … in accordance with … Rabbi Yanai, as Rabbi Yanai says: We are dealing with a courtyard … Rabbi Yehoshua holds … inside the doorway is … like inside … and … he is moving utensils … houses in the courtyard. … And Rabbi Tarfon holds … inside the doorway is … like outside … and therefore, he is moving utensils … courtyard in the courtyard,
a mortar, … is … Rabbi Neḥemya,

One who carries out a person with his garments on him, and his sandals on his feet, and his rings on … his hands, … is exempt, whereas if he carried them out as they are, … he is liable

And … a basket with a stone inside it … And why … basket should be a base for a prohibited object, … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Here, we are dealing with a basket full of fruit. … And let him throw the fruit and throw … stone … and take … in his hands, … As Rabbi Elai … Rav said … to fruits that become soiled … Here, too, … to fruits that become soiled
And let him shake them … Rav Hiyya bar Ashi said … Rava said: Here, we are dealing with a broken basket … stone serves as a side of the basket

And one may move … teruma … . Rav Ḥisda said: They only taught … where … pure … is on the bottom and … impure … is on the top. … However, … pure … is on the top and the impure … is on the bottom, he takes the pure … and leaves the impure
And when … pure … is on the bottom too, let him throw … and take … Rabbi Elai said … Rav said: … to fruits that become soiled

raises an objection … One may move impure teruma with the pure … and with the non-sacred produce, whether the pure is on the top and the impure is on the bottom, or whether the impure is on the top and the pure is on the bottom. … a conclusive refutation of … Rav Hisda.
Rav Ḥisda … said to you: The mishna, … for the purpose of … itself, … for the purpose of … its place,
What impelled Rav Ḥisda to establish the mishna … for the purpose of … itself?

Rava said: The mishna … precise in accordance with … as it is taught in the latter clause, … coins that are on a cushion, he shakes the cushion and … fall. And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … only taught … for the purpose of … itself. However, … for the purpose of … its place, he may move it, … are still on it. And from … that the latter clause … for the purpose of … itself, the first clause, too, … for the purpose of … itself.
Rabbi Yehuda says: One may even lift … And why … Isn’t he rendering … fit
Rabbi Yehuda holds in accordance with … Rabbi Eliezer, … said: Teruma … placed in its pure … state.
As we learned … se’a … teruma that fell into less than one hundred … mixture. … And … from the mixture fell into a different place … Rabbi Eliezer says: … renders it a … mixture … definite teruma
And the Rabbis say: … mixture only renders … a … mixture according to … proportion
Say that you heard … to … stringently. Did you hear … to … leniently?

Rather, … stated his … in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon, as we learned … se’a … teruma fell into one hundred … and he did not manage to lift … until another … fell … this … is prohibited. … And Rabbi Shimon permits

And from what … Perhaps there, they are disagreeing with regard to this: That the first tanna holds: Even though … fell one after another, it is as … they fell at once, and this … fell into fifty … and this … fell into fifty … And Rabbi Shimon holds: The first … was nullified … into one hundred … and this … will be nullified in one hundred and one
Rather, … stated his … in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar. As it was taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: … he casts his eyes on this side … and he eats from a different side … .
And does … hold in accordance with

Doesn’t he disagree with him? As it was taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: One may lift … a mixture of one hundred … and one … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: One casts his eyes on this side … and he eats from a different side
Rabbi Yehuda is more far-reaching than … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.
MISHNA: … a stone, … on the mouth of a barrel, one tilts … on its side, and … falls. If … was among … barrels, … he lifts … and … tilts it on its side, and … falls.
coins that are on a cushion, he shakes the cushion and … fall. If there was bird dung … on … he wipes it with a rag, … was … of leather, … he places water on it until … ceases.
GEMARA: Rav Huna said … Rav said: They only taught … where one forgets … However, if he places … becomes a base for a prohibited object,
If … was among … barrels, … Who is … tanna … that any place that there is a prohibited … and a permitted … we … exert … for the permitted … we … not exert … for the prohibited

Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. As we learned … one who selects legumes on a Festival, … Beit Shammai say: He selects food and eats … And Beit Hillel say: He selects in his usual manner, … in his lap or in a large vessel.

And it was taught … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: In what … are these matters, … stated: … where the … food is greater than the … waste. However, if … waste is greater than the … food, everyone agrees … one selects … food
And here, … isn’t it comparable to … the food … greater than the waste,
Here, too, since if he wants to take … wine cannot be taken until he removes the stone, … like … waste … greater … than the food,

If … was among … barrels, he lifts … It was taught … : Rabbi Yosei says: … the barrel was placed in a storeroom … or … glass vessels were placed beneath it, … he lifts … to a different place, and he tilts it on its side, and … falls. And … he takes from … what he needs, and restores … to its place.
coins that are on a cushion, … Rav Hiyya bar Ashi said … Rav said: They only taught … where one forgets … however, if he places … becomes a base for a prohibited object

Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: They only taught … for the purpose of … itself; but … for the purpose of … its place, he moves … with … still on it. And likewise, Hiyya bar Rav from Difti taught … They only taught … for the purpose of … itself, but … for the purpose of … its place, he moves … with … still on it.

coins that are on a cushion, he shakes … Rabbi Oshaya said: … one forgot a purse … in the courtyard … he places a loaf … or a baby on it and moves it. … Rav Yitzhak said: … one forgot a brick in the courtyard, he places a loaf … or a baby on it and moves it. 
Rabbi Yehuda bar Sheila said … Rabbi Asi said: Once, they forgot a saddlebag [diskaya] full of coins in a main street, and they came and asked Rabbi Yoḥanan, and he said to them: Place a loaf or a baby on it, and move it.
Mar Zutra said: The halakha is in accordance with all these statements in … forgets. … Rav Ashi said: … one forgot, … also not … and they only stated … a loaf or a baby for … a corpse alone.

Abaye … place a spoon on bundles … Rava … place a knife on a … young dove and move it. Rav Yosef said … How sharp is the halakha of children? Say … the Sages stated … where one forgets, … did they say … ab initio?
Abaye … said: If not … I am an important person, why … I … a spoon on … bundles? Aren’t … suited to lean upon?
Rava said: If not … I am an important person, why … I … a knife on a young dove? Isn’t … suited … raw meat?
The reason … is … it is suited … raw meat; … it is not suited … raw meat, no, … Is that to say … Rava holds in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda,
Didn’t Rava say to his attendant … Roast a duck for me, and throw its intestines to the cat.
There, since … will putrefy … on his mind from yesterday.

So too, it is reasonable … that Rava holds in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, as Rava taught: A woman may not enter the wood storehouse to take a … poker … And … a poker that broke, it is prohibited to kindle … it on a Festival, as one may kindle … with vessels … but one may not kindle … with broken vessels … Conclude from it
MISHNA: Beit Shammai say: One … clear bones and shells … from the table … And Beit Hillel say: One … remove the entire board [tavla] … and shake … it,
One … clear … crumbs from the table, … less than an olive-bulk, and pea and lentil pods. … because it is animal fodder.

a sponge, if it has leather … a handle, one may wipe … with it, and if not, one may not wipe … with it … And the Rabbis say: Both this, … and that, … may be moved on Shabbat and it does not become ritually impure.
GEMARA: Rav Naḥman said: … we have only Beit Shammai in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, … and Beit Hillel in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon,
One … clear … crumbs from the table. … supports … Rabbi Yoḥanan, as Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … crumbs that are less than an olive-bulk, it is prohibited to destroy them by hand
pea … pods … Whose … is it … Rabbi Shimon, who is not … set-aside.

Say the latter clause … a sponge, if it has leather … a handle, one may wipe … with it, and if not, one may not wipe … with it. We have arrived at … Rabbi Yehuda, … said: An unintentional act is prohibited,
In that … even Rabbi Shimon agrees … as it is Abaye and Rava who both say: Rabbi Shimon agrees in … Cut off its head will it not die,
those pits of Aramean dates, … it is permitted to move … since … are fit … due to their origin, … And … of Persian … is prohibited.
Shmuel … carry them along with bread. … shin, resh, nun, mem, shin, peh, zayin … a mnemonic … Shmuel’s … with his reasoning, as Shmuel said: A man may perform all his needs with bread.

Rabba would move them along with a pitcher of water. Rav Huna, son … Rav Yehoshua, would render them a chamber pot with excrement. … Rav Ashi said to Ameimar: And may one create a chamber pot with excrement ab initio?

Rav Sheshet would dispose of … with his tongue. Rav Pappa would dispose of them behind the divan … They said about Rabbi Zekharya ben Avkolas that he would turn his face … back of the divan and dispose of them.

MISHNA: … a barrel … that broke … one may rescue from it food … three meals, and … say to others: Come and rescue … for yourselves. … provided that one does not soak up … One may not squeeze fruits … to extract liquids from them. And if … seeped out on their own, it is prohibited … Rabbi Yehuda says: If … for eating, … that seeps from them … is permitted. … And if … for liquids, … that seep from them … are prohibited. … honeycombs that one crushed on Shabbat eve, and … seeped … on their own … they are prohibited, and Rabbi Eliezer permits

GEMARA: It was taught … One may not soak up wine and … may not collect oil … that one will not conduct … in the manner that he conducts … during the week. The Sages taught … one’s fruit was scattered in a courtyard … one may collect them from hand to hand, … and eat … However, … not … into a basket or into a box, … that one will not conduct … in the manner that he conducts … during the week.

One may not squeeze fruit … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: Rabbi Yehuda concedes to the Rabbis with regard to olives and grapes. … What is the reason … Since they are … for squeezing, one had in mind … And Ulla … Rav said: Rabbi Yehuda was in disagreement even with regard to olives and grapes. And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda with regard to other fruits, and the halakha is not in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda with regard to olives and grapes.
Rabba said … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said … Rabbi Yehuda would concede to the Rabbis with regard to olives and grapes, and the Rabbis would concede to Rabbi Yehuda with regard to other fruit.

Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Abba: … with regard to what do they disagree? He said to him: When you find … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: It stands to reason that they disagree with regard to mulberries and pomegranates,

As it was taught … olives from which one squeezed oil and grapes from which one squeezed wine … he … brought them into … whether … for … food or whether … for … liquids, that which seeps from them … is prohibited. … mulberries from which one squeezed water, … and pomegranates from which one squeezed wine, … and he brought them into … brought them in for … food, what seeps from them is permitted. And … for … liquids, and … without specifying … what seeps from them is prohibited. … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda. And the Rabbis say: Whether … for … food or whether … for … liquids, what seeps from them is prohibited.

And does Rabbi Yehuda maintain that … undesignated … is prohibited? Didn’t we learn … A woman’s milk … renders … ritual impurity, … volitionally and … unvolitionally? … milk of an animal only renders … ritual impurity … volitionally

Rabbi Akiva said: It is an a fortiori inference … Just as a woman’s milk, which is intended only for young … renders … ritual impurity … volitionally and … unvolitionally, the milk of an animal, which is intended for both young and old, is it not logical that it should render … ritual impurity, both … volitionally and … unvolitionally? They said to him … If a woman’s milk … ritual impurity … unvolitionally, as … the blood of her wound is … ritual impurity, … the milk of an animal … ritual impurity

unintentionally, as the blood of its wound is ritually pure, … said to them: I am … stringent with regard to milk than with regard to blood, as … one milks … for medicinal purposes, … ritual impurity, and … one lets … for medicinal purposes, … ritually pure, … They said to him: … baskets of olives and grapes will prove … as liquid that seeps from them volitionally … ritual impurity. … unvolitionally is ritually pure,

What, is it not … volitionally … is pleased … and … unvolitionally … to … indeterminate … Just as … olives and grapes, which are … designated for squeezing … unvolitionally, … it has no … mulberries and pomegranates, which are not … designated for squeezing, is it not all the more so

No, … volitionally … is indeterminate, … unvolitionally … one revealed his mind-set … said: I am not pleased … And if you wish, say … baskets of olives and grapes are different; since … stands to be lost, one renounces it from the outset.

We have found … Rabbi Yehuda conceded to the Rabbis with regard to olives and grapes, … From where do we … the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Yehuda with regard to other fruits … As it was taught … One may squeeze
plums and quinces and crab apples. However, … not … pomegranates, … from the house of Menashya bar Menaḥem would squeeze pomegranates

And from where … is … of the Rabbis? Perhaps it is … Rabbi Yehuda. … And let … also be … Rabbi Yehuda: Say that you heard … Rabbi Yehuda, … seeped out on its own … did you hear … squeezing … ab initio? Rather, what have you to say? Since they are not … designated for squeezing, … even ab initio. … even if you say … the Rabbis, … Since they are not … designated for squeezing, … even ab initio. … learn from it … is … the Rabbis. … learn from it.
from the house of Menashya bar Menaḥem would squeeze pomegranates … Rav Naḥman said: … halakha is in accordance with … from the house of Menashya bar Menaḥem.

Rava said to Rav Naḥman: … Menashya ben Menaḥem a tanna … And if you say … halakha is in accordance with this tanna, who held in accordance with … from … Menashya ben Menaḥem, … because he held in accordance with … Menashya ben Menaḥem, the halakha is in accordance with his opinion? … Menashya ben Menaḥem … the majority of the world?

Yes, … as we learned … maintains thorns in a vineyard, Rabbi Eliezer says: He rendered … forbidden … And the Rabbis say: Only … that people … maintain renders … forbidden. And Rabbi Ḥanina said: What is the reason for … Rabbi Eliezer? Because in Arabia they maintain the thorns of the fields … to their camels.
Is this comparable? Arabia … a place, … Here, … his opinion … irrelevant by … all other men.

Rather, this is the reason … in accordance with … Rav Ḥisda, … Rav Ḥisda said: … beets that one squeezed and … placed … in a ritual bath, … invalidates the ritual bath … change of appearance. … Aren’t … not designated for squeezing? Rather, what have you to say? Since he ascribed it significance, it is … a liquid. Here, too, … since he ascribed it significance, it is … a liquid.

Rav Pappa said … because it is something with which one may not make a ritual bath ab initio, … Anything with which one may not make a ritual bath ab initio, … invalidates the ritual bath … change of appearance,

We learned … there, … wine or vinegar or … discharge, … fell into … and changed its appearance, … invalid. … Who is the tanna … that … discharge is … liquid? Abaye said: It is Rabbi Ya’akov, as it was taught … Rabbi Ya’akov says: … discharge is like … a liquid. And what … reason … said that … discharge that emerges at the outset, … is ritually pure, … because he does not want its existence;

Rabbi Shimon says: … discharge is not like … a liquid. And what … reason … said that the … sap that emerges from the bale of the olive press … is … ritually impure? Because it is impossible … it … not … drops of oil

What is … between them? … There is … between them … that comes after extensive pressing; … Rava said: … because it is something with which one may not make a ritual bath … and it … invalidates a ritual bath … change of appearance.

Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: A person may squeeze a cluster of grapes … into a pot … however, … not … into an … bowl. Rav Ḥisda said: From the statement of our Rabbi, … we learn … one may milk a goat into a pot … however, … not … into an … bowl. … Apparently, he holds … liquid that comes into food … it is food.
Rami bar Ḥama raised an objection … a zav who milks a goat, the milk is ritually impure … And if you say … liquid that comes … into food is food … With what … rendered susceptible
As Rabbi Yoḥanan said … the … drop, which is smeared on the top of the teat … here too, … of the drop which is smeared on the top of the teat.
Ravina raised an objection … one who is ritually impure … a corpse who squeezed olives or grapes

exact … an egg-bulk, … is ritually pure. … more than an egg-bulk, … is ritually impure. And if you say … liquid that comes into food is … food, in what … rendered susceptible … He raised the objection and he resolved it: … where … squeezes into an … bowl,

Rabbi Yirmeya said: … parallel to … tanna’im. … one who smooths … by … grapes … was not rendered susceptible … Rabbi Yehuda says: It was rendered susceptible … What, do they not disagree about this? … Sage held that liquid that comes into food is food, … and … Sage held … it is not food

Rav Pappa said … everyone agrees that liquid that comes into food is not food, and here they disagree with regard to liquid that goes to waste, … Sage, … held … it is … a liquid … and … Sage held that it is not a liquid. And … the dispute between these tanna’im, as it was taught … one who cuts olives with soiled, … hands, … are rendered susceptible … to dip them in salt, … are not rendered susceptible

to ascertain whether his olives have reached … to be harvested or not, they are not rendered susceptible … Rabbi Yehuda said: They are rendered susceptible … What, do they not disagree with regard to this? … Sage, … held … liquid … which stands to … waste, is liquid … and … Sage held that it is not liquid
Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said: … These tanna’im, … disagreed with regard to liquid that stands … to waste, and those tanna’im, … disagreed with regard to liquid that stands … to shine it.
Rabbi Zeira said … Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said … Rav said: A person may squeeze a cluster of grapes into a pot … however, … not … into a bowl … And … fish for its brine … even into a bowl.

Rav Dimi sat and stated this halakha. Abaye said to Rav Dimi: You teach … in the name of Rav and it is not difficult for you; we teach it in the name of Shmuel and it is difficult for us … Did Shmuel say … a fish for its brine even into a bowl? Wasn’t it stated … pickled vegetables that one squeezed? Rav said: … themselves … it is permitted … their liquid, he is exempt … but it is prohibited

And … boiled vegetables, whether … themselves … or whether … for their liquids, it is permitted … And Shmuel said: … both pickled vegetables and boiled vegetables, … for … themselves, it is permitted, and … for their liquids, he is exempt … but it is prohibited

He said to him: … By God! … my eyes have seen it, and not another’s” … I heard … from the mouth of Rabbi Yirmeya, and Rabbi Yirmeya … from Rabbi Zeira, and Rabbi Zeira … from Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi, and Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi … from Rav,

the matter itself. … pickled vegetables that one squeezed, Rav said … for themselves, it is permitted, … for their liquids he is exempt … but it is prohibited … and … boiled vegetables, … both for themselves and for their liquids it is permitted. And Shmuel said: … both this, … and that, … for … themselves … is permitted; … for their liquids, one is exempt, but it is prohibited … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … both pickled vegetables and boiled vegetables, … themselves it is permitted; … for their liquids, he is liable to … a sin-offering

raises an objection … One may squeeze pickled vegetables on Shabbat for the purpose of … Shabbat but not for the conclusion of Shabbat. And one may not squeeze olives and grapes … and if one squeezed … liable to … a sin-offering. … difficult … to … Rav, … difficult … to … Shmuel, … difficult … to … Rabbi Yoḥanan, … Rav interprets … according to his … reasoning, Shmuel interprets … according to his … reasoning, … Rabbi Yoḥanan interprets … according to his … reasoning.

Rav interprets … according to his … reasoning … One may squeeze pickled vegetables on Shabbat for the purpose of Shabbat, but not for the conclusion of Shabbat. In what … is this statement said? … for themselves; however, … for their liquid, … exempt … but it is prohibited … And … boiled vegetables, whether … for themselves or … for their liquid, it is permitted. And … olives and grapes, one may not squeeze … and if one squeezed them … he is liable to … a sin-offering.

Shmuel interprets … according to his … reasoning … One may squeeze pickled vegetables on Shabbat for the purpose of Shabbat, … the same is true for boiled vegetables. In what … is this statement said? … for themselves; however, … for their liquids, … not liable … but it is prohibited … And … olives and grapes, one may not squeeze … and if one squeezed … liable to … a sin-offering.

Rabbi Yoḥanan … interprets … according to his … reasoning … One may squeeze pickled vegetables for the purpose of Shabbat but not for the conclusion of Shabbat, … both to pickled vegetables and to boiled vegetables. In what … is this statement said? … for themselves, but … for their liquids, one may not squeeze … and if one squeezed … he becomes like one who squeezed olives or grapes, and he is liable to … a sin-offering.

Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said … Rav said: By Torah law, one is only liable for stomping … olives and grapes, … And similarly, it was taught … the school of Menashe: By Torah law, one is only liable for stomping on olives and grapes. … And … witness … from the mouth of … witness, … is valid
only for testimony … a woman’s
A dilemma was raised before … hearsay testimony in testimony … a firstborn … what is … Rav Ami prohibited … and Rav Asi permitted

Rav Ami said to Rav Asi: Didn’t the school … Menashya teach … hearsay testimony is only valid in testimony … a woman … say: … only … in testimony for which … a woman is valid. … Rav Yeimar deemed hearsay testimony … Mareimar called him: Yeimar who permits the firstborn; … And the halakha is … hearsay testimony is valid with regard to a firstborn

honeycombs … When Rav Hoshaya came from Neharde’a, he came and brought a baraita with him: … olives and grapes that one crushed before Shabbat and … seeped out on their own … are prohibited … and Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon permit

Rav Yosef said … Did he … come to teach us an additional person? … Abaye said to him: He is teaching us a great deal, as if … from the mishna … I would have said: It is there that it is … initially … food and ultimately … food, … However, here, … which initially … food and ultimately … liquid, say … not … he is teaching us

MISHNA: Any … that was … placed in hot water, … before Shabbat, one may soak it in hot water … on Shabbat. And anything that was not placed in hot water before Shabbat, one may rinse it in hot water on Shabbat … with the exception of old salted … and small salted fish and … kolyas ha’ispanin … for which rinsing … itself is completion of the prohibited labor

GEMARA: … In what case … Rav Safra said: In the case of the chicken of Rabbi Abba, … And Rav Safra said: One time I happened to come there and he fed me … and if not … Rabbi Abba gave me three-leaf-, … old wine to drink, I would have been forced

The Gemara relates that Rabbi Yoḥanan would spit from the thought of Babylonian kutaḥ, … Rav Yosef said: Then we should spit from … Rabbi Abba’s chicken, … And furthermore, Rav Gaza said: … one occasion I happened to come there, … and I prepared Babylonian kutaḥ, … all of the sick people of the West, … asked me for it.

Anything that was not … in hot water … one … rinsed … what is … Rav Yosef said: … one rinsed … liable to … a sin-offering … Mar, son of Ravina, said: We, too, have also learned … Except for old salted fish and kolyas ha’ispanin, rinsing itself is completion of their prohibited labor … learn from this

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Asi were sitting before Rabbi Yoḥanan, and Rabbi Yoḥanan was sitting and dozing. … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said to Rabbi Asi: For what … are the fowl in Babylonia fatter … He said to him: … go to the desert of Gaza … and I will show you … fatter than them. … For what … Festivals in Babylonia more joyous … Because … they are poor, … For what … are Torah scholars in Babylonia distinguished … Because they are not well-versed in Torah. … For what … are gentiles … contaminated? … Because they eat abominable creatures and crawling things,

Rabbi Yoḥanan woke up … and said to them: … children, did I not tell you this, … “Say to wisdom: You are my sister, … if the matter is as clear to you as … your sister is forbidden to you, say it, and if not, do not say it; … They said to him: Then will the Master tell us … some of them? … Why are … fowl in Babylonia fatter … Because they were not exiled, as it says: “Moab has been at ease since his youth and he has settled on his lees, … and did not go into captivity;

And here … from where do we … that … were exiled? As it was taught … Rabbi Yehuda says … no person passed through … Judea … fifty-two years, as it is stated: “I will raise crying and wailing for the mountains … from the bird of the heavens to the beast [behema, … all have fled and gone” … Behema has a numerical value of fifty-two,

Rabbi Ya’akov said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: They all returned except for the kolyas ha’ispanin, as Rav said: Those inclines of Babylonia return the water … to the spring of Eitam … And this … because its spine is not strong, it could not ascend

For what … Festivals in Babylonia more joyous … Because they were not … in that curse … as it is written: “And I will cause all of her happiness to cease, her Festival, her New Moon, and her Shabbat and all her Festivals” … And it is … written: “My soul hates your New Moons and your Festivals; they are a burden to Me; … What is … “They are a burden to me”? Rabbi Elazar said … the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: Is it not enough for the Jewish people that they sin before Me, that they … burden Me to know which harsh decree I will bring upon them? Rabbi Yitzḥak said: … there is not a single Festival on which troops did not come to Tzippori … And Rabbi Ḥanina said: There is not a single Festival on which an egmon and a kamton and a branch bearer, … did not come to Tiberias

For what … the Torah scholars in Babylonia distinguished … Because they are not native to that place … as people say … In … city, … my name; in … not … city, … my clothing. … to come Jacob will take root, Israel will bud and blossom” … Rav Yosef taught: These are the Torah scholars in Babylonia, who add buds and blossoms to the Torah.
Why are gentiles … contaminated? … they did not stand on Mount Sinai. As when

the snake came upon Eve, … it infected her with … contamination, … Jewish people stood at Mount Sinai, their contamination ceased, … gentiles did not stand at Mount Sinai, … their contamination never ceased. Rav Aḥa, the son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi: What … converts? … said to him: Even though they … were not … their guardian angels were … as it is written: … with he that stands here with us today before the Lord our God, and with he that is not here

disagrees with Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, as Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Until three generations … contamination did not cease from our forefathers: Abraham fathered Ishmael, … Isaac fathered Esau; … Jacob fathered twelve tribes in whom there was no flaw.

MISHNA: A person may break a barrel … to eat dried figs from it, provided he does not intend to make a vessel. And one may not perforate the plug of a barrel … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda. And the Rabbis permit … one may not perforate … on its side. And if it was … perforated, one may not apply wax to it … because … he spreads … Rabbi Yehuda said: An incident … came before Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai in … Arav, and he said: I am concerned for him, … to … a sin-offering
GEMARA: Rabbi Oshaya said: They only taught … pressed … However, … separated, … not … And … not … separated

raises an objection … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: A person may bring a barrel of wine and cut off … top … with a sword and place it before the guests on Shabbat without concern … That … the Rabbis, … our mishna is … Rabbi Neḥemya,

And what forced Rabbi Oshaya to establish the mishna in accordance with … Rabbi Neḥemya … to … pressed … Let him establish … to separated … and … the Rabbis.
