Rava said: The mishna … difficulty for him; why did … teach particularly … dried figs? Let him teach … fruit. Rather, learn from here that … pressed

It was taught in one … baskets of dried figs or of dates, one may untie … unbraid … and cut … And it was taught in another … One may untie … but one may not unbraid or cut … not difficult. This … the Rabbis. That … Rabbi Neḥemya. As it was taught … Rabbi Neḥemya says: Even a large spoon and even a cloak and even a knife may only be taken … for their … use,

raised a dilemma before Rav Sheshet: What is … to perforate a barrel with a spear [burtiya] on Shabbat? … one intends to … an opening … and … prohibited, or perhaps … one … intends to … generosity and it is permitted? … said to them: He intends to … an opening … and it is prohibited.

raises an objection … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: One may bring a barrel of wine … and cut off its top with a sword. … There, … he certainly intends to … generosity … here, … if it were … he intends … generosity, let him open

And one may not perforate the plug … Rav Huna said: … dispute … on top … however, … from the side, everyone agrees that it is prohibited, … And that is … is teaching: One may not perforate it on its side. … Rav Ḥisda said: … dispute … from the side; however, … on top, everyone agrees that it is permitted, and … that which … is teaching: One may not perforate it on its side, there … the barrel itself,

The Sages taught … One may not create a new hole … on Shabbat. And if one seeks to add … one may add … and some say … one may not … add … And … that one may perforate … an old hole, … ab initio. And … the first tanna, … What is different … creating a new hole is not … he is creating an opening? … adding … he is also creating an opening.

Rabba said: … by Torah law, any opening that is not made to … insert and to remove is not … an opening, … And it was the Sages who issued a decree … because … a chicken coop, … to let in air and to let out heat, … And … if one seeks to add … one may add … one will certainly not come to add to … in a chicken coop,

because … vermin … And … some say … one may not add … sometimes one does not properly … initially, and comes to expand it … Rav Naḥman taught in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: … halakha is in accordance with … Some say.

And … agrees that one may perforate an old hole … ab initio. Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: They only taught … in a place where … is made to strain … however, … to reinforce … prohibited … What are the circumstances … to strain … what are the circumstances … to reinforce … Rav Ḥisda said: … above … the wine, that is … to strain … below … the wine, that is … to reinforce … Rava said: … below … the wine is also … to strain … and what are the circumstances … to reinforce … where one perforated it below the sediment.

Abaye said to Rava: … was taught that supports your … A house … sealed … has … four cubits … one broke its doorposts … it does not have … four cubits … A house … sealed … does not render all of its surroundings ritually impure; … one broke its doorposts, … it renders all of its surroundings ritually impure.

reed … Rav prohibited … and Shmuel permitted … cutting … ab initio, everyone agrees … it is prohibited, … restoring … everyone agrees that it is permitted. When they disagree is … has been cut but not … inserted … The one who prohibits … we issue a decree … perhaps one will come to cut … ab initio … and the one who permits … we do not issue a decree

parallel to … tanna’im: One may not cut a … tube on a Festival, and needless to say, … on Shabbat. … fell, one may restore it … on Shabbat, and needless to say, … on a Festival. And Rabbi Yoshiya is lenient

Rabbi Yoshiya: On which … If you say … the first clause … isn’t he creating a vessel, … Rather, … to the latter clause … the first tanna also permits … Rather, … it was cut but not inserted … there is … between them: One Sage, … held that we issue a decree … and one Sage held that we do not issue a decree. … Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, taught … in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: … halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yoshiya.

And … And if … was … perforated, … oil: Rav prohibited … and Shmuel permitted … The one who prohibits … we issue a decree … due to … wax. And the one who permits … we do not issue a decree … Rav Shmuel bar bar Ḥana said to Rav Yosef: … You told us explicitly in Rav’s name: Oil is permitted

Tavut the hunter said … Shmuel said: … this myrtle leaf, it is prohibited … What is the reason … Rav Yeimar of Difti said: … a decree … due to … an … spout … Rav Ashi said: … a decree … lest one cut … What is … between them? … There is … between them … were … cut and placed,

felt cloths … Rav prohibited … and Shmuel permitted … With regard to … soft … everyone agrees … it is permitted, … With regard to … hard … everyone agrees … it is prohibited. When they disagree, … with regard to … intermediate … The one who prohibits … appears as … a burden, and the one who permits … it does not appear as … a burden,

this … to Rav was not stated explicitly … rather, it was stated by inference, … As Rav happened … to a certain place … there was not … room … he went … and sat in a karmelit. They brought him felt … he did not sit … One who saw … assumed … because it is prohibited … cloths … however, that is not so, … Rav … proclaim … it is permitted … felt … And it was in deference to our Rabbis … he did not sit on it, … And who were … Rav Kahana and Rav Asi,

MISHNA: One may place a … dish into an … pit … so that it will be protected … and … good … water … into bad, … so that … will cool off. And … cold water … in the sun so that … will be heated. … Someone whose garments fell into water … on the road may … walk … them and need not be concerned … reaches the outer courtyard … he spreads them in the sun … but not opposite the masses,
GEMARA: … obvious … Lest you say: Let us issue a decree … due to … leveling holes … it teaches us

good water into bad water … obvious … necessary … the latter clause … cold water … in the sun. … This, too, is obvious. … Lest you say that we should issue a decree … perhaps one will come to insulate it in hot ashes … it teaches us

one whose … fell … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: Wherever the Sages prohibited … due to … appearance … even in the innermost chambers … it is prohibited, … We learned … one may spread them in the sun but not opposite the masses, … It is … tanna’im, as it was taught … One may spread them out in the sun but not opposite the masses. Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon prohibit
Rav Huna said:

One who shakes his cloak on Shabbat … is liable to … a sin-offering … We only stated … with regard to new … but with regard to old … we have no … with … And we only stated … with regard to black … but with regard to white or red … we have no … And this … when one is particular about … them

Ulla happened to … Pumbedita, … he saw rabbis shaking their cloaks … He said: The Rabbis are desecrating Shabbat. Rav Yehuda said to … shake … in his presence. We are not at all particular about this,
Abaye was standing before Rav Yosef. … said to him: Give me my hat. … saw that there was dew on it, … he hesitated to give … to him, … said to him: Shake … throw … we are not at all particular

Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who goes out with a cloak folded … resting on his shoulder on Shabbat is liable to … a sin-offering … This … was also taught … Clothing merchants who go outside with cloaks folded and resting on their shoulders on Shabbat are liable to … a sin-offering. And they did not say … only with regard to clothing merchants; rather, any person … and … only stated … because it is the … manner for merchants to go out this way.

And … a shopkeeper who goes out with coins bound in his cloak is liable to … a sin-offering. And they did not say … only with regard to a shopkeeper; rather, any person … and … only stated … it is the … manner of a shopkeeper to go out this way. And runners, … may go out … with scarves on their shoulders, … And they did not say … only with regard to runners; rather, any person … but it is … the … manner of runners to go out this way.

Rabbi Yehuda said: There was an incident involving Hyrcanus, son of Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus, who went outside with a scarf on his shoulder on Shabbat. However, a thread … was tied around his finger … When this matter came before the Sages, they said: … even if a thread is not tied around one’s finger. … Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda taught in the name of Rav Ḥisda: … halakha … even if a thread … is not tied around one’s finger.

Ulla happened … to the house of Asi bar Hini. … asked him: What is … to make a spout … on Shabbat? … said to them … this is what Rabbi Elai said: It is prohibited to make a spout on Shabbat. … What is … spout … Rabbi Zeira said: … Babylonian pockets,

Rabbi Yirmeya was sitting before Rabbi Zeira … said to him: What is … this … He said to him: … prohibited … And what is … this? He said to him: … prohibited. Rav Pappa said: Grasp this principle: Any … to gather … is prohibited, … any … that is … to beautify oneself … permitted, as … Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, who was beautifying himself with his garment

When Rav Dimi came … he said: … one occasion, Rabbi … went out into a field, and the two sides of his cloak were resting on his shoulders. Yehoshua ben Zeiruz, son of the father-in-law of Rabbi Meir, said before … In … this, didn’t Rabbi Meir hold one liable to … a sin-offering? … said to him: Was Rabbi Meir exacting to that … Rabbi … lowered his cloak

When Ravin came … he said: It was not Yehoshua ben Zeiruz; rather, it was Yehoshua ben Kefusai, Rabbi Akiva’s son-in-law, … he said: In … this, didn’t Rabbi Akiva hold one liable to … a sin-offering? … said to him: Was Rabbi Akiva exacting to that … Rabbi … lowered his cloak … When Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda came, he said: … it was stated … was asked,

MISHNA: One who bathes … in … cave water or in the water of Tiberias and dried himself even with ten towels may not carry them in his hand, … However, ten people may … one towel … dry their faces, hands, and feet, and may carry them in their hands.

One may smear oil … and … rub … however, one may not exert himself … and one may not scrape … one may not go into a swampy river [kurdima], … And one may not make a drug to induce vomiting, nor may one align a young … nor may one reset a break … One whose hand or foot was dislocated may not move them about … in cold … however, one may wash … in the typical manner, and if one is cured … he is cured.

GEMARA: … teaches … cave water … similar to the … water of Tiberias; just as the water of Tiberias is hot, so too the cave water is hot. … one who bathes, after the fact, yes, … one may not … ab initio, … by inference

rinsing one’s entire body … well … even ab initio … whose … It is … Rabbi Shimon, as it was taught … One may not rinse himself … neither with hot … nor with cold … the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Shimon permits … Rabbi Yehuda says … With hot … it is prohibited … with cold … it is permitted.

And dried himself off even with ten towels. … The first clause teaches us a novel … and the latter clause teaches us a novel … The first clause: … teaches us a novel … that … even … these … which do not have much water … in them. … since he is one … he … come to squeeze … And the latter clause teaches us a novel … even these … that they have … much water … since they are many … they remind each other

The Sages taught … One may dry himself with a towel … and leave it in the window … and one may not give it to the bath attendants, because they are suspect in this matter … Rabbi Shimon says: One may dry himself with a single towel and carry it in his hand into his home,
Abaye said to Rav Yosef: What is the halakha … said to him: There is Rabbi Shimon, there is Rabbi … there is Shmuel, … there is Rabbi Yoḥanan,

Rabbi Shimon … as we have … stated … Rabbi … as it was taught … Rabbi … said: When we would study Torah with Rabbi Shimon in Tekoa, we would carry oil and towels from the courtyard to the roof and from the roof into an enclosure … until we reached the spring in which we would bathe, … Shmuel … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said … One may dry himself with a towel and carry it in his hand into his home. Rabbi Yoḥanan … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … halakha … one may dry himself with a towel and carry it in his hand into his house.

And did Rabbi Yoḥanan … say that? Didn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan state … the halakha is in accordance with an unattributed mishna, … And we learned … and dried himself even with ten towels, he may not carry them in his hand. … teaches it in accordance with … ben Ḥakhinai,

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Bath attendants may bring women’s bathing garments [balarei] to the bathhouse … as long as they cover their heads and the majority of their bodies with them, … large scarf … one must tie its two ends … below … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … below the shoulders. … Rava said to the inhabitants of … Meḥoza: When you transport clothing for the soldiers … extend them beneath your shoulders

One may smear oil and rub … The Sages taught … One may smear oil … and rub … intestinal … on Shabbat, … provided he does not do so in the manner in which he does during the week. … How … does one do … Rabbi Ḥama bar Ḥanina said: One … smears oil and afterward rubs … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One smears oil and rubs simultaneously.

However, one may not exert himself … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It is prohibited to stand on the floor of … Deyomset … because it warms and heals … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: The entire period … Deyomset … is twenty-one days; and Shavuot is included. … raises a dilemma: Is Shavuot on this side, … or on this side, … Come … hear … Shmuel said: All … drinks are effective from Passover to Shavuot; … Perhaps there, … it is … the cooler the world, the better … however, here, … due to the heat, … the warmer the world, the better.
Rabbi Ḥelbo said: The wine of Phrygia [Perugaita] and the water … the Deyomset deprived Israel … ten … tribes.

Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh happened … there, … he was drawn after them, … his … learning was forgotten. When he returned, he stood to read from a … scroll … was supposed to read … “This month shall be for you [haḥodesh hazeh lakhem]” … Have their hearts become deaf … haḥeresh haya libbam], … The Sages … asked for … mercy on him, and his learning was restored.

And that is … we learned … Rabbi Nehorai says: Exile yourself to a place of Torah and do not say that it will follow you, as … your colleagues will establish it in your hands, and do not rely on your understanding … It was taught: Rabbi Nehorai was not his name, but rather Rabbi Neḥemya was his name; and some say … Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh was his name … And why was he called Rabbi Nehorai? … because he would illuminate [manhir] the eyes of the Sages in halakha.

However, one may not scrape … The Sages taught … One may not scrape … with a scraper on Shabbat. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: If one’s feet were dirty with mortar and excrement he may scrape … in the usual manner … and need not be concerned … Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda’s mother made him a silver scraper
one may not enter a swampy river … What is the reason … Due to the mud,

one may not make a drug to induce vomiting … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: They only taught … with a drug, … however, … by hand is permitted. It was taught … Rabbi Neḥemya says: Even during the week, … it is prohibited … because … loss of food.

And … one may not align a young … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … swaddling an infant … well … Didn’t we learn … one may not align … There, … the bones, … of the spine, because … appears like … building.
one may not reset a break … Rav Ḥana of Baghdad said … Shmuel said:

halakha … one may reset a break … Rabba bar bar Ḥana happened … to Pumbedita … he did not enter Rav Yehuda’s lecture. … sent for Adda, his attendant, … said to him: Go drag him … He went and dragged him … came and found … teaching … one may not reset a break … He said to him: This is what Rav Ḥana of Baghdad said … Shmuel said: … halakha … one may reset a break … said to him: Ḥana is ours, … and Shmuel is ours, and … I did not … hear … did I not rightfully drag you

one whose hand was dislocated … Rav Avya was … sitting before Rav Yosef and his hand became dislocated. … he said to him: What … this? … It is prohibited. … And what … this … said to him: It is prohibited. In the meantime, his hand … was healed.

said to him: What is your dilemma? We learned … one whose hand or foot was dislocated … may not … move it about in cold water; however, he may rinse it in the usual manner, and if it is healed, it is healed. … said to him: … as didn’t we learn … one may not reset a break, and Rav Ḥana of Baghdad said … Shmuel said … the halakha is … one may … reset a broken bone. … said to him: Were all these woven together in a single weave? Where it was stated … it was stated; where it was not stated, it was not stated.

MISHNA: One may borrow jugs of wine and jugs of oil from another … as long as one does not say … to him: Loan me. And similarly, a woman … from another loaves … And if … does not trust him … may leave his cloak with him … and make … calculation with him after Shabbat. And similarly, … the eve of Passover in Jerusalem, when … occurs on Shabbat, one … may leave his cloak with him, … and take … his Paschal lamb, and … make … calculation with him after the Festival.

GEMARA: … Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye: What is different … let me borrow, … And what is different … loan me … He said to him: … let me borrow, … will not come to write … loan me … will come to write

But since on weekdays there are times one intends to say loan me and … says let me borrow, and … is not particular about his … he comes to write … on Shabbat he will also come to write. … said to him: On a weekday, when there is no difference if one says loan me or let me borrow, … are not particular about his … come to write … On Shabbat, since … let me borrow was allowed by the Sages, … loan me was not permitted, the matter is recognizable. … and … will not come to write.

Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye: Now, since the Sages said that … all matters of a Festival, as much as we can change … we change, these women who fill their pitchers with water, what is the reason they do not change … Because it is not possible … How would they do it … those who … fill a large pitcher should fill a small pitcher … they would … add … walking … those who … fill a small pitcher would fill a large pitcher … they would … add … load.
we should … spread a cloth … may come to … squeezing … we would cover it with a lid, sometimes it is severed … and one will … come to tie it. Therefore, … it is impossible

And Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye: … learn … one may not clap … or clap one’s hand against one’s body, or dance on a Festival? And we see, … that people do … and we do not say anything to … them. … And according to your reasoning, … this … Rava said: One may not sit … at the entrance … the post, … lest an object roll away … and he come to bring it … And yet we see that … put down their jugs and sit at the entrance of the alleyway, and we do not say anything to … them. Rather, … Leave the Jewish people … It is better that they be unwitting … and … they not be intentional

understood from this … this … applies only to rabbinic … but not to Torah … that is not so. There is no difference … rabbinic … and Torah … For … adding to Yom Kippur … is from the Torah, and we see … who eat and drink … up until nightfall, and we do not say anything to them.

And similarly, a woman … loaves … from another … on Shabbat that it is prohibited, but on a weekday it seems well. … let us say that the mishna is not in accordance with … Hillel, for we learned … And thus Hillel would say: A woman may not loan a loaf … to another until she calculates … monetary … lest wheat become more valuable and they come to … interest.
Even if you say … Hillel, … This … in a place … the price … is set, … this … in a place … its price is not set.

if … does not trust … was said … loans on a Festival: Rav Yosef said … cannot be claimed … And Rabba said … can be claimed … Rav Yosef said … cannot be claimed … for if you say … it can be claimed, … come to write … Rabba said … can be claimed, for if you say … it cannot … will not give him … and … will refrain from rejoicing on the Festival.

We learned … if he does not trust him, he may leave his cloak with him … Granted, … if you say … cannot be claimed, … Due to this, he leaves his cloak with him and makes a calculation with him after Shabbat. However, if you say … can … be claimed … why … would he leave his cloak with him? Let him give him … and bring him to court … say: I do not want to stand in judgment … judges;
Rav Idi bar Avin raised an objection … one who slaughters a cow and divides it … on Rosh HaShana … if … was a full … month, … cancels … And if … not … does not cancel
If … cannot be claimed … what is … cancels? … It is different there, … for it has become clear that … was a regular weekday.

Come … hear … from … the latter clause … If … not … does not cancel … Granted, if you say … can be claimed, that which was taught that it does not cancel … But if you say … it cannot be claimed, why … it does not cancel … if … gives him … he may take it.

by inference that, in the first clause … if … gives him … he may not take it? … first clause … must say to him: I relinquish … the latter clause … he does not need to say to him: I relinquish … as we learned … one repays a debt during the Sabbatical Year, … should say to him: I relinquish
And if … says to him: Nonetheless, … he may accept it due to that which is stated: “And this is the manner of the release [devar hashemitta],
Rav Avya would take collateral … Rabba bar Ulla would circumvent

And similarly, on the eve of Passover … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: A person may consecrate his Paschal lamb on Shabbat and his Festival … offering on the Festival. … Shall we say … supports him? … And similarly, … the eve of Passover in Jerusalem which occurred on Shabbat, one may leave one’s cloak with him and take his Paschal lamb and make … calculation with him after the Festival.
with what are we dealing here? With a … in which one registers others … with him in … his Paschal lamb. … that was … consecrated from the outset.
But we learned … One may not initially register for an animal on the Festival. … here is different. Since … regularly … with him, … is like … one who registered for it from the outset.

But Rabbi Hoshaya taught: One … may go to a shepherd to whom he normally goes, and … may give him a lamb … for his Paschal lamb, and he may consecrate it and fulfill his obligation with it. … There, too, … Since he normally goes to him … consecrated it beforehand, … But it taught that one may consecrate it, … consecration by valuation. … rabbinic,

Did Rabbi Yoḥanan … say this? But Rabbi Yoḥanan stated … halakha … in accordance with an unattributed mishna, … And we learned … One may not consecrate, or take a valuation vow, or consecrate … or separate terumot … tithes; they said … a Festival, … an a fortiori inference … on Shabbat … not difficult. Here, … to obligations that have a set time, … There, … obligations that do not have a set time,

MISHNA: One may count his guests … and his appetizers, … from memory; but … not … from a written … A person may draw lots with his children and family members at the table … as long as he does not intend to set a large portion against a small portion … And one may cast lots … for sanctified foods on a Festival, but not for the … portions.
GEMARA: … What is the reason … Rav Beivai said: … a decree lest one erase … Abaye said: … a decree lest one read regular … documents.

What is … between them? … There is … between them … writing is on a wall and … raised … According to the one who says … lest one erase … we are not concerned … But according to the one who says … lest one read … we are … concerned

And according to the one who says … lest one erase, we should … be concerned lest one read … And furthermore, are we … not concerned lest one erase … But wasn’t it taught … one may not read by the light of a lamp … and Rabba said: Even … two statures … high, and even … two plow handles, and even … ten houses one atop the other, one may not read

Rather, there is … between them … writing … on a wall and it is low down. According to the one who says … lest one erase, … we are concerned … according to the one who says … lest one read … we are not concerned … a wall will not be confused with a document,

And according to the one who says … lest one read, we should … be concerned lest one erase. Rather, there is … between them … engraved on a tablet or on a board. According to the one who says … lest one erase, … we are not concerned. … According to the one who says … lest one read … we are concerned.

According to the one who says … lest one erase, we should … be concerned lest one read … And if you say: A tablet or a board will not be confused with a document, but wasn’t it taught … One may count how many … inside, and how many … outside, and how many portions he will place before them from writing that is on the wall, but not from writing that is on a tablet or a board?

What are the circumstances … If you say that it was written … what is the difference here, … and what is the difference here, … Rather, is it not … that has been engraved, and … it teaches … from writing that is on the wall but not from writing that is on a tablet or a board?

Rather, … actually … that the writing was on a wall and was raised. And … what was difficult for you, … Rabba’s … Rabba … tanna’im, as it was taught … One may count one’s guests and one’s appetizers from memory, but not from a written … Rabbi Aḥa permits … from a written … that is on a wall.

What are the circumstances … If you say that it is written below, … we should be concerned … perhaps one will erase … Rather, is it not … in which it is written and … is raised … and conclude from this that … of Rabba is … tanna’im? … conclude from this
these tanna’im are like those tanna’im, … as it was taught … One may not look in a mirror on Shabbat … Rabbi Meir permits … in a mirror that is fixed on a wall.
What is different … fixed on a wall? … that, in the meantime, … one will remember … that is not fixed … also … in the meantime one will remember.

here we are dealing with a metal mirror, and … as Rav Naḥman … Rabba bar Avuh said, for Rav Naḥman said … Rabba bar Avuh said: For what … did … say … a metal mirror is prohibited … Because a person may remove hanging hairs with it,

The Sages taught … writing that is under a picture or under graven images [deyokenaot], it is prohibited to read it on Shabbat … And … image itself, even on a weekday it is prohibited to look at it, because it says: “Do not turn toward idols [al tifnu el ha’elilim] … What is the … derivation? … Rabbi Ḥanin said: Do not push God [al tefannu El] out of your mind

a person may draw lots with one’s children … With one’s children and family members, yes, … but with another … not. What is the reason … as Rav Yehuda … Shmuel said, … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: Members of a group … who are particular with each other … are in violation of … measuring, and weighing, and counting … and … of … lending and repaying on a Festival.
And according to Beit Hillel, … even … interest.

If … so, … one’s children and family members also. … one’s children and family members, this is the reason … It is like … Rav Yehuda … Rav said, for Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: It is permitted to loan to one’s children and family members with interest, in order to let them experience a taste of … interest.
If … so, … a big portion against a small portion also.

Yes, it is indeed so, and … is incomplete and it teaches the following: A person may draw lots with his children and his family members at the table, … even … a large portion against a small portion. What is the reason … in accordance with … Rav Yehuda … Rav said. … with one’s children and family members, yes, … with others it is not. What is the reason … in accordance with … Rav Yehuda … Shmuel said: … a large portion against a small portion is prohibited … for other people, even on a weekday. What is the reason? Due to … dice,

one may draw lots for … What … But not for the … portions? Rabbi Ya’akov, son of the daughter of Ya’akov, said … But … not … for the weekday [ḥol] portions on a Festival. … obvious. … Lest you say … since … is written: … for your people are like those that strive with the priest” … even … weekday portions … also … teaches us

And Rabbi Ya’akov, son of the daughter of Ya’akov, said: Anyone … another to be punished on his account, … do not bring him within the partition of the Holy One, Blessed be He, … From where do we … If you say … because … It is written: “And the Lord said: Who will entice Ahab to go up and fall at Ramot Gilad? And one said: In this manner, and another said: In that manner. And the spirit came out and stood before the Lord and said: I will entice him. … And it said: I will go out and will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all of his prophets. And He said: You shall entice him and will prevail. Go out and do this”

And we said: What … spirit? Rabbi Yoḥanan said: This is the spirit of Naboth … And what is … Go out, … Rav said: … Leave from … My partition. … But perhaps there, the reason is as it is written: “One who speaks lies shall not dwell

Rather, … from here: “You are filled with shame instead of honor. Drink, you, and be like one who is uncircumcised, … “You are filled with shame instead of honor”; this … Nebuchadnezzar. “Drink, you, and be like one who is uncircumcised”; this is … Zedekiah, … One … that the entire verse is written about Nebuchadnezzar. And furthermore, … Zedekiah, the righteous one, what could he have done to him? … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said … When that wicked man wanted to do this to that righteous man,

Rather, … from here: “Punishment is also not good for the righteous” … There is no … not good other than evil. And it says: “For You are not a God that desires wickedness, evil will not dwell with You” … You, God, are righteous and evil shall not dwell … in Your place of dwelling.

From where … inferred that this … ḥalashim, is a word for lots? As it is written: “How have you fallen from heaven, O day-star, son of the morning! How have you been cut down to the ground, casting lots [ḥolesh] over the nations!” … Rabba bar Rav Huna said: … teaches … that he, … would cast lots [ḥolesh] for the royal leaders … in order to know whose day … homosexual relations. And it is written: “All the kings of the nations, all of them … And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … that they rested from homosexual relations.

And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: All of the days … of that wicked man, laughter could not be found in the mouth of any creature, as it is stated: “The whole earth is at rest and is quiet; they break forth into singing” … by inference … until now there was not any song.
And Rabbi Yitzḥak said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It is prohibited … to stand in … the house of that wicked man, … it is stated … “And demons shall dance there”

And Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: At the time … that wicked man, … wanted to do to that righteous man, … this … his foreskin was stretched three hundred cubits, and it surrounded the entire … feast, as it is stated: … You are filled with shame instead of honor. Drink, you, and be … one who is uncircumcised [vehe’arel]” … arel, … has a numerical value of three hundred.

And Rav Yehuda … said … Rav said: When that wicked man descended into Gehenna, everyone who had … descended to Gehenna trembled, … they said, … Perhaps he is coming to rule over them; or is he coming to be weakened like them? As it is stated: … Have you also become weak like us? Have you become like us [eleinu nimshalta]?” … A Divine Voice emerged and said: “Whom do you pass in beauty? Go down and be laid with the uncircumcised”
How has the oppressor ceased. The exactor of gold has ceased” … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: … this nation that said:
Measure and bring … has ceased. And some say … said: Bring very, very much, without measure.

“And surpassing greatness was added unto me” … Rav Yehuda said … Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said: This teaches that … rode atop a male lion and tied a serpent to its head, fulfilling what was said … “And the beasts of the field I have also given him to serve him”

MISHNA: A person may not hire workers on Shabbat … a person may not tell another … to hire workers for him. One may not … wait for nightfall at … the Shabbat boundary … to hire workers for himself or to bring produce … But he may wait for nightfall … to guard … and … bring produce … in his hand, … Abba Shaul stated a … principle: … anything that I am permitted to discuss … I am permitted to wait for nightfall … for its sake.
GEMARA: … obvious. What is the difference between him and another? … Rav Pappa said: Another … a gentile. Rav Ashi strongly objects to this: … telling a gentile … rabbinic prohibition.

Rather, Rav Ashi said: Even if you say … another Jew, … This is what it is teaching us: One may not say to another … Hire workers for me, but one may say to another: Does it seem that you will join me this evening? … And … whose … the mishna? … in accordance with … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa; as it was taught … A person may not say to another … Does it seem that you will join me this evening? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa says: A person may say to another … Does it seem that you will join me this evening?

Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa. And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: What is the reason for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa’s … As it is written … nor pursuing your business, nor speaking of it” … speaking is prohibited, … contemplating … is permitted.

Rav Aḥa bar Rav Huna raised a contradiction to Rava: Did Rabbi Yoḥanan … state … speaking is prohibited, … contemplating is permitted? Consequently, … contemplation is not tantamount to speech. But Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It is permitted to think … in any place except for a bathhouse and a bathroom. … It is different there, for … we need … therefore, your camp shall be sacred … and … not
here, too, … it is written: “So that He see no unseemly thing [davar] in you” … That … It is needed for … Rav Yehuda, for Rav Yehuda said: Opposite a naked gentile, it is prohibited to recite Shema,

Why did … teach … particularly … a gentile? Even … Jew, … also … is stated … There is no need. … There is no need … a Jew, … prohibited … However, … a gentile, since it is written about him: “Whose flesh is as the flesh of donkeys” … say that it seems well … teaches us
say … it is indeed so, … The verse … said … and they did not see their father’s nakedness”

And is it speaking … prohibited … But Rav Ḥisda and Rav Hamnuna both said: It is permitted to make calculations pertaining to a mitzva on Shabbat, and Rabbi Elazar said … one may apportion charity for the poor on Shabbat. And Rabbi Ya’akov bar Idi said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One may attend to … saving a life or for communal needs on Shabbat, and one may go to a synagogue to attend to communal affairs on Shabbat.

And Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One may go to theaters [tarteiot], and circus performances [kirkesaot], and courthouses [basilkaot] to attend to communal affairs on Shabbat. And … the school of Menashe taught: One may … pair off children … be betrothed on Shabbat, and … for a child … to teach him … books and to teach him a craft. … the verse said: “Nor pursuing your business, nor speaking of it” … your business … are prohibited … the business of Heaven, … is permitted

Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: … calculations of: What is it to you, [mallakh], … and of: What … does it have [ma bekhakh], … permitted to make them on Shabbat. … was also taught … Calculations … that have passed … that will be in the future may not be calculated … What is it to you,
and of: What … does it have, … permitted to calculate them.

raises a contradiction … One may make calculations that are unnecessary, but one may not make calculations that are necessary on Shabbat. How … One may say to another: I sent out such and such … workers to this field, and I spent such and such … dinar for this home. But he may not say to him: I spent such and such … and I am going to spend such and such … in the future.
And according to your reasoning, it itself, … is difficult for you, … Rather, … This … he has payment with him … this … in which he does not have payment with him

one may not wait for nightfall … The Sages taught: There was an incident with a pious man … a breach was made in … his field, and … he decided to fence it in. And … he remembered that it was Shabbat. And that pious man refrained from fixing the fence … And a miracle was done for him, and a caper bush grew in … And from it … received his livelihood and the livelihood of the members of his household.
Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: A person is permitted to say to another … I am going to such and such city tomorrow, for if there were small guardhouses [burganin] one … walk.

We learned … One may not wait for nightfall at … the Shabbat boundary … to hire workers or bring produce … Granted, … in order to hire workers, … one may not hire … But … to bring produce, … Let us say that … if there were partitions there, one may … bring … You find … produce … that is … attached

But Rabbi Oshaya taught: One may not wait for nightfall at the … the Shabbat boundary in order to bring in hay and straw … Granted, … straw; you find … attached … But hay, … how do you find … to rotten straw,
Come … hear … One may wait for nightfall at the … to attend to the needs of a bride or the needs of a corpse. … for the needs of a bride or a corpse, yes, … for the needs of another person, no,

Granted, … another … similar to attending to … a bride, you find … to cut him a myrtle … But … a corpse, what is it … To bring for it a coffin and shrouds. And it teaches … a corpse, yes, … but … another … not.
And why … Let us say that … if there were partitions there, one may … bring … a corpse, you also find … to cut a garment for

But one may wait for nightfall … And … even if he has not … the blessing of distinction [havdala] … But didn’t Rabbi Elazar ben Antigonos say in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov … it is prohibited for a person to tend to his … affairs … before he recites havdala? And if you say … in which one … recited havdala during prayer, … didn’t Rav Yehuda say … Shmuel said … one who recites havdala in prayer must … recite havdala over a cup … And if you say … in which one … recited havdala over a cup … does one have a cup … in the field? Rabbi Natan bar Ami explained … before Rava: They taught … among wine presses,

Rabbi Abba said … to Rav Ashi: In the West, … we say this … The One who distinguishes between the sacred and the mundane, and … we attend to our needs, … Rav Ashi said: When I was in the house of Rav Kahana, he would say: The One who distinguishes between the sacred and the mundane, … we would cut wood

Abba Shaul stated a … principle: … anything that I am … dilemma: To which … Abba Shaul’s … refer? If you say … relates to the first clause … One may not wait for nightfall at the … to hire workers or to bring produce,

this … Anything that I am permitted to discuss … I am permitted to wait for nightfall for its sake, … should have … anything that I am not permitted to discuss … I am not permitted to wait for nightfall for its sake, … Rather, it is referring to the latter clause … But he may wait for nightfall … to guard … and he may bring produce in his hand. … It should have … Anything for which I am permitted to wait for nightfall I am permitted to discuss.

Actually, it is referring to the latter clause … and Abba Shaul relates to this … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: It is permitted for a person to say to another … Guard … produce that is in your boundary for me, and I will guard … produce in my boundary for you. And … Abba Shaul said to the first tanna: Do you not agree … it is permitted for a person to say to another: Guard … produce that is in your boundary for me, and I will guard … produce that is in my boundary for you?

And say … anything that I am permitted to discuss, I am permitted to wait for nightfall for its sake. … principle, what … to include? … to include that which the Sages taught … One may not wait for nightfall at the Shabbat boundary … to bring an animal … is standing … outside of the boundary, one may call it … come … Abba Shaul said a … principle: … anything that I am permitted to discuss … I am permitted to wait for nightfall for its sake.

And … one may wait for nightfall to attend to the needs of a bride and the needs of a corpse, … to bring it a coffin and shrouds. And one may say to him, … Go to such and such place … and if you do not find them in that place, bring … from such and such a place. … If you do not find … for one hundred … buy them for two hundred. … Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says: … provided one does not mention to him … amount … the transaction.

MISHNA: One may wait for nightfall at the Shabbat boundary to attend to the needs of a bride and the needs of a corpse, … to bring him a coffin and shrouds. … a gentile brought flutes on Shabbat … a Jew may not eulogize with them … unless they were brought from a nearby location … made someone a coffin and dug him a grave … a Jew may be buried in it. However, if it was … for a Jew, … may never be buried in it.
GEMARA: … What … from a nearby location? Rav said: … from a location that is actually nearby, … And Shmuel said: … we are concerned that it may have stayed overnight … outside the … wall,

The language of the mishna is precise according to Shmuel’s … as it teaches: … made someone a coffin and dug him a grave … a Jew may be buried in it. Consequently, … it is uncertain … it is permitted. Here, too, … it is uncertain … it is permitted.

And … was taught in accordance with … Rav: … a city in which … Jews and gentiles live and in which there is a bathhouse that functions on Shabbat, if there is a majority of gentiles … in the evening, … may bathe in it immediately. If there is a majority of Jews … must wait until … to heat up water … half … and half … it is prohibited … and … must wait until … to heat up water … Rabbi Yehuda says: In … a small bath, if there is a ruling power … may bathe in it immediately

What is … A ruling power? Rav Yehuda said … Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rav Yehuda, said: … if there is an important person in … who has ten slaves who heat ten water jugs [kumkumin] for him at once in a small bath, it is permitted … to bathe in it immediately

made someone a coffin and dug him a grave … Why? Here, too, one should … wait … for them to do … Ulla said: … in which … is located in … street. … Granted, … grave, … coffin, what is there to say? … Rabbi Abbahu said: … in which … placed over the grave

MISHNA: One may perform all of the needs of the dead … One may smear oil … and rinse it … and … provided that one does not move any of its limbs, … one may … remove a pillow from beneath it and … place it on … sand in order

to delay … one may tie the jaw … not … that it will rise … but … that it will not continue … And similarly, … a … beam that has broken … one may support it with a bench or with long … a bed. … not … that the beam will rise … but … that it will not continue

GEMARA: … But didn’t Rav Yehuda say … Shmuel said: There was an incident with a student of Rabbi Meir who followed him into the bathhouse … wanted to rinse the ground. … said to him: One may not rinse … smear the ground … said to him: One may not smear … The ground … can be confused with the ground … a corpse cannot be confused with the ground,

What does … all include … to include that which the Sages taught: One may bring cold vessels and metal vessels and place them on … stomach so that it does not swell. And one may seal up its orifices so that air will not enter them

And … Solomon also said in his wisdom … “Before the silver cord is snapped asunder”; this is … the spinal cord. “And the golden bowl [gullat] is shattered”; this is … the member, … “And the pitcher is broken at the fountain”; this is … the stomach, … “And the wheel [galgal] falls, shattered, into the pit”; this is … excrement

And similarly, it says … “And I will spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your Festival offerings” … Rav Huna said, and some say … Rav Ḥagga … said: … those people who neglect the words of the Torah and turn all of their days into Festivals. Rabbi Levi said … Rav Pappi said … Rabbi Yehoshua said: Three days after … the stomach … bursts and falls onto his face and says to him: Take what you have put inside me.
MISHNA: One may not shut … of the dead on Shabbat … And one may not … on a weekday while the soul departs. … And one who shuts … while the soul departs is a murderer

GEMARA: The Sages taught: One who shuts … while the soul departs is a murderer. … analogous to a lamp that is gradually becoming extinguished … a person places his finger on it, it is immediately extinguished. It was taught … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: One who wants the eyes of a corpse to close should blow wine up its nose, and place oil between its eyelids, and grab hold of its two big toes, and … will shut by themselves.

was taught … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: … a living day-old baby, one desecrates Shabbat … deceased David, king of Israel, one does not desecrate Shabbat. … a day-old baby we desecrate Shabbat … the Torah says: Desecrate one Shabbat for him so that he can observe many Shabbatot. … deceased David, king of Israel, one does not desecrate … once a person dies he is idle from mitzvot. And this is what Rabbi Yoḥanan said … “Set apart among the dead [bametim ḥofshi], … Once a person dies, he becomes free [ḥofshi] from the mitzvot.

And it was … taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said: It is not necessary to protect a live day-old baby from a weasel or from mice, … But … Og, the king of Bashan, … dead, it is necessary to protect … him from a weasel or from mice, as it is stated: “And the fear of you and the dread of you [ḥittekhem] shall be … As long as a person is alive [ḥai], he is feared by the animals. Once he dies, he is no longer feared.

Rav Pappa said: We hold … a lion does not pounce upon two … But … We see that it does pounce … That … in accordance with … Rami bar Abba said: An animal does not overpower a person until he appears to it as an animal, as it is stated: “But man does not abide in honor, he is like the beasts that perish” … Rabbi Ḥanina said: It is prohibited to sleep alone in a house, and anyone who sleeps alone in a house will be seized by … Lilith.

It was … taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Perform … while you … find … and you have … and you are still under your … control. And … Solomon also said, in his wisdom: “And remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come … these are the days of old age. “And the years arrive when you will say: I have no desire for them”; these are the days of Messiah, in which there is neither merit nor liability.

disagrees with … Shmuel, for Shmuel said: There is no … between this world and the days of Messiah except for subjugation … kingdoms alone, … as it is stated: “For the poor will never cease from the land,

It was taught … Rabbi Elazar HaKappar says: A person should always request … mercy with regard to this condition … for if he does not come … his son will, and if his son does not come … his grandson will, as it is stated: … for due to this thing [biglal hadavar hazeh] … tanna from the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: … it is a wheel [galgal] that turns in the world, … Rav Yosef said: We hold … a Torah scholar will not become poor. … But we see that they do become poor. … if there is … who becomes poor, he will … never … go around … at … doors.

Rabbi Ḥiyya said to his wife: When a poor person comes … be quick to give him bread so that they will be quick … to your children. She said to him: … you cursing them, … He said to her: It is a verse that is written, … “Due to this thing,” and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught … it is a wheel that … turns in the world. … it was taught … Rabbi Gamliel, son of Rabbi … says: … “And He will show you mercy and have compassion on you and multiply you” … anyone who has compassion for … creatures will receive compassion from Heaven, and anyone who does not have compassion for … creatures will not receive compassion from Heaven.

“Before the sun and the light … are darkened, … this … the forehead and the nose … “And the moon”; this … the soul, … “And the stars”; these are the cheeks. “And the clouds return after the rain”; this is the light of a person’s eyes, which goes … after one cries … Shmuel said: … the tear … until … forty years, one’s vision returns … From here on, … it does not return,

And … Rav Naḥman said: … eye shadow, until … forty years, it enhances … From here and on, even if one fills it … as a weaver’s pin [avisana degirda’ei], it will maintain … it will not enhance … What is he teaching us … the more eye shadow … the more beneficial

Rabbi Ḥanina’s daughter died, he did not cry over her. His wife said to him: Have you … let a chicken out of your house, … He said to her: … twice, … bereavement and … blindness. … He held in accordance with the … Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Ketzarta: There are six … tears, three … are good … and three … are bad. … from smoke, and from crying
and from … the bathroom are bad … from … drugs, and from laughter, and from … produce are good

“On the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, … shall bow themselves, … “On the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble”; this … the flanks and ribs … “And the strong men shall bow themselves”; these are the thighs, … “And the grinders cease”; these are the teeth, … “And those that look out the windows shall be dimmed”; these are the eyes,

emperor said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya: What is the reason you did not come to the House of Avidan? … said to him … The snowy mountain is surrounded with ice, … his dogs do not bark, … his grinders have ceased grinding, … the school of Rav they say … I am searching for that which I have not lost,

It was taught … Rabbi Yosei bar Kisma says: … two … are better than the three … Woe to the one who goes and does not come … What is this … Rav Ḥisda said: Youth. … when Rav Dimi came … he said: Youth is a crown of roses; old age is a crown of thorns. … taught in the name of Rabbi Meir: Grind … with your teeth and … find in your feet … as it is stated: “For we were sated with our bread and were well, and saw no evil” … Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda: Large-toothed one; untie your sack, … and insert your food. Until … forty years, food is beneficial; from here and on, drinking is beneficial.

A certain eunuch … said … to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa … How … it from here to Karḥina? … He said to him: It is the same as … from here to … Gozen, … said to him: A bald buck … for four … He said to him: A castrated goat [ikkara shelifa] … for eight.

saw that … was not wearing shoes. … said to him: … on a horse … king. … on a donkey … a free man. And one who wears shoes is … a human being. … neither this nor that, … who is buried … is better than him. He said to him: Eunuch, eunuch, you said to me three things, … hear three … The glory of a face is the beard, the joy of the heart is a wife, … “the portion of the Lord is children” … blessed is the Omnipresent who has denied you all of them, … He said to him: … a bald man quarrel? He said to him: … a castrated male goat … rebuke?

Rabbi … said to Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥalafta: For what … did we not greet you during the Festival the way that my fathers greeted your fathers? … said to him: … the rocks … have become tall, … near have become far away, … two … have been made into three … that which brings peace to the house, … is no more.

“And the doors shall be shut in the marketplace”; these are a person’s orifices, … “When the sound of the grinding is low”; because the stomach is not grinding … “And one shall start up at the voice of a bird”; … that even a bird will wake him from his sleep. “And all the daughters of music shall be brought low”; … that even the voices of male and female singers will seem to him like … conversation,

And even Barzilai the Gileadite said to David: “Today I am eighty years old, can I discern between good and bad? … from here … that the minds of the elderly change … “Can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink”; from here … that the lips of the elderly crack and wither. “Can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women”; from here … that the ears of the elderly become heavy.

Rav said: Barzilai the Gileadite was a liar … For there was a particular maidservant in the house of Rabbi … who was ninety-two years old, and she would taste … in the pots. Rava said: … Barzilai the Gileadite was steeped in promiscuity, and anyone who is steeped in promiscuity is overtaken by old age … It was taught … Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, says: As Torah scholars grow older, wisdom is increased in them, as it is stated: “With aged men is wisdom; and length of days brings understanding” … And as ignoramuses grow older, foolishness is increased in them, as it is stated: “He removes the speech of men of trust and takes away the understanding of the aged”

“Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high”; … that even a small knoll … seems to him, … like the highest of mountains. “And terrors shall be on the road”; … that while he is walking on the road he will have terrors, … “And the almond tree shall blossom”; this is the hip bone … “And the grasshopper [ḥagav] shall drag itself along [yistabbel]”; … this … buttocks [agavot] … “And the caper berry shall fail”; this is … desire

Rav Kahana was reading … verses before Rav. When he got to this verse, … sighed. … said: … derive from this that Rav’s desire has ceased. Rav Kahana … said: What is … that which is written: … “For He spoke and it was”; this is a woman … “He commanded and it stood”; these are the children … taught … A woman is … a flask full of feces, … and her mouth is full of blood, … and they all run after her

“For a person goes to his eternal home” … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: This teaches that each and every righteous person is given a dwelling place … in accordance with his honor. … a parable … a king enters a city along with his servants. When they enter, they all enter through a single gate; … when they sleep, each one is given a dwelling place in accordance with his honor.
And Rabbi Yitzḥak said: What is … that which is written: “For childhood and youth [shaḥarut] are vanity” … things that a person does in his youth darken [mashḥirim] his face … as he grows old

And Rabbi Yitzḥak said: The maggots … are as painful to the dead as a needle in the flesh of the living, as it says … “But his flesh is in pain for him, … Rav Ḥisda said: A person’s soul mourns for him … all seven days … as it is stated: And his soul mourns over him,” and it is … written: “And he mourned his father seven days”
Rav Yehuda said: … a deceased person who has no comforters, … ten people should go and sit in his place … a certain person who died in Rav Yehuda’s neighborhood … who did not have … comforters,
every day … Rav Yehuda would take ten … and … sit in his place, … After seven days … appeared … Rav Yehuda in his dream and said to him: Put your mind to rest, for you have put my mind to rest.

Rabbi Abbahu said: Everything people say before the deceased, he knows, until … is sealed … the top-stone. Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi … disagreed with regard to … this … One … said … until … is sealed … the top-stone, … And one … said … until the flesh decomposes.

The one who said … until the flesh decomposes … which is written … “But his flesh grieves for him, and his soul mourns over him” … The one … said … until … is sealed … the top-stone … which is written … “And the dust returns to the earth as it was,

The Sages taught … “And the spirit returns to God who gave it” … give it to Him as He gave it to you; … in purity, you too … in purity. … a parable of a king of flesh and blood who distributed royal garments to his servants. The wise ones folded them and placed them in a box [kufsa] … the foolish ones went and worked in them. … a period of time the king requested … his garments … wise ones returned them to him pressed, … the foolish ones returned them dirty. The king was happy to greet the wise ones and angry to greet the foolish ones.

With regard to the wise ones he said: My garments shall be given … to the storehouse, and let them go to their homes in peace. And with regard to the foolish ones he said: My garments shall be given to the launderer, and they, … will be locked up in prison

The Holy One, Blessed be He, also … With regard to the bodies of the righteous, … it states: “He enters into peace, they rest on their beds … And with regard to their souls, it states: “And the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life … with regard to the bodies of the wicked, it states: “There is no peace, says the Lord, for the wicked” … and with regard to their souls, it states: “And the souls of your enemies He shall sling out in the hollow of a sling”

It was taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: The souls of the righteous are stored beneath the Throne of Glory, as it is stated: “And the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life” … And … of the wicked are continuously tied up, and one angel stands at … end of the world and another angel stands at … end of the world and they sling the souls … to one another, as it is stated: “And the souls of your enemies He shall sling out in the hollow of a sling”

Rabba said to Rav Naḥman: What … of middling people, … said to him: … if I were dead I would not … to tell you … Shmuel said as follows: These and those, … are handed over to Duma, … these, … have rest, and these, … do not have rest. Rav Mari said: … the righteous will … become dust, as it is written: “And the dust returns to the earth as it was”

The diggers who were digging in Rav Naḥman’s land … Rav Aḥai bar Yoshiya, … rebuked them. They came and said to Rav Naḥman: A … person … rebuked us. … came and said to … Who is the Master, … said to him: I am Aḥai bar Yoshiya. … said to him: … Didn’t Rav Mari say … the righteous will turn to dust? … said to him: And who is Mari, whom I do not know? … said to him: … there is an … verse which is written: “And the dust will return to the earth as it was”

said to him: Whoever taught you … Ecclesiastes did not teach you … Proverbs, for it is written … but envy is the rotting of the bones” … anyone who has envy in his heart … his bones rot … anyone who does not have envy in his heart, his bones do not rot.

touched him … saw that he had substance. … said to him: Let the Master arise … into my house. … said to him: You have revealed … you have not even studied Prophets, … for it is written: “And you shall know that I am the Lord when I open up your graves

We learned there … Rabbi Eliezer says: Repent one day before your death. Rabbi Eliezer’s students asked him: But does a person know the day … he will die? Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said … a parable … to a king who invited his servants to a feast and did not set a time for them … The wise among them adorned themselves and sat at the entrance to the king’s house. a donkey, a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor, … one places it on the donkey, … one neither gives it to the deaf-mute, nor the imbecile, nor the minor. there is neither a gentile nor a donkey nor a deaf-mute nor an imbecile nor a minor there, what … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: There was another manner … and the Sages did not want to reveal it. … what … There was another manner? … move … each less than four cubits, … Why didn’t the Sages want to reveal this … due to … “It is the glory of God to conceal a thing; but the glory of kings is to search out a matter” … And here, what glory of God is there … lest … come to carry … four cubits in the public domain.
It was taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: On that day they … a large se’a … Rabbi Yehoshua said: On that very day they … a minimal se’a,

the Master said: … there is no gentile with him, one places … on the donkey. … Isn’t he … driving a … animal? And the Torah stated: … you shall not perform any manner of labor,

Rava said: … two … responses … statement … One … as it is written: “You shall have one law [Torah] for him that does unwittingly … But the soul that does with a high hand, … The entire Torah is juxtaposed to idolatry, … Just as … idolatry … when he performs an action with his body, … here too, … only if he performs an action with his body,

taught his halakha in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan to exempt … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who drives a … animal on Shabbat is exempt from any

unwittingly, he is not liable … sin-offering … all of … the Torah were juxtaposed to … idolatry, … intentionally, he is also not liable … as we learned … One who desecrates Shabbat by … a matter that for its unwitting … liable … a sin-offering, and for its intentional … liable to be executed by stoning. … a matter that for its unwitting … not liable … a sin-offering, for its intentional … not liable … stoning.

he is not … liable … for … prohibition … it is a prohibition that was … given, … as a warning of court-imposed capital punishment, and … any prohibition that was given as a warning of court-imposed capital punishment, … one is not flogged for its

he reached the outer courtyard, … and the bags … Rav Huna said: … one’s animal was laden with glass vessels, … he may bring cushions and blankets and place … beneath … and untie the ropes and … the bags fall

Abaye found Rabba sliding his son on the back of a donkey … He said to him: The Master is making use of living creatures … said to him: … they are sides, the Sages did not issue a decree … them. raised an objection to … two … by a person, and one … on a tree … valid … However, one may not enter it on the festival … What, … not … where one carved … in the tree … these are sides … sides … prohibited?

a stake in a tree and hung a … - … - … basket from it … above ten handbreadths … his eiruv is not a … eiruv. … below ten handbreadths … his eiruv is a … eiruv.

Rav Ashi said: Now that you said … sides is prohibited, … this ladder … elevated … a person may not lean it against the palm tree … because it is … sides … Rather, he should lean it on stakes … external … the palm tree. And when … climbs … he should not place his foot on the stakes. Rather, he should place it on the rungs

that it is taught in the first clause … Neither … small … nor … large … it can be inferred … Rabbi Yehuda … daka, he meant an actual small … difficult.
come … hear … One may chop

pumpkins before an animal and an … carcass before dogs. Is this not … pumpkins … similar to an … carcass? Just as an … carcass is soft, so too, … pumpkins … are soft. GEMARA: … What is … One may not forcibly overfeed? Rav Yehuda said: One may not … it creates a trough inside of its stomach. … Is there … in that manner? … Yes; and as Rav Yirmeya of Difti said: I saw … Arab who fed … a kor … and loaded it … kor

was taught in accordance with … Rav Yehuda: What is hamra’a and what is halata? Hamra’a … lays … and forces its mouth open and feeds it vetch and water simultaneously … Halata … one feeds … standing and gives it to drink … standing, … and one gives it vetch separately and water separately,

It is … Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda. And this … applies only … where one alters … How does one alter … Rav Ḥisda said: … a little bit at a time.

Rabbi Ḥanina said to … Go … tell the son of Leiva’i, … It is not the constellation of the day … that determines … rather, … the constellation of the hour … determines … One who was … under … the sun will be a radiant person; he will eat from his own … and drink from his own … and his secrets will be exposed.  One who was … under … Jupiter [tzedek] will be a just … [tzadkan]. Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: And just … in … mitzvot.

raises an objection … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: … an ukla, … of spices, a liter of vegetables, ten nuts, five peaches, two pomegranates, … one citron, … And Gursak bar Darei said in the name of Rav Menashya bar Sheguvlei, … in the name of Rav: And similarly, … with regard to an eiruv. … These … should also be like peaches,
These … are important, … but these … are not important,

Rav Yosef said: May his Master, … forgive Rav Menashya bar Sheguvlei, … I stated before him … concerning a mishna, and he stated it concerning the baraita, … As we learned … One may not give a pauper … at the threshing floor less than half a kav of wheat or … a kav of barley. What is the strength of this over that? … If you say … because … spices was … taught in this … and spices are not fit for eating … wasn’t … wheat and barley taught here … and they … are not … fit for eating

Rather, it is because it was taught … half a log of wine. And Rav said: One may establish an eiruv with two-quarters … of wine, … Since we require so much … learn from here … when Rav said: And similarly, … with regard to an eiruv, he said it about this mishna … conclude from this
The Master said: And … food … for two meals for … an eiruv. Rav Yosef thought to say … unless there is … meal of this … and … meal of that … Rabba said to him: … even … half, a third, or a quarter

itself, … Rav said: One may establish an eiruv with two-quarters … of wine. … Do we … need so much? Wasn’t it taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: … wine … enough to eat … with it, … vinegar … enough to dip … in it, … olives and onions … enough to eat them … two meals.
There, … to cooked wine,

The Master said … vinegar … is enough to dip … in it. Rav Giddel said that Rav said: Enough to dip in it the food of two meals … of vegetables. Some say … Rav Giddel said that Rav said: … vegetables that are eaten in two … meals,

The Master … said … olives and onions … to eat them … the food of two meals. … May one establish an eiruv with onions? not difficult. This … to … leaves, … that … to … bulbs, … As it was taught … ate an onion and died early … we need not ask from what he died, … And Shmuel said: They only taught … with regard to the leaves; but with regard to … bulbs, we have no … with it. has not grown … a span, … however, if it has grown … a span, we have no … with it.

Rabbi Zeira said that Shmuel said: One may establish an eiruv with beer, and it invalidates a ritual bath with … three log, … Rav Kahana strongly objects to this: … obvious, for what is the difference between this and dye-water? And how much … establish an eiruv? Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Yosef, thought to say before Rav Yosef … Two-quarters … of beer. … As we learned … one carries out wine … enough … for diluting a cup, … And … was taught about … Enough … for diluting a fine cup. … What … a fine cup? … A cup of blessing. And Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said: A cup of blessing must contain a quarter of a quarter- … so that … dilutes … it amounts to a … quarter- … And … in accordance with … Rava … as Rava said: Any wine that is not … diluted … three … water to one … is not … wine.
And we learned in the latter clause … And … all other liquids, and … all waste water, … a quarter- … Since there, … one to four, … here, too, … one to four
And this is not so. There, … less than that … is insignificant. However, here, … not … as it is common for people to drink a cup … in the morning and a cup … in the evening, and they rely on them
How many dates … Rav Yosef said: … dates … a kav. Rav Yosef said: From where do I say this … As it was taught … ate dried figs … and paid dates … may a blessing come upon him.

What are the circumstances … If you say … according to the value … he ate a zuz … and he paid a zuz … what is … May a blessing come upon him? He ate a zuz and paid a zuz. Abaye said to … he actually ate a zuz … and he paid a zuz … And what … May a blessing come upon him? For he ate something that buyers are not eager … and he paid him something that buyers are eager
shetita, … Rav Aḥa bar Pineḥas said: Two large spoonfuls … kisanei, … Abaye said: Two Pumbeditan bunei,
Abaye said: Mother, … told me: These roasted grains are good for the heart and drive away … thoughts.
