Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: … anything that serves as a relish … enough to eat … with it, … And … anything that is not a relish, … enough to eat … of it. … raw meat … enough to eat … of it. Roasted meat … Rabba said: Enough to eat … with it. … And Rav Yosef said: Enough to eat … of it,

Rav Yosef said: From where do I say this … For these Persians eat pieces of … meat [tabahakki] without bread, … Abaye said to him: But are the Persians a majority of the world? … Didn’t we learn … Clothing of the poor, … poor people … Clothing of the wealthy … the wealthy.
But the clothing of the wealthy … not … for the poor

And if you say: … here … stringent, … there … stringent, … Wasn’t it taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: One may establish an eiruv for an ill or elderly … with … food that is enough for him … however, for a glutton, … an average meal for the typical person? … difficult.
Did Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar … say this? Wasn’t it taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Og, king of the Bashan, … opening as … his full size?
And … Abaye … There, … what should we do? Should we cut … into pieces and carry it out?
A dilemma was raised before … Do the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, or not? Come … hear … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Og, king of the Bashan, … an opening of four
There, … where there are many small openings, and there is … one that is four … with certainty that when one widens … he will widen that

Rav Ḥiyya bar Rav Ashi said that Rav said: One may establish an eiruv with raw meat … Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya said: One may … establish an eiruv with raw eggs. … How many … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: One. Sinai, … said: Two.

One who vows that nourishment … is permitted … water … It is … salt and water … are not considered nourishment, but all … items are considered nourishment. Let us say … this is a refutation of … Rav and Shmuel. As it was Rav and Shmuel who both said: One only recites the blessing: Who creates … kinds of nourishment, over the five species … alone,
Did we not … refute … on one occasion … let us say … there is a refutation of their … from here as well.
Rav Huna said: … says: Anything that nourishes … to me. … it is water and salt … as they do not nourish, but all … items … do nourish.

Didn’t Rabba bar bar Ḥana say: When we were following Rabbi Yoḥanan to eat of the fruits of Genosar, … when we were … of a hundred … each and every … would take ten … when we were … of ten, each and every … would take a hundred … And each hundred of these … could not fit into a three-se’a basket. And … would eat them all and … say: I swear that I have not … tasted something that nourishes. … Say … sustaining food,
Rav Huna said … Rav said: … I swear that I shall not eat this loaf, one may … establish an eiruv for him with it … This loaf … to me, one may not establish an eiruv for him with it,
raises an objection … one who vows … from a loaf, one may … establish an eiruv for him with it. What, is it not … who said: … to me? … No, … where he said: … this
So too, it is reasonable … as it was taught in the latter clause: When … when one said: I swear that I shall not taste it.

But … he said: … to me, what … So too, one may not establish an eiruv for him with it. … if so, … Instead of teaching … This loaf is consecrated … one may not establish an eiruv for him with it, as one may not establish an eiruv with consecrated … let him make … distinction in the case … itself … In what … is this statement said? … one said: … this … But if one said: … to me, one may not establish an eiruv for him with it.
Rav Huna … said to you: Rather, what … wherever … said: … to me, one may establish an eiruv … a difficulty … first clause

is incomplete, and it teaches the following: … one who vows … from a loaf, one may … establish an eiruv for him with it. And even if one said: … to me, it is as though he said: I swear that I shall not taste it.

Nevertheless, … difficulty … according to … Rav Huna. … He stated … in accordance with … Rabbi Eliezer; as it was taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: … I swear that I shall not eat this loaf, one may establish an eiruv for him with it; … This loaf … to me, one may not establish an eiruv for him with it.

Did Rabbi Eliezer … say this? Wasn’t it taught … This is the principle: … a person … prohibits himself from … food, … one may establish an eiruv for him with … food was prohibited to a person, … one may not establish an eiruv for him with it. Rabbi Eliezer says: … This loaf … to me, one may establish an eiruv for him with it. … This loaf is consecrated … one may not establish an eiruv for him with it, as one may not establish an eiruv for him with consecrated
two tanna’im … according to Rabbi Eliezer.

One may establish an eiruv for a nazirite with wine … The mishna … not … in accordance with … Beit Shammai, as it was taught … Beit Shammai say: One may not establish an eiruv for a nazirite with wine and for an Israelite with teruma. Beit Hillel … say: One may establish an eiruv for a nazirite with wine and for an Israelite with teruma. Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai: Do you not concede
that one may establish an eiruv for an adult … on Yom Kippur,
said to them: Indeed [aval], … said to them: Just as one may establish an eiruv for an adult on Yom Kippur, so … one may establish an eiruv for a nazirite with wine and for an Israelite with teruma.
And … Beit Shammai … There, … there is … a meal that was fit … while it was still day, … Here, … there is no meal that was fit … while it was still day,

In accordance with whose … not … in accordance with … Ḥananya, as it was taught … Ḥananya says: The whole … of Beit Shammai, … they did not concede to … joining … until … he carries out his bed and his utensils to there,

In accordance with whose … is … that was taught … one established an eiruv in black … he may not go out in white … in white, he may not go out in black. According to whose … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: It is … Ḥananya, and … in accordance with … Beit Shammai.

And according to … Ḥananya, … with black … he may not go out, but in white … he may go out? Didn’t … say … until one carries out his bed and his utensils … this is what it said: … one established an eiruv … in white … and he needed black … he may not go out even in white … In accordance with whose … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: It is … Ḥananya, and … in accordance with … Beit Shammai.
Summakhos … says: … with … non-sacred … But … a nazirite with wine, … does not … disagree. What is the reason … can ask … his nazirite status,
If so, … teruma as well, one can ask … its … If one asks … will return to … tevel,
Let him separate … for … from … somewhere else … Ḥaverim, … are not suspected of separating … not … near
Let him separate … from … itself … where, … it would not contain the amount
What … necessary … Rather, … Summakhos agrees with … the Rabbis, who say: Anything that is … due to a rabbinic decree [shevut], … issued the decree … during twilight.

In accordance with whose … is … that we learned … There are … they stated … are all in accordance with the … person … the handful of … a meal-offering, and the handfuls of incense … and one who drinks a cheekful on Yom Kippur, and with regard to the … two meals’ … nourishment for an eiruv. … In accordance with whose … Rabbi Zeira said: It is … Summakhos, who said: We require that which is fit for him,

Let us say … disagrees with … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar. As it was taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: One may establish an eiruv for an ill or elderly … with … food that is enough for him … But for a glutton … an average meal for the typical person.
interpret … an ill or elderly … But … a glutton, … his opinion is rendered irrelevant by the opinions of all other people.

for a priest in a beit haperas, … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: … a person may blow … beit haperas … and … walk … Rabbi Yehuda bar Ami said in the name of Rav Yehuda: A beit haperas that has been trodden … is pure,
Rabbi Yehuda says: … even … a cemetery, … It was taught: … because … can interpose and walk … a carriage, a crate, or a cupboard. … he holds … A moving tent is called a tent,

a dispute between the following tanna’im, as it was taught … one who enters the land of the nations, … in a carriage, a crate, or a cupboard, Rabbi … renders … impure. Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, renders … pure.
With regard to what do they disagree? One Sage, … holds … a moving tent is not called a tent. … And … Sage, … holds … a moving tent is called a tent,
And … that which was taught … Rabbi Yehuda says:
One may establish an eiruv for a priest who is … pure with teruma that is … pure … on a grave, … How does he go … In a carriage, crate, or cupboard,
Isn’t … once … was placed … became defiled, … where … had not yet been rendered susceptible … Or … that was kneaded with fruit juice,
How can he bring it … With flat wooden utensils … do not contract … impurity.
Doesn’t … cover … He may bring it on the edge
If … so, … what is the reason … They hold … it is prohibited to acquire a home with items from which benefit is prohibited.
by inference that Rabbi Yehuda holds … it is permitted … holds … mitzvot were not given for benefit.

But … that which Rava said: Mitzvot were not given for benefit, let us say … he stated his halakha … in accordance with … tanna’im. … Rava … said to you: If they hold that one may establish an eiruv only for the sake of a mitzva, all would agree … mitzvot were not given for benefit. … Here, they disagree with regard to this: One Sage, … holds: One may establish an eiruv only for the sake of a mitzva. … And one Sage, … holds: One may establish an eiruv even for a voluntary matter.
But … that which Rav Yosef said … One may establish an eiruv only for the sake of a mitzva, let us say … he stated his halakha in accordance with … tanna’im.

Rav Yosef … said to you: … all agree … one may establish an eiruv only for the sake of a mitzva, and all agree … mitzvot were not given for benefit, and they disagree with regard to this: One Sage, … holds: Once … acquired his … eiruv, he is indifferent to its safeguarding, … And one Sage, … holds: It is pleasing to him that … is safeguarded, for if he needs … he can eat it.

MISHNA: One may establish an eiruv with demai, … and … with … first tithe whose teruma has been taken … and with … second tithe and consecrated articles that have been redeemed; and priests … with ḥalla,
However, … not … with tevel, … nor with first tithe whose teruma, … has not been taken, nor with … second tithe or consecrated articles that have not been redeemed.

GEMARA: … demai? Isn’t it unfit for him? … Since if he wants, he could declare his property ownerless, and he would be a poor … and … be fit for him, … now too, … it is … fit for him … As we learned … One may feed the poor demai,
and … soldiers demai.
Rav Huna said: It was taught … Beit Shammai say: One may not feed the impoverished demai. And Beit Hillel say: One may feed the impoverished demai.
with first tithe … has been taken. … It is obvious … It is only necessary … preceded … on the stalks, … and the teruma of the tithes was taken from it … teruma gedola was not taken from it.

And … in accordance with … Rabbi Abbahu … Reish Lakish said, as Rabbi Abbahu said … Reish Lakish said: First tithe, … where … preceded … on the stalks, is exempt from teruma gedola, as it is stated: “And you shall set apart from it a gift for the Lord, even a tenth part of the tithe” … A tenth part of the tithe, … I told you, … And … not … teruma gedola and the teruma of the tithe.

Rav Pappa said to Abaye: If so, even … preceded … in a pile, … said to him: With regard to your … the verse states: “From all that is given to you, you shall set apart that which is the Lord’s teruma”
And what did you see … This … has become grain, and that … did not … become grain.

with … second tithe and consecrated … that have been redeemed. … It is obvious … was only needed … where one … paid the principle but did not pay the … fifth … And … teaches us … the … fifth does not invalidate
But … with tevel, … obvious, … is only needed with regard to tevel that is considered tevel by rabbinic decree. … For example, if one planted … in an imperforated container,
not … with first tithe whose teruma has not been taken. … It is obvious, … is only needed … preceded … the pile, and … teruma of the tithe was taken from it, … teruma gedola was not taken from it,
Lest you say … as Rav Pappa said to Abaye, … teaches us as … responded to
not … with … second tithe or consecrated … that have not been redeemed. … It is obvious

is only needed … where he redeemed them, … did not redeem them properly, … second tithe that was redeemed with an unminted coin [asimon]. And the Torah says … And bind up [vetzarta] the money … money that has a form [tzura] … upon it;
consecrated property, … where one redeemed it … for land … as the Torah states: “He will give the money and it shall become his.”

MISHNA: … one sends his eiruv in the hands of a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor, … or in the hands of one who does not accept … eiruv, it is not … eiruv. … if one told another … to receive it from him … it is a … eiruv.
GEMARA: … Is a minor not … Didn’t Rav Huna say: A minor may collect the … eiruv … not difficult, … here, … to an eiruv of … borders. … There, … to an eiruv of courtyards.
Or … in the hands of one who does not accept … eiruv. … Who … Rav Ḥisda said: A Samaritan [Kuti],

And if he told another … to receive … from him, it is a … eiruv. … Let us be concerned that perhaps … not bring … as Rav Ḥisda said … where he stands and watches him. Here, too, … where … stands and watches him
let us be concerned that perhaps … not take … from … as … Rav Yeḥiel said … presumption … an agent fulfills his agency. Here, too, … presumption … agent … fulfills his agency.

Where were … Rav Ḥisda and Rav Yeḥiel stated? … They were stated with regard to … as it was taught … one gave … to … elephant, and it brought it … to a monkey, and it brought it … it is not a … eiruv. But if he told another … to receive it from … it is … eiruv. … But perhaps … will not bring … to … Rav Ḥisda said: … to … where … stands and watches it … perhaps … will not accept it from … Rav Yeḥiel said: … presumption … an agent fulfills his agency.
Rav Naḥman said: With regard to Torah … not … presumption that an agent fulfills his agency;
with regard to rabbinic … presumption … an agent fulfills his agency. And Rav Sheshet … said: … both this, … and that, … presumption … an agent fulfills his agency.
Rav Sheshet said: From where do I say this? As we learned … Once the omer has been offered, … the new crop is immediately permitted.

And those far … are permitted … from midday and on, … Isn’t … the new … a Torah law? And … it was taught: And those far … are permitted … from midday and on. Is this not because … presumption … an agent fulfills his agency?
And … Rav Naḥman, … There, … the reason that was … taught: Because we know that the court will not be indolent

And some say … Rav Naḥman said: From where do I say this … As it was taught … the reason … because we know that the court will not be indolent … It is the court … will not be indolent … but … agent may … be indolent
And Rav Sheshet … said to you … the court … by midday, … agent, … the entire day.

Rav Sheshet said: From where do I say … As it was taught … A woman who is responsible … childbirth or … ziva … brings money and puts it in … box … immerses … and … eat sacrificial food at nightfall. What is the reason … Is it not because we say … presumption … an agent fulfills his agency,
And … Rav Naḥman … There, … in accordance with … Rav Shemaya, as Rav Shemaya said: … presumption … the court of priests would not leave … until all the money in the … box has been spent

Rav Sheshet said … From where do I say this? As it was taught … One who says to another … Go and gather for yourself figs from my fig tree, … may eat casually from them … he must … tithe them … with certainty … Fill this basket for yourself with figs from my fig tree, he may eat from them casually … and … he must tithe them … demai,

In what … is this statement said? … an am ha’aretz. But … a ḥaver, … may eat … and he need not tithe … the statement of Rabbi … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, says … In what … is this statement said? … am ha’aretz. But … a ḥaver, … may not eat … until he tithes … because ḥaverim, … are not suspected of separating teruma … from … not adjacent
Rabbi … said: My statement appears … than Father’s statement: It is better that ḥaverim should be suspected of separating … from … not adjacent … and they should not feed amei ha’aretz … tevel.
disagreed only … That one Sage, … holds … are suspected … and one Sage, … holds … they are not suspected … But all … presumption … an agent fulfills his agency,

And Rav Naḥman … There, … in accordance with … Rav Ḥanina Ḥoza’a, as Rav Ḥanina Ḥoza’a said: There is … presumption with regard to a ḥaver that he does not release anything that is not tithed from his possession.
The Master said: … in what … is this statement said? … an am ha’aretz. However, … a ḥaver, … may eat … and he need not tithe … the statement of Rabbi

This am ha’aretz, … to whom did he speak? If you say that he spoke to his fellow am ha’aretz, … He must tithe them as demai? Would … comply … Rather, … to an am ha’aretz who told a ḥaver … say … the latter clause … My statement appears … than Father’s statement, … It is better that ḥaverim should be suspected of separating … from … not adjacent … and they should not feed amei ha’aretz … tevel. What is the relevance of amei ha’aretz there?
Ravina said: The first clause … to an am ha’aretz who spoke to a ḥaver, … the latter clause … to a ḥaver who spoke to an am ha’aretz, and a different ḥaver heard him … Rabbi

holds: That ḥaver, … may … eat … and he is not required to tithe … as the first ḥaver certainly separated tithes for … And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel … says: … may not eat … until he has tithed … for ḥaverim are not suspected of separating … from … not adjacent … And Rabbi … said to him: It is better that ḥaverim should be suspected of separating … from … not adjacent … and they should not feed amei ha’aretz … tevel.

With regard to what … do they disagree? … Rabbi … holds: It is preferable to a ḥaver that he commit a minor transgression, … an am ha’aretz will not commit … major transgression … And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds: It is preferable to a ḥaver that an am ha’aretz commit a major transgression, and that he … not commit even a minor transgression.

MISHNA: … one placed … in a tree above ten handbreadths … his eiruv is not a … eiruv; … below ten handbreadths, his eiruv is … eiruv. … he placed … in a pit, even … it was a hundred cubits deep, his eiruv is … eiruv.

GEMARA: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba sat, and … Rabbi Asi and Rava bar Natan, and Rav Naḥman sat beside them, and they sat and said: This tree … where does it stand? If you say it stands in the private domain, what … to me … above … below … The private domain ascends to the sky,

Rather, … that … stands in the public domain; … Where … intend to establish his Shabbat residence? If you say that … intended to … Shabbat residence … above, he and his eiruv are in one place. … Rather, … intended to establish his Shabbat residence … below; … isn’t he making use of the tree

Actually, … that … stands in the public domain, and that he intended to establish his Shabbat residence … below, … And … is … Rabbi … who said: Anything that is … due to a rabbinic decree [shevut], … did not issue the decree … during twilight,

Rav Naḥman said to them: Well … and Shmuel said similarly … They said to him: Have you, … gone so far in your explanation … They, too, explained … in this … Rather, this is what they said to … Have you established this … as part of your … study … He said to them: Yes. … it was also … stated … Rav Naḥman said … Shmuel said: Here, we are dealing with a tree standing in the public domain, … ten … high and four … wide. … and … intended to establish his Shabbat residence below … And … is … Rabbi … who said: Anything that is … due to a rabbinic decree, … did not issue the decree … during twilight.

Rava said … They only taught … with regard to a tree that stands beyond the outskirts of the city, … However, … a tree that stands within the outskirts of the city, even … above ten … it is a … eiruv, as the city is considered as though it were filled in
If so, … beyond the outskirts of the town, … also … Since Rava … said: One who places his eiruv … has four cubits … a private domain; and a private domain rises to the sky.
Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rav Mesharshiya, said: Here, we are dealing with a tree that leans out … beyond four cubits
and he intended to establish his Shabbat residence at its base. And what … above and below, … it … again in an upright
Isn’t … if one wants, he can … bring it by way of … leaves,

where … the masses … shoulder … on it, … and … is in accordance with … Ulla, as Ulla said: … a pillar … nine … in the public domain, and the masses … shoulder … and someone threw … and it came to rest upon it, he is liable,
What is … Rabbi … and what is … the Rabbis?

As it was taught … If one placed … in a tree above ten handbreadths … his eiruv is not … eiruv. … below ten handbreadths, his eiruv is … eiruv, but he is prohibited to take it … within three … he is permitted to take it … one placed … in a basket and hung it on a tree, even above ten handbreadths, his eiruv is … eiruv; … the statement of Rabbi … And the Rabbis … say: … any … a location where it is prohibited to take … his eiruv is not … eiruv.
to which … the Rabbis state … If you say … to the latter clause … let us say that the Rabbis hold … the sides … is prohibited, … Rather, … to the first clause,

Rav Sheshet said: … you will not say the reason … Rabbi Meir’s … uncertainty whether … established an eiruv … did not establish an eiruv, … that … he is … a donkey driver … a camel driver. However, … certainty … did not establish an eiruv he is not … a donkey driver … a camel driver,
Rather, … even … certainty … did not establish an eiruv … a donkey driver … a camel driver, as here he certainly did not establish an eiruv, and … he is … a donkey driver … a camel driver.
MISHNA: One who … went out beyond … limit, even … one … may not reenter. Rabbi Eliezer says: … two … he may reenter; … three … he may not reenter.

GEMARA: Rabbi Ḥanina said: … one of his feet was within the … limit, and his other foot was beyond the … limit, he may not reenter, as it is written: “If you turn away your feet [raglekha] due to Shabbat” … is written … your foot

But wasn’t … taught … one of his feet was within the … limit, and his other foot was beyond the … limit, he may reenter. … whose … is this … It is … of Aḥerim, as it was taught … Aḥerim say: He is attributed to the place where the majority of his body

Some say … Rabbi Ḥanina said: … one of his feet was within the … limit, and his other foot was beyond the … limit, he may reenter, as it is written: “If you turn away your feet due to Shabbat” … We read … your feet,
But wasn’t … taught … He may not reenter? … stated … in accordance with … Aḥerim, as it was taught … He is attributed to the place where the majority of his body

Rabbi Eliezer says: … two … he may reenter; … three … he may not reenter. … But wasn’t it taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: … one … he may reenter; … two … he may not reenter. … not a difficulty. This, … he moved … the first … and is … standing two … however, that, … he moved … the second … and is … standing three

But wasn’t it taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: Even … one cubit … he may not enter. … When that … was taught … one measuring … As we learned … And … one … is … measuring … with regard to whom … said one provides him … two thousand cubits, even if his measurement ended in a cave

MISHNA: … one … whom it grew dark … outside the … limit … even … one cubit … he may not enter … Rabbi Shimon says: Even … fifteen cubits … he may enter … because the surveyors do not precisely demarcate the measures; … due to those who err.
GEMARA: … taught … Due to those who err in their measurement.
MISHNA: How does one extend … cities … a house is recessed and … house protrudes, … a turret [pagum] is recessed and … turret protrudes … there were remnants … ten handbreadths high,
and bridges and monuments … in which there is a residence, one extends the measure … opposite them … And … one renders … like a square tablet so that it gains the corners,
GEMARA: … Rav and Shmuel … One taught … me’abberin, … and one taught … me’abberin,
The one who taught me’abberin … limb … ever … limb. … And the one who taught me’abberin … a pregnant woman … ubbera
the Machpelah Cave, … Rav and Shmuel … One said: … two rooms, one … in … the other. And one said: … a room and … story above it.
Granted, … according to the one who said … one … above the other, … that is … Machpelah, double. However, according to the one who said … two rooms, one … in … the other, … what … Machpelah?
that it is doubled with … in pairs. … “Mamre … Kiryat Ha’Arba, … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: … the city of the four couples … Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebecca, … Jacob and Leah.

“And it came to pass in the days of Amraphel” … Rav and Shmuel … one said: Nimrod was his name. And why was his name called Amraphel? … As he said [amar] … and cast [hippil] our father Abraham into the fiery furnace, … And one said: Amraphel was his name. And why was his name called Nimrod? Because he caused the entire world to rebel [himrid] … God during his reign.
“There arose a new king over Egypt, … Rav and Shmuel … One said: … actually … new … and one said: … his decrees were new.
The one who said … actually … new … that it is written … new. And the one who said that his decrees were new … from … that it is not written: And … died, and … reigned,
And according to the one who said that his decrees were new, isn’t it written: “Who knew not Joseph”? … What is … “Who knew not Joseph”? … that he … like one who did not know Joseph at all.
mnemonic … Eighteen and twelve we studied, with regard to David, and he will understand.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: I spent eighteen days with Rabbi Oshaya the Distinguished [Beribbi], and I learned from him only one matter in our Mishna. … How does one extend cities, … with an alef.

Is this so? Didn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan say: Rabbi Oshaya the Distinguished had twelve students, and I spent eighteen days among them, and I learned the heart of each and every one, … and the … wisdom of each and every one?

he learned the heart of each and every one and the wisdom of each and every one, … he did not learn … tradition. … if you wish, say … From … themselves he learned … from … himself he did not learn … And if you wish, say … say … in our Mishna

And Rabbi Yoḥanan said … When we were studying Torah with Rabbi Oshaya, … we would sit four in each … cubit. … Rabbi … said: When we were studying Torah with Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua, we would sit six in each … cubit.

Rabbi Yoḥanan said … Rabbi Oshaya the Distinguished … in his generation as Rabbi Meir … in his generation: Just as … Rabbi Meir, in his generation his colleagues were unable to fully grasp … his thinking … so … Rabbi Oshaya; his colleagues were unable to fully grasp … his thinking.
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The hearts, … of … early … like the doorway to the Entrance Hall … and … of … later … were like the doorway to the Sanctuary, … And we, … are like … eye of a fine needle.
early … Rabbi Akiva, … later … Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua. Some say … early … Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua … later … Rabbi Oshaya the Distinguished. And we are like … eye of a fine needle.

Abaye said: And we, … are like a peg in the wall with regard to … study. … Rava said: And we are like a finger in wax [kira] with regard to logical reasoning. … Rav Ashi said: We are like a finger in a pit with regard to forgetfulness.

Rav Yehuda said that Rav said: … the people of Judea, who were particular in their speech … their Torah … endured for them; … the people of the Galilee, who were not particular in their speech, their Torah … did not endure for them.

Is … matter at all dependent on … particular … Rather, … the people of Judea, who were precise in their language and … would formulate mnemonics … their Torah … endured for them; … the people of the Galilee, who were not precise in their language and … would not formulate mnemonics, their Torah … did not endure for them.
the people of Judea, … studied from one teacher, their Torah … endured for them, … the people of the Galilee, who did not study from one teacher, … their Torah … did not endure for them,

Ravina said: … the people of Judea, who would … disclose the tractate … their Torah … endured for them; … the people of the Galilee, who would not disclose the tractate … their Torah … did not endure for them.

David would disclose the tractate … Saul would not disclose the tractate … With regard to David, who would disclose the tractate, it is written: “Those who fear You will see me and be glad” … With regard to Saul, who would not disclose the tractate … it is written: “And wherever he turned himself
he did them mischief”
And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: From where … that the Holy One, Blessed be He, forgave him for that sin, … As it is stated … and tomorrow shall you and your sons be with me” … “with me” … within my partition

Rabbi Abba said: If there is anyone who can ask the people of Judea, who are precise in their language, … we learned … me’abberin … or me’abberin … was … we learned … akkuzo … or did we learn akkuzo … They would know.
One asked … and they said to him: Some teach me’abberin … and some teach me’abberin … Some teach akkuzo … and some teach akkuzo

the people of Judea are precise in their speech, … What is … As … a certain person from Judea who said to those … I have a cloak to sell. They said to him: What color is your cloak? He said to them: Like beets on the ground,

the people of the Galilee, who are not precise in their speech. What is … As it was taught … that … a certain person from the Galilee who would walk and say … Who has amar? Who has amar? They said to him: Foolish Galilean, … a donkey [ḥamor] to ride, or wine [ḥamar] to drink, wool [amar] to wear, or a lamb [imar] to slaughter.
a certain woman who wanted to say to her friend: … come and I will feed you milk [ta’i de’okhlikh ḥelba]; … she said to her: My neighbor, … lioness eat you [tokhlikh lavya].

a certain woman who came before a judge … she said to him: Master, servant [Mari kiri, … I had a beam and they stole you from me … tafla havet li ugenavukh min … And it was so … that when they would hang you upon it, your feet would not reach the ground.
The maidservant in the house of Rabbi … when she would speak enigmatically, … she would say as follows: The ladle … is … knocking against … the jug, … Let the eagles fly to their nests,
And when … wanted them to sit, she would say to them: Let us remove … from another … and let the ladle … in the jug like a ship sailing in the sea.
when Rabbi Yosei bar Asyan would speak enigmatically, he would say: Prepare for me an ox in judgment on a poor mountain.
And when he would inquire about an inn, he would say as follows: This man here is raw; what is this good that there is?

When Rabbi Abbahu would speak enigmatically, he would say as follows: Make the coals the color of an etrog; beat the golden ones, … and make me two speakers-in-the-dark, … Some say … And they shall make me in them, … two speakers-in-the-dark.

the Sages said to Rabbi Abbahu: Show us [hatzpinenu] where Rabbi Elai is hiding [tzafun], … He said to them: He rejoiced with the latter [aḥaronit] Aharonic [Aharonit] girl; she is lively [eiranit] and kept him awake [vehiniratu].
Some say … a woman,
And some say … a tractate.
They said to Rabbi Elai: Show us where Rabbi Abbahu is hiding, … He said to them: He has taken counsel with the one who crowns, … and has gone south … hingiv … to Mephibosheth,

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya said … In … my days, no person defeated me … except for a woman, a young boy, and a young girl. What is … a woman … One time I was staying at a certain inn … prepared me beans. On the first day I ate them and left nothing over, … second … and left nothing over. … she over-salted them … As soon as I tasted … I withdrew my hands from them.
She said to me: My Rabbi, why aren’t you eating … I said to her: I have already eaten during the daytime. She said to me: You should have withdrawn your hand from bread

She … said to me: My Rabbi, perhaps you did not leave a remainder … on the first … Isn’t this what the Sages said: One need not leave a remainder in the pot [ilpas], but one must leave a remainder on the plate

What is … a young girl? One time I was walking along the path, and the path passed through a field, and I was walking on it. A certain young girl said to me: My Rabbi, isn’t this a field? … I said to her: Isn’t it a well-trodden path … She said to me: Robbers like you have trodden it.

What is … a young boy? One time I was walking along the path, and I saw a young boy sitting at the crossroads. And I said to him: On which path shall we walk … to the city? He said to me: This … is short and long, and that … is long and short. I walked on the … short and long. When I approached the city I found that gardens and orchards surrounded it,

I went back … said to him: My son, didn’t you tell me … short? He said to me: And didn’t I tell you … long? I kissed him on his head and said to him: Happy are you, O Israel, for you are all exceedingly wise, from your old to your young.

Rabbi Yosei HaGelili was walking along the way, … met Berurya. He said to her: On which path shall we walk … to Lod? She said to him: Foolish Galilean, didn’t the Sages say: Do not talk much with women? You should have said … Which … to Lod?
Berurya came across a certain student who was whispering his studies

She kicked him … said to him: Isn’t it written as follows: “Ordered in all things and secure” … if … is ordered in your 248 limbs, … it will be secure, and if not, it will not be secure. … it was … taught … Rabbi Eliezer had a student who would study quietly, … after three years he forgot his studies.
It was taught … Rabbi Eliezer had a student who was liable for … burning, … against God, … said: Let him … he served a great person.

Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda: Keen scholar [shinnana], open your mouth and read … open your mouth and study … in order that … should endure in you and … you should live a long life, as it is stated: “For they are life to those who find them, and health to all their flesh” … Do not read: “To those who find them [lemotzeihem],” but … “to those who express them [lemotzi’eihem],” with … mouth.
Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda, … Keen scholar, grab and eat, grab and drink, as the world from which we are departing is like a wedding feast,

Rav said to Rav Hamnuna: My son, if you have … do well for yourself. … as there is no pleasure in the netherworld, and death does not tarry. And if you say: I will … leave for my children, who told you the law of the netherworld, … People are similar to grass of the field, … these blossom, … and these wither
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: One who is walking along the way without a companion … should engage in Torah … as it is stated … “For they shall be a graceful wreath [livyat ḥen]

One who feels … in his head should engage in Torah … as it is stated: “For they shall be a graceful wreath for your head.” One who feels … in his throat should engage in Torah … as it is stated: “And chains about your neck.” One who feels … in his intestines should engage in Torah … as it is stated: “It shall be health to your navel” … One who feels … in his bones should engage in Torah … as it is stated: “And marrow to your bones” … One who feels … in his entire body should engage in Torah … as it is stated: “And health to all their flesh”

Rav Yehuda, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya, said: Come and see that the attribute of flesh and blood is unlike the attribute of the Holy One, Blessed be He. The attribute of flesh and blood … a person gives a drug to his fellow, it is good for this … and it is harmful to that … But … the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so; He gave the Torah to the Jewish people, … it is a drug of life for one’s entire body, as it is stated: “And health to all their flesh.”

Rav Ami said: What is … that which is written: “For it is a pleasant thing if you keep them within you; let them be firmly attached together to your lips” … When are words of Torah pleasant? When you keep them within you … And when will you keep them within you? When they will be attached together to your lips,

Rabbi Zeira said … from here: “A man has joy in the answer of his mouth; and a word in due season, how good it is” … When does a man have joy? When an answer … is in his mouth. Another version: When does a man have joy in the answer of his mouth? When … A word in due season, how good it is,

Rabbi Yitzḥak said … from here: “But the matter is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may do it” … When … very near to you? When it is in your mouth and in your heart, that you may do it,

Rava said … from here: “You have given him his heart’s desire, and have not withheld the request of his lips, Selah” … When have You given him his heart’s desire? When You have not withheld the request of his lips, Selah,

Rava raised an … contradiction … it is written: “You have given him his heart’s desire,” … it is written: “And You have not withheld the request of his lips, Selah,” … is fortunate, “You have given him his heart’s desire,” … is not fortunate, … “You have not withheld the request of his lips, Selah.”

of the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov taught … Wherever it states netzaḥ … Selah, … va’ed … will never cease. Netzaḥ, as it is written: “For I will not contend forever; neither will I be eternally [lanetzaḥ] angry”

Selah, as it is written: “As we have heard, so have we seen in the city of the Lord of Hosts, in the city of our God; may God establish it forever, Selah” … Va’ed, as it is written: “The Lord shall reign forever and ever [va’ed]”

mnemonic: Chains, cheeks, tablets, engraved. Rabbi Eliezer said: What is … that which is written: “And chains about your neck” … If a person makes himself like a chain that hangs loosely on the neck, … and … seen but not seen, … his … study will endure. But if not, … his … study will not endure.

And Rabbi Eliezer … said: What is … that which is written: “His cheeks are like a bed of spices” … If a person makes himself … like this … bed upon which everyone treads, and like this spice with which everyone perfumes himself, … his … study will endure. But if not, his … study will not endure.

And Rabbi Eliezer … said: What is … that which is written: “Tablets [luḥot] of stone” … If a person makes his cheeks [leḥayav] like this stone that does not wear away, his … study will endure. But if not, … his … study will not endure.
And, … Rabbi Eliezer said: What is … that which is written: … engraved upon the tablets” … had the first tablets, … not been broken, the Torah would never have been forgotten from the Jewish people,
Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: … no nation or tongue would … have ruled over them, as it is stated: “Engraved … do not read … engraved … ḥarut] but … freedom [ḥeirut].

Rav Mattana said: What is … that which is written: … And from the wilderness they went to Mattanah” … If a person makes himself … like this wilderness, … upon which everyone treads, his … study will endure … And if not, his … study will not endure.

Rav Yosef had a grievance against Rava, son of Rav Yosef bar Ḥama, … When the eve of Yom Kippur arrived, … said: I will go and appease him. He went and found … attendant mixing him a cup … He said to … Give … to me, and I will mix … He gave it to … mixed it. … when he tasted … he said: This mixture is similar to the mixture … Rava, son of Rav Yosef bar Ḥama, … said to him: It is I.

said to him: Do not sit on your knees until you have explained these verses to me: What is … that which is written: “And from the wilderness to Mattanah; and from Mattanah to Nahaliel; and from Nahaliel to Bamoth; and from Bamoth to the valley

said to him: If a person makes himself … like this wilderness, … upon which everyone treads, the Torah will be given to him as a gift [mattana]. And once it is given to him as a gift, he inherits it [neḥalo] … God [El] … as it is stated: “And from Mattanah to Nahaliel.” And once God has made it His inheritance, he rises to greatness, as it is stated: “And from Nahaliel to Bamoth,”

And if he becomes haughty, the Holy One, Blessed be He, lowers him, as it is stated: “And from Bamoth to the valley.” And if he repents, the Holy One, Blessed be He, raises him … up, as it is stated: “Every valley shall be exalted”

Rav Huna said: What is … that which is written: “Your flock found a dwelling in it; You, O God, prepare of Your goodness for the poor” … If a person makes himself like an animal that tramples … and eats … and some say, … that soils and eats, … his … study will endure. And if not, his … study will not endure. And if he does so, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will Himself prepare him a feast, as it is stated: “You, O God, prepare of Your goodness for the poor,”

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said: What is … that which is written: “He who guards the fig tree shall eat its fruit” … Why were matters of Torah compared to a fig tree? Just as this fig tree,
whenever a person searches it … he finds figs in it, … so … matters of Torah. Whenever a person meditates upon them, he finds in them … meaning.

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said: What is … that which is written: “A loving hind and a graceful roe, … Why were matters of Torah compared to a hind? To tell you … just as … a hind, its womb is narrow and it is cherished by its mate each and every hour like the first hour, so … matters of Torah are cherished by those who study them each and every hour like the first hour.

“And a graceful roe” … That … bestows grace upon those who study it. “Let her breasts satisfy you at all times”; why were matters of Torah compared to a breast? Just as … a breast, whenever a baby searches it … he finds milk in it, so … matters of Torah. Whenever a person meditates upon them, he finds … meaning in them.

“And be you ravished always with her love”; … as was … Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat. They said of him, of Rabbi Elazar, that he would sit and engage in Torah … in the lower marketplace of Tzippori, and his cloak was lying in the upper marketplace of Tzippori. … it was taught … Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Elazar said: One time a person came to take … and found a serpent on it

of the school of Rav Anan taught: What is … that which is written: “You that ride on white donkeys, you that sit on rich cloths, and you that walk by the way, tell of it” … “You that ride on white donkeys”; these are Torah scholars, who travel from city to city and from province to province to study Torah. “White [tzeḥorot]” … who make it … as noon … tzahorayim … “You that sit on couches [midin]” … who judge [danin] an absolutely true judgment. “And you that walk”; these are the masters of Bible, … “By the way”; these are the … masters of Mishna. “Tell of it”; these are the masters of Talmud, … as all their conversation is … matters of Torah.

Rav Sheizvi said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya: What is … that which is written: “The slothful man [remiyya] will not roast [yaḥarokh] his catch” … The deceitful [rammai] hunter will not live [yiḥyeh] a long life [ya’arikh].
Rav Sheshet said: … a deceitful hunter … roast?
When Rav Dimi came … he said: This is comparable to a hunter who is hunting birds; if he breaks … wings … one by one … will be secured, and if not, … will not be secured.

Rabba said that Rav Seḥora said that Rav Huna said: What is … that which is written: “Wealth gotten through vanity … hevel … shall be diminished; but he that gathers little by little shall increase” … If a person turns his Torah into bundles … ḥavilot, … will diminish. And if not, … he that gathers little by little shall increase.
Rabba said: The Sages know this, but … transgress it, … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: I did this, … and … has … endured.

The Sages taught … What was the order of teaching … Moses learned … from the mouth of the Almighty. Aaron entered … and Moses taught him his lesson … Aaron moved … and sat to the left of Moses. … sons entered, and Moses taught them their lesson … sons moved … Elazar sat to the right of Moses and Itamar … to the left of Aaron. Rabbi Yehuda … said: Actually, Aaron would return to … the right of Moses. The elders entered and Moses taught them their lesson. The elders moved … the entire nation entered and Moses taught them their lesson. Therefore, Aaron had … four times, his sons … three … the elders … twice, and the entire nation … once.
Moses … departed … and Aaron taught … his lesson … Aaron … departed … his sons taught … their lesson. His sons … departed … the elders taught … their lesson. Hence everyone, … four times.

From here Rabbi Eliezer said: A person is obligated to teach his student … four times. And … an a fortiori inference: If Aaron, who learned from Moses … and Moses … from the mouth of the Almighty, … this … an ordinary … from the mouth of an ordinary … how much more so

Rabbi Akiva says: From where … that a person is obligated to teach his student until he learns … As it is stated: … and teach it to the children of Israel; … And from where … until … is organized in their mouths? As it is stated: “Put it in their mouths,”
And from where … that … must show … the reasons … As it is stated: “Now these are the judgments which you shall set before them”
They should all have studied from Moses … in order to give honor to Aaron and his sons, and … honor to the elders.

Aaron should have entered and studied from Moses; his sons should … have entered and studied from Aaron; the elders should … have entered and studied from … sons; and … they should have gone … and taught all of the Jewish people. … Since Moses had studied … from the mouth of the Almighty, it would be … effective

The Master said … Rabbi Yehuda says: Actually, Aaron would return to … the right of Moses, … In accordance with whose … was it taught … three … were walking along the way, the teacher … in the middle and the greater … to his right and the lesser … to his left? Shall we say … it is … Rabbi Yehuda and not … the Sages?
even say … the Sages, … due to the trouble to Aaron
Rabbi Perida had a certain student whom he would … teach four hundred times, and … learn … One day they requested … for a mitzva matter … taught … but … did not … learn

said to him: What is different now … He said to him: From the time that they said to the Master … there is a mitzva matter … my mind was distracted … and every moment I said: Now the Master will get up, now the Master will get up … said to him: Pay attention … and I will teach you, … He taught him again an additional four hundred times.

a Divine Voice emerged and said to him: … preferable to you that four hundred years be added … or that you and … your generation … merit the World-to-Come? He said: … that I and my generation merit the World-to-Come. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said … Give him both;
Rav Ḥisda said: The Torah can be acquired only with … signs … as it is stated: “Put it in their mouths.” Do not read … Put it [simah], but … Its sign [simanah],

Rav Taḥalifa of the West, … heard this … went … said it before Rabbi Abbahu, … said: You learn this … from there; we learn it from here, … “Set up signposts [tziyyunim] for yourself; establish you … Establish … signs for the Torah. And from where … that this … tziyyun denotes a sign? As it is written … and any sees a human bone, he shall set up a sign … tziyyun … by it”

Rabbi Eliezer said … from here: “Say to wisdom, you are my sister, and call understanding, your kinswoman [moda]” … Establish signs [moda’im] … the Torah. Rava said … Set appointed times [mo’adim] for Torah

And this … is … what Avdimi bar Ḥama bar Dosa said: What is … that which is written: “It is not in heaven…nor is it beyond the sea” … “It is not in heaven” … that if it were in heaven, you would have to ascend after it, and if it were beyond the sea, you would have to cross after it,
Rava said: “It is not in heaven” … is not to be found in someone who raises his mind over it, like the heavens, … nor is it to be found in someone who expands his mind over it, like the sea,
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: “It is not in heaven” … is not to be found in the haughty, … “Nor is it beyond the sea” … it is not to be found among merchants or traders

The Sages taught … How does one extend … cities? … long, … as it is. … round, one creates … corners for it, … square, one does not create … corners for it. … was wide on one side and narrow on the other side, one regards it as though … were … equal

one house … was protruding like a turret, or … two houses … protruding like two turrets, one regards them as though a cord is stretched over their … and one measures two thousand cubits … from there. … was shaped like a bow or like … gamma, one regards it as though … full of houses and courtyards, and one measures two thousand cubits … from there.
The Master said: … long, … as it is. … obvious. … It was necessary … only … where … long and narrow. Lest you say: Let us give its breadth … of its length … it teaches us

square, one does not create … corners for it. … obvious. … It was necessary … only … where … is square but … square is not … four … of the world, … Lest you say: Let us … square with the four … world, it teaches us
one house … was protruding like a turret, or … two houses … protruding like two turrets, … Now, … one house, you said … two houses, is it necessary
It was necessary … only … on two … sides … Lest you say: … from one side, we say … from two sides we do not say … it teaches us

was shaped like a bow or like … gamma, one regards it as if … full of houses and courtyards, and one measures two thousand cubits … from there. Rav Huna said: … a city that is shaped like a bow, … If there are less than four thousand cubits between … two ends … one measures … from the … bowstring … But if … not … one measures … from the bow
Did Rav Huna … say … Didn’t Rav Huna say: … the wall of a city that was breached, … 141⅓
Rabba bar Ulla said: … not difficult. Here, … on … one side, … there, … from two sides,
