and … eat … from beneath … trees that shed fruit … on Shabbat; and they … designate … corner … vegetables, … And the Sages reprimanded

GEMARA: … The Sages taught: King Hezekiah performed six actions. With regard to three … conceded to him; and with regard to three … did not concede to him. … he dragged the bones of his father … on a bier of ropes … and … conceded to him. He ground the copper snake … and … conceded to him. He suppressed the Book of Cures, and they conceded to him.

And with regard to three … did not concede to him. He cut off the doors of the Sanctuary and sent them to the King of Assyria, and they did not concede to him … He sealed the waters of the upper Gihon … and they did not concede to him, … He intercalated … of Nisan during Nisan, and they did not concede to him.

They … graft palm trees the entire day … How did they perform … Rabbi Yehuda said: They brought fresh myrtle, strong beer … from the … laurel tree, and barley flour that was cast into a vessel, and forty days has not passed … They boiled them … and poured … into the core of the palm tree. … any … standing within four cubits of that … if they did not perform this … it would immediately wither … Rav Aḥa, son … Rava, said: They placed a branch of a male palm tree on the female,

bundle Shema. … How did they do … Rabbi Yehuda said … they recited: “Hear Israel: The Lord is our God, the Lord is One … and they would not pause … Rava said: They … pause … but … they would say: Today shall be on your heart, … Today it will be on your heart, and tomorrow it will not be on your heart. The Sages taught … How would they bundle Shema? They recited: “Hear Israel, the Lord is our God the Lord is One,” without pausing; … the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda says: They paused, but they would not recite: Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom for ever and ever.
What is the reason that we recite … in accordance with … which Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish interpreted homiletically.

As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said … “And Jacob called his sons and said, Gather around and I will tell you … Jacob wanted to reveal to his sons … the end of days … but the Divine Presence abandoned him, … He said: Perhaps … Heaven forfend, one of my descendants is unfit, as … Abraham, from whom Ishmael emerged, and … my father Isaac, from whom Esau emerged. His sons said to him: Hear Israel, … the Lord is our God, the Lord is One. They said: Just as there is only one … in your heart, so too, there is only one in our hearts. At that moment Jacob our father said … Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom for ever and ever,

The Rabbis said: What should we do? Shall we recite … Moses our teacher did not say it … Shall we not recite it? … Jacob said it. … they established that … should be recited surreptitiously. Rabbi Yitzḥak said … the school of Rabbi Ami said: … analogous to the daughter of a king who smelled … spices … the pot … If she tells … she will be disgraced, … she does not say … she will … suffering. Her servants began to bring … surreptitiously.
Rabbi Abbahu said: … instituted that … should recite it aloud due to the grievance of the heretics. … In Neharde’a, where there are no heretics, they recite it surreptitiously even now.

The Sages taught … The people of Jericho performed six actions, three … with the will of the Sages and three against the will of the Sages. And these … with the will of the Sages: They … graft palm trees the entire day … and they … bundle Shema; and they … harvest … before the omer … And these … against the will of the Sages: They … pile … before the omer; and they … make breaches in … their gardens and their orchards to feed fallen … to the poor during drought years, … on Shabbat and Festivals; and they … permit … consecrated branches of carob and of sycamore … the statement of Rabbi Meir.

Rabbi Yehuda said to him: … if they acted … with the will of the Sages, all people would do so, … Rather, … these … and those … were performed against the will of the Sages. With regard to three … reprimanded them; and with regard to three … did not reprimand them.

And these … did not reprimand them: They … graft palm trees the entire day; and they … bundle Shema; and they … harvest and pile … before the omer … And these … reprimanded them: They … permit … consecrated branches of carob and of sycamore … they … make breaches in … their gardens and orchards on Shabbat and Festivals, in order to feed the poor fallen fruit during drought years; and they … designate … the … corner … vegetables. And the Sages reprimanded them

And … Rabbi Yehuda maintain … harvest … was against the will of the Sages? Didn’t we learn … The people of Jericho … harvest before the omer, … with the will of the Sages, and they … pile … before the omer, against the will of the Sages, but the Sages did not reprimand them?

Whom did you hear that said: Reprimanded and did not reprimand? … Rabbi Yehuda, … And … Rabbi Yehuda is teaching … they … harvest … will of the Sages. … And according to your reasoning, these … are … four: … Rather, delete harvest … here.

permit … consecrated branches of carob and of sycamore … They said: Our fathers consecrated … the tree trunks, and … we can permit the consecrated branches … of carob and of sycamore … we are dealing with the growth that came afterward, and they hold in accordance with … one who said: There is no misuse … with regard to … growth. And the Rabbis hold: Although there is no misuse … in any case, there is a prohibition.

created breaches … Ulla said … Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: … dispute … with regard to … the upper palm branches [makhebedot]. The Sages hold: We issue a decree … lest … climb … and pick … And the people of Jericho hold: We do not issue a decree lest one climb … and pick … However, with regard to … lower palm branches [keifin], everyone agrees … permitted.

Rava said to … But aren’t they set-aside, … And if you say: … since they are fit for … ravens, … now, … prepared for … a person is not … prepared for … dogs, as we learned … Rabbi Yehuda says: If … was … not a carcass on Shabbat eve, it may not … because it was not … prepared … prepared for ravens … prepared for a person?

said to … Yes, … prepared for … a person is not prepared for dogs, as any item that is fit for a person, one does not remove it from his thoughts; … prepared for ravens is … prepared for … a person. Any item that is fit for … a person, his thoughts are upon it.

When Ravin came … Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: … dispute … with regard to … the lower palm branches, as the Sages hold: … is prepared for ravens is not prepared for a person. And the people of Jericho hold: … is prepared for ravens is prepared for a person. However, … on upper branches, everyone agrees … prohibited, … we issue a decree lest one climb … and pick

And … designate … the … corner [pe’a] … vegetables. … And aren’t the people of Jericho … that which we learned … A principle was stated with regard to the … corner … Anything that is food, and is protected, and grows from the ground, and is gathered as one, and … brings it in … for preservation is obligated in … corner

Anything that is food; … to exclude the after-growths of woad and safflower. … the … corners … And is protected; … to exclude ownerless … And grows from the ground; … to exclude truffles and mushrooms, … And is gathered as one; … to exclude … fig … And one brings it in … for preservation; … to exclude vegetables,

Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: Here we are dealing with turnip heads, … they disagree with regard to bringing it in … for preservation by means of another substance. … One Sage, … holds: Storage by means of another substance … is considered storage. And one Sage, … holds: It is not considered storage, … corner

The Sages taught: Initially, they would designate the … corner … from turnips and cabbages. Rabbi Yosei says: … even from leeks [kaflot]. And it was taught in another … They would designate the … corner … from turnips and leeks. Rabbi Shimon says: … even from cabbages.

Let us say … there are three tanna’im … No, there are … two tanna’im … and the first tanna … Rabbi Shimon is Rabbi Yosei. And the first tanna … Rabbi Yosei is Rabbi Shimon. And what … even … the first

The Sages taught: The son … Bohayan designated … the … corner … of vegetables, and his father … found the poor laden … vegetables and standing at the opening of the garden … He said to them: My sons, cast … from upon yourselves and I will give you twice … tithed … Not because I begrudge … Rather, it is because the Sages say: One does not designate … the … corner … of vegetables.
Why … for him to say to them: Not because I begrudge … so they would not say: He is putting us off,

The Sages taught: Initially, … would place the hides … consecrated … in the Parva chamber. In the evening, they would distribute them to the members of the family … And the powerful … take them by force … decreed that they would distribute them each Shabbat eve, … all the … watches came and took … together.
Yet still the prominent priests … would take them by force. … the owners … arose and consecrated … to Heaven

said: Not a few days passed before they had plated the entire sanctuary with golden tablets … were one cubit by one cubit and as thick as a golden dinar. And … for the … pilgrimage they would remove … and place them on a stair of the Temple Mount so that the pilgrims would see that the craftsmanship … was beautiful and without flaw [dalam].
It was … taught … Abba Shaul says: There were sycamore tree trunks in Jericho, and powerful people would take them … by force. The owners stood and consecrated … to Heaven.

With regard to … and those like them, Abba Shaul ben Batnit said in the name of Abba Yosef ben Ḥanin: Woe is me due to … the house of Baitos, woe is me due to their clubs. Woe is me due to … the house of Ḥanin; woe is me due to their whispers … Woe is me due to … the house of Katros; woe is me due to their pens … Woe is me due to … the house of Yishmael ben Piakhi; woe is me due to their fists. … that … were High Priests, and their sons were … treasurers, and their sons-in-law were … overseers [amarkalin]. And their servants strike the people with clubs,

the Sages taught: … the … courtyard … cried four cries, … first … Leave here, sons of Eli, who defiled God’s Sanctuary … And an additional cry: Leave here, Yissakhar of Kfar Barkai, who honors himself and desecrates … consecrated … Heaven. … wrap … in silk [shirai] and perform the service.

And … the … courtyard cried additionally: Lift your heads, O gates, and let … Yishmael ben Piakhi, the student of Pinehas … enter and serve as High Priest, … And … the … courtyard cried additionally: Lift your heads, O gates, and let Yoḥanan ben Narbbai, the student of Pinkai, enter and fill his belly with … of offerings … Heaven,

They said about Yoḥanan ben Narbbai that he … would eat three hundred calves, and drink three hundred jugs of wine, and eat forty se’a of doves for dessert. They said: … all the days of Yoḥanan ben Narbbai there was no leftover … in the Temple, … What … happened to Yissakhar of Kfar Barkai? They said: The king and the queen were sitting … The king said … goat … is better … and the queen said lamb … better … They said: Who can prove … The High Priest … as he offers sacrifices all day … came,

signaled … with his hand … If goat is better, let … sacrificed as the daily offering. … The king said: Since he … has no reverence … the monarchy, … sever his right … He gave a bribe and … severed his left hand. The king heard … and … sever his right hand … Rav Yosef said: Blessed is God Who took retribution [mitarpesei] from Yissakhar of Kfar Barkai in this world

Rav Ashi said: Yissakhar of Kfar Barkai did not study … Mishna … As we learned … Rabbi Shimon says: Lambs take precedence … goats in every place … might … because it is a … select species. … the verse states: “If he brings a lamb as his offering” … teaches that both … are equal. Ravina said: … even read the Bible … as it is written: “If a lamb” … “if a goat” … If one wishes let him bring a lamb; if one wishes let him bring a goat.

MISHNA: The daily … offering is slaughtered at eight and a half … and is sacrificed, … at nine and a half … On the eves of Passover, … it is slaughtered at seven and a half … and sacrificed at eight and a half … whether … during the week or on Shabbat. … Passover eve occurs on Shabbat eve, … is slaughtered at six and a half … and sacrificed at seven and a half … and the Paschal lamb … thereafter.
GEMARA: … From where are these matters

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: … the verse … says: “The one lamb you shall offer in the morning and the second lamb you shall offer in the afternoon [bein ha’arbayim]” … Divide … between two evenings. … Two and a half hours here … and two and a half hours there … and … one hour … to perform

Rava raised an objection: … on the eves of Passover … is slaughtered at seven and a half … and sacrificed at eight and a half … both during the week and on Shabbat. And if it could enter your mind … that … eight and a half hours by Torah law, how can we do it earlier

Rather, … Rava said: The mitzva of the daily offering … from when the … evening shadows slant … What is the reason … the verse states: In the afternoon [bein ha’arbayim], … from the time that the sun begins to … westward [ma’arav].
Therefore, on the rest of the days of the year, when there are … vow … and free-will … As the Merciful One says … the fats of the peace-offerings … upon it”
And the Master said … “The fats of the peace-offerings upon it” … “Upon it,” … complete all the … offerings. … we postpone … for two hours, and sacrifice it at eight and a half

eves of Passover, … when there is the Paschal lamb … after … we advance … one hour and sacrifice it at seven and a half … Passover eve occurs on Shabbat eve, when there is also the roasting … which does not override … Shabbat … we establish … its halakha … at six and a half
The Sages taught … like its arrangement during the week, so is its arrangement on Shabbat; … the statement of Rabbi Yishmael. Rabbi Akiva says: Like its arrangement on Passover eve.

What is … saying? … Abaye said: This is what it is saying: … like its arrangement on Passover eve … during the week, … so is its arrangement on Passover eve … on Shabbat, … the statement of Rabbi Yishmael. Rabbi Akiva says: Like its arrangement on Passover eve that occurs on Shabbat eve, … so is its arrangement … on Shabbat, … the mishna that teaches … both during the week and on Shabbat, is … Rabbi Yishmael.

with regard to what … do … disagree? … They disagree about … the additional offerings … precede the bowls … Rabbi Yishmael holds that the additional offerings precede the bowls. … sacrificed the additional offerings at six … and … the bowls at seven … he sacrificed the daily offering at seven and a half … Rabbi Akiva holds … the bowls precede the additional offerings. … bowls at five … the additional offerings at six … and sacrificed the daily offering at six and a half

Rava strongly objects to this … Is Rabbi Akiva teaching: Like its arrangement on Passover eve that occurs on Shabbat eve? He … merely teaches: Like its arrangement on Passover eve. … Rather, Rava said … This is what … is saying: Like the arrangement … on an ordinary … during the week, so is its arrangement on Shabbat … on Passover eve. … the statement of Rabbi Yishmael. Rabbi Akiva says: Like its arrangement on Passover eve … the mishna that teaches … both during the week and on Shabbat is … of Rabbi Akiva.

with regard to what … do they disagree? They disagree with regard to the … the meat will become warm … Rabbi Yishmael holds that we are concerned lest the meat become warm … And Rabbi Akiva holds: We are not concerned lest the meat become warm

If, … we are not concerned … let us sacrifice … at six and a half … holds: The additional offerings precede the bowls … sacrifice the additional offerings at six … and … the bowls at seven … and … sacrifice the daily offering at seven and a half

Rabba bar Ulla strongly objects to this … Does … teach: Like the arrangement … during the week, so is its arrangement on Shabbat … on Passover eve; … the statement of Rabbi Yishmael? … simply teaches: So is its arrangement on Shabbat.
Rather, Rabba bar Ulla said: … this is what it is teaching: Like its arrangement on an ordinary … during the week, so is its arrangement on an ordinary Shabbat, … the statement of Rabbi Yishmael,

Rabbi Akiva says: Like its arrangement on an ordinary Passover eve … so is its arrangement on an ordinary Shabbat. … And the mishna, which teaches … whether during the week or on Shabbat, … all opinions,

with regard to what … do … disagree? They disagree concerning whether a decree should be issued on account of … vows and free-will offerings. Rabbi Yishmael holds that we issue a decree for Shabbat due to weekdays. … And Rabbi Akiva holds that we do not issue such a decree.

If we do not issue … a decree, … Let us sacrifice it at six and a half hours. … holds that the additional offerings precede the bowls … additional offerings at six … and … the bowls at seven … sacrifices the daily offering at seven and a half

raises an objection … The daily offering is sacrificed throughout the entire year in accordance with its law. … it is slaughtered at eight and a half … and sacrificed at nine and a half … And on the eve of Passover it is slaughtered at seven and a half … and sacrificed at eight and a half … If … occurs on Shabbat it is as if it occurred on a Monday, … the statement of Rabbi Yishmael. Rabbi Akiva says: … like its arrangement on the eve of Passover

Granted, according to … Abaye, … works out well, … But according to … Rava, … difficult. … Rava could have said to you: Do not say: It is as if it occurred on a Monday. Rather say: … like an ordinary Monday,

raises an objection … occurs on Shabbat, … in accordance with its arrangement all year long, … the statement of Rabbi Yishmael. Rabbi Akiva says: … in accordance with its arrangement on an ordinary Passover eve. Granted, according to … Rava, … works out well. But according to … Abaye, … difficult.

Abaye can say to you: Do not say … In accordance with its arrangement all year long. Rather, say: In accordance with its arrangement every year; … the statement of Rabbi Yishmael. … Rabbi Akiva says … in accordance with its arrangement on Passover eve that occurs on Shabbat eve.

The Sages taught: From where … that no … shall precede the daily morning offering? The verse states: … he shall prepare the burnt-offering upon it … What is the … derivation? … Rava said: “The burnt-offering,” … the first burnt-offering,

And from where … that nothing is sacrificed after the daily afternoon offering? The verse states: “And shall cause the fats of the peace-offerings to go up in smoke upon it.” … What is the derivation? Abaye said: “Upon it.” … peace-offerings, … But peace-offerings … not … upon, … its counterpart,

Rava strongly objects to this … say it is peace-offerings that we must not sacrifice … but burnt-offerings we may sacrifice, … Rather, Rava said: “The peace-offerings [hashelamim] upon it” … completes [hashlem] … all other sacrifices.
The Sages taught … The daily offering precedes … the Paschal lamb, the Paschal lamb precedes … incense, … incense precedes … lamps
An item, … about which it is stated: “In the evening” and “in the afternoon,” should be … after an item, … about which it is not stated “in the evening,” but only “in the afternoon.”

If that is so, … the … incense and the … lamps … should also precede the … Paschal lamb. The item, … about which it is stated “in the evening” and “in the afternoon” should be … after the item about which it is stated only: … in the afternoon

It is different there, … as the Merciful One … excludes … it [oto], … As it was taught … from evening to morning … “from evening to morning” … you shall allocate … its measure … it will burn from evening until morning.

Alternatively, … There is no rite that is valid from evening until morning but this one alone, … What is the reason … the verse said … “Aaron and his sons shall set [ya’arokh] it [oto] in order, … from evening to morning.” … it, … is from evening until morning, but no other … from evening until morning.
juxtaposes the … incense to the … lamps,

it was … taught … in accordance with our difficulty … The daily … offering precedes … the incense, … the incense precedes … the lamps, and … the lamps precedes the Paschal lamb. … An item, … about which it is stated “in the evening” and “in the afternoon” should be delayed until after an item, … about which it is stated only “in the afternoon.”

isn’t “it” written … This … “it” is necessary, … to exclude a rite that is … inside … And what is … incense. It could have entered your mind to say that since it is written: “And when Aaron lights the lamps in the afternoon he shall burn it” … say … we should light the lamps first and then we should burn the incense, … the Merciful One excludes … it,”
However, … why do I … “in the afternoon he shall burn it,” … this is … the Merciful One is saying: … at the time when you light the lamps, the incense should … be burning.

The Sages taught … Nothing may precede the daily morning offering but … the incense alone, as it is stated about … “In the morning, in the morning.” And … the incense, an item about which it is stated: “In the morning, in the morning,” as it is written: “And Aaron shall burn upon it incense of sweet spices; in the morning, in the morning, … should precede an item, … about which only one morning is stated:

And … nothing may be delayed … after the daily afternoon offering but … incense, … lamps, … the Paschal lamb, and one who lacks atonement on Passover eve, … immerses a second time … and he eats his Paschal lamb in the evening.
Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says … even one who lacks atonement on the rest of the days of the year … that he immerses and eats sacrificial food … in the evening.

Granted, according to the first tanna, … The positive … of the Paschal lamb, which … with it … karet … will come and override the positive … of completion. … does not … karet, … However, … Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, … what … is the strength of this positive … than … that positive
Ravina said … Rav Ḥisda said: Here we are dealing with … a bird … a sin-offering. … as … the altar has only … blood.
Rav Pappa said: Even if you say … an animal sin-offering, … brings them up and leaves them overnight on the top of the altar.
But isn’t there … a guilt-offering … Granted, according to Rav Pappa, … is … leave it overnight … However, according to Rav Ḥisda, what can be said, … They say: … sacrificed his guilt-offering.

But isn’t there … a burnt-offering … And if you say … the burnt-offering does not prevent … wasn’t it taught … Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, … says: Just as … his sin-offering and his guilt-offering prevents … so too does … his burnt-offering.

And if you say, … that … offered his burnt-offering; may his burnt-offering be brought before his sin-offering? Wasn’t it taught … and he shall offer that which is for the sin-offering first … what … does the verse state … If it is to teach that … should … prior to the burnt-offering, it is already stated: “And he shall offer the second as a burnt-offering according to the ordinance”
Rather, this is a paradigm … that all sin-offerings should precede all burnt-offerings that come with them. … And we maintain … even the sin-offering of a bird precedes a burnt-offering … animal.
Rava said: … burnt-offering of a leper is different … as the Merciful One says
“And the priest shall offer the burnt-offering” … that has already been offered.

Rav Shemen bar Abba said to Rav Pappa: According to your … that you said he brings them up and leaves them overnight at the top of the altar, do we stand and perform an action for the priests whereby they may come to a mishap. As they … think that … that day, and … they may burn them … He said to him: Priests are vigilant

Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana, and some say it Rav Huna, son of Rav Natan, … to Rav Pappa: But, isn’t … as long as the sacrificial parts … have not been burned … the priests may not eat the meat? As it was taught … might … that the priests would be permitted … the breast and thigh, … prior to burning the sacrificial parts … Therefore, the verse states: “And the priest shall burn the fat upon the altar, … and … then: “The breast shall be for Aaron and his sons.

And, … as long as the priests have not eaten the meat … the owners … have not achieved … atonement, as it was taught … “And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made … teaches that the priests eat, and … the owners … achieve atonement.

He said to him: Since it is impossible … they rendered … as ones that became ritually impure or were lost. … As it was taught … might … if the sacrificial parts became ritually impure or were lost, the priests would not be entitled to the breast and thigh, … the verse states: “And the breast shall be for Aaron and his sons” … in any event

Rav Kahana raised a contradiction: It is written … “Neither may the fat of My festive-offering remain overnight until morning” … that … may not remain overnight … into the morning … but it may remain all through the night. … it is written: “And he shall burn upon it the fat of the peace-offerings” … Upon it you shall complete all the offerings,
raised the objection and he resolved it: … were left over

Rav Safra raised a contradiction before Rav: … it is written: “Neither shall the sacrifice of the feast of Passover be left over until morning” … it may not remain overnight … into the morning … but it may remain all through the night. … However, … it is written: “The burnt-offering of each Shabbat on its own Shabbat … the burnt-offering of a weekday is not offered on Shabbat, and the burnt-offering of a weekday is not offered on a Festival.

said to him: Rav Abba bar Ḥiyya already raised … contradiction before Rabbi Abbahu, and he answered him: Here, … we are dealing with … the fourteenth … occurs on Shabbat, as the fats of a Shabbat … may be sacrificed … on a Festival.

He said to him: Because the fats of Shabbat … may be sacrificed on a Festival, shall we arise and say that this verse is written … with regard to … the fourteenth … that occurs on Shabbat, … He said to him: Leave … this verse alone, since it compels itself to be established

MISHNA: The Paschal lamb that … slaughtered not for its … purpose, … received … carried … sprinkled … not for the purpose … or … for its … purpose and not for its … purpose; or not for its … purpose and for its … purpose; … disqualified.

How … for its … purpose and not for its … purpose? … for the purpose of the Paschal lamb and for the purpose of a peace-offering. … not for its … purpose and for its … purpose? … for the purpose of a peace-offering and for the purpose of a Paschal lamb.
GEMARA: Rav Pappa raised a dilemma: … Did we learn … one rite, … Or, did we learn … two rites,
we learn … with regard to one rite, … is … Rabbi Yosei, who said that a person is held … even for the conclusion of his statement?
For if … Rabbi Meir, … he said: Hold … the first expression,
Or perhaps … teach … two rites. … even … Rabbi Meir, who said … hold … the first expression, this … applies … in one rite, but in two rites … he concedes that it disqualifies.

They said: To which … does this … If we say … for a different purpose and … for its own purpose, … whether … during one rite or during two rites, whether according to … Rabbi Meir or according to … Rabbi Yosei, … is disqualified from the first … as also Rabbi Yosei holds that a person is held accountable even for the conclusion of his statement. … Rather, … for its own purpose and … for a different purpose; what

Come … hear … A Paschal lamb … sacrificed for a different purpose, and he received … and carried … and sprinkled … for a different purpose, … What … are the circumstances? If we say … as it was taught, … why do I need … he intended … all of them, … disqualified from the first

Rather, is this not what … is teaching: A Paschal lamb … slaughtered for a different purpose, or alternatively, … slaughtered it for its own purpose, but received … and carried … and sprinkled … for a different purpose, or alternatively, he slaughtered it, and received … and carried … for its own purpose, but sprinkled … for a different purpose, … it is … two rites,

say the latter clause … For its own purpose and for a different purpose. … What are the circumstances? If we say … during two … rites, that is … the first clause … Rather, must we not … during one rite, … according to … Rabbi Yosei, who said that a person is held accountable even for the conclusion of his statement?

No, actually … during two … rites, and … The first clause … one is standing at … the slaughter and thinking about slaughtering … alternatively, he is standing … sprinkling … and thinking about sprinkling

The latter clause … one is standing at … the slaughter and thinking about sprinkling … he said: I am hereby slaughtering the Paschal lamb for its own purpose, … to sprinkle its blood for a different purpose. And … teaches us … that one can intend from one rite to another rite, … And this was the question … by Rav Pappa

Come … hear … Or for a different purpose and for its own purpose, … is disqualified. … What … are the circumstances? If we say … about two rites, … Now … you … said that … for its own purpose, and … for a different purpose, … is disqualified, is it necessary to say … for a different purpose, and … for its own purpose?
Rather, isn’t … during one rite? And since the last clause … about one rite, the earlier clause … also … about one rite,
No, actually … about two rites, and by right it was not necessary … Since … taught … for its own purpose and for a different purpose, it also taught … for a different purpose and for its own purpose.

Come … hear … If … slaughtered … for … who cannot eat it, … for … not registered for it, … for uncircumcised or ritually impure … it is disqualified. Here, … it is obvious … during one rite, … And since the latter clause, … about one rite, the first clause, … also … about one rite,
Are … comparable? … this … as it is, and that … as it is. The latter clause, … about one rite, … the first clause, … either about one rite … or about two rites

Come … hear … for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it, it is valid. … What … are the circumstances? If we say … during two … rites, … then the reason … is that he had the … intention at … sprinkling, … because there is no intent concerning those who can eat it during the sprinkling.

But … during one rite, such as the slaughter, during which intent with regard to those who will eat … is effective, … is disqualified. … for we maintain that … some of those who are to eat … not disqualified.
Rather, doesn’t it … one rite, … And since the latter clause … one rite, the first clause, … also … one rite,
Are … comparable? … this … as it is and that … as it is. … the latter clause … about one rite, … the first clause, … either about one rite or about two rites.

A dilemma was raised before … A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered on the rest of the days of the year … for its own purpose and for a different purpose, what is its … Does … for a different purpose come and nullify … for its own purpose … make it valid, or not?

When Rav Dimi came … he said: I raised this question in the presence of Rabbi Yirmeya … Since … for its own purpose validates it at its proper time, … and … for a different purpose validates it not at its proper time, … Just … for its own purpose, which validates it at its proper time, does not nullify … for a different purpose, … so too, … for a different purpose, which validates it not at its proper time, does not nullify … for its own purpose, and it is disqualified.

And … said to me: No, … If you say … for a different purpose, … because … applies to all offerings, … can you … say … about … for its own purpose … that does not apply to all offerings but to the Paschal lamb alone?

What … about … Rava said: A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered on the rest of the days of the year … for its own purpose and for a different purpose is valid. … In an … undetermined … stands … for its own purpose, … But nevertheless, when he slaughters it for a different purpose, it is valid.

Apparently, … for a different purpose comes and nullifies … for its own purpose; … also … when … slaughters … for its own purpose and for a different purpose, … for a different purpose … comes and nullifies … for its own purpose.

Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rava: Perhaps … where … said … is different from … where he did not say … for those who can eat it and those who cannot eat it, it is valid, but wherever he slaughters it only for the sake of those who cannot eat it, it is disqualified. Now, why … Surely in an … undetermined … stands … for those who can eat it. … Rather, … where … said … is different from … where he did not say … So too, … where he … said … is different from … where he did not say

said to him: Are … comparable? Granted, there, … as long as … did not uproot … at … slaughter, in an … undetermined … it certainly stands … for its own purpose; … But here, … in an … undetermined … does it stand … for those who … eat it?
perhaps these will withdraw and others will come and register for it. For we learned … register … and withdraw from it until it is slaughtered.

A dilemma was raised before … a Paschal lamb that one slaughtered on the rest of the days of the year with a change of owner, … what is its … Is a change of owner like a change of sanctity? … And it validates it, … Or, … not,

Rav Pappa said: I raised this question in the presence of Rava … Since a change in sanctity invalidates it … in its proper time, … and a change in owner, … invalidates it in its proper time, … Just as a change in sanctity, which invalidates it in its proper time, validates it … after its proper time, a change in owner, which invalidates it in its proper time, also validates it … after its proper time.
And … said to me: No, … If you say … about a change in sanctity, … because the disqualification it … is in … itself, … and it applies to all four of the rites,

And … applies after death. … it applies to communal … as it does to … an individual. … can you … say … with regard to a change in owner … Its disqualification is not in … itself; and it does not … to all four rites … and it does not … after death, … and it does not … to communal … as it does to … an individual,

And even though two … are not … accurate … two, at least, are accurate. … For what is different about a change in owner … its disqualification … not being in … itself? Is it that its disqualification is merely … thought? … a change of sanctity is also merely a disqualification … thought

And furthermore, … that which was said, … a change in owner does not … after death, … According to Rav Pineḥas, son of Rav Ami, who said that … a change in owner applies after death, … what is there to say? … at least two … are accurate.

Rather, … Rava said: A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered on the rest of the days of the year with a change of owner is considered like one that does not have an owner. … at its … time … and it is disqualified.

MISHNA: … slaughtered … for … who cannot eat it … those who did not register … people who are uncircumcised or for those who are ritually impure, … is disqualified. … for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it; for those who have registered for it and for those who have not registered for it; for the circumcised and for the uncircumcised; for the ritually impure and for the ritually pure, it is valid,

slaughtered … before midday it is disqualified, as it is stated: … in the afternoon” … slaughtered it before the daily … offering it is valid, as long as another … stirs its blood … until the … daily offering is sprinkled. And if … is sprinkled … it is … valid,

GEMARA: The Sages taught … How so … for those who cannot eat it? … for the sake of a sick person or for the sake of an old person … How so … for those who did not register for it? … one group registered for it, and one slaughtered it for the sake of a different group.
From where are these matters, … As the Sages taught … “According to the number of” teaches that the Paschal lamb is slaughtered only for those who have registered for it.

might … he slaughtered it for those who did not register for it, he would be … as one who has violated a commandment, … valid … the Torah teaches … “according to the number” … “you shall make your count”; the verse repeated it to make … indispensable,
Rabbi … says: … is Aramaic [Sursi], like one who says to his fellow: Slaughter [kos] me this lamb,

We have found … for those who have not registered for it … from where do we … for those who cannot eat it? … the verse says: “According to every man’s eating you shall make your count”; those who eat it are juxtaposed, … to those who are registered

slaughtered … for … circumcised on condition that uncircumcised … achieve atonement through the sprinkling … Rav Ḥisda said: … disqualified. Rabba said: … valid. … Rav Ḥisda said … disqualified … intent … for uncircumcised … at … the sprinkling. Rabba said … valid … intent … uncircumcised … not during the sprinkling.
