And … logically … Since lack of circumcision disqualifies … and … ritual impurity disqualifies … Just as … ritual impurity, partial impurity was not made to be like full impurity, … so too, with lack of circumcision; partial lack of circumcision was not made to be like full lack of circumcision,

Or … go this way … Since lack of circumcision disqualifies … and … time disqualifies … Just as … time, partial … was made to be like … entire … time, … so too, with lack of circumcision; partial lack of circumcision was made to be like full lack of circumcision,

Let us see to which it is similar, … we derive a matter, … that does not apply to all offerings, from … matter, … that does not apply to all offerings, … And … time, which applies to all … offerings, should not … prove

Or, … go this way: We derive a matter, … for which no allowance … from its rule, from a matter, … for which no allowance … from its rule, … And … ritual impurity should not … prove … as … an allowance … from its rule.
the verse states: “This,” … What … “this”? If you say … all … uncircumcised … disqualified, … part of … it is not disqualified, this is derived from … “and all uncircumcised males,”

Rather, is this not what it is teaching: The verse states: “And all uncircumcised … all … uncircumcised is … disqualified, … part … uncircumcised it is not disqualified. And if you say … the same is true of sprinkling … all uncircumcised, … is in any event disqualified; … the verse states: “This,” … It is during slaughter that if all … uncircumcised, … is disqualified; but during sprinkling, even … all … uncircumcised, it is not disqualified.
And if you say: What is the leniency of sprinkling … there is no intent concerning those who may eat … during the sprinkling.

And Rav Ḥisda … on the contrary, … in the opposite direction. The verse states: “And all uncircumcised … all … uncircumcised is … disqualified, … part … uncircumcised, it is not disqualified. … however, … sprinkling, even … part … it is disqualified. And if you say … the same is true of sprinkling … that … is not disqualified unless all … the verse states “this” … slaughter that part of … does not disqualify … but … sprinkling even part of … disqualifies
And if you say: What is the stringency of sprinkling … piggul … is established only during sprinkling.

Rav Ashi strongly objects to this … From where … that this … “and all uncircumcised … means that all … Perhaps this … “and all [kol] uncircumcised … means that any … is uncircumcised. … the Merciful One says … “This,” … is not disqualified unless all of it … uncircumcised, … there is no difference between slaughtering and sprinkling. … Rather, Rav Ashi said: Rav Ḥisda and Rabba

disagree with regard to this verse, … “And it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him” … For him and not for his fellow. … Rabba holds … another … similar to him: Just as he is eligible for atonement … so … another who is eligible for atonement. … to exclude this uncircumcised person, who is not eligible for atonement.
And Rav Ḥisda holds … this uncircumcised person as well, since he is obligated … he is … eligible for atonement … Since if he wants, he can make himself fit
But does Rav Ḥisda accept … since? … But it was said … one who bakes on a Festival for … during the week: Rav Ḥisda said he is flogged … Rabba said he is not flogged.
Rabba said he is not flogged … Since if guests arrive, … fit for him … now too, … fit for him, and he is not flogged. … Rav Ḥisda said he is flogged; we do not state … since.

Granted, … of Rabba and … of Rabba is not difficult. Here, … an action is lacking, … there, … no action is lacking … But … of Rav Ḥisda … of Rav Ḥisda … difficult … They say, … When Rav Ḥisda does not … since, … to be lenient … to be stringent … he does

Mar Zutra, son of Rav Mari, said to Ravina: … teaches: Since lack of circumcision disqualifies … and ritual impurity … disqualifies … Just as … ritual impurity, partial impurity was not made to be like full impurity, so too, … lack of circumcision, partial lack of circumcision was not made to be like full lack of circumcision. … this ritual impurity, what are the circumstances? If you say … the ritual impurity of the people … what … partial impurity was not made to be like full impurity? … that if there are four or five people who are impure and four or five people who are pure, those who are impure do not disqualify those who are pure.

with regard to lack of circumcision as well, … do not disqualify … as we learned … for … circumcised and uncircumcised people, it is valid. What is different … impurity, that … it is obvious to him … And what is different … lack of circumcision, that … he is in doubt
Rather, … impurity of the meat … And what … partial impurity was not made to be like full impurity? … that if one of the limbs became impure, that which became impure we burn and the rest we eat.

How did you establish … impurity of the meat. … say the latter clause … We derive a matter that does not apply to all offerings, … from a matter that does not apply to all offerings, … and … time, which applies to all offerings, should not … prove anything … what … impurity … If we say … impurity of the meat, why … it does not apply to all offerings?

Rather, it is obvious … impurity of the people … And what … it does not apply to all offerings? … that with regard to all offerings, an uncircumcised person and one who is ritually impure … send their offerings … however, with regard to the Paschal lamb, an uncircumcised person and one who is impure cannot send their offerings. … the first clause … impurity of the meat, while the latter clause … impurity of the people.
said to … Yes, … arguing from the … category of impurity,

And if you wish, say … The latter clause … also … impurity of … meat. And what is … it does not apply to all offerings? … that with regard to all offerings, whether the fats … have become impure and the meat … remains, … the meat has become impure and the fats remain, … may sprinkle the blood,
the Paschal lamb, … the fats have become impure and the meat remains … may sprinkle the blood; … meat has become impure and the fats remain … he may not sprinkle the blood,

How did you establish … impurity of … meat. … say the next clause … We derive a matter, … for which no allowance … from its rule, from a matter, … for which no allowance … from its rule. And … ritual impurity should not … prove … as there are … an allowance … from its rule, … What … If you say
impurity of the meat, where is it permitted … Rather, it is obvious … about impurity of the people. And where is an allowance … from its rule? … in the community;
the first clause … impurity of the meat, … the latter clause … impurity of the people. … Yes, … argues from the … category of impurity

And if you wish, say … entire … impurity of the meat, and where is it permitted … in … impurity of the Paschal lamb, as we learned … A Paschal lamb that comes in impurity, … be eaten in impurity, as from the very outset it came only to be eaten.

Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, raised an objection … a Paschal lamb that has passed its … year, … he slaughtered it at its … time … for its … purpose … and similarly, … he slaughtered another … for the purpose of a Paschal lamb at its … time, … Rabbi Eliezer disqualifies … and Rabbi Yehoshua validates it,
The reason … is … at its … time; … But if it was not … at its … time, it is valid … But why … Let us say: Since … disqualifies … at its … time, … also disqualify … not at its … time.

Rav Pappa said: It is different there … as the verse said: “And you shall say: It is a Passover sacrifice … “it” … as it is, … It, … not … for the purpose of other … and other … not … for its purpose,

At its … time, … is disqualified … for the purpose of other … other … are disqualified … for its purpose, … not at its … time, … for the purpose of other … is valid, other … for its purpose … are … valid.

Rabbi Simlai came before Rabbi Yoḥanan. He said to him: Would the Master teach me the Book of Genealogies? … said to him: Where are you from? He said to him: From Lod. … And where is your … residence? … In Neharde’a. … said to him: … we teach … neither to Lodites nor to Neharde’ans, and certainly … you who … from Lod and your residence is in Neharde’a, … pressured … he agreed

said to him: Teach me … in three months. … took a clod … threw it at him, … said to him: Berurya, wife of Rabbi Meir … daughter of Rabbi Ḥananya ben Teradyon, … learned three hundred halakhot in one day from three hundred Sages, and nonetheless she did not fulfill her responsibility … in three years … And you say … in three months?
When … was taking leave to go, he said to … my teacher, … What is … between … for its … purpose and for a different purpose, … for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it,

He said to him: Since … you are a Torah scholar, come and I will tell you … for its … purpose and for a different purpose, … disqualification is in … itself; … for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it, … disqualification is not in … itself,
for its … purpose and for a different purpose, it is impossible to identify its prohibition; … for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it, it is possible to identify its prohibition.

for its … purpose and for a different purpose applies … in … four rites, … for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it does not … during … four rites, … for its … purpose and for a different purpose … that applies to communal … as … to individual … for those who can eat it and those who cannot eat it does not … to the community as … to an individual.

Rav Ashi said … its disqualification is in … itself and … it is impossible to identify its prohibition are one … thing; … what is the reason that … says … its disqualification is in … itself? … because it is impossible to identify its prohibition,
Rami bar Rav Yuda said … Rav said … From the day the Book of Genealogies was hidden … the strength of the Sages has been weakened, and the light of their eyes has been dimmed,
Mar Zutra said: … from … Azel … to … Azel … bore four hundred camels of expositions

It was taught … Aḥerim say: … first the circumcised people and then the uncircumcised people, … valid. … the uncircumcised people … the circumcised people, it is disqualified. … What is different … the circumcised people … the uncircumcised people, … that … is valid? … that … we require that all the people … be uncircumcised, and … is not … the uncircumcised people … the circumcised people, … also … that … we require that all the people … be uncircumcised, and … is not
Let us say that Aḥerim hold that slaughter is not … until the end, … in accordance with … Rava … As Rava said: It is still a dispute,

Therefore, … one put the circumcised people before the uncircumcised people, … circumcised people applies … uncircumcised people does not apply. … one put the uncircumcised people before the circumcised people, … uncircumcised people applies, … circumcised people does not apply.

Rabba said: No, … Actually, Aḥerim hold that slaughter is … from beginning to end, and with what are we dealing here? … where one decided in his mind … for both of them, both circumcised and uncircumcised people, and he verbally expressed … For uncircumcised people, but did not have a chance to say: For circumcised people, before the slaughter was … finished … For uncircumcised people. And it is with regard to this … that they disagree: Rabbi Meir, … holds that we do not require that one’s mouth and heart be the same; … And the Rabbis hold that we require that his mouth and heart be the same.

But does Rabbi Meir hold that we require that his mouth and heart be the same? … raises a contradiction … one who intended to say … teruma, but he … said … tithe; … tithe but … said teruma; … I will not enter this house, but … said: That … I will not derive benefit from this person, but he said: From that … he has not said anything until his mouth and heart are the same.

Rather, Abaye said … The first clause … he said: … the first … for circumcised people and the second … even for uncircumcised people, so that in the second … even circumcised people are included. … The latter clause … he said: … the first … for uncircumcised people … the second … for circumcised people, so that in the first … circumcised people are not included,

And Rabbi Meir follows … reasoning, as he says … piggul status can be conferred … at half of what renders it permitted. … And the Rabbis … follow … reasoning, as they say … piggul status cannot be conferred at half of what permits

MISHNA: One who slaughters the Paschal lamb with leavened bread … violates a negative commandment, … Rabbi Yehuda says: Even … the daily … offering … Rabbi Shimon says: … the Paschal lamb on the fourteenth … for its … purpose … is liable; … for a different purpose he is exempt. And … all other offerings … whether … for their … purpose or … for a different purpose, he is exempt.

And during the festival … for its … purpose he is exempt. … for a different purpose … he is liable … And … all other offerings … whether … for their … purpose … for a different purpose, he is liable. … with the exception of a sin-offering that he slaughtered for a different purpose
GEMARA: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: One is never liable … unless the leavened bread belongs to the one who slaughters … or to the one who sprinkles

to one of the members of the group; … only if … is with him in the Temple courtyard … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … even if … is not with him in the Temple courtyard. With regard to what … they disagree? If you say … they disagree … “with” … next to, … that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish holds that “with” … next to, … and Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that … “with,” we do not require … next to … they have already disagreed about this once
As we learned … one who slaughters a thanks-offering inside … its bread, … is outside the wall, the bread has not become sanctified,

What … outside the wall? Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … outside the wall of Beit Pagei, … but … outside the wall of the Temple courtyard, it has been sanctified, as we do not require … “with” … next to … Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish … said: Even … outside the wall of the Temple courtyard, it has not been sanctified. Apparently, … we require … “with” … next to
Rather, … they disagree about an uncertain warning. … they also disagreed about this once

it was stated … an oath that I will eat this loaf today, and the day passed and he did not eat it, Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish both said … he is not flogged … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: He is not flogged because it is a prohibition whose … does not involve an action, … for any prohibition whose … does not involve an action one is not flogged; however, an uncertain warning is considered a … warning.

And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: He is not flogged because it is an uncertain warning, and an uncertain warning is not considered a warning. … But for a prohibition whose … does not involve an action one is flogged.

They say … Actually, … they disagree about … “with” … next to, and it is necessary … As, if they disagreed … with regard to leaven, I would have said … it is … with regard to that … that Rabbi Yoḥanan said that … “with,” we do not require … next to … because it is a prohibition, and wherever it is, it is.

However, with regard to sanctification of the bread, it becomes sanctified only inside … say that … concedes to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish that we require … “with” … next to … if it is inside, it is sanctified; and if not, it is not sanctified. … just as it is … a vessel used in the … service, … it is necessary

And had we been taught … with regard to sanctification of the bread, I would have said that … in this … did Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish say that we require … “with” … next to it, … that if it is inside … it is sanctified; and if not, it is not sanctified. But with regard to leavened bread, he concedes to Rabbi Yoḥanan that … “with,” we do not require … next to … for it is a prohibition and wherever it is, it is. … it is necessary

Rav Oshaya asked Rabbi Ami … the slaughterer does not have … but one of the members of the group does have, what is … said to him: Is it written: You shall not offer … with your leavened bread, … It is written: “You shall not offer with leavened bread”

said to … If so, even if someone at the end of the world … also … said to him … the verse says: “You shall not offer,” … “Neither shall … be left … “You shall not offer with leavened bread” … those who are governed … “neither shall be left over,”
Rav Pappa said: Therefore, … the priest who burns the fats … transgresses the negative commandment … Since he is included in … leaving over sacrificial parts

it was taught … in accordance with … Rav Pappa: One who slaughters the Paschal lamb with leavened bread … transgresses a negative commandment. When? When … to the slaughterer, or to the one who sprinkles … or to one of the members of the group. … to someone at the end of the world, he is not bound to him, … And … he slaughters … or he sprinkles … or he burns … liable. But one who pinches … a bird, … on the fourteenth … he does not transgress anything.

raises a contradiction … One who slaughters the Paschal lamb with leavened bread … transgresses a negative commandment. Rabbi Yehuda says: Even … the daily … offering … They said to him: They stated … only with regard to the Paschal lamb. When … When the slaughterer, or the one who sprinkles … or one of the members of the group has … If someone at the end of the world had … he is not bound to him.

And … he slaughters … or he sprinkles … or he pinches … or he sprinkles … liable. But one who scoops a handful … from a meal-offering … does not transgress a negative commandment, … One who burns the sacrificial parts … does not transgress a negative commandment.
a contradiction between … pinching … pinching. … a contradiction … burning … burning.
And according to your reasoning … ask about … itself, as … it teaches: They said … only to the Paschal lamb, and then it teaches … he slaughters … or he sprinkles … or he pinches … or he sprinkles

Rather, … this … and that … Rabbi Shimon. … there is no contradiction between … pinching … pinching: Here, … to the fourteenth … there, … the intermediate days of the festival … And … this … and that … Rabbi Shimon,
no contradiction between … burning … burning, … is … tanna’im … There is one who compares burning to slaughtering, … and there is one who does not compare

Rabbi Yehuda says: … even for … the daily … offering … What is the reason for Rabbi Yehuda’s … He … said to you … “My sacrifice” … the sacrifice that is designated to Me; and what is it? … the daily offering,

Rabbi Shimon says: On the fourteenth … the Paschal lamb … What is the reason for Rabbi Shimon’s … As it is written: “My sacrifice [zivḥi],” “My sacrifice [zivḥi],” two times, … read: A sacrifice [zevaḥ], … My sacrifices [zevaḥai].

To … what halakha does the Merciful One divide them … and not … write: My sacrifices? … to say … at the time when there is a sacrifice, … one is not liable for My sacrifices. … at a time when there is no sacrifice, … one is liable … My sacrifices
during … the Festival for its … purpose … one is exempt … The reason … that … for a different purpose; but … without … intent … exempt,
Why … a Paschal lamb … during the rest of the days of the year … a peace-offering? … Learn from this that a Paschal lamb … on the rest of the days of the year requires uprooting,

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Gamda said: … it emerged from the group, … and they said … where the owners … were ritually impure … by a corpse … and they were deferred to the second Passover. … presumably stands … as a Paschal lamb,

MISHNA: The Paschal lamb was slaughtered in three groups, … as it is stated: “And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it … Assembly, congregation, and Israel. … The first group … entered, … the Temple courtyard became filled … they closed the doors of the Temple courtyard. They sounded uninterrupted, broken, and uninterrupted … blasts,

The priests stood in rows … and in their hands … bowls [bezikhin] of silver and bowls of gold … a row entirely … silver … and a row entirely … gold … were not mixed … The bowls did not have … bases … perhaps … set them down … and … the blood would congeal

An Israelite would slaughter … and a priest would receive … hand it to another … and the other … to another. … receive a full … and return … an empty … priest who was closest to the altar would sprinkle a single sprinkling … against the base

The first group exited … and the second group entered; the second group left … and the third group entered. As it was done by the first … so was it done by the second and third … recite hallel. If they finished … they … a second time, and if they … a second time, they … a third time, although … they never … a third time, … Rabbi Yehuda says: The third group never reached … “I love that the Lord hears … because its people were few

As it was done during the week, so was it done on Shabbat; only that … the priests would rinse the Temple courtyard, … contrary to the wishes of the Sages, … Rabbi Yehuda says: … would fill a cup with the blood … that was … mixed … sprinkle it with a single sprinkling upon the altar. But the Rabbis did not agree with

How would one suspend and flay … Iron hooks [unkelayot] were secured into the walls and pillars, and upon them one would suspend … and flay … anyone lacked a place … to suspend and flay … there were thin, smooth rods there, … he would place on his … shoulder and on another’s shoulder, and … he would suspend … Rabbi Eliezer says: … the fourteenth

occurred on Shabbat, … he would rest his hand on another’s shoulder and the other’s hand on his … shoulder and suspend … and flay … He would tear … and remove its sacrificial parts, … He would place … in a large basin [mageis] and burn them on the altar.
the first group would exit and remain on the Temple Mount; the second … the rampart, … and the third … would stand in its place … it became dark, they would … go out and roast their Paschal lambs,

GEMARA: Rabbi Yitzḥak said: The Paschal lamb is slaughtered only in three groups of … thirty people … What is the reason … Assembly, congregation, and Israel, … We are uncertain … at the same time … one after another.

Therefore, … we require three groups of thirty people … As, if … at the same time, … have … and if … one after another, … have … Therefore, … even fifty … suffice. … Thirty enter and perform … ten … enter and ten … leave … and … ten … enter and ten … leave
the first group entered, … It was stated … Abaye said: We learned … closed by themselves. Rava said: We learned … that … would close

What is … between them? The … between them is … whether we rely on a miracle. Abaye said: We learned … that the doors closed by themselves; as many … as entered, entered, and we rely on a miracle … Rava said: We learned … that … close … and we do not rely on a miracle

And that which we learned … Rabbi Yehuda said: Heaven forbid that Akavya ben Mahalalel was banned; … the Temple courtyard would not close on any man from Israel … wisdom and fear of sin as Akavya ben Mahalalel; Abaye … explain … according to his opinion, and Rava … explain … according to his opinion. Abaye … explain … according to his opinion … No man from Israel was in the Temple courtyard when it closed by itself … wisdom and fear of sin as Akavya ben Mahalalel. Rava, … explain … according to his opinion … No … from Israel was in the Temple courtyard when they closed it … wisdom and fear of sin as Akavya ben Mahalalel.
The Sages taught: No one was ever crushed … in the Temple courtyard, except for one Passover in the days of Hillel when an old man was crushed, and they called … the Passover of the crushed.

The Sages taught: Once, King Agrippa wished to set his eyes on the multitudes [ukhlosin] of Israel … said to the High Priest: Set your eyes on the Paschal lambs; … took a kidney from each one, … and six hundred thousand pairs of kidneys were found there, double … those who left Egypt. … excluded those who were ritually impure or at a great distance, … and there was not a single Paschal lamb that did not have more than ten people registered for it. They called that … the Passover of the crowded,
take a kidney? … he have to burn it … He … subsequently he burned them. … Isn’t it written: “And … shall burn it … he must not mix … fats of this … with … another;
He subsequently burned them one by one … Wasn’t it taught … shall burn them … that all … at the same time? Rather, … merely … seizure; … he took it from them until they brought him something else

the priests stood in rows … What is the reason … If you say … perhaps … would take a gold … and … return a silver … Here, too, … perhaps … would take a two-hundred- … and … return a … Rather, … that this … is … more attractive.

the bowls did not have … bases. … the Sages taught … None of the bowls in the Temple had … bases … with the exception of the bowls of frankincense … the showbread, … perhaps … would rest them on the bread and the bread would break.

An Israelite would slaughter … and a priest would receive … Is it not sufficient … not an Israelite … teaches us this … itself, that … slaughter … by a non-priest … is valid. … the priest receives … comes to teach us that from receiving and onward … a commandment … upon the priesthood,

pass … to another … Learn from this that carrying without walking, … is … carrying … Perhaps … would move a little … Rather, what does this … teach us? … It teaches us … “in the multitude of people is the king’s glory”
receive a full … and return an empty … But the opposite … not … supports … Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, as Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: One must not postpone … mitzvot.
the priest who was closest to the altar … Who is the tanna … the Paschal lamb … sprinkling … Rav Ḥisda said: It is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

As it was taught … Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says: … you shall sprinkle their blood upon the altar and you shall burn their fat … It is not stated: Its blood, but … “their blood.” … it is not stated: Its fat, but … “their fat.” … teaches with regard to the firstborn … the tithed animal and the Paschal lamb, … that they … require placement of their blood and sacrificial parts on the altar,

From where do we … requires … base? Rabbi Elazar said: This is derived … sprinkling … sprinkling … with regard to a burnt-offering. Here, it is written: “You shall sprinkle their blood upon the altar;” there, it is written … and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall sprinkle its blood round about upon the altar” … Just as … burnt-offering must … a base, so too, … Paschal lamb must … a base.
And from where do we … the burnt-offering itself … the verse said: … at the base of the altar of the burnt-offering, … Apparently, … a burnt-offering requires … the base,
the first group exited, … It was taught … It was called the lazy group … But it would not have been sufficient without this … What, … should … have done?

Nonetheless, … should have hurried themselves … As … was taught … Rabbi … says: The world cannot … without a perfume merchant or without a tanner [bursi], … fortunate is he whose profession is … perfume merchant, … woe to him whose profession is … tanner. … the world cannot … without males or without females; … fortunate is he whose children are males, … woe to him whose children are females.

in the same manner that … was performed during the week, … Contrary to the wishes of whom? … Rav Ḥisda said: It was contrary to the wishes of Rabbi Eliezer, … As, if … the Rabbis, … don’t they say … rabbinic decree? And … rabbinic decrees … not … in the Temple.

What is … As it was taught … One who milks … or sets milk to curdle … or makes cheese … a dried fig-bulk; one who sweeps … or sprinkles … or removes honeycombs, … unwittingly on Shabbat, he is liable … a sin-offering, … intentionally on a Festival, he is flogged with forty … the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Rabbis say … Both this, … and that, … are … only due to rabbinic decrees.

Rav Ashi said: You can even say … contrary to the wishes of the Rabbis, … and … is … Rabbi Natan. As it was taught … Rabbi Natan says … a rabbinic prohibition … necessary … they permitted … a rabbinic prohibition … not … necessary … they did not permit

Rabbi Yehuda says … would fill a cup … the blood that was mixed … It was taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: He would fill a cup with the mixed blood, so that if … the blood of one … was spilled, this … would render … fit.

said to Rabbi Yehuda: But … had not been received in a vessel … How do they know … Rather, this is what … said to … Perhaps … had not been received in a vessel … said to them: I, too, spoke only about … that had been received in a vessel.
How does … know … Priests are vigilant, … But if they are … vigilant, why did … spill? … Owing to the speed with which they worked, … spilled.

But isn’t blood squeezed … mixed with it? … Rabbi Yehuda … to his … reasoning, as he says … blood squeezed … is proper blood … As it was taught … blood squeezed … a warning, … Rabbi Yehuda says: … karet,
Didn’t Rabbi Elazar say … Rabbi Yehuda concedes with regard to atonement … does not make atonement? As it is stated: … for it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of life”
blood with which life leaves … makes atonement … blood with which life does not leave … does not make atonement. … Rather, Rabbi Yehuda … to his … reasoning, as he said: Blood does not nullify blood.

It was taught … Rabbi Yehuda said to the Rabbis: According to your statement … why did they plug … the Temple courtyard … They said to him: It is praiseworthy of the sons of Aaron, … to walk in blood up to their ankles,
Doesn’t … interpose … is moist and … does not interpose. As it was taught … blood, ink, milk, and honey, … dry, … interpose … moist, they do not interpose.

But don’t their garments become soiled? And we learned … garments were soiled and he performed … rite … his rite is invalid, … And if you say that they raised their garments … Wasn’t it taught … his linen garment [middo]” … middo … according to his measure [kemiddato], … not too short and not too long? … while carrying the … limbs to the ramp … which is not … a rite,

And … not … But from the fact that … requires priesthood, … it is … a rite. As it was taught … “And the priest shall bring it all … upon the altar; … this … the carrying of the limbs to the ramp. Rather, … while carrying wood to the wood pile … which is not a rite.
how did they walk … while carrying the limbs to the ramp and while carrying the blood … They would walk on platforms

how one would suspend and flay … he would tear it … remove its sacrificial parts … place them in a large basin in order to burn them. … Is that to say that he himself, … would burn them? … say: In order to burn them on the altar,
The first group exited … It was taught … Each and every one would place his Paschal lamb in its hide and cast … behind him … Rav Ilish said: … Arab merchants [tayya’ut].

MISHNA: These … matters … Paschal lamb … override Shabbat, … Its slaughter, the sprinkling of its blood, the cleaning of its intestines and the burning of its fats … However, its roasting and the washing of its intestines, … do not override Shabbat; … Carrying … bringing it from outside the Shabbat limit and cutting off its wart do not override Shabbat, … Rabbi Eliezer says: … override

Rabbi Eliezer said: … not … an a fortiori inference? If slaughter, which is … as a … labor, … overrides Shabbat … these … due to rabbinic decree, should they not override Shabbat? Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: … a Festival proves … permitted on it … as labor, … and … it is forbidden … on it … due to rabbinic decree.

Rabbi Eliezer said to him: What is this, Yehoshua? … What proof … optional … to a mitzva? … Rabbi Akiva responded and said … Sprinkling … proves … for it is … for … a mitzva, … and it is … due to rabbinic decree, and … it does not override Shabbat, … So, too, you should not be surprised about these … that although they are … for … a mitzva and they are … due to rabbinic decree, they do not override Shabbat.

Rabbi Eliezer said to him: … With regard to this … I infer … If slaughter, which is … labor, overrides Shabbat, is it not right that sprinkling … which is … due to rabbinic decree, should override Shabbat?

Rabbi Akiva said to … Or … reverse … If, … sprinkling … which is … due to rabbinic decree, does not override Shabbat, … slaughter, which is … as a … labor, is it not right that it should not override Shabbat? … Rabbi Eliezer said to him: Akiva, … You have … uprooted what is written in the Torah: … in its appointed time” … whether it is a weekday or Shabbat.

said to … My teacher, bring me an appointed time … for these … like the appointed time … with respect to slaughter. … Rabbi Akiva stated a principle: Any prohibited labor … that can be performed on the eve of Shabbat does not override Shabbat; slaughter, which cannot be performed on the eve of Shabbat, overrides Shabbat.

GEMARA: The Sages taught … occurs … This law was forgotten by the sons of Beteira, … The fourteenth … once occurred on Shabbat, … they forgot and did not know whether the Paschal lamb overrides Shabbat or not. They said: Is there any person who knows whether the Paschal lamb overrides Shabbat or not? They said to them: There is a certain man … who came up from Babylonia, and Hillel the Babylonian is his name. … he served the two … eminent … of the generation, Shemaya and Avtalyon, and … knows whether the Paschal lamb overrides Shabbat or not. … sent … and called for him. They said to him: Do you know whether the Paschal lamb overrides Shabbat or not? He said to them: Have we … one Paschal lamb during the year that overrides Shabbat? Do we not have many more than two hundred Paschal lambs, … during the year that override Shabbat?

They said to him: From where do you … He said to them: “Its appointed time” is stated with regard to the Paschal lamb and “its appointed time” is … stated with regard to the daily offering, … Just as … “its appointed time,” which is stated with regard to the daily offering, … overrides Shabbat, so too “its appointed time,” which is stated with regard to the Paschal lamb, … overrides Shabbat.

And furthermore, it is an a fortiori … If the daily offering, … is not punishable by karet, overrides Shabbat, is it not right that the Paschal lamb, … is punishable by karet, should override Shabbat?

they immediately seated him at the head and appointed him Nasi over them, and he expounded the laws of Passover that entire day. … he began rebuking them [mekanteran] them with words. He said to them: What caused … to you, that I should come up from Babylonia and become Nasi over you? … the laziness in you … you did not serve the two … eminent … of the generation … Shemaya and Avtalyon.

They said to … Our teacher, … forgot and did not bring a knife on the eve of Shabbat … what is … He said to them: I … heard this halakha … but I have forgotten … But leave … to the Jewish people; if they are not prophets … they are the sons of prophets,

The next day, … one whose Paschal offering was a lamb … stuck it in its wool; … one whose Paschal offering was a goat, … stuck it between its horns. … saw the incident and remembered the halakha … and said: This … I received from the mouths of Shemaya and Avtalyon,

The Master said … “Its appointed time” is stated with regard to the Paschal lamb and “its appointed time” is stated with regard to the daily offering. Just as “its appointed time,” which is stated with regard to the daily offering, … overrides Shabbat, so too “its appointed time,” which is stated with regard to the Paschal lamb, … overrides Shabbat. And from where do we … that the daily offering itself overrides Shabbat? If we say because “in its appointed time” is written in its regard, “in its appointed time” is also written with regard to the Paschal lamb.

Rather, … “its appointed time,” … does not indicate to … Here too, … “its appointed time” does not indicate to him … Rather, … the verse … states: “The burnt-offering of Shabbat on its Shabbat, beside the continual burnt-offering … it may be inferred that the daily burnt-offering is brought … on Shabbat.

The Master said … And furthermore, it is an a fortiori inference: If the daily offering, … is not punishable by karet, overrides Shabbat, is it not right that the Paschal lamb, … is punishable by karet, should override Shabbat? … there is room to refute … What … the daily offering … That it is frequent, … and … consumed … first told them the a fortiori inference, but they refuted it … and then he told them the verbal analogy,

But since … learned … verbal analogy … why do I … an a fortiori … Rather, he said it for them, … Granted, you did not learn the verbal analogy … one may not expound a verbal analogy on one’s own. … But an a fortiori … which one can derive on one’s own, you should have derived … They said to him: It is a faulty a fortiori
The Master said … The next day, one whose Paschal offering was a lamb stuck … in its wool, … goat stuck it between its horns

But … he did work with consecrated … in accordance with … Hillel, as it was taught … They said about Hillel … no one ever misused his burnt-offering. … rather he would bring it … unconsecrated … to the Temple courtyard and … consecrate it, and … place his hand on its … and slaughter it.

how could they consecrate the Paschal offerings … on Shabbat? Didn’t we learn … One may not consecrate … take a valuation vow, consecrate … or separate terumot and tithes. They stated all of these … a Festival, … an a fortiori inference … on Shabbat

This … applies only to obligatory … that do not have a set time … But obligatory … that have a set time, … one may consecrate … For Rabbi Yoḥanan said: A person may consecrate his Paschal lamb on Shabbat and his Festival peace-offering on the Festival.

But is he not driving a laden animal? … driving a laden animal in an unusual manner, … Even driving a laden animal in an unusual manner … granted that there is no prohibition by Torah law, … there is at least a rabbinic prohibition.

This is … what … asked … an act that is permitted by Torah law, and a rabbinic decree stands before it … what … uprooting … in an unusual manner, in a situation … a mitzva? … said to them: I … heard this halakha but I have forgotten … But leave … to the Jewish people … if they are not prophets, they are the sons of prophets.

Rav Yehuda said that Rav said: Anyone who acts haughtily, if he is a … scholar, his wisdom departs from him; … if he is a prophet, his prophecy departs from him. … if he is a … scholar, his wisdom departs from him … from Hillel, for the Master said … began to rebuke them with words. … saying to them: I … heard this halakha, but I have forgotten … if he is a prophet his prophecy departs from him … from Deborah, as it is written: “The villagers ceased, they ceased in Israel, until I, Deborah, arose, I arose a mother in Israel” … as it is written … “Awake, awake, Deborah; awake, awake, utter a song”

Reish Lakish said: Any person who becomes angry, if he is a … scholar, his wisdom departs from him, … if he is a prophet, his prophecy departs from him. … if he is a … scholar his wisdom departs from him … from Moses, as it is written: “And Moses became angry with the officers of the host, … And … it is written … “And Elazar the priest said to the men of war who went to the battle: This is the statute of the law, which the Lord commanded Moses” … by inference that … had become hidden from Moses due to

if he is a prophet, his prophecy departs from him, … from Elisha, as it is written … “Were it not that I have regard for the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judea, I would not look toward you, nor see you” … and it is … written: “But now bring me a minstrel; and it came to pass when the minstrel played that the hand of the Lord came upon him”

Rabbi Mani bar Patish said: Whoever becomes angry, even if greatness has been apportioned to him from heaven, he is lowered … From where do we … From Eliab, … as it is stated: “And Eliab’s anger burned against David and he said: Why did you come down, and with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your insolence and the evil of your heart, for you have come down to see the battle” … And when Samuel went to anoint him … concerning all of … it is written: “The Lord has not chosen this one” … whereas with regard to Eliab it is written: “And the Lord said to Samuel: Look not at his appearance, nor at the height of his stature, for I have rejected him” … by inference that until now He had loved him,

We have found … the daily offering and the Paschal lamb override Shabbat. From where do we … that they … override ritual impurity? … They say: Just as … Paschal lamb is derived from … the daily offering in regard to … Shabbat, so too the … daily offering is derived from … the Paschal lamb in regard to ritual impurity;

And … the Paschal lamb itself, from where do we … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: For the verse states: … Any man … who shall be impure by reason of a corpse, … a … individual … deferred to the second Pesaḥ … but the … community … is not deferred to the second Pesaḥ; rather, they observe … in … ritual impurity.
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said to Rabbi Yoḥanan: … say … individual … deferred to the second Pesaḥ, … the community has no remedy, neither on the first Pesaḥ nor on the second Pesaḥ.

Rather, Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish … said … from here: … that they send out from the camp any leper and any zav and anyone impure by reason of a corpse” … Let … say … those who are ritually impure due to a corpse, and not say … zavin and lepers, and I would say … If those ritually impure due to a corpse, … are sent out … zavin and lepers … all the more so … not
Rather, … you have a time when zavin and lepers are sent out … but those who are ritually impure due to … a corpse are not sent out. And what is this … a Paschal lamb is brought in impurity,

Abaye said: If so, … let us also say … should … say zav and those ritually impure due to a corpse and not say leper, and I … say … zav is sent out, … a leper, … all the more so … not … Rather, … you have a time when … lepers are sent out, but zavin and those ritually impure due to … a corpse are not sent out. And what is this … a Paschal offering is brought in impurity,

And if you say that it is … so … didn’t we learn … a Paschal lamb is brought in … ritual impurity, zavim and zavot, menstruating women and women after childbirth, … may not eat from it; but if they ate, they are exempt
Rather, Abaye said: Actually, … from the first verse … If so, … the Merciful One should have written: “Any man who shall be impure.” Why do I … “by reason of a corpse”?

And if you say … these … “by reason of a corpse” come for this … it is … one who is ritually impure due to … a corpse that is deferred to the second Pesaḥ but the rest of those who are impure are not … For wasn’t it taught … might … only those ritually impure due to … a corpse and those on a distant journey observe the second Pesaḥ. From where … zavin, lepers and those who had relations with menstruating women … Therefore, the verse states: “Any man,” … why do I … “by reason of a corpse” that the Merciful One writes,

Rather, this is … is saying: … individual … are deferred to the second Pesaḥ, but the … community … is not deferred to the second Pesaḥ; rather, they observe … in … ritual impurity. And when … the community observes … in … impurity, … ritually impure due to … a corpse, … but … other … impurity, they do not observe
Rav Ḥisda said: A leper, … who went in beyond his boundary, … is … exempt … as it is stated: … he shall dwell in isolation, his dwelling shall be outside the camp”
“He shall dwell in isolation” … he shall dwell alone, … “His dwelling shall be outside the camp” … the verse has transmuted … into a positive mitzva.

An objection was raised against … A leper, … who went in beyond his boundary, … with forty … zavin and zavot, … who went in beyond their boundaries, … with forty … And one who is ritually impure due to … a corpse is permitted to enter … the Levite camp.

And not only did they say that one who is ritually impure due to a corpse … but even a corpse itself … as it is stated: “And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him” … “with him” … within his boundary,

This is … tanna’im, for it was taught … “He shall dwell in isolation” … he shall dwell alone, … that other ritually impure people, … should not dwell with him. … might … zavin and those who are ritually impure due to … a corpse are sent to one camp, … Therefore, the verse states: … and they shall defile not their camps … give a camp for this one and a camp for that one; … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

Rabbi Shimon says: It is not necessary … surely … says: … that they send out from the camp any leper and any zav and anyone impure by reason of a corpse” … Let … say … those who are ritually impure due to a corpse, and not say … those impure as a zav, and I … say … If those ritually impure due to a corpse are sent out … all the more so … not … zavin … why is a zav stated? To give him a second camp,

Let … say … zav, and not say … a leper, and I … say … zavin are sent out, all the more so … not … lepers … Why … is a leper stated? To give him a third camp … When … says … “He shall dwell alone,” the verse has transmuted … into a positive command.

What is the stringency of a zav over one who is ritually impure due to a corpse? That … impurity … issues out upon him from his … body, … on the contrary, … one who is ritually impure due to a corpse is more severe, as he requires sprinkling … third and seventh

the verse states … “impure” … “and anyone impure.” … to include one who is ritually impure due to … a creeping animal. … and … a zav is more severe than one who is ritually impure due to … a creeping animal.
And what is his stringency? … As we have said, … on the contrary, … a creeping animal is … severe, for it imparts ritual impurity … through an accident. … They say
In a case like this, … a zav also becomes impure through an accident, in accordance with … Rav Huna, for Rav Huna said: The first sighting of a zav establishes ritual impurity … through an accident.

What is the stringency of a leper over a zav? That … is required to let his hair grow and rend his garments and he is prohibited from marital relations, … on the contrary, … a zav is … severe, for … imparts ritual impurity to that upon which he lies or sits … and he imparts ritual impurity to an earthenware vessel through movement.
The verse states … “zav” … “and any zav,” … to include a person who experienced a seminal emission, … and … a leper is more severe than a person who experienced a seminal emission.
And what is his stringency? … As we said, … On the contrary, … one who experienced a seminal emission is … severe, for he becomes ritually impure … with any amount.

He holds in accordance … Rabbi Natan, as it was taught … Rabbi Natan says in the name of Rabbi Yishmael: … a zav … needs … a blockage of the tip of the … organ. But the Rabbis did not agree with him. … And one who experienced a seminal emission is compared to a zav
why do I … “and any leper”? … it is written “any zav,” it is also written “any leper,”
Rabbi Yehuda … Rabbi Shimon spoke well

He needs that … for that which was taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: … might … if zavin and lepers pushed and entered … courtyard during … a Paschal lamb that is brought in … impurity, … perhaps they would be liable … Therefore the verse states: “That they send out from the camp any leper and any zav and anyone impure by reason of a corpse” … at a time when those impure due to a corpse are sent out, zavin and lepers are sent out … those impure due to a corpse are not sent out, zavin and lepers are not sent out,

The Master said … “zav” … “and any zav” … to include a person who experienced a seminal emission. … supports … Rabbi Yoḥanan, for Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The tunnels … were not sanctified … and a person who experienced a seminal emission is sent outside the two camps
raises an objection … a person who experienced a seminal emission is like … contact with a creeping animal. What, is … not … their … camps, … No, … their impurity,
their impurity? Impurity until evening is … written … about this one, … And impurity until evening is … written about that one, … Rather, is it not … their camps,

No, actually … their impurity, and it teaches us that a person who experienced seminal emission is … the same … as … contact with a creeping animal … Just as contact with a creeping animal imparts ritual impurity through an accident, … so too a person who experienced a seminal emission becomes ritually impure through an accident,
raises an objection:

one who had relations with a menstruating woman is like … one who is ritually impure due to a corpse. With regard to what … If we say … their impurity, … impurity for seven days is … written about this one, … and impurity for seven days is … written about that one,
Rather, is it not … their camps, … And from the … the latter clause … their camps, … the earlier clause … also … their camps, … Are … comparable? This … as it is, and that … as it is;

The Gemara raises an objection … a leper is more severe than a zav and … a zav is more severe than one who is ritually impure … a corpse, … to the exclusion of a person who experienced a seminal emission, for … one who is ritually impure … a corpse is more severe than his

What … to the exclusion … Is … not … he is excluded from the category of a zav and enters the category of one who is ritually impure … a corpse, for … one who is ritually impure … by a corpse is more severe than his … and … he is permitted in the Levite camp.

No, … excluded from the camp of one who is ritually impure … a corpse, and he enters the camp of a zav, … And although … one who is ritually impure … a corpse is more severe than his … and … is permitted in the Levite camp, … we compare him to that to which he is similar.

A tanna taught … before Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi: … “He shall go outside the camp,” this is the camp of the Divine Presence. “He shall not come within the camp,” this is the Levite camp. From here … a person who experienced a seminal emission must go out from two camps.

said to … You have not yet brought him in … you … send him out? … Another version, … You have not yet sent him out … you … bring him in? … Rather, … say … “Outside the camp,” this is the Levite camp. “He shall not come within the camp,” this is the camp of the Divine Presence.

Ravina strongly objects to … Say … this and that … to the camp of the Divine Presence, … that he violates a positive … and a negative … If so, let the verse say … “He shall go outside the camp, he shall not come within,” … Why do I … “the camp”? Conclude from this … to give him a different camp;

cleaning the intestines … What is … cleaning the intestines? Rav Huna said: … that he punctures them with a knife … Rav Ḥiyya bar Rav said: … the secretions of the intestine, which come out through the pressure of the knife

Rabbi Eliezer said: What is Ḥiyya bar Rav’s reason … As it is written: … and the ruins of the fat ones [meḥim] shall wanderers eat” … From where may it be inferred … As Rav Yosef translates … “And the righteous shall inherit the possessions of the wicked.”

“Then shall the lambs feed as in their pasture … kedavram].” Menashya bar Yirmeya said that Rav said: As was said about them … kamedubar bam], … what … “as was said about them”? Abaye said: … “And the ruins of the fat ones shall wanderers eat.” Rava said to him … Granted, were it written … “the ruins … as you said. Now that it is written “and the ruins,” … it states something else,

Rather, Rava said: … in accordance with … Rav Ḥananel said that Rav said. For Rav Ḥananel said that Rav said: In the future, the righteous will resurrect the dead. It is written here: “Then shall the lambs feed [vera’u] as in their pasture,” … and it is written there: … let them feed [yiru] in Bashan and Gilad as in the days of old”

“Bashan” is … Elisha, who came from the Bashan. … As it is stated: … and Yanai and Shafat in the Bashan” … and it is written: “Here is Elisha ben Shafat who poured water on the hands of Elijah” … “Gilad” is … Elijah, as it is stated: “And Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the inhabitants of Gilad, said”

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said: In the future the righteous will resurrect the dead, as it is stated: “Old men and old women shall yet again dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, and every man with his staff in his hand for very age” … And … it is written: “And you shall lay my staff on the face of the child”

Ulla raised a contradiction … it is written: “He will destroy death forever, … And … it is written: … for the youngest shall die a hundred years old” … not difficult: Here, … Jews, … there, … gentiles, … What are gentiles doing there … As it is written: “And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vineyard workers”

Rav Ḥisda raised a contradiction … it is written: “Then the moon shall be confounded and the sun ashamed, … And … it is written: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, … not difficult: Here, … to the World … to … Come, … there, … to the days of the Messiah.

If so, … Rabbi Meir says … even one who … slaughters … for the purpose of communal offerings … is exempt? … even though he first slaughtered the … communal offerings at the beginning. And … you understand … If there, … he did not perform a mitzva … Rabbi Yehoshua … exempted … where he did perform a mitzva, … deem him liable?

perhaps … in accordance with … Rav Beivai bar Abaye. For Rav Beivai bar Abaye said: … teruma … on the eve of Passover, whose time is pressing,

He said to him: All your words are astonishing; from where … service in this time … He said to him: It says

“I have given you the priesthood as a service of gift; and the stranger that comes near shall be put to death” … they made the eating of teruma in the outlying areas, … like the service of the Temple.
one … slaughtered … for those who cannot eat it … It is obvious. Since there, … it is invalid, here, … he is liable, … Since the latter clause … taught … exempt … the first clause taught … liable,

Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana said to his son: When you go before Rabbi Zerika, ask him: According to the opinion that says that one who inflicts a destructive wound is exempt, … one who slaughtered … for those who cannot eat it is liable? … What has he improved
He has improved … if … ascended … they do not descend.

slaughtered … and it was found to have a blemish, he is liable … What has he improved … He has improved … on the … eyelid, and in accordance with … Rabbi Akiva, who said … if … ascended … they do not descend

slaughtered … and it was found to have a hidden condition that would cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa], he is exempt … if … is visible, … is liable. … What has he improved … He has improved … removed it from … an animal carcass [neveila],
Ravina strongly objects to this: … that which was taught … one who … slaughters a sin-offering on Shabbat outside … for … idolatry is liable to … three sin-offerings for it: … What has he improved
Rav Avira said: … he removed it from … limbs from a living creature.

one slaughtered … and it became known … Rav Huna said that Rav said: … a guilt-offering that was consigned to grazing: … And … slaughtered it without specifying … it is valid as a burnt-offering. … apparently holds that it does not require uprooting.
If so, … when it has not … been consigned … also … decree … after … atonement … due to … before … atonement

From where do you say … As we learned … A guilt-offering whose owner has died or whose owner has achieved atonement … grazes until it becomes unfit, … it is sold and its money is used for a … free-will burnt-offering. Rabbi Eliezer says: … die … Rabbi Yehoshua says: … it is sold, and he brings a burnt-offering … with its money.
with its money … indeed … but … itself … not … a decree … after … atonement … due to … before … atonement … learn from it
Rav Ḥisda raised an objection to Rav Huna … one slaughtered … and … it became known that the owners had withdrawn

And it was taught … with regard to this … on a weekday, in a case like this, … it should be burned immediately. Granted, if you say … requires uprooting … this is … a Paschal offering. And since it has no owners, its disqualification is in … itself, … therefore it should be burned immediately.

But if you say … does not require uprooting, … it was a peace-offering from the beginning, … due to what … is its disqualification? Due to something else, … that he slaughtered it after the daily afternoon offering, … it should require … its form decays,

As it was taught … This is the principle: Any … whose disqualification is in … itself should be burned immediately … in the blood … in the owners, … its form … decay, … should it be taken out to the place of burning.
Rather, do not say … slaughtered without specification is valid as a burnt-offering. Say rather … slaughtered it as a burnt-offering, it is valid. … apparently … requires … uprooting.

according to Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Gamda, who … said … it was thrown out from the group … and they … said … where the owners … were ritually impure … by a corpse … and they were pushed off to the second Pesaḥ,
it is … this … requires … uprooting, … but in general it does not require uprooting. … what is there to say,

Rather, Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said: With what are we dealing here … where they designated … before midday, … and the owners died after midday, such that … was … fit and … rejected: … anything that was … fit and … rejected does not return to being fit.
Is this reason … for anyone but Rav, … But Rav … said … living creatures cannot be … rejected.

Rather, Rav Pappa said: … whose … is this … It is … Rabbi Eliezer, who said: And similarly, … one slaughtered another … for the purpose of a Paschal offering, … disqualified. … its disqualification is in … itself,
But if it is … Rabbi Eliezer, he would deem him liable also to bring a sin-offering … for Rabbi Eliezer does not accept … one who errs in regard to a mitzva is exempt

Rather, Rav Yosef, son of Rav Salla the Ḥasid, explained before Rav Pappa … whose … is this … It is … Yosef ben Ḥonai. As we learned … Yosef ben Ḥonai says: … that are slaughtered for the purpose of a Paschal offering or for the purpose of a sin-offering are disqualified, … It is apparent … its disqualification is in … itself and therefore it should be burned immediately. But with regard to exemptions … he holds in accordance with … Rabbi Yehoshua,

Rav Ashi said … Rav said … in accordance with … Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka. As it was taught … Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says: If … has time in the day to clarify whether the owners withdrew or died or became ritually impure, he is liable … and … its form … decay, and … it should be taken out to the place of burning. What is the reason … Is it not because … it does not require uprooting?

From where … Perhaps … is because he agrees with the tanna of the school of Rabba bar Avuh, who said … even piggul, … also requires decay of form, for he derived … “iniquity” … “iniquity” … with regard to leftover

For if you do not say so, … the owners became ritually impure, what is there to say? … it certainly requires uprooting, for Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Gamda said … it was thrown out from the group … where the owners … were ritually impure … by a corpse … and they were pushed off to the second Pesaḥ.
Rather, it is clear … as he answered at the beginning, … is … Yosef ben Ḥonai.

MISHNA: How does one roast the Paschal lamb? One brings a spit [shappud] of pomegranate … and thrusts it into the mouth … until … its anus, and … puts its legs and entrails inside it … the statement of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili. Rabbi Akiva says: … this is a type of cooking. … Rather, one suspends … outside it. One … not roast the Paschal lamb on the … spit nor on … grill [askela]. … Rabbi Tzadok said: There was an incident with Rabban Gamliel, who said to his slave Tavi: Go and roast the Paschal lamb for us on the grill.

GEMARA: … Let them bring a metal … once part of it is hot, it is all hot, and … roasted due to the … spit. And the Merciful One states … roasted in fire and not roasted through something else. … Let them bring … of palm … Since … has grooves … it gives off … water … is as though it is cooked. … Let them bring … of fig … Since it is hollow … it gives off water, and it is as though … is cooked.
Let them bring … from an oak … from a carob … from a sycamore, … since it has knots … it gives off water

from a pomegranate … also has knots. … Its knots are smooth. … And if you wish, say … a branch … year, which does not … have knots. … But there is the place it was cut … One leaves the place it was cut outside

the mishna is not in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, as it was taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: Just as … a spit of wood … is not burned, … so … a spit of metal … does not become burning hot. … said to him: … this, … part of it is hot, it is all hot. And … that, … part of it is hot, not all of it is hot,
one places the legs … It was taught … Rabbi Yishmael … call … Tokh, tokh, … Rabbi Tarfon … call it: Helmeted kid.

The Sages taught: Which is the kid roasted whole that it is prohibited to eat on the nights of Passover in modern times, … any … that one roasted all at once … one of its limbs is severed … one of its limbs is boiled, it is no … a kid roasted whole.
Now, one can say … one of its limbs is severed, although one roasts it together with … you said … no … is … boiled, … is … necessary … Rav Sheshet said: … where one boiled … while it was attached
Rabba said: This stuffing … is permitted, … Abaye said to him: But … absorbs blood … He said to him: As it absorbs it, so it … emits it.

Let us say that … supports him: He places its legs and its entrails inside … What is the reason … not because we say: As it absorbs it, so it emits it? … Say it is different there, … Since there is the place of the slaughter, which is hollow
flows

Let us say … supports him: … the heart … tear it and remove its blood … he did not tear it … he tears it after it is cooked, … and it is permitted. What is the reason … Is it not because we say … as it absorbs it, so it emits it,
A heart is different … it is smooth
Is that so? Didn’t Ravin the Elder wrap a particular young dove in dough for Rav … and … said to him: If its dough … good, give me … and I will eat? … That … fine flour [semida], which is crumbly

Didn’t Rava happen … to the house of the Exilarch, and they breaded a young goose for him, … he said: If I had not seen that … is … clear as a white, … coin, I … not eat from it … And if it should enter your mind … as it absorbs it so it emits it, why … particularly because it was clear? Even if it was not clear, … also … There, … white … which is firm

And the halakha is … of fine flour, whether it turned red … or did not turn red, it is permitted. … of white … If it is clear like a white coin, it is permitted; if not, it is prohibited. … of other … flour, … turned red, it is prohibited; … it did not turn red, it is permitted.

this … stuffing … The one who prohibits … even … the opening … downward, … And the one who permits … even … the opening … upward. … And the halakha is that stuffing is permitted even … the opening … upward,

Raw meat [umtza] … testicles … and … veins … Rav Aḥa and Ravina disagreed about this. … In all … the Torah, … Rav Aḥa is stringent and … Ravina is lenient, and the halakha is in accordance with … Ravina to be lenient. … except for these three, … Rav Aḥa is lenient and Ravina is stringent, and the halakha is in accordance with … Rav Aḥa to be lenient.

this … raw meat that became red … one cut it and salted it, … permitted even to … a pot … put it on a spit … it is permitted … flows … placed it on coals, Rav Aḥa and Ravina disagreed about … this … one prohibited … and one permitted … The one who prohibited … to shrivel … And the one who permitted … draws out … And the halakha … draws out

And, so too, … testicles: … cut them and salted them, they are permitted even to … a pot. … hung them on a spit … they are permitted … flows … placed them on coals, Rav Aḥa and Ravina disagreed about this; one prohibited … and one permitted … The one who prohibited … it shrivels, and the one who permitted … draws out

And, so too, … veins: … cut them and salted them, it is permitted even to … a pot. … hung them on a spit … the place of the … slaughter is … downward, it is permitted … flows … placed it on coals, Rav Aḥa and Ravina disagreed about this … one prohibited … and one permitted … The one who prohibited … it shrivels, and the one who permitted … draws out … And the halakha … draws out

This … raw meat, whose vinegar became red … is forbidden. … its vinegar did not become red, it is permitted. Ravina said: Even … its vinegar did not become red, it is forbidden; it is impossible that it does not have streaks of blood. Mar bar Ameimar said to Rav Ashi: Father, … would swallow … Some say Rav Ashi himself would swallow it.
Mar bar Ameimar said to Rav Ashi: … father, … vinegar in which he had soaked … one time … he would not soak … in it again. … what … different from weak vinegar, in which we soak … There, the
sharpness of the fruit … in its pure, … Here, the sharpness of the fruit does not … in its pure,

one … not roast the Paschal lamb … an incident … to contradict … is incomplete and is teaching the following: And if it is a perforated grill, … it is permitted. And … Rabbi Tzadok said … there was an incident with Rabban Gamliel, who said to his slave Tavi: Go and roast the Paschal lamb for us on the perforated grill.

Rav Ḥinnana bar Idi raised a dilemma before Rav Adda bar Ahava: … an oven that one fired with peels of … orla, … he swept it … and he baked bread in it, according to the opinion that prohibits … what is … He said to him: The bread is permitted.

said to him: But didn’t Rav Ḥinnana the Elder say … Rabbi Asi said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … an oven that one fired and swept … and … roasted the Paschal lamb in it, this is not … roasted in fire, as it is stated … roasted in fire, … roasted in fire; … two times,
The reason … the Merciful One reveals … Roasted in fire, roasted in fire, twice. But … the Merciful One had not revealed … I would have said … is … roasted in fire.
said to … The Merciful One reveals it there, … and we learn from it

And if you wish, say … There, … the reason … is that the Merciful One writes “roasted in fire” twice. But … the Merciful One had not written “roasted in fire” twice, I would have said that the Merciful One is particular about fire, … and even if one swept it, it is … roasted in fire. … But here, … the Merciful One is particular about the prohibited fuel, and it is not here

The Sages taught: … one cuts … and places it on coals, Rabbi … says: I say that this is … roasted in fire, … Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami raised a contradiction to Rav Ḥisda: Did Rabbi … say that coals are … fire?

raised a contradiction … a burn from fire” … nothing other … it is burned by fire … is burned by a coal, by burning ash, by burning lime, by burning plaster [gipsis], or … anything … and … comes from fire, to include … water heated by fire, from where … The verse states: A burn, a burn, … it includes
The reason is that the Merciful One includes … A burn, a burn. But … the Merciful One had not included … a burn, a burn, … coals are not … fire,
He said to him: … wood coal, … not necessary … the verse to include it. … Where a verse is necessary … to … piece of metal
And are … pieces of metal not … fire? But with regard to a daughter of a priest … it is written: … in fire she shall be burned” … and Rav Mattana said: … they would prepare for her … bar of lead.
It is different there, as the verse states … “in fire she shall be burned.” … “she shall be burned” … to include all burnings that come from fire.

all the more so fire itself … Let us surround her … bundles of branches and burn her … It comes … “burning” … “burning” … the sons of Aaron: Just as below, … a burning of the soul and the body remained, … so too, here, … burning of the soul and the body remains.
Let us … her with … water heated by fire. … due to … Rav Naḥman, as Rav Naḥman said … the verse states: “And you shall love your fellow as yourself” … select for him a kind death.

Once there is … Rav Naḥman, why do I … the verbal analogy … Say … If not … verbal analogy, I would have said that burning the soul … the body remains is not … burning. And if … due to … Rav Naḥman … we should add many bundles of branches so that she would die quickly. … teaches us
But … for what do I need … “in fire”? … To exclude lead from its source.

Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira: … anywhere that it is written: “In fire she shall be burned” … to include all … burning that come from fire? But … bulls that are burned, … which it is written: “And he shall burn it on wood in fire, … and it was taught … In fire, and not in burning lime and not in burning plaster?

He said to him: How can … be compared? There, … it is written: “In fire,” and … subsequently … she shall be burned, … to include all … burning that come from fire. Here, … it is written: “And he shall burn it on wood in fire.” At the end … fire, to say that … fire, yes, … something else, no,
There, too, … burning is written at the end, as it is written

“Where the ash is poured it shall be burned” … Say: That … “it shall be burned” is needed for that which was taught … It shall be burned even though there is no ash there, … “It shall be burned” … although the fire has consumed most of it,

Ravina said … Combine and teach … “a burn from fire,” I have … nothing other … which one was burned by a fire or by a coal. … burned by hot ash, by burning lime, or by burning plaster, or by anything … and … comes from fire, to include water heated by fire, from where … The verse states: A burn, a burn, … it includes

Rava raised a contradiction: Did Rabbi … say … coals are called fire? And we raise a contradiction … coals, … might … smoldering … Therefore, the verse states: Fire. If … fire, … might … a flame. Therefore, the verse states: Coals. How … One brings from the … flickering, … Apparently, … coals are not called fire.

Say … Isn’t this … itself difficult? You said: … coals, … might … smoldering. Apparently, … flickering … are … fire. Say the latter clause … If … fire, … might … Therefore, the verse states: Coals. Apparently, even flickering … are not … fire,

And Rav Sheshet said, … This is what … is teaching: … coals, … might … whether smoldering or flickering. Therefore, the Torah states: Fire. If … fire, … might … a flame. Therefore, the verse states: Coals. How … He brings from the flickering … In any event, … coals, … are not called fire. … a difficulty … Rabbi

Abaye said … answer … as follows: … coals, … might … smoldering and not flickering. Therefore, the verse states: Fire. If … fire, … might … one wanted a flame he … bring … he wanted a coal he … bring … Therefore, the Torah states: Coals. How … He brings from the flickering

Rabba said: … he wanted a coal he … bring … if he wanted a flame he … bring … what circumstances … a flame without a coal be found? … where one smears a utensil with oil and lights it on fire. … this, why do I … a verse to exclude it … Now, in front of a king of flesh and blood one does not do this, … in front of the King of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He, … not all the more so

Rather, Rava said … answer as follows: … coals, … might … smoldering and not flickering; therefore, the verse states: Fire. If … fire, … might … one should bring half coal and half fire, … by … he enters … inside … and it will be all coal. Therefore, the verse states: “And he shall take a coal-pan full of burning coals from upon the altar” … from the time of … taking they should be coals
a dilemma was raised before … omemot … or omemot … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: … “The cedars in the garden of God could not hide it [amamuhu]”

MISHNA: … touched … earthenware … of an oven, one … peel … its place … of … gravy … dripped on the earthenware and … returned to it, … one … remove its place. … of … gravy dripped onto … flour, one … remove a handful of … its place,

smears … with teruma oil, if … a group of priests they may eat it, … If … of Israelites, … if … raw, one … rinse it … and if it is roasted, one … peel off the outer … one smears … with oil of … second tithe, he may not demand money for it from the members of the group, as one … not redeem second tithe in Jerusalem.
GEMARA: … It was stated … a hot … into … hot … all agree
forbidden, … cold … into … cold … all agree it is permitted; … hot … into a cold … a cold … into a hot … Rav said: The upper one prevails. … And Shmuel said: The lower one prevails.

We learned … of the gravy of … dripped onto the earthenware and returned to it, one … remove its place. It … enter your mind … cold earthenware. Granted, according to … Rav, who said the upper one prevails, … due to this … one … remove its place. … the gravy goes and heats the earthenware, and then the earthenware heats the gravy, and when the gravy returns to the Paschal lamb, the Paschal lamb becomes roasted from the heat of the earthenware, and the Merciful One states … “Roasted in fire” … and not roasted due to something else.

But according to … Shmuel, who said the lower one prevails, since the earthenware is cold, it cools down the gravy. … why must he remove its place? … As Rabbi Yirmeya said … Shmuel said … hot flour. Here, too, … hot earthenware.

We … learned … of … gravy dripped onto flour, one … remove a handful of … its place. It … enter your mind … cold flour. Granted, according to … Rav, who said the upper one prevails, … due to this … one … remove a handful … its place, as … heats the flour around it, and the flour then heats … and the gravy is roasted from the heat of the flour, and the Merciful One states … “Roasted in fire,” and not roasted due to something else.

But according to … Shmuel, who said the lower one prevails, since the flour is cold it cools down … why do I … One … remove a handful … its place? It should be enough for one to remove … its place, … Rabbi Yirmeya said … Shmuel said: … hot flour.

We learned … one smears … with teruma oil, if … a group of priests they may eat it, … If … of Israelites, … if … raw, one … rinse it … and if it is roasted, one … peel off the outer … Granted, according to Rav, who said the upper one prevails, for this … it is sufficient … peel, because the upper one is cold

But … to Shmuel, who said: The lower one prevails, since … is hot, it absorbs … why is it enough for it … peel … It should be entirely forbidden. … Smearing is different because it is done with only a minute amount.
was taught … in accordance with … Shmuel: … hot … into hot … it is forbidden. And, so too, cold … that one put into hot … is forbidden. … hot … into cold … and … cold … into cold … one … rinse

hot … into cold … one … rinse … Since it is hot, until … cools it, it is impossible that it will not absorb a little … it should at least require … peel; … Rather, say … hot … into cold … one … peel … cold … into cold … one … rinse

It was taught … another … Hot meat that fell into hot milk, and so too, cold … that fell into hot … is prohibited. … hot … into cold … and … cold … into cold … one … rinse … hot … into cold … one … rinse … Since it is hot, until … cools it, it is impossible that it will not absorb a little … it should at least require … peel. Rather, say … hot … into cold … one … peel … cold … into cold … one … rinse

the Mar Yanuka, … and Mar Kashisha, … sons of Rav Ḥisda, said to Rav Ashi: Once Ameimar happened to … our place and we did not have wine … We brought him beer and he did not recite havdala, and he passed the night fasting, … The next day we exerted ourselves and brought him wine, and he recited havdala and tasted some … The next year he again happened … to our place. … we did not have wine … we brought … beer. He said: If so, … is the wine of the province. He recited havdala … and tasted some

learn from … three … Learn from it … one who recites havdala in the prayer … must recite havdala … over a cup, … And learn from it … it is prohibited for a person to eat before he recites havdala. And learn from it … one who did not recite havdala at the conclusion of Shabbat … recite havdala anytime … the entire week,

Rav Huna raised a dilemma before Rav Ḥisda: What is … to recite kiddush over date beer? understood from it … it is kiddush that one … not recite over it, but one … recite havdala … Rav Ḥisda said to them … Rav said as follows: Just as one … not recite kiddush over … so one … not recite havdala over it. And Rava said: One who recites kiddush over beer, his … drink should be beer. … Rav … found … Rav Huna reciting kiddush over beer. He said to him: Abba, … has started to acquire coins with beer.

The Sages taught: One … recite kiddush only over wine, and one … recite blessings only over wine. … Is that to say that one does not say the blessing: By Whose word all things [shehakol] came to be, over beer and water?
