In the name of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, they said … one … recite kiddush

by tasting any amount of wine. Rabbi Yosei, son of Yehuda, says … a cheekful. Rav Huna said … Rav said, and Rav Giddel from … Neresh likewise teaches: One who recites kiddush and tastes a cheekful has fulfilled … and if not, … has not fulfilled
Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: I teach this … not … Giddul bar Menashya, nor Giddul bar Minyumei, but rather … plain … Giddul, … What is … practical difference … To raise a contradiction … his … his
adjacent to minḥa time … A dilemma was raised before … we learn … adjacent to … greater minḥa [minḥa gedola], … or perhaps we learned … adjacent to … lesser minḥa [minḥa ketana],
we learn … adjacent to … the greater minḥa, … because of the Paschal lamb, lest one come to be drawn after
and he will end up refraining from performing the Paschal lamb? Or perhaps we learned … adjacent to the lesser minḥa, and … due to matza. … perhaps he will come to eat the matza … excessive eating,

Ravina said: Come … hear … Even King Agrippa, who regularly eats … at nine hours, … on that day … he … not eat until dark. … Granted, if you say … we learned … adjacent to the lesser minḥa, this is … the greatness of Agrippa,
However, if you say … we learned … adjacent to the greater minḥa, what is the greatness of Agrippa? … prohibition … taken effect at the outset, … Rather, … we learned … adjacent to the lesser minḥa,
Ultimately, what is the greatness of Agrippa? The time of the prohibition had arrived. … Lest you say … nine hours for Agrippa is considered like four hours for us, … teaches us
Rabbi Yosei said: … however, one … dip … types of refreshments, … Rabbi Yitzḥak … dip … vegetables. That … was also taught … the waiter … dip in the intestines … and place them before the guests
And although there is no … proof for … matter, … is an allusion to … matter, … it is stated: “Break up for yourselves a fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns”
Rava would drink wine the entire day of Passover eve, so … whet his appetite … to eat more matza at night. Rava said: From where do I say it, that wine whets … As we learned

between these cups … if one wants to drink he … drink. … between the third and fourth … one … not drink. And if you say that … satisfies … why … one drink … He will … eat matza … an excessive eating. Rather, learn from … that … whets

Rav Sheshet would fast the entire eve of Passover. … Shall we say … Rav Sheshet maintains … we learned … adjacent to the greater minḥa, and … is due to the Paschal lamb, lest one be drawn … and come to refrain from performing … the Paschal lamb.

And … Rav Sheshet maintains in accordance with that … that Rabbi Oshaya said … Rabbi Elazar said: Ben Beteira would deem valid a Paschal lamb that was slaughtered in the morning on the fourteenth … for its own purpose, … from the morning it is … time … a Paschal lamb … as the whole day is fit for the Paschal lamb.
As … maintained … “bein ha’arbayim” … between the evening of yesterday and the current evening
They say … No, … Rav Sheshet was different, as he was delicate [istenis], for if he would taste some … in the morning, … food … at night would not be effective for him.

even the poorest of Jews … not eat until he reclines. It was stated … matza requires reclining, … bitter herbs do not require reclining. … wine, it was stated in the name of Rav Naḥman … requires reclining, and it was … stated in the name of Rav Naḥman … does not require reclining.

And … do not disagree … This … to the first two cups, and that … to the last two cups. … Some say … in this manner and some say it in that manner. … Some say it in this manner, … the first two cups require reclining, as it is now that freedom begins. … last two cups do not require reclining, … what was … was.

And some say it in that manner … on the contrary, … last two cups require reclining, … at that time that there is freedom. … first two cups do not require reclining, as one still says: We were slaves. … Now that it was stated so, and it was stated so, … these … and those require reclining.

Lying on one’s back is not called reclining. Reclining to the right is not called reclining, … And not only that, but … perhaps the windpipe will precede the esophagus. … and one will come into danger

A woman … with her husband is not required to recline, but if she is an important woman, she is required to recline. A son … with his father is required to recline. A dilemma was raised before … What is … a student … with his teacher?

Come … hear … Abaye said: When we were in the house of … Master, … we reclined on each other’s knees, … When we came to the house of Rav Yosef, … said to us: You need not … the fear of your teacher is like the fear of Heaven.
raises an objection: A person must recline … of anyone, and even a student … with his teacher … When that … was taught, … with regard to a craftsman’s apprentice,

A dilemma was raised before … What is … a waiter? … Come … hear … as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: A waiter who ate an olive-bulk of matza while reclining has fulfilled … reclining, yes, … not reclining, no, … Learn from … requires reclining. … learn from it
And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Women are obligated in these four cups
As they too were … in that miracle

Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: These four cups must contain … for diluting a significant cup. … one drank them undiluted, … fulfilled … one drank them all at once, … fulfilled … one gave his sons or the members of his household to drink from them, … fulfilled
one drank them undiluted … fulfilled … Rava said: … fulfilled … wine, … not fulfilled … freedom,

one drank … all at once, Rav said … fulfilled … wine … not fulfilled … four cups, … one gave his sons or the members of his household to drink from them, … fulfilled … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: And this is … if he … drank the majority of the cup.

raises an objection … These four cups must contain … quarter … whether … is undiluted or diluted, whether … new or aged. Rabbi Yehuda says: It must have the taste and appearance of wine. In any event, … is teaching … of … quarter- … and … you said … a significant cup.
They say … this and that are one … measure. … What … Enough for diluting a significant cup, which … said? … for each and every one … This … quarter … for all of them
Rabbi Yehuda says … must have … taste and appearance … Rava said: What is the reason … of Rabbi Yehuda? As it is written: “Look not upon wine when it is red”
The Sages taught … All are obligated in these four cups, including men, women, and children. Rabbi Yehuda said: What benefit do children receive from wine? … Rather, one distributes to them

roasted grains and nuts on Passover eve, so that they will not sleep and … they will ask … They said about Rabbi Akiva that he would distribute roasted grains and nuts to children on Passover eve, so that they would not sleep and … they would ask. It was taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: One grabs the matzot on the nights of Passover. … on account of the children, so … they will not sleep

It was taught … They said about Rabbi Akiva … in … his days he never said … time had come to arise … in the study hall. … except for the eves of Passover and the eve of Yom Kippur, … On the eve of Passover, … on account of … children, so that … they would not … sleep … And … the eve of Yom Kippur, … so that … would … feed their children.

The Sages taught: A man is obligated to gladden his children and the members of his household on a Festival, as it is stated: “And you shall rejoice on your Festival, … With what … one make them rejoice? With wine.

Rabbi Yehuda says: … men with what is fit for them and women with what is fit for them. … Men with what is fit for them, … with wine. And … women, with what … Rav Yosef teaches: … in Babylonia with colored clothes … in Eretz Yisrael with … pressed linen clothes

It was taught … Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: When the Temple is standing, rejoicing is only through … meat, as it is stated: “And you shall sacrifice peace-offerings and you shall eat there and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God” … And now that the Temple is not standing … rejoicing … only by … wine, as it is stated: “And wine that gladdens the heart of man”

Rabbi Yitzḥak said: The vessel … brine [moraysa] that was in Tzippori was the same … as the log in the Temple, and with it … measure the quarter … of Passover. … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The old eighth … that was … in Tiberias was greater than this … by … quarter … and with it we measure … quarter … of Passover.

Rav Ḥisda said: The quarter … of the Torah is two fingerbreadths by two fingerbreadths … by the height of two fingerbreadths and one half fingerbreadth and one-fifth of a fingerbreadth. … as it was taught … “And he shall bathe all his flesh in the water” … that there should be nothing interposing between one’s flesh … the water. … “in the water” … in the water of a ritual bath. … “all his flesh” … water that his whole body can enter … And how much is that?
A cubit, by a cubit, by a height of three cubits. And the Sages measured … measure … the water … for a ritual bath … forty se’a.
Rav Ashi said: Ravin bar Ḥinnana said to me: The table of the Temple, … was … parts. For if it should enter your mind … was firmly connected … how could … immerse a cubit in a cubit?
What is the difficulty? Perhaps … would immerse it in the sea that … Solomon built, … As Rabbi Ḥiyya taught: The sea that Solomon built contained … one hundred and fifty ritual purification baths.

not … him less than four … How could the Sages establish a matter through which one will come to … danger? But wasn’t it taught … A person … not eat pairs, … and he … not drink pairs … and he … not wipe himself with pairs; and he … not attend to his … needs in pairs.
Rav Naḥman said … the verse said: “It was a night of watching … is a night that remains guarded from … harmful spirits
Rava said … The cup of blessing … it combines … for the good, … and it does not combine for the bad. … Ravina said: The Sages instituted four … cups, … in a manner … freedom. … each and every one
is a distinct mitzva

one … not attend to his … needs in pairs. … Why … he has changed his mind? … Abaye said: This is … is saying, … One … not eat in pairs nor drink in pairs, and … he … not attend to his … needs … even once, lest he is weakened … and will be harmed

The Sages taught … drinks in pairs his blood is upon his head, … Rav Yehuda said: When … When one did not … view the marketplace … However, if he saw the marketplace … he has permission … Rav Ashi said: I saw Rav Ḥananya bar Beivai … Upon … each cup, he would leave … and view the marketplace.

And we said … only … to set out on the road … but … in his home … no … Rabbi Zeira said: And … to sleep is comparable to … setting out on the road. … Rav Pappa said: And going to the bathroom is comparable to setting out on the road. … And … in his home, … no … But Rava would count the beams

And … Abaye, when he would drink one cup, his mother would … place two cups in his two hands … And … when Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak would drink two cups, his attendant would … place one … cup in his hand, … one cup, … place two cups in his two hands. … An important person is different.

Ulla said: Ten cups contain no element of … pairs. Ulla … in accordance with his reasoning … as Ulla said, and some say it was taught in a baraita: The Sages instituted … ten cups … in the house of a mourner … And if it could enter your mind … ten cups do contain the element of … pairs, how could the Sages arise and institute something that … bring a person to … danger? However, eight cups do contain the element of … pairs.
Rav Ḥisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna both say … shalom, combines … for the good … does not combine for the bad. … However, six cups do contain the element of … pairs.
Rabba and Rav Yosef both say … viḥuneka … combines … for the good … does not combine for the bad. However, four cups do contain the element of … pairs.
Abaye and Rava both say … veyishmerekha, … It combines for the good … does not combine for the bad.

And Rava follows his … reasoning … as Rava … the Sages to leave … four cups … Although Rava bar Livai was injured … was not concerned … the matter … as he said: That … because … challenged me during the … lecture.

Rav Yosef said: Yosef the Demon said to me: Ashmedai, the king of the demons, is appointed over all … pairs, and a king is not called a harmful spirit. … Some say … in this manner: On the contrary, he is an angry king … does what he wants, … that a king … breach the fence … in order to form a path for himself, and none … protest his

Rav Pappa said: Yosef the Demon said to me: … two … we … kill … four, we do not kill … four, we harm … With … two, whether … unwittingly or intentionally, … With … four, … intentionally, yes, … unwittingly, no,

And if one forgets and it happens that he goes outside … what is his solution? … take his right thumb in his left hand, and his left thumb in his right hand, and say as follows: You, … and I are three, … And if he hears … that says: You and I are four, … say to it: You and I are five. And if he hears it say: You and I are six, … say to it: You and I are seven. … there was an incident … until … a hundred and one, and the demon burst
Ameimar said: The chief of witches said to me: One who encounters witches … say this … Hot feces in torn date baskets in your mouth, witches; may your hairs fall out … your crumbs, … should scatter

your spices, … should scatter; the wind should carry away the fresh saffron that you witches hold … As long as I was shown favor … and you showed me favor, I did not come here. Now that I have come here, your favor toward me has cooled and you should find favor.

in the West, … they were not particular with regard to pairs. Rav Dimi from Neharde’a was particular … even with regard to the signs on a barrel; … There was an incident … and the barrel burst. … The rule of the matter … all who are particular … are particular with him; and … one is not particular, they are not particular with him. However, one is required to be concerned

When Rav Dimi came … he said: … two eggs, two nuts, two cucumbers, and another matter, … a halakha … to Moses from Sinai … But the Sages are uncertain … what the other matter is, and … the Sages decreed that all pairs … due to … other matter.

And … that which we said … ten, eight, six, … four do not … with pairs, we said only with regard to harmful spirits. However, with regard to witchcraft, we are concerned even with regard to … a greater

like that … a certain man who divorced his wife. She went and married a shopkeeper … Every day, … would go and drink wine … would perform witchcraft upon him, and it would not be effective for her … him because he was careful with regard to pairs.

One day he drank a lot, and he did not know how much he drank. Until … sixteen … he was lucid and was careful with regard to himself, … From here onward he was not lucid and was not careful to … himself, and she caused him to leave … a pair, … As he walked, a certain Arab met him and, … said to him: It is a dead man who walks here. He went and hugged a palm tree … the palm tree dried out … and he burst.

Rav Avira said: Plates and loaves do not contain the element of … pairs. … The rule of the matter … anything … was completed by people, … they do not contain the element of … pairs. … was completed by Heaven, … with regard to types of food, we are concerned.

a store does not contain the element of … pairs. … changed one’s mind … does not contain the element of … pairs, … a guest … does not contain the element of … pairs, … a woman does not contain the element of … pairs, … But if … an important woman, we are concerned.
Rav Ḥinnana, son of Rav Yehoshua, said: Isparegus, … combines … for the good, … and does not combine for the bad,
Ravina said in the name of Rava: … pairs, … stringent … And … say … pairs … lenient … Rav Yosef said: Two … of wine and one … of beer do not combine; two … of beer and one … of wine do combine.
And … your mnemonic … This is the rule: … anything attached to … is more stringent than … is ritually impure; … is more lenient than it, … is ritually pure.
Rav Naḥman said … Rav said: … two … before the table … and one … over the table they combine, … one … before the table … and two … over the table they do not combine;
Rav Mesharshiya strongly objects to this … Is that to say that we need to resolve the … table? … We need to resolve … the person, and … the person … is … resolved.
Rather, Rav Mesharshiya said: Everyone agrees … two … over the table … and one after the table … they do not combine. … like that incident … Rabba bar Naḥmani,
Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: Any … diluted combines

except for water. … And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even water … Rav Pappa said: We said this statement only … hot … into cold … and cold … into hot water. … However, … hot … into hot … or cold … into cold … no,

Reish Lakish said: … four matters. The one who performs them, his blood is upon his … head, and … liable for his own life, … One who relieves himself … between a palm tree and a wall, one who passes between two palm trees, one who drinks borrowed water, and one who passes over spilled water, even if his wife poured it out in front of him.

one who relieves himself between a palm tree and a wall, we said … only when there are not four cubits … However, … there are four cubits, we have no … with it. … And … when there are not four cubits, we said … only when … have no other route … However, … have another route, we have no … with it.

And … one who passes between two palm trees, we said … only if a public domain does not cross between them. However, … a public domain crosses between them, we have no … with it, … And … one who drinks borrowed water, we said … only if a minor borrowed it. However, … an adult … we have no … with it.

And even … a minor borrowed it, we said … only … in a field, where … is not found. However, in a city, where … can be found, we have no … with it. And even in a field, we said … only … water; however, … wine and beer, we have no … with it.

And … one who passes over spilled water, we said … only if no one sprinkled dirt over it and no one spat in it. However, if … sprinkled dirt over it or spat in it, we have no … with it. And we said … only if the sun did not pass over it, … and sixty steps … have not passed over it. However, … the sun passed over it and sixty steps passed over it, we have no … with it. And we said … only if he was not riding a donkey and not wearing shoes; however, if he was riding a donkey and wearing shoes, we have no … with it.

And … this … where there is no … concern for witchcraft, … However, where there is … concern for witchcraft, even if all of these … are … we are … concerned. And … a certain man who was riding a donkey and wearing shoes. … and his shoes shrank and his feet shriveled up.
The Sages taught: Three … not … pass between … not walk between … A dog, a palm tree, and a woman. And some say: Also a pig. And some say: Also a snake.
And if they pass between them, what is the remedy … Rav Pappa said: He … begin … with … God and conclude with … God.
Alternatively, he … open … lo, … and … conclude … lo:

these two … between whom a menstruating woman passes, if she is at the beginning of her menstruation she kills one of them, … If she is … the end of her menstruation … causes a fight between them. What is his remedy? He … open … with … God and he … conclude with … God,

These two women, who are sitting at a crossroads, one on this side of the road and the other on the other side, and they are facing each other, they are certainly engaging in witchcraft. What is … remedy … If there is another route, he … go by it. And if there is no other route, if there is another person with him, they … hold hands and switch … And if there is no other person with him, he … say as follows: Iggeret, Azlat, Asiya, Belusiya are killed by arrows.

One who meets a woman when she is ascending from the ritual immersion of a mitzva, … if he has intercourse … first, a spirit of immorality overtakes him; if she has intercourse first, a spirit of immorality overtakes her. What is his remedy? He … say this: “He pours contempt upon princes, and causes them to wander in the waste, where there is no way”

Rav Yitzḥak said: What … is written: “Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me” … This is … who sleeps in the shadow of a single palm tree, and in the shadow of the moon. … And with regard to … in the shadow of a single palm tree, we said … only if the shadow of another … does not fall upon him. However, … the shadow of another … falls upon him, we have no … with it.

But … that … was taught … who sleeps in the shadow of a single palm tree in a courtyard and one who sleeps in the shadow of the moon, his blood is upon his … head. What are the circumstances? If we say that the shadow of another … does not fall on him, … also … in a field. Rather, … one not conclude from … courtyard, even if the shadow of another … fell on him, … learn from it
And … to the shadow of the moon, we said … only … in the west. However, … in the east, we have no … with it.

One who relieves himself on the stump of a palm tree will be seized by a spirit of sickness, and one who places his head on the stump of a palm tree will be seized by a spirit of a headache … is cut down, he … will be killed. If … is uprooted, he will … be uprooted and will die. … This … applies … he does not place his legs upon it; however, … he places his legs upon it, we have no … with it.

are five … shadows: The shadow of a single palm tree, the shadow of … kanda, the shadow of a caper-bush, and the shadow of … sorb … Some say: Also the shadow of a ship and the shadow of a willow. The … rule of the matter … Whatever has many branches, its shadow is dangerous.

And any tree whose wood is hard, its shadow is dangerous, except for … kero masa. Although its wood is hard, its shadow is not dangerous, as the demon said to her son: Leave the kero masa … alone, as it … that … that killed your father. And … killed … Rav Ashi said: I saw that Rav Kahana avoided all … of shadows.
near the caper-bush … ruḥei. … near the sorb trees … shida. … on roofs … rishfei. … What is … practical difference … for … an amulet

near the caper-bush … a creature with no eyes. What is … difference … to fleeing … it. … Once a Torah scholar went to relieve himself near a caper-bush. He heard … coming and fled from it. When … went, it grabbed a palm tree … The palm tree dried out and … burst.
near the sorb tree … sheidei. … This sorb … that is close to the city … no less than sixty demons. … What is … practical difference … for writing an amulet

A certain ruler of a city walked and stood by a sorb … that was near a city. Sixty sheidei … came upon him and he was in danger. One of the Sages who did not know that it was a sorb tree of sixty sheidei came and wrote him an amulet for one shida … heard that there was a celebration inside … and … were singing: The scarf of … Master is like that of a Torah scholar, … we checked the Master and he does not know … barukh, … one of the Sages, who knew that it was a sorb tree of sixty sheidei, came and wrote an amulet … sixty demons. He heard them saying: Clear your items away from here.

ketev meriri, … There are two … of ketev … one … before noon … and … one … in the afternoon. … that … before noon is called ketev meriri, and it appears in a jug of kutaḥ, … revolves around inside it. … in the afternoon is called ketev yashud tzaharayim … and it appears inside the horn of a goat and revolves around inside it like a sifter.

Abaye was coming and walking … And Rav Pappa was walking on his right and Rav Huna, son … Rav Yehoshua, … on his left. … saw a certain ketev meriri coming on his left side and he switched Rav Pappa to his left and Rav Huna, son … Rav Yehoshua, to his right. Rav Pappa said … I, what is different that you were not concerned about … me? … said to him: The time is in your favor.

From the first of Tammuz to the sixteenth of … certainly found. From here onward … uncertain whether they are found or whether they are not found. And they can be found in the shadow of a sea squill that has not grown a cubit, and in the shadow … morning and evening when … is less than a cubit. And they are mostly … in the shadow of a privy.
Rav Yosef said: These three matters cause blindness to the light … One who combs his hair … dry, one who drinks … dripping … and one who puts on shoes when his feet are wet

hanging in one’s house, … causes poverty. … as people say … He who hangs the basket hangs his sustenance, … And we said this only … bread; however, … meat and fish, we have no … with it. … it is the common practice … Bran [parei] in the house causes poverty. … crumbs in the house cause poverty. … Shabbat nights, … or on Tuesday nights, … harmful spirits rest on them.

The administering angel … food is called Nakid, … The administering angel … poverty is called Naval. … A plate … on a jug causes poverty. One who drinks water from a plate causes … pain. … who eats cress without washing his hands will be afraid for thirty days.

who lets blood and does not wash his hands will be afraid for seven days. … who cuts his hair and does not wash his hands will be afraid for three days. … who cuts his nails and does not wash his hands will be afraid for one day, and he will not know what is frightening … hand on … nostrils … a way to … afraid. … hand on his forehead is a way … asleep.

taught: … food and drink … under … bed, even if they are covered with iron vessels, an evil spirit rests upon them. The Sages taught: A person … not drink water on Tuesday nights or on Shabbat nights, … And if he drinks … his blood is upon his … head, due to … danger. … What is … danger? … evil spirit

And if he is thirsty, what is his remedy? … He … say … seven voices that David said over the water, and afterward he … drink. As it is stated: “The voice of the Lord is upon the waters; God of glory thunders, even the Lord upon many waters. The voice of the Lord is powerful; the voice of the Lord is full of majesty. The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars; the Lord breaks in pieces the cedars of Lebanon. … The voice of the Lord hews out flames of fire. The voice of the Lord shakes the wilderness; the Lord shakes the wilderness of Kadesh. The voice of the Lord makes the hinds to calve, and strips the forests bare; and in His temple all say: Glory”

And if … not … he … say as follows: Lul, Shafan, Anigron, Anirdafin, … I sit between the stars, I walk between thin … fat … And if … not … if there is … person with him, he … wake him and say to him: So-and-so, son of so-and-so, I thirst for water; and then … drink. And if … no … knock the cover on the cup and then drink. And if … not … he … throw some … in it and then drink.

The Sages taught: A person … not drink water from rivers or from ponds at night. And if he drank, his blood is upon his … head due to the danger. … What is … danger? The danger of blindness. … And if he is thirsty, what is his remedy? If there is … person with him, he … say to him: So-and-so, son of so-and-so, I thirst for water. And if … no … he … say to himself: So-and-so, my mother said to me … beware of shavrirei, … Shavrirei berirei rirei yiri ri; I thirst for water in white … cups.
And … even … from the charity plate. … obvious
is necessary only … even according to … Rabbi Akiva, who said: Make your Shabbat … weekday and do not be beholden to … beings. … Here, … concedes … due to … to publicize the miracle.

the school of Eliyahu taught … although Rabbi Akiva said: Make your Shabbat … a weekday and do not be beholden to … beings; however, one … perform some small … in his house … What … this … Rav Pappa said: … small, fried fish. As we learned … Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima says: Be bold like a leopard, light like an eagle, run like a deer, and … strong like a lion to perform the will of your Father in Heaven.

The Sages taught: Rabbi Akiva commanded Rabbi Yehoshua, his son, … seven matters: My son, do not sit at the high point of a city, … and study … And do not live in a city whose leaders are Torah scholars,

And do not enter your house suddenly, … all the more so … the house of another, … And do not withhold shoes from your feet, … Wake up and eat, in the summer due to the heat, … and in the winter due to … the cold. And make your Shabbat … a weekday and do not be beholden to … beings. And exert yourself … with a person upon whom the hour smiles,

Rav Pappa said … Do not buy from him and do not sell to him. … Rather, form a partnership with him. And now … that Rav Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said: What … which is written: “You have blessed the work of his hands” … anyone who took a peruta from Job would be blessed, … even if … to buy from him or to sell to him it is well,

Rabbi Akiva commanded Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai … five matters when … was imprisoned. … said to him: Rabbi, teach me Torah. … said … I will not teach you, … said to him … If you will not teach me, I will tell Yoḥai … father, and he will turn you over to the government. … said: My son, … more than the calf wishes to suck, the cow wants to suckle, … said to him: And who is in danger? Isn’t the calf in danger,

said to him: … if you wish to strangle yourself, hang yourself on a tall tree. … And when you teach your son, teach him from a corrected text. … What is … that … Rava said, and some say Rav Mesharshiya … to … a new … once a mistake enters … entered

Do not cook in a pot in which your colleague cooked … What is … this … a divorced woman in the lifetime of her … husband. As the Master said: … a divorced man marries a divorced woman, there are four minds in the bed … And if you wish, say … even with regard to … a widow, as
not all fingers are equal.
a mitzva and a great … body … eat fruits without payment. … a mitzva and … pure body … marries a woman, … and he will … have children.
Our holy rabbi, … commanded his sons … four matters: Do not live in Shekhantziv … because they are mockers. And they will draw you in to their mockery
Do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman. … Some say … that you … not go to sleep without reciting Shema, … And some say … that you … not marry a convert,
And some say … actual … an Aramean woman, and … due to … incident involving Rav Pappa.

And do not avoid paying taxes, lest they find you and confiscate everything you own. And do not stand before an ox when it emerges from the marsh because Satan dances between its horns, … Rabbi Shmuel said: … to a black ox, and … during the days of Nisan,
Rav Oshaya teaches … One distances himself fifty cubits from an innocuous ox [shor tam], … From a forewarned ox [shor muad], … eyeshot.

taught citing the name … Rabbi Meir, … the head of the ox … basket, go up to the roof and kick the ladder out from underneath you … Rav said: The cry … to … an ox … hen hen. The cry to … a lion … zeh zeh. The cry to … a camel … da da. The cry to … a ship … heleni, hayya, hela, vehilook, hulya.

Abaye said: Hide, fish, and a cup, hot water, and eggs, and white lice all cause … other matter, … Hide … one who sleeps on a tanner’s hide … Fish … shibuta … in the days of Nisan. … cup … the leftovers of small fried fish. Hot water … very hot water that … pours on himself. Eggs … one who steps on eggshells. White lice … one who washes his garment but does not keep it for eight days before wearing it again, … creates these lice. And … cause … other matter,

Rav Pappa said: … a house in which there is a cat, a person … not enter there barefoot. What is the reason? Because the cat … kill a snake and eat it, and the snake has small bones, and if … bone gets into one’s foot it cannot be removed, and he will be in danger. Some say … a house in which there is no cat, a person … not enter there in the dark. What is the reason? … perhaps a snake will wrap itself around him without … knowing and he will be in danger.

Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, commanded Rabbi … three matters. … mem, kuf, shin … a mnemonic … Do not inflict a blemish upon yourself. … What … Do not have a court case against three … as one will be your opponent and two … witnesses … And do not stand over … a purchase when you do not have … money

Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, commanded Rabbi … your wife has immersed, do not engage … with her on the first night. … Rav said: And … to a menstruating woman … by Torah … Since … a presumption … the flow … is open, perhaps … zava … will continue

Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, commanded Rabbi … three matters: Do not go out alone at night; do not stand naked before a candle; and do not enter a new bathhouse, lest it collapse … Until when … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Until twelve months … And do not stand naked before a candle, … as it was taught … One who stands naked before a candle will become epileptic, and one who engages in intimacy by candlelight will have epileptic children.

the Sages taught: One who engages in intimacy in a bed upon which a baby is sleeping, that child becomes epileptic. And we said … only if … is not … one year old; however, … is one year old we have no … with it, … And … we said this only … that is sleeping near … feet; but … is sleeping near his head … we have no … with it. And we said this only if he does not place his hand on … but … he places his hands on … we have no … with it.

Do not go out alone at night, … as it was taught … not go out alone at night, neither on Tuesday nights nor on Shabbat nights, … because … Agrat, daughter of Maḥalat, she and 180,000 angels of destruction go out … And … each and every one … has permission to destroy by itself,

Initially, … were present every day. Once … met Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa … said to him: Had they not announced about you in the Heavens: Be careful of Ḥanina and his Torah, I would have placed you in danger. He said to her: If I am … important in Heaven, I decree upon you that you … never travel through inhabited places. She said to him: I beg you, leave me a little space. He left for her Shabbat nights and Tuesday nights.

And furthermore, once … met Abaye … said to him: Had they not announced about you in the Heavens: Be careful of Naḥmani, … and his Torah, I would have placed you in danger. He said to her: If I am … important in Heaven, I decree upon you that you … never pass through inhabited places. … But we see that, … pass through … say … These
are … on the paths [gazyata] … as horses … flee … and … come to lead them

And … said to Rav Asi: Do not live in a city where horses do not neigh and where dogs do not bark, … And do not live in a city where the mayor is a doctor, … And do not marry two … if you … marry two, marry a third

Rav said to Rav Kahana: … to turn over a carcass than to turn over his word, … Skin a carcass in the market and take payment, but do not say: I am a priest, or: I am a great man, and this matter disgusts me. … you ascend to the roof, … your food with you. … one hundred pumpkins in the city … a zuz, place … the corners
Rav said to Ḥiyya, his son: Do not … drinking medications, … And do not leap over a ditch, … And do not pull out a tooth, … And do not provoke a snake … And do not provoke a gentile,
the Sages taught: … three … one … not provoke: A small gentile, and a small snake, and a small … scholar. What is the reason? Because their authority stands behind their ears.

Rav said to Ayvu, his son: I struggled … you halakha but … did not succeed, … Come … I will teach you … mundane matters: Sell your merchandise while the dust … on your feet. … anything you sell … regret … except for wine, which you … sell without regret.
Open your purse … open your sack … a kav from the ground than a kor from the roof.

dates in your storeroom, run to the brewery … And how many … Rava said: Up to three se’a. Rav Pappa said: If I were not a beer manufacturer I would not have become wealthy. Some say … Rav Ḥisda who said: If I were not a beer manufacturer I would not have become wealthy. … What is … sudana, … Rav Ḥisda said: A pleasant secret [sod na’e] and acts of loving kindness,
Rav Pappa said: Anything … by means … requires collection, … Any sale on credit is uncertain whether or not … will come … And … if it … come … the money is bad.

Rabbi Yoḥanan said three matters, citing the people of Jerusalem: When you go to war do not go out first, but go out last. … so that … you will enter … first. And … make your Shabbat … weekday and do not be beholden to … beings. And exert yourself … with one upon whom the hour smiles.

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said three matters, citing the people of Jerusalem: Do not indulge in a shameful act … because of the incident that occurred … your daughter has grown up, … free your … slave and give … to her … And be careful with your wife with regard to her first son-in-law, … What is the reason … Rav Ḥisda said: Due to … licentiousness. Rav Kahana said: Due to … money … either of these … happen,

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Three … among those who inherit the World-to-Come: One who lives in Eretz Yisrael; one who raises his sons to … in Torah study; and one who recites havdala over wine at the conclusion of Shabbat. … What is … that … who … leaves some of … for havdala.

Rabbi Yoḥanan … said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, proclaims about … three … of people every day, … About a bachelor who lives in a city and does not sin … about a poor person who returns a lost object to its owners … and about a wealthy person who tithes his produce in private, … Rav Safra was a bachelor living in a city.

the tanna taught … before Rava and Rav Safra, Rav Safra’s face lit up … Rava said to him: … like the Master. Rather, … Rav Ḥanina and Rav Oshaya, who were cobblers in Eretz Yisrael, and they would sit in the marketplace of prostitutes and fashion shoes for prostitutes. And … would enter … look at them. … did not raise their eyes to look at … swore, … as follows: By the lives of the holy Sages of Eretz Yisrael.

The Holy One, Blessed be He, loves three … One who does not get angry; one who does not get drunk; and one who is forgiving. The Holy One, Blessed be He, hates three … One who says one … with his mouth and … another in his heart, … one who knows testimony about another … and does not testify on his behalf; and one who observes a licentious matter … by another … and testifies against him alone.

like … where Tuveya sinned … and Zigud came alone to testify about him before Rav Pappa. … Zigud be lashed. … said to him: Tuveya sinned and Zigud is lashed, … He said to him: Yes, as it is written: “One witness shall not rise up against a man” … and you testified against him alone. You have merely given him a bad reputation.

Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak said … Rav said: … he is … permitted to hate him, as it is stated: “If you see the donkey of he who hates you lying under its load” … What … who hates you … If you say … a gentile who hates … but wasn’t … taught … He who hates, of … spoke, is a Jew who hates … not a gentile who hates

Rather, … obvious … a Jew who hates … But is one permitted to hate … But isn’t it written: “You shall not hate your brother in your heart” … Rather, … where there are witnesses that he performed a sin. … everyone … also hate him. What is different … Rather, is it not … to a case like this, when he saw him … a licentious matter?

Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: … a mitzva to hate him, as it is stated: “The fear of God is to hate evil” … Rav Aḥa, son … Rava, said to Rav Ashi: What is … to … tell his teacher … he … will hate him? … said to him: If … knows … trusted by his teacher as two … he … tell him, and if … not … not tell him.
The Sages taught: … three … whose lives are not lives, … The compassionate, the hot tempered, and the delicate. Rav Yosef said: All of these … are … in me.
the Sages taught: … three … hate other … Dogs, roosters, and the Persian priests. And some say: Also prostitutes. And some say: Also Torah scholars in Babylonia.
the Sages taught: … three … love one another: Converts, slaves, and ravens.

Four … cannot be endured … An arrogant pauper; a wealthy person who denies … a lecherous old man; and a leader who lords over the community for no cause. And some say: Also one who divorces his wife once and twice and takes her back
And … the first tanna … Sometimes … her marriage contract, is large, … Alternatively, he has children with her and cannot divorce her,
Canaan commanded his sons … five matters … Love one another, love robbery, love promiscuity, hate your masters, and do not speak the truth.

Six matters are said with regard to a horse: … loves promiscuity, … loves war, its demeanor is arrogant, it despises sleep, it eats much, and it excretes little. And some say: … also attempts to kill its master in war.

Seven … ostracized by Heaven, … A Jew who does not have a wife; and one who has a wife but has no sons; and one who has sons whom he does not raise to … Torah study; and one who does not have phylacteries on his head, and phylacteries on his arm, and ritual fringes on his garment, and a mezuza in his doorway; and one who withholds shoes from his feet. And some say: Also one who does not sit with a group … of a mitzva.
Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Shmuel bar Marta said … Rabbi Yosei of Hutzal: From where … that one … not consult astrologers? As it is stated: “You shall be wholehearted with the Lord your God”

And from where … one who knows about another that he is greater than him, even in one matter, that he must treat him with respect? As it is stated: “Because a surpassing spirit was in him, the king thought to set him over the whole realm”
And … observing … pure blood, … is prohibited to engage in intimacy … Until when … Rav said: … a set interval of time

taught: … Yosef of Hutzal … is … Yosef the Babylonian. … he is … Isi ben Gur Arye, he is Isi ben Yehuda, he is Isi ben Gamliel, … he is Isi ben Mahalalel. And what is his … name? His … name … Isi ben Akavya. … Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Tavla is … Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Ḥakla, … is Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Ela.
Rabbi Yitzhak ben Aḥa … of halakha is … Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Pineḥas … of aggada. And your mnemonic … Listen my brothers and friends [shimu na aḥai vere’ai].

Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said, citing Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Elai: Eat an onion [batzal] and sit in the shade [batzel], … but do not eat … geese and chickens, as your heart will pursue you, … less to your food and your drink and … more on your house,

When Ulla came … he said … they say … proverb in the west, … One who eats a fat tail [alita] must hide in the attic [aliyata] … One who eats vegetables [kakulei] can lie down in the city’s garbage [kiklei]

MISHNA: … poured … the first cup … Beit Shammai say: One recites the blessing over the … day, … and thereafter he recites the blessing over the wine: … And Beit Hillel say: One recites the blessing over the wine and thereafter recites the blessing over the day.

GEMARA: The Sages taught … matters … between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel with regard to … a meal. Beit Shammai say: … one recites a blessing over the … day and thereafter recites a blessing over the wine, because the day causes the wine to come … The day has … been sanctified and the wine has not yet come.

And Beit Hillel say: One recites the blessing over the wine and thereafter recites a blessing over the day, because the wine causes kiddush to be recited. … Alternatively, the blessing over wine is … frequently and the blessing over the day is not … frequently, … a frequent … and an infrequent … the frequent … takes precedence … And … halakha … in accordance with the statement of Beit Hillel.
What is alternatively? … And if you say … there … two … and here … one; … they are two … a frequent … and an infrequent … the frequent … takes precedence
And … halakha … in accordance with the statement of Beit Hillel. … obvious … as a Divine Voice emerged … If you wish, say … before the Divine Voice
if you wish, say … after the Divine Voice … Rabbi Yehoshua, who said … one disregards a Divine Voice

MISHNA: … brought … before … He dips the ḥazeret … before he reaches the … the bread, … They brought before him matza and … and ḥaroset, and … two cooked dishes … although … ḥaroset is not a mitzva … Rabbi Eliezer ben Tzadok says: … a mitzva … And in … the Temple … they brought before him the body of the Paschal lamb.

GEMARA: Reish Lakish said: That is to say … mitzvot require intent. … since one does not eat … at the time of his obligation to … bitter herbs, … Who creates fruit of the ground. And … perhaps he did not intend … bitter herbs, … therefore … needs to dip it again for the purpose of bitter herbs. For if it could enter your mind … mitzvot do not require intent, why do you … two dippings? But he … dipped … once.
From where … Perhaps … actually mitzvot do not require intent. And that which you said, why do I … two dippings, … so that there … be a conspicuous … for the children,

And if you say: … so, let … teach us … other vegetables … taught us … other vegetables, I would have said … where there are other vegetables that one requires two dippings, … however, … only ḥazeret, he does not require two dippings, … teaches us … even … ḥazeret he requires two dippings, so that there be a conspicuous … for the children.
And furthermore, it was taught … one ate … doubtfully tithed produce, … he has fulfilled … he ate them without … intent … he has fulfilled … If he ate them in halves, … he has fulfilled
And … provided that he does not pause between eating … the other … more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf
is … tanna’im, as it was taught … Rabbi Yosei says: Although one … dipped the ḥazeret … a mitzva to bring before him ḥazeret and ḥaroset, and two cooked dishes.

And still … from where … Perhaps Rabbi Yosei maintains … mitzvot do not require intent, and … that we require two dippings is so that there … be a conspicuous … for the children. … If so, … what … mitzva?
What … two cooked foods … Rav Huna said: Beets and rice. … Rava would seek beets and rice … since … came from Rav Huna’s mouth.

Rav Ashi said: Learn … from … of Rav Huna, … no … who is concerned about that … of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri. As it was taught in … Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says: Rice is a type of grain … and one is liable … karet for … its leavened … and one fulfills his obligation with it on Passover,

Ḥizkiya said: … even … fish and … egg that … on it. Rav Yosef said: … requires two types of meat … one in remembrance of the Paschal lamb and … one in remembrance of the Festival … Ravina said: … even … the bone … gravy

obvious … where there are other vegetables … one recites over … other vegetables the blessing: Who creates fruit of the ground, and eats, … And then, … he recites the blessing: … eating bitter herbs, … and eats

what is … where there is only lettuce … Rav Huna said: One initially recites the blessing: Who creates fruit of the ground, over the bitter herbs, … and eats … And ultimately, … one recites the blessing: … eating bitter herbs, over … and eats

Rav Ḥisda strongly objects to this … after one fills his belly with … he then recites … blessing over it? Rather, Rav Ḥisda said: Initially one recites … blessings over … Who creates fruit of the ground, and: … eating bitter herbs, and he eats … and later … he eats lettuce without a blessing.

In Syria, they act in accordance with … Rav Huna. And Rav Sheshet, son … Rav Yehoshua, acted in accordance with … Rav Ḥisda. … And the halakha is in accordance with … Rav Ḥisda. … Rav Aḥa, son … Rava, would seek other vegetables … to preclude himself from … the dispute.

Ravina said: Rav Mesharshiya, son … Rav Natan, said to me … Hillel said as follows, citing tradition: A person … not wrap matza and bitter herbs together and eat … because … today, … matza … by Torah … and … bitter herbs … by rabbinic … And … bitter herbs, … by rabbinic … come and nullify … matza, … by Torah

And even according to the one who says … mitzvot do not nullify each other, that … by Torah … with … by Torah … by rabbinic … with … by rabbinic … However, … by Torah … with … by rabbinic … by rabbinic … comes and nullifies … by Torah

Who is the tanna that you heard … mitzvot do not nullify each other? It is Hillel, as it was taught … They said about Hillel that he would wrap … together and eat them, as it is stated: “They shall eat it with matzot and bitter herbs”

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … colleagues disagree with him, as it was taught … might … one … wrap … together and eat them in the manner that Hillel eats them; … the verse states: “They shall eat it with matzot and bitter herbs,” … even this, … by itself, and that, … by themselves. Rav Ashi strongly objects to this … If so, … what … even

Rather, Rav Ashi said: This is what this tanna is teaching: … might … one fulfills his obligation with them only if he wraps … together and eats them in the manner that Hillel eats them. … the verse states: “They shall eat it with matzot and bitter herbs,” … even … by itself and … by themselves.

Now that the halakha was stated neither in accordance with … Hillel nor in accordance with … the Rabbis, … recites the blessing: … eating matza, and eats … And then he recites the blessing: … over eating bitter herbs, and eats … And then he eats matza and lettuce together without a blessing in remembrance of the Temple, in the manner of Hillel
Rabbi Elazar said … Rav Oshaya said: Anything that is dipped in a liquid … requires … washing of … hands. … Rav Pappa said: Learn from … that … this lettuce

must submerge it in the ḥaroset, due to … poison … For if it could enter your mind … need not … submerge … why do I … wash hands … He did not touch … Actually, I will say to you: … need not submerge … and … poison dies. … from the smell … But … why do I … washing of hands … Perhaps one will submerge

And Rav Pappa said: A person … not leave bitter herbs in the ḥaroset … lest the sweetness … nullify its bitterness. And … require a … taste, and … not … Rav Ḥisda authorized Rabbana Ukva … and he taught: … washed his hands for the first dipping, … wash his hands … for the second dipping.
The Sages said … before Rav Pappa … was stated generally, … For if it could enter your mind … was stated here, … why do I … washing of … hands twice? … has … washed his hands once.
Rav Pappa said to them: On the contrary, … was stated … here, … For if it could enter your mind … was stated in general, why do I … two dippings?

Rather, what … was stated … here, … why do I … two washings of … hands? He has … washed his hands once. They say … Since he needs to recite … Haggadah and hallel … perhaps he will divert his thoughts and … will touch

Rava said: … one swallowed matza … he has fulfilled … one swallowed bitter herbs … he has not fulfilled … one swallowed matza and bitter herbs … he has fulfilled … of … matza, … he has not fulfilled … of … bitter herbs. … wrapped … in … net, … and swallowed them, he has not fulfilled … even of eating matza.

Rav Shimi bar Ashi said: Matza … before each and every … bitter herbs … before each and every … and ḥaroset … before each and every … And … one … remove the table only from before the one reciting … Haggadah.
Rav Huna says: All … also … before the one who recites … Haggadah. … And the halakha is in accordance with … Rav Huna.

Why does one remove the table? The school of Rabbi Yannai say: So that the children will notice … and they will ask: … Abaye was sitting before Rabba … He saw that they were removing the table from before him, and he said to … We have not yet eaten, and you are taking the table away from us? Rabba said to him: You have exempted us from reciting … Why is … different [ma nishtana],

Shmuel said … “The bread of affliction [leḥem oni]” … bread over which one answers [onim] matters, … That was also taught … Leḥem oni … bread over which one answers many matters. Alternatively, … “leḥem oni” is … written … Just as … the manner of a poor … to … a piece
so too, here … a piece … Alternatively: Just as the manner of a poor person … he heats … and his wife bakes … so too here; … he heats the oven and his wife bakes

although … ḥaroset is not a mitzva. … And if … is not a mitzva, for what … bring it … Rabbi Ami said: … due to … poison … Rav Asi said: … poison in lettuce … a radish. … for the poison in a radish … leeks. … the poison in leeks … hot … for the poison in all … hot … In the meantime, … let him say … Poison, poison, I remember you, and your seven daughters, and your eight daughters-in-law.

Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says … a mitzva. … What … mitzva? … Rabbi Levi says: … in remembrance of the apple, … And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … in remembrance of the mortar … Abaye said: Therefore, … must … tart and … must … thick. … tart in remembrance of the apple, and … must … thick in remembrance of the mortar.

was taught … in accordance with … Rabbi Yoḥanan: … spices … in remembrance of the hay … ḥaroset … is in remembrance of the mortar. Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, said: … the small shopkeepers in Jerusalem would say as follows: Come and take spices for yourselves for … mitzva.
MISHNA: … poured the second cup for … and here the son asks his father … And if the son does not have the intelligence … his father teaches him

Why is this night different from all other nights? As on all other nights we eat leavened bread and matza … on this night all … matza. As on all other nights we eat other vegetables; on this night … bitter herbs. … As on all other nights we eat … roasted, stewed, … cooked meat, … on this night all … roasted … As on all other nights we dip … once; … on this night … twice.

And according to the intelligence … of … son, his father teaches him … He begins with … disgrace and concludes with … glory. And he expounds from … “An Aramean tried to destroy my father” … until he concludes … the entire section.

GEMARA: The Sages taught: … his son is wise … asks him. And if he is not wise, his wife asks him. And if … not … he asks himself. And even … two Torah scholars who know the halakhot of Passover … ask each other.

Why is this night different from all other nights? As on all other nights we dip once; … on this night … twice. Rava strongly objects to this … Is that to say … every … day there is no alternative … dip once? … Rather, Rava said … this is what … is teaching: As on all other nights we are not obligated to dip even once; … on this night … twice.
Rav Safra strongly objects to this … obligatory for the children? … Rather, Rav Safra said … this is what … is teaching: We do not … dip even once; … on this night … twice.
begins … with disgrace and concludes with glory. … What … With disgrace? Rav said … At first our forefathers were idol worshippers, … And Shmuel said: … We were slaves.

Rav Naḥman said to his servant, Daru: … a slave who is freed by his master, who gives him gold and silver, what … the slave say to him? … said to him: He must thank and praise … He said to him: … you have exempted us from reciting … Why is this … different, … began to recite: We were slaves.
MISHNA: Rabban Gamliel would say: Anyone who did not say

these three matters on Passover has not fulfilled his obligation: … Paschal lamb, matza, and bitter herbs. … Paschal lamb … because the Omnipresent passed over [pasaḥ] the houses of our forefathers in Egypt, as it is stated: “That you shall say: It is the sacrifice of the Lord’s Paschal offering for He passed over

It was taught … Rabbi Yishmael said: One time I was walking along the road and I found one of … descendants … I said to him: Your fathers sought to enhance their honor and sought to diminish God’s honor … Now, … the honor of God remains as it was, … He diminished their honor,
