What … “And I have come due to your words” … This is as it is written: “And there stood before them seventy men of the Elders of the house of Israel, and Jaazaniah, son of Shaphan, standing in the midst of them, each man with his censer in his hand, and a thick cloud of incense went up” … “And the form of a hand was put forth, and I was taken by a lock of my head; and a spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the gate of the inner court that faces northward where

there was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes jealousy” … “And he brought me into the inner court of the Lord’s House, and behold at the opening of the Entrance Hall … of God, between the porch and the altar were about twenty-five men with their backs toward the Temple of the Lord, and their faces toward the east, and they worshipped the sun toward the east” … From the fact that it is stated “and their faces toward the east,” is it not clear that their backs were to the Sanctuary, … Rather, what … the verse states “their backs toward the Temple of the Lord”? This teaches that they would uncover … and defecate downward,

The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Michael, … Michael, your nation has sinned … He replied: Master of the Universe, … it be enough for the good … among them … He said to him: I will burn them and the good among them … Immediately, … “He spoke to the man clothed in linen and said: Go in between the wheelwork and beneath the cherub, and fill your hands with coals of fire from between the cherubs, and scatter them over the city; and he came before my eyes” … Immediately: “And the cherub stretched out his hand from between the cherubs into the fire that was between the cherubs, and took and put it into the hands of him that was clothed in linen, who took it and went out”

Rav Ḥana bar Bizna said … Rabbi Shimon Ḥasida said: If it were not for the fact that the embers cooled … from the hand of the cherub to the hand of Gabriel, … not a remnant or a refugee of the enemies of the Jewish people, … would have survived.

And it is written: “And behold, the man clothed in linen with the slate by his side, reported the matter saying: I have done as You have commanded me” … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: At that moment, they cast out Gabriel from behind the curtain [pargod], … and they struck him with sixty blows [pulsei] of fire. They said to him: If you did not do it, you did not do it; if you did do it, why did you not do it according to what you were commanded … Moreover, … you already did it, do you not have … One should not deliver … about destruction?

They … brought Dubiel, the ministering angel of the Persians and put him in the place of [baḥarikei] … and he served for twenty-one days. As it is written: “But the prince of the kingdom of Persia stood opposed to me for twenty-one days, but, lo, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me and I remained there beside the kings of Persia” … they gave him, … twenty-one kings … the seaport … Mashhig.

said: Write for me that the Jews … taxes [akarga] … They wrote it for him … Write for me that the Sages … taxes. They wrote … for him. When they wanted to sign … Gabriel stood from behind the curtain and said: “It is vain for you who rise early who sit up late to eat the bread of sorrow, for He gives His beloved sleep” … What … “for He gives His beloved sleep” … Rav Yitzḥak said: These are the wives of Torah scholars who disturb … sleep in this world … and … merit the World-to-Come. … They did not listen to

He said before Him: Master of the Universe, if all the wise men of other nations were placed on one side of the scale, and Daniel the beloved man were on the other side, would he not outweigh them? The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: Who is the one who teaches the virtue of My children? They said to Him: Master of the Universe, … Gabriel. He said to them: Let him come … is stated: “And I have come due to your words” … God … said … Let him ascend. They brought him up.

He came … found Dubiel … holding the letter in his hand. … wanted to take … from him, … swallowed it. Some say the letter was written, but it was not signed. Some say it was also signed, … when he swallowed it, … was erased. … This is … in the kingdom of Persia, there are … who pay taxes and there are … who do not pay taxes, … “And when I depart from him, the prince of Greece comes” … screamed and screamed … but no one listened to him.

If you wish, say … that bathing is considered affliction, from where do we … As it is written: “And to Ebiathar the priest the king said: Get to Anatoth to your fields, for you are deserving of death. But I will not put you to death today, because you carried the Ark of the Lord God before David my father, and because you have been afflicted in all that my father was afflicted” … And it is written with regard to David: “For they said the people is hungry, and weary, and thirsty in the wilderness” … Hunger … from … bread … and thirst … from … water … weary … from what? Is it not from bathing? … And perhaps … wearing shoes?
Rather, … Rav Yitzḥak said: … from here: “As cold water on a weary soul, … But perhaps … from … drinking? … Is it written: As cold water in a weary soul? … “on a weary soul” is written,

wearing shoes … from where do we … As it is written: “And David went up by the ascent of the Mount of Olives, and wept as he went up, and he had his head covered, and was walking barefoot” … Barefoot … of what? Is it not … of wearing shoes? … perhaps … from a horse and whip.

Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: … from here, … “Go and loose the sackcloth from your loins, and remove your shoe from your foot” … And it is written: “And he did so, walking naked and barefoot” … Barefoot … of what? Is it not … wearing shoes? … And say … with patched shoes. Because if you do not say this, … actually naked? Rather, … ragged garments. Here too, … in patched shoes.

Rather, … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said … from here: … “Withhold your foot from being barefoot, and your throat from thirst” … Keep yourself from sin, so that your feet will not come to be barefoot; keep your tongue from idle talk, so that your throat will not come to be thirsty.
From where do we … conjugal relations is called affliction? As it is written, … “If you shall afflict my daughters, and if you shall take … wives
“If you shall afflict … from conjugal relations, “and if you shall take … from … rival … And say that this … and that … rival … Is it written: If you take? “And if you shall take” is written.

And say that this … and that … are referring to … rival … One … his … rivals. … And one … rivals who … come to him from the world … similar … “if you shall take.” … Is it written: If you take and if you afflict? … “if you shall afflict and if you shall take” is written.

Rav Pappa said to Abaye: But conjugal relations themselves are called affliction, as it is written: … and he lay with her and afflicted her” … He said to him: There, … afflicted her from different relations,

The Sages taught: It is prohibited to bathe part of the body … the whole body. But if one is dirty from mud or excrement, he … bathe in his … manner, and he … not be concerned … it is prohibited to … part of the body just as … the whole body. But if one was sick … or if one had scabs on his head … he … smear … in his … manner, and he … not be concerned
The school of Menashe taught … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: A woman … rinse one hand in water, … and give bread to her child, and she … not be concerned
They said about Shammai the Elder that he did not want to feed … with one hand, … they decreed that he must feed … with two hands, … What is the reason … Abaye said: Due to … Shivta,
The Sages taught: One who goes to greet his father or his teacher, or to greet one who is greater than him … cross … until his neck is in the water, and he … not be concerned

A dilemma was raised before them, … What … a teacher … to … student? … Come … hear … Rav Yitzḥak bar bar Ḥana said: I saw Ze’iri, who went … to Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi, his student. Rav Ashi said: … that … Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi who went to Ze’iri, his teacher.

Rava permitted those … right side … to pass through the water to guard the fruit … Abaye said to Rava: … was taught that supports your … Guards of fruit … cross … until their necks are in the water, and they … not be concerned

Rav Yosef permitted … people … Bei Tarbu to cross in the water to come to the lecture … on … He did not, … permit them to go … Abaye said to him: If so, you are obstructing them … in the future. … Some say … permitted them to come and permitted them to go … Abaye said to him: Granted, … to come, that is well. But what is the reason … to go … So as not to obstruct them … in the future.

Rav Yehuda and Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda were standing on the bank of the Pappa River next to the Ḥatzdad crossing, and Rami bar Pappa was standing on the other side … He raised his voice to them … What is … crossing over to come to you to ask a halakha? Rav Yehuda said to him: … Rav and Shmuel who both say: One … cross … provided that he does not remove his hand from under the hem of his cloak. … Some say … Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda said to him: We learned … cross over, provided … he does not remove his hand from the hem of his cloak.

Rav Yosef strongly objects to this: And on a weekday is it permitted … in such … But isn’t it written … “He measured a thousand cubits, and he led me through the water; the water was ankle deep” … here … is permitted to pass through … up to the ankles.

“Again he measured a thousand and he led me through the water, the water was knee deep” … here … is permitted to pass through … up … the knees. “He measured a thousand and led me through the water up to the waist” … here … is permitted to pass through … up to the waist. From this … forward: “And he measured a thousand, a river that I could not pass through”
Abaye said: … a river … flowing water is different.

One might think … could cross … by swimming. The verse states: “For the water had swollen into saḥu waters” … What … “saḥu waters” … a boat … shiyuta], as sailing [shayta] is … called swimming [sayḥa]. I might have thought … could pass across in a small boat [burni]. … the verse states: “No galley with oars shall go” … might have thought he could pass through in a large boat. … the verse states: “Neither shall a fishing boat [tzi adir] be able to cross it” … From where … be inferred … Rav Yosef translated … A fishing boat [sfinat tzayyadin] will not travel on it and a large ship will not cross it.

Rabbi Yehuda ben Pazi said: Even the Angel of Death does not have permission to pass through it … as it is written here: “No galley with oars [ani shayt] can travel” and … it was written there: … From going to and fro [mishut] the earth

Rabbi Pineḥas said in the name of Rav Huna of Tzippori: The spring that comes forth from inside the Holy of Holies … at first … and resembles grasshoppers’ antennae … Once it reaches the opening of the Sanctuary it becomes … as … thread of … warp; once it reaches the Entrance Hall … it becomes … as … thread of … woof, … Once it reaches the opening of … courtyard it becomes like the mouth of a small jug. This is as we learned … Rav Eliezer ben Ya’akov says: Water,

in the future, will bubble from under the threshold of the Temple. From this … forward, … will grow in strength and rise until it reaches the opening of David’s house, … When it reaches the opening of David’s house, it will become a flowing river in which zavim and zavot, menstruating women, and women after childbirth will bathe … As it is stated: “On that day there shall be a fountain opened for the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for purification and for sprinkling”
Rav Yosef said: From here, there is an allusion that a menstruating woman must … sit up to her neck in water, … But the halakha is not in accordance with his

well … Yom Kippur … there are no shoes, … Shabbat, when there are shoes, what … Neḥemya, the son-in-law of the Nasi, said: I saw Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi come to a pool of water … and they crossed it while wearing
well … shoes … what is there to say … sandals? … Rav Riḥumi said: I saw Ravina cross … wearing … Rav Ashi said: If he is … sandals, … not … ab initio,

The Exilarch came to … Rav Natan’s study hall in Hagronya. Rafram and all the Sages came to the lecture, … Ravina did not come. The next day, … Rafram wanted to remove … Ravina from the mind … the Exilarch, … What is the reason … the Master did not come to the lecture? He said to him: My foot hurt. … You should have put shoes on. … It was the back of the foot

You should have worn sandals, … He said to him: There was a pool of water on the way … He said to him: You should have crossed it wearing … He said to him: Does the Master not hold … Rav Ashi said: … not … sandals … ab initio?

Yehuda bar Gerogarot taught: It is prohibited to sit on … clay on Yom Kippur. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: … clay … dripping wet, … Abaye said … dripping wet enough to make something else wet. Rav Yehuda said: … permitted to cool off with fruit … Rav Yehuda … cooled off … a squash

Rabba cooled off by … a baby [yanuka] … Rava cooled off with a silver cup. Rav Pappa said: … silver cup … full, it is prohibited; … not full, it is permitted. … a ceramic … this and that are prohibited, since … seeps through … Rav … said: A silver cup that is not full is also prohibited because it can slip [mizderiv]

Ze’eira bar Ḥama, … host … Rabbi Ami, and Rabbi Asi, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, and all the Sages of Caesarea … said to Rav Yosef, son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: Son of a lion, come, I will tell you … a wonderful custom that your father used to perform. He had a cloth that … on the day before Yom Kippur by soaking it in water and … making it … like a dried cloth. And the next day he wiped his face, hands, and feet with it. … the day before the Ninth of Av, … soak the … in water and the next day pass it over his eyes.

Similarly, when Rabba bar Mari came … he said: The day before the Ninth of Av they bring one a cloth, and he … soak it in water and place it under his head. The next day, … he … wipe his face, hands, and feet … On the day before Yom Kippur, they bring one a cloth, and he … soak it in water and … make it like a dried cloth. The next day, he … pass it over his eyes. Rabbi Ya’akov said to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Taḥlifa: You told us the opposite. … and we objected to you … wringing,

Rav Menashya bar Taḥalifa said … Rav Amram said … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: They asked Rabbi Elazar … an Elder who sits … in a yeshiva receive permission … to permit … firstborn animals permitted, … to … firstborn animals permitted, or not?

What are they asking? … This is what they are asking, like this … Rav Idi bar Avin, … said: This matter, … was given to the house of the Nasi to raise its stature. … must permission be received, … Or, perhaps because … is an Elder who sits … in a yeshiva, there is no need. Rav Tzadok ben Ḥaluka rose to his feet and said: I saw Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra, who was an Elder who sat in the yeshiva and who stood before the grandfather of this … ask permission … to permit firstborn animals.

Rabbi Abba said to him: … was not how the incident was. Rather this was the incident: Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra was a priest, and he raised the following dilemma: Is the halakha in accordance with … Rabbi Meir, … said: One who is suspect in … area … not judge it and … not testify … it? … Or perhaps the halakha is in accordance with … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, … said: … is believed about his fellow but is not believed about himself. He resolved … him: … halakha is in accordance with … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
They raised … dilemma … them, … What is … going out in sandals made of

cork on Yom Kippur? … Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Naḥmani stood on his feet … and said: I saw that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi went out on Yom Kippur in cork sandals, and I said to him: What … on a communal fast … He said to me: … no different, … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: I saw Rabbi Elazar from Nineveh go out in cork sandals on a communal fast day, and I said to him: What … on Yom Kippur? He said to me: … no different, … Rav Yehuda went out … in reed sandals. Abaye went out in … palm fiber. Rava went out in … reeds. … Rabba bar Rav Huna wrapped a scarf around his feet and went out.

Rami bar Ḥama raised an objection: … an amputee … go out with his … prosthetic leg … these are the words of Rabbi Meir. But Rabbi Yosei prohibits it. And … was taught in that regard … And they agree that it is prohibited to go out wearing it on Yom Kippur. … Abaye said: There, … there are rags … due … pleasure

Rava said to him: And if … is not a garment, … rags make it into a garment? … And furthermore, any … pleasure that is not … shoes, is it prohibited on Yom Kippur? … And Rabba bar Rav Huna would wrap a scarf on his feet and go out, … Furthermore, … From … that it teaches in the latter clause: If … has a receptacle … for rags it … ritual impurity … it may be inferred that in the first clause we are not dealing with … has … rags.

Rather, Rava said: Actually, according to everyone, … is … a shoe, and with regard to Shabbat this is what they disagree about: One Sage, … holds that we decree … lest … slip off and one come to carry it four cubits … and one Sage, … holds that we do not decree

The Sages taught: Young children are permitted … all of … except for wearing shoes. … What is different … wearing shoes? … because … will say … adults did this for him, … those … also, … they will say … adults did this for him, … they … say that they did this for him yesterday,

say … shoes as well. They … say that they did this for him yesterday. … shoes, it is impossible … did it for him yesterday, … As Shmuel said: He who desires a taste of death should put on shoes and go to sleep.

But … is teaching … they are permitted … ab initio. … Rather, … The Sages decreed … those … that are not … for … growth, … the Sages did not decree … those … that are … for … growth. … Abaye said: … mother told me: A child’s growth … hot water and oil … he grows a little, … egg with kutaḥa, … When he grows a little … vessels to break, … Rabba … bought cracked ceramic vessels for his children, and they broke them

the king and the bride … wash their faces … Who is … the mishna? … Rabbi Ḥananya ben Teradyon, as it was taught … The king and the bride … not wash their faces … Rabbi Ḥananya ben Teradyon says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer: A king and a bride … wash their faces. … A new mother … not wear shoes … Rabbi Ḥananya ben Teradyon says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer: A new mother … wear shoes.

what is the reason … the king … Because it is written: “Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty” … What is the reason … a bride … So that she should not … repulsive to her husband. … Rav said to Rabbi Ḥiyya: For how long … a bride? He said to him: As it was taught … we do not prevent the bride from wearing perfumes … the entire … thirty days
A new mother … wear shoes. … Due to the cold
Shmuel said: If … due to the danger of scorpions, he is permitted
one who eats … volume of a large date … Rav Pappa asked:

The large date-bulk that they said … with its pit or without its pit? Rav Ashi asked … a bone … a barley-grain-bulk … with its husk or without its husk? … a wet … or a dry … Rav Ashi did not ask … that Rav Pappa … it is stated … Large, … as large as possible, … Rav Pappa did not ask … that Rav Ashi … Wet … is called shibbolet … without its shell … is called ushla.

Rava said … Rav Yehuda said: The volume of a large date that they said … larger than an egg-bulk. The Sages have an … tradition that with this … mind … is settled, … Less than this … the mind is not settled. … raises an objection … An incident … They brought a cooked dish to Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai to taste, and … to Rabban Gamliel two dates and a tankard of water. … said … Bring them up to the sukka, … And … was taught in that regard: … did not … because that is the halakha, … Rather, they wished to be stringent upon themselves
And when they gave Rabbi Tzadok food … less than an egg-bulk … he held it in a cloth … And he ate it outside of the sukka and did not recite … afterward.

an egg-bulk is required … a sukka. If it should enter your mind … volume of the large date that they spoke of is larger than … an egg-bulk, … Now, … two dates without their pits are not … an egg. … can the volume of a large date and its pit … greater than that of an egg-bulk? Rav Yirmeya said: Yes, … two dates without their pits are not equal … an egg-bulk, the volume of a large date and its pit are larger than an egg-bulk, … Rav Pappa said: This … that people say: … two kav of dates … one kav and more of pits,

Rava said: … There, … this is the reasoning … due to … are fruit, and fruit need not … a sukka … raises an objection. Rabbi … said: When we would learn Torah with Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua, they brought before us figs and grapes, and we ate them as a casual meal outside of the sukka. … a casual meal, yes, … a fixed meal … not … say we ate them as if … a casual meal, … outside of the sukka,
If you wish, say … We ate … as a fixed meal, and we ate bread as a casual meal with … outside of the sukka.

Let us say that … supports … Therefore, if one completed … with types of sweets, he has fulfilled … If it should enter your mind … fruit … required … a sukka, … let it teach fruit. … What … types of sweets … fruit. … And if you wish, say … a place where fruits are uncommon,

Rav Zevid … said: … the volume of a large date that they spoke … is less than an egg-bulk, as we learned … Beit Shammai say: … leaven, … the volume of an olive-bulk … leavened bread … is the volume of a large date.

And we discussed it: What is the reason … of Beit Shammai? … let the Merciful One write … “Leavened bread,” and … not need … “Leaven.” I would say, … If leavened bread, whose leavening ability is … strong, is prohibited … an olive-bulk, all the more so … not leaven, whose leavening ability is strong … the Merciful One distinguishes … them … taught you … the measure for one is not … the measure for the other. … leaven … an olive-bulk, … leavened bread, … volume of a large date.

And if it should enter your mind … The volume of the large date that they spoke … is greater than an egg-bulk, since Beit Shammai are searching for the measure … larger than an olive-bulk, … let them teach an egg-bulk … Alternatively, if they are … the same … they should have taught an egg-bulk, … Rather, … not conclude from here that the volume of a large date is less than an egg-bulk?

From where … Perhaps I could actually say to you … the volume of a large date that they said is larger than an egg-bulk; … normal … an egg-bulk, … Alternatively, … that … are equal, and … chose … one of them.

Rather, … from here: How much … to obligate … an invitation … zimmun] … An olive-bulk … the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda says: An egg-bulk … With regard to what do they disagree? Rabbi Meir holds … “And you shall eat”; this … eating. “And be satisfied”; this … drinking. … eating … an olive-bulk. Rabbi Yehuda holds: “And you shall eat and be satisfied” … eating that causes satisfaction, and what is that? … an egg-bulk.

And if it should enter your mind … the volume of the large date that they spoke … is larger than an egg-bulk, … Now … an egg-bulk satisfies, … it does not settle the mind, … Rather, … not conclude from … the volume of a large date that they said is less than the size of an egg-bulk? … of an egg-bulk satisfies … the volume of a large date … settles his mind.
It was taught … Rabbi … says:

All the measures … an olive-bulk, except for … food … impure, because the verse changed its expression … and the Sages altered the measure … The proof of this, … Yom Kippur. … How did the … verse changed its expression? … from: … shall not be afflicted” … How did the Sages change its measure? … the volume of a large date-bulk,
And what … A proof for this … Yom Kippur? … If … there, … I would have said that that is the style of the verse,

From where do we … impure foods … the volume of an egg-bulk? Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Elazar said that the verse states: “Of all food [okhel] which may be eaten [ye’akhel], … food that comes on account of food, … And which … is that? A chicken egg. … And say … a kid, … It lacks ritual slaughter. … And say … a ben pekua. … requires cutting,
say … egg … bulk … bar yokhani. … If you grasped many, you did not grasp anything; if you grasped few, you grasped something. … say … a very small bird’s egg.
Rabbi Abbahu himself said: … “Of all food which may be eaten.” … food that you … eat at one time. The Sages estimated: The esophagus cannot hold more … a chicken’s egg,
Rabbi Elazar said: One who … eats … fat … today must write down the … measure … lest another court come … and increase the measure.

What does … increase the measure? If we say … will obligate … an offering … bulk … a small olive, … - … Wasn’t it taught … not to be done, and be guilty” … one who repents due to his awareness, … brings an offering for his unwitting
one who does not repent due to his awareness … does not bring an offering for his unwitting
Rather, … will not obligate … an offering until he has … of a large olive,
According to what entered his mind initially, … obligate … an offering … small olive, what … increase the measure? … perhaps there will be an increase in offerings … due to … measure

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Measures and punishments are halakha … to Moses from Sinai. … The punishments … are written … Rather, this is … said: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Measures … for punishments are halakha … to Moses from Sinai.

This was also taught … Measures of punishments are halakha … to Moses from Sinai. Others say: … were instituted by the court of Jabez. … Isn’t it written: “These are the mitzvot which the Lord commanded Moses for the children of Israel at Mount Sinai” … that a prophet is not permitted to introduce … element … from here on. Rather, … forgot … reestablished

one who drinks a cheekful … Rabbi Yehuda said … Shmuel said: This does not … cheeks actually full. Rather, … if one pushes … to one side … and it appears as though his cheek were full. … Didn’t we learn … A cheekful, … Say: Like … cheeks full

raises an objection … How much … drink … to be liable? Beit Shammai say: A quarter- … and Beit Hillel say: … cheeks full. Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Eliezer: Like … cheeks full … Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: … amount … swallow
Is … preferable to the mishna? Since it was established … so that it appears … so too, … that looks like … If so, … this is … Rabbi Eliezer, … between them … a paltry cheekful,
Rav Hoshaya strongly objects to this … If so, … this is … Beit Shammai’s leniencies and Beit Hillel’s stringencies, … He said to him:
When … was asked, … the question was asked … about Og, king of Bashan, … it is Beit Shammai … stringent,

Rabbi Zeira strongly objects to this … What is different … eating, … that all people … volume of a large date; and what is different … drinking, where each and every … according to his own measure, … Abaye said to him: The Sages have … tradition … the volume of the large date, that … this … settles his mind, … less than this … does not settle … drinking, his mind is settled with … his own … but his mind is not settled … of his fellow

Rabbi Zeira strongly objects to this … Is everyone … with … the volume of a large date, and … Og, king of Bashan, … with the volume of a large date? … Abaye said to him: The Sages have … tradition that this … settles his mind, … less than this … does not settle his mind. However, everyone … greatly … Og, king of Bashan, … a little

Rabbi Zeira strongly objects to this … fatty meat, … volume of a large date, … grapevine shoots, … with the volume of a large date? Abaye said to him: The Sages have … tradition that with this … one’s mind is settled, … with less than this … his mind is not settled. However, … fatty meat, … greatly … grapevine shoots, … a little

Rava strongly objects to this: … of an olive-bulk … within … to eat a half-loaf of bread. … volume of a large date, … within … to eat a half-loaf of bread. … Abaye said to him: The Sages have … tradition that … this … his mind is settled; but … a longer … his mind is not settled,

Rava strongly objects to this: … volume of a large date … within … to eat a half-loaf of bread; … half of a half-loaf, … within … to eat a half-loaf of bread. Rav Pappa said to him: … Leave … ritual impurity of the body … because that is not by Torah law

What is the rationale … of the one who said: … primary … song … with the mouth? … as it is written: “And it came to pass, when the trumpeters and the singers were as one to make one sound”

And … the other … too, … isn’t it written: “And Hezekiah commanded … This is what … is saying: “The song of the Lord began,” … with the mouth; “with the instruments of David, King of Israel,” … to sweeten the sound,

And … the other … too, … isn’t it written: “And it came to pass, when the trumpeters and the singers were as one,” … This is what … is saying: … singers … similar to the trumpeters; just as trumpeters … with an instrument, so too … singers … with an instrument.

MISHNA: One who did not see the Celebration of the Place of the Drawing … never saw celebration in his days. … At the conclusion of the first Festival … descended … to the Women’s Courtyard, where they would introduce a significant repair, … There were golden candelabra … there … And … four basins … of gold at the top … And … four ladders for each and every … and … four children from the priesthood trainees, and in their hands … pitchers … of 120 log … that they would pour into each and every basin. From the worn trousers of the priests and their belts they would loosen … and with them they would light … And … there was not a courtyard in Jerusalem that was not illuminated from the light of the Place of the Drawing
pious and … men of action would dance before

with flaming torches … in their hands, and they would say before them passages of song and praise … And the Levites … on lyres, harps, cymbals, and trumpets, and countless … musical instruments. … on the fifteen stairs that descend from the Israelites’ courtyard to the Women’s Courtyard, corresponding to the fifteen … Ascents in Psalms, … upon which … Levites stand with musical instruments and recite … song.

And … Two priests stood at the Upper Gate that descends from the Israelites’ courtyard to the Women’s Courtyard, with two trumpets in their hands. … the rooster crowed … they sounded a tekia, and sounded a terua, and sounded a tekia. … they … reached the tenth stair … sounded a tekia, and sounded a terua, and sounded a tekia, … they reached the … Courtyard … sounded a tekia, and sounded a terua, and sounded a tekia.

they reached the ground … sounded a tekia, and sounded a terua, and sounded a tekia. They continued sounding … until they reached the gate … which … exits to the east, … they reached the gate … which … exits to the east, they turned from … east to … west, … and said: Our ancestors who were in this place … “with their backs toward the Sanctuary of the Lord, and their faces toward the east; and they worshipped the sun toward the east” … and we, our eyes are to God. Rabbi Yehuda says … they would repeat and say: We are to God, and our eyes are to God.

GEMARA: The Sages taught: One who did not see the Celebration of the Place of the Drawing … never saw celebration in his life. One who did not see Jerusalem in its glory, never saw a beautiful city. One who did not see the Temple in its constructed … never saw a magnificent structure. … What is … Abaye said, and some say … Rav Ḥisda … This … building of Herod,

With what … did he construct it? Rava said: … with stones of … marble and white marble [marmara]. Some say: … with stones of blue marble and white marble. … one row … protruded and one row … indented, so that the plaster would take … He thought to plate … with gold, … the Sages said to him: Leave it … as it is better this way, as … it has the appearance of waves of the sea.

It is taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: One who did not see the great synagogue [deyofloston] of Alexandria of Egypt never saw the glory of Israel. They said … was like a large basilica [basileki], … a colonnade within a colonnade. At times there were six hundred thousand … and … six hundred thousand … in it, twice the number of those who left Egypt. In it there were seventy-one golden chairs [katedraot], corresponding to the seventy-one … of the Great Sanhedrin, each of which … no less than twenty-one thousand talents of gold. And … a wooden platform at the center. The sexton of the synagogue … stand on it, with the scarves in his hand. And … when … reached … to answer amen, … waved the scarf and all the people … answer amen.

And … would not sit mingled. Rather, the goldsmiths … among themselves, and the silversmiths among themselves, and the blacksmiths among themselves, and the coppersmiths among themselves, and the weavers among themselves. And when a poor … entered there, he would recognize people … his craft, and he would turn to … there. And from there … his livelihood … the livelihood … members of his household,

Abaye said: All of … were killed by Alexander … of Macedonia. … What is the reason … they were punished … due to … that they violated … this verse: “You shall henceforth return no more that way” … and they returned.

When … arrived, he found them, … that they were reading … in the … scroll: “The Lord will bring a nation against you from far, … He said, … Now, since that man sought to come by ship in ten days, … a wind carried it and the ship arrived in … five days, … he set upon them and slaughtered them.

At the conclusion of … Festival … What … significant repair? Rabbi Elazar said … it is like that which we learned: … were smooth, … initially. … surrounded … with a balcony [gezuztra]. And they instituted that … women should sit above and … men below.

The Sages taught … Initially, women would … on the inside … and the men … on the outside … And they would come to … levity … instituted that the women should sit on the outside and the men on the inside, and still they would come to … levity. … they instituted … that the women would sit above and the men below.
How could one do so, … But isn’t it written … “All this … in writing, … the Lord has made me wise by His hand upon me,
Rav said: They found a verse, and interpreted it homiletically

“The land will eulogize, each family separately; the family of the house of David separately, and their women separately, … They said: And are … matters not … a fortiori? If in the future, … when … are involved in … eulogy and … the evil inclination does not dominate them, … the Torah says: Men separately and women separately; … now that they are involved in … Celebration … and … the evil inclination dominates them, … all the more so
what is the nature of this eulogy? … Rabbi Dosa and the Rabbis disagree concerning this … One said … for Messiah ben Yosef who was killed … And one said … for the evil inclination that was killed.

Granted, according to the one who said … Messiah ben Yosef who was killed, this … which is written … “And they shall look unto Me because they have thrust him through; and they shall mourn for him, as one mourns for his only son” … However, according to the one who said … for the evil inclination that was killed, … need to conduct a eulogy … this? … one should conduct a celebration. Why, … did they cry?

as Rabbi Yehuda taught: In the future, … God will bring the evil inclination and slaughter it in the presence of the righteous and in the presence of the wicked. … the righteous … appears to them as a high mountain, and … the wicked … appears … them as … strand of hair. These weep and those weep. The righteous weep and say: How were we able to overcome so high a mountain? And the wicked weep and say: How were we unable to overcome this strand of hair? And even the Holy One, Blessed be He, will wonder with them, as it is stated … “So says the Lord of hosts: If it be wondrous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, it should also be wondrous in My eyes”

Rav Asi said: Initially, … the evil inclination is like a strand of a spider’s web [bukhya]; and ultimately it is like … ropes of a wagon, as it is stated: “Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as if it were with a wagon rope”

The Sages taught: To Messiah ben David, who is destined to be revealed swiftly in our time, the Holy One, Blessed be He, says: Ask of Me anything and I will give you … as it is stated: “I will tell of the decree; … this day have I begotten you, ask of Me, and I will give the nations for your inheritance, … Once … saw Messiah ben Yosef, who was killed, he says … Master of the Universe, I ask of you only life; … says to him: Life? … before you stated … your father, David, already prophesied about you … as it is stated: “He asked life of You, You gave it to him;

Rabbi Avira, and some say Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, taught: The evil inclination has seven names. The Holy One, Blessed be He, called it evil, as it is stated: “For the inclination of a man’s heart is evil from his youth” … Moses called it uncircumcised, as it is stated: “And circumcise the foreskin of your hearts” … David called it impure, as it is stated: “Create for me a pure heart, O God” … by inference, there is an impure

Solomon called it enemy, as it is stated: “If your enemy is hungry, give him bread to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink; for you will heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord will reward you” … Do not read … And the Lord will reward you [yeshalem lakh]; rather … will reconcile it to you [yashlimenu lakh].

Isaiah called it a stumbling block, as it is stated: “And He will say: Cast you up, cast you up, clear the way, take up the stumbling block out of the way of My people” … Ezekiel called it stone, as it is stated: “And I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh” … Joel called it hidden one, as it says: “But I will remove the northern one [hatzefoni] far off from you” … The Sages taught … “But I will remove the northern one [hatzefoni] far off from you,” … this is … the evil inclination. … that it is always hidden [tzafun] in the heart of man.

“And will drive it to a land barren and desolate” … where there are no people for … to incite. … “With its face toward the eastern [hakadmoni] sea” … as it set its eyes on the First … mukdam … Temple and destroyed it, and killed the Torah scholars that … in it; “and its end toward the western [ha’aḥaron] sea” … as it set its eyes on the Second … aḥaron … Temple and destroyed it, and killed the Torah scholars that … in it; “its foulness may come up, and its ill odor may come up” … as it forsakes the nations of the world and incites the enemies of … Jewish people: … “Because it has done greatly” … Abaye said: And … Torah scholars more than … everyone

like this … as Abaye once heard a certain man say to a certain woman: Let us rise early and go on the road. … said … I will go … prevent them from … the prohibition … He went after them … three parasangs in a marsh … When they were taking leave of each other, he heard that they were saying: … a long distance … and the company was pleasant company.

Abaye said: … if … it had been one whom I hate, … he would not have been able to restrain himself … he went and leaned against the doorpost, … and feeling regret. A certain Elder came … taught him: Anyone who is greater than another, his … inclination is greater than his.
Rabbi Yitzḥak said: A person’s inclination overcomes him each day, as it is stated: “Only

evil all day” … Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person’s … inclination overcomes him each day and seeks to kill him, as it stated: “The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to kill him” … And if not for the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who assists … he would not overcome it, as it is stated: “The Lord will not leave him in his hand, nor suffer him to be condemned when he is judged”

The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: If this scoundrel, … accosted you, … drag it to the study hall … If it is … a stone, it will be dissolved … If it is … iron, it will be shattered. … If it is … stone, it will be dissolved, as it is written: “Ho, everyone who is thirsty, come you for the water” … and it is written: “Stones were worn by water” … If it is … iron, it will be shattered, as it is written: “Is not My word like fire, says the Lord; and like a hammer that shatters rock”

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The evil inclination incites a person … in this world, and … testifies against him in the next world, as it is stated: “He that delicately brings up his servant from a child shall have him become a master [manon] at the last” … as in Rabbi Ḥiyya’s … alef … tet … beit … ḥet, … Witness … sahada … is called manon.

Rav Huna raised a contradiction … It is written: “For the spirit of harlotry caused … to err” … And it is … written: … is within them” … Initially, it causes them to err … and ultimately, … within them.

Rava said: Initially, … called … a traveler … Subsequently, … calls it a guest, … Ultimately, … calls it man, … As it is stated … “And there came a traveler to the rich man, and he was reluctant to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to prepare for the guest” … And it is written … “And he took the poor man’s lamb, and prepared it for the man that was come to him.”
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: A man has a small organ … If he starves … is satiated; … if he satiates … is starving, … as it is stated: “When they were fed, they became full,

Rav Ḥana bar Aḥa said … in the school of Rav say: … four … the Holy One, Blessed be He, … regrets that He created them, … And these are they: Exile, Chaldeans, and Ishmaelites, and the evil inclination. Exile, as it is written: “Now therefore, for what am I here, says the Lord, seeing that My people is taken away for naught” … Chaldeans, as it is written: “Behold the land of the Chaldeans, this is the people that was not”

Ishmaelites, as it is written: “The tents of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure, in whatsoever God brings with His hand” … The evil inclination, as it is written: … and her that I corrupted”

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Were it not for these three verses … the legs of the enemies of … Jewish people, … would have collapsed, … One, as it is written: “And her that I corrupted,” … And one, as it is written: “Behold, as the clay in the potter’s hand, so are you … And the other … “And I will take away the heart of stone out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh”
Rav Pappa said: … from this … as well: “And I will put My spirit within you,

“The Lord then showed me four craftsmen” … Who are these four craftsmen? Rav Ḥana bar Bizna said … Rabbi Shimon Ḥasida said: … Messiah ben David, Messiah ben Yosef, Elijah, and the righteous … Priest, … Rav Sheshet raised an objection: If so, … that which is written … “And he said to me: These are the horns that scattered Judea” … these … are coming for their enemies,

said to … Go to the end of the verse: “These then are come to frighten them, to cast down the horns of the nations, which lifted up … horn against the land of Judah to scatter it.” … said to him: Why … I … with … Ḥana in … aggada,

“And this shall be peace: When the Assyrian shall come into our land, and when he shall tread in our palaces, then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight princes among men” … Who are these seven shepherds? … David … in the middle; Adam, Seth, and Methuselah are to his right; Abraham, Jacob, and Moses are to his left. And who are the eight princes among men? … Yishai, Saul, Samuel, Amos, Zephania, Zedekiah, Messiah, and Elijah.

And there were four ladders … taught: The height of the candelabrum … is fifty cubits. And … four children from the priesthood trainees … and in their hands jugs of oil … of 120 log … A dilemma was raised: … 120 log altogether, or perhaps each and every … Come … hear … And in their hands … jugs of oil, each … of thirty log, that were all … 120 log.

taught: And these … were superior … to the son of Marta, daughter of Baitos, … They said about the son of Marta, daughter of Baitos, that he would take two thighs of a large bull … that … purchased for one thousand zuz, and walk … heel to toe, … his brethren the priests would not allow him do so, due to … “In the multitude of people is the King’s glory”
what … superior? If we say it is due to the weight … these … thighs are heavier … Rather, … there, … ramp … and … four … and … not steep; here … ladders, and … very steep.
And there was not a courtyard in Jerusalem … taught:
a woman would … sort wheat by the light of the … Place of the Drawing

The pious and the men of action … The Sages taught … some of them would say … Happy is our youth, … that did not embarrass our old age. These are the pious and the men of action, … And some would say: Happy is our old age, that atoned for our youth … These are the penitents. … these and those say: Happy is he who did not sin; and he who sinned should repent and … will absolve him.

It is taught … They said about Hillel the Elder that when he was rejoicing at the Celebration of the Place of the Drawing … he said this: If I am here, everyone is here; and if I am not here, who is here? … He would … say this: To the place that I love, there my feet take me, … If you come to My house, I will come to your house; if you do not come to My house, I will not come to your house, as it is stated: “In every place that I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you”

Additionally, he saw one skull that was floating on the water … he said to it: Because you drowned … they drowned you, and those that drowned you will be drowned. … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The feet of a person are responsible for him; to the place where he is in demand, there they lead him.

these two Cushites who would stand before Solomon: “Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha” … they were scribes of Solomon. One day … saw that the Angel of Death was sad. He said to him: Why are you sad? He said to him: They are asking me … these two Cushites who are sitting here. … handed them to the demons … and sent them to the district of Luz, … When they arrived at the district of Luz, they died.

The following day, … saw that the Angel of Death was happy. He said to him: Why are you happy? He replied: In the place that they asked me … there you sent them. … Immediately, Solomon began … and said: The feet of a person are responsible for him; to the place where he is in demand, there they lead him.

It is taught … They said about Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel that when he would rejoice at the Celebration of the Place of the Drawing … he would take eight flaming torches and toss one and catch another, … and, … they would not touch each other. And when he would prostrate himself, he would insert his two thumbs into the ground, and bow, and kiss the floor … and straighten, and … not any … creature … could do that … And this was the … kidda

Levi demonstrated a kidda before Rabbi … and came up lame. … And is that what caused him … But didn’t Rabbi Elazar say: One should never speak impertinently toward … above; as a great person … spoke impertinently toward … above, … and came up lame. And who … Levi. … this and that caused him
Levi would walk before Rabbi … with eight knives. Shmuel … before King Shapur with eight glasses of wine … Abaye … before Rabba with eight eggs. Some say … with four eggs.

It is taught … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya said: When we would rejoice … the Celebration of the Place of the Drawing … we did not see sleep in our eyes … How so? … first hour … the daily morning offering … From there … to … prayer … from there, to … the additional offerings; from there, … to … the additional prayer. From there … to the study hall … from there to the eating and drinking … from there to the afternoon prayer. From there … to the daily afternoon offering … From this … forward, … to the Celebration of the Place of the Drawing

Is that so? But didn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan say: … an oath that I will not sleep three days, one flogs him … and he … sleep immediately … Rather, this is what … is saying: We did not experience the sense of … sleep, because they would … doze on each other’s shoulders.

fifteen stairs … Rav Ḥisda said to one of the Sages who was organizing aggada before him: Did you hear … these fifteen … Ascents … corresponding to what did David say them? He said to him … this … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: At the time that David dug the drainpipes … the depths rose and sought to inundate the world. … David recited the fifteen … Ascents and caused them to subside. … If so, … fifteen … Ascents? They should have been … Descents.

said to him: Since you reminded me … matter, this is … was … stated: At the time that David dug the drainpipes, … the depths rose and sought to inundate the world. David said: Is there anyone who knows whether it is permitted to write the … name

on an earthenware shard? … we will … throw it into the depths, and … will subside. There was no one who said anything to him. David said: Anyone who knows … to say and does not say … may he be strangled in his throat. … Ahithophel raised an a fortiori argument on his own … And just as … to make peace between a man and his wife … the Torah said: My Name that was written in sanctity will be erased on the water to establish peace for the whole world in its entirety, all the more so … He said to … It is permitted.

He wrote the … name on an earthenware shard and cast it into the depths, and the … the depths subsided sixteen thousand cubits. When he saw that they subsided excessively, he said: The higher … the moister … the world. He recited the fifteen … Ascents and elevated them fifteen thousand cubits, and established them at … one thousand cubits. Ulla said: Learn from here that the thickness of the earth … is one thousand cubits. … But don’t we see that … we dig a little, … water emerges? Rav Mesharshiyya said: That is from the ascent of the Euphrates

And two priests stood … at the Upper Gate that descends … Rabbi Yirmeya raised a dilemma: … tenth stair … that he would descend five … and stand on the tenth … Or perhaps … that he would descend ten … and stand on the fifth … shall stand
The Sages taught: By inference, from … that it is stated: “And their faces toward the east,” don’t I know that “their backs … toward the Sanctuary of the Lord”?
Rather, … what … does the verse state: “Their backs toward the Sanctuary of the Lord”? … It teaches that they would expose themselves and defecate downward,

We are to God, and to God are our eyes. … Is that so? … Didn’t Rabbi Zeira say: One who … says: Listen, listen, is … who says: We give thanks, we give thanks, … Rather, this is what they said: They bow toward the east, … we give thanks to God, and our eyes turn in hope to God,

MISHNA: One … no fewer than twenty-one … blasts in the Temple, and one … no more than forty-eight. … Each day there were twenty-one … blasts in the Temple: Three … for the opening of the gates … nine for the daily morning offering, and nine for the daily afternoon offering, … And … with the additional offerings they would add nine additional blasts.
And on Shabbat eve they would add six … Three to stop the people from … labor, … and three … to demarcate between sacred and profane.

Shabbat eve during the festival … there were forty-eight … Three … for the opening of the gates; three for the upper gate; and three for the lower gate; and three for the filling of the … water, … and three … upon the altar; nine for the daily morning offering; and nine for the daily afternoon offering; and nine for the additional offerings; three to stop the people from work; and three … to demarcate between sacred and profane,

GEMARA: … The mishna is not in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: The one who … minimize … shall not minimize … fewer than seven … And one who … add … shall not add … sixteen. … what do they disagree? … Rabbi Yehuda holds: … tekia, terua, tekia is … one blast. And the Rabbis hold: A tekia … separately and a terua … separately.

What is the rationale … of Rabbi Yehuda? … the verse states: “And you shall sound [utkatem] a terua” … and it is written: “A terua they will sound [yitke’u]” … How is it … a tekia and a terua … one … And … the Rabbis … This comes … a plain … preceding it and following it. … And from where does Rabbi Yehuda derive … preceding it and following it? … He derives it from … a second time”

And what is the rationale … the Rabbis? … as it is written: “And when congregating the people you shall sound a tekia and shall not sound a terua” … And if it enters your mind … tekia … terua are … one … would the Merciful One say to perform half a mitzva and not to perform … half … And … Rabbi Yehuda … That … came merely as a signal

And … the Rabbis … it is a signal … the Merciful One rendered it a mitzva. … In accordance with whose … is this statement of Rav Kahana: There is no … between a tekia and a terua at all … In accordance with whose … in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda. … If … Rabbi Yehuda; … obvious.
Lest you say … even in accordance with … the Rabbis, … to exclude … of Rabbi Yoḥanan who said: … one heard nine blasts in nine … hours on the day … he fulfilled his obligation. … teaches us
And say it is indeed so … If so, what is … At all,

Shabbat eve during the festival … However, … is not teaching … the tenth stair. … whose … mishna? It is … Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov, as it is taught … Three … at the tenth stair. Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says: Three … upon the altar.
The one who says … at the tenth stair does not say … upon the altar; and the one who says … upon the altar does not say … at the tenth stair.

What is the rationale … of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov? … Since he sounded … for the opening of the gates, for what do I … to sound … at the tenth stair? That is not a gate. Therefore, … preferable … upon the altar. And the Rabbis hold that since he sounded … for the filling … the water, why do I … upon the altar? Therefore, it is preferable … at the tenth stair.

When Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina came from the south … he brought a baraita with him … “And the children of Aaron, the priests, will sound the trumpets” … no … the verse to state: “Shall sound,” as it is already stated: “And you shall sound the trumpets for your burnt-offerings and your peace-offerings” … And what … the verse states: “Shall sound”? … all according to the additional offerings … one sounds … teaches … and he said its … to say that one sounds … for each and every additional offering

We learned … Shabbat eve during the festival … there were forty-eight … And if it is so, … Let … teach … Shabbat during the Festival, … you find … fifty-one … Rabbi Zeira said: … because one does not sound … for the opening of the gates on Shabbat;

Rava said: Who is this who is not concerned about the flour … First, … we learned … each day, … And furthermore, even if they are equal to each other, … let … teach: … Shabbat during the Festival there are forty-eight … You would learn two … from … You would learn from it that … of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov … And you would learn from it … of Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina,

Rather, Rava said: … because one does not sound … for filling … water on Shabbat, … were considerably fewer … And let … also teach … Rosh HaShana that occurs on Shabbat, as … there are three additional offerings: … additional offering of Rosh HaShana, … additional offering of the New Moon, … additional offering of Shabbat.

Shabbat eve during the Festival is necessary … to teach … in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov … Is anyone saying: Let … teach this … and let him not teach that … Let him teach this … and let him teach that … he taught … and omitted … What … did he omit, that he omitted
He omitted … Passover eve.

If … due to … Passover eve, that is not an omission, … who … this … It is Rabbi Yehuda, who said: … never in the all the days of the third shift did it reach … to recite: “I love that the Lord hears … because … people … were few.
But didn’t we establish … not in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda? … And perhaps this tanna … holds in accordance with … in one … and disagrees with him in one
But … What … did he omit, that he omitted this … He omitted … Passover eve that occurs on Shabbat eve, … you eliminate six … and incorporate six
And one … no more than forty-eight … And … no … But isn’t there Passover eve that occurs on Shabbat, where if … to Rabbi Yehuda, … fifty-one … if … to the Rabbis, … fifty-seven blasts?

When … teaches … matters that … every year; … Passover eve that occurs on Shabbat, … that does not … each and every year, he does not teach. … Is that to say … Shabbat eve during the Festival occurs every year? There are times when you do not find … And what are the circumstances? … where the first Festival … occurs on Shabbat eve,

when the first Festival … of … happen to occur on Shabbat eve, we postpone it … What is the reason … Since if the first Festival … occurs on Shabbat eve, when is Yom Kippur … on Sunday. Therefore, … we postpone
And do we postpone it … But didn’t we learn … The fats of … Shabbat … may be sacrificed on Yom Kippur

And Rabbi Zeira said: When we were … in the school of Rav in Babylonia, they said … that which was taught … Yom Kippur that occurs on Shabbat eve they did not sound … and … at the conclusion of Shabbat they would not recite havdala … everyone agrees … when I ascended to there, … I found Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, who was sitting and saying … is … Rabbi Akiva,
not difficult. This, … the Rabbis, … this … is … Aḥerim,
As it is taught … Aḥerim say: Between … Shavuot … Shavuot … and … between Rosh HaShana … Rosh HaShana … there is … only four days … And if it was a leap year … five

raises an objection: … the New Moon that occurs on Shabbat, the song of the New Moon supersedes the song of Shabbat. And if it is so, … let us recite the song of Shabbat and let us recite the song of the New Moon.

a certain … person … said: … I merit to go up there … and … I learn … teaching from the mouth of its Master; … When he went up there … he found Rabbi Zeira … said to him: … the Master say … halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon? … said to him: No, … I said: It stands to reason

said … Aren’t they much older than he? … Rather, … spoke in … the opinion of Rabbi Meir.

this … applies only to rabbinic … but … Torah … However, this is not so; … no different … by Torah … or … by rabbinic … we do not say anything to them. … that … the extension of Yom Kippur. … is by Torah … and … eat and drink until darkness … but we do not say anything to them,
