But if one stipulated … with regard to them … all according to his condition.

Abaye and Rava, who both say … where one says: I am not removing … from them throughout twilight. … no sanctity devolves upon them … However, … wood of a sukka, sanctity devolves upon it … it … set aside … for … seven

And … what … different from that which was stated … separated seven etrogim for … the seven … days, … Rav said: He fulfills … through each and every one … and … he may eat it immediately … And Rav Asi said: He fulfills … through each one, and he may eat it the following day,
There, … nights are divided from the days, … each and every day is its own mitzva, … here, … where … nights are not divided from the days, … all … days are considered as one long day.

MISHNA: One may bring wood … from … field, … from that which has been gathered … And … from a karpef … even from the scattered … What is a karpef? … any … that is near a city, … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Yosei says: Any … into which one … enter … with a key … even … within the Shabbat limit.
GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: One may not bring wood except from … gathered in a karpef. … But didn’t we learn … from a karpef, even from scattered … The mishna … an individual

as it is taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree with regard to … scattered in fields that one may not bring … nor with regard to … gathered in a karpef that one may bring … With regard to what did they disagree? … with regard to scattered … in a karpef and gathered … in fields, as Beit Shammai say: He may not bring … and Beit Hillel say: He may bring

Rava said: … reed leaves and vine leaves, although they are gathered … and placed … since if a wind comes it will scatter them, … are … considered scattered and are … prohibited. … if one placed a vessel on them the day before … it seems well

What is a karpef? … A dilemma was raised before … what … is … speaking? … any … that is near a city, provided that it has a key, … and Rabbi Yosei comes to say: Since it has a key, even … within the Shabbat limit … also

Or perhaps this is what … is saying: Any … that is near a city … whether it has a key or does not have a key, and Rabbi Yosei comes to say: … even … within the Shabbat limit, but specifically if it has a key. However, if it does not have a key, even … near a city … also not

Come … hear from … that it is taught … Rabbi Yosei says: Any … into which one enters with a key, even within the Shabbat limit, … learn from this … Rabbi Yosei stated two … as leniencies. … learn from here … Rav Salla said … Rabbi Yirmeya said: … halakha … in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei as a leniency;

MISHNA: One may not chop wood … neither from beams … nor from a beam that broke on a Festival, … And one may not chop … neither with an ax, nor with a saw, nor with a sickle, … Rather, one may … with a cleaver.

GEMARA: … But didn’t you say in the first clause … one may not chop … at all … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: … is incomplete and is teaching the following: One may not chop … from the pile of beams … nor from a beam that broke on the Festival … However, one may chop … from a beam that broke on the eve of the Festival,

when one chops … one may not chop … neither with an ax, nor with a saw, nor with a sickle, but with a cleaver. … This … is also taught … One may not chop wood, neither from the pile of beams nor from the beam that broke on the Festival … as it is not considered prepared.
not … with an ax. Rav Ḥinnana bar Shelemya said in the name of Rav: They taught … only … with its female … But … with its male … is permitted

It … obvious … we learned … with a cleaver, … lest you say: This applies only … a cleaver, … but … an ax … and … a cleaver … say: Since this side, … is prohibited, the other, side, … also … prohibited. … teaches us

And some teach this … to the latter clause … Rather, with a cleaver. Rav Ḥinnana bar Shelemya said in the name of Rav: They taught … only with its male … but … with its female … it is prohibited. … obvious. … we learn … not … an ax? … lest you say: This … applies … an ax, but … an ax and a cleaver, … say: Since this side, … is permitted, the other, … side … also … permitted. … teaches us
MISHNA: … a house that is filled with produce … and a hole formed … one may remove … through the place of the hole. … Rabbi Meir says: One may even make a hole ab initio and take

GEMARA: … Why … Isn’t … dismantling a tent, … Rav Naḥumi bar Adda said … Shmuel said: … to bricks … one on top of the other [aveira delivni] … Is that so? But didn’t Rav Naḥman say: … these bricks remaining from a building, it is permitted to handle them on Shabbat, since they are fit to sit on; … one arranged them … he has certainly set them aside

Rabbi Zeira said: … On a Festival they said … but … not … on Shabbat … This … was also taught … Rabbi Meir says: One may even make a hole … ab initio and remove … they said … a Festival, but not … Shabbat.
Shmuel said: … fastenings … that … to the ground … one may untie … but one may not unravel … nor cut … that are on … vessels, … untie, or unravel, or cut … both … Shabbat and … a Festival,
raises an objection … fastenings that … to the ground, … on Shabbat one may untie … but not unravel or cut … on a Festival, one may untie or unravel or cut

whose … is this … It is … Rabbi Meir, who said: One may even make a hole and remove … ab initio, whereas the Rabbis disagree with him … and I spoke in accordance with … the Rabbis. … And do the Rabbis disagree with him with regard to … sealed to the ground? But isn’t it taught … The Rabbis concede to Rabbi Meir with regard to … sealed to the ground that one may untie … on Shabbat but not unravel or cut … while on a Festival one may untie or unravel or cut

he, … who spoke in accordance with … that tanna, as it is taught … fastenings that are to the ground, … one may untie … but not unravel or cut … both … Shabbat and … a Festival. And … those … of a vessel, on Shabbat one may untie … but one may not unravel or cut … on a Festival one may untie, or unravel, or cut
You have … answered the first clause … However, the latter clause … difficult
whose … is this … It is … Rabbi Neḥemya, … as he said: All vessels may be handled only in the manner of their … use.

If … Rabbi Neḥemya, why … particularly Shabbat? … even on a Festival, … And if you say … a distinction … to Rabbi Neḥemya between a rabbinic decree of Shabbat, … and a rabbinic decree of a Festival, … Does he differentiate

But isn’t it taught … one … one may kindle … with vessels, but one may not kindle … with shards of vessels, … And it is taught … another … One may kindle … both with vessels and with shards of vessels. And it is taught … another … One may kindle … neither with vessels nor with shards of vessels.
And … is resolved … not difficult; this … Rabbi Yehuda, … This … Rabbi Shimon, … This … Rabbi Neḥemya,
two tanna’im … in accordance with … Rabbi Neḥemya.

MISHNA: … one may not hollow out … a lamp … because he … creates a vessel. And … one may not produce charcoal … on a Festival … And … one may not cut the wick, … Rabbi Yehuda says: … he may cut it … in a fire

GEMARA: Who … taught … hollowing out a lamp is … a vessel, … Rav Yosef said: It is Rabbi Meir, as it is taught … From when is an earthenware vessel susceptible to ritual impurity? … from when its work is completed, … the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehoshua says: … from when … is fired in the furnace.
Abaye said to him: From where … Perhaps Rabbi Meir stated … only there, … since they are fit to contain something. … But here, for what … is … fit? … to contain … coins.
Some say … Rav Yosef said: … is … Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, as we learned: Ḥaraniyyot pots [ilpasin] … pure … of a tent over a corpse, … impure by the carrying of a zav,
Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says: … even pure … carrying of a zav because their labor is not completed;
Abaye said to him: Perhaps … Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, stated … only there, … since they are fit to contain something. But here, … for what is … fit? … to contain … coins.

The Sages taught: One may not hollow out a lamp, and one may not create ḥaraniyyot pots on a Festival. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits … ḥaraniyyot pots. … What is … ḥaraniyyot? Rav Yehuda said: … of a city [iraniyyot]. … What is … iraniyyot? Abaye said: … villagers’ bowls
And one may not produce charcoal … obvious … For what is … fit; … Rabbi Ḥiyya taught: It is necessary … only … handing … over to bathhouse attendants [olyarin] … for that day.
And on that day is it permitted … As Rava said … to sweat, and … before … decree … Here, too, … to sweat, and … before … decree
And one may not cut a wick into two, … What is different … that one may not … with a knife?

he … mends a vessel? … in the fire, he is also preparing a vessel … Rabbi Ḥiyya taught … He cuts it by fire in the mouth of two candles. … Rav Natan bar Abba said … Rav said: One may moḥet a wick on a Festival. … What is … moḥet? Rav Ḥanina bar Shelemya said in the name of Rav: To remove the dark;

Bar Kappara taught: Six matters were stated with regard to … a wick … three … are to be stringent and three … are to be lenient. … to be stringent … One may not spin … it ab initio on a Festival, and one may not singe it in fire … and one may not cut it into two. … to be lenient … One may crush it by hand, … and one may soak it in oil … and one may cut it by fire in the mouth of two candles.

Rav Natan bar Abba said … Rav said: The wealthy … of Babylonia will descend to Gehenna … such as this: Shabbetai bar Marinus happened to come to Babylonia. He requested … a business venture, … and they did not give … him. … to sustain him with food, they likewise refused to sustain him.

He said: These … but they came from the mixed multitude, as it is written: “And show you compassion, and have compassion upon you, … Anyone who has compassion … creatures, it is known that he is of the descendants of Abraham, our father, and anyone who does not have compassion … creatures, it is known that he is not of the descendants of Abraham, our father.

Rav Natan bar Abba said … Rav said: Whoever looks to the table of others … the world is dark for him. … for it is stated: “He wanders abroad for bread: Where is it? He knows the day of darkness is ready at his hand” … Rav Ḥisda said: Even his life is no life,

the Sages taught: … three … lives are not lives, and they are as follows: One who looks to the table of others … and one whose wife rules … him; and one whose body is ruled by suffering. And some say: Even one who has only one robe. … And the first tanna, … It is possible … to examine his clothes
MISHNA: One may not break earthenware … And one may not cut paper in order to roast salted … on it.
And one may not sweep out … an oven or stove … But one may press down

And one may not draw two barrels together … to place a pot on them, … And one may not prop a pot … with a piece of wood, … And similarly, with a door. And one may not lead an animal with a stick … on a Festival; and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, permits
GEMARA: … What is the reason … Because one … preparing a vessel

And one may not sweep out an oven or stove. Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef taught before Rav Naḥman: And if it is not possible to bake unless one sweeps it out, it is permitted. … to the wife of Rabbi Ḥiyya: A part of a brick fell into … oven on a Festival, … Rav Ḥiyya said to her: See, … I want good-quality bread. … Rava said to his attendant: Roast for me a duck … and be careful not to singe

Ravina said to Rav Ashi: Rav Aḥa from Hutzal said to us that the master, … to plaster … the oven for him on a Festival. … He said to him: We rely on the bank of the Euphrates … And this applies only when one wrapped … the day before, … Ravina said: And … ashes … permitted,

One may not draw two barrels together … Rav Naḥman said: … stones of a lavatory, … it is permitted to put them together … on a Festival. Rabba raised an objection to Rav Naḥman: … one may not draw two barrels together … to place a pot on them? … He said to him: There, … it is different, because one makes a tent.

Rabba the Younger, … said to Rav Ashi: However, if … so, … on a Festival, one built … bench [itztaba], … one does not make a tent, so too, … that it is permitted? He said to him: … There, … the Torah prohibited … a permanent construction, … the Torah did not prohibit … a temporary construction. The Sages, … decreed against … a temporary construction … due to a permanent construction. … here, … due to the dignity … the Sages did not decree with regard to it.
Rav Yehuda said: … this bonfire, … from above to below it is permitted, … from below to above, it is prohibited,
And similarly, … eggs … And similarly, … a pot … And similarly, … bed, … And similarly, … barrels

And one may not prop a pot with a piece of wood, and similarly a door. … With regard to a door, … enter your mind? … Rather, say … And similarly, … a door … The Sages taught: One may not prop a pot with a piece of wood, and similarly a door, as wood is … only for kindling. … And Rabbi Shimon, … permits

And one may not lead an animal with a stick on a Festival, but Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, permits … Shall we say … Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, holds in accordance with … his father, … who is not … muktze, … No, … this … even Rabbi Shimon concedes … because … looks like one who is going to the market [ḥinga]

a bamboo … Rav Naḥman prohibits it … and Rav Sheshet permits it. … of a wet … everyone agrees … prohibited; … When they disagree, … of a dry … The one … prohibits … said to you: Wood is only for kindling, … And the one … permits … said to you: … what is it to me to roast with it … What is it to me to roast with its coals?

Some say … In the case of a dry … everyone agrees … permitted; when they disagree, … in the case of a wet … The one … prohibits … it is not fit for kindling. And the one … permits … said to you: Isn’t it … fit for a large fire, … And the halakha … a dry … is permitted … a wet … is prohibited.

Rava taught: A woman may not enter a storehouse of wood … to take from them a firebrand, … And a firebrand that broke may not be kindled on a Festival, for one may kindle … with vessels but one may not kindle … with shards of vessels,

Is that to say that … Rava holds in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, who is … muktze? But didn’t Rava say to his attendant: Roast a duck for me, and throw its innards … There, since … become rancid … from yesterday, … his mind was on them.

MISHNA: Rabbi Eliezer says: … a person may remove a sliver … that is before him, in order to clean with it … his teeth. And he may collect … from a courtyard and kindle … for anything in a courtyard is … prepared … The Rabbis say: He may collect … from … before him … and kindle
One may not produce fire, neither from wood, … nor from stones … nor from … dirt; nor from tiles … nor from water … And … one may not whiten tiles … to roast upon them
GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said:
Animal fodder, … does not have … due to the preparing of a vessel.

Rav Kahana raised an objection to Rav Yehuda … One may handle … a spice tree … to smell them and to wave them before a sick person … And he may crush it … and he may smell it. … he may not cut it … to smell it; and if he did cut it, he is exempt … but it is prohibited … to clean his teeth with it, he may not cut it, and if he did cut it, he is liable … a sin-offering
said to … Now, … exempt but prohibited … a difficulty to my … Is it required … liable … a sin-offering? … rather, … When that … was taught, … hard … hard … be crushed

is incomplete and is teaching the following: … one may crush it and smell it … cut it and smell it. In what … is this statement said? With regard to soft … but with regard to hard ones, one may not cut them. And if he did cut it he is exempt, but it is prohibited … to clean his teeth with it, he may not cut it, and if he did cut it, he is liable … a sin-offering.
is taught … one … One may cut it and smell it, and … is taught … another … One may not cut it to smell it. Rabbi Zeira said … Rav Ḥisda said: … is not difficult. … this … to soft … that … to hard

Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov strongly objects to this: With hard ones, why not? … what … is … different from that which we learned … A person may break a barrel … to eat dried figs from it, provided that he does not … intend to make a vessel, … And furthermore, … Rava bar Rav Adda and Ravin bar Rav Adda, who both say: When we were at the house of Rav Yehuda, he would break and give us many sticks … they were … fit for handles of axes and hatchets.

is not difficult; this … Rabbi Eliezer, … that … the Rabbis. As it is taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: … a person may take a sliver … from before him to clean his teeth with it, and the Rabbis say: One may take … only from an animal’s trough; … And they agree that he may not pluck it. And if he did pluck it to clean his teeth with it … to … open a door with it, … unwittingly on Shabbat, he is liable … a sin-offering. … intentionally on a Festival, he receives the forty … the words of Rabbi Eliezer.

And the Rabbis say: Both this and this, … it is … only due to a rabbinic decree. … Rabbi Eliezer, who states there … liable … a sin-offering, … here, … exempt, but it is prohibited. … the Rabbis who state there, … exempt but it is prohibited, … here, … permitted ab initio.

And … Rabbi Eliezer not accept this … that we learned … A person may break a barrel … to eat dried figs from it, provided that he does not … intend to make a vessel? … Rav Ashi said: When that … was taught, … with regard to a vessel patched with pitch [mustaki],

And one may collect … from the courtyard … The Sages taught: One may collect … from a courtyard and kindle … everything in a courtyard is … prepared, provided he does not arrange it in piles, and Rabbi Shimon permits … With regard to what do they disagree; … One Sage, … holds: It looks as though he is collecting for tomorrow and another day, … And one Sage, … holds: His pot proves his
one may not produce … fire … What is the reason … Because he creates … on a Festival.
one may not whiten tiles … What does one … do; … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Here we are dealing with new tiles, … because
it is necessary to test them … And some say: Because it is necessary to harden them

We learned … there: … trampled … or threw it … wall, or if an animal crushed it, … twitching … if … waited, … from … time … until … time … and he … slaughtered it, it is kosher, … Rabbi Elazar bar Yannai said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Antigonus: It requires examination
Rabbi Yirmeya inquired of Rabbi Zeira: What is … with regard to slaughtering it on a Festival? Do we assume on a Festival … a flaw or not?

He said to him … We … learned … one may not whiten tiles … roast on them. And we discussed it: What does he … do? And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Here we are dealing with new tiles, … because … needs to test them,
He said to him: … we learned … that … because it is necessary to harden them

is taught … One brings the fire, and one brings the wood, and one places the pot … and one brings the water … and one puts spices into … and one stirs … they are all liable … But wasn’t it taught … the last one is liable and all … are exempt? … is not difficult. This … in which he brought fire at the outset, … that … in which he brought fire at the end.

Granted, all of them performed an action … But … one who places the pot … what … has he performed? Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Here we are dealing with a new pot, and due to whitening tiles they applied … it.

The Sages taught … New ovens and stoves are similar to all vessels that … carried in a courtyard … However, one may not anoint them with oil, nor rub them with a rag, nor cool them with cold … harden them … And if … in order to bake … this is permitted.
The Sages taught … one may scald the head and the feet … and one may singe them in fire … but one may not smear them with clay, nor earth, nor lime … And one may not shear … with scissors,

one may not trim … the vegetable with its … shears, but one may prepare kundas and akaviyot, … And one may kindle … and bake in a large baker’s oven [purnei], and one may heat water in an antikhi, … but one may not bake in a new baker’s oven lest it break.

The Sages taught … One may not blow … with bellows, … but one may blow … with a tube, … And one may not mend a skewer nor sharpen it. The Sages … taught … One may not break a reed … to roast salted … but one may crack a nut … with a rag, and there is no concern lest it tear,
MISHNA: And Rabbi Eliezer further stated … A person may stand over … storage,
on Shabbat eve during the Sabbatical Year, … and say: From here, … I will eat tomorrow. And the Rabbis say: … unless he marks … and … says: From here to there

GEMARA: We learned … there: … Children who hid figs … on Shabbat eve … and they forgot and did not separate tithes, … after the conclusion of Shabbat, they may not eat until they have separated tithes. And we also learned … One who transfers figs in his courtyard in order to … dry … his children and the members of his household may … partake of them … a casual … and they are exempt

Rava inquired of Rav Naḥman: … Shabbat, what is … whether it establish … to tithe … muktze … an item whose labor has not been completed, … Do we say … since it is written: “And call Shabbat a delight” … establishes … even for an item that has not … labor completed? Or perhaps … establishes … an item whose labor is completed, … an item whose labor is not completed it does not establish

said to … Shabbat establishes … both … an item whose work is completed and things whose work is not completed. … said to … But say … Shabbat … similar … a courtyard: Just as a courtyard establishes … only … the work on an item is completed, so too, Shabbat … establish only an item whose work is completed … said to … we have it as an ordered teaching that Shabbat establishes both things whose work is completed and things whose work is not completed.

Mar Zutra, son of Rav Naḥman, said: We, too, have learned … And Rabbi Eliezer further stated … a person may stand over … storage … on Shabbat eve during the Sabbatical Year … The reason is that … Sabbatical Year, … which … is not obligated to … tithes. However, if … in the other years of the Sabbatical … so too, … prohibited … What is the reason … Is it not because Shabbat establishes

there it is different: Since he said: From here I will eat tomorrow, he has … established for himself … with them, … If so, why … particularly Shabbat? Even … on a weekday … also … This … teach us … that untithed produce … it is … prepared with regard to Shabbat, in that if one transgressed … and corrected it … it is … corrected.
But isn’t it … the remaining … is restored … And we have heard … Rabbi Eliezer … said: Anywhere that its leftovers are restored, it is not established

as we learned … One who removes olives from a vat [ma’atan] … may dip … one by one in salt and eat … And if he dipped and placed … before him, … ten, … liable … Rabbi Eliezer says: … from a ritually pure vat is liable … from a ritually impure vat is exempt because he returns the surplus

And we discussed it: What is different … the first clause … and what is different … the latter clause; … And Rabbi Abbahu said: The first case … to a ritually pure vat and a ritually impure person, … He may not return
the latter clause … to a ritually impure vat and a person … ritually impure, who may return
The mishna also … with … a ritually pure storage … and a ritually impure person, who may not return them … But aren’t they already returned?

Rather, Rav Shimi bar Ashi said: … Rabbi Eliezer, you said? … Rabbi Eliezer … to his … reasoning, as he said … teruma … establishes … And, all the more so, Shabbat … as we learned … Fruits from which teruma has been separated before their work was completed, Rabbi Eliezer prohibits eating from them … a casual … but the Rabbis permit

Come … hear … from the latter clause … And the Rabbis say: … unless one marks … and says … From here to there. … The reason is that the eve of Shabbat … the Sabbatical Year is not fit for tithes; but during … other years of the Sabbatical … are fit for … tithes, … are prohibited. What is the reason? Is it not because Shabbat … establishes

No, … there it is different. Since he said: From here to there I will eat tomorrow, he has … established … If so, why discuss … Shabbat; even on a weekday as well … This … teach us, … that untithed produce … it is … prepared with regard to Shabbat, in that if one transgressed … and tithed it, it is tithed.
And we raise a contradiction … If one was eating from a cluster … and came in from a garden, … to a courtyard, Rabbi Eliezer says: He may finish … Rabbi Yehoshua says: He may not finish.
if it grew dark on … the night of Shabbat, … Rabbi Eliezer says: He may finish, … And Rabbi Yehoshua says: He may not finish.

There, the reason is as he taught … Rabbi Natan says: … not that when Rabbi Eliezer said: He may finish, … he may finish in the courtyard … but rather … He may exit the courtyard and finish. And … not that when Rabbi Eliezer said: He may finish, … he may finish on Shabbat … but rather, … he may wait until the conclusion of Shabbat and finish.
when Ravin came … he said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Whether … Shabbat; or … teruma … or … a courtyard … or … a transaction; all of these … establish … only … items whose labor is completed.
Shabbat … to exclude … Hillel, as it is taught … One who gathers fruits from one place to another … to reap … and the day sanctified upon them, … Rabbi Yehuda said: Hillel prohibits … himself.

a courtyard … to exclude … of Rabbi Ya’akov. As we learned … One who was transporting figs in his courtyard to make them into dried figs, his children and the members of his household may eat from them … a casual … and they are exempt from tithes. And … is taught in that regard: Rabbi Ya’akov obligates … and Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, exempts

teruma … to exclude … of Rabbi Eliezer. As we learned … Fruits from which teruma had been separated before their work was completed, Rabbi Eliezer prohibits eating from them … a casual … and the Rabbis permit

a transaction … as we learned … one who acquires figs from an am ha’aretz in a place where most people press … he may … partake of them … a casual … And … he … tithe them as doubtfully tithed produce,

learn from … three … Learn from here … a transaction establishes … only with regard to an item whose work is completed, … And learn from here … most … am ha’aretz separate tithes, … And … learn from here … One may tithe doubtfully tithed produce … from an am ha’aretz, even with regard to something whose work is not completed.

to exclude that which we learned … One who exchanges fruits with his friend, … this one to eat and that one to eat, … this one to make them into dried fruit and for that one to make them into dried fruit, this one to eat and that one to make them into dried fruit, … obligated … Rabbi Yehuda, … says: … to eat is obligated, … to make them into dried fruit is exempt

MISHNA: One may lower produce, … through a skylight on a Festival, … however, … not … on Shabbat. And one may cover produce … with cloths … due to a leak … and similarly … jugs of wine and jugs of oil … And one may place a vessel beneath a leak … on Shabbat,
GEMARA: … It was said: Rav Yehuda and Rav Natan … One … taught mashilin, … and … one taught mashḥilin.

Mar Zutra said: The one who teaches mashilin is not mistaken, and the one who teaches mashḥilin is not mistaken, … The one who teaches mashilin is not mistaken, as it is written: “For your olives will fall [yishal]” … And he who teaches mashḥilin is not mistaken, as we learned … The shaḥul and the kasul. … Shaḥul … whose thigh is dislocated, … kasul … one of whose thighs is higher than the other.
Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said … One who teaches mashirin is not mistaken, and one who teaches mashḥirin is not mistaken, and one who teaches manshirin is not mistaken.

One who teaches mashirin is not mistaken, as we learned … Rabbi Yishmael says: A nazirite may not wash … his head with clay … because it causes hair to fall off [mashir], … And one who teaches mashḥirin is … not mistaken, as we learned … The sheḥor, … and a barber’s scissors, even if … are detached, are subject to ritual impurity.

And one who teaches manshirin is not mistaken … as we learned … One whose clothes fell down [nashru] into water … may … walk in them … and he need not be concerned … Alternatively, … from that which we learned … What is gleaning [leket], … That which falls [nosher] during reaping.

We learned … one may lower produce through a skylight on a Festival. … Up to how much … Rabbi Zeira said … Rav Asi said, and some say … Rav Asi said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … like that which we learned … One may clear out four or five sacks of hay or grain … due to visitors, … or due to suspension of … the study hall,

But perhaps there it is different, since there is … suspension of … the study hall … But here, where there is no suspension of … the study hall, … not … Alternatively: There, this is the reasoning that four or five sacks are permitted: Because Shabbat is severe … and they will not come to belittle it; but … a Festival, which is … lightly and which … might come to belittle, … not … at all.
Alternatively, … from the other perspective: There, this is the reasoning … Because there is no monetary loss … But here, where there is monetary loss … even a larger amount

We learned elsewhere, … But … may not … a storeroom. And Shmuel said: What is … But not a storeroom? … But one may not finish … the entire storeroom … lest he come to level out depressions … What would be … here,

it is there, on Shabbat, that it is prohibited, because … severe, but … a Festival, which … lighter … it is acceptable. Or perhaps … There, … there is suspension of … the study hall, … you say … not … Here, … where there is no suspension of … the study hall, … not all the more so

And here we learned … One may lower produce through a skylight on a Festival, and Rav Naḥman said: They taught … only with regard to the same roof, … but … from … roof to … roof … not … And … is also taught … One may not carry from … roof to … roof, even when … roofs are on the same level

There, … what is … all the more so … Shabbat, … severe … Or perhaps … It is here, … that … prohibited … because a Festival … lightly … and they might … come to belittle it; but … Shabbat, which is severe … and … they will not come to belittle it, it is acceptable
Or perhaps … If here, … when there is … loss of … produce, you say … not … there, … when there is no … loss of produce, … not all the more so

Here, … we learned … he may not lower them by … a rope through the windows, nor may he take them down by way of ladders. There, … what is … here, … on a Festival, that … prohibited, … does not … suspension of … the study hall; but … Shabbat, when there is … suspension of … the study hall, it is acceptable
Or perhaps … Here, … when there is … loss of … produce, you say … not … There, … where there is no … loss of produce, … not all the more so … shall stand

And one may cover produce … Ulla said: And even a row of bricks … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: … produce, which is fit … And Rabbi Yitzḥak follows … reasoning … as Rabbi Yitzḥak said: A vessel, … may be handled … only … for something that may … be handled on Shabbat,

We learned … One may cover produce with cloths, … Produce, yes, … a row of bricks, no. … the same is true even … a row of bricks, … since … taught in the first clause … One may lower produce, … he taught also in the latter clause: One may cover produce.
We learned … And similarly … jugs of wine and jugs of oil … With what are we dealing here? With … that are untithed,
So, too, it is … reasonable … as if it enters your mind … jugs of wine and jugs of oil … permitted … didn’t … teach in the first clause … produce?
it was necessary for … jugs of wine and jugs of oil, … it could enter your mind to say … were concerned over a substantial loss, … with regard to a minor loss, … they were not concerned, … teaches us
We learned … One may place a vessel beneath a leak on Shabbat. … leakage … that … fit
Come … hear … One may spread a mat over bricks on Shabbat … that were left over from building … which are … fit for … sitting on
Come … hear … One may spread a mat over stones on Shabbat, … of rounded … mekurzalot … stones, which … fit for … in the lavatory

Come … hear … One may spread a mat over a beehive on Shabbat … in the sun due to the sun, and in the rain due to the rain, provided he does not have the intent to trap … There, too, … when there is honey

Rav Ukva from Meishan said to Rav Ashi: … well with … the summer, when there is honey, … in the rainy season, … what can be said? … is necessary only for those two honeycombs … Are those two honeycombs … muktze, … With what … are we dealing here? … when … had in mind … them

But if he did not have in mind … them … what … prohibited … rather than teaching: As long as he does not have the intent to trap … let it make a distinction within the case itself … In what … is this statement said, … When he had in mind … but … he did not have in mind … them, it is prohibited.
This is what … is saying: Even if he had in mind … provided he does not have intent to trap

In what … did you establish … In accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, who, … holds … muktze … say the latter clause … Provided he does not have the intent to trap. … we have come to … Rabbi Shimon, … said: An unintentional act is permitted
And … you understand … of Rabbi Shimon … But didn’t Abaye and Rava both say: Rabbi Shimon concedes … in … Cut off its head and will it not die?
actually all of … Rabbi Yehuda, and with what … are we dealing here? … that has windows, … And … you … not say, according to Rabbi Yehuda: Provided he does not have intent to trap
but rather say … Provided he does not make it a trap … obvious … Lest you say: … whose type is … trapped … prohibited … whose type is not … trapped, … permitted … teaches us

Rav Ashi said … Is it taught … In the summer, and: In the rainy season? … it is taught: In the sun due to the sun and in the rain due to the rain. … of the … days of Nisan and the … days of Tishrei, when there is … sun and there is … rain, and … there is … honey
And one may place a vessel beneath a leak … on Shabbat. … taught … If the vessel became full … he may pour out … and repeat … and … not refrain
Abaye’s millhouse … developed a leak … came before Rabba … said to him: Go … bring your bed into … so that … will be … like a container of excrement, … and … remove

Abaye sat … and posed a difficulty: And may one initiate … a container of excrement, … ab initio? In the meantime, … Abaye’s millhouse collapsed. He said: I had … coming to me for having gone against the words of my master,
Shmuel said: … a container of excrement and a container of urine, it is permitted to remove them … to a garbage heap. And when he returns … he must place water in it … and … return it,

understood from … a container of excrement on account of the vessel, … Yes, … by itself, … No, … Come … hear that a certain … mouse was discovered in Rav Ashi’s storeroom … spices … isparmekei … Rav Ashi said to them: Take hold of it by its tail and remove it.
MISHNA: Any act for which one is liable due to a rabbinic decree … rest [shevut]; … because it is optional, … because it is … mitzva, … on Shabbat, one is liable for it on a Festival
And these are … as shevut: One may not climb a tree … nor ride on an animal, nor swim in the water, nor clap … nor clap … thigh, nor dance.
And the following … because they are optional, … One may not judge, nor betroth … nor perform ḥalitza, … nor perform levirate marriage.
And the following … because of the … mitzva … One may not consecrate, nor take a valuation vow … nor consecrate … nor separate teruma and tithes
spoke … all these … with regard to a Festival; all the more so … on Shabbat. … There is no … between a Festival and Shabbat, except for … food alone,
GEMARA: … One may not climb a tree. … a decree … lest one detach
Nor ride on an animal: … a decree … lest one go beyond the … limit … learn from here … the … limits, … is by Torah law? … Rather, … a decree … lest one cut off a branch
Nor swim in the water: … a decree … lest one make a swimmer’s barrel,
Nor clap … nor clap his hand on the thigh, nor dance: … a decree … lest one fashion a musical instrument
And the following … because they are optional, … One may not judge. … But doesn’t one perform … mitzva … No, … necessary … where there is … who is more … than he.
Nor betroth … But doesn’t one perform a … mitzva … No, … necessary
because … he … has a wife and children,
Nor perform ḥalitza, nor perform levirate marriage: … But doesn’t one perform a mitzva … No, … necessary … when there is an older … the … mitzva is for the oldest … to perform levirate marriage,
And … all these … what is the reason … a decree lest one write
And the following … because of the … mitzva … One may not consecrate, nor take a valuation vow, nor consecrate … a decree due to … commerce.
And one may not separate terumot and tithes. … obvious … Rav Yosef taught: It is necessary … only … to give it to a priest on the same day.

And this applies only to produce that … untithed produce, … the day before … However, produce that became untithed now … such as dough … separating ḥalla from it, one may separate … and give … to a priest
those … because they are optional, … not because … rabbinic decree … rest [shevut]? … those … because they are mitzvot, … not because of shevut?

Rabbi Yitzḥak said: … is speaking … There is no need, … there is no need … plain shevut, … is prohibited, but even shevut of an optional act, … is also prohibited. And there is no need … shevut of an optional act is prohibited, but even shevut of … mitzva is also prohibited.
spoke … all these … with regard to a Festival; … raises a contradiction … One may lower … through a skylight … on a Festival, but not on Shabbat.
Rav Yosef said: … not difficult, … this … Rabbi Eliezer, … that … Rabbi Yehoshua.

As it is taught … it and its offspring … fell into a pit … Rabbi Eliezer says: One may raise the first in order to slaughter it and … slaughter it, and … the second, he provides it sustenance in its place so that it will not die

Rabbi Yehoshua, … says: One may raise the first with the intent of slaughtering it and … not slaughter it. Then he may go back and employ artifice … and he raises the second. … if he … desires he may slaughter this … if he … desires he may slaughter that
Abaye said to … From where … Perhaps Rabbi Eliezer stated … only thus far, there … where it is possible to sustain … But here, … no possibility … through providing sustenance, … not
Alternatively, … Rabbi Yehoshua stated … only thus far, there … because it is possible to employ artifice … But here, … where it is not possible to employ artifice, … not
Rather, Rav Pappa said: … not difficult, … this … Beit Shammai, … that … Beit Hillel.
As we learned … Beit Shammai say: … one may not take out a child … nor a lulav, nor a Torah scroll … and Beit Hillel permit
Perhaps that is not so, … Beit Shammai stated … only thus far, there … transferring … but not … moving … Is that to say … moving is not … for the sake of taking out
MISHNA: … animals and vessels … is as the feet of … owner, … one who delivers his animal to his son or to a shepherd … these are as the feet of the owner,
Vessels that … are designated for … one of the brothers in the house … these are as his feet, … And … that are not designated … these are as a place where … may … go.

One who borrows a vessel from another on the eve of a Festival, … as the feet of the borrower … on the Festival … as the feet of the lender, … And similarly, a woman who borrowed spices from another … or water and salt … her dough, these … are as the feet of both of them; … Rabbi Yehuda exempts … in the … water, because it … no substance
GEMARA: … The mishna

not in accordance with … Rabbi Dosa. As it is taught … Rabbi Dosa says, and some say Abba Shaul says: One who purchases an animal from another on the eve of a Festival, even if he did not deliver it to him until the Festival … it is as the feet of the purchaser. And one who delivers his animal to a shepherd, even if he did not deliver it to him until the Festival … it is as the feet of the shepherd.
You … even say … Rabbi Dosa, and … not difficult. Here, … to … one shepherd. … There, … to … two shepherds. … is also precise … as it teaches: To his son or to a shepherd, … learn from this

Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Dosa, … And did Rabbi Yoḥanan … say this? But didn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan say … the halakha … follows an unattributed … a mishna? And we learned … Animals and vessels are as the feet of the owner.
And did we not establish … here … with … one shepherd, … there … with … two shepherds?

The Sages taught: … two … who borrowed one robe in partnership … this … to go to the study hall with it … morning and that … to enter … feast with it … evening, … this one made a joining … for himself to the north … and that … made an eiruv for himself to the south … the one who made an eiruv for himself to the north may walk … to the north … as … the feet of the one who made an eiruv for himself to the south,
And … the one who made an eiruv for himself to the south may walk … to the south … as … feet of the one who made an eiruv for himself to the north,
And if they made … limits … in the center, … then each … may not move … from its place
It was said: … two … who purchased a barrel … or an animal in partnership … Rav said: … barrel is permitted … but … animal is prohibited, … And Shmuel said: … barrel is also prohibited
What does Rav hold? If he holds … there is … designation, … even … animal should be permitted. And if he holds … there is no … designation, … even … barrel should be prohibited.

Actually, … he holds there is … designation, … an animal is different, as … limits absorb from each other. … Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav: … were not concerned about the prohibition of muktze, … they were concerned about the prohibition of … limits. … Rav was silent
What … was … about … Rabbi Hoshaya said: … there is … designation, … And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: There is no … designation,

And does Rabbi Hoshaya … hold there is … designation? But didn’t we learn … a corpse in a house that has many entrances, all … are ritually impure, … if one of them was … opened, … that … is impure, while all the others are pure, … one … intended to remove … through … one of … or through a window that is … four by four … saves all the … entrances
Beit Shammai say: And this … if he had this intention before the dead person died, … And Beit Hillel say: … even … after the dead person died.
And it is stated with regard to this … Rabbi Hoshaya said: … to purify the entrances from that point and onward; … From here and onward: Yes, … retroactively: No.
Reverse … Rabbi Hoshaya said: There is no … designation, and Rabbi Yoḥanan said: There is … designation.
And does Rabbi Yoḥanan … accept … designation? But didn’t Rav Asi say … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Brothers who divided … are … purchasers … and … they must return … to each other in the Jubilee
And if you should say: When does Rabbi Yoḥanan not accept … designation? … in … Torah law, … he does hold … in … rabbinic law,
But does he accept … in … rabbinic law? Didn’t … Ayo teach

Rabbi Yehuda … said: A person may not make a stipulation with regard to two … things at once, … Rather, … if the rabbi comes from the east his eiruv in the east … from the west, his eiruv in the west … However, … here and … there, … not
And we discussed … with regard to this … What is different … here and … there, … there is no … designation. … as well, … east and … west, … there is no … designation.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan said … rabbi had already arrived … Apparently, … Rabbi Yoḥanan does not accept … designation
Rather, … Actually, do not reverse … And when does Rabbi Oshaya not hold … designation? … Torah … But with regard to … rabbinic … he does accept
Mar Zutra taught in … lesson: … halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Oshaya
Shmuel said: An ox of a fattener, … is as the feet of all people. … an ox of a shepherd, … is as the feet of … that city,

one who borrows a vessel from another on the eve of a Festival, … obvious … No, … necessary … where one did not deliver … to him until the Festival … Lest you say: … did not establish it in … possession … teaches us

supports … Rabbi Yoḥanan, as Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who borrows a vessel from another on the eve of a Festival, even if he did not give it to him until the Festival … it is as the feet of the borrower.

on the Festival … it is as the feet of the lender. … obvious. … No, … necessary … is accustomed to borrowing … from … Lest you say … establishes it in his possession … teaches us … certainly says … Perhaps he will find someone else … and he will go and borrow from him.

And similarly, a woman who borrowed … from another … When Rabbi Abba ascended … he said: May it be … will that I say a statement … that will be accepted … When he ascended, … Rabbi Yoḥanan, Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappi, and Rabbi Zeira, and some say … Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, and Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa, and … were sitting and saying … Why … But let … water and salt be … nullified in the dough, … Rabbi Abba said to them:
If … kav of wheat became mingled with ten kav of another’s wheat, … the latter eat … and rejoice? … laughed at him. He said to them: … I take your cloaks … They again laughed at him.

Rabbi Oshaya said: They did well to laugh at him. … What is different … wheat … with barley … did not say … to them … because that is … type … with … that is not its … type. … A type … with … not … type becomes nullified, … wheat … with wheat … as well. Although, according to Rabbi Yehuda, … is not nullified, according to the Rabbis … is certainly nullified.

Rav Safra said … Moses! … spoken well … But, did … not hear … this … that Rabbi Ḥiyya of Ketosfa’a said in the name of Rav: One who removes pebbles from another’s … granary is obligated … pay him the value of wheat
Apparently, … he has reduced his measure … Here, too, … one has reduced his measure,
Abaye … said to … And … the master not differentiate between money that has claimants, … and money that does not have claimants,
said to him: And according to your reasoning, … this … Rav Ḥisda said: … animal carcass can be nullified in … a slaughtered … because … a slaughtered … cannot attain the status of carcass,
slaughtered … is not nullified by the carcass, as it is possible for a carcass to attain the status of a slaughtered

Here, too, … that if … has owners … it is not nullified … And if you say: … it is indeed so, but isn’t it taught: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri said: Ownerless objects acquire residence … although they have no owner, it is as though they have an owner?
said to … Are you comparing … prohibitions, … to monetary … a prohibition, … can be nullified, … money cannot be nullified.
And what is the reason
Abaye said: … a decree … lest … make dough in partnership
Rava said … Spices are made … to … taste … taste is not nullified,
And Rav Ashi said … because … is an object whose prohibition is temporary, … and … anything whose prohibition is temporary cannot become nullified, even … in one thousand.

Rabbi Yehuda exempts … in … water. … water, yes, … salt, no, … But isn’t it taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: Water and salt are … nullified, whether in a dough or in a pot … not difficult. … this … salt of Sodom, … that … to … isterokanit salt.
But isn’t it taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: Water and salt are nullified in dough but not in a pot, due to its sauce. … not difficult. This … to a thick … That … to a thin

MISHNA: A coal … as the feet of the owner, … But a flame … anywhere, … a coal of consecrated property … misuse … But … flame, … one may not … benefit … he is not … misuse, … one who takes out a coal … to the public domain … liable … a flame is exempt.

GEMARA: The Sages taught … Five things were stated with regard to a coal, … (1) Coal is as the feet of the owner … whereas a flame … anywhere. (2) One … misusing … with a consecrated coal, whereas … a flame, … one may not benefit … but he is not … misusing … (3) Coal … idol worship is prohibited … whereas … a flame … is permitted … (4) One who carries out a coal to the public domain is liable, whereas … a flame is exempt. (5) One who is prohibited by a vow … benefit from another is prohibited from … his coal, but … permitted … from his flame.

What is different … a flame … idol worship, that … permitted … and what is different … consecrated … that … prohibited … idol worship, which is repulsive … and from which … people … maintain separation, the Sages did not decree … with regard to it. … consecrated property, which is not repulsive and from which people do not … maintain separation, … the Sages did decree with regard to it

one who carries out a coal to the public domain … liable, whereas … a flame is exempt. … But isn’t … taught … One who carries out a flame of any size … is liable? Rav Sheshet said: … where one carried out … with a wooden chip.
But … let it derive … due to … wooden chip, … that does not have the … measure … as we learned … one who carries out wood … enough … to cook an egg … easiest
Abaye said … where one smeared a vessel with oil, and lit a fire on it, … let it derive … due to … vessel … to … an earthenware
And … let it derive … due to … earthenware … with … that is not of … measure … as we learned … earthenware … enough to place between one … frame and another, … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.
But … that which we learned … One who carries out a flame is exempt, … what circumstances … be found? … where one fanned … with his hand … into the public domain

MISHNA: … a cistern of an individual, … is as the feet of the individual … And … the people … a particular town is as the feet of the people of that town. And … of those who come up … from Babylonia, … as the feet of whoever fills

GEMARA: Rava raised a contradiction to Rav Naḥman: We learned … a cistern of an individual is as the feet of the individual; and … raised a contradiction … flowing rivers and flowing springs are as the feet of all people. Rava said: With what are we dealing here … With … collected … And it was also said … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin said … Shmuel said: … to collected

And … of those who come up … from Babylonia, … as the feet of whoever fills … It was stated … filled … another and gave … to … Rav Naḥman said: … as the feet of the one for whom they were filled; Rav Sheshet said: … as the feet of the one who filled
With regard to what … do they disagree? … One Sage, … holds … cistern is ownerless, … And one Sage, … holds … is … by … partners,
Rava raised a challenge to Rav Naḥman … I am hereby … to you … ḥerem, … the one prohibited by the vow, … is prohibited

You are hereby … to me … ḥerem, the one making the vow is … prohibited … I am hereby … to you … you to me … they are both prohibited … from one another. And they are permitted … to those who come up from Babylonia, … but they are prohibited … of that city,

And the following are items of those coming up from Babylonia, … The Temple Mount, the chambers, and the courtyards … and a cistern … in the middle of the road. And these are … of that city: The street, and the synagogue, and the bathhouse.

And if you say … a cistern … is … by partners, … why … permitted … But didn’t we learn … partners who took a vow … benefit from one another are prohibited to enter … courtyard … to wash … in a cistern
So too, … to wash … But … with what are we dealing here? … to filling … this one fills from his … and that one fills from his
And does Rav Naḥman hold … there is … designation? But didn’t we learn … brothers … partners, they are obligated to … a kalbon, … are exempt from … animal tithe,
And … liable for the animal tithe, … they are exempt from the kalbon,
And Rav Anan said: … taught … only when they divided kids against lambs or lambs against kids,
However, … they divided kids against kids and lambs against lambs, … say … This is his portion … reach him from the first moment,
But Rav Naḥman said: Even if they divided kids against kids and lambs against lambs, … not say … this is his portion … reach him from the first moment.

Rather, everyone agrees … is an ownerless cistern, but here they disagree over … One who picks up a found article … on behalf of his friend. … Sage, … holds … acquires … And … Sage, … holds … does not acquire it.

MISHNA: … one who had produce in a different city … and the residents of that city … to bring him some of his produce, they may not bring … to him. … However, if … placed an eiruv … his produce is like his
one who invited guests to … him … they may not carry in their hands … portions … unless he transferred ownership of their portions to them on the eve of the Festival,

GEMARA: It is stated … one who deposits produce with another … Rav said: … as the feet of the one with whom they were deposited. And Shmuel said: … as the feet of the … owner. … Let us say … Rav and Shmuel follow their … reasoning, as we learned … If … brought in … with … permission, the owner of the courtyard is liable … And Rabbi … said: … is never liable … unless the homeowner … accepts upon himself … to watch

And Rav Huna said … Rav said: The halakha is in accordance with the statement of the Rabbis, … that Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi … let us say … Rav spoke … in accordance with … the Rabbis, … And Shmuel spoke … in accordance with … Rabbi

Rav … said to you: I said … even in accordance with … Rabbi … Rabbi … stated … only there, … because in … ordinary … does not accept upon himself … watching … But here, … has accepted upon himself … of watching

And … Shmuel … said: I said … even in accordance with … the Rabbis, … the Rabbis stated … only there, … because it is a person’s, … preference that his ox … be established in the jurisdiction of the owner of the courtyard, … that if … does damage … will not be liable. But here, is it a person’s preference for his produce to be in another’s jurisdiction

We learned … However, if … placed an eiruv, … his produce is like his … And if you say … as the feet of the one with whom they were deposited, … if … placed an eiruv, what of it? … Rav Huna said … the … school of Rav said … where … designated a corner … for

Come … hear … one who invited guests to … him, they may not carry in their hands … portions … unless he transferred ownership of their portions to them on the eve of the Festival. And if you say … as the feet of the one with whom they were deposited, … if he transferred ownership to them by means of another … what of it? … Here too, since he transferred ownership to them by means of another … it is considered as … one who designated a corner for him,
And if you wish, say … transferring ownership is different
Rav Ḥana bar Ḥanilai … hung meat on the bar of the door … He came before Rav Huna … said to him: If you … hung … go take it, but if … hung … for you, you may not take it.

And if he … hung … may he … take … But wasn’t Rav Huna … Rav, and Rav said … as the feet of the one with whom it was deposited, … it is different, … the bar of the … door, … is considered similar to … one who designated a corner for him.
Rav Hillel said to Rav Ashi: And if they hung … for him, may he … not take … But didn’t Shmuel say: An ox of a fattener, … is as the feet of all people,

Ravina said to Rav Ashi: And if … hung … for him, may he … not take … But didn’t Rabba bar bar Ḥana say … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Dosa, … Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana: And if they hung … for him, may he … not take … But didn’t we learn … animals and vessels is as the feet of … owner?

Rather, … Rav Ḥana bar Ḥanilai is different … as he is a great man and occupied with his studies, and this is what … said to him: If you … hung … you … mark on … and your attention was not diverted from it, … may go … take … However, if … hung … for you, you … diverted your attention … and you may … not take
MISHNA: … one may not water and slaughter desert … However, one may water and slaughter domestic … These are … domestic … that sleep in the city … Desert … that sleep in the pasture
GEMARA: … Why, … do I … to say: One may water and slaughter? … teaches us … matter incidentally: That a person should … water his animal and … afterward slaughter … due to the adhesion of the skin

The Sages taught … Which are desert … and which are domestic ones? Desert … all those that go out … at Passover … and graze in the pasture … and enter … at the first rainfall, … And these are domestic … All that go out … and graze outside the … boundary but come and sleep within the boundary … Rabbi … says: Both these and those are … domestic … Rather, these are desert animals … All those that go out and graze in the pasture and do not enter the settled area, neither in the summer nor in the rainy season.

And does Rabbi … accept … muktze? But didn’t Rabbi Shimon, son … Rabbi … inquire of Rabbi … Unripe dates … to ripen … what is … according to Rabbi Shimon … He said to him … There is no … muktze according to Rabbi Shimon,
except for … dried figs and raisins … alone. These

If you wish, say … these … are also considered similar to dried figs and raisins, … And if you wish, say … he stated … in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Shimon, … he himself does not hold accordingly.

And if you wish, say … he was speaking, … in accordance with the words … the Rabbis … According to my … there is no … muktze … But … according to your approach, … agree with me, in any event, … where they go out and graze on Passover and enter again at the first rainfall, they are … domestic animals … But the Rabbis said to him: No, … are desert animals.
Rosh Hashanah: MISHNA: They are four … New Year, … On the first of Nisan is the New Year for kings; … And … for … the Festivals,
On the first of Elul is the New Year for animal tithes; … Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say: … on the first of Tishrei.
On the first of Tishrei is the New Year for … years, … for … Sabbatical Years and Jubilee Years, … for planting, … and for … vegetables,

There are years whose rains are abundant, and there are years whose rains are scare. There are years whose rains fall in their proper time, … there are years whose rains do not fall in their proper time.

a year whose rains fall in their proper time, to what … it be compared? To a servant whose master gave him his … portion on Sunday. … found … dough is baked properly … and it is eaten properly, … a year whose rains do not fall in their proper time, to what … it be compared? To a servant whose master gave him his portion on Shabbat eve, … found … dough is baked improperly, and it is eaten improperly.

a year whose rains are abundant, to what … it be compared? To a servant whose master gave him his portion … at once. … found … the mill grinds … from a kor … as it grinds … from … kav … And … found … dough is diminished from a kor, as it diminishes from a kav.

a year whose rains are scarce, to what … it be compared? To a servant whose master gave him his portion little by little. … found that … that the mill … ground from a kor … it grinds … from … kav. … found … dough … diminished from a kor … diminished from a kav.

Alternatively, when its rains are abundant, to what … be compared? To a person who kneads clay. If he has a lot of water, … water is not used up … the clay … well kneaded. If he has … a little water, … water … used up and the clay will not be well kneaded.

The Sages taught: Once all the Jewish people ascended for … pilgrimage Festival to Jerusalem and there was not … water for them to drink. Nakdimon ben Guryon, … a certain … officer [hegemon] … said to him: Lend me twelve wells of water for the pilgrims, and I will give back to you twelve wells of water. And if I do not give … to you, I will give you twelve talents of silver. And … set him a time

When the … time arrived and no rain had fallen, in the morning … sent … to … Send me either … water or … coins that you owe me. … sent … to him: I still have time, … the entire day is mine. At noontime … sent … to him: Send me either … water or … coins that you owe me. … sent … to him: I still have … left in the day. … sent … to him: Send me either … water or … coins that you owe me. … sent … to him: I still have … left in the day. That officer ridiculed him, saying: … the entire year rain has not fallen,
and now it will rain? He entered the bathhouse in … joy, … As the master entered the bathhouse in his joy, Nakdimon entered the Temple in … sadness. He wrapped himself … and stood in prayer.

He said before … Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that I did not act for my own honor, nor did I act for the honor of my father’s house. Rather, I acted for Your honor, so that there should be water for the Festival pilgrims. Immediately the sky became overcast and rain fell until the twelve cisterns were filled with water, and … they overflowed.

As the master left the bathhouse, Nakdimon ben Guryon left the Temple. When they met one another, … said to him: Give me … money you owe me … the extra water … said to him: I know that the Holy One, Blessed be He, has shaken His world and caused rain to fall only for you. went back and entered the Temple, wrapped himself … and stood in prayer. He said before … Master of the Universe, let it be known that You have beloved ones in Your world. Ahijah the Shilonite cursed … by … a reed: “For the Lord will smite Israel as a reed is shaken in the water.” … Just as this reed stands in a place of water, and its shoots replenish … and its roots are numerous … and even if all the winds in the world come and blow against it, they cannot move it from its place, rather, it sways with them … the winds subside, and the reed … stands in its place,

The Sages … taught … A person should always be soft like a reed, and he should not be stiff like a cedar. He walked behind … until they reached … city. holds in accordance with this … as Rabbi Yannai said: A person should never stand in a place of danger and say: A miracle will be performed for me, … lest a miracle is not performed for him. that when he had … medicine, he would fill … jug … and hang it from the doorpost of his house, saying: All who need, let him come and take … And there are … who say: He had a remedy … Shivta … tradition, … And … he would place a water jug and hang … saying: Anyone who needs, let him come … that he will not be in danger.

due to … there are many soldiers in … Meḥoza,

A certain old man came and taught … him: … who, … says … Give a shekel to my sons … week, but … where, … they are fit … court to give them a sela, … they give them a sela. … But if he said: Give them only a shekel, … gives them only a shekel

if one said: If … die, others should inherit … in their stead, … whether he said: Give them … whether he said: Give them only … gives … only a shekel … said to … whose … is this … It is … Rabbi Meir, who said: It is a mitzva to fulfill the statement of the dead.

They said about Naḥum of Gam Zu that he was blind in both eyes, both his arms were amputated, both his legs were amputated, and his entire body was covered in boils. He said to them: My sons, remove the vessels first, and afterward remove my bed, as I can guarantee you that as long as I am in the house, the house will not fall. … they removed the vessels and afterward they removed his bed, and … the house collapsed.

His students said to him: Rabbi, since you are … a wholly righteous man, … why has this … befallen you? He said to them: My sons, I brought it upon myself. … As once I was traveling along the road to my father-in-law’s house, and I had with me a load … three donkeys, one of food, one of drink, and one of delicacies. A poor person came and stood … in the road, saying: My rabbi, sustain me. I said to him: Wait until I unload the donkey, … I had not managed to unload the donkey before his soul left

I went and fell upon his face and said: May my eyes, which had no compassion on your eyes, be blinded; may my hands, which had no compassion on your hands, be amputated; may my legs, which had no compassion on your legs, be amputated. And my mind did not rest until I said: May my whole body be covered in boils. … said to him: … woe to us that we have seen you in this … He said to them: Woe is me if you had not seen me in this

And why did they call him Naḥum of Gam Zu? … that … any matter that occurred to him, he … say: This too is for the good [gam zu letova]. Once, the Jews wished to send a gift [doron] to the house of the emperor. They said: Who should go … Let Naḥum of Gam Zu go, as he is accustomed to miracles. They sent with him a chest [sifta] full of jewels and pearls, … he went and spent the night in a certain inn. During the night, these residents … took all of … the chest, and filled it with earth.

When he arrived there, … they opened the chest … saw that it was filled with earth. The king wished to put all … to death. He said: The Jews are mocking me. … said: This too is for the good. Elijah … came and appeared before … as one of … said to … Perhaps this earth is from the earth of their father Abraham. As when he threw earth, it turned into swords, … stubble, it turned into arrows, as it is written … “His sword makes them as the dust, his bow as the driven stubble”
There was one province that … were unable to conquer. … tested it … and conquered … entered his treasury and filled … chest with precious jewels and pearls and sent him off with great honor.

When … came to spend the night at that … inn, … said to him: What did you bring with you … that he bestowed upon you such great honor? He said to them: That which I took from here, I brought there. … They tore down their inn and brought … to the king’s palace. They said to him: That earth that was brought here was from our … tested … and it was not found … and he … these residents … put to death.

on a single day, … or … over … four days, this is not … pestilence. And a city that sends out five hundred infantrymen, for example, the village of Amiko, and three dead are removed from it on three consecutive days, this is … pestilence.
on one day or over four days, … pestilence.

Drokart … sent out five hundred infantrymen, and three dead were removed from it on one day. Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda decreed a fast … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: In accordance with whose opinion … in accordance with … Rabbi Meir.
as … said: … liable … its … goring were separated, … its … goring were near … not all the more so

said to … If so, let me arise … to the Master, … said to him: … better … one hundred dinars … son of a peras, … should come to one hundred dinars … son of one hundred dinars; but one hundred dinars … son of one hundred dinars, should not come to one hundred dinars … son of a peras.

there was … pestilence in Sura, … in the neighborhood of Rav there was no pestilence. … therefore thought … due to Rav’s great merit. … it was revealed to them in a dream … Rav’s merit was too great … this matter too small for … Rav … Rather, … due to … a certain man, who … lend his hoe [mara] and shovel [zevila] … for burial.

they said to Rav Yehuda: There is pestilence among the pigs. Rav Yehuda decreed a fast. … Let us say … Rav Yehuda maintains … a plague affecting one species … affect all species, … No, … pigs are different, as their intestines are similar to … humans.

reason … a lady … a maidservant. … a maidservant and a maidservant, … But … they said to Shmuel: There is pestilence in … Bei Ḥozai, he decreed a fast … is different there. Since there are caravans … will join and accompany … in

said to him: Please … what did you suspect of us? … He said to them: I said … a ransom of prisoners became available for the Sages, … but they were … embarrassed to say … me … said to him: Now … let the Master take … He said to them: From that moment … I put them out of my mind … for charity.

not difficult, … this is what … is saying: … seen in the city during the day, … an outbreak; … in the city at night, … not an outbreak. Alternatively, … in the field, even during the day, … not an outbreak.

the … itself. … climbed to the roof and took a baby from … cradle, … an outbreak. … is obvious … Rav Pappa said: … a hunter’s hideout.

An incident … which Elders descended from Jerusalem to their cities … A dilemma was raised before … grain to fill … oven, or perhaps … bread to fill an oven?

For the following … they sound the alarm … on Shabbat: … The Sages taught: … a city that is surrounded by gentile … or a river … both a ship tossed about at sea and an individual who is being pursued by gentiles, or by thieves, or by an evil spirit, … they sound the alarm … on Shabbat.
