Shimon the Timnite says: … even for pestilence, … A dilemma was raised before … the Rabbis did not agree with him … on Shabbat, … on a weekday they agreed with him? Or perhaps they did not agree with him at all,

Come … hear, as it is taught … One cries out for … pestilence on Shabbat, and needless to say on weekdays. Rabbi Ḥanan ben Pitom, the student of Rabbi Akiva, says in the name of Rabbi Akiva: One does not cry out for pestilence at all.

on … trouble that should not befall the community, … The Sages taught … For any trouble that should not befall the community, they sound the alarm for it, except for an overabundance of rain. … What is the reason … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Because one does not pray over an excess of good.

And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: From where … that one does not pray over an excess of good? … is stated: “Bring the whole tithe into the storeroom, … What … “That there shall be more than sufficiency [ad beli dai]”? Rami bar Ḥama said: … that your lips will be worn out [yivlu], … from saying enough [dai].

Rami bar Rav Yud said: … they do sound the alarm over … That … is also taught … a year whose rains are abundant, the members of the priestly watch … would send … to the members of the non-priestly watch: Cast your eyes on your brothers in the Diaspora … that their houses … become their graves.

They asked Rabbi Eliezer: How much rain must fall … they … pray that it should not fall … He said to them … so that a person stands at … Keren Ophel and dips his feet in water. … But isn’t it taught … his hands … I said to you … his feet, … like his hands,
Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: I … saw Keren Ophel, … that an Arab was positioned below, … while riding a camel and … a spear in his hand, he looked like a worm [iniva].

The Sages taught: “Then I will give your rains in their season” … neither drunk nor thirsty; rather, a moderate … For as long as the rains are abundant, they muddy … the land, and it does not give out … produce. Alternatively,
“In their season” … on Wednesday eves, … and on Shabbat eves,

As we found … the days of Shimon ben Shetaḥ that rain … fell for them on Wednesday eves and on Shabbat eves, until wheat grew … as kidneys, and barley … as olive pits, and lentils as golden dinars. And they tied … of … an example [dugma] for … generations, to convey … how much … sin causes, as it is stated: … Your iniquities have turned away these things, and your sins have withheld the good from you”

And we likewise found … in the days of Herod … they were occupied in the building of the Temple, and rain would fall at night. And the next day the wind would blow, the clouds would disperse, the sun would shine, and the people would go out to their work. And … knew … the work of Heaven … by their hands.

An incident … which … sent … to Ḥoni HaMe’aggel. … The Sages taught: Once, most of … Adar had passed but rain had … not fallen. They sent … to Ḥoni HaMe’aggel: Pray, and rain will fall. He prayed, but no rain fell. He drew a circle … and stood inside it, in the manner that the prophet Habakkuk did, as it is stated: “And I will stand upon my watch and set myself upon the tower,

said before … Master of the Universe, Your children have turned their faces toward me, as I am like a member of Your household. … I take an oath by Your great name that I will not move from here until you have mercy upon Your children … Rain began to trickle … His students said to him: Rabbi, we have seen … you … but … we will not die. It appears to us that … rain is falling only … to dissolve your oath,

said … I did not ask for this, but … rain to … cisterns, ditches, and caves. … began to fall furiously, until each and every drop … as the mouth of a barrel, and the Sages estimated that no drop was less than a log … His students said to him: Rabbi, we have seen … you … and we will not die, … it appears to us that rain is falling only to destroy the world.

said before … I did not ask for this … but … rain of benevolence, blessing, and generosity. … fell in their standard manner, until all of the people … ascended to the Temple Mount due to the rain. They said to him: Rabbi, just as you prayed that … should fall, so too, pray that they should stop. He said to them: This is … I received, that one does not pray over an excess of good.

Nevertheless, bring me a bull. … a thanks-offering … They brought him a bull … a thanks-offering. He placed his two hands on its … and said before … Master of the Universe, Your nation Israel, whom You brought out of Egypt, cannot … either an excess of good or an excess of punishment. You grew angry with them … and they are unable to bear … You bestowed upon them … good, and they were … unable to bear … May it be Your will that the rain stop and that there be relief for the world. Immediately, the wind blew, the clouds dispersed, the sun shone, and everyone went out to the fields and gathered for themselves truffles and mushrooms

Shimon ben Shetaḥ relayed to … If you were not Ḥoni, I would have decreed ostracism upon you. For were … years like the years of Elijah, when the keys of rain … in Elijah’s hands, … wouldn’t the name of Heaven have been desecrated by your

However, what can I do to you, as you nag God and He does your bidding, like a son who nags his father and … does his bidding. And … says to … Father, take me to be bathed in hot water; wash me with cold water; give me nuts, almonds, peaches, and pomegranates. And … gives him. About you, the verse states: “Your father and mother will be glad and she who bore you will rejoice”

The Sages taught: What … the members of the Chamber of the Hewn Stone, … send to Ḥoni HaMe’aggel? … “You shall also decree a matter, and it shall be established for you; and the light shall shine upon your ways.

“You shall also decree a matter”; you, … decree from below, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, fulfills your statement from above. “And the light shall shine upon your ways”; a generation that was in darkness, you have illuminated … with your prayer.

“When they cast down, you will say: There is lifting up”; a generation that was cast down, you lifted it up with your prayer. “For He saves the humble person”; a generation that was humble in its transgression, you saved it through your prayer. “He will deliver the one who is not innocent”; a generation that was not innocent, you have delivered it through your prayer. “And he will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands”; you have delivered … through the clean work of your hands.

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: All the days … of that righteous man, … he was distressed over … this verse: “A song of Ascents: When the Lord brought back those who returned to Zion, we were like those who dream” … He said … Is there … who can sleep and dream for seventy years?

One day, he was walking along the road … he saw a certain man planting a carob tree. … said to him: This … after how many years … bear … said to him: … until seventy years … said to him: Is it obvious to you that you will live seventy years, … He said to him: That man … found a world … of carob trees. Just as my ancestors planted for me, I too am planting for my descendants.

sat and ate bread. Sleep overcame him and he slept. A cliff formed around him, and he disappeared from sight and slept for seventy years. When he awoke, he saw a certain man gathering … said to him: … you the one who planted … said to him: I am his son’s son. … said to him: … learn from this that I … slept for seventy years, … he saw that his donkey had sired several herds

went home and said to … Is the son of Ḥoni HaMe’aggel alive? They said to him: His son is no … his son’s son is … He said to them: I am Ḥoni HaMe’aggel. They did not believe him. He went to the study hall, … heard the Sages say … His halakhot are as enlightening … as in the years of Ḥoni HaMe’aggel, for when … would enter the study hall he would resolve for the Sages any difficulty they had. … said to them: I am he, but they did not believe him and did not pay him proper respect. … became very upset, prayed for mercy, and died. Rava said: This … that people say: Either friendship or death,

Abba Ḥilkiyya was the son of Ḥoni HaMe’aggel’s son. And when the world was in need of rain they would send Sages to him, and he would pray for mercy, and rain would fall. Once the world was in need of rain, … the Sages sent a pair of Sages to him … that he would pray for mercy and rain would fall. They went to his house but they did not find him … They went to the field and found him hoeing … They greeted him,

but he did not return their greetings. Toward evening, as he was gathering firewood, he placed the wood and hoe on one shoulder and his cloak on the … shoulder. … the entire way he did not wear his shoes, … when he reached water he put on his shoes. When he reached … shrubs and thorns he lifted up his clothes. When he reached the city, his wife came out to greet him, adorned … When he reached his house, his wife entered first, he entered afterward, and afterward the … Sages entered. He sat and ate bread, but he did not say to the Sages: Come … eat, … He divided bread to his children; to the elder … one piece and to the younger … two.

said to his wife: I know that these Sages have come due to the rain. Let us go up to the roof and pray for mercy. Perhaps the Holy One, Blessed be He, will be appeased, and it will rain, and we will not receive credit ourselves … They went up to the roof. He stood in one corner and she stood in … corner. Clouds began to form on that side where his wife … When he descended, he said to … Why have the Sages come? They said to him: The … Sages have sent us to the Master, … that you should pray for mercy for rain. He said to them: Blessed is God, Who did not require you to … Abba Ḥilkiyya,

We know that the rain has come on the Master’s account. However, let the Master … say … to us these aspects … that are puzzling to us: What is the reason … when we greeted the Master, the Master did not return our greeting? He said to them: I am a day laborer, … and I said … not delay … And what is the reason … the Master carried the firewood on one shoulder and … cloak on … shoulder? He said to them: It was a borrowed robe. I borrowed it for this … and I did not borrow it for that purpose,

What is the reason … the entire way the Master did not wear his shoes, but when he reached water he put on his shoes? He said to them: The entire way I can see … in the water I cannot see. … What is the reason … when the Master reached shrubs and thorns, he lifted up his clothes? He said to them: This … will heal … but this … will not heal

What is the reason … when the Master reached the city, the Master’s wife came out adorned … He said to them: … so that … I will not set my eyes upon another woman. … What is the reason … she entered first, and afterward the Master entered, and … afterward we entered? He said to them: Because you have not been checked

What is the reason … when the Master ate bread, … did not say to us: Come … eat? … Because there is not enough bread … and I said … I should not gain credit from the Sages for nothing, … What is the reason … the Master gave the older child one piece … and the younger child two? He said to them: This … stays at home, … but this … sits … in the synagogue,

And what is the reason … clouds began to form on that side where the Master’s wife stood … Because my wife is frequently at home, and she gives bread to the poor, and … her … benefit … immediate, … I give money … and … the benefit … is not immediate, … Alternatively, … certain hooligans [biryonei] were living in our neighborhood, I prayed that they should die, but she prayed that they should repent. And … they repented.

Ḥanan HaNeḥba was the son of Ḥoni HaMe’aggel’s daughter. When the world was in need of rain, the Sages would send schoolchildren to him, and they would grab him by the hem of his cloak and say to him: Father, Father, give us rain. He said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, act on behalf of these … who cannot distinguish between … Father … Who can provide rain, and … father who cannot provide rain. … And why was he called Ḥanan HaNeḥba? Because he would hide [maḥbi] himself in the lavatory

Rabbi Zerika said to Rav Safra: Come … see what the difference … the powerful men of Eretz Yisrael and the pious men of Babylonia. … the pious men of Babylonia, … Rav Huna and Rav Ḥisda. When the world is in need of rain, … Let us assemble together and pray for mercy, … perhaps the Holy One, Blessed be He, will be appeased and bring rain.

the powerful men of Eretz Yisrael, such as Rabbi Yona, the father of Rabbi Mani, … When the world was in need of rain, he enters his house and say to … Give me my sack [gevalki] and I will go and buy myself a dinar of grain. When he went outside, he went and stood in a low place, as it is written: “Out of the depths I have called You, O Lord” … And he would stand in a secluded place, and cover … with sackcloth, and pray for mercy, and rain would come. When he would come home, they would say to him: … the Master bring grain? He said to them: I said … since rain has … come, … relief in the world

And furthermore, … Rabbi Mani, … son, was persecuted by … of the house of the Nasi. He prostrated himself upon his father’s grave and said … Father, Father, these men are persecuting me. One day, … were passing there, … the legs of their horses became stuck … until they accepted upon themselves not to persecute

And furthermore, … Rabbi Mani was frequently found before Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Elyashiv, … said to him: The wealthy members of my father-in-law’s house are persecuting me. … said: May they become poor, … And … they became poor. … said … they are pressuring me … said: May they become rich … And … they became rich.

said to … The members of my household, … are not acceptable to me, … said: What is her name? … Ḥana. … Let Ḥana grow beautiful, and … she grew beautiful. … said … She acts haughtily toward me, … He said to him: If so, let Ḥana return to her homely … and she returned to her homely

These two students, who were sitting before Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Elyashiv, said to him: Let the Master pray for mercy on our … that we should become very wise. He said to them: … was … with me … but I sent it away.
Rabbi Yosei bar Avin was frequently found before Rabbi Yosei from Yokrat. … he left him and came … before Rav Ashi,

One day … heard … studying … Shmuel said: … one who removes a fish from the sea … when … on … the size of a sela … has dried up, … liable … said to … And let the Master say … between its fins. … said to him: And doesn’t the Master maintain that Rabbi Yosei ben Rabbi Avin said this … said to him: I am he.

said to him: And didn’t the Master … before … frequent … of Rabbi Yosei from Yokrat? … said to him: Yes. … said to him: And what is the reason … the Master left … and came here? … said to him: … a man who has no mercy on his … son, and no mercy on his daughter. How, … could he have mercy on me?

What is … his son? One day … hired … laborers to … field. It grew late and he did not bring them food. … said to the son of … We are starving. They were sitting under a fig tree, … said: Fig tree, fig tree. Yield your fruits, … father’s workers may eat. … yielded … and they ate.

In the meantime, his father came … said to … Do not be angry with me for being late, as I was engaged in a mitzva, and until just now I was traveling … They said to him: … the Merciful One satisfy you just as your son satisfied us … He said to them: From where … They said: Such-and-such an incident occurred. … said to … My son, you troubled your Creator … the fig to yield its fruit not in its … time, … died before his time.

What is … his daughter? He had … beautiful daughter. One day … saw a certain man piercing a hole in the hedge … and looking at … said to him: What is this? … said to him: My teacher, if I have not merited taking her … I not … merit to look at her? Rabbi Yosei said to her: My daughter, you are causing people distress. Return to your dust, and let people no … stumble … due to you.

He had a certain donkey that people hired each day … In the evening they would send it back … the money for its hire on its back, and … go to its owner’s house. But if they added or subtracted from … would not go. One day … forgot a pair of sandals on … and it did not move until they removed … from … after which it went off.

Whenever the charity collectors would see Elazar of … Birta, they would hide from him, as any … had with him he would give them, … One day, … went to the market to purchase … for his daughter’s dowry. The charity collectors saw him and hid from him.

He went and ran after them, saying to them: I adjure you, … in what … are you engaged? They said to him: … of an orphan boy and an orphan girl. He said to them: … by the Temple service that they take precedence over my daughter. He took everything he had with him and gave it to them. He was left with one … dinar, … he bought himself wheat, and … ascended … and threw it into the granary.

wife came and said to her daughter: What has your father brought? She said to … Whatever he brought he threw into the granary. She went to open the door of the granary, … saw that the granary was full of wheat, … it was coming out through the doorknob, and the door would not open … to the wheat. … daughter went to the study hall … said to … Come and see what He Who loves You, … has performed for you. He said to her: … by the Temple service, … as you … is consecrated … and you have … in it only as one of the poor Jews.

Rabbi Yehuda Nesia decreed a fast … prayed for mercy, but rain did not come. He said, … How great … between … Samuel of Rama, … and … Yehuda ben Gamliel. Woe to the generation that is stuck … woe to him in whose days this has occurred. He grew upset, and rain came.

In the house of the Nasi a fast was declared, but they didn’t inform Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish … In the morning they informed them. Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yoḥanan: … We did not accept … upon ourselves the evening before, … said to him: We are drawn after

a fast was declared in the house of the Nasi, but rain did not come. Oshaya, the youngest … of the group … taught them … “Then it shall be, if it shall be committed in error by the congregation, it being hidden from their eyes”
a parable … involving a bride who is in her father’s home … As long as her eyes are beautiful, her body need not be examined, … her eyes are bleary [terutot], her entire body requires examination.

servants … came and placed a scarf around his neck and tormented him … His townsmen said to them: Let him be, as he also causes us pain … since we see that all his actions are for the sake of Heaven we do not say anything to him and let him be. You too … let him be.

Rabbi … declared a fast but rain did not come. Ilfa descended … before him, and some say … Rabbi Ilfi. He recited: He Who makes the wind blow, and the wind … blew. … Who makes the rain come, and … the rain came. … said to him: What are your … deeds, … He said to him: I live in an impoverished city, in which there is no wine for kiddush or havdala. I go to the effort of bringing … wine for kiddush and havdala, and I … fulfill their duty.

Rav happened … a certain place … he decreed a fast but rain did not come. The prayer leader descended … before him … recited: He Who makes the wind blow, and the wind blew. … said: … Who makes the rain fall, and the rain came. … said to him: What are your … deeds? He said to him: I am a teacher of children, and I teach the Bible to the children of the poor as to the children of the rich, and … anyone who cannot … I do not take anything from him. And I have a fishpond, and any … who neglects … I bribe him with … and calm him, and soothe him until he comes and reads.
Rav Naḥman decreed a fast, prayed for mercy, but rain did not come. … said: Take Naḥman … throw him from the wall to the ground, … He grew upset, and rain came.

Rabba decreed a fast. He prayed for mercy, but rain did not come. They said to him: But when … Rav Yehuda decreed a fast, rain would come. He said to them: What can I do? If … due to … study, we are superior to … as in the years of Rav Yehuda all of their learning

was … of Nezikin, … and we learn … six orders … And when Rav Yehuda reached … Uktzin, … a woman who pickles a vegetable in a pot, … and some say … olives that are pickled with their leaves are ritually pure, … he would say: … the disputes between Rav and Shmuel that we see here.

And we, … learn … Uktzin in thirteen yeshivot, while, … when Rav Yehuda would remove one of his shoes … the rain would … come, … And … we cry out all day and no one notices us. … If … due to … deeds, if there is … who has seen me do anything … let him say … but what can the great … of the generation do when their generation is not worthy,

Rav Yehuda saw two people wasting bread, … He said: I … learn from … this … there is plenty in the world. He cast his eyes … and there was a famine. The Sages said to Rav Kahana, son of Rav Neḥunya, the attendant of … The Master, who is frequently present … persuade him to leave by way of the door nearest the market, … persuaded … and he went out to the market, … he saw a crowd.

He said to them: What is this … They said to him: … by a container [kuspa] of dates that is for sale. He said: … I … learn from this … a famine in the world. He said to his attendant: … remove my shoes … He removed one of his shoes and rain came. When he began to take off the other … Elijah came and said to him: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: If you remove … other … I will destroy the … world

Rav Mari, son of Shmuel’s daughter, said: … I was standing on the bank of the Pappa River. I saw angels who appeared as sailors bringing sand and filling ships … and it became fine flour. Everyone came to buy … I said to them: Do not purchase this … as it is the product of miracles. Tomorrow, boats filled with wheat will come from Parzina,

Rava happened … to … Hagrunya. He decreed a fast, but rain did not come. He said to … Everyone, continue your fast … The next morning he said to them: Whoever had a dream last night, let him say … Rabbi Elazar of Hagronya said to them: … was recited to me in my dream. Good greetings to a good master from a good Lord, Who in His goodness does good for His people. … said: I … learn from this … it is a favorable time to pray for mercy. He prayed for mercy and rain came.

a certain man who was sentenced to be flogged by Rava’s court because he had relations with a gentile woman. Rava flogged … and he died … matter was heard … the house of … King Shapur, he wanted to punish Rava … Ifra Hormiz, mother of King Shapur, said to her son: Do not interfere … with the Jews, as whatever they request from … their Master, He gives them.

He said to her: What is this … They pray for mercy and rain comes. He said to her: … as that … because it is the time for rain, … Rather, … let them pray for mercy now, in … season of Tammuz, and let rain come. … sent … to Rava: Direct your attention and pray for mercy that rain may come. He prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.

He said before … Master of the Universe, … “O God, we have heard with our ears, our fathers have told us, what work You did in their days, in days of old” … but we have not seen it with our … eyes. … rain came until the gutters of Meḥoza … poured into the Tigris … father came … appeared to him in a dream and said to him: Is there … who troubles Heaven so much … said to him: Change your place … He changed his place, and the next day he found that his bed had been slashed by knives.

Rav Pappa decreed a fast, but rain did not come. His heart became weak … he swallowed [seraf] a bowl [pinka] of porridge, and prayed for mercy, but rain … did not come. Rav Naḥman bar Ushpazti said to him: If the Master swallows another bowl of porridge, rain will come. … embarrassed and grew upset, and rain came.

Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa was traveling along a road … it … to rain. He said before … Master of the Universe, the entire world is comfortable, … but Ḥanina is suffering, … The rain ceased. When he arrived at his home, he said before … Master of the Universe, the entire world is suffering … and Ḥanina is comfortable? The rain … come

Rav Yosef said, … What effect does the prayer of the High Priest have against … Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa? As we learned … would recite a brief prayer in the outer chamber. … What … he pray? Ravin bar Adda and Rava bar Adda both say in the name of Rav Yehuda … May it be Your will, Lord our God, that this year shall be rainy and hot. … Is heat a good … On the contrary, it is unfavorable.

Rather, … If … hot, may it … be rainy and moist … And let not the prayer of travelers enter Your presence. Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, in the name of Rav Yehuda, concluded … May the rule of power not depart from the house of Judea. And may Your nation Israel not depend upon each other for sustenance, nor upon another nation.

Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: Each and every day a Divine Voice emerges … and says: The entire world is sustained by … My son Ḥanina … and … Ḥanina, My son, a kav of carobs, … is sufficient … from … Shabbat eve to … Shabbat eve. … wife would heat the oven every Shabbat eve and create … smoke,

due to embarrassment, … She had a certain evil neighbor … said … Now, I know that they have nothing. What, … is all this … She went and knocked on the door … embarrassed, and she ascended to an inner room [inderona].

A miracle was performed for … as … saw the oven filled with bread and the kneading basin filled with dough. She said to … So-and-so, so-and-so, bring a shovel, as your bread is burning. She said to … I too went inside for that … taught: She too had entered … to bring a shovel, because … accustomed to miracles

wife said to him: Until when will we continue to suffer this … He said to her: What can we do? … Pray for mercy that something will be given to you … He prayed for mercy … like … palm of a hand emerged and gave him one leg of a golden table. That night, his wife saw in a dream … the future, … the righteous will eat at a golden table that has three legs, but … on a table that has two legs.

he said to her: Are you content that everyone will eat at a complete table and we … at a defective table? She said to him: But what can we do? Pray for mercy, that … be taken from you. He prayed for mercy, and it was taken … taught … The last miracle was greater than the first, as … is learned … does not take back.

one … evening, … saw that his daughter was sad. He said to her: My daughter, why are you sad? She said to him: I confused a vessel of vinegar for a vessel of oil and I lit … Shabbat lamp with … He said to her: My daughter, what are you concerned … He Who said to the oil … burn can say to the vinegar … burn. … taught: … burned continuously the entire day, until they brought from it light for havdala.

Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa had some goats. … said to him: … are damaging … He said to them: If they are causing damage, let them be eaten by bears. But if … not … each of them, … evening, bring a bear … between its horns. … evening, each one brought in a bear … between its horns.

had a certain neighbor who was building a house, but the ceiling beams … not … reach … She came before … said to him: I built my house, but my … beams do not reach the walls. He said to her: What is your name? She said to him: … Ikku. … If so [ikku], may your beams reach

taught: … reached … until they jutted out a cubit from this side and a cubit from that side. And some say … they extended with segments [senifin], … It is taught … Palaimo says: I saw that house, and its beams jutted out a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side. And they said to me: This … house that Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa roofed by means of his prayer.

And Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa, from where did he have goats? Wasn’t he poor, … And furthermore, the Sages … said: One may not raise small, domesticated animals in Eretz Yisrael, … Rav Pineḥas … An incident … a certain man passed by the entrance of … house and left chickens there. And Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa’s wife found them

And … said her: Do not eat of their eggs, … And … laid many eggs, and chickens … And … were distressing them, they sold them and bought goats with their proceeds. Once that same man who lost the chickens passed by and said to his companion: Here is where I left my chickens. Rabbi Ḥanina heard … said to him: Do you have a sign … them? He said to him: Yes. He gave him the sign and took the goats. … And these are the very goats that brought bears … between their horns.

Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat was hard-pressed … an act … was performed on him, but he did not have anything to taste … He took a clove of garlic and put it in his mouth. His heart became weak and he fell asleep. The Sages came to inquire … his … saw him weeping and laughing, and a ray of light was shining from his forehead.

When he awoke they said to him: What is the reason that you were laughing and crying? He said to them: … that … the Holy One, Blessed be He, was sitting with me, and I said to Him: Until when will I suffer … in this world? And He said to me: Elazar, My son, … convenient … you that I return the world to its … beginning? Perhaps you will be born in an hour of sustenance

I said before Him: … all this, … and … a possibility … I said to Him: … that I have … lived more … or … that I will live … He said to me: … that you have lived … I said before Him: If so, I do not want

He said to me: As a reward for saying: I do not want, I will give you in the World-to-Come thirteen rivers of pure balsam oil as large as the Euphrates and the Tigris for you to enjoy. I said before Him: This and no more? He said to me: But … what will I give to your colleagues? I said to Him: And do I request … from a person, who does not have enough? … He … snapped His finger [askutla] on my forehead and said to me: Elazar, my son, My arrows … upon you, My arrows.

Rabbi Ḥama bar Ḥanina decreed a fast but rain did not come. They said to him: Didn’t Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi decree a fast and rain came? It is taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: There is no handbreadth … from above toward which … the deep does not rise three handbreadths. … But isn’t it taught … two handbreadths? … not difficult. Here, … to worked … there, … to unworked

they were fasting … and rain fell for them before sunrise, … The Sages taught: … they were fasting … and rain fell for them before sunrise, … not complete … after sunrise, they … complete … the statement of Rabbi Meir. only on a satisfied soul and a full stomach. … Is that so? But Rav Pappa happened … the synagogue of Avi Govar … and he decreed a fast, and rain fell for them before midday, and … he recited hallel … and … they ate and drank. … The inhabitants of … Meḥoza are different, as drunkenness is common among them.

MISHNA: At three times in the year priests raise their hands … four times in … day, in the morning prayer, in the additional prayer, in the afternoon prayer, and … in the closing of the gates, … During … fasts … and during non-priestly watches [ma’amadot], … and on Yom Kippur.

the early prophets, … instituted … twenty-four priestly watches, … For each and every priestly watch there was … non-priestly watch in Jerusalem of priests, Levites, and Israelites

When … time arrived … priestly watch to ascend, … priests and Levites … ascend to Jerusalem … And … the Israelites … to that priestly watch, … assembled in their towns and read the act of Creation. any day that has … hallel, … there is no … non-priestly watch in the morning prayer. … an additional offering, … not … at the closing prayer. … a wood offering … no … in the afternoon prayer. … the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

times … the wood … of priests and the people. … nine … On the first of Nisan, the descendants of Araḥ ben Yehuda; on the twentieth of Tammuz, the descendants of David ben Yehuda; on the fifth of Av, the descendants of Parosh ben Yehuda; on the seventh of … the descendants of Jonadab ben Rechab; on the tenth of … the descendants of Sena’a ben Binyamin; on the fifteenth of … the descendants of Zattu ben Yehuda.

the tablets were broken … the daily offering was nullified … the city … were breached; … Apostemos … burned a Torah scroll; and … placed an idol in the Sanctuary.

from when … Av begins, one decreases … rejoicing. … the week in which the Ninth of Av occurs, it is prohibited to cut one’s hair and to launder … but … on Thursday … are permitted in deference to Shabbat. … the eve of the Ninth of Av a person may not eat two cooked dishes … neither eat meat nor drink wine. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: … adjust … Rabbi Yehuda obligates one to overturn the bed … but the Rabbis did not agree with him.

Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: There were no days as joyous for the Jewish people as the fifteenth of Av and as Yom Kippur, as on them the daughters of Jerusalem would go out in white clothes, … borrowed … so as not to embarrass one who did not have … All the garments … require immersion,

And the daughters of Jerusalem would go out and dance in the vineyards. And what would they say? Young man, please lift up your eyes and see what you choose for yourself … Do not set your eyes toward beauty, but set your eyes toward … family, … “Grace is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the Lord, she shall be praised” … and it … says: “Give her the fruit of her hands, and let her works praise her in the gates”

And similarly, it says … “Go forth, daughters of Zion, and gaze upon King Solomon, upon the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, and on the day of the gladness of his heart” … “On the day of his wedding”; this is the giving of the Torah … “And on the day of the gladness of his heart”; this is the building of the Temple, may it be rebuilt speedily in our days.

GEMARA: … At three times in the year priests raise their hands … Do fast days and … non-priestly watches have an additional prayer? … is incomplete and is teaching the following: At three times in the year priests raise their hands each time they pray, and on some of these … four times a day, … the morning prayer, … the additional prayer, … the afternoon prayer, and in the closing of the gates, … And these are … three times: … fasts, non-priestly watches, and Yom Kippur.

Rav Naḥman said … Rabba bar Avuh said: This … is the statement of Rabbi Meir. However, the Rabbis say: The morning prayer and the additional prayer have … the raising of the hands, … the afternoon prayer and the closing prayer [ne’ila] do not have the raising of the hands.

Rabbi Yehuda says: The morning prayer and the additional prayer have … the afternoon prayer and ne’ila do not have the raising of the hands. Rabbi Yosei says: Ne’ila has the raising of the hands; the afternoon prayer does not have the raising of the hands.

With regard to what … disagree? Rabbi Meir maintains: What is the reason … priests do not spread their hands … every day in the afternoon prayer? … due to … drunkenness, … now, … there is no … drunkenness,

Rabbi Yehuda maintains … the morning prayer and the additional prayer, when drunkenness is not common on every … day, the Sages did not issue a decree … during them. … the afternoon prayer and ne’ila, when drunkenness is common on every day, the Sages issued a decree … during them,
Rabbi Yosei maintains … the afternoon prayer, which is … every day, the Sages issued a decree concerning it, … ne’ila, which is not … every day, the Sages did not issue … decree to it,

Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Meir. And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The people act in accordance with … Rabbi Meir. And Rava said: The custom is in accordance with … Rabbi Meir.

And Rav Naḥman said … the halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei. … And … the halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei. … And nowadays, what is the reason … priests spread their hands … in the afternoon prayer of a fast? … Since they spread … near sunset, … considered like ne’ila,

In any event, … everyone agrees … it is prohibited … a drunken … to raise his hands … From where are these matters … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of bar Kappara: Why is the portion of the priest who recites the benediction … juxtaposed with the portion of the nazirite … to say … just as it is prohibited … a nazirite … wine, so too, it is prohibited for a priest who recites the benediction … wine.

Rabbi Zeira’s father, and some say … Oshaya bar Zavda, strongly objects to this … If … Just as it is prohibited … a nazirite … pits, … so too, … prohibited for a priest who recites the benediction … pits. … Rabbi Yitzḥak said … the verse states: “To minister to Him and to bless in His name” … Just as … is permitted … who ministers … of … pits, so too, … is permitted … a priest who recites the benediction … of … pits.
If … just as … ministers … not … blemished, so too, a priest who recites the benediction … not … blemished. … is … juxtaposed to a nazirite,
And what did you see that you juxtaposed … in … a leniency? … juxtapose for a stringency, … are … support … by rabbinic … and … as a leniency,

these are … non-priestly watches: Since it is stated: “Command the children of Israel.” … What is … saying … is saying as follows: … non-priestly watches, … And what is the reason that they instituted non-priestly watches? Since it is stated: “Command the children of Israel and say to them: My offering of food, which is presented to Me made by a fire,

But how can a person’s offering be sacrificed when he is not standing next to it? The early prophets, … instituted twenty-four priestly watches. For each and every priestly watch there was … watch in Jerusalem of priests, Levites, and Israelites. … time arrived … priestly watch to ascend, … priests and Levites … ascend to Jerusalem.

The Sages taught: … twenty-four priestly watches in Eretz Yisrael, and twelve in Jericho. … Twelve in Jericho? … there are too many of them, … Rather, … twelve of which were in Jericho. … When … time arrived … priestly watch to ascend, half the priestly watch would ascend from … Eretz Yisrael to Jerusalem, and half the priestly watch would ascend from Jericho, in order to provide water and food to their brothers in Jerusalem

Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: Priests, Levites, and Israelites … indispensable for the offering, … It is taught in a baraita … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar … Priests, Levites, and musical instruments are indispensable for the offering. … With regard to what … disagree? One Sage, … holds … the main … of … song … vocal, and one Sage, … holds … the main … of … song … with a vessel,

raises an objection … Moses instituted for the Jews eight priestly watches, four from Elazar and four from Itamar. And David and Samuel came and established them as twenty-four, as it is stated: “Whom David and Samuel the seer ordained in their set office” … This is what … is saying: Through their ordination by David and Samuel of Rama … they established them as twenty-four.

The Gemara asks: What is: And it says? … And if you would say … just as the descendants of Elazar increased, so too, the descendants of Itamar increased, … eight … were initially four, … come … hear: “One father’s house taken for Elazar, and proportionately for Itamar,” … a conclusive refutation of … Rav Ḥama bar Gurya,
Rav Ḥama bar Gurya … said to you … is … tanna’im, … and I stated … in accordance with that tanna who said … eight
The Sages taught: … priestly watches ascended from the … exile, … And these are … Jedaiah, Harim, Pashhur, and Immer. The prophets among … arose

and divided them and established them as twenty-four … mixing them up, and putting them in a receptacle [kalfei] … Jedaiah came and drew his portion and the lot of … other … six. Harim came and … drew his portion and the lot of … other … six. And likewise Pashhur, and likewise Immer.

And likewise the prophets among them stipulated that even … Jehoiarib, who … headed the priestly watches, ascended … Jedaiah would not be demoted from its place … Jedaiah … precedence, and Jehoiarib … subordinate to it.

And the Israelites of that priestly watch assembled in their towns and read the act of Creation. … From where is this matter, … Rabbi Ya’akov bar Aḥa said … Rav Asi said: Were it not for … non-priestly watches … heaven and earth would not continue to exist, as it is stated: “And he said: Lord God, by what shall I know that I shall inherit it?”

Abraham said: Master of the Universe, perhaps the Jews … sin before You. … You treat them as … the generation of the flood and the generation of the dispersion, … said to him: No. … said before … Master of the Universe, tell me, with what shall I inherit it? … said to … “Take for Me a three-year-old heifer, and a three-year-old goat,

The Sages taught: The members of the priestly watch would pray for the offerings of their brothers, … that it should be accepted with favor. What is the reason … not … on Sunday? Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Due to the Christians, … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said: Because it is the third day after the creation

Reish Lakish said: … due to the added soul, as Reish Lakish said: An added soul is given to man on Shabbat eve, … at the conclusion of Shabbat it is removed it from him, as it is stated: “He ceased from work and rested … vayinafash … Since one has rested … woe for the soul [vai nefesh] … lost,

Rav said: … repeats … And Shmuel said: … split … And … Rav, who said … repeats, what is the reason … he did not say … split … maintains … any verse that was not divided by Moses, we do not divide it.

And Shmuel … what is the reason there, … Because it is not possible … Here too, it is not possible
And Shmuel said … splits … What is the reason … he did not say … repeats … decree due to those who enter … a decree due to those who leave

raises an objection … A chapter … of six verses … be read by two … and … of five … by one. And if the first … reads three … the second … two … of that chapter and one … another chapter. And some say … three … as one may not begin to read a chapter … fewer than three verses.
According to the one who said … repeat … let … repeat … And according to the one who said … split … let … split … It is different there,
as … has space,

A long passage is read by two … in the morning prayer and in the additional prayer. any day that has … hallel, … it has no … non-priestly watch … What is … difference between this and that, … These … by Torah law, but these … by rabbinic law,

times … wood offering of priests and the people. The Sages taught: Why was it necessary to state … times … wood offering of priests and the people? They said … When the people of the exile ascended … they did not find … in … chamber … And these … arose and donated from their own

and with … were … priests and Levites, and anyone … The Sages taught: Who were the descendants of those who deceived … with a pestle and the descendants of those who packed dried figs?

They said … Once, the evil kingdom … issued … of apostasy against the Jews, that they may not bring wood for the arrangement … and that they … not bring first fruits to Jerusalem. And when they reached the guards, … said to them: Where are you going? They said to them: … to prepare two round cakes of pressed figs with the mortar that is … before us and with the pestle that … our shoulders. As soon as they passed … they decorated the baskets … and brought them to Jerusalem.

taught: This … the descendants of Salmai of Netophat. … The Sages taught: Who are the descendants of Salmai of Netophat? … Once, the evil kingdom … issued … of apostasy against the Jews, that they may not bring wood for the arrangement … that the Jews … not ascend for the … Festival.

They said to them: … to bring … doves from the dovecote that is … before us and with these ladders that are on our shoulders. As soon as they had passed … they dismantled … and took them up to Jerusalem.
And about these … and … like them, … says: “The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing” … And about Jeroboam, son of Nevat, and his ilk, it is stated: “But the name of the wicked shall rot”

On the twentieth of … the descendants of Pahath Moab ben Yehuda. … taught: The descendants of Pahath Moab ben Yehuda are the descendants of David ben Yehuda. … the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yosei says: These are the descendants of Joab, son of Zeruiah,

If it … Rabbi Yehuda, let him teach … the descendants of David ben Yehuda returned … a second … And if … Rabbi Yosei, let him teach … descendants of Joab, son of Zeruiah, returned … a second

on the first of Tevet there was no non-priestly watch … Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Ḥisda, said to Rav Ashi:

Rav Ashi said to him: Now, … overrides … which is not its own, … not all the more so … its own … said to … is what I am saying to you: … let it override only its own

said to him: There is Rabbi Yosei, who holds in accordance with your … as it is taught … Rabbi Yosei says: … any day on which there is an additional offering, there is a non-priestly watch. … To which non-priestly watch … If we say … the non-priestly watch of the morning prayer, but the first tanna also said this. Rather, … non-priestly watch of the additional prayer. … not override … its own

Rather, … of the afternoon prayer. … the wood offering overrides … Rather, is it not … in the closing prayer? … learn from this … overrides its own … not override … that is not its own. … learn from this

Rav happened … Babylonia, … he saw that they were reciting hallel on a New Moon. … he thought to stop them, … Once he saw that they were omitting … he said: … learn from this … they are maintaining the custom of their forefathers, … is taught … An individual should not begin … but if he has begun he should complete

said to Him: “These also reel through wine, and stagger through strong drink; … they stumble [paku] in judgment [peliliyya]” … paku … only to Gehenna, as it is stated: “That this shall not be a cause of stumbling [puka] to you” … and … peliliyya … only to judges, as it is stated: “And he shall pay as the judges determine [bifelilim]”

let the king and Haman come this day to the banquet … The Sages taught … What did Esther see to invite Haman … Rabbi Elazar says: She hid a snare for him, as it is stated: “Let their table become a snare before them”

prepared for him” … taught … he had prepared for himself.

said to … With what were you occupied? They said to him: When the Temple is standing, one who pledges a meal-offering would bring a handful of fine flour and achieve atonement with it. said to him: Stand up, put on these garments and ride on this horse, for the king wants you … said to him: I cannot … until I enter the bathhouse … bei vanei … and trim my hair, for it is not proper conduct to use the king’s garments in this state

And Parshandatha … the ten sons of Haman” … Rav Adda from Jaffa said: … the ten sons of Haman and … “ten” must be said in one breath. What is the reason … their souls all departed together. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … vav in … “Vaizatha” … must be elongated as a pole, like a steering oar of a ship [liberot]. What is the reason … they were all hanged on one pole.

Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa said … Rabbi Sheila, a man of the village of Timarta, interpreted … homiletically: All … the songs … are written … a half brick arranged upon a whole brick and a whole brick arranged upon a half brick,

This is the principle for all songs in the Bible except … this song, … and … the kings of Canaan … a half brick arranged upon a half brick and a whole brick arranged upon a whole brick, … What is the reason … So that they should never rise from their downfall.
“And the king said to Esther the queen: The Jews have slain … in Shushan the capital, … Rabbi Abbahu said: This teaches that an angel came and slapped him on his mouth,

“But when she came before the king, he said with a letter” … “He said”? It should have said: “She said,” … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: She said to … Let it be said by … mouth, … that which is written in the letter
“Words of peace and truth” … Rabbi Tanḥum said, and some say … Rabbi Asi … teaches that … requires scoring, … as the Torah itself,

And the decree of Esther confirmed … “the decree of Esther” indeed … “the matters of the fasts” … not? … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … “The matters of the fasts … And the decree of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim,”

“For Mordecai the Jew was second to the king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted by the majority of his brethren” … “By the majority of his brethren,” but not by all his brethren. … teaches that some … of the Sanhedrin parted from him,

Rav Yosef said: Studying Torah is greater than saving lives, as initially, … Mordecai was mentioned after four … but at the end … after five. … At first it is written: “Who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan” … but in the end … it is written: “Who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahmani, Mordecai, Bilshan”
Rav said, and some say … Rav Shmuel bar Marta … Studying Torah is greater … than building the Temple. … for as long as Baruch ben Neriah was alive … Ezra, … did not leave him and go up

Rabba said … Rav Yitzḥak bar Shmuel bar Marta said: Studying Torah is … more … than honoring one’s father and mother, … that for all those years that our father Jacob spent in the house of Eber … he was not punished … As the Master said:

Why were the years of Ishmael mentioned … In order to reckon through them the years of Jacob. As it is written: “And these are the years of the life of Ishmael, a hundred and thirty-seven years” … How much older was Ishmael than Isaac? Fourteen years. As it is written: “And Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to Abram” … And it is written: “And Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him” … And it is written … “And Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them” … how old was Ishmael when Jacob was born? Seventy-four. How many of his years remained … Sixty-three,

And it was taught … Jacob our father was sixty-three years old at the time he was blessed by his father, and at that same time Ishmael died. … As it is written: “When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed … then Esau went to Ishmael and took for a wife Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, … the sister of Nebaioth” … From the fact that … is stated: “the daughter of Ishmael,” do I not know that she was the sister of Nebaioth? … This teaches that Ishmael betrothed her … and … died, and Nebaioth her brother married her off.

sixty-three … and … fourteen until Joseph was born, this … seventy-seven … And it is written: “And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh” … This … a hundred and seven … seven … of plenty and … two of famine, … this … a hundred and sixteen

But it is written: “And Pharaoh said to Jacob, How many are the days of the years of your life? And Jacob said to Pharaoh, The days of the years of my sojournings are a hundred and thirty years” … which is … hundred and sixteen

Rather, learn from here … As it is taught … Jacob was … in the house of Eber for fourteen years … in hiding … Eber died … two years after Jacob our father went down to Aram-naharaim, … left … there, … then went … to Aram-naharaim. … when … stood at the well … he was seventy-seven years old.

And from where do we … that … was not punished … As it is taught … It turns out that Joseph was away from his father for twenty-two years, just as Jacob our father was away from his … father … Jacob … thirty-six … the fourteen … that he was in the house of Eber are not counted,

ultimately, … Laban’s house for … twenty years. … Rather, … because on his journey … he tarried … two years … as it is taught … left Aram-naharaim and came to Sukkot, and spent eighteen months there, as it is stated: “And Jacob journeyed to Sukkot, built himself a house, and made booths [sukkot] for his cattle” … He then was in Bethel for six months, and he brought offerings,

MISHNA: … one who reads the Megilla out of order, … he has not fulfilled … he read it by heart, … if he read it in … translation … in any … language … he has not fulfilled … However, for those who speak a foreign language, one may read … in … foreign language. And one who speaks a foreign language who heard … Ashurit, … has fulfilled

If one read … at intervals, … or … he is dozing off, he has fulfilled his obligation. If one was writing … or expounding upon it, or correcting it, … If he had intent … he has fulfilled his obligation, but if not, he has not fulfilled
If … was written … with sam or with sikra or with komos or with kankantom, … on neyar or on diftera, … he has not fulfilled … unless … is written in Ashurit, … upon parchment and with ink.

GEMARA: … From where are these matters … Rava said: The verse states … according to their writing, and according to their appointed times … Just as their appointed times cannot be out of order, … so too, their writing must not be out of order.

Is reading written here at all? … observing” … is written … as it is written: “That they should unfailingly observe these two days … Rather, … from here, as it is written: “And that these days should be remembered and observed … Remembering is juxtaposed to observing, … Just as observing cannot be out of order, … so too, remembering, … may not be out of order.
taught … also to hallel, and also to the recitation of Shema, and … to … prayer,
From where do we … hallel … Rabba said: As it is written … “From the rising of the sun until its setting … Rav Yosef said: … “This is the day that the Lord has made”
Rav Avya said: … “Blessed be the name of the Lord” … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said, and some say … Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov … here, … “From now and for evermore”

reciting the Shema … As it is taught … The recital of the Shema must be as it is written, … the statement of Rabbi … But the Rabbis say: … in any language. … What is the reason of Rabbi … The verse states:
“And … shall be” … “shall be” as they are, … And … the Sages, what is the reason … The verse states: “Hear, … in any language that you hear,

And … Rabbi … as well, isn’t it … written, “hear”? … This … is necessary … Make heard to your ears what your mouth is saying, … And … the Sages … hold like the one who said … one recites the Shema but does not make it audible to his ears, he has … fulfilled

And … the Sages as well, isn’t it … written, “And … shall be”? … That … is necessary … that one must not recite … out of order, … And from where does Rabbi … that one must not recite … out of order? … Words, … “the words,” … And … the Sages … words … “the words” is inconsequential according to them.
Shall we say that Rabbi … maintains … the entire Torah may be recited in any language? As, if it enters your mind … may be recited only in the sacred tongue, … why do I … to write “and … shall be”
it is … necessary … it might have entered your mind … “hear” … as … the Sages, … the Merciful One writes … “and … shall be,”
Shall we say … that the Sages maintain … the entire Torah must be recited … in the sacred tongue, … As, if it enters your mind … may be recited in any language, why do I … to write “hear”
it was … necessary … it could enter your mind to say … “and … shall be” … as … Rabbi … the Merciful One writes … “hear”

prayer … From where do we … As it is taught … Shimon HaPakuli arranged the eighteen blessings … before Rabban Gamliel in their … order in Yavne, … Rabbi Yoḥanan said, and some say that it was taught in a baraita: A hundred and twenty Elders, … among them several prophets, established … eighteen blessings … in their … order,

The Sages taught … From where … that one says … the Patriarchs, … As it is stated: “Ascribe to the Lord, mighty ones” … And from where … that one … says … mighty deeds? As it is stated … “Ascribe to the Lord glory and strength” … And from where … that one … says … holiness? As it is stated … “Give to the Lord the glory due to His name; worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness”

And why did they see … to say … understanding after … holiness? As it is stated: “They shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall revere the God of Israel” … “They also that erred in spirit shall come to understanding” … And why did they see … to say … repentance after … understanding? As it is written: “And they will understand with their heart, repent, and be healed”

If so, … let … say … the … healing should be said after … repentance. … This cannot enter your mind, as it is written: “And let him return to the Lord, and He will have compassion upon him; and to our God, for He will abundantly pardon”

But what did you see to rely on this … Rely on the other … Another verse, … written: “Who forgives all your iniquities, Who heals all your diseases, Who redeems your life from the pit” … Is that … to say that … redemption and healing … forgiveness? But isn’t it written: “Repent, and be healed” … That … not … the … healing from illness, but rather … the … healing of forgiveness,

And why did they see … to say … redemption as the seventh … Rava said: Since … destined to be redeemed in the seventh … consequently, they fixed … as the seventh … But didn’t the Master say … In the sixth … sounds … in the seventh … wars; and upon the conclusion of the seventh … the son of David, … will come? … war … is also the beginning of the redemption
And why did they see … says … healing as the eighth … Rabbi Aḥa said: Since circumcision was assigned to the eighth … requires healing, consequently, they established … as the eighth

And why did they see … says the blessing of … years as the ninth … Rabbi Alexandri said: … in reference to those who raise the prices … as it is written: “Break the arm of the wicked” … And when David expressed this … he expressed it in the ninth

And why did they see … says … the ingathering of … exiles after the blessing of the years? As it is written: “And you, O mountains of Israel, you shall shoot forth your branches, and yield your fruit to My people Israel; for they will soon be coming” … And once the exiles have been gathered, judgment will be meted out to the wicked, as it is stated: “And I will turn my hand against you and purge away your dross as with lye” … and … it is written: “And I will restore your judges as at first”

And once judgment is meted out to the wicked, the transgressors, … will cease to be. … and one includes evildoers with them, as it is stated: “And the destruction of the transgressors and of the sinners shall be together, … shall cease to be”

And once the heretics cease to be, the horn, … of the righteous will be exalted, as it is written: “All the horns of the wicked will I cut off; but the horns of the righteous shall be exalted” … And he includes the righteous converts along with the righteous, as it is stated: “You shall rise up before the hoary head, and honor the face of the elder” … and adjacent to this … “And if a stranger sojourns with you”
And where will the horns … be exalted? In Jerusalem, as it is stated: “Pray for the peace of Jerusalem; they who love you shall prosper”
And once Jerusalem is rebuilt, … David, will come, as it is stated:

“Afterward the children of Israel shall return, and seek the Lord their God and David their king” … And once … David comes, … prayer will come, as it is stated: “I will bring them to My sacred mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer”

And after prayer comes, the … service will arrive, as it is stated … “Their burnt-offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted on My altar” … And when the … service comes, … come thanksgiving, as it is stated: “Whoever sacrifices a thanks-offering honors Me”

And why did they see … says the Priestly Benediction after … thanksgiving? As it is written: “And Aaron lifted up his hand toward the people and blessed them, and he came down from sacrificing the sin-offering, and the burnt-offering, and the peace-offerings”
say … before the … service? … It should not enter your mind … as it is written: “And he came down from sacrificing the sin-offering.” Is it written … to sacrifice … it is written, “from sacrificing,”
said … after … the … service, … It should not enter your mind … as it is written: “Whoever sacrifices a thanks-offering
What did you see to rely on this … Rely … on the other … It stands to reason … service and thanksgiving, … are one matter.

And why did they see … says … Grant peace, after the Priestly Benediction? As it is written … “And they shall put My name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them” … the blessing of the Holy One, Blessed be He, is peace, as it is stated: “The Lord blesses His people with peace”
Now, since … a hundred and twenty Elders, including many prophets, established the … prayer in its … order, what … Shimon HaPakuli arranged … forgot them, and … arranged them again.

beyond this it is prohibited … to declare the praises of the Holy One, Blessed be He, … Rabbi Elazar said: What is … which is written: “Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord? Who can declare all His praise?” … For whom is it fitting to utter the mighty acts of the Lord? … for one who can declare all His praise.

Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … one who excessively declares the praises of the Holy One, Blessed be He, … is … uprooted from the world, … As it is stated: “Shall it be told to Him when I speak? If a man says … he would be swallowed up”

Rabbi Yehuda, a man of Kefar Gibboraya, and some say … a man of Kefar Gibbor Ĥayil, taught: What is … which is written: “For You silence is praise” … The … remedy of all is silence, … When Rav Dimi came … he said: In the West, … they say … a word is … sela, silence is … two.

If one read … by heart he has not fulfilled … From where do we … Rava said: … derived … remembrance … remembrance. It is written here, … “That these days should be remembered” … and it is written elsewhere: “And the Lord said to Moses: Write this for a memorial in the book, … Just as there, … in a book, … so too here, … in a book.

But from where … that this remembrance … reading … Perhaps … merely looking into … It should not enter your mind … “Remember … might … in his heart. … when it says … “You shall not forget” … it is … referring to forgetting from the heart. How, … do I uphold … “remember”? … with the mouth.

If one read … in … translation he has not fulfilled … What are the circumstances … If we say that … was written in … biblical text, … and he read it in … translation, … this is … by heart, … No, … necessary … was written … in … translation, and he read it … in … translation.

However, for those who speak a foreign language, one may read … in … foreign language. … But didn’t you say … If he read it in any … language he has not fulfilled … Rav and Shmuel, who both say: … the Greek foreign language,
What are the circumstances … If we say that … was written in Ashurit, … and he read it in Greek, this is … by heart, … Rabbi Aḥa said … Rabbi Elazar said: … was written in the Greek foreign language

And Rabbi Aḥa … said … Rabbi Elazar said: From where … that the Holy One, Blessed be He, called Jacob El, … As it is stated: … and he called it El, God of Israel” … as if it enters your mind … Jacob called the altar El, it should have … And Jacob called it … But … He called Jacob El; and who called him El? The God of Israel.
raises an objection … If one read … in Coptic [Giptit], Ivrit, Elamite, Median, or Greek, he has not fulfilled
is comparable only to that … in Coptic to Copts, … Ivrit to Ivrim, in Elamite to Elamites, or in Greek to Greeks, he has fulfilled

if so, … why did Rav and Shmuel establish the … mishna as … to Greek? Let them interpret it … to any foreign language … Rather, the mishna … like the baraita, … and that which was stated … Rav and Shmuel was said … general … Rav and Shmuel both say: The Greek language is acceptable for everyone,

But doesn’t … teach … Greek to Greeks … yes, … for everyone … no, … agree with … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. As we learned … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Even … books … did not permit them to be written … other than Greek,

let them state … The halakha is in accordance with … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel. … Had they said … that the halakha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, I would have said … this applies … to the other books … but … the Megilla, of which it is written: “According to their writing,” I would say … not … teach us
And one who speaks a foreign language who heard … in Ashurit, … has fulfilled … But isn’t … he does not understand what they are saying? … It is just as it is … women and uneducated people;

Ravina strongly objects to … Is that to say … we, … know … ha’aḥashteranim benei haramakhim … But … mitzva of reading … and publicizing the miracle … Here too, … mitzva of reading … and publicizing the … miracle,

If one reads … at intervals … seirugin … he has fulfilled … the Sages did not know what is … seirugin. … they heard the maidservant in Rabbi … house saying to the Sages who were entering the house intermittently … How long are you going to enter seirugin seirugin?
the Sages did not know what is … ḥalogelogot, … they heard the maidservant in Rabbi … house saying to a certain man who was scattering purslane: How long will you go on scattering your ḥalogelogot?

the Sages did not know what is … wisdom…salseleha and it will exalt you” … they heard the maidservant in Rabbi … house talking to a certain man who was twirling his hair, saying to him: How long will you go on twirling … mesalsel … your hair?

The Sages did not know what is … “Cast upon the Lord your yehav” … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: One time I was traveling with a certain Arab … Tayya’a … and I was carrying a load, and he said to me: Take your yehav and throw it on my camel,
the Sages did not know what is … “And I will tatei it with the matatei of destruction” … they heard the maidservant in Rabbi … house saying to her friend: Take a tateita and tati the house,
the Sages taught … If one reads the Megilla at intervals, … he has fulfilled

out of order, … he has not fulfilled … Rabbi Mona said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda: Even … at intervals, if he pauses … enough … to finish … the whole … he must go back to the beginning … Rav Yosef said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Mona, … stated … in the name of Rabbi Yehuda.

Abaye said to Rav Yosef: … enough … to finish … the whole … from … where he is … until the end? Or perhaps … from the beginning until the end. He said to him: … from the beginning until the end, … if … so … you would be subjecting your statement to the … circumstances

Rabbi Abba said … Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said: Rav said … the halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Mona, but Shmuel said … the halakha is not in accordance with … Rabbi Mona. … This is how they taught … in Sura. … in Pumbedita they taught … like this: Rav Kahana said … Rav said … the halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Mona, but Shmuel said … the halakha is not in accordance with … Rabbi Mona. Rav Yosef said: Grasp … Rav Beivai in your hand, … Shmuel takes into consideration … individual … As we learned … a woman … waiting for her brother-in-law and … brothers betrothed … sister, they said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira: We say to … Wait … until your older brother acts,
Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.
The Sages taught … If the scribe … omitted letters or … verses … and the reader read … as a translator … when translating, … he has fulfilled

raises an objection … If … contains letters that are blurred or torn, … If their imprint is … visible, … is fit … but if not, it is unfit. … This … not difficult. This … the whole of … this … in … part of it.

while he is dozing off, he has fulfilled his … What are the circumstances of … dozing off? Rav Ashi said: … asleep yet not … asleep, awake yet not … awake. If someone calls him he answers. And he is … he does not know … to provide … reasoning, but when people remind him … he remembers

Rather, … which a … Megilla is lying before him … and he was reading from … verse by verse and … writing … in … Let us say that … supports … Rabba bar bar Ḥana, as Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It is prohibited to write … a single letter … not … from a written text. … as perhaps … where this is what happened to be

the … itself, Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: It is prohibited to write … a single letter … not … from a written text. … raises an objection … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said: … an incident involving Rabbi Meir, who went to intercalate the year in Asia … And there was no … there … so he wrote … by heart and read … it.

Rabbi Abbahu said: Rabbi Meir is different, as in him is fulfilled … “And let your eyelids look straight before you” … Rami bar Ḥama said to Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti: What is … “and let your eyelids … afapekha],” … “look straight … yaishiru … before you”? And the halakha is … Phylacteries do not require scoring, … mezuzot require scoring. … both these and those, … written … not … from a written text. What is the reason … These … are well known
was written with sam … Sam … samma. … sikra, Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: Its name … sikreta, … Komos … koma,
Kankantom … ḥarta de’ushkafei, … Diftera … that was processed with salt and flour, but not with gallnuts. Neyar … maḥaka,
unless … is written in Ashurit. … As it is written … “According to their writing and according to their time”

“upon parchment and with ink.” … From where do we … derived … writing … writing. It is written here … “Then Esther the queen, … wrote … and it is written there: “Then Baruch answered them: He pronounced all these words to me with his mouth, and I wrote them with ink on the parchment”

MISHNA: … a resident of an … town who went to a walled city, … a resident of a walled city who went to an … town … If he is destined to return to his … place, he reads … according to … his … place, and if not, … he reads with them,
from where must a person read the Megilla in order to fulfill his obligation? Rabbi Meir says: … all of it. Rabbi Yehuda says: … from … a certain Jew” … Rabbi Yosei says: From “After these things”

GEMARA: Rava said: They taught … only … one who is destined to return … on the night of the fourteenth … But if he is not destined to return on the night of the fourteenth, although … he reads with … Rava said: From where do I say this? We have found … an unwalled town. … from where do we … a walled city … It is … logical reasoning: Since one who is in an unwalled town for the day is called someone from an unwalled town, … one who is in a walled city for a day is called someone from a walled city.

And Rava said … Someone from a village, where … who went to a town, reads … with … in all circumstances, … What is the reason … This … should … read … as the residents of the towns, but the Sages showed leniency toward the … villages … so that they … supply water and food to their brethren in the cities … This, … applies … when … is in his place, … but when he is in a town, he is required to read like the residents of the town,

Abaye raised an objection to … A resident of a walled city who went to … town, in all circumstances, … reads … according to … his … place. … Can it enter your mind that the resident of a walled city … the matter depend on whether … he will be returning … Rather, is it not … A resident of a village
But did you not emend … teach: He reads … with
from where must a person read the Megilla … It is taught … Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai says: … “On that night”

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: And all of … were expounding the same verse. … “Then Esther the queen, … and Mordecai the Jew, wrote about all the acts of power … The one who said … in its entirety … the power of Ahasuerus,

And the one who said … from “There was a certain Jew” … the power of Mordecai. And the one who said … from “After these things” … the power of Haman. And the one who said … from “On that night” … the power of the miracle,
Rav Huna said: … from here: … and of that which they saw concerning this matter, and that which had befallen them,

And the one who said … from “After these things” … That which Haman “saw” in that he became incensed with all the Jews. “Concerning this matter” … because “Mordecai did not bow down, nor prostrate himself before him” … “And that which had befallen them” … “he and his sons were hanged on the gallows”

Rabbi Ḥelbo said … Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said … Rav said: The halakha is in accordance with the statement of the one who says … in its entirety. And … even according to the one who said … “There was a certain Jew” … must … be written in its entirety.

Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said: If one reads from a Megilla that was written together with … the Writings he has not fulfilled … Rava said: We said … only … is not a little shorter or longer … But if it is a little shorter or longer … we have no … with it,
