He came before Rav Ashi … said to him: What is … to going to them now, … said to him: Since it is now that you will find them, … on other days you will not find them, … this is … like merchandise that will be lost, and it is … permitted.
So too, it is taught … with regard to idol worship like this case: One may go

to a fair of … gentiles … and buy animals, slaves, maidservants, houses, fields, and vineyards … And he may write … and confirm … in their courts [arkaot] … because it is as if he were rescuing … from their hands,

Rav permitted Ḥiyya bar Ashi to weave … traps [oharei] on the intermediate days of a Festival. … What is the reason … it is the work of a layman. However, … nets [izlei] are prohibited. What is the reason? It is the work of a craftsman,

Rav Yehuda permitted Ami the oven maker to construct ovens … and Rabba bar Ashabi to craft sieves. … Is that … so? Didn’t Rabba bar Shmuel teach … And they … agree that one may not construct a new oven … not difficult: Here, … to the summer, … there, … the rainy season,

MISHNA: One may construct a railing for a roof or a balcony … the work of a layman, but not … the work of a craftsman. One may plaster the cracks … and roll over them with a roller, … with a hand or a foot, but not with a presser,
the hinge … and the cylinder … and the … beam … and a lock and a key that broke, one may fix them on … a Festival … provided that he does not intend … to do his labor on the Festival
And … all preserved food from which one can eat on the Festival, … he … preserve them

GEMARA: … What are the circumstances … the work of a layman? Rav Yosef said: … with palm branches and … bay trees, … It was taught in a baraita … he fills in … with stone but he does not plaster … with clay.

One may plaster the cracks … and roll over them with a roller, … Now … you said … it is permitted … with a roller, is … necessary … with a hand or a foot? … this is what … is saying: One may plaster the cracks … and roll over them as if with a roller, … with a hand or a foot, but not with a presser,

the hinge … and the cylinder … and the … beam … and a lock and a key that broke, one may fix them on … a Festival. … raises a contradiction … Until the days … hammers would beat in Jerusalem … until his days, yes, … but from then on, no,
This … not difficult: There, … smiths, … here, … of carpenters,

Rav Ḥisda strongly objects to this: … will say … a loud noise is prohibited, … a soft noise is permitted. Rather, Rav Ḥisda said … not difficult … This … sickles, … that … chisels. Rav Pappa said: Here … before the decree … there … after the decree.

Rav Ashi said: That … Rabbi Yehuda; … this … Rabbi Yosei. As Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said: Who is the tanna … taught … on … a Festival … with a change, … with … a matter that will be lost … not in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei,
Ravina said: In accordance with whose … do we now lift the lintel above the door … on the intermediate days of a Festival … In accordance with whose … in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei,
preserved food from which he can eat on the Festival, he … preserve them … Bedita … overflowed, … fish … Everyone went and trapped and brought … fish, … Rava permitted them to salt … of

Abaye said to him: Didn’t we learn … all preserved food from which he can eat on the Festival, he … preserve them … said to him: Since they initially brought … with the intention of eating … and if one would leave them … they would be ruined, they are … like merchandise that will be lost, and … is permitted.
And some say … Rava permitted them to trap … to bring them … and to salt … Abaye said to him: Didn’t we learn … all preserved food from which he can eat on the Festival, he … preserve them

said to him: These … can also be eaten … by pressing … as in that … of Shmuel, … they prepared … for him by pressing … sixty times and he ate … Rava happened … to the house of the Exilarch … they prepared … for him by pressing … sixty times, and he ate
Rav … happened … to the house of Rav Shapir, … they brought before him a certain fish, … one- third … cooked, one-third … salted … one-third … broiled.

Rav said: Adda the fisherman told me … a fish … close to spoiling is … best. And Rav … said: Adda the fisherman told me: … a fish, broil it with its brother, … place it in its father, … eat it with its son, … and drink after it its father,

And … Rav said: Adda the fisherman told me: … fish, cress, and milk, let the body carry them and let not the bed carry them, … And Rav said: Adda the fisherman told me: … fish, cress, and milk, … water and not beer, … beer and not wine,

MISHNA: … one who had … turned over his olives … and mourning … befell him … or … unavoidable accident … or … workers misled him, … he may … load the beam … initial … leave it … until after the Festival; … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says: He may press … and complete … and … plug … in its … manner.

GEMARA: … opens … with … mourning and ends … with … the Festival, … Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said: That is to say: Actions that are permitted on … a Festival are prohibited during the days of one’s mourning.

Rav Ashi said … is speaking … It is not necessary, … It is not necessary … during the days of his mourning, when … is rabbinic, it is permitted … but even on the … Festival, when the prohibition against … labor is by Torah law, … in a case of a loss the Sages permitted

It is taught … in accordance with … of Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi: These are actions that … perform for the mourner during the days of his mourning: … his olives have … been turned over, they may load … for him … and … his cask … to be plugged, or … his flax … to be lifted out of the soaking pool … or … his wool … to be lifted from the cauldron … They … irrigate his field when his turn for water arrives,

Rabbi Yehuda says: They also sow for him a plowed field or a field set aside for flax, … said to him: If … is not sown in the early … it can be sown in the later … if it is not sown with flax, it can be sown with another species.

Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: … his olives have … been turned over and there is no skilled worker … but him, … his cask … to be plugged and there is no skilled worker … but him, … his flax … to be lifted out of the soaking pool, or his wool … to be lifted from the cauldron, and there is no skilled worker … but him, he may perform … in private.

Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said further: If … was a craftsman … the public, … or a barber or a bath attendant for the public, and the time of the Festival arrived, … and there is no … skilled worker … but him, … he may perform

Tenant farmers, … and leasers, … and contractors, … those for whom others may perform … donkey drivers, camel drivers, and sailors … those … may not perform … However, if they … were leased or hired out to others, then they may perform … A day laborer, even … in a different city … may not perform … a commission for others was his responsibility, even if it was by contract … he may not perform

even if it was by contract … it is not necessary … not by contract … On the contrary, … by contract it is considered as … his … Rather, … say … whether by contract or not by contract, he may not perform
he commissioned others … his work, … in his house they may not perform … in another house they may perform

Maryon, son of Ravin, and Mar, son of Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, held a team of … oxen … between them, … An event, … befell Mar, son of Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, and he detached his … from the team, … Rav Ashi said: A distinguished man like Mar, son of Rav Aḥa, is behaving this … Granted, he is not concerned about his own loss, … is he not concerned about the loss of others, … Isn’t it taught … If they … were hired out or leased to others, then they may perform
But … maintains: An important person is different.
Shmuel said: … contractors, … it is prohibited … within … the … limit … Outside the … limit, … it is permitted.
Rav Pappa said: And even outside the … limit, we said only … when there is no … city in close proximity to there, but if there is … city in close proximity to there, it is prohibited,

Rav Mesharshiyya said: And even when there is no … city in close proximity, we said … only on Shabbatot and Festivals, when … people do not routinely go there, … However, on the intermediate days of a Festival, when … people routinely come and go from there … it is prohibited.

Mar Zutra, son of Rav Naḥman, … contractors built a mansion [apadana] for him outside the … limit. Rav Safra and Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana happened … but they did not enter it, … And there are … who say: Even he, … did not enter it.

But didn’t Shmuel say: … contractors, within … the … limit, it is prohibited … outside the … limit it is permitted? … An important person is different … And there are … who say: He provided them with assistance with straw

Rav Ḥama permitted the bath attendants [abunagrei] of the Exilarch’s house to work for them, … on the intermediate days of a Festival. He said … Since they do not take payment … are … conferring a favor … and we have no … with it.

The Sages taught … may receive contract work on … Festival … to execute it after the Festival, but it is prohibited … during the Festival … The principle of the matter … Any … that … may perform … he may tell a gentile to perform, and any … that he may not perform … he may not tell a gentile to perform. It is taught … another … may receive contract work on … a Festival … to execute it after the Festival, provided that he does not measure, weigh, or count, … in the … manner as he does on an … weekday.
The Sages taught … One may not breed an animal, … on the intermediate days of a Festival, … Similarly, one may not breed a firstborn … nor an unfit consecrated animal.

It is taught … another … One may not breed an animal on the intermediate days of a Festival. Rabbi Yehuda says: … a she-donkey yearns … one may breed her with a male, lest she cool off, … all other animals … they are … brought into corrals
The Sages taught … One may not enclose … on Shabbatot, or on Festivals, or on the intermediate days of a Festival. But if … came on their own … it is permitted,

And one may not assist … nor may one provide them with a shepherd to … herd their sheep … were hired by the week, by the month, by the year, … by the septennial … one may assist them and provide them with a shepherd to herd their sheep. … Rabbi … says: On Shabbat … as a favor, … on a Festival, … for food; … on the … the Festival, … for pay. Rav Yosef said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi

MISHNA: And similarly, … one whose wine was … in the … pit … and mourning … or … unavoidable accident befell him, or … misled him, … he may draw off … and complete … and … plug … in its … manner; … the statement of Rabbi Yosei. Rabbi Yehuda says: He should construct a wooden panel … so that … will not sour.

GEMARA: … And … necessary, as, if … teaches us … the first … in that … does Rabbi Yosei say … because … oil, the … loss is considerable. However, … wine, where the loss is not … considerable, … that he concedes to Rabbi Yehuda … And if he teaches us … the last … in that … did Rabbi Yehuda say … but in the other … say that he concedes to Rabbi Yosei … necessary

Rav Yitzḥak bar Abba said: Who is the tanna … during the intermediate days of the Festival … an altered fashion … with regard to a matter that, … loss? … not … Rabbi Yosei’s … Rav Yosef said: … halakha … in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei,

asked of Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak: What is … to sealing a barrel of beer during the intermediate days of the Festival? … He said to them: Sinai, … said: … halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei. … Say that Rabbi Yosei said … about wine, … about beer does he say
wine, what is the reason … because the loss … is considerable; … beer as well, there is a loss … as Abaye said: … mother told me: … of six se’a that is sealed than … of eight … that is not sealed,

Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said … Rav said: The halakhot relating to … a Festival resemble the halakhot relating to the Samaritans in the halakha. … With regard to what … the halakha … Rav Daniel bar Ketina said … Rav said: … to convey that they are sterile, and one may not learn … one from one another

For … Shmuel said: One may seal a jug with pitch, but one may not seal a barrel with pitch … Rav Dimi from Neharde’a said: One may seal a barrel with pitch, but one may not seal … jug with pitch. … This Sage, … was … concerned about … loss, … And this Sage, … was concerned about … exertion
Abaye stated … We have a tradition … the halakhot of … a Festival are like the halakhot of Shabbat:
Some of … exempt … are … prohibited, and some of them … permitted ab initio.

Rav Huna had his crop harvested for him on … a Festival. Rabba bar Rav Huna raised an objection to … Rav Huna … One may grind flour on … a Festival for the sake of the Festival, but … not for the sake of the Festival, … prohibited. … a matter that, … loss on the Festival, it is permitted to perform … on … the Festival. … a matter that … in loss … the Festival, it is prohibited

In what … is this statement said? In … detached from the ground, but … attached to the ground, even if it all will be lost, … is prohibited … And if one does not have anything to eat, … he may reap and bind sheaves, and thresh, and winnow … and separate … and grind … provided that he does not thresh with cows,

said to … is an individual … and we do not hold in accordance with it; as it is taught … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel stated a principle in the name of Rabbi Yosei: … an item that is … detached from the ground, even if … a portion of it will be lost … it is permitted … whereas … that are … attached to the ground, even if all of them will be lost, it is prohibited

But if … Rabbi Yosei, … let him thresh even with cows. … Rav Yitzḥak bar Abba say: Who … taught … on … a Festival … an altered manner … with regard to a matter that … a loss … not in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei,
said to you: Here, too, since one does not always thresh with cows, … now … is also not … an altered manner.

The Sages taught … One may grind … on … a Festival for the sake of the Festival, but … not for the sake of the Festival, … prohibited. And if he ground and left … over, it is permitted … one may cut down trees on … a Festival for the sake of the Festival, but … not for the sake of the Festival … prohibited. And if he cut down … and left … over, it is permitted

One may brew beer on … a Festival for the sake of the Festival, but … not for the sake of the Festival, … prohibited. And if he brewed … and left … over, it is permitted … provided that he does not employ an artifice,

raises a contradiction … One may brew beer on … a Festival for the sake of the Festival, but … not for the sake of the Festival, … prohibited. … both … date beer and … barley beer. And even though he has old … he may employ an artifice and drink from the new … This … is … tanna’im, as it is taught … One may not employ an artifice in this regard, … Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says: One may employ an artifice.

Rav had his crop harvested on the intermediate days of a Festival. Shmuel heard … was dismayed. … Shall we say … Shmuel holds in accordance with the individual … No, it was a crop of wheat, which would not have been ruined
What is the reason … Rav acted in this manner? … one who does not have anything to eat, … And … Shmuel … did not complete … for him. Alternatively, an important person … is different,

Rabbi Yehuda Nesia … went out … with a coral seal [ḥumreta] … and drank water heated by a gentile cook. Rabbi Ami heard … was dismayed … Rav Yosef said: What is the reason … he was dismayed? If … because of the coral seal, isn’t … taught … Bracelets, nose rings, and rings are like all … utensils that may be carried in a courtyard?

if … because … drank water heated by a gentile cook [kapeila], didn’t Shmuel bar Yitzḥak say … Rav said: … anything that is eaten raw, … it is not subject to … food cooked by gentiles? … An important person is different,
Rav Ḥananel said … Rav said: A person may chop down a palm tree on … a Festival, although he needs only its sawdust. … Abaye cursed it,

Rav Ashi had a forest [ava] in Shelaniya. He went to cut it down on the intermediate days of the Festival. Rav Sheila from Shelaniya said to Rav Ashi: What is your opinion … that … Rav Ḥananel said … Rav said: A person may chop down a palm tree on … a Festival even though he needs only its sawdust? Didn’t Abaye curse … said to him: I did not hear … that is to say, … I do not hold … The … ax … slipped … was about to cut off his leg. He left it, … and came back again

Rav Yehuda permitted uprooting flax, cutting hops, and uprooting sesame plants … Abaye said to Rav Yosef: Granted, … flax, … suitable for … a cover [ḥafifa] … hops, … suitable for … beer, but for what are sesame plants suitable, … They are suitable for the seeds [nazyei] on them,

Rabbi Yannai had an orchard whose time … arrived during the intermediate days of the Festival. He harvested it … The following year, everyone delayed … their orchards until the intermediate days of the Festival. Rabbi Yannai declared … his orchard ownerless that year,

MISHNA: A person may bring his fruit in … because … about thieves, and he may draw his flax out of the soaking pool so that it is not ruined … provided that he does not plan … his work on … the Festival. And … all … if one planned … his labor on … the Festival, … must be lost
GEMARA: … taught … provided that he brings them into his house discreetly.
Rav Yosef had … beams, … he brought into … during the day

Abaye said to him: But isn’t it taught … provided that he brings them into his house discreetly? … said to him: Discretion … to these … is … the day, since at night more people are required, and … torchbearers [medokhrei denura] are needed, … the matter … noticeable.
And he may draw his flax out of the soaking pool … Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira: … one planned … his labor on … a Festival, and he died … what is … Should his children be penalized after him
if you might say
one who slit the ear of a firstborn … penalized his son after him, … because the prohibition is by Torah law.
And if you might say … one who sold his slave to a gentile and … died … penalized his son after him, … because every day … is in the gentile’s possession precludes him from
What, … here, … the Sages penalized the man … and he is no longer … or perhaps the Sages imposed a penalty on the money, … and it … exists

said to … You … learned … A field whose thorns were removed during the Sabbatical Year may be sown in the eighth year, … if it had been improved … or if it had been enclosed … it may not be sown in the eighth year. … And Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: We have a tradition … improved … and … died, his son may sow it. Apparently, the Sages penalized … him, … the Sages did not penalize his son. Here, too, … the Sages penalized him, … the Sages did not penalize his son.

Abaye said: We have a tradition … rendered impure another’s ritually pure items and died … did not penalize his son after him … What is the reason … damage that is not evident, … is not considered damage … the Sages penalized … the Sages did not penalize his son.
MISHNA: One may not purchase houses, slaves, and cattle … unless … for the sake of the Festival, or … for the needs of the seller who does not have anything to eat.

GEMARA: Rava asked Rav Naḥman: What is … wages … who does not have anything to eat? … said to him: We learned … Or … for the needs of the seller, if he has nothing to eat. What is added by … add … wages … said to him: No, … is … explaining

Abaye raised an objection … Promissory notes may not be written on … a Festival, but if … does not trust … or if he has nothing to eat, he may write … What is added … If he has nothing to eat? … the wages … Conclude from it

Rav Sheshet raised an objection … And the Rabbis say: … three crafts … perform labor until midday on Passover eve, … the tailors, the barbers, and the launderers, … The tailors … as a layperson … sew in his … manner during the intermediate days of the Festival. … The barbers and the launderers … as those who arrive from overseas … one who leaves prison … cut … hair and wash … on the intermediate days of the Festival
And if it enters your mind … wages … who does not have anything to eat is permitted … all … labor should also be permitted … as there is … the wages … who does not have anything to eat.

Rav Pappa strongly objects to this: If that is so, … building … should be permitted … as a wall that tilts toward the public domain … may be demolished and rebuilt in the usual manner … due to the danger
Ravina … strongly objects to this: If that is so, a scribe [lavlar] … should be permitted … as one may write betrothal deeds, bills of divorce, and receipts

Rather, Rav Ashi said … Are you raising a contradiction … a Festival and … the fourteenth … a Festival because it involves … exertion, and in a situation of … loss the Sages permitted … the fourteenth … is due to the need … for the Festival, … Whatever is needed for the Festival, … the Sages permitted, … whatever is not needed for the Festival, the Sages did not permit.

MISHNA: One may not move … from house to house … but he may move … to his courtyard … One may not bring … utensils from the house of a craftsman … if one is concerned about them … he may move them to another courtyard.
GEMARA: … But didn’t you say in the first clause … one may not move … at all, … Abaye said … In the latter clause we come to … the house in his courtyard

And one may not bring … utensils from the house of a craftsman. Rav Pappa said: Rava tested us … We learned … one may not bring … utensils from the house of a craftsman. And this raises a contradiction to … One may take utensils to and bring them from the house of a craftsman, even if they are not … for the sake of the Festival.

And we answered him: Here, … to the fourteenth … here, … to the intermediate days of a Festival. … if you wish, say … this and that … to the intermediate days of a Festival, … here, … where he trusts … here, … where he does not trust

And … it is taught … One may bring … utensils from the house of a craftsman; for example, a jug from the jug-maker's house and a cup from the glass-blower’s house, … But … not … wool from the dyer’s house or utensils from the craftsman’s house, … But if … has nothing to eat, he may give him his wages … and leave … with him. And if he does not trust … he may … leave it in a house near him. And if he is concerned about … lest they be stolen, he may move them to another courtyard. And if he does not trust … he may bring them into his house discreetly.
You have … explained … one may bring … one may take … difficult, as … teaches: One may not bring … And … all the more so, one may not take … Rather, it is clear as we answered initially

MISHNA: … figs … may be covered with straw … Rabbi Yehuda says: One may even condense … Those who sell produce, clothing, and utensils may sell … in private, for the sake of the Festival. Fishermen, and groats makers [dashoshot], and … pounders, … may ply … in private for the sake of the Festival. Rabbi Yosei says: They were stringent with themselves

GEMARA: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Asi disagree about … and both of them … in the name of Ḥizkiyya and Rabbi Yoḥanan. One said: Cover … lightly … condense … densely. And … one said: Cover … whether lightly or densely, … condense … making it as if … a pile … This is also taught … One may condense, … making it as if … a pile … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.
those who sell produce, clothing, and utensils may sell … in private, … asked: … they were stringent with themselves, … that they did not work at all … or perhaps … that they did … in private,

Come … hear: Those who sell produce, clothing, and utensils may sell … in private, for the sake of the Festival. Rabbi Yosei says: The merchants of Tiberias were stringent with themselves not to sell at all, … Hunters of animals, fowlers, and fishermen may hunt … discreetly for the sake of the Festival. Rabbi Yosei says: The hunters of Akko were stringent with themselves not to hunt at all. Groats makers … ḥilka, targis, and tisanei, crack … in private for the sake of the Festival. Rabbi Yosei says: The groats makers of Tzippori were stringent with themselves not to crack … at all.
Abaye said: … ḥilka … one … into two; … targis … one … into three; … tisanei … one … into four. When Rav Dimi came … he said: … emmer wheat.

raises an objection … Ḥilka, targis, and tisanei are … ritual impurity everywhere. Granted, according to the one who said … one … into two, into three, and into four, due to that … they are … impurity everywhere, as they … become fit … But according to the one who says that … is emmer wheat … why is it susceptible to … impurity everywhere, … it has not … become fit
where, for example, … was husked, since if it had not been … soaked in water, it would not have been possible to husk it. And why, … is it called ḥilka? … because their husks [ḥelkayhu] were removed.

raises an objection … One who vows to … from … grain [dagan] … prohibited to … of even dry Egyptian beans, and … is permitted … of fresh … And … permitted … of rice, … of ḥilka, and targeis, and tisnei. Granted, according to the one who said … one … into two, one … into three, and one … into four, it is fine, as … it leaves the category of grain. But according to the one who says … emmer wheat, it is … a proper grain. … difficult.

Rav Huna permitted the spice merchants [kerufayata] to go … sell … in their usual manner in the marketplace … Rav Kahana raised an objection to … a store opens into a row of pillars … may open and close it in his usual manner

open to the public domain, he may open … one … and … close the other. And on the eve of the last day of the festival … he may take out … and adorn the markets of the city with fruit in honor of the last day of the Festival. … For the honor of the last day of the Festival, yes, … not for the honor of the Festival, … not
not difficult: This … to … fruit, … this … to … spices,

MISHNA: And these may shave … on … a Festival: One who comes from a country overseas; and … from a house of captivity; and one who comes out of prison … and one who had been ostracized … and the Sages released him … and similarly, one who … requested of a Sage … and was released … and the nazirite … and the leper … his … impurity … his … purity.
And these may launder … on … a Festival: One who comes from a country overseas; and one who … from a house of captivity; and one who comes out of prison
and one who had been ostracized and the Sages released … and similarly, one who … requested from a Sage … and was released

Hand towels; and barbers’ towels, … and body-drying towels, … Zavim, … zavot, … menstruating women; women who have … given birth; and all others who leave … ritual impurity for … ritual purity … these … are … permitted … But all other people are prohibited
GEMARA: … What is the reason … all other people are prohibited

As we learned … the members of the priestly watch … and the members of the non-priestly watch … are prohibited from cutting … hair or laundering … But on the Thursday … they are permitted … in deference to Shabbat.

And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: What is the reason … in order that they not enter their watch when they are untidy. … Here, too, … in order that they … not enter the Festival when they are untidy.
Rabbi Zeira asks: If one lost an item on the eve of a Festival … since … a victim of circumstances beyond his control, … he is permitted … Or perhaps since it is not … evident … not
Abaye said, … would say: All the … Syrian cakes are forbidden, … the Syrian cakes of Baitos are permitted?

And according to your reasoning, that which Rabbi Asi said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Anyone who has only one shirt is permitted to launder it on the intermediate days of a Festival, there too, … will say: All the … Syrian cakes are forbidden … the Syrian cakes of Baitos are permitted.
Wasn’t it … said about this … Mar, son of Rav Ashi, said: His belt is proof for him,

Rav Ashi taught … Rabbi Zeira asks: … a craftsman who lost an item on the eve of a Festival … what is … since he is a craftsman, it is … evident … Or perhaps since … are not … evident as in those … not … shall stand

from a country overseas … The mishna is not in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: One who comes from a country overseas … must not shave … due to … he left … without permission.

Rava said: … to travel, all agree … it is prohibited … for … sustenance, … all agree … it is permitted … They disagree only … to … profit, … One Sage, … compares him … to travel, and the other Sage, … compare him … for … sustenance.

raises an objection … Rabbi … said: … statement of Rabbi Yehuda seems … when he left without permission, and the statement of the Rabbis … when one left with permission. … What is … without permission? If we say … to travel, didn’t you say … all agree … it is prohibited … Rather, … for … sustenance. … didn’t you say … all agree … it is permitted … Rather, … obvious … profit.

Say the latter clause … The statement of the Rabbis seems … when one left with permission. … What is … with permission? If we say … for … sustenance, didn’t you say … all agree … it is permitted … Rather, … for … profit. … didn’t you say … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda seems … in this

This is what … is saying: The statement of Rabbi Yehuda seems … to the Rabbis … where one left without permission. And what is … to travel, as even the Rabbis disagree with … only … for … profit, but … to travel they agree with … And the statement of the Rabbis seems … to Rabbi Yehuda … where one left with permission. Rabbi Levi said: A mourner … the first three days … should see himself as though a sword were lying between his two thighs, … From the third to the seventh … as if … were lying opposite him in the corner, … From this … forward it is as if … was moving before him in the marketplace,
And … of women … never … due to … honor. … Neharde’a say: They only taught
a woman … in childbirth, … But … other women may be set down
Rabbi Elazar said: Even … other women … as it is written: “And Miriam died there and was buried there” … the … burial was close to … death.

Rabbi Elazar said … Miriam also died by … kiss, … This is derived … “there” … “there” … with regard to Moses. … For what … was it not … stated with regard to her, … “by the mouth of the Lord”? … because it would be unseemly to say such a thing,

Rabbi Ami said: Why was … death of Miriam juxtaposed to the portion … the red heifer? To tell you: Just as the red heifer atones … so too, the death of the righteous atones … Rabbi Elazar said: Why was … death of Aaron juxtaposed to … the priestly garments? … just as the priestly garments atone … so too, the death of the righteous atones

The Sages taught … dies suddenly … this is death … snatching. … became sick for a day and died, this is an expedited death. Rabbi Ḥananya ben Gamliel says: This is death at a stroke, as it is stated: “Son of man, behold, I am about to take away from you the delight of your eyes at a stroke” … And … it is written: “So I spoke to the people in the morning and at evening my wife died”
two days and died, this is a quickened death. … three … rebuke. … four … reprimand. … five … this is the … death of all people.

Rabbi Ḥanin said: What is the verse … “Behold, your days approach that you must die” … “Behold [hen]” … one; “approach [karvu],” … two; “your days [yamekha],” … two; … this is five. … hen … one? Because in the Greek language they call … one hen.
dies when … fifty years … this is death through karet, … fifty-two years … this is the death of Samuel from Ramah. … sixty, this is death at the hand of Heaven.
Mar Zutra said: What is the verse … As it is written: “You shall come to your grave in a ripe age [bekhelaḥ]” … “ripe age” [bekhelaḥ] has the numerical value of sixty,

seventy … old age. … eighty … strength, as it is written: “The days of our years are seventy, or if by reason of strength, eighty years” … Rabba said: … from fifty to sixty years … is death by karet. And … all of these years were not counted … due to the honor of Samuel from Ramah,

when Rav Yosef turned sixty he made a holiday for the Sages. … he said: I have passed … karet. Abaye said to him: Master, … though you have passed the karet of years, have you, Master, escaped the karet of days? … He said to him: Grasp at least half in your hand,

Rav Huna died suddenly, … the Sages were concerned … Zuga from Hadayeiv taught them … They taught … only when … had not reached … strength, … But if he had reached … strength … this is death by way of a … kiss.

Rava said: … life, children, and sustenance do not depend on … merit, but rather they depend upon fate. As, Rabba and Rav Ḥisda were both pious Sages; … Sage … pray … and rain would fall, and … Sage … pray and rain would fall.
Rav Ḥisda lived for ninety-two years, … Rabba lived for … forty … The house of Rav Ḥisda … sixty wedding feasts, … house of Rabba … sixty calamities.
In the house of Rav Ḥisda … the finest flour [semida] … for the dogs, and it was not asked after, … In the house of Rabba, … barley bread … for people, and it was not found

Rava said: These three things I requested from Heaven, two … were given to me, … one was not given to me: … wisdom of Rav Huna and the wealth of Rav Ḥisda and they were given to me. … humility of Rabba bar Rav Huna, … it was not given to me.

Rav Seorim, Rava’s brother, sat before Rava, … he saw that … was dozing, … said to … Master, tell him, … not to torment me. … said to … Master, are you not a friend of … said to him: Since … fate has been handed over … no longer pays heed to me. … said to … Master, appear to me … appeared to him. … said to … Master, did you have pain … He said to him: Like the prick … when letting blood.

Rava sat before Rav Naḥman, … he saw that … was dozing, … said to … Master, tell … not to torment me. … said to him: Master, are you not an important person … said to him: … who is important? Who is honorable? Who is complete?

said to … Master, appear to me … he appeared to him. … said to him: Master, did you have pain … said to him: Like the removal of hair from milk, … were the Holy One, Blessed be He, to say to me: Go … to that world, … as you were, I would not want to go, for the fear of … is great.
Rabbi Elazar was … eating teruma, … appeared to him. He said to … I am eating teruma; is it not called sacred? … The moment passed,
appeared to Rav Sheshet in the marketplace. … said to … in the market like an animal? Come to … house

appeared to Rav Ashi in the marketplace. … said to … Give me thirty days so that I may review my studies, for you say … Fortunate is he who comes here … with his learning in his hand. On the thirtieth day … came … said to … What is all of this? … The foot of … bar Natan is pushing … and one sovereignty does not overlap with its counterpart, even … one hairbreadth.
was unable … Rav Ḥisda because his mouth was never silent from study. … went … sat on the cedar … the study hall of the Sages. The cedar cracked and … was silent … able to … him.

could not come near Rabbi Ḥiyya, … One day … appeared to him as a poor person. He came and knocked on the door. He said to … Bring out bread for me, … he took out … for him. … said … Master, do you not have mercy on a poor person? Why, then, do you not have mercy upon that man, … revealed … to him, … showed him a fiery rod … surrendered … to him.
MISHNA: On … a Festival women may wail … but they may not clap [metapeḥot] … Rabbi Yishmael says: Those who are close to the bier may clap.
On New Moons, Hanukkah and Purim, … may … wail and clap … On both … and on … they may not lament. … the deceased has been buried they may neither wail nor clap.

What is … wailing? … when they all wail together … a lament? … when one speaks and they all answer after her … as it is stated: “And teach your daughters wailing and everyone her neighbor lamentation”
But with regard to the future, … states: “He will destroy death forever; and the Lord, God, will wipe away tears from off all faces
GEMARA: What do … say? Rav said: … Woe over him who is … departing; woe over … the pledge,

Rava said: The women … Shekhantziv, … would say as follows: Woe over him who is … departing; woe over … the pledge. And Rava said: The women of Shekhantziv would say … The bone has been removed from the jaw and the water returns to the kettle.

And Rava said: The women of Shekhantziv would say … Wrap and cover the mountains … as … the son of the high and distinguished. Rava said: The women of Shekhantziv would say: Lend … a cloak of fine wool … for a free man whose sustenance has been depleted.

And Rava said: The women of Shekhantziv would say: … runs and tumbles at the ford and … he borrows. And Rava said: The women of Shekhantziv would say: Our brothers, the merchants, will be examined at their places … And Rava said: The women of Shekhantziv would say: Death is like death, … and suffering is like interest.

It is taught … Rabbi Meir would say … “It is better to go to the house of mourning … and the living will lay it to his heart” … Matters relating to death. … that eulogizes will be eulogized … that buries … will be buried … that loads … will be … treated … that raises … will … raise … over him.
And some say: … who does not raise himself … will be raised … as it is written: … For it is better to be told, step up here,

The Sages taught … When the sons of Rabbi Yishmael died, four Elders entered to console him: Rabbi Tarfon, Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, and Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Tarfon said to them: Know that … is a great Sage and well versed in aggadot. Let none of you interrupt the words of another, … Rabbi Akiva said: And I … last.
Rabbi Yishmael, … opened and said … Many are his sins. … his bereavements came in … succession … he troubled his teachers once and … a second time

Rabbi Tarfon answered and said: … “But let your brethren, the whole house of Israel, bewail the burning that the Lord has kindled” … Are … matters not … a fortiori: If, with regard to Nadav and Avihu, who had performed only one mitzva … as it is written: “And the sons of Aaron brought the blood to him” … this … the sons of Rabbi Yishmael, … all the more so

Rabbi Yosei HaGelili answered and said: … “And all Israel shall mourn for him, and bury him” … Are … matters not … a fortiori: If, with regard to Abijah, son of Jeroboam, who did only one good thing, as it is written: “Because in him there is found some good thing … this … the sons of Rabbi Yishmael all the more so

What … one … thing … Rabbi Zeira and Rabbi Ḥinnana bar Pappa … One said: He abandoned his guard post. … And he … went up … for the pilgrimage Festival. And one said: He removed the guards [pardesaot] that his father, Jeroboam, had placed along the roads so that … Israel would not go up … for the pilgrimage Festivals.

Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya answered and said: … “But you shall die in peace; and with the burnings of your fathers, the former kings that were before you, so shall they make a burning for you” … Are … matters not … a fortiori: If, with regard to Zedekiah, king of Judea, who had performed … one mitzva … for he had Jeremiah lifted out of the mire … this … the sons of Rabbi Yishmael all the more so

Rabbi Akiva answered and said: … “On that day shall there be a great mourning in Jerusalem, like the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon” … Rav Yosef said: Had it not been for the … translation of this verse, we would not have known what it is saying,

At that time the mourning in Jerusalem will be as great as the mourning over Ahab, son of Omri, who was slain by Hadadrimmon, son of Tabrimmon, and like the mourning over Josiah, son of Amon, who was slain by Pharaoh the lame in the valley of Megiddon.

Are … matters not … a fortiori: If, with regard to Ahab, king of Israel, who did … one good thing … as it is written: “And the king was propped up in his chariot facing Aram” … this, … all the more so … the sons of Rabbi Yishmael

Rava said to Rabba bar Mari: It is written with regard to Zedekiah: “You shall die in peace,” but … it is written: “And he put out Zedekiah’s eyes” … said to him: Rabbi Yoḥanan said as follows: … that Nebuchadnezzar died in … lifetime

And Rava … said to Rabba bar Mari: It is written with regard to Josiah: “Behold, therefore I will gather you unto your fathers, and you shall be gathered into your grave in peace” … and … it is written: “And the archers shot at King Josiah; … And … Rabbi Yehuda said … Rav said: … they made … like a sieve.
said to him: Rabbi Yoḥanan said as follows: … that the Temple was not destroyed in his lifetime,
Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The consolers are not permitted to speak words … until the mourner opens … As it is stated: … After this Job opened his mouth” … And afterward: “And Eliphaz the Temanite answered

Rabbi Abbahu said: From where … the mourner reclines at the head [rosh] … As it is stated: “I chose out their way, and sat as chief [rosh], and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforts [yenaḥem] the mourners”
yenaḥem means that he comforts others, … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: … is written … yinaḥem,
Mar Zutra said: … from here: … “And the revelry [mirzaḥ] of those who stretched themselves out shall pass away [sar]” … mirzaḥ, … [ … ] … is made a prince [sar] over those who … stretched out

Rabbi Ḥama bar Ḥanina said: From where … that a groom reclines at the head … As it is stated: “As a bridegroom decks himself [yekhahen] with a garland” … Just as a priest [kohen] … at the head … so too, a bridegroom … at the head

From where do we … the priest himself … As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: … “You shall sanctify him, … with regard to all matters of sanctity: To be first to begin … to be first to recite the Grace … and to be first to take a portion
Rabbi Ḥanina said: The soul’s departure from the body is as difficult
as … for a knotted rope [tzippori] to pass through an eye [veshet] … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … as … for a halyard [pitirei] to pass through an eye [veshet].

And Rabbi Levi bar Ḥayyata said: One who departs from the deceased should not say to him: Go to peace, but rather … Go in peace. One who departs from the living should not say to him: Go in peace, but rather … Go to peace.
One who departs from the deceased should not say to him: Go to peace, but rather: Go in peace, as it is stated: “And you shall go to your fathers in peace;

One who departs from the living should not say to him: Go in peace, but rather: Go to peace, as David said to Absalom: “Go in peace” … he … went and was hanged; … Jethro said to Moses: “Go to peace” … he went and was successful.

And Rabbi Levi said: Anyone who leaves from the synagogue … to the study hall or … from the study hall to the synagogue, … merits to receive the Divine Presence, as it is stated: “They go from strength to strength, every one of them appears before God in Zion”
Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi said … Rav said: Torah scholars have no rest, even in the World-to-Come, … as it is stated: “They go from strength to strength, every one of them appears before God in Zion.”
Chagigah: MISHNA: All are obligated … in the … appearance, … except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor; and a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite, and women, and slaves who are not emancipated; and the lame, and the blind, and the sick, and the old, and one who is unable to ascend … on his … legs.

Who … a minor … Any … who is unable to ride on his father’s shoulders and ascend from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount; … the statement of Beit Shammai. And Beit Hillel say: Any … who is unable to hold his father’s hand and ascend … from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount, as it is stated: “Three times [regalim]”
Beit Shammai say: The … appearance … two silver … and the Festival peace … silver ma’a … And Beit Hillel say: The … appearance … silver ma’a and the Festival peace … two silver

GEMARA: … to add what … to add one who is half-slave half-freeman. … And according to … Ravina, who said: One who is half-slave half-freeman is exempt from the appearance … All, … to add what? … to add … lame on … first day … and was healed on … second day

This works out well according to the one who said … all … redress one another, … However, according to the one who said … all … redress the first … All, … to add what? … to add … blind in one of his eyes.

And … not in accordance with … this tanna, as it is taught … Yoḥanan ben Dehavai says in the name of Rabbi Yehuda: … blind in one of his eyes is exempt from the … appearance, as it is stated: … will appear [yera’e] … will see [yireh] … in the … manner that one comes to see, so he comes to be seen: Just as … to see … with both one’s eyes, so too … to be seen … with … both his eyes.

And if you wish, say … Actually, … as we said initially, … And … which … a difficulty to … of Ravina, … not difficult: Here … the initial … mishna, … there, … in accordance with the ultimate … mishna. As we learned … One who is half-slave half-freeman serves his master one day … himself one day. … the statement of Beit Hillel.
Beit Shammai said to them:
You have remedied … his master, … but his own … you have not remedied. … He is unable to marry a maidservant, … He … unable … a free woman,

he should be idle … but isn’t it … the world was created only for procreation, as it is stated: “He did not create it to be a waste; He formed it to be inhabited” … Rather, for the betterment of the world we force his master to make him a freeman, and … writes a bill to … half his value … And Beit Hillel … retracted … to rule in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai

Except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor. … is teaching … a deaf-mute is similar to an imbecile and a minor: Just as an imbecile and a minor … who are not of sound mind, so too the deaf-mute [ḥeresh] … who is not of sound mind. And … teaches us as we learned … The ḥeresh, whom the Sages discussed everywhere, … who does not hear and does not speak, … one who speaks but does not hear … one who hears but does not speak are obligated

We … learned this, as the Sages taught … One who speaks but does not hear, this is a deaf … hears but does not speak, this is a mute. … this … and that … are … as those who can see and hear … to all matters.

And from where … that one who speaks but does not hear is a deaf … hears but does not speak is a mute? As it is written: “But I am as a deaf man, I hear not; and I am as a dumb man [illem] who does not open his mouth” … If you wish, say … as people say: His speech has been taken [Ishtakeil Milulei];
one who speaks but does not hear … one who hears but does not speak … obligated … Isn’t it taught … one who speaks but does not hear … one who hears but does not speak … exempt?

Ravina said, and some say … Rava … is incomplete and is teaching the following: All are obligated in … appearance … and rejoicing … except for a deaf … who speaks but does not hear … who hears but does not speak, … is exempt from … appearance. And even though he is exempt from … appearance, he is obligated in … rejoicing. But one who does not hear and does not speak, and an imbecile and a minor, … exempt even from rejoicing, since they are exempt from all the mitzvot mentioned in the Torah,

That … is also taught … All are obligated in … appearance and in rejoicing, except for a deaf … who speaks but does not hear … one who hears but does not speak, as they are exempt from … appearance. And even though they are exempt from … appearance,

obligated in rejoicing. And one who does not hear and does not speak, an imbecile, and a minor are … exempt even from rejoicing, since they are exempt from all the mitzvot mentioned in the Torah. … What is different with regard to … appearance, that … are exempt … And what is different with regard to … rejoicing, that they are obligated?

With regard to … appearance, … derives … appearance … appearance … of assembly, … As it is written, … “Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones” … and it is written … “When all of Israel come to appear”

And there, … from where do we … As it is written … “That they may hear, and that they may learn” … and it is taught … “that they may hear” excludes one who speaks but does not hear; … “and that they may learn” excludes one who hears but does not speak,

Is that to say that one who … not … speak … not … learn? But … two mute people who were in the neighborhood of Rabbi … sons of the daughter of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda, and some say … sons of the sister of Rabbi Yoḥanan … Whenever Rabbi … would enter the study hall they would … enter and sit before … and they would nod their heads … and move their lips.
And Rabbi … prayed for … mercy upon them, and they were healed. And it was discovered that they had learned … halakha, … Sifra, … Sifrei, … and the entire Talmud.

Mar Zutra said … read into … That they may teach [yelamdu], … Rav Ashi said … is certainly … That they may teach. As, if it enters your mind … “That they may learn,” … and … since he is not … speak he … not … learn, … since he is not … hear he is not … learn,
this … derived from: “That they may hear,” … Rather, … is certainly … “That they may teach,”
Rabbi Tanḥum said: One who is deaf in one ear is exempt from … appearance … as it is stated … in their ears”

But this … “In their ears,” is necessary … the ears of the entire Jewish people. … That … is derived from … “Before all Israel” … If … from: “Before all Israel,” I would say … even though they cannot hear; … the Merciful One writes: “In their ears,” and that … they … hear.
That … is derived from: “That they may hear”
Rabbi Tanḥum said: One who is lame in one leg is exempt from … appearance, as it is stated: … times [regalim]

But … “regalim” is necessary … exclude people with artificial legs. … That … derived from: … occasions [pe’amim] … as it is taught … “pe’amim”: Pe’amim means nothing other … legs. And so it says: “The foot shall tread it down, even the feet of the poor and the steps [pa’amei] of the needy” … and it says: “How beautiful are your feet [fe’amayikh] in sandals, daughter of the prince”

Rava taught: What is … which is written: “How beautiful are your feet in sandals, daughter of the prince [nadiv]”? How pleasant are the feet [raglehen] of the Jewish people when they ascend to … on the pilgrimage Festival [regel]. “Daughter of the prince”: … the daughter of Abraham our father who is called a prince, as it is stated: “The princes of the peoples are gathered together, the people of the God of Abraham” … “the God of Abraham,” and not the God of Isaac and Jacob? Rather, … “the God of Abraham,” as … was the first of the converts.

Rav Kahana said … Rabbi Natan bar Manyumi taught in the name of Rabbi Tanḥum: What is … that which is written … and the pit was empty, there was no water in it” … By inference from that which is stated: “And the pit was empty,” don’t I know that there was no water in it? Rather, … there was no water in it, but there were snakes and scorpions in it.

The Sages taught: … an incident involving Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka and Rabbi Elazar ben Ḥisma, when they went to greet Rabbi Yehoshua in Peki’in. … said to them: What novel … was … today in the study hall? They said to him: We are your students and we drink … your water, … He said to them: Even so, there cannot be a study hall without a novelty.

Whose week was it, … It was Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya’s week. … And on what … was the lecture today? They said to him: … about the portion of … assembly. … And what … did he interpret homiletically with regard to

“Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones” … If men come to learn, … women, … come … to hear, why do the little ones come? … in order … give a reward to those who bring them, … said to them: … good pearl … was in your hands, and you tried to conceal it from me?
Additionally, … interpreted … homiletically: “You have affirmed, this day, … the Lord … And the Lord has affirmed you, this day,

The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the Jewish people: You have made Me a single entity in the world, … And … I will make you a single entity in the world, … You have made Me a single entity in the world, as it is written: “Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One” … And … I will make you a single entity in the world, as it is stated:
“And who is like Your people, Israel, one nation in the land?”

And … also commenced … and taught: … “The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails well fastened are those that are composed in collections; they are given by one shepherd” … Why are matters of Torah compared to a goad? To tell you … just as this goad directs the cow to her furrow to bring forth … life to the world, so too the words of Torah direct those who study them from the paths of death to the paths of life. … If so, … Just as this goad is movable … so too matters of Torah are movable … the verse states: “Nails,”

If so, … Just as this nail is diminished … and does not expand, … so too matters of Torah are … diminished and do not expand. … the verse states: “Well fastened [netuim].” Just as this plant [neti’a] flourishes and multiplies, so too matters of Torah flourish and multiply. “Those that are composed in collections [ba’alei asupot]”: These are Torah scholars who sit in many groups [asupot] and engage in Torah … these … render … ritually impure and these render it pure; these prohibit … and these permit … these deem … invalid and these deem it valid.

Lest a person say: Now, how can I study Torah … The verse states … they are all “given from one shepherd.” One God gave them; one leader, … said them from the mouth of the Master of all creation, Blessed be He, as it is written: “And God spoke all these words”

So too you, … make your ears like a funnel and acquire for yourself an understanding heart to hear … the statements of … who render … ritually impure and the statements of … who render … pure; the statements of … who prohibit … and the statements of … who permit … the statements of … who deem … invalid and the statements of … who deem … valid. … he said to them in these words: No generation … orphaned, … if Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya dwells among it.

But … should have told … directly, … due to an incident that occurred. As it is taught … an incident involving Rabbi Yosei ben Durmaskit, who went to greet Rabbi Eliezer in Lod. … said to him: What novel … was … today in the study hall?
said to him: … counted … and concluded … Ammon and Moab … one separates the poor man’s tithe … in the Sabbatical Year.

said to him … Yosei, extend your hands and catch your eyes, … He extended his hands and caught his eyes. Rabbi Elazar wept and said … “The counsel of the Lord is with them who fear Him; and His covenant, to make them know it”

said to … go … say to … Do not be concerned … to your counting, … This is … I received from Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, who heard from his teacher, and his teacher from his teacher: … a halakha … to Moses from Sinai … Ammon and Moab one separates the poor man’s tithe in the Sabbatical Year. What is the reason? Those who ascended from Egypt conquered many cities, and those who ascended from Babylonia did not conquer them
because the first consecration … it … sanctified … for its time and it … not sanctified forever, … And … left those … so that the poor … could rely upon … in the Sabbatical Year,
taught … after … mind was put at ease, he said: May it be … will that Rabbi Yosei’s eyes should return to their place. And … returned.

The Sages taught: Who is … an imbecile? One who goes out alone at night, and one who sleeps in a cemetery, and one who rends his garment. It was stated … Rav Huna said: … until there are all … at the same time. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … even … of one of
What are the circumstances … If he performs them in a deranged manner, … even … of one … If … does not perform these … in a deranged manner, … even … all of them … not

Actually, … who performs these … in a deranged manner, but … one who sleeps in the cemetery, … say that he is doing … in order that an impure spirit should settle upon him. … And … one who goes out alone at night, … say … a fever took hold of him … And … one who tears his garments, … say … he is a man … thought, … since one performed all of these … they are

like … that gored an ox, a donkey, and a camel. … and becomes forewarned for every … Rav Pappa said: If Rav Huna had heard that which is taught … Who is an imbecile? This is one who destroys whatever is given to him, he would have retracted
A dilemma was raised before … When … would have retracted … would he have retracted … from … one who tears his garments, as … is similar … Or perhaps he would have retracted … all of … shall stand
And a tumtum and a hermaphrodite … The Sages taught, … “males,” … to exclude women … “your males,” … to exclude a tumtum and a hermaphrodite … “all your males,” … to include … minors.
The Master said … “Males” … to exclude women. … Why do I … a verse … this … After all, … is a positive, time-bound mitzva, and women are exempt from any positive, time-bound mitzva.
was necessary, … it could enter your mind to say: Let us derive … Appearance, … Appearance, … with … assembly … Just as there, women are obligated … so too here, women are obligated … teaches us

The Master said … “Your males” … to exclude a tumtum and a hermaphrodite. … Granted, … a hermaphrodite was necessary, … it could enter your mind to say … since he possesses an aspect of masculinity, … he should be obligated … teaches us … is a being unto itself,
However, … a tumtum, … is … uncertainty, is a verse necessary to exclude an uncertainty? Abaye said: … when … testicles … are on the outside,

The Master said … “All your males” … to include minors. … Didn’t we learn … except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor? Abaye said: … not difficult. Here, … to a minor who has reached … training … There, … to a minor who has not … reached … training … a minor who has reached … training is … by rabbinic law. … Yes, it is indeed so, and the verse is a mere support

Rather, for what … does … verse: … come? … that which Aḥerim … As it is taught … Aḥerim say … a scrimper, … and a melder of copper, … and a tanner … are … exempt from … appearance, … because it is stated: “All your males,” … one who is able to ascend with all your males … excluding those who are not suited to ascend with all your males,
