And the Rabbis say: … is the very same as the lights created on the first day, but they were not suspended … until the fourth day.

Rav Zutra bar Tuvya said … Rav said: The world was created through ten attributes: Through wisdom, through understanding, through knowledge, through strength, through rebuke, through might, through righteousness, through justice, through kindness, and through mercy.

through wisdom and through understanding, as it is written: “The Lord founded earth with wisdom, and established the heavens with understanding” … through knowledge, as it is written: “With His knowledge the depths were broken up” … through strength and through might, as it is written: “Who by Your strength sets fast the mountains, who is girded about with might” … through rebuke, as it is written: “The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at His rebuke” … through righteousness and justice, as it is written: “Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne” … through kindness and mercy, as it is written: “Remember Your mercies, O Lord, and Your kindnesses, for they are from times of old”

And Rav Yehuda said … Rav said, … When the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the world, it continued to expand like two balls of a warp, … until the Holy One, Blessed be He, rebuked it and made it stand still, as it is stated: “The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at His rebuke” … And this is … Reish Lakish said: What is … which is written: “I am the Almighty God … El Shaddai … I am He Who said to the world “enough [dai],” … Reish Lakish said: When the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the sea, it continued to expand until the Holy One, Blessed be He, rebuked it and made it dry, as it is stated: “He rebukes the sea and makes it dry, and desiccates all the rivers”

the Sages taught: Beit Shammai say: The heavens were created first and afterward the earth was created, as it is stated: “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth” … And Beit Hillel say: … earth was created first, and heaven after it, as it is stated: “On the day that the Lord God made earth and heaven”

Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai: According to your words, … a person build a second floor and build … the house afterward? As it is stated: “It is He Who builds His upper chambers in the heaven, and has founded His vault upon the earth” … Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel: According to your words, … a person make a stool … and make a seat afterward? As it is stated: “So said the Lord: The heavens are My seat, and the earth My footstool” … But the Rabbis say: … this and that were created as one, for it is stated: “Indeed, My hand has laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand has spread out the heavens; when I call to them, they stand up together”

And the others, … what, … is … “together”? … that they do not separate from each other. … the verses contradict each other, … Reish Lakish said: When they were created, He … created … heavens and afterward created the earth, but when He spread them … He spread … the earth and afterward He spread … the heavens.

What is … “heaven” [shamayim]? Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: … shesham mayim, … It was taught in a baraita: … esh umayim, … teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, brought them … and combined them together, and made … firmament from them.

Rabbi Yishmael asked Rabbi Akiva … when they were walking along the way. He said to him: You who served Naḥum of Gam Zu for twenty-two years, who would expound … every … et in the Torah … what would he expound from … “The heaven and the earth” … et hashamayim ve’et ha’aretz … He said to him: … Had it stated: … I would have said: Shamayim is the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, … Since it states “et hashamayim ve’et ha’aretz,” … shamayim … actual heaven … aretz … actual earth.

Why do I … “and the earth” [et ha’aretz]? To … heaven preceded earth … “And the earth was unformed and void” … After all, … began with heaven first; what is different … recount the creation of earth … The Sage of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: … a parable of a flesh-and-blood king who said to his servants: Rise early … to my entrance. He arose and found women and men … Whom does he praise? Those who are unaccustomed to rising early but … rose early,

It is taught … Rabbi Yosei says: Woe to them, the creations, who see and know not what they see; … stand and know not upon what they stand. … Upon what does the earth stand? Upon pillars, as it is stated: “Who shakes the earth out of its place, and its pillars tremble” … pillars … upon water, as it is stated: “To Him Who spread forth the earth over the waters” … waters … upon mountains, as it is stated: “The waters stood above the mountains” … mountains … wind, as it is stated: “For behold He forms the mountains and creates the wind” … wind … upon a storm, as it is stated: “Stormy wind, fulfilling His word” … storm hangs upon the arm of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is stated: “And underneath are the everlasting arms”

stands on twelve pillars, as it is stated: “He set the borders of the nations according to the number of the children of Israel” … And some say: … seven pillars, as it is stated: “She has hewn out her seven pillars” … Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua says: … on one pillar and a righteous person is its name, as it is stated: “But a righteous person is the foundation of the world”
Rabbi Yehuda said: There are two firmaments, as it is stated: “Behold, to the Lord your God belongs the heaven and the heaven of heavens”

Reish Lakish said: … seven … and they are as follows: Vilon, Rakia, Sheḥakim, Zevul, Ma’on, Makhon, … Aravot. … Vilon, … does not contain anything, but enters at morning and departs … evening, and renews the act of Creation daily, as it is stated: “Who stretches out the heavens as a curtain [Vilon], and spreads them out as a tent to dwell in” … Rakia, … in which … sun, moon, stars, and zodiac signs are fixed, as it is stated: “And God set them in the firmament [Rakia] of the heaven” … Sheḥakim, … in which mills stand and grind manna for the righteous, as it is stated: “And He commanded the heights [Sheḥakim] above, and opened the doors of heaven; and He caused manna to rain upon them for food,

Zevul, … is … of … Jerusalem and … Temple, and … altar is built, and … Michael, the great minister, stands and sacrifices an offering upon it, as it is stated: “I have surely built a house of Zevul for You, a place for You to dwell forever” … And from where do we … that … is called heaven? As it is written: “Look down from heaven and see, from Your holy and glorious abode [Zevul]”

Ma’on, … is where … groups of ministering angels who recite song at night and are silent during the day out of respect for Israel, … as it is stated: “By day the Lord will command His kindness, and in the night His song is with me”

Reish Lakish said: Whoever occupies … with Torah at night, the Holy One, Blessed be He, extends a thread of kindness over him by day, as it is stated: “By day, the Lord will command His kindness,” and what is the reason … “by day, the Lord will command His kindness”? Because “and in the night His song,” … “is with me.” And some say … Reish Lakish said: Whoever occupies himself with Torah in this world, which is comparable to night, the Holy One, Blessed be He, extends a thread of kindness over him in the World-to-Come, which is comparable to day, as it is stated: “By day, the Lord will command His kindness, and in the night His song is with me.”

Rabbi Levi said: Anyone who pauses from words of Torah to occupy himself with mundane conversation will be fed with the coals of the broom tree, as it is stated: “They pluck saltwort [maluaḥ] with wormwood [alei siaḥ], and the roots of the broom tree [retamim] are their food” … And from where do we … that … is called heaven? As it is stated: “Look forth from Your holy Ma’on, from heaven”

Makhon, … is where there are storehouses of snow and storehouses of hail, and the upper chamber of harmful dews, and the upper chamber of drops, and the room of tempests and storms, and the cave of mist. And the doors … fire. … For it is stated: “The Lord will open for you His good storehouse,

these … located in heaven? … they … located on the earth. As it is written: “Praise the Lord from the earth, sea monsters and all depths, fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind, fulfilling His word” … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: David requested mercy with regard to them, … and He brought them down to earth. He said before Him: Master of the Universe, “You are not a God that has pleasure in wickedness, evil shall not sojourn with You” … You are righteous, O Lord. … evil should sojourn in Your vicinity. … And from where do we … that … is called “heaven”? As it is written: “And You shall hear … heaven, the Makhon of Your dwelling”

Aravot, … that contains righteousness; justice; righteousness, … the treasuries of life; the treasuries of peace; the treasuries of blessing; the souls of the righteous; the spirits and souls that are to be created; and the dew that the Holy One, Blessed be He, will use to revive the dead. … Righteousness and justice … as it is written: “Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne” … righteousness, as it is written: “And He donned righteousness as armor” … the treasuries of life, as it is written: “For with You is the source of life” … And the treasuries of peace … as it is written: “And he called Him the Lord of peace” … And the treasuries of blessing, as it is written: “He shall receive a blessing from the Lord”

The souls of the righteous … as it is written: “And the soul of my master shall be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord, your God” … Spirits and souls that are to be created … as it is written: “For the spirit that enwraps itself is from Me, and the souls that I have made” … The dew that the Holy One, Blessed be He, will use to revive the dead … as it is written: “A bountiful rain You will pour down, God; when Your inheritance was weary, You confirmed it”

There, … ofanim, … seraphim, … holy divine creatures, and the ministering angels, and the Throne of Glory. The King, God, … living, lofty, exalted One dwells above them in Aravot, as it is stated: “Extol Him Who rides upon the skies [Aravot], Whose name is God” … And from where do we … that … is called “heaven”? … learned … “rides” … “rides”: Here, it is written: “Extol Him Who rides upon the skies [Aravot],” and there, it is written: “Who rides upon the heaven as your help”

And darkness and clouds and fog surround Him, as it is stated: “He made darkness His hiding place, His pavilion round about Him; darkness of waters, thick clouds of the skies” … And is there darkness before Heaven, … But isn’t it written: “He reveals deep and secret things, He knows what is in the darkness, and the light dwells with Him” … not difficult. This

to … inner houses, … that … to … outer houses. And Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: There is one more firmament … above the heads of the divine creatures, as it is written: “And over the heads of the divine creatures there was the likeness of a firmament, like the color of the terrible ice”

Until here, you have permission to speak; from this … forward you do not have permission to speak, as it is written in the book of Ben Sira: Seek not things concealed from you, nor search those hidden from you. Reflect on that which is permitted to you; you have no business with secret matters. It is taught … Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said: What response did the Divine Voice provide to that wicked man, … when he said: “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High” … A Divine Voice came and said to him: Wicked man, son of a wicked man, descendant, … of Nimrod the wicked, who caused the entire world to rebel against Him during … his reign.

How many are the years of man? Seventy years, as it is stated: “The span of our life is seventy years, or if we are strong, eighty years” … Now is … not from the earth to the firmament a walking … of five hundred years, and the thickness of the firmament … a walking … of five hundred years, and a similar … between each and every one of the firmaments?

above them, … are the divine creatures. The feet of the divine creatures correspond … to all … the ankles of the animals correspond to all of them, the shins of the animals correspond to all of them, the knees of the animals correspond to all of them, the thighs of the animals correspond to all of them, the bodies of the animals correspond to all of them, the necks of the animals correspond to all of them, the heads of the animals correspond to all of them, … the horns of the animals correspond to all of them. Above them … Throne of Glory: The feet of the Throne of Glory correspond to all of them, the Throne of Glory corresponds to all of them, … living, almighty, lofty, exalted King dwells above them. And you, … say: “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the Most High” … “Yet you shall be brought down to the netherworld, to the uttermost parts of the pit”

Nor … the … Chariot to an individual. Rabbi Ḥiyya taught: But one may transmit to him, … the outlines … Rabbi Zeira said: One may transmit the outlines … only to the president of the court, … and to anyone whose heart inside him is concerned, … There are … who say … whose heart inside him is concerned.

Rabbi Ami said: The secrets of the Torah may be transmitted only to one who possesses … five characteristics: “The captain of fifty, and the man of favor, and the counselor, and the cunning charmer, and the skillful enchanter” … And Rabbi Ami said … The words of Torah may not be transmitted to a gentile, as it is stated: “He has not dealt so with any nation, and as for His ordinances, they have not known them”

Rabbi Yoḥanan said to Rabbi Elazar: Come and I will teach you the Design of the … Chariot. … said to him: … not … aged … When he grew old, Rabbi Yoḥanan had … passed away. Rabbi Asi said to him: Come and I will teach you the Design of the … Chariot. He said to him: Had I merited, I would have learned … from Rabbi Yoḥanan, your teacher.

Rav Yosef would study the Design of the … Chariot … the Elders of Pumbedita would study the act of Creation. They said to … Let the Master teach us the Design of the … Chariot. He said to them: … teach me the act of Creation. After they taught him … they said to him: Let the Master teach us the Design of the … Chariot. He said to them: We learned with regard to them … “Honey and milk are under your tongue” … matters that are sweeter than honey and milk should remain under your tongue.

Rabbi Abbahu said: … here, … “The lambs … kevasim … will be for your clothing” … Things that constitute the concealed matters of the world should be under your clothing; … they said to him: We have learned them, … up to … “And He said to me, son of man” … He said to them: … these … are … Design of the … Chariot,

raises an objection … Until where is the Design of the … Chariot … Rabbi … says: Until the latter “And I saw” … Rabbi Yitzḥak says: Until … “the electrum” … Until “And I saw,” we teach … from this … forward, … transmit … outlines. There are … who say: Until “And I saw,” we transmit the outlines; from this … forward, if he is wise … can understand of his own accord, yes, … If not, … not
And may one teach about the electrum … But wasn’t there a certain youth … expounded the electrum, and fire came out and consumed him, … youth was different, for his time … had not … arrived.

Rav Yehuda said: Indeed, that man is remembered for good, and Ḥananya ben Ḥizkiya was his name, … were it not for him, the book of Ezekiel would have been suppressed. … that its words contradicted the words of Torah, … What did he do? They brought up to him three hundred barrels of oil, … and he sat in an upper chamber and expounded it,

The Sages taught: An incident … involving a youth who was reading the book of Ezekiel in the house of his teacher, and … was … comprehend the electrum, and fire came out of the electrum and burned him. And they sought to suppress the book of Ezekiel … Ḥananya ben Ḥizkiya said to them: If this … wise, … all … wise
What is … electrum? Rav Yehuda said:

speaking animals of fire. … ḥayyot esh memallelot … It was taught in a baraita: At times they are silent; at times they speak. When the divine speech emerges from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, they are silent; and when the divine speech does not emerge from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, they speak.

“And the divine creatures ran and returned like the appearance of a flash of lightning [bazak]” … What is … “ran and returned”? Rav Yehuda said: Like fire that is emitted from a furnace, … What is … “like the appearance of a flash of lightning”? Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: Like the fire that is emitted … between … earthenware

“And I looked and, behold, a stormy wind came out of the north, a great cloud, with a fire flashing up, so that a brightness was round about it; and out of its midst was like the color of electrum, out of the midst of the fire” … Where did … go? Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: It went to conquer the entire world under the wicked Nebuchadnezzar. And why was all of this necessary? … So that the nations of the world would not say: The Holy One, Blessed be He, delivered His children into the hands of a lowly nation. … The Holy One, Blessed be He, said … Who caused Me to be an attendant to worshippers of molten images, … It was the sins of Israel that led Me

“Now as I beheld the divine creatures, behold, one wheel [ofan] was upon the earth near the divine creatures” … Rabbi Elazar said: … a certain angel who stands on the earth and its head reaches the divine creatures. It was taught in a baraita: … is named Sandalfon, who is taller than his colleague by a distance of five hundred years, and he stands behind the … Chariot and weaves crowns for his Maker. … Is that so? … But isn’t it written: “Blessed be the Lord’s glory from His place” … by inference … no one knows His place? … by saying a name for the crown, and … goes and sits on … head

Rava said: All that Ezekiel saw, … Isaiah saw … To what may Ezekiel be compared? To a villager who saw the king … And to what may Isaiah be compared? To a city dweller who saw the king. … Reish Lakish said: What is … which is written: “I will sing to the Lord, for He is highly exalted” … sing to He Who is exalted above the exalted. As the Master said: The king of the beasts … the lion, the king of the domestic animals … the ox, the king of the birds … the eagle, and man is exalted … over them, but the Holy One, Blessed be He, is exalted above all of them and above the entire world,

One verse states: “As for the likeness of their faces, they had the face of a man; and the four had the face of a lion on the right side; and the four had the face of an ox on the left side” … And it is … written: “And each one had four faces: The first face was the face of the cherub, and the second face was the face of a man, and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle” … but it does not include … an ox … Reish Lakish said: Ezekiel requested mercy … it, … and had it turned into a cherub. He said before Him … Master of the Universe. … an accuser [kateigor] become a defender [saneigor]?

What is … “cherub”? Rabbi Abbahu said: Like a baby … keravya … for in Babylonia they call a baby ravya. Rav Pappa said to Abaye: However, if that is so, what is … that which is written: “The first face was the face of the cherub, and the second face was the face of a man, and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle”? The face of a cherub is … the face of a man; … a large face, … small face

One verse states: “Each one had six wings; … and another verse states: “And every one had four faces, and every one of them had four wings” … not difficult, … here, … to the time when the Temple is standing, … there, … to the time when the Temple is not standing, … it is as if … the wings of the animals were diminished

Which of … were diminished? Rav Ḥananel said … Rav said: Those with which they recite song. … it is written here: “And with two it flew … yeofef … And one called to the other and said” … and it is written: “Will you set … hata’if] your eyes upon it? It is gone”

And the Rabbis say … those with which they cover their feet, for it is stated: “And their feet were straight feet” … Now if … had not been diminished, how would he know … perhaps they were … revealed, … see them. Because if you do not say so, … “And the likeness of their faces, they had the face of a man” … so too … that these … were diminished … Rather, … that they were revealed and he saw them. Here too, they were revealed and he saw them.
How can … be compared? Granted, … his face … it is proper conduct … to reveal … before his Master, … his feet, … not proper conduct to reveal … before his Master.

One verse states: “A thousand thousands ministered to Him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him” … and another verse states: “Is there a number to His troops?” … not difficult, … here, … to the time when the Temple is standing; there, … to the time when the Temple is not standing, … it is as though the heavenly entourage [pamalya] were diminished.

It is taught … Rabbi … says in the name of Abba Yosei ben Dosai: “A thousand thousands ministered to Him” … number … a single troop, … “And to his troops, there is no number”. And Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said: … “a thousand thousands ministered to Him,” … to the River Dinur, as it is stated: “A fiery [dinur] river issued and came forth from before him; a thousand thousands ministered to it, and a myriad myriads stand before it”

From where does … flow? … From the perspiration of the divine creatures. And where does … flow to? Rav Zutra bar Toviya said … Rav said: Upon the heads of the wicked in Gehenna, as it is stated: “Behold, a storm of the Lord has gone forth in fury, a whirling storm; it shall whirl upon the head of the wicked” … And Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: … over those who were snatched away, … as it is stated: “Who were snatched away before their time, whose foundation was poured out as a stream” … It is taught … Rabbi Shimon HeḤasid said … These … those nine hundred and seventy-four generations that were snatched away; … been created
before the creation of the world, but they were not created. … The Holy One, Blessed be He, acted by planting … them in each and every generation, and they are the insolent ones of the generation,

And Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said … “Who were snatched [kumtu]” … is written for a blessing, … These are Torah scholars, who shrivel [mekamtin], … themselves over the words of Torah in this world. The Holy One, Blessed be He, reveals a secret to them in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: “Whose foundation [yesodam] was poured out as a stream”

Shmuel said to Ḥiyya bar Rav: Son of great ones, come and I will tell you something of the great things that your father would say: Each and every day, ministering angels are created from the River Dinur, and they recite song … and … cease … as it is stated: “They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness” … And … disagrees with … of Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani, as Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yonatan said: … each and every word that emerges from the mouth of the Holy One, Blessed be He, an angel is created, as it is stated: “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made, and by the breath of His mouth all their hosts”

One verse states: “His raiment was as white snow, and the hair of his head like pure … wool” … and it is written: “His locks are curled, black as a raven” … not difficult. Here … in the … academy, … there … at war, for the Master said: There is no finer … in an academy than an old man, and there is no finer … than a youth.

One verse states: “His throne was fiery flames” … and … verse states: “Till thrones were placed, and one who was ancient of days sat,” … not difficult. One … for Him and one … for David, as it is taught … One … for Him and one for David; … the statement of Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Yosei HaGelili said to him: Akiva, how long shall you make the Divine Presence profane, … Rather, … One for judgment and one for righteousness.

accept … from him, or did he not accept … from him? … Come … hear … One … for judgment and one … for righteousness; … the statement of Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said to him: Akiva, what are you doing … with … aggada? … Take [kelakh] your words to … plagues and tents. … Rather, … One … for a seat and one … for a small seat. … seat … to sit on, … small seat … for His footstool, as it is stated: “The heavens are My seat, and the earth My footstool”

When Rav Dimi came … he said: Isaiah cursed Israel with eighteen curses, and his mind was not calmed, … until he said to them the … following verse: “The child shall behave insolently against the aged, and the base against the honorable”

What are these eighteen curses? … As it is written: “For behold, the Master, the Lord of hosts, shall take away from Jerusalem and from Judah support and staff, every support of bread, and every support of water; the mighty man, and the man of war; the judge, and the prophet, and the diviner, and the elder; the captain of fifty, and the man of favor, and the counselor, and the cunning charmer, and the skillful enchanter. And I will make children their princes, and babes shall rule over them”

“Support”; these are masters of the Bible. “Staff”; these are masters of Mishna, such as Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima and his colleagues. … Rav Pappa and the Rabbis disagreed with regard to this. One … said: … six hundred orders of Mishna, and … one said: … seven hundred orders of Mishna,

“Every support of bread”; these are masters of Talmud, as it is stated: “Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine that I have mingled” … “And every support of water”; these are the masters of aggada, who draw people’s hearts like water by … aggada. “The mighty man”; this is the master of halakhic tradition, … “And the man of war”; this is one who knows how to engage in the discourse of Torah, … in the war of Torah. “A judge”; this is a judge who judges a true judgment truthfully. “A prophet”; as it literally indicates. “A diviner”; this is a king. … For it is stated: “A divine sentence is on the lips of the king” … “An elder”; this is one fit for … an academy.

“A captain of fifty,” do not read … “sar ḥamishim,” rather … “sar ḥumashin”; this is one who knows how to engage in discourse … the five books of [ḥamisha ḥumshei] the Torah. Alternatively, “a captain of fifty” … in … Rabbi Abbahu, for Rabbi Abbahu said: From here … that one may not appoint a disseminator over the public … less than fifty years … “And the man of favor”; this is … for whose sake favor is shown to his generation. … above, such as Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa, … below, for example: Rabbi Abbahu, … in the house of … emperor.

“The counselor”; … who knows how to intercalate years and determine months, … “The cunning”; this is a student who makes his rabbis wise … “Charmer [ḥarashim]”; … that when he begins speaking matters of Torah, all … are as though deaf [ḥershin], … “The skillful”; this is one who understands something … from something else … “Enchanter [laḥash]”; this … who is worthy of having words of the Torah that were given in whispers [laḥash], … transmitted to him.
“And I will make children their princes” … What is … “And I will make children [ne’arim] their princes”? Rabbi Elazar said: These are people who are devoid [meno’arin] of mitzvot;

“And babes [ta’alulim] shall rule over them”; Rav Pappa bar Ya’akov said: … foxes [ta’alei], sons of foxes. … And … mind was not calmed until he said to them: “The child shall behave insolently against the aged, and the base against the honorable” … these are people who are devoid of mitzvot, … will behave insolently toward one who is as filled with mitzvot as a pomegranate. “And the base [nikleh] against the honorable [nikhbad]”; … one for whom major [kaved] … are like minor ones [kalot] in his mind will come and behave insolently with one for whom … minor … are like major ones in his mind.

Rav Ketina said: Even at the time of Jerusalem’s downfall, trustworthy men did not cease to exist … as it is stated: “For a man shall take hold of his brother of the house of his father, … You have a cloak, be our ruler” … Things that people … covered as with a cloak, … are under your hand,

What is … “And this stumbling block” … Things that people cannot grasp unless they have stumbled over them, … are under your hand. Although … “shall swear that day, saying: I will not be a healer, for in my house there is neither bread nor a cloak; you shall not make me ruler of a people” … “Shall swear [yissa],” yissa is none … than an expression of an oath, as it is stated: “You shall not take [tissa] the name of the Lord your God … “I will not be a healer [ḥovesh]” … I was never … of those who sit [meḥovshei] in the study hall; “for in my house there is neither bread nor a cloak,” as I possess … neither … Bible, nor Mishna, nor Gemara.

But perhaps it is different there, for if he had said: I have learned, they would have said to him: Tell us, … he would have said … he learned and forgot, … What is … “I will not be a healer,” … I will not be a healer at all,

Is that so? But didn’t Rava say: Jerusalem was not destroyed until trustworthy men ceased to exist in it, as it is stated: “Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now and know, and seek in its broad places, if you can find a man, if there is any that acts justly, that seeks truth, and I will pardon her” … not difficult:
This … to words of Torah, … that … to commerce. With regard to words of Torah, they were … with regard to commerce, they were not.

The Sages taught: An incident … involving Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, who was riding on a donkey and was traveling along the way, and … Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh, was riding a donkey behind him. … said to him: My teacher, teach me one chapter in the Design of the … Chariot. He said to him: … I not taught you: And one may not … to an individual, unless he is a Sage who understands on his own accord? … said to him: My teacher, allow me to say before you one thing that you taught me. … He said to him: Speak.

Immediately, Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai alighted from the donkey, and wrapped … and sat on a stone under an olive tree. … said to him: My teacher, for what reason did you alight from the donkey? He said: … possible that … you are expounding the Design of the … Chariot, and the Divine Presence is with us, and the ministering angels are accompanying us, that I should ride on a donkey? Immediately, Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh began … the Design of the … Chariot and expounded, and fire descended from heaven and encircled all the trees in the field, and all … began reciting song.

What song did they recite? “Praise the Lord from the earth, sea monsters and all depths…fruit trees and all cedars…praise the Lord” … An angel responded from the fire, saying: This is the very Design of the … Chariot, … Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai stood and kissed … on his head, and said: Blessed be God, Lord of Israel, who gave our father Abraham a son … who knows … to understand, investigate, and expound the Design of the … Chariot. There are some who expound … well but do not fulfill … well, … who fulfill … well but do not expound … well, … you expound … well and fulfill … well. Happy are you, our father Abraham, that Elazar ben Arakh came from your loins.

And when … matters, … were recounted before Rabbi Yehoshua, he was walking along the way with Rabbi Yosei the Priest. They said: We too shall expound the Design of the … Chariot. Rabbi Yehoshua began expounding. And that was the day of the summer solstice, … heavens became filled with clouds, and there was the appearance of a kind of rainbow in a cloud. And ministering angels gathered and came to listen, like people gathering and coming to see the rejoicing of a bridegroom and bride.

Rabbi Yosei the Priest went and recited … matters before Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, … said … Happy are … you, and happy are … who gave birth to you; happy are my eyes that saw this, … As for you and I, … in my dream … we were seated at Mount Sinai, and a Divine Voice came to us from heaven: Ascend here, ascend here, … large halls … teraklin … and pleasant couches are made up for you. You, your students, and the students of your students are invited to … third group,

Is that so? But isn’t it taught … Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says: There are three lectures. … Rabbi Yehoshua lectured … matters before Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai; Rabbi Akiva lectured before Rabbi Yehoshua; … Ḥananya ben Ḥakhinai lectured before Rabbi Akiva. However, Rabbi Elazar ben Arakh was not included … who lectured and were … lectured to were included; … who lectured and were not lectured to were not included. … But wasn’t … Ḥananya ben Ḥakhinai, who was not lectured to, and … he is included? … actually lectured before one who lectured

The Sages taught: Four entered the orchard [pardes], … and they are as follows: Ben Azzai; and ben Zoma; Aḥer, … and Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Akiva, … said to them: When, … you reach pure marble stones, do not say: Water, water, … because it is stated: “He who speaks falsehood shall not be established before My eyes”

Ben Azzai glimpsed … and died. And with regard to him the verse states: “Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones” … Ben Zoma glimpsed … and was harmed, … And with regard to him the verse states: “Have you found honey? Eat as much as is sufficient for you, lest you become full from it and vomit it” … Aḥer chopped down the shoots … Rabbi Akiva came out safely.

They asked ben Zoma: What is … castrating a dog? … He said to them: … shall you do so in your land” … any … that is in your land, you shall not do … They … asked ben Zoma: … to be a virgin who became pregnant, what is … A High Priest … Are we concerned for … Shmuel? Shmuel says:
I can engage in intercourse several times without blood. … Or, perhaps … Shmuel is not common … He said to them: … Shmuel is not common, and we are concerned that she may have conceived in a bath.
Didn’t Shmuel say: Any semen that is not shot like an arrow cannot fertilize? … initially, … it was shot as an arrow, … also

the Sages taught: There was once an incident with regard to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya, who was standing on a step on the Temple Mount, and ben Zoma saw him and did not stand before him … said to him: From where … and where are you going, ben Zoma, … He said to him: … I was looking upon … between the upper waters and the lower waters, as there is only … a mere three fingers between them, as it is stated: “And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters” … like a dove hovering over its young without touching … Rabbi Yehoshua said to his students … Ben Zoma is still outside;

Now, … “And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,” when was … On the first day, … the division … occurred on the second day, as it is written: “And let it divide the waters from the waters” … And how much, … Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: Like the thickness of a thread; and the Rabbis said: Like … the boards of a bridge. Mar Zutra, and some say … Rav Asi, said: Like two robes spread one over the other, … And some said: Like two cups placed one upon the other.

Aḥer chopped down the saplings, … With regard to him, the verse states: “Do not let your mouth bring your flesh into guilt” … What was … He saw … Mitatron, who was granted permission to sit and write the merits … Israel. He said: … a tradition … above there is no sitting; no competition; no … back before Him, … and no lethargy. … he said: Perhaps, … Heaven forbid, there are two authorities,

They removed Mitatron … and smote him … sixty rods [pulsei] of fire, … They said … What is the reason … when you saw … you did not stand before him? … was granted permission to erase the merits of Aḥer … A Divine Voice went forth saying: “Return, rebellious children” … apart from Aḥer.

said: Since that man, … has been banished from that world, let him go out and enjoy this world. Aḥer went astray. He went … found a prostitute … solicited her … She said to him: And … you not Elisha ben Avuya? … He uprooted a radish from a patch … on Shabbat and gave it to her, … said: He is other

Aḥer asked Rabbi Meir … after he had gone astray. He said to him: What is … which is written: “God has made even the one as well as the other” … said to him: Everything that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created, He created … corresponding to it. He created mountains, He created hills; He created seas, He created rivers.

said to him: Rabbi Akiva, your teacher, did not say so, but … He created the righteous, He created the wicked; He created the Garden of Eden, He created Gehenna. Each and every … has two portions, one in the Garden of Eden and one in Gehenna. … merits … righteous, he takes his portion and the portion of his … colleague in the Garden of Eden; … culpable … wicked, he takes his portion and the portion of his colleague in Gehenna.

Rav Mesharshiyya said: What is the verse … With regard to the righteous, it is stated: “Therefore in their land they shall possess double” … with regard to the wicked, it is stated: “And destroy them with double destruction”

Aḥer asked Rabbi Meir … after he had gone astray. What is … which is written: “Gold and glass cannot equal it; neither shall its exchange be vessels of fine gold” … He said to him: … words of Torah, which are as difficult to acquire as gilded vessels and vessels of fine gold but are as easy to lose as glass vessels. … said to him: Rabbi Akiva, your teacher, did not say so, but … Just as golden vessels and glass vessels have a remedy even when they have broken, … so too a Torah scholar, although he has transgressed, has a remedy. … said to him: … you too, return … He said to him: I have already heard … behind the … curtain, … “Return, rebellious children,” … apart from Aḥer.

The Sages taught: There was once an incident involving Aḥer, who was riding on a horse on Shabbat, and Rabbi Meir was walking behind him to learn Torah from him. … said to him: Meir, turn back, for I have already estimated … according to the steps of my horse … the Shabbat boundary ends here, … said to him: You, too, return … He said to him: But have I not already told you … I have already heard behind the … curtain: “Return, rebellious children,” apart from Aḥer?

took hold of him … brought him to the study hall. … said to a child, … Recite your verse … to me. He recited … to him: “There is no peace, said the Lord, concerning the wicked” … He brought him to another study hall. … said to a child: Recite your verse to me. He recited to him: “For though you wash with niter, and take for you much soap, yet your iniquity is marked before Me” … He brought him to another study hall. … said to

a child: Recite your verse to me. He recited to him: “And you, spoiled one, what are you doing, that you clothe yourself with scarlet, that you deck yourself with ornaments of gold, that you enlarge your eyes with paint? In vain you make yourself fair”

He brought him to another synagogue, until he had brought him into thirteen synagogues, … all … recited to him similar … At the last one, he said to him: Recite your verse to me. He recited to him: “And to the wicked [velerasha] God says, what is it for you to declare My statutes” … That child had a stutter, … it sounded as though he were saying to him: Vele’elisha, … God says. … Some say … had a knife, and he tore … apart and sent him to … thirteen synagogues. And others say … said: Had I a knife, I would have torn him apart.

When … passed away, … declared … he should not be judged, nor brought into the World-to-Come. He should not be judged … because he occupied … with Torah, … And he should not be brought into the World-to-Come because he sinned. Rabbi Meir said: It is better that he be judged … and be brought into the World-to-Come. When I die … and I will cause smoke to rise up from his grave, … When Rabbi Meir passed away, smoke rose up from … grave of Aḥer,

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … a mighty … to burn his teacher? … was one … among us … and we cannot save him? If we hold him by the hand, who will remove him … who? … said: When I die I will have … smoke extinguished from his grave, … when Rabbi Yoḥanan passed away, … smoke ceased … from … grave of Aḥer. A certain eulogizer … Even the guard at the entrance could not stand before you, our rabbi.

The daughter of Aḥer came before Rabbi … said to him: Rabbi, provide me with sustenance, … He said to her: Whose daughter are you? She said to him: I am the daughter of Aḥer. He said to her, … Is there still of his seed … in the world? But isn’t it stated: “He shall have neither son nor grandson among his people or any remaining in his dwellings” … She said to him: Remember his Torah, and do not remember his deeds. Immediately, fire descended and licked Rabbi … bench. Rabbi … wept and said: If … those who treat … with contempt … such … how much more so … for those who treat it with honor.

And Rabbi Meir, how could he learn Torah from … mouth of Aḥer? But didn’t Rabba bar bar Ḥana say … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: What is … which is written: “For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek Torah from his mouth; for he is an angel of the Lord of hosts” … If the rabbi is similar to an angel of the Lord of hosts, … they should seek Torah from his mouth; but if not, they should not seek Torah from his mouth.

Reish Lakish said: Rabbi Meir found a verse and interpreted it homiletically: “Incline your ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply your heart to My knowledge” … It does not state “to their knowledge,” but “to My knowledge.” … the Sages,
Rav Ḥanina said … from here: “Listen, daughter and consider, and incline your ear; forget also your own people and your father’s house”
the verses contradict each other, … not difficult. This … to an adult; … that … to a minor,

When Rav Dimi came … he said: In the West, … say: Rabbi Meir ate a half-ripe date and threw the peel away. … Rava taught: What is … which is written: “I went down into the garden of nuts, to look at the green plants of the valley” … Why are Torah scholars compared to nuts? To tell you: Just as this nut, despite being soiled with mud and excrement, its content is not made repulsive, … so too a Torah scholar, although he has sinned, his Torah is not made repulsive.

Rabba bar Sheila found Elijah … said to … What is the Holy One, Blessed be He, doing? … said to him: He is stating halakhot transmitted by all of the Sages, but in the name of Rabbi Meir He will not speak. He said to him: Why? … Because he learned halakhot from the mouth of Aḥer. He said to him: Why … Rabbi Meir found a pomegranate … ate its contents … throwing away its peel. He said to him: … Now … is saying: My son, Meir, says: When a person suffers, … how does the Divine Presence express itself? Woe is Me from My head, woe is Me from My arm, … If the Holy One, Blessed be He, suffers … such … over the blood of the wicked, how much more so … over the blood of the righteous that is spilled.

Shmuel found Rav Yehuda leaning on the bar of the door, crying. He said to him: Long-toothed one [shinnana], what are you crying … He said to him: Is … a small … that which is written with regard to Sages … “Where is he who counted, where is he who weighed? Where is he who counted the towers?” … “Where is he who counted”; for they would count all the letters of the Torah. “Where is he who weighed”; for they would weigh … minor and major … of the Torah. “Where is he who counted the towers”; for they would teach three hundred halakhot … involving … closet floating in the air.

And Rabbi Ami said: Doeg asked Ahithophel three hundred questions with regard to a closet floating in the air, … And we learned … Three kings and four commoners have no portion in the World-to-Come, … we, … what will be of us? He said to him: Long-toothed one, there was mud [tina] in their hearts,
Aḥer, what … Greek tunes never ceased from his mouth. … they said about Aḥer: When he would stand … in the study hall, many heretical books, … fall from his lap.

Nimos HaGardi, asked Rabbi Meir: … all wool that enters the cauldron … emerge colored? … He said to him: Whoever was clean when … with his mother, … emerge … all … not clean when … with their mother … not emerge

Rabbi Akiva ascended in safety and descended safely. With regard to him, the verse states: “Draw me, we will run after you; … And even Rabbi Akiva, the ministering angels sought to push … The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them: Leave this Elder, for he is fit to serve My glory.
What … expound … Rabba bar bar Ḥana said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … “And He came [ve’ata] from the holy myriads” … He, … is unique [ot] among His myriads
And Rabbi Abbahu said: … “Preeminent above a myriad” … He is exemplary among His myriad.
And Reish Lakish said: … “The Lord of hosts is His name” … He is the Master in His host.

And Rav Ḥiyya bar Abba … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … “But the Lord was not in the wind. And after the wind, an earthquake; the Lord was not in the earthquake. And after the earthquake, fire; … the Lord was not in the fire. And after the fire, a still, small voice,” … “And behold, the Lord passed by”

The Sages taught: Six … were said with regard to demons: … three … like ministering angels, and … three … like humans. … three … like ministering angels: They have wings like ministering angels; and they fly from one end of the world to the other like ministering angels; and they know what will be in the future like ministering angels.
Should it enter your mind that they know … Rather, they hear from behind the curtain … like ministering angels.
And … three … to humans: They eat and drink like humans; they multiply like humans; and they die like humans.

Six … were said with regard to humans: … three … like ministering angels, … three … like animals. … three … like ministering angels: They have intelligence like ministering angels; and they walk upright like ministering angels; and they speak in the holy tongue like ministering angels. … three … like animals: They eat and drink like animals; and they multiply like animals; and they emit excrement like animals.

Whoever looks at four things, it would have been better for him had he never entered the world: … Granted, … what is above, what is below, … what is after. … fine, … But before … what has happened has happened.

Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar both say: … a parable … a flesh-and-blood king who said to his servants: Build for me large palaces on a garbage dump. They went and built … for him. … the king does not desire … mention the garbage dump.

Whoever has no concern for the honor of his Maker deserves to have never come to the world. … What is … Rabbi Abba said: This is … who looks at a rainbow. Rav Yosef said: This is … who commits a transgression in private. … Looking at a rainbow … as it is written: “As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord”

Rav Yosef said: This is … who commits a transgression in private, in accordance with Rabbi Yitzḥak, as Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Whoever commits a transgression in private, it is as though he pushed … the feet of the Divine Presence, as it is stated: “Thus said the Lord: The heavens are My seat, and the earth My footstool”

is that so? But didn’t Rabbi Ela the Elder say: If a person sees that his inclination is overcoming him, he should go to a place where he is unknown, and wear black, and wrap himself in black, … and do … what his heart desires, but let him not desecrate the Name of Heaven in public. … not difficult. This … when one is capable of overcoming his inclination … That … when one is incapable of overcoming his inclination.

Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Naḥmani, the disseminator … Reish Lakish, interpreted … homiletically: Whoever looks at … three things, his eyes will grow dim: … at a rainbow, at a Nasi, and at the priests. … At a rainbow, as it is written: “As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on the day of rain, … this was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord” … At a Nasi, as it is written: “And you shall put of your splendor upon him” … who looks at the priests when the Temple is standing, as they would stand on their platform and bless Israel with the ineffable name,

Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Naḥmani, the disseminator … Reish Lakish, interpreted … homiletically: What is … which is written: “Trust not in a companion, do not put your confidence in an intimate friend” … If the evil inclination says to you: Sin, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, will forgive, do not trust … since it is stated: “Trust not in a companion [rei’a].” And rei’a is referring to none other … the evil [ra] inclination, as it is stated: “For the inclination of the heart of man is evil [ra]”

And “intimate friend” is referring to none other … the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is stated: “You are the intimate friend of my youth” … Lest you say: … who will testify against me? The stones of the house and the beams of the house of … person testify against him, as it is stated: “For the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it”

And the Sages say: A person’s soul … testify against him, as it is stated: “Guard the doors of your mouth from she who lies in your bosom” … What thing lies in a person’s bosom? You must say it is … soul. Rabbi Zerika said: … two ministering angels who accompany him, … they testify against him, as it is stated: “For He will command His angels over you, to guard you in all your ways” … And the Sages say: A person’s limbs testify against him, as it is stated: “Therefore you are My witnesses, says the Lord, and I am God”

MISHNA: Yosei ben Yo’ezer says not to place … Yosef ben Yoḥanan, says to place … Yehoshua ben Peraḥya says not to place … Nitai HaArbeli says to place … Yehuda ben Tabbai says not to place … Shimon ben Shataḥ says to place … Shemaya says to place … Avtalyon says not to place … Hillel and Menaḥem did not disagree … Menaḥem departed … Shammai entered … Shammai says not to place … Hillel says to place
The first … served as Nasi, and their counterparts … deputy Nasi.

GEMARA: The Sages taught: Three of the first pairs who say not to place hands and two of the last pairs who say to place hands served as Nasi, and their counterparts … deputy Nasi; … the statement of Rabbi Meir. And the Rabbis say … Yehuda ben Tabbai … deputy Nasi and Shimon ben Shataḥ … Nasi.

Who is the tanna … that which the Sages taught … Rabbi Yehuda ben Tabbai said: … I will … see the consolation … if I did not kill a conspiring witness. … to counter the views of the Sadducees, who would say: Conspiring witnesses are not executed unless the sentenced one has been executed.

Shimon ben Shataḥ said to him: … I will … see the consolation … if you did not shed innocent blood, as the Sages said: Conspiring witnesses are not executed unless they are both found to be conspirators; … And they are not flogged … unless they are both found to be conspirators. And … they do not pay money unless they are both found to be conspirators.
Yehuda ben Tabbai immediately accepted upon himself not to rule … law unless he was in the presence of Shimon ben Shataḥ,

All of Yehuda ben Tabbai’s days, he would prostrate himself on the grave of that executed … and his voice was heard … The people thought that it was the voice of that executed … said to them: It is my voice, … you … know … for tomorrow, … he will die, and his voice will no … be heard.
Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi: … perhaps … appeased … Or, … prosecuted him by the law

Whose … this … Granted, if you say … with … Rabbi Meir, … said … Shimon ben Shataḥ was deputy Nasi … Rabbi Yehuda ben Tabbai was Nasi, that … he … issued a halakhic ruling in the presence of Shimon ben Shataḥ … But if you say … the Sages, who said: Yehuda ben Tabbai … deputy Nasi … Shimon ben Shataḥ … Nasi, … May … deputy Nasi issue a halakhic ruling in the presence of … Nasi?
No; what … accepting upon himself … He spoke … to joining … Even … joining … I will also not join

Menaḥem departed and Shammai entered. … To where did … depart? Abaye said: He departed and went astray. … Rava said: He departed for the king’s service. … This is also taught … Menaḥem departed for the king’s service, and eighty pairs of students dressed in silk robes left with him

Rav Shemen bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: A rabbinic decree [shevut] should never be taken lightly in your eyes, since placing hands … is prohibited only as a rabbinic decree … the greatest … of each generation disputed it.
is obvious. … necessary for him … a rabbinic decree related to a mitzva.
This too is obvious. … to exclude … of the one who said … they disagree with regard to the actual … placing hands, … He … teaches us … it is a rabbinic decree … of their dispute,

Rami bar Ḥama said: … learn from here, … placing hands … we also require … with all his strength. For if it enters your mind … we do not require all his strength, what … does one violate … Let him place

The Gemara raises an objection … “Speak to the children of [benei] Israel” … “And he shall place … the sons of Israel place … but the daughters of Israel do not place … Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yishmael say: It is optional for the daughters of Israel to place

Rabbi Yosei said: … Abba Elazar related to me … On one occasion, we had a calf for a peace-offering, and we brought it to the Women’s Courtyard, and women placed … on it. … not because there … placing hands in … women, but in order to please the women, … if it enters your mind … we require … with all one’s strength, … we perform work with consecrated … in order to please … women? … Rather, isn’t it … conclude from this … we do not require … with all one’s strength?

Actually, I … say to you … we do require … with all one’s strength, … by saying to them: Ease your hands … If so, … Not because there … place hands in … women, … Let him derive … it is not … placing hands at all.
Rabbi Ami said: He stated one … and another. One … that it is not … placing hands at all, … and another … in order to please the women.
Rav Pappa said: Learn from this … sides are … prohibited, for if it enters your mind … sides are permitted, … to place … on the sides, … Rather, … not conclude from this … sides are prohibited?
Rav Ashi said: Even … you say that sides are permitted … anything that is near … back … considered as its back.

MISHNA: Beit Shammai say: One may bring peace-offerings … but one may not place … on them, … However, … not … burnt-offerings … And Beit Hillel say: One may bring peace-offerings and … burnt-offerings, and one places … hands on … them.

the festival of Shavuot occurs on the eve of Shabbat, Beit Shammai say: The day of slaughter … after Shabbat, … And Beit Hillel say: The day of slaughter is not after Shabbat. … But … concede that if … occurs on Shabbat, the day of slaughter … after Shabbat.
the High Priest would not dress in his … garments … And all were permitted to eulogize and fast … not to uphold … the opinion of … who would say: Shavuot … after Shabbat.

GEMARA: Rabbi Elazar said … Rabbi Oshaya said: From where … that … Shavuot … can be redressed, … all seven … As it is stated: … on the festival of Passover, and on the festival of Shavuot, and on the festival of Sukkot” … the festival of Shavuot to the festival of Passover by analogy: Just as one can redress the failure to bring the offering on the festival of Passover on all seven … so too, on the festival of Shavuot, one can redress the failure to bring the offering for all seven,

But perhaps … say … to the festival of Sukkot by analogy: Just as the Festival … of Sukkot can be redressed for all eight … so too can the festival of Shavuot be redressed for all eight … Eighth … is an independent pilgrimage Festival

say that … they said that … Eighth … is an independent pilgrimage Festival, this applies only to the issue of peh, zayin, reish, kuf, shin, beit, … Eighth … But with regard to the redress … it … redress for the first … as we learned … One who did not celebrate … on the first day of the … Festival can celebrate … throughout the pilgrimage Festival … and … the last day
If you grasped many, you did not grasp anything; if you grasped few, you grasped something.

But … for … what halakha did the Merciful One write the festival of Sukkot … to … analogy to the festival of Passover, … Just as the festival of Passover requires lodging … so too the festival of Sukkot requires lodging
And there, … from where do we
as it is written … “And you shall turn in the morning and go to your tents”

We learned … the festival of Shavuot occurs on the eve of Shabbat, Beit Shammai say: The day of slaughter is after Shabbat; and Beit Hillel say: It does not have a day of slaughter. What, is it not … it does not have a day of slaughter at all; … No, … it does not require a day of slaughter.

And what does this teach us; that … are sacrificed on their day? But they have … disputed this once, as we learned … Beit Shammai say: One may bring peace-offerings … but one may not place … hands on them. However, … not … burnt-offerings … and Beit Hillel say: One may bring peace-offerings and … burnt-offerings, and one places … hands on … them.
necessary, for had … taught us … this … with regard to this … that Beit Shammai state … because … possible … on the following day, … but there, … you … say … they agree with Beit Hillel
And had it taught us … that … with regard to that … that Beit Hillel state … because … not possible … on the following day, … but here, … you … say … they agree with Beit Shammai. … necessary

Come … hear … One who did not celebrate … the seven days of Passover, or … the eight days of the festival … or … the first day of Shavuot may no longer celebrate … Does … not … the Festival day of Shavuot … No, … day of slaughter, … If so, let us … resolve from here, … that … one day of slaughter … Say … Days of slaughter.

Come … hear … as Rabba bar Shmuel taught … Torah said … count … days, as it is stated: … and … sanctify … month … count days … and … sanctify the festival of Shavuot … as it is stated: “You shall count fifty days” ( … ). … Just as … month is … for … by which it is counted, … so too, Shavuot … Does … not … we learn from … month? … just as … a month, … one day, so too Shavuot … one day,

Rava said: And … you understand … Is that to say … Shavuot we count days … we do not count weeks? Didn’t Abaye say: … a mitzva to count days, … as it is written: … you shall count fifty days” … and … a mitzva to count weeks, as it is written: “Seven weeks you shall count for yourself, … and further, it is written: “The festival of weeks [shavuot]”

the school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov, … taught … The verse states … “And you shall make a proclamation … “And when you reap … Which is the Festival on which you make a proclamation and … reap, … You must say it is the festival of Shavuot.
When … If we say … to the Festival day … permitted to reap on a Festival? … Rather, is it not … to … redress?

As a cage is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit.

Do not suffer from tomorrow’s trouble, … as you do not know what a day will bring. Perhaps … tomorrow comes, … not … he … consequently upset over a world that is not his. Prevent a crowd from inside your house, … and do not … bring all … your house. … a crowd seeks your welfare, … Reveal a secret to … one in a thousand,

Rabbi Asi said: The … son of David, will not come until all the souls of the body have been finished, … As it is stated: “For the spirit that enwraps itself is from Me, and the souls that I have made” … It is taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: Anyone who does not engage in … fruitful and multiply … as though he sheds blood, as it is stated: “Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed” … and it is written … afterward: “And you, be fruitful and multiply”

Rabbi Ya’akov says: It is as though he diminishes the … Image, as it is stated: “For in the image of God He made man” … and it is written … afterward: “And you, be fruitful … Ben Azzai says: … as though he sheds blood and … diminishes the … Image, as it is stated: “And you, be fruitful and multiply,”

They said to ben Azzai: There … expounds well and fulfills … well, … fulfills well and does not expound well. But you, … expound well … and … you do not fulfill well … Ben Azzai said to them: What shall I do, as my soul yearns for Torah, … It is possible for the world to be maintained by others,

It is … taught … another … Rabbi Eliezer says: Anyone who does not engage in … fruitful and multiply … as though he sheds blood, as it is stated: “Whoever sheds the blood of man,” and … near it: “And you, be fruitful … Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says: … as though he diminishes the … Image. Ben Azzai says: … They said to ben Azzai: There is … expounds well, etc.
The Sages taught … “And when it rested, he would say: Return, Lord, to the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel”

teaches that the Divine Presence does not rest upon less than two thousands and two ten-thousands of the Jewish people, … there were two thousands and two ten-thousands of the Jewish people, less one, and this … did not engage in … fruitful and multiply, is he not found … caused the Divine Presence to be depart from the Jewish people?

Abba Ḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer: … liable to death, as it is stated … and they had no children” … had children they would not have died. Upon wood and stones?

MISHNA: … married a woman and stayed with her … ten years and she did not give birth, he is no … permitted to neglect … he divorced her she is permitted to marry another … and the second … is permitted to stay with her … ten years. And if she had a miscarriage, he counts … from the time of the miscarriage.

Although there is no … proof for the matter … an allusion to the matter, … after Abram had dwelled ten years in the land of Canaan, … to teach you that … dwelling outside of Eretz Yisrael do not count … his tally. Consequently, … he was sick … or she was sick, or … the two of them … imprisoned in jail, … does not count … his tally.

Rava said to Rav Naḥman: Let us derive from Isaac … as it is written: “And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah … and it is written … “And Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them” … said to him: Isaac … was infertile,

If so, Abraham … was also infertile. … requires that … for … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba … because Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Why were Ishmael’s years counted … In order to determine through them the years of Jacob,

Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Isaac our father was infertile, as it is stated: “And Isaac entreated the Lord concerning [lenokhaḥ] his wife … It is not stated … for [al] his wife, but lenokhaḥ, … teaches that they were both infertile. … If so, … “And … let Himself be entreated of him”? … should say: And … let Himself be entreated of them. … because the prayer of a righteous individual … the son of a righteous individual is not similar to the prayer of a righteous individual … the son of a wicked individual,

Rabbi Yitzḥak said: For what reason were our forefathers … infertile? Rabbi Ami said: Abraham and Sarah were … tumtumin, … as it is stated: “Look to the rock
from where you were hewn, and to the hole of the pit from where you were dug” … and it is written … “Look to Abraham your father and to Sarah who bore you”

Rav Naḥman said … Rabba bar Avuh said: Our mother Sarah was … sexually underdeveloped woman [aylonit], as it is stated: “And Sarah was barren; she had no child” … she did not have even a place, … for a child.

Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Sheilat, said in the name of Rav: They taught … only … in former generations, whose years … numerous, … However, … in later generations, whose years are few, … two and half years … corresponding to … three pregnancies. Rabba said … Rav Naḥman: … three years, corresponding to … three remembrances … as the Master said: On Rosh HaShana Sarah, Rachel, and Hannah were remembered,
Rabba … said: These principles are not … Now … who established … mishna? Rabbi … in the days of … David, … the years … were … diminished, as it is written: “The days of our years are seventy years,
And … this … Perhaps he did not merit to be built from her; perhaps … she who did not merit … She, since she is not commanded … fruitful and multiply, is not punished.

Is that so? Didn’t the Sages say to Rabbi Abba bar Zavda: Marry a woman and have children, and he said to them: If I had merited, I would … have … from … first … There, … was … putting the Rabbis off … as … Rabbi Abba bar Zavda became impotent from Rav Huna’s discourse.

Rav Giddel became impotent from Rav Huna’s discourse, Rav Ḥelbo became impotent from Rav Huna’s discourse, … Rav Sheshet became impotent from Rav Huna’s discourse. … Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov was afflicted by suskhinta, … They suspended him from the cedar … the study hall, and … green … leaf emerged from him, … Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: We were sixty elders … and they all became impotent from Rav Huna’s discourse, aside from me, as I fulfilled with regard to myself … “Wisdom preserves the life of he who has it”
divorced … she is permitted … A second … yes, … a third … no.

Come … hear, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: An incident … involving four sisters in Tzippori, that … first … circumcised … and he died, … second … and he died, … third … and he … died. … fourth … came before Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, … said to her: Do not circumcise
Perhaps if … third … come … he would also have said to her … If so, what is … of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba’s testimony? … Perhaps … teach us that sisters establish a presumption
Rava said: Now that you have said … sisters establish a presumption, a man should not marry a woman from a family of epileptics or from a family of lepers, … And this … was established three times,

Which … was about this … When Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef came … he said: An incident occurred before Rabbi Yoḥanan in the synagogue of … Maon on … Yom Kippur that occurred on Shabbat. … first … circumcised … and he died; … second … and he … died. … third … came before him, … said to her: Go and circumcise
Abaye said to … See … as you are permitting … a prohibition and a danger.

Abaye relied on this … and went … married Ḥuma, the daughter of Isi, son of Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rav Yehuda. … had … married Raḥava of Pumbedita, and he died, … Rav Yitzḥak, son of Rabba bar bar Ḥana, and he died; and he, … married her … and he died

Rava said: Is there … who performs an action like this … himself … Wasn’t it he, … who said … Avin is reliable … Yitzḥak the Red, … is not reliable? … Avin returns … Yitzḥak the Red does not return … And furthermore, say that they disagree with regard to … circumcision, … do … argue with regard to marriage?

Yes, and it is taught … was married to … first … and he died, to a second … and he … died, she may not get married to a third … the statement of Rabbi … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: She may get married to a third … she may not get married to a fourth

Granted with regard to circumcision … there are families whose blood is thin … and there are families whose blood clots. What is … between them? … There is … between them … where … betrothed her and died … alternatively, … where he fell off a palm tree and died.

Rav Yosef, son of Rava, said to Rava: I inquired of Rav Yosef … halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi … and he said to me: Yes. … halakha is in accordance with … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and he said to me: Yes. Was he mocking me

said to him: No, there are unattributed … and he resolved for you … marriage and lashings … in accordance with … Rabbi … set patterns … and a forewarned ox, … in accordance with … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

Marriage … that which we said … lashings … as we learned … One who was flogged … and repeated … court places him in a … vaulted chamber and they feed him barley until his stomach bursts. … set patterns … as we learned … A woman does not

establish a set pattern … for herself, … until she has established it three times. … she is not purified from her set pattern until it is uprooted from her three times, … And … forewarned ox … as we learned … An ox does not become forewarned until … testify … it … three times.

The Sages taught: … was married to … first … and she did not have children, … to … second … and she did not have children, she may not get married to a third … unless … to one who … has children … she got married to one who does not have children … she is divorced without … marriage contract,

A dilemma was raised before … she was married to a third … and she did not have children … what is … those first … can demand … her … Can … say to her: It has been revealed … that it was you who caused … or perhaps … can say to them: It is now that … I have become weak, … reasonable … she can say to them: It is now that I have become weak.

dilemma was raised before … she was married to a fourth … and she had children … what is … she can demand … third … We say to her: Your silence is preferable to your speech, … as he can say to her: I did not divorce you with this understanding,

he said … from her, … and she said … from him, Rabbi Ami said: … matters between him and her, she is believed. … What is the reason … She is certain … shoots like an arrow, … he is not certain … shoots like an arrow.

he says: I will go … marry a … woman and examine myself … Rabbi Ami said: Even in this … must divorce … and give … marriage contract, as I say … whoever marries a woman in addition to his … wife must divorce … and give … marriage contract. … Rava said … a man may marry several women in addition to his … wife, and … as long as he has … to support them
he said: You miscarried within … ten … and she said: I did not miscarry, Rabbi Ami said: Even in this … she is believed, because if it is so that she miscarried she … not establish herself as barren

she miscarried, and … miscarried again, and miscarried again, she has been established to … miscarriages, … he said she miscarried twice, and she said … three … Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Elazar said: There was an incident … the study hall and they said … she is believed, because if it is so that … not miscarried … she … not establish herself … miscarriages.

On the contrary, … “And conquer it [vekhivshuha],” indicates … two … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: It is written … And conquer it [vekhivsha], … Rav Yosef said: … from here: … I am God Almighty, be fruitful and multiply [perei urvei]” … and it does not state: Be fruitful and multiply [peru urvu]

And Rabbi Ile’a said in the name of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon: Just as it is a mitzva for a person to say that which will be heeded, so is it a mitzva for a person not to say that which will not be heeded. … Rabbi Abba says: … obligatory … as it is stated: “Do not reprove a scorner lest he hate you; reprove a wise man and he will love you”

And Rabbi Ile’a … said in the name of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon: It is permitted for a person to depart … in a matter … peace, as it is stated: “Your father commanded … So you shall say to Joseph: Please pardon
Rabbi Natan says: … a mitzva … as it is stated: “And Samuel said: How can I go, and Saul will hear and kill me”

taught … the school of Rabbi Yishmael: Great is peace, as even the Holy One, Blessed be He, departed … it. As, initially it is written … “And my lord is old” … and in the end it is written … “And I am old”

Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says … It was stated … Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, … One said … halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, and one said … halakha is not in accordance with … Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka.
Conclude that it was Rabbi Yoḥanan who said … halakha is not … as Rabbi Abbahu sat and said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan … halakha … and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, … turned their faces

What … was … about … Come … hear, as Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina said … Rabbi Abbahu said … Rabbi Asi said: There was an incident … before Rabbi Yoḥanan in the synagogue of Caesarea … and he said … must divorce … and give … marriage contract. If it enters your mind … that she is not commanded … what is … a marriage contract doing
Perhaps … in … she came … due to … claim,

like … a certain … who came before Rabbi Ami … She said to him … Give me … marriage contract. He said to her: Go … you are not commanded … She said to him: In her old age, what will be with this woman, … said: … such as this, we certainly force

A certain … came before Rav Naḥman … He said to her: You are not commanded … She said to him: Does this woman not require a staff for her hand and a hoe for … burial? … said: … such as this, we certainly force

Yehuda and Ḥizkiyya, were twins, … one … was fully developed after nine … and one was fully developed at the beginning of the seventh … Yehudit, the wife of Rabbi Ḥiyya, had … birthing pain … changed her clothes … and came before Rabbi Ḥiyya … She said: Is a woman commanded … fruitful and multiply? He said to her: No. She went and drank an infertility potion.
Eventually the matter was revealed, … He said to her: If only you had given birth to one more belly for me, … As the Master said: Yehuda and Ḥizkiyya … brothers … Pazi and Tavi,
sisters,

Are … not commanded … Didn’t Rav Aḥa bar Rav Ketina say … Rabbi Yitzḥak said: … an incident with a certain woman who … half-slave and half-free woman … and they forced her master and he made her a free … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: … treated her in a loose manner.

MISHNA: A widow … to a High Priest, … a divorcée or a yevama who performed ḥalitza [ḥalutza] … to a common priest … brought … into … slaves of usufruct [melog] … or slaves of guaranteed investment, … slaves of usufruct … do not partake of teruma … slaves of guaranteed investment do partake

And these are slaves of usufruct … if … die, their death … her … and if they increase … their increase … her … Although … is obligated in their sustenance, they do not partake of teruma, … And these are slaves of guaranteed investment: … if they die, their death … his … and if they increase … their increase … his … Since he bears … responsibility … their … they partake of teruma,

an Israelite woman who married a priest … and … brought slaves … into … whether … slaves of usufruct … or slaves of guaranteed investment, they partake of teruma. And … the daughter of a priest who married an Israelite and … brought slaves … into … whether … slaves of usufruct … or slaves of guaranteed investment, they do not partake of teruma,

GEMARA: … slaves of usufruct … do not partake of teruma. … Why … Let … be like … his acquisition who acquired an acquisition, as it is taught … From where … to a priest who married a woman and acquired slaves that they partake of teruma? As it is stated: “But if a priest buys any soul, the purchase of his money, he may eat of it”

And from where … to … wife … who acquired slaves and … slaves who acquired slaves, that … may … partake of teruma? As it is stated: “But if a priest buys any soul, the purchase of his money, he may eat of it,” … his acquisition acquired an acquisition, … partakes … slaves of usufruct
anyone who … partake … enable … to partake … anyone who does not partake … cannot enable … to partake.
And … cannot enable … to partake? But aren’t … uncircumcised … and all impure … who do not partake … and … they enable … to partake … there, … their mouths hurt,
But isn’t … a son born from an incestuous or adulterous relationship [mamzer] … who does not partake … enables
Ravina said … is referring … an acquisition who partakes … acquisition … partakes … enables … to partake, … who does not partake, … cannot enable … to partake.

And Rava said … By Torah … partake … And it was the Sages who issued a decree … them … so that … would say: I do not partake … my slaves do not partake … she is … a prostitute to him. … therefore come to divorce her,
Rav Ashi said … decree lest she have … partake … after … death
However, if … so, … Israelite woman who marries a priest should not enable … to partake … decree, lest she have them partake … after … death.

Rather, Rav Ashi said … with a widowed priestess, … as she is likely to rationalize … Initially, … partook of the teruma of my father’s house. I … married this … and they partook of the teruma of my husband. And now … I have returned to the original circumstance, … And she does not realize that … initially she did not render herself a woman disqualified from marrying a priest [ḥalala], … now, … she rendered herself a ḥalala,
works out well … a widowed priestess. … widow … an Israelite woman, what can be said? … With regard to widowhood, the Sages did not distinguish
It was stated: … who brings appraised, … property into her … husband, … she says: I am taking my belongings, and he says: I am … give you … monetary … the halakha … whom? Rav Yehuda said:
The halakha … her; … And Rav Ami said: The halakha … him;

Rav Yehuda said … the halakha … her because … the assets of her paternal family, … they are hers. Rabbi Ami said that the halakha … him, since the Master said … If they die, their death … his … and if they increase … their increase … his … Since he bears … responsibility for their … they partake … Rav Safra said … Does … teach … they are his? … teaches … he bears … responsibility for their … but actually they are not his.

Rabba and Rav Yosef sat at the conclusion of Rav Naḥman’s sermon, and they sat and said: It is taught … in accordance with … Rav Yehuda, and it is taught … in accordance with … Rabbi Ami. it is taught … in accordance with … Rav Yehuda: … brings appraised, … property … to her husband, if the husband wishes to sell … he may not sell … And not only … even … brought … into … her … an appraised, … of his own, … if the husband wishes to sell … he may not sell … either … sold … for subsistence, … was an incident … this … before Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and he said: … the husband … he may repossess … from the purchasers,

Rava said: The dead has acquired it, … Nanai, son of Rav Yosef, son of Rava, said to Rav Kahana: But didn’t Rava say … Rav Naḥman said … the halakha is in accordance with … Rav Yehuda? … He said to him: Doesn’t Rav Yehuda admit that … has not yet been collected? Rava … to his … reasoning, as Rava said: Consecration … leavened bread

What is he teaching us? … assets of her paternal family are hers? Rav Yehuda … said this once, … lest you say … this applies … where she comes to collect her marriage contract, … but to give money and take … not … teaches us

said to him: Since you testified before us about … an Israelite woman … to a priest, … the daughter of a priest … to a priest and he died and left her pregnant, her slaves should not partake of teruma either, due to the fetus’s share.

raises an objection … said to Rabbi Yosei: Since you testified before us about … an Israelite woman … to a priest, … the daughter of a priest … to a priest, what is … He said to them: … I heard … but … this … I did not hear

males, … may partake … But … isn’t there a fetus … holds

no matter what, … If this … with which she is pregnant, is a son, it is no better than this … who … exists. … If it is a daughter, … Why does … partake … by … a rabbinic ordinance. … as long as … has not emerged into the atmosphere of the world, the Sages did not establish
