are necessary, for if only the … were stated, I would say: This applies ab initio, but after the fact even two … he teaches us that the halakha does not follow this pair … If he would have told us only that the halakha does not follow this pair, but rather the first tanna, I would say … after the fact, but they must require five … ab initio, … it is necessary

he said … Where is your father? He said to him: … in the city. Where is your mother? He said: In the city. … set his gaze upon them, … and both … died.

this is what … said: A mistaken ḥalitza is always valid, … a mistaken bill of divorce is always invalid. A coerced ḥalitza and a coerced bill of divorce are sometimes valid and sometimes invalid. … the one who says … I want to … the one who does not say: I want to

she says: “My brother-in-law refused to establish a name for his brother in Israel, he did not wish to consummate the levirate marriage” … and … he says: “I do not wish to take her” … And they would say … in the sacred … language … “His yevama shall approach him, before the Elders, and remove his shoe from on his foot and spit before him” … this spittle … visible to the judges. “And … respond and say: So shall it be done to the man who does not build his brother’s house” … Up until this point … would prompt … to recite

GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said: … the mitzva of ḥalitza: She recites … he recites … she removes … and spits, and recites: … What is … teaching us? This is … the mishna. … This teaches us … the mitzva is like this, … but if one switched the order, we have no … with it,

And he should not read to the … do not” by itself, … “Wish to … by itself, as it sounds … like: I do wish to take her. Rather, … “I do not wish to take her.” Rava said: It is a … interruption in the matter. And we have no … an interruption in the matter … .

He said to him: … Rava concedes concerning … “He did not wish to consummate the levirate marriage,” … Abaye … said: One who writes a bill of ḥalitza must write as follows: We prompted her to recite from “My brother-in-law refused” until “he did not wish to consummate the levirate marriage” … and we prompted him to recite from … not” until “take her” … And we prompted her to recite from “So shall” … until “he who had his shoe removed”
Mar Zutra would score … and write the whole … passage … Mar bar Idi strongly objected to this: But it is unable to be written … the halakha is in accordance with … Mar Zutra,

Abaye said: … spat, but the wind seized … she did nothing, … What is the reason … We require … “she spit before him,” … Therefore, if he is tall and she is short and the wind seized it, … “before him” is satisfied, … But if she is tall and he is short, we require that the saliva reach the space across from his face, and afterward it may go

Rava said: … she ate garlic and spat, … she ate gargishta clay, … and spat, she did nothing … What is the reason … We require that “she shall spit” on her own, and this is not … And Rava said: The judges must see the spittle when it leaves the mouth of the yevama, … as it is written: “Before the Elders…and spit,”

“And his name shall be called in Israel: The house of he who had his shoe removed,” there is a mitzva upon the judges to recite this but … not … for the students … is taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: Once we were sitting before Rabbi Tarfon and a yevama came to perform ḥalitza. He said to us: You must all answer: “He who had his shoe removed,” “He who had his shoe removed,” “He who had his shoe removed,”
MISHNA: … Beit Shammai say: Only betrothed girls may refuse. … But Beit Hillel say … betrothed and fully married
Beit Shammai say: … at … husband and not at … yavam. … But Beit Hillel say: … at … husband or … yavam.
Beit Shammai say: … in the presence of … But Beit Hillel say: … either in his presence or in his absence. Beit Shammai say: … in court. But Beit Hillel say: … either in court, or not in court.

Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai: She may refuse as long as she is a minor, even four or five times … Beit Shammai said to them: The daughters of Israel are not to be treated with disregard … Rather, she refuses … And … she must wait until she reaches majority, and refuse, and marry.

GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: What is the reason of Beit Shammai … because there are no conditions with regard to marriage. … And if a married … would refuse, … they will come to say that there … condition with regard to marriage.
But what is there to say if she entered the marriage canopy but did not … engage in sexual intercourse? … There are no conditions with regard to a wedding canopy,
But what is there to say if the father delivered his daughter to the agents of the husband … The Sages did not distinguish

And … Beit Hillel, … It is known that marriage of a minor girl is by rabbinic … Rabba and Rav Yosef both say: Beit Shammai’s reason is that a man would not readily render his sexual act licentious sexual intercourse.

What is there to say if she entered the marriage canopy but did not engage in sexual intercourse, … It would not be satisfactory for him, … if … would be a forbidden marriage canopy, … What is there to say if the father delivered his daughter to the agents of the husband? … The Sages did not distinguish … And … Beit Hillel … Since there is both betrothal and a marriage contract … no one will come to say that his sexual act was licentious intercourse.

Rav Pappa said: … reasoning for Beit Shammai’s … is because of … profits … and … reasoning for Beit Hillel’s … is … because of … profits … reasoning for Beit Shammai’s … is because of … profits … for if you say that a married … may perform refusal, then the husband … might seize … from her and consume them, as ultimately she stands to leave … And Beit Hillel … On the contrary: Since you say she may refuse, he will … improve … He will think: if … do not … her relatives will advise her … and they will take her from him.

Rava said: This is the reasoning of Beit Shammai: A man will not bother to make a marriage feast and … lose it. … And Beit Hillel … The marriage is convenient for both of them … so as to generate publicity about them that … married.

Beit Shammai say: … at … husband … Rabbi Oshaya said: … may direct a refusal against a levirate betrothal but she may not direct a refusal against his … bond. … Rav Ḥisda said: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Oshaya? … levirate betrothal, which is consensual, she can nullify … bond, which … against her will, she cannot nullify
But … consummation … may be against her will

and she can nullify it, … Rather, … consummation … and … levirate betrothal, … which he performs, she can nullify … the … bond, which the Merciful One imposes upon her … cannot nullify … Ulla said: She may direct her refusal even to his … bond. What is the reason? … nullifies the original marriage,

Rava raised an objection to … Ulla. … any … could perform refusal but does not perform refusal, her rival wife performs ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage. … Why? Let her perform refusal now and nullify the first marriage … and let her rival wife enter into levirate marriage. … A rival wife of a forbidden relative is different, … as Rami bar Yeḥezkel taught … who refuses her husband is permitted to his father, … a yavam is forbidden to his father.
Evidently, at the time when she happens … she appears to be his … daughter-in-law. … Here, too, … at the time she happened … she appears to be his daughter’s rival wife,

Rav said: … refuses this … is forbidden to that … just as it is … concerning a … who has … a bill of divorce … Is it not so that since … who has … a bill of divorce is forbidden to one of them, … she is forbidden to all of them? Here too, it is no different.

And Shmuel said: If she refused this … she is permitted to that … and it is not comparable to … who has … a bill of divorce. … who has … a bill of divorce, it is he who performed the act … to her, … Here, she is performing an act on him, as she says: I do not desire you and I do not want you, … It is you whom I do not desire, but I may desire your fellow.

Rav Asi said: If she refuses this … she is permitted even to him … Shall we say that he holds in accordance with … Rabbi Oshaya, who said: She cannot refuse his levirate bond, … In the case of one yavam … she can indeed nullify the … bond. … here, we are dealing with two yevamin, and there cannot be refusal of half a … bond.

When Ravin came … he said … Rabbi Yoḥanan … refuses this … is permitted to the brothers, and they did not agree with him. … Who did not agree with him? Abaye said: … Rav, … Rava said: … Rabbi Oshaya, … And some say: … Rav Asi

Beit Shammai say: … in the presence of … It is taught … Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai: But … wife of Pishon the camel driver refuse … in his absence? Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel: Pishon the camel driver measured using a defective standard, … and therefore the Sages measured him with a defective standard [midda kefusha].
Since he was consuming the profits … it is obvious that … she was married, … But didn’t Beit Shammai say that a married … cannot perform refusal? … They tied him in two knots,

Beit Shammai say: … before a court, … We learned … elsewhere … Ḥalitza and refusals … in the presence of three … Who … taught this? Rabba said: It is Beit Shammai … Abaye said: You … even say … Beit Hillel. Beit Hillel state only that we do not require expert judges … but we do require three

As it is taught … Beit Shammai say: Before a court, and Beit Hillel say: … before a court or not before a court, but both this … and that … concede that three … are required. Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda and Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, validate … of two. Rav Yosef bar Manyumi said … Rav Naḥman said: The halakha is in accordance with that pair.

Beit Shammai say: She refuses … And … she must wait until she reaches majority, and refuse, and marry. … Didn’t she … refuse once? … Shmuel said: … until she reaches majority and says: I wish … my initial refusal,
Ulla said: Two … are taught … Either she should refuse, and … has matured … should become betrothed; or she should refuse and marry immediately.
Granted, … Ulla is … that which is taught: Until she reaches majority and marries. … But according to … Shmuel, … should have … Until she reaches majority and says … difficult

MISHNA: Who is a minor girl who needs to perform refusal … Any … whose mother or brother married her off with her consent. If they married her off without her consent, she need not refuse … Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says: Any girl who … cannot keep her betrothal, … safe does not need to refuse,

Rabbi Elazar says: The act of a minor girl is nothing, … Rather, … as though she were … seduced … daughter of a non-priest married to a priest may not eat teruma, … the … daughter of a priest married to an Israelite may eat teruma.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says … any obstruction … due to the man, it is as if she were his wife. … any obstruction in the matter that is not due to the man, it is as if she were not his wife.

GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said, and some say it was taught in a baraita: At first, they would write a bill of refusal in this manner: I do not desire him, I do not want him, and I do not wish to be married to him. Once they saw that the text was too long, the … said:
may come to be confused with a bill of divorce … they decreed … as follows: On such and such a day, so-and-so, the daughter of so-and-so, performed refusal in our presence,

The Sages taught: What … a refusal? … she said: I do not want so-and-so as my husband, … I do not want the betrothal in which my mother and brothers had me betrothed, … Rabbi Yehuda said more than that: Even if she is sitting in a bridal chair [apiryon] going from her father’s house to her husband’s house and said … I do not want so-and-so as my husband, this … a refusal.

Rabbi Yehuda said … more than that: Even if guests are reclining at her husband’s house and she is standing and serving them drinks … and … said to them: I do not want so-and-so as my husband, this … a refusal, … Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda said more than that: Even if her husband sent her to a shopkeeper to bring him an article of his and she said: I do not want so-and-so as my husband, there is no greater refusal than this.

Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says: Any girl … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus. … taught: … a minor girl who did not refuse … but who went and married … it was said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira: Her … marriage constitutes her refusal,

A dilemma was raised before … What is … if she was betrothed … Come … hear … a minor girl did not refuse … but went and became betrothed … said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira: Her betrothal constitutes her refusal.

A dilemma was raised before … Do the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira or not? … if you say … they do disagree … with regard to betrothal … or … also … with regard to marriage? And if you say … they disagree even with regard to marriage, is the halakha in accordance with his opinion or is the halakha not in accordance with his opinion? And if you say that the halakha is in accordance with his opinion, is … with regard to marriage, or is … even with regard to betrothal?
Come … hear: Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira … halakha, … by inference … disagree.

But still, you should raise the dilemma: … when she had initially been married or perhaps … was betrothed … Come … hear: The daughters-in-law of Abdan rebelled … Rabbi … sent a pair of Sages to examine them … women said to … See, it is your husbands that are coming. They said back to them: Let them be your husbands.

Rabbi … said: There is no greater refusal than this. What … Is it not that they were … married? … No, they were merely betrothed, … The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira … even with regard to her marriage to the first

Rabbi Elazar says: … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: I reviewed all the opinions of the Sages … and I did not find any person who applied a consistent standard with regard to a minor like Rabbi Elazar … For Rabbi Elazar portrayed her as a girl walking with … in a courtyard, who stands up from his bosom … and immerses … and partakes of teruma by evening

It is taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: The act of a minor girl is nothing, … And her husband has no rights to items she finds, nor to her earnings; nor … to annul her vows; he does not inherit her … and … he may not become ritually impure on her account … The principle is: … his wife in any sense, except that she must perform refusal

Rabbi Yehoshua says: … her husband has rights to items she finds, and to her earnings; and … to annul her vows; and he inherits her … and … he must become ritually impure on her account … The principle is: She is his wife in every sense, except that she can leave … by … refusal

Rabbi … said: The statement of Rabbi Eliezer appears … than the statement of Rabbi Yehoshua, as Rabbi Eliezer applied a consistent standard with regard to a minor, while Rabbi Yehoshua applied an inconsistent standard. … what … inconsistent? … If she is his wife, … should require a bill of divorce
According to Rabbi Eliezer too, … if she is not his wife, she should not be required to perform refusal either. … But shall she leave with no

Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says: … What are the circumstances of an obstruction due to the man, and an obstruction that is not due to the man? Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: … proposed marriage to her and she said: … on account of so-and-so, my husband, this is an obstruction that is due to the man. … because the men … are not suitable for me, this is an obstruction that is not due to the man,

Abaye bar Avin and Rav Ḥanina bar Avin both say: If … gave her a bill of divorce, this is an obstruction … due to the man, … he is prohibited from … her close relatives, and she is prohibited from … his close relatives; and, … she is disqualified from … the priesthood. … if she refuses him, this is an obstruction … not due to the man. … he is permitted to … her close relatives, and she is permitted to … his close relatives, and she is not disqualified from the priesthood,

But it is taught … below, … refuses a man, he is permitted to … her close relatives and she is permitted to … his close relatives, and he has not disqualified her from … the priesthood. If he gave her a bill of divorce, he is prohibited from … her close relatives, and she is prohibited from … his close relatives, and he has disqualified her from … the priesthood. … is explaining

MISHNA: … refuses a man, he is permitted to … her close relatives, … and she is permitted to … his close relatives, … and he has not disqualified her from … the priesthood, … he gave her a bill of divorce, … he is prohibited from … her close relatives, and she is prohibited from … his close relatives, and he has disqualified her from … the priesthood.

If he gave her a bill of divorce but … remarried her, and … refused him and married another … and then she was widowed or divorced … she is permitted to return to him. … if she refused him and he … remarried her, and … he gave her a bill of divorce and she married another … and she was widowed or divorced, she is forbidden to return to him,
This is the principle … If the bill of divorce followed the refusal … she is forbidden to return to him. If the refusal followed the bill of divorce, she is permitted to return to him.

refuses … man and marries another, and he divorces her, … another … and refuses him, and … another … and he divorces her, this is the principle … anyone she leaves by means of a bill of divorce, it is prohibited for her to return to him. … by means of refusal, she is permitted to return to him.
GEMARA: … Apparently, refusal comes and nullifies a bill of divorce.

raises a contradiction … refuses … man and marries another, and he divorces her, … another … and refuses him, and … another … and he divorces her, this is the principle: … anyone she leaves by means of a bill of divorce, she is prohibited from returning to him. … by means of refusal, she is permitted to return to him. Apparently, a refusal of another man does not come and nullify one’s … bill of divorce.
Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: … disjointed, … he who taught this … did not teach that

Rava said: What is the difficulty … Perhaps … refusal of him nullifies his bill of divorce, while … refusal of the other man does not nullify … bill of divorce. … what … is … refusal of the other man different, that it does not nullify his bill of divorce? … because she is familiar with the intimations and gestures [keritzotav] … he will lead her astray and bring her back … the refusal against … himself also should not nullify his … bill of divorce, as, since she is familiar with his intimations and gestures, he will lead her astray and bring her back
But he already tried to … her astray and she was not … astray.

But if there is a difficulty, it is … between … another man and … another man … is difficult, … If she refused him and he … remarried her, and … he gave her a bill of divorce and she married another … and she was widowed or divorced, she is prohibited from returning to … The reason is … that she was widowed or divorced … But if she had refused … she would be permitted to return to … Apparently, a refusal of the other man … come and nullified his bill of divorce,

raises a contradiction, … refuses … man and marries another and he divorces her, and … another and refuses him, this is the principle: … anyone she leaves by means of a bill of divorce, she is prohibited from returning to him. … by means of refusal, she is permitted to return to him. Apparently, refusal of the other man cannot come and nullify his own bill of divorce.
Rabbi Elazar said: … disjointed, … who taught this … did not teach that … Ulla said: … where she was divorced three times. Since … she appears to be an adult,

who … taught … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: … What is … which is written: “We have drunk our water for money; our wood comes to us for a price” … During the time of danger, … this halakhic ruling was requested: If she, … left her first husband by means of a bill of divorce and her second by refusal, what is … with regard to her returning to the first?
hired one person for four hundred dinars … and asked Rabbi Akiva, … in prison … and … forbidden. They asked Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira in Netzivin, … and … forbidden.
Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, said: This … was unnecessary: If you … permitted a prohibition … excision from the World-to-Come [karet], … not … all the more so … the … prohibition

Rather, this … they asked: If … was the wife of someone’s mother’s brother, a secondary … to him … and … his paternal brother married her and died, … what is … May she refuse now and uproot the first marriage … so that her rival wife may enter into levirate marriage? … in a case … a mitzva … is refusal after … death valid or not?
hired two people for four hundred dinars, and they came and asked Rabbi Akiva in prison and he … prohibited. … Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira in Netzivin and he … prohibited.
Rav Yitzḥak bar Ashyan said: Rav concedes that she is permitted to the brother of the man to whom she is forbidden.
obvious. … is he, … whose hints and gestures she recognizes, but not … his brother, … lest you say: Issue a decree … this … due to … that … he teaches us

And there are … who say … Rav Yitzḥak bar Ashyan said: Just as she is forbidden to him, … so is she forbidden to his brothers. … But she is not familiar with their intimations and gestures. … It is a … decree concerning the … brothers due to him,
MISHNA: … one who divorces a woman and remarries her … is permitted to … yavam,

but Rabbi Elazar prohibits … Likewise, … one who divorces an orphaned … girl … and remarries her … she is permitted to the yavam … and Rabbi Elazar prohibits … A minor girl whose father married her off, … and who was … divorced … is like an orphan during the lifetime of … father, … And if … remarries her … everyone agrees … she is forbidden to the yavam
GEMARA: … Eifa said: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Elazar, … because she was forbidden to him at one time; … The Sages said to Eifa: If that is so, she should also not require ḥalitza,
And if you would say: Indeed, … isn’t it taught … It was said in the name of Rabbi Elazar … she performs ḥalitza? Rather, Eifa said: I do not know the reason for … Rabbi Elazar.

Abaye said: This is the reasoning of Rabbi Elazar: He is uncertain whether the death … determines … or … the original marriage determines … If death determines … then she has happened before him for levirate marriage, … If the original marriage determines … then she was forbidden to him for a time
Rava said: Actually, it is obvious to Rabbi Elazar that death determines … However, everyone is well informed with regard to divorces. … while not everyone is well informed with regard to remarriage,
On the contrary, her return … since she is living with him, generates publicity, … Are we not dealing … a case in which he remarried her in the evening and died in the morning?

Rav Ashi said: This is the reasoning of Rabbi Elazar: He decreed … these, … due to … an orphan in the lifetime of … father, … and he … remarried her. … So too, this is reasonable based on what was taught in the latter clause … A minor girl whose father married her off and who was … divorced … is like an orphan during her father’s lifetime. And if … remarries her … everyone agrees that she is forbidden to the yavam
What … of stating … It is obvious. Rather, is it not teaching us Rabbi Elazar’s reason for decreeing that these … due to that … Learn from here

It is taught … in accordance with … Rav Ashi: The Rabbis concede to Rabbi Elazar concerning a minor girl whose father married her off and who was divorced, that she is like an orphan in the lifetime of … father, and … if … remarried her, she is forbidden to the yavam, because her divorce was a full-fledged divorce … while her remarriage was not a full-fledged remarriage,

In what … is this statement said? … where he divorced her while she was a minor and he remarried her while she was … a minor. But if he divorced her while she was a minor and remarried her when she was … an adult, or if he remarried her while she was a minor and she matured … while with him, and he … died, she may either perform ḥalitza or enter into levirate marriage. It was said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: She must perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage,
Rava asked Rav Naḥman: What is … the rival wife of … rival wife … He said to him: She herself is … a rabbinic decree, … And will we … proceed to issue a decree to … a decree? … rival wife

Isn’t it taught … It was said in the name of Rabbi Elazar: … she and her rival wife must perform ḥalitza? … Would it enter your mind … She and her rival wife? … Rather, should it not … Either she or her rival wife must perform ḥalitza, … Are you not emending … emend it as follows: She … perform ḥalitza; her rival wife may either perform ḥalitza or enter into levirate marriage.

MISHNA: … two brothers are married to two minor sisters, and the husband of one of them dies … this … shall be exempt … due to … as … sister … his wife. The same … two deaf-mute women, … an adult and … a minor, … the husband of the minor dies, the minor shall leave due to … sister … a wife,
if the husband of the adult dies, … Rabbi Eliezer says: We instruct the minor, … to refuse him,
Rabban Gamliel says: If … refuses … her refusal is valid. And if not, she should wait until she reaches majority, … and that … shall be exempt … due to … sister … a wife.
Rabbi Yehoshua says: … woe [ee] to him for his wife, woe to him for his brother’s wife. … He must release his own wife with a bill of divorce … his brother’s wife by … ḥalitza.

GEMARA: … Is it permitted … Doesn’t bar Kappara teach: A person should always cling to three things and distance himself from three things. He should cling to three things: To ḥalitza … to bringing about peace, and to the nullification of vows. And he should distance himself from three things: From refusal; and from … deposits, … and from serving as a guarantor. … A refusal for a mitzva is different,

the … itself. Bar Kappara taught: A person should always cling to three things: To ḥalitza; … in accordance with … Abba Shaul, as it is taught … Abba Shaul said: One who marries his yevama for … beauty, … for the sake of matrimony … or for some other reason, … it is as if he is having intercourse with a woman forbidden to him, and in my eyes … almost as if his offspring were a mamzer.
bringing about peace, as it is written “Seek peace and pursue it”

And Rabbi Abbahu said: It is derived … pursuit … pursuit. It is written here: “Seek peace and pursue it” … and it is written there: “He who pursues righteousness and mercy finds life, prosperity, and honor” … for the nullification of vows, this is in accordance with … Rabbi Natan, as it is taught … Rabbi Natan says: … one who vows, it is as if he built … altar … And one who fulfills that … it is as if he sacrificed an offering on this

And one should distance himself from three things: From refusals, … perhaps she will grow up and regret … From deposits … by an inhabitant of the same city, as … home as his home. … From serving as a guarantor: This is referring to Sheltziyyon guarantees,

As Rabbi Yitzḥak said: What is … which is written: “He who serves as a guarantor for a stranger shall suffer evil; … Evil after evil will befall those who accept converts, and Sheltziyyon guarantors, and one who confounds himself in matters of halakha. … those who accept converts: This is in accordance with … Rabbi Ḥelbo. As Rabbi Ḥelbo says: Converts are difficult for the Jewish people like a leprous sore on the skin.

Sheltziyyon guarantors because they practice: Pull out, thrust in. … one who confounds himself in matters of halakha, as it is taught … Rabbi Yosei says: Anyone who says he has no Torah, has no Torah. … obvious? Rather, anyone who says he has nothing other … Torah, has nothing other … Torah.

But isn’t … also obvious? … Rather, … he does not even have Torah. What is the reason? Rav Pappa said: The verse states: That you may learn them and perform them, … anyone who is engaged in performing … is engaged in … study, while anyone not engaged in performing … is not engaged in … study;

And if you wish, say: Actually, it is as you initially said: Anyone who says he has nothing other … Torah has nothing other … Torah. Rather, … is necessary … teaches others and they go and perform … Lest you say that there is reward for him in it, … teaches us

And if you wish, say … one who confounds himself in matters of halakha … to a judge who had a case come before him, and he learned … a ruling … and he likens one matter to the other … and he has a teacher … but he does not go and ask

As Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yonatan said: A judge should always view himself as if a sword were placed between his thighs, … and as if Gehenna was open beneath him, as it is stated: “Behold, it is the bed of Solomon; sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel. … because of dread in the night” … because of the dread of Gehenna, which is similar to the night.

Rabban Gamliel says: If … refuses … Rabbi Elazar raised a dilemma to Rav: What is Rabban Gamliel’s reasoning? … because he holds that the betrothal of a minor girl is in suspension and when she reaches majority, the betrothal reaches majority, … with her? … even if he did not engage in intercourse

Or perhaps, is it because he holds that … betroths the sister of his yevama, … the yevama is exempt and is released … If he engaged in sexual intercourse with … yes, … if he did not engage in intercourse with his … not exempt

Rav said to him: This is Rabban Gamliel’s reasoning: Because he holds that … one who betroths the sister of his yevama, the yevama is exempt and is released, … if he engaged in sexual intercourse … yes, … if he did not engage in intercourse … not

Rav Sheshet said: I say that Rav said this halakha when he was dozing and lying down, … As it is taught … one who betroths a minor girl, her betrothal is in suspension. What … in suspension? Is it not that when she reaches majority, the betrothal reaches majority with her … even if he did not have intercourse with her

Ravin, son of Rav Naḥman, said to … This matter, … of a minor girl remains in suspension, … If he has sexual intercourse … yes, … if he does not engage in intercourse … not … For she says … He has an advantage over me … and I have an advantage over him,

But does Rav … think that … if he has intercourse with her … yes, her … but if he did not engage in intercourse with her, … no, … Wasn’t it stated … a minor who had not refused … and reached majority, and … went and married … Rav said: She does not require a bill of divorce from the second … And Shmuel said: She does require a bill of divorce from the second

What, is it not … where he did not have intercourse … No, … where he did have intercourse with her. … If … where he had intercourse with her, what is Shmuel’s reasoning? … holds that … anyone has sexual intercourse … intention is that the intercourse … the initial betrothal

But … they already disagreed about this once, as it was stated … betrothed … on … condition, and married her without mentioning … Rav says: She requires a bill of divorce from him, and Shmuel says: She does not require a bill of divorce from him.

Rav says she requires a bill of divorce from him, … since he married her, he … retracted his condition, … And Shmuel says: She does not require a bill of divorce from him, … anyone who has sexual intercourse … intention is that the intercourse … the initial betrothal

necessary … for if only that … was stated, … In this case Rav says … since there is a condition … but when he had intercourse … he retracted the condition. But in this … say that … would concede to Shmuel … And if only this … was stated, … Shmuel said that … in this … but in that … say … he would concede to Rav. … necessary

And did Rav … say … when he engaged in sexual intercourse with her, yes, … and if he did not have intercourse with her, no, … Wasn’t there an incident in … Neresh where … was betrothed when she was a minor, and she reached majority, and … seated her in a bridal chair … and another … came and seized her from him … And Rav Bruna and Rav Ḥananel, the students of Rav, were there and they did not require her … a bill of divorce from the latter

Rav Pappa said: … in Neresh their … marry … and afterward they seat her in the bridal chair. … Rav Ashi says: … This … acted improperly. Consequently, they treated him improperly … and the Sages abrogated his betrothal.

Ravina said to Rav Ashi: … works out well if … betrothed her with money, … If he betrothed her by means of intercourse, what … The Sages rendered his sexual act a licentious sexual act, … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Eliezer, … Likewise, Rabbi Elazar said: The halakha is in accordance with … Rabbi Eliezer.

With regard to a gentile, if he intended … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: They taught … only … where he intended to permit … but … he … intended to testify … his testimony is … testimony. … How do we know … Rav Yosef said: … he came to the court and said: So-and-so died, allow his wife to marry, this is … intending to permit … He died, this is … intending to testify.

was also stated … Reish Lakish said: They taught … only when one intended to permit … but if he … intended to testify … his testimony is … testimony. Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him: Didn’t such an incident occur involving … Oshaya the Distinguished, who permitted … with eighty-five Elders? He said to … They taught … only when he intended to permit … but if he … intended to testify … his testimony is … testimony. But the Rabbis did not concur with him

But, … that … is taught … the mishna: With regard to a gentile, if he intended … his testimony is not … testimony, … How can you find … when he speaks offhandedly, … Like that … who was going around saying: Who is … the house of Ḥivvai; who is … the house of Ḥivvai? Ḥivvai has died. And … Rav Yosef allowed … wife to marry. … a certain … who was going around saying: Alas for the brave horseman who was in Pumbedita, for he is dead. And Rav Yosef, and some say Rava, allowed his wife to marry.

a certain … who was going around saying: Who is … the house of Ḥasa? Ḥasa has drowned. Rav Naḥman said: By God! The fish have eaten Ḥasa. … Due to Rav Naḥman’s statement, … Ḥasa’s wife went and married, and no one said anything to her … Rav Ashi said: Learn … from this … That which the Sages said, … an endless body of water, his wife is prohibited … this applies … ab initio, but if … married … we do not take her away from him.

There are … who say … Rav Naḥman … allowed his wife to marry. He said: Ḥasa is a great man; if it was so that he emerged … the incident would have generated publicity. … That is not so. It is not different … a great man … is not different … not a great man. … after the fact, yes, … not … ab initio.

a certain gentile said to a Jew: Harvest the fodder and give it to my animals on Shabbat, and if not, I will kill you like I killed so-and-so the Jew, for I said to him: Cook me a pot … on Shabbat, and he didn’t cook … for me, so I killed him. The wife … heard … and … came before Abaye … He deferred … her
three … Festivals, … Rav Adda bar Ahava said to her: Go before Rav Yosef, whose knife is sharp,

She went before him … he resolved … based on this baraita: … a gentile who was selling fruit at the market and said: These fruits are from the first three years of the tree’s growth [orla]; … they are from Azeka, … are fourth-year produce, … he … said nothing … he intended only to enhance … his goods,

Abba Yudan of Sidon said: An incident … involving a Jew and a gentile who traveled on the road, and … the gentile came and said: Alas for the Jew who was with me on the road, for he died, and I buried him. And … allowed his wife to marry.

And … another incident involving … people who … with a collar [kolar] … were walking to Antokhya. And … a certain gentile came and said: Alas for the … collared people, for they died, and I buried them. And … allowed their wives to marry. And … another incident involving sixty people who were walking to the siege [karkom] of Beitar, and … a gentile came and said: Alas for those sixty people who were walking on the road … Beitar, for they died, and I buried them. And … allowed their wives to marry.

MISHNA: … may testify … by candlelight or by moonlight. And … may allow … to marry based on … a disembodied voice … an incident with regard to a certain … who stood at the top of a mountain and said: So-and-so, son of so-and-so, from such and such a place died. They went and found no person there, but … they … allowed the wife of … to marry.

another incident in Tzalmon, … where a particular … said: I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so. A snake bit me and I am dying. And they went … but could not recognize him, … they went … and allowed his wife to marry

GEMARA: Rabba bar Shmuel said: … taught … Beit Shammai say: … may not allow … to marry based on … a disembodied voice; … And Beit Hillel say: … may allow … to marry based on … a disembodied voice. … What is … teaching us … This is … our mishna, … teaches us this: That if an anonymous … is found … that … may not allow … to marry … it is … Beit Shammai,
they … went and found no … Perhaps it was a demon. Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: They saw that he had the form of a person, … They, … also appear similar … They saw that he had a shadow.

But they also have a shadow. … where they saw that he had a shadow of a shadow. … But perhaps they also have a shadow of a shadow? Rabbi Ḥanina said: Yonatan the demon … said to me: They have a shadow, … they do not have a shadow of a shadow.
And perhaps it was a rival … The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: During a period of danger, one may write and give … although … do not know

MISHNA: Rabbi Akiva said: When I descended to Neharde’a, … to intercalate the year, I found … Neḥemya of Beit D’li. He said to me: I heard that … in Eretz Yisrael do not allow a woman to remarry based on … a single witness, except for Yehuda ben Bava. And I told him: That is so. He said to me: Tell … in my name: You know that the country is confounded by … troops, … I received this tradition from Rabban Gamliel the Elder, that … may allow a woman to remarry based on … a single witness.
And when I came and presented the matter before Rabban Gamliel … he rejoiced at my words and said: We have found a companion … with Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava,

As a result of this event, Rabban Gamliel remembered that people were murdered in Tel Arza, and Rabban Gamliel … allowed their wives to remarry based on … one witness. And … they established … to allow … to remarry based on hearsay testimony, a slave’s testimony, a woman’s testimony, … a maidservant’s testimony. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua say: … may not allow a woman to remarry based on … one witness. Rabbi Akiva says: … not … based on … a woman, nor based on … a slave, nor based on … a maidservant, nor based on … close relatives.

GEMARA: … Does Rabbi Akiva hold … not … based on … woman’s testimony? But isn’t it taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Akiva: A woman is trusted to bring her … bill of divorce … based on … a fortiori … If women, … whom the Sages said are not deemed credible to say … husband died, are … trusted to bring … bills of divorce, … is it not logical that this … who is deemed credible to say … her husband died, should be trusted to bring her … bill of divorce?

it is … the women who the Sages mentioned who are not deemed credible. In general, a woman is deemed credible, … This … not difficult. Here, … before they established … There, … after they established

MISHNA: They said to … an incident occurred involving Levites who traveled to Tzoar, the city of date palms. And one of them became ill, and they brought him to an inn [pundak] … Upon their return … they said to the innkeeper, … Where is our friend? She told them: He died, and I buried him. And … they allowed his wife to remarry. And shouldn’t a priestess, … be … as an innkeeper?
said to them: When … will be as … the innkeeper, … she shall … be deemed credible. The innkeeper brought them his staff, and his bag, and the Torah scroll that was in his possession,

GEMARA: … What … unfavorable … innkeeper … Rav Kahana said: She was a gentile innkeeper, and she was … speaking offhandedly … this is his staff, and this is his bag, and this is the grave in which I buried him. And similarly, Abba, son of Rav Minyumi, son of Ḥiyya, taught: She was a gentile innkeeper, and she was speaking offhandedly, … this is his staff, and this is his bag, and this is the grave in which I buried him.
But didn’t they say to her: Where is our friend? … Once she saw them, she cried. They said to her: Where is our friend? … she said to them: He died, and I buried him.

The Sages taught: An incident … involving a certain … who came to testify before Rabbi Tarfon with regard to a woman … He said to him: My son, how do you come to know testimony … this woman … He said: He and I were traveling on the road … and a troop … chased after us. He hung onto an olive branch, and tore it off … and forced the troop to withdraw.

I said to him, … Lion [arye], may your strength continue to be firm. He said to me: From where do you know that my name is Arye? That is what they call me in my city: Yoḥanan, son of Rabbi Yehonatan, the lion from the village Shiḥayya. After a while, he fell sick and died, … And Rabbi Tarfon allowed his wife to marry

But didn’t Rabbi Tarfon require inquiry and interrogation … Isn’t it taught … An incident … involving a certain person who came before Rabbi Tarfon to present testimony … a woman’s … He said to him: My son, how do you know this testimony? He told him: He and I were traveling on the road … and a troop … chased after us. He hung onto a fig branch, and tore it off, and forced the troop to withdraw … I said to him: May your strength continue to be firm, lion. He said to me: You have intuited my name well, for that is what they call me in my city: Yoḥanan, son of Yonatan, the lion from the village Shiḥayya. … After a while, he fell sick and died.

said to him, … Did you not tell me … Yoḥanan, son of Yonatan, from the village Shiḥayya, … Lion? He replied to him: No. Rather, this is what I told you: … Yoḥanan, son of Yonatan, the lion from the village Shiḥayya. Then … cross-examined him … two or three times, and … kept his statements consistent, so Rabbi Tarfon allowed his wife to marry.
This is … tanna’im, as it is taught … does not examine witnesses … of women by means of … inquiry and interrogation; … the statement of Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Tarfon says: … examine
And they disagree about … Rabbi Ḥanina, as Rabbi Ḥanina said: By Torah law, both … monetary law and … capital law … by means of inquiry and interrogation … as … is stated: “You shall have one law”
And … what reason did the Sages say that … monetary law do not require inquiry and interrogation … So as not to lock the door in the face of … borrowers.

And with regard to what do they disagree … Sage, … holds … since there is the … marriage contract … to take … it is considered … like cases of monetary law … And … Sage, … holds … since, … we permit … married woman to … the world, … it is considered … like … capital law,
Rabbi Elazar said … Rabbi Ḥanina said: Torah scholars increase peace in the world, as it is stated: “And all your children shall be taught of the Lord, and great shall be the peace of your children”
Ketubot: MISHNA: A virgin is married on Wednesday and a widow on Thursday. … that twice a week courts convene in the towns, on Monday and Thursday, … that if … had a claim concerning … virginity … he would go early … to court

GEMARA: Rav Yosef said … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: Due to what … did they say that a virgin is married on Wednesday? … because we learned … If the time … arrived, … and they were not married, … eat from his … and, … eat teruma.
One might think … time arrived on Sunday, … he would provide her sustenance … Therefore, we learned: A virgin is married on Wednesday.

Rav Yosef said … Lord of Abraham, … makes … is taught dependent on … is not taught, … Which is taught and which is not taught? … this … is taught … that … is taught. … Rather, … makes … is taught … whose reason is explicit, dependent on … is taught … whose reason is not explicit.

Rather, if it was stated, this … it was stated: Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: Due to what … did … say … a virgin is married on Wednesday? … that if … had a claim concerning … virginity, he would go early … to court … But … let her marry on Sunday, as … if … had a claim concerning … virginity, he would go early … to court … Sages were assiduous in seeing to the well-being of Jewish women … so that … would exert … in … the … feast for three days: Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday, and on Wednesday, he marries her.

And now that we learned … were assiduous … that … which we learned … If the time arrived and they were not married, … eat from his … and eat teruma, … If … time arrived on Sunday, since … unable to marry … he is not obligated to provide her sustenance
Therefore, … fell ill, or if … fell ill, or … where she began to menstruate [peirsa nidda] … not provide her sustenance

And there are … who raised it as a dilemma: If … fell ill, what is … There, … what is the reason … due to … that he was forced … And here too, isn’t he forced … Or, perhaps … There, he was forced by an ordinance that was instituted by the Sages … However, here, … not
And if you say that if he fell ill, he provides her sustenance … if she fell ill, what is … Can he say to her: I am standing here … Or perhaps she can say to him that his field was inundated,
And if you say that … she … say to him that his field was inundated, … she became a menstruating woman … what is
at the time of her set period [vista], do not raise the dilemma,

as … she cannot say to him … his field was inundated. … When you … raise a dilemma … not at the time of her set period. What … Since it is not the time of her set period, … she can say to him that his field was inundated. Or, perhaps since there are some women whose set period changes, … is like … the time of her set period,
Rav Aḥai resolved … If the time arrived and they were not married, … eat from his … and eat teruma. It doesn’t teach: And … didn’t marry, … Rather, … And … were not married,

What are the circumstances … If the … postpone … why do they eat from his … and eat teruma? Rather, is it not … where they were compelled … in that manner, … and it teaches: … eat from his … and eat teruma,

Rav Ashi said: Actually, I will say to you: In any … of unavoidable circumstances, … she doesn’t eat … and … where … postpone the wedding. And by right, … should have taught: They didn’t marry, … And since … the first clause … in … it taught the latter clause in
Rava said: And … to bills of divorce that is not so. Apparently, Rava maintains that unavoidable circumstances … no … to bills of divorce.

From where does Rava … this … If we say it is from that which we learned … This is your bill of divorce, if I do not return from now until … twelve months, and he died within … twelve months, … is not a bill of divorce. … he died, … is when it is not a bill of divorce, … he fell ill, … it is a bill of divorce
And perhaps, actually I will say to you … he falls ill it is also not a bill of divorce, … And … that … itself … to teach us that there is no bill of divorce posthumously.

there is no bill of divorce posthumously? Wasn’t it … taught in the first clause … This is your bill of divorce if I die, … This is your bill of divorce … from this illness, … This is your bill of divorce after I die, he said nothing.

Perhaps … to exclude that which our Rabbis … as it is taught … And our Rabbis permitted her to remarry, … And we said: Who are our Rabbis … Rav Yehuda said … Shmuel said: … the court that permitted … oil … they hold in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei, who said: The time … in a document proves … it
And rather, … latter clause … from now if I do not return from now until … twelve months, and he died within … twelve months, this … is a bill of divorce. … he dies, … the same is true … he fell ill.
Perhaps … specifically … he died, … he is not amenable … happen before … yavam,

Rather, … from this … where a certain … who said to … If I do not return from now until after thirty days … let this be a bill of divorce. He came at the end of thirty days, … but was prevented … by the ferry … He said to the … See that I have come, see that I have come. Shmuel said: … is not considered … a return.
And perhaps unavoidable circumstances that are common … are different, since he should have stipulated … and he did not stipulate … he brought the failure … upon himself.
Rather, Rava is stating … his own reasoning. … due to virtuous women and due to licentious women. … due to virtuous women … as, if you said: Let it not be a bill of divorce,

sometimes, where he was not … unavoidably … and … thinks … unavoidably, she will sit deserted, … And … due to licentious women … as, if you said: Let it not be a bill of divorce, … sometimes, when he was … unavoidably and she thinks … not … unavoidably, … and remarries. And … that the bill of divorce is void, and her children … mamzerim,
And is there a matter where by Torah … it is not a bill of divorce, but due to virtuous women and due to licentious women we permit a married woman to others?
Yes, … anyone who betroths … betroths … upon the agreement of the Sages, … the Sages invalidated his betrothal
Ravina said to Rav Ashi: … works out well … he betrothed … with money, … he betrothed … with intercourse, what can be said? … The Sages rendered his intercourse licentious intercourse.
Some say, … Rava said: … the same is true with regard to the matter of bills of divorce. … apparently Rava maintains: Unavoidable circumstances … with regard to bills of divorce.

The Gemara raises an objection … This is your bill of divorce if I do not return from now until … twelve months, and he died within … twelve months, … is not a bill of divorce. … he died, … is when it is not a bill of divorce, … he fell ill … it is a bill of divorce
Actually, I will say to you … one falls ill it is also not a bill of divorce, … And … that … itself teaches us that there is no bill of divorce posthumously.
there is no bill of divorce posthumously? Wasn’t it already taught in the first clause … Perhaps … to exclude … of our Rabbis.

Come and hear … from now if I have not returned from now until … twelve months, and he died within … twelve months, … this … is a bill of divorce. What, is it not that the same is true … he fell ill? … specifically … he died, … he was not amenable … happen before … yavam,

Come and hear … from … a certain … who said to … If I do not return from now until thirty days … let this be a bill of divorce. He came at the end of thirty days, … but was prevented … by the ferry … He said to the … See that I have come, see that I have come. Shmuel said: … is not considered … a return.
Perhaps unavoidable circumstances that are common … are different, since he should have stipulated … And … stipulate … he brought the failure upon himself.

Rav Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said: … teach … only from … the ordinance of Ezra that courts are in regular session only on Monday and Thursday. However, prior to … the ordinance of Ezra, when courts … regular … every day, a woman was married on any day
Prior to … the ordinance of Ezra? What was … was … This is what … is saying: If there are courts … regular … today, as … prior to … the ordinance of Ezra, a woman is married on any day
Don’t we require … were assiduous … where he … exerted himself

What is … were assiduous? … as it is taught … Due to what … did … say … a virgin is married on Wednesday? … that if … had a claim concerning … virginity, he would go early … to court … But … let her marry on Sunday, as … if … had a claim concerning … virginity, he would go early … to court … were assiduous in seeing to the well-being of Jewish women … so that … would exert … in … the … feast for three days, Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, and on Wednesday, he marries her.

And from … danger and onward, the people adopted the custom to marry on Tuesday … and the Sages did not reprimand them. And on Monday one may not marry … However, if it is due to the coercion, … permitted. … One isolates the groom from the … bride, … first … on Shabbat evening, because … he inflicts a wound,
What is … danger … If we say … said that a virgin who is married on Wednesday will be executed, … that they adopted the custom … Let them … abolish

Rabba said: … said that a virgin who is married on Wednesday will … intercourse with the prefect [hegmon] first. … Is that … danger? It is coercion. … as there are virtuous women who give their lives … and they will come to … danger.
And … let … instruct … that … coercion … permitted … there are licentious women … And … there are also … priests,

And let … abolish … A decree of religious persecution [shemada] is likely to be abrogated, and we do not abolish a rabbinic ordinance in the face of a decree of religious persecution. … If so, … will come on Tuesday too, … for … uncertainty … uproot himself

And on Monday one may not marry … However, if it is due to the coercion, it is permitted. … What is … coercion … If we say it is referring to that which we mentioned … there … calls it danger, and here he calls it coercion. Furthermore, there … adopted the custom … here … permitted.

Rava said: … where they said: A general … are coming to the city … What are the circumstances? If … where … comes and passes … let … postpone … Rather, it is necessary … where he comes and establishes … In any case, let one marry on Tuesday. … his entourage [asperava] arrives on Tuesday.

And if you wish, say … What is … Due to the coercion? … as it is taught … If one’s bread was baked, and his animal slaughtered, and his wine diluted, … and the father of the groom or the mother of the bride died … one moves the corpse into a room, and the bride and groom … to the wedding canopy

And … engages in intercourse … mitzva, and … withdraws … And … observes the seven days of … feast, … and thereafter he observes the seven days of mourning. And throughout those days … sleeps among the men, and … sleeps among the women, … And … one does not withhold jewels from the bride … entire thirty-day
And … specifically … the father of … groom or the mother of … bride … as … there is no … person who … exert … for them. … However, … the opposite … no,
Rafram bar Pappa said … Rav Ḥisda said: … taught … only if one … placed water on the meat. … However, if he did not place water on the meat, it … sold.

Rava said: And in a city, … even if he placed water on the meat it … sold, … Rav Pappa said: And in a village, even if he did not place water on the meat, it cannot … sold, … Where do you find … of Rav Ḥisda … Rav Ashi says: … like … Mata Meḥasya, which is removed from … a city, … and removed from … a village,

taught in accordance … Rav Ḥisda: If one’s bread was baked, and his animal slaughtered, and his wine diluted, and he placed water on the meat, and the father of the groom or the mother of the bride died, one moves the corpse into a room, and the bride and groom … to the wedding canopy, … engages in intercourse … mitzva, … withdraws … And … observes the seven days of … feast, and thereafter observes the seven days of mourning. And throughout those days … sleeps among the men, and his wife sleeps among the women,

And likewise, … whose wife began to menstruate … he sleeps among the men and she sleeps among the women, … However, … do not withhold jewels from the bride … entire thirty-day … In any event, the … may not engage in intercourse … neither on Shabbat evening, … nor … conclusion of Shabbat.

The Master said: He sleeps among the men and she sleeps among the women. … supports … of Rabbi Yoḥanan, as Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Although they stated that there is no mourning … on a Festival, yet one observes matters of privacy,
Rav Yosef, son of Rava, taught in the name of Rava: They taught … only if he did not engage in intercourse … However, if he engaged in intercourse … his wife sleeps with him,
But here, … we are dealing … where he … engaged in intercourse … and … teaches: He sleeps among the men and she sleeps among the women. … When he states … concerning … his wife began menstruating,
doesn’t it state: And likewise,
This is what … is saying: And likewise, … whose wife began to menstruate, and he had not … engaged in intercourse … he sleeps among the men, and his wife sleeps among the women.
Is that to say that … mourning is more lenient in his … than … a menstruating woman?

But didn’t Rav Yitzḥak bar Ḥanina say … Rav Huna said: All tasks that a woman … performs for her husband, a menstruating woman performs for her husband, except for pouring … cup; arranging … bed; and washing his face, hands, and feet, … Whereas with regard to mourning, it is taught … Although they said that a man may not compel his … wife, to paint … blue or to rouge [pokeset] … in truth they said that she may pour … the cup; arrange his bed; and wash his face, hands, and feet.
not difficult. Here, … in … mourning; there, … in … mourning.
But isn’t it taught … The father of the groom and the mother of the bride? … When … teaches … concerning the rest

And do … distinguish between his mourning and her mourning? But isn’t it taught … one whose father-in-law or mother-in-law died, he may not compel his wife to paint … blue or to rouge … Rather, he overturns his bed, … and observes … mourning … with her. And likewise, if … father-in-law or mother-in-law dies, she is not allowed to paint … blue or to rouge … Rather, she overturns her bed and observes … mourning … with him.

Teach with regard to his mourning: He sleeps among the men and his wife sleeps among the women. … doesn’t … teach: And likewise? … When … teaches … painting and rouge. … doesn’t … teach: With him? What, … it not … with him … in bed, … No, … with him at home, and … as that which Rav said to Ḥiyya, his son, … Before her, observe mourning … not before her, do not observe mourning

Rav Ashi said … Can you compare the mourning here with mourning in general? Mourning in general is stringent, and one will not come to take it lightly. … mourning here, … since the Sages were lenient, one will come to take it lightly.

What leniency … If we say … which … teaches: … engages in … intercourse … mitzva … withdraws … there, … due to … that mourning has not yet taken effect upon him. … If … Rabbi Eliezer, … until the … emerges from the entrance of the house … If … Rabbi Yehoshua, … until the covering of the grave is sealed.
Rather, … which … teaches: … observes the seven days of feast … and thereafter he observes the seven days of mourning.

The Master said … In any event, the … may not engage in intercourse … neither on Shabbat evening, nor … conclusion of Shabbat. Granted, on Shabbat evening … due to the … a wound … However, at the conclusion of Shabbat, why … not
Rabbi Zeira said:
due to calculations

Abaye said to him: And are calculations for a mitzva prohibited … But wasn’t it Rav Ḥisda and Rav Hamnuna who both said: … calculations for a mitzva, … permitted to reckon them on Shabbat? And Rabbi Elazar said: One may allocate charity to the poor on Shabbat. And Rabbi Ya’akov said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One goes to synagogues and study halls to supervise matters … multitudes on Shabbat. And Rabbi Ya’akov bar Idi said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One supervises matters of saving a life on Shabbat.

And Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yonatan said: One goes to theaters [tartiyyaot] and circuses [karkiyyaot] to supervise matters … multitudes on Shabbat, … And … of the school of Menashya taught: … makes matches [meshadkhin] … for a young girl to be betrothed on Shabbat, and … for a young boy to teach him Torah and to teach him a craft.

Rather, Rabbi Zeira said: It is a decree lest one slaughter a young fowl on … Abaye said to him: If … so, Yom Kippur that occurs on Monday should be postponed … a decree lest one slaughter a young fowl … There, … for himself, he is not preoccupied, … Here, … for others … preoccupied. Alternatively, there, … he has an interval … Here, he does not have an interval
Now that we have come to this … Shabbat evening, too, … a decree lest one slaughter a young fowl

raises a dilemma: Is a virgin married on Wednesday and … engage in intercourse on … Wednesday, and we are not concerned … his resolve … cool … Or perhaps, a virgin is married on Wednesday but engages in intercourse on Thursday, as we are concerned that his resolve will cool.

Come and hear … as bar Kappara taught: A virgin is married on Wednesday and engages in intercourse on Thursday, since the blessing to the fish: … was stated … A widow is married on Thursday and engages in intercourse on Friday, since the blessing … was stated to man … the reason is due to the blessing, but with regard to … his resolve cool, we are not concerned.
If so, a widow should also engage in intercourse on Thursday, since the blessing to the fish was stated then. … the blessing of man … is preferable for him.

Alternatively, … due to … were assiduous … as it is taught … Why did … say that a widow is married on Thursday and engages in intercourse on Friday? … because if you say that she should engage in intercourse on Thursday, on the next day … go to … his craft early … the Sages were assiduous in seeing to the well-being of Jewish women … that … rejoice with her … three days: Thursday, … and Shabbat eve, … and Shabbat.
What … is there between … blessing … and … were assiduous? … There is … between them … an idle person, … Alternatively, … a Festival that occurs on Shabbat eve.

Bar Kappara taught: The handiwork of the righteous is greater than the creation of heaven and earth, as with regard to the creation of heaven and earth it is written: “My hand also has laid the foundation of the earth, and My right hand has spanned the heavens” … Whereas with regard to the handiwork of the righteous it is written: “The place which You have made for Yourself to dwell in, Lord, the Sanctuary, Lord, which your hands have established” (Exodus 15:17).
