Now that you have arrived at this … you … even say … Rabbi Shimon, … of the Rabbis, … remove three … for guests and wayfarers, … of Rabbi Ḥidka, … remove two … for guests and wayfarers.

Rabbi Yosei said: Only … allotted her barley. … But … it is … in Edom that they eat barley, … in the rest of the world they do not eat … This is what … is saying: Only Rabbi Yishmael, who was near Edom, allotted her a double … of barley … of wheat, since Edomite barley is bad,
And he … give her half a kav … legumes … And yet wine is not taught … This supports … of Rabbi Elazar, as Rabbi Elazar said:

Wines are not allotted to a wife. And if you say … “I will go after my lovers who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink” … items that a woman desires [mishtokeket]. And what are these? Jewelry

Rabbi Yehuda of the village of Neviraya, and some say of the village of Nefor Ḥayil, interpreted … From where … that one does not allot wines for a woman? As it is stated: “So Hannah rose up after she had eaten in Shiloh and after he had drunk” … “He had drunk,” and not: She had drunk.

However, if that is so, … “she had eaten,” … indeed … and … he did not eat? … We say … from … that the verse changed its language. Since … was already dealing with her, what is the reason … changed … learn from this … “he had drunk” … but she did not drink.

raises an objection … accustomed … she is given … accustomed … is different, as Rav Ḥinnana bar Kahana said … Shmuel said: … accustomed … she is given one cup, … is not accustomed … she is given two cups.

What is … saying? … Abaye said: This is what … is saying: … she is accustomed … in the presence of her husband … two cups, … is not in the presence of her husband she is given one cup. … she is not accustomed … in the presence of her husband … only one cup, … is not in the presence of her husband she is not given … at all.

And if you wish, say … she is accustomed … she is given … for … pudding [tzikei], … in a pot. As Rabbi Abbahu said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: An incident … involving the daughter-in-law of Nakdimon ben Guryon, … The Sages apportioned for her … two se’a … wine for pudding, from one Shabbat eve to another. She said to them, … So may you apportion for your … daughters … taught: She was a widow waiting for her yavam, and … the Sages did not answer amen after her

taught … One cup … good for a woman; two … is a disgrace, … three … verbally request … four … even request … a donkey in the marketplace, as … she is not particular … Rava said: They taught … only if her husband is not with her. However, … her husband is with her, we have no … with it.

But … Hannah was … in which her husband was with her, … a guest is different, as Rav Huna said: From where … that a guest is prohibited from … conjugal relations? As it is stated: “And they rose up in the morning early, and worshipped before the Lord, and returned, and came to their house to Ramah; and Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and the Lord remembered her” … now, … yes, … at the outset, … no,

Abaye’s wife, Ḥoma, came before Rava … She said to him: Apportion sustenance for me, … apportioned … for her. … Apportion wine for me … said to her: I know that Naḥmani, … did not drink wine. … She said to him: By the Master’s life, … he would give … to drink in cups [shufrazei] as large as this. … While she was showing him … her arm became uncovered, … a light had shined in the courtroom.

Rava arose, went home, … requested … from … daughter of Rav Ḥisda. … daughter of Rav Ḥisda said to him: Who was … now in the courtroom? … He said to her: Ḥoma, Abaye’s wife, … went after … struck her with the lock of a chest [kulpei deshida] until she drove her out of the entire … Meḥoza, saying to her: You have … killed three … and … you come to kill another

The wife of Rav Yosef, son of Rava, came before Rav Neḥemya, son of Rav Yosef, … She said to him: Apportion sustenance for me. … apportioned … for her. She said to him: Apportion wine for me … He apportioned … for her. He said to her: I know that the residents of Meḥoza … drinking wine,

the wife of Rav Yosef, son of Rav Menashya of D’vil, came before Rav Yosef. She said to him: Apportion sustenance for me. He apportioned … for her. … Apportion wine for me. He apportioned … for her. … Apportion silk … for me. … said to her: Why … silk … She said to him: For you, for your friends, and for your friends’ friends.
And he … give her a bed, a soft mat, … Why does he … to give her a soft mat and … mat … Rav Pappa said: … of a place where it is the custom to fill a bed with ropes. Because … age [mevager] her,

The Sages taught: One does not give … a pillow and a cushion. In the name of Rabbi Natan, they said: One … give her a pillow and a cushion. … What are the circumstances? If it is her … manner … what is the reason for … the first tanna … And if it is not her … manner, what is the reason for … Rabbi Natan?

No, … necessary … where … his manner … but … not her manner. The first tanna holds … says to her: When I go away … I will take … and when I come … I will bring it with me. And Rabbi Natan holds … she … say to him: Sometimes it happens … at twilight and you are unable to bring it … and you … take my … and you … make me lie on the ground.
And he … give her a cap, … Rav Pappa said to Abaye:

This tanna … left naked but wearing shoes, … said to him: The tanna is standing, … a mountainous region, in which she cannot do without three pairs of shoes, … And in passing, … teaches us that he should give them to her on a Festival, so that she will rejoice in them

And he … give her clothes … of fifty dinars. Abaye said: … fifty simple [peshitei] dinars, … From where … From … that it teaches: In what … is this statement said? … with … the poorest of Jews. However, … of a prominent man, all … in accordance with his prominence. And if it enters your mind … literally fifty dinars, from where … a poor man … fifty dinars? … Rather, learn from this … fifty simple dinars.

And he may not give her new … The Sages taught: Leftover sustenance … to the husband, … leftover, worn clothes … to the wife. … worn clothes … to the wife, why … she … Raḥava said: … as she covers herself with them during her days of menstruation, so that she does not become repulsive to her husband.
Abaye said: We have a tradition … leftover, worn clothes … a widow … to … heirs. … it is … there, … so that she does not become repulsive to her husband … here, … let her become repulsive.
he gives her a silver ma’a, … What is … She eats, … Rav Naḥman said: … literally … she eats … Rav Ashi said: … sexual relations.

The mishna states: And she eats with him … Shabbat evening … Granted, according to the one who says … eating, this … is … that which is taught: She eats. However, according to the one who says … sexual relations, what is … She eats? … a euphemism, as it is written: … she eats, and wipes her mouth, and says: I have done no wickedness”

raises an objection: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says, … She eats on Shabbat evening and … Shabbat. Granted, according to the one who says … eating, this … is … that which is taught: And Shabbat, … However, according to the one who says … sexual relations, are there sexual relations on … Shabbat? But didn’t Rav Huna say: The Jewish people are holy and … do not engage in sexual relations during the day? … Rava said: … in a dark house, it is permitted

And if she is nursing, … Rabbi Ulla the Great taught at the entrance to the house of the Nasi: Although … said … a person is not … to sustain his sons and daughters when they are young, still, he … sustain the very young ones.
Until when … Until the age of six, in accordance with … Rav Asi, as Rav Asi said: A six-year-old minor may go out by … his mother’s eiruv,

From where … from … that it teaches: If she is nursing, … is reduced from her earnings and is added … for her sustenance. What is the reason … not because … needs to eat … with her? … But perhaps … because she is … ill

If so, let … teach: If she was ill. What … If she was nursing? … But perhaps … teaches us this, … ordinary … nursing women are … ill, … It was stated … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Wine is added for … as wine is good for milk.
MISHNA: … object found by a wife and … earnings … to her husband. And … her inheritance, … enjoys the profits … in her lifetime. … her humiliation and her degradation, … to her.

Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says: When … that … in a concealed … she … two parts, … and … one … And when … that … in an exposed … he … two parts, … and she … one … His … should be given … immediately. And … her … land should be purchased with it, and he enjoys the profits

GEMARA: … What is … teaching us? We … learned … the father is entitled, in … his daughter, to … her betrothal, … with money, with a document, or through sexual intercourse. … is entitled to … object … she finds, and to her earnings, and to … nullification of her vows … receives her bill of divorce … but he does not enjoy the profits … in her lifetime. … she is married, the … husband are greater than his, as … enjoys the profits … in her lifetime.
was necessary for … her humiliation and her degradation, … a dispute between Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira and the Rabbis.
A tanna teaches … before Rava: … object found by a wife … to her; Rabbi Akiva says … to her husband. … said to … Now, if, … surplus
which is … her earnings … Rabbi Akiva says … to her, … objects … she found, … not all the more so

as we learned … that I produce … konam, … to your mouth, he need not nullify … Rabbi Akiva says: He should nullify … lest she produce surplus … more than … is fitting for him, … Rather, reverse … objects found by a wife … to her husband; Rabbi Akiva says: … to her.

But when Ravin came … didn’t … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: With regard to surplus that is not … through … effort, everyone agrees that it is … husband’s. Where they disagree … of surplus that is … through … effort. The first tanna holds … to her husband, and Rabbi Akiva holds … to her. … Rav Pappa said: … object found by … comparable to surplus that is … through … effort, … dispute between Rabbi Akiva and the Rabbis.
Rav Pappa raises a dilemma: … she performed two … for him simultaneously, what is … Ravina raises a dilemma: … three or four … simultaneously, what is … shall stand

her humiliation and … her degradation … Rava bar Rav Ḥanan strongly objects to this: If that is so … humiliated another’s horse, … that also … is required to give him … humiliation? … And … a horse subject to humiliation? … Rather, … if one spat on another’s clothing, … that also … be required to give him … humiliation?

And if you would say … indeed … but didn’t we learn … he spat … and the saliva reached him, or … he uncovered a woman’s head, or … he removed his garment from … he is obligated to give him … four hundred dinars, … And Rav Pappa said: They taught … only … his … However, … his garment, … exempt. … on one’s garment, he does not … dishonor, … one’s wife … she … dishonor,

Ravina said to Rav Ashi: However, if that is so, … one humiliated a poor person of noble descent, where there is dishonor for all members of the family, … also that he is required to give … humiliation to all members of the family? … said to him … There, … not … they themselves … Here, … one’s wife is … his own self,
MISHNA: … one who pledges … money for his son-in-law … and his son-in-law dies … The Sages said: … can say … To your brother, I wanted to give … but to you I do not want to give
pledged to bring in for him one thousand dinars … he … pledges, … fifteen hundred dinars against them. … And against … appraisal … he pledges one-fifth less

appraisal … at one hundred dinars and … is … worth one hundred dinars, … he has … only one hundred dinars. … appraisal … one hundred dinars … she is giving thirty-one sela and … dinar, … And … four hundred … she is giving five hundred, … what
son-in-law pledges … he pledges one-fifth less

GEMARA: … The Sages taught: Needless to say, … first … a Torah scholar and … second … an ignoramus, … But even … first … an ignoramus and … second … a Torah scholar, … may say: To your brother, I wanted to give … to you I do not want to give

pledged to bring him one thousand … These … are the same as the first clause of the mishna, … teaches … a large appraisal … and he … teaches … a small appraisal … teaches … appraisal … and he … teaches … appraisal

MISHNA: … she pledged to bring him money … her sela, … becomes six … groom accepts upon himself … ten … to the account … for each and every hundred dinars … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Everything … in accordance with the regional custom.
GEMARA: … This is … he pledges against them fifteen hundred dinars.

taught … large … capital … taught … small … capital. And … necessary … because if he taught … large capital, which … abundant profit, … However, … small capital, which … small profit, … say … not … necessary … And … if … taught us … small capital, … because … little expense, … However, … large capital, … which … abundant expense, … say … not … necessary
son-in-law accepts upon himself … ten dinars to the account. … What … account? Rav Ashi said: … an account … of perfumes … And Rav Ashi said: This statement was said only … in Jerusalem,
Rav Ashi raises a dilemma: … of … hundred dinars that are appraised … or of … hundred dinars that are accepted

If you say … hundred dinars that is accepted, … first day or … each day? If you say … every day, … first week … or each week? If you say … each week, … first month or each month? If you say … each month, … first year … or each year? … shall stand

Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: … an incident involving … daughter of Nakdimon ben Guryon. When the Sages designated for her four hundred gold … for her account of perfumes, … for … on that same day, she … said to them: This … you … pledge for your … daughters, and they answered after her: Amen.

The Sages taught: … an incident involving Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai. When he was riding on a donkey and leaving Jerusalem, and his students were walking after him … he saw a certain young woman who was gathering barley from among the dung of the animals of Arabs. … When she saw him, she wrapped herself in her hair, … stood before him.

She said to him: My teacher, sustain me. … he said to her: My daughter, who are you? She said to him: I am … daughter of Nakdimon ben Guryon. He said to her: My daughter, the money of your father’s household, where did … go? … She said to him: My teacher, is it not … say such a proverb in Jerusalem: Salt for money is lacking [ḥaser]? … And some say … kindness [ḥesed] … And … of your father-in-law’s house, … where is it? She said to him: This one came and destroyed that one;

She said to him: My teacher, … you remember when you signed on my marriage contract? He said to his students: I remember that when I signed on the marriage contract of this … and I read in it, … a thousand thousands, … gold dinars … from her father’s house, aside from that … from her father-in-law. Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai cried and said: How fortunate are you, Israel, … when … performs the will of … Omnipresent, no nation or tongue … rule over them; and when … does not perform the will of the Omnipresent, He delivers them into the hand of a lowly nation. Not … into the hand of a lowly nation, but even into the hand of the animals of a lowly nation,
And did not Nakdimon ben Guryon perform charity? Isn’t it taught … They said about Nakdimon ben Guryon … when he would leave his home … to the study hall, … fine woolen garments … would

spread underneath him … and … the poor … come and fold them up from behind him … If you wish, say that he acted … for his own honor, … And if you wish, say that as he should have done, he did not do. As people say, according to the camel … the burden.

It is taught … Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, said … I will … see the consolation … if I did not see her gathering barley … from between the hooves of horses in Akko. I recited this verse about her: “If you know not, O you fairest among women, go your way forth by the footsteps of the flock and feed your kids, … Do not read … “your kids [gediyotayikh]” but rather … your bodies [geviyotayikh].

Rav Shemen bar Abba said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … she brings him gold … appraises it, and it is … according to its value, … raises an objection … the gold is like utensils … What, is it not … like … which diminish, … No, … like utensils of gold, which do not diminish. … If so, … should have … like its … utensils,

And moreover, … It is taught … gold is like utensils … gold … are like silver … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: In a place where … were accustomed not to exchange them, … appraises them, and they are … at their appraised worth, … To which … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel … If we say … on the latter clause … by inference … that the first tanna holds … even in a place where … were accustomed not to exchange them. But they are not used

Rather, is it not … on the first clause … and this is what … is saying: … gold is like utensils. What … utensils? Utensils of silver. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel … says: … it is like gold … in a place where they are accustomed not to exchange it

No, actually … on the latter clause … and … because they are used … with difficulty. … And … they disagree about this: … Sage, … holds since they are used … we increase … for … And … Sage, … holds since they are used … only with difficulty, we do not increase … for her.

If you wish, say … entire … is … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and … is incomplete and this … it is teaching: … gold is like utensils … gold dinars are like money. In what … is this statement said? In a place where … accustomed to exchange the … However, in a place where the … accustomed not to exchange the … appraises their … and they are … at their appraised worth. … the statement of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, as Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: In a place where the … accustomed not to exchange them, … appraises their … and they are … at their appraised worth.
in any case, … should have … like its … utensils … difficult. If you wish, say … With what are we dealing here? With smashed gold … Rav Ashi said: … with granules
Rabbi Yannai said: … spices in Antioch, … are like money. … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: … camels in Arabia, a woman may collect … marriage settlement from them.

Rav Pappi said: … those robes in Bei Mikhsei, a woman may collect … marriage settlement from them … And Rav Pappi said: … these sacks in Rodya and ropes in Kimḥonya, a woman may collect … marriage settlement from them. Rava said: Initially, I would have said … those money pouches [arnakei] in Meḥoza, a woman may collect … from them. What is the reason? They rely on them, … Once I saw that they take them and … are used, and when they find land they buy … with them … I said … rely on land.

MISHNA: … one who marries … his daughter … unspecified, he must not give her less than fifty dinars. … pledged to bring her … bare, … the husband should not say: When I bring her into my house, I will clothe her with my clothing, … Rather, he must clothe her while she is yet in her father’s house, … And similarly, … who marries … an orphan girl, … must not give her less than fifty dinars. If there are … in the … fund, … provide … for her, … according to her dignity.

GEMARA: Abaye said: … fifty dinars … provincial … From where … From … that the latter clause teaches: If there are … in the … fund, … provide … for her, … according to her dignity. And we say: What is … fund? Raḥava said: … charity fund. And if it enters our minds … fifty actual, … dinars, if there are … in the fund, how many … do we give him? … Rather, conclude from this … fifty provincial dinars.

The Sages taught: … an orphan boy and an orphan girl who have come … to be supported … provide for the orphan girl … and afterward … provide for the orphan boy. … because it is the way of a man to circulate about the entryways … and it is not a woman’s way to circulate … an orphan boy and orphan girl
who have come … to be married … marry … the orphan girl … and afterward … marry … the orphan boy, because the humiliation of a woman … is greater than that of … man.

The Sages taught: … an orphan … who has come to marry, … rent a house for him, arrange for him a bed and all his utensils, and thereafter … marry him a wife, as it is stated: … sufficient for his deficiency in that which is deficient for him” … “sufficient for his deficiency,” this … the house. “Which is deficient”; this … bed and table. “For him [lo]”; this … a wife. And similarly … states: “I will make him [lo] a helpmate for him”

the Sages taught: “Sufficient for his deficiency”; … you are commanded with respect to … to support him, but you are not commanded with respect to him to make him wealthy, … “Which is deficient for him”; … even a horse upon which to ride and a servant to run in front of him … They said about Hillel the Elder that he obtained for a poor person of noble descent a horse upon which to ride and a servant to run in front of him. One time he did not find a servant to run in front of him, and … ran in front of him … three mil,

The Sages taught: … an incident involving the people of the Upper Galilee, who bought for a poor person of noble descent from … Tzippori a litra of meat every day. … a litra of meat, what is the novelty … Rav Huna said: … a litra of meat of poultry, … And if you wish, say … for … a litra … actual … meat. … Rav Ashi said … there, … it was a small village, … every day they would lose … animal … for him.

A certain … came before Rabbi Neḥemya … He said to him: On what do you … dine? He said to him: … on fatty meat and aged wine. … Is it your wish to belittle yourself … with me in … lentils, … He partook with him of lentils, and he died, … said: Woe to this one who was killed … Neḥemya. … On the contrary, … should have said: Woe to Neḥemya who killed this one. … Rather, … he, … who should not have pampered himself so

A certain person came before Rava … He said to him: On what do you … dine? He said to him: On a fattened hen and aged wine. He said to him: And were you not concerned for … a burden to the community … He said to him: Is that to say … from their … I eat? I eat from … the Merciful One. … as we … learned … “the eyes of all wait for You, and You give them their food in its time” … At their time, is … stated, rather “in its time.” … teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives each and every one his … sustenance at its proper time,

In the meantime, … Rava’s sister, who had not seen him for thirteen years, came. And … she brought him a fattened hen and aged wine. Rava said … What is this that … in front of me … said to him: I have responded [na’aneti] to your … Arise … eat.

The Sages taught: … does not have … and does not want to be supported … provide him … as a loan … and … go back and give … to him as a gift; … the statement of Rabbi Meir. And the Rabbis say: … give him … as a gift, and … go back and give … to him as a loan. … as a gift? … he does not … take it … Rava said: … to begin … with him … as a gift.

he has … but does not want to support himself … give him … as a gift, and then … go back and collect … from him. … go back and collect from him? … subsequently he would not take … Rav Pappa said: … after … death. … Rabbi Shimon says, … he has … and does not want to be supported … do not get involved with him, … he does not have and does not want to be supported … say to him: Bring collateral and take … so that his mindset should be raised for him,

The Sages taught … “Ha’avet”; this … who does not have … and does not want to be supported … that … provide him … as a loan and go back and give … to him as a gift. “Ta’avitenu”; this … who has … and does not want to support … that … provide … as a gift, and then … go back and collect from … after … death. … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Rabbis say: … he has … and does not want to support … do not get involved with him. … How then do I uphold … “ha’avet ta’avitenu”? … The Torah spoke in the language of men,

Mar Ukva … a pauper in his neighborhood, … was accustomed every day to toss four dinars for him into the … hinge of the door. One day … said: I will go … see who is doing this service for me. That day Mar Ukva was delayed in the study hall, … his wife came with him

When … saw that … was turning the door, … went out after them … ran … from before him … they entered a certain furnace whose fire was … raked … Mar Ukva’s legs were being singed, … his wife said to him: Raise your legs and set them on my legs, … became distraught. … she said to him: I am … found inside the house, and … my assistance is ready

And what … all this? … as Mar Zutra bar Toviya said … Rav said, and some say … Rav Huna bar Bizna said … Rabbi Shimon Ḥasida said, and some say … Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: It is preferable for a person to deliver himself into a fiery furnace so that … not whiten … face … his friend in public. From where do we … From the … Tamar, as it is written: … she was brought forth,

Mar Ukva … pauper in his neighborhood, … was accustomed to send to him four hundred dinars every … eve of Yom Kippur. One day he sent … to him by the hand of his son. … returned … said to him: … does not need … said: What did you see … I saw them spilling old wine … for him, … said: … pampered this much … He doubled … and sent them to him.

When … was dying, he said: Bring me my charity records. He found that it was written there … seven thousand … siankei, … dinars, … He said: My provisions are light, and the way is far. … He got up … spent half … his … money … How did he do this? But didn’t Rabbi Ilai say: In Usha they instituted: One who spends … he should not spend more than one-fifth … This … applies … while he is alive, … perhaps he will descend from his holdings … But after death, we have no … with it.
Rabbi Abba would wrap coins in his scarf and toss … behind him … And … would place himself at the homes of the poor … And he would incline his eyes … from swindlers

Rabbi Ḥanina … a certain pauper … was accustomed to send to him four dinars … every Shabbat eve. One day he sent it in the hand of his wife. She came … said to him: … does not need … What did you see … I heard them saying to him … With what do you … dine:

Silver, … tablecloths [telei] or gold, … tablecloths? … said: This is what Rabbi Elazar said: Come and let us appreciate the swindlers … because were it not … them, … we would be sinning every day … as it is stated: … and he cry to the Lord against you, and it be sin in you”

And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Rav of Difti taught: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa says: … anyone who averts his eyes from the … charity, … is as if he engages in idol worship. … written here … “Beware that there be not a base [beliya’al] thought in your heart … and … written there … “Certain base [beliya’al] fellows … gone out” … Just as there, … idol worship, so too here, … idol worship.

The Sages taught: One who … blinds his eye, and one who bloats his stomach … and one who … crushes [mekape’aḥ] his leg, … will not depart from the world before he comes to this … one who receives charity and does not need it, his end … he will not depart from the world before he comes to this

We learned in a mishna elsewhere … do not require him to sell his house and his accessories … And … not … But isn’t it taught … he was … use gold wares, he should … use silver wares. … silver wares, … copper wares.

Rav Zevid said: This … not difficult. This … of a bed and a table, … that … of … cups and plates. … What is different … cups and plates, that … not … because he says: … disgusting to me, … a bed and a table … also say: I do not accept … upon myself, … Rava, son of Rabba, said: … of a silver comb
Rav Pappa said: This … not difficult. Here, … before he comes to … collecting … There, … after he comes to … collecting

MISHNA: … orphan girl whose mother or brothers married her off, … with her consent … And … wrote for her … of one hundred or of fifty dinars, she may, upon reaching majority, exact from … that is fit to be given to her

Rabbi Yehuda says: If … married off the first daughter … should be given to the second … in the same manner that he gave … to the first … And the Rabbis say: … sometimes a person … poor and … becomes wealthy, or … wealthy … becomes poor, … Rather, … appraises the property and gives her

GEMARA: Shmuel said: … to … support … evaluates … based on … the father … raises an objection: … The daughters are sustained and supported from the property of their father. How so? We do not … say: If her father were … alive, he would give her such and such … Rather, … appraises the … property and gives her … What, is it not … support … the husband, … Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: No, … to her own support

And Rabbi Eliezer further said: … may broach … by … a new situation, but the Rabbis prohibit … How … said: It is … like an offering [konam] that I will … derive benefit from so-and-so, and … became a scribe [sofer], … or if … was marrying off his son … and … said: Had I known that he would become a scribe, or that he would be marrying off his son in the near … I would not have vowed.
Entering this house is konam … and … became a synagogue, … he said: Had I known that it would become a synagogue, I would not have vowed, … Rabbi Eliezer permits … and the Rabbis prohibit
GEMARA: … What … there are no vows, … Abaye said: … If so, vows are not dissolved properly.
And Rava said: … If so, there are no requests … of vows to a halakhic authority.

We learned … And the Rabbis concede to Rabbi Eliezer with regard to … a matter that is between him and his father and mother, that … may broach … with him by … the honor of his father and mother. Granted, according to Abaye, who said: If so, vows are not dissolved … here, since he was impudent toward him … he was impudent toward him

But according to Rava, who said: If so, there are no requests … to a halakhic authority, here, … why … broach … say … Since it is not sufficient … for all vows not … a halakhic authority, … here too, … may broach

And Rabbi Eliezer further said: … may broach … by … a new situation, … What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer? Rav Ḥisda said: For the verse states … “For all the men are dead … But death is a new circumstance, … from here that … may broach … by … a new situation.

And … the Rabbis, what is their reason … They hold: These … had they … died? But Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: Wherever it is stated … striving … or standing … they are none other than Dathan and Abiram. … Rather, Reish Lakish said: … that they lost their property

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Any person who does not have children is considered like a dead … as is stated … “Give me children, or else I am dead” … And it was taught … Four are considered as … dead: A pauper, and a leper, and a blind … and one who has no children. A pauper, as it is written: “For all the men are dead” … A leper, as it is written … “Let her not, I pray, be as one dead” … And a blind … as it is written: “He has made me to dwell in dark places, as those that have been long dead” … And one who has no children, as it is written: “Give me children, or else I am dead”

It is taught … one prohibited by a vow from deriving benefit from another, they dissolve … for him only in the presence … From where are these matters … Rav Naḥman said: As it is written: “And the Lord said to Moses in Midian: Go, return to Egypt; for all the men are dead” … said to him: In Midian you vowed … go and dissolve your vow in Midian. … For it is written: “And Moses was content [vayo’el] … ala means nothing other than an oath, as it is written: “And he…brought him under an oath [ala]”

“And he also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God” … What … his rebellion? … Zedekiah found Nebuchadnezzar eating a live rabbit, … He said to him: Take an oath to me that you will not reveal my … and this matter will not emerge … took an oath

He said to them: Can one request … of an oath? They said to him: Yes. He said to them: … in the presence … or even not in his presence? They said to him: … in his presence. taught: She had a false tooth [shen totevet], … and Rabbi Yishmael made her a gold tooth from his own … When Rabbi Yishmael died, a certain eulogizer began … about him like this: Daughters of Israel, weep for Rabbi Yishmael, who clothed you.

a certain Babylonian who went up to Eretz Yisrael … married a woman … He said to her: Cook two lentils, … for me. She cooked … two lentils for him. He grew angry with her. the father nullified … and the husband did not nullify … the husband nullified … and the father did not nullify … is not nullified. And needless to say, … if one of them ratified

if … due to … a married woman, … a different verse is written … “And if … vowed in her husband’s house” … Say … both … with regard to a married woman. And if you would say: Why do I … two verses … with regard to a married woman? … to say that the husband cannot nullify earlier

if you wish, say that … “she be” indicates betrothal

her father heard … and nullified … for her but the husband did not manage to hear … before the father died, this is what we learned … the father dies, the authority … does not revert to the husband, … her husband heard … and nullified … for her, and the father did not manage to hear … before the husband died, this is what we learned … If the husband dies, the authority reverts to the father.
her husband heard and nullified … for her, and the father did not manage to hear … before he died, the husband cannot nullify … as the husband can nullify … only in partnership

her father heard and nullified … for her, and the husband did not manage to hear … before he died, the father may go back and nullify … husband’s portion, … Rabbi Natan said: This … is the statement of Beit Shammai, … Beit Hillel say … he cannot nullify
