Let us say that … of Rav Naḥman is … tanna’im, … No, … that everyone agrees with … Rav Naḥman, and here they disagree about this: … Sage, … holds: … one’s degradation is preferable to him than … his physical pain. … And … Sage, … holds that … physical pain is preferable to a person than … his degradation,
she was dressed in white … taught: If black … are becoming to her, … she is covered in unsightly garments.

she was wearing gold adornments … Isn’t … obvious? Now … renders her unattractive … is it necessary … these … Lest you say … with these … she has more degradation, as people say … Undressed, naked, and wearing shoes. … teaches us

And afterward … would bring … rope, … Rabbi Abba raised a dilemma before Rav Huna: What is … an Egyptian rope will preclude … with regard to a sota? … is so that her clothes will not fall off her, and … a small ribbon [tziltzul] would also suffice. Or, perhaps … because … the Master said: She girded … with … ribbon … therefore the priest brings … an Egyptian rope, … and ties it above her breasts. … indispensable.
said to him: You learned … And afterward … would bring an Egyptian rope … so that her clothes would not fall off her.

And anyone who desires to watch her may watch, … This … is itself difficult, … you say: And anyone who desires to watch her may watch. Apparently, … is no difference … men and … is no difference … women; … And then … teaches: And all of the women are permitted to watch her, … women, yes, … men, no,
Abaye said: Interpret … to women, … Rava said to him: But … teaches … anyone who desires to watch her may watch,

Rather, Rava said: Anyone who desires to watch her may watch, … is no difference … men … is no difference … women. And … women are obligated to watch her, as is stated: … that all women may be chastened not to do after your lewdness”

MISHNA: … With the measure that a person measures, he is measured with it. … she, … adorned herself to … a transgression, the Omnipresent … she … rendered unattractive; she exposed herself for … a transgression, … the Omnipresent … her … exposed … she began her transgression with … thigh and afterward with … stomach, therefore the thigh is smitten first and then the stomach, and the rest of all … body … not escape
GEMARA: Rav Yosef says: Although the measure … has ceased, … with a measure … has not ceased,

As Rav Yosef says, and Rabbi Ḥiyya similarly teaches: From the day that the Temple was destroyed, although the Sanhedrin ceased, … four … capital punishment have not ceased. … But they have ceased; … Rather, … The law of … four … capital punishment has not ceased.

One who is liable … stoning either falls from a roof or an animal mauls him … One who is liable … burning either falls into a fire … or a snake bites him, … One who is liable to … slaying … either is turned over to the authorities … or robbers come upon him … One who is liable … strangling either drowns in a river … or dies of diphtheria [seronekhi],

It is taught … Rabbi … would say: From where … that with the measure that a person measures, he is measured with it? As it is stated: “In full measure [besase’a], when you send her away, you contend with her”

I have … only … a se’a, … From where … to include … a half-se’a [tarkav] and a half-tarkav; a kav and a half-kav; a quarter-kav and half of a quarter-kav; an eighth-kav [toman] and an ukla, … From where … The verse states: “For every boot [sa’on] stamped with fierceness, … Rabbi
And from where … that each and every peruta combine … to a great sum, … The verse states: … adding one thing to another, to find out the account”

And we found this with regard to a sota, that with the measure with which she measured, she is measured with it: She stood by the opening of her house to exhibit herself to … therefore a priest has her stand at the Gate of Nicanor and exhibits her disgrace to all; she spread beautiful shawls [sudarin] on her head for … therefore a priest removes … kerchief from her head and places it under her feet; she adorned her face for … therefore

her face becomes sallow … she painted her eyes for … therefore her eyes bulge … she braided her hair for … therefore a priest unbraids her hair … she indicated to … with a finger … therefore her fingernails fall off; she girded herself for … with a ribbon … therefore a priest brings an Egyptian rope and ties … for her above her breasts; she extended her thigh for … therefore her thigh falls away

She received … upon her stomach, therefore her stomach swells; she fed him delicacies of the world, therefore her offering … animal food, … she gave him fine wine to drink in fine cups, therefore a priest gives her bitter water in an earthenware mekeida, … to drink.
She acted in secret; … “Who dwell in secret, with the Most High” … turns … face to her, as it is stated: “The eye of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying: No eye shall see me;
Alternatively, she acted in secret, … the Omnipresent revealed it in the open, as it is stated: “Though his hatred be concealed with deceit, his wickedness shall be revealed before the congregation”
And since Rabbi … derives … from: … adding one thing to another, to find out the account” … why do I … “For every boot stamped with fierceness” … to … by the measure,
And since he derives it from “for every boot stamped with fierceness,” why do I … “in full measure, when you send her away, you contend with her”

to … as … by Rav Ḥinnana bar Pappa, for Rav Ḥinnana bar Pappa says: The Holy One, Blessed be He, does not punish a nation … until its time to be banished, … as it is stated: “In full measure, when you send her away,

Is that so? But didn’t Rava say: Why … three cups … that are stated with regard to Egypt … One that it drank in the days of Moses … one that it drank in the days of Pharaoh Neco, … and one that it will drink in the future with its companions,

And if you would say … those … have gone, and these … are different ones, but isn’t it taught … Rabbi Yehuda said: Minyamin, an Egyptian convert, was a friend of mine from among the students of Rabbi Akiva, … Minyamin the Egyptian convert said: … I … a first- … Egyptian … and … I married … first- … Egyptian … I will marry off my son, … a second- … to … second- … Egyptian … in order that my son’s son will be permitted to enter into the congregation.

Rather, if … was stated … was stated like this: Rav Ḥinnana bar Pappa says: The Holy One, Blessed be He, does not punish … king until his time to be banished, as it is stated: “In full measure, when you send her away, you contend with her”

Ameimar teaches that … of Rav Ḥinnana bar Pappa with regard to this: What is … which is written: “For I the Lord change not; and you, sons of Jacob, are not consumed” … “For I the Lord change [shaniti] not” … I did not strike a nation and repeat [shaniti] … it, … “And you, sons of Jacob, are not consumed,” … This is … as that which is written: … I will consume My arrows upon them” … My arrows are consumed … and they, … are not consumed
Rav Hamnuna says: The Holy One, Blessed be He, does not punish a person until his se’a, … is filled, as it is stated: “In the fullness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits;

Rav Ḥinnana bar Pappa interpreted … homiletically: What is … which is written: “Rejoice in the Lord, you righteous, praise is comely for the upright [nava tehilla]” … Do not read … Praise is comely [nava]; rather, … A house [naveh] of praise. This … Moses and David, whose enemies did not rule over their achievements,

David, … as it is written: “Her gates are sunk into the ground” … Moses, as the Master said: When the first Temple was built, the Tent of Meeting was sequestered, … its boards, its clasps, and its bars, and its pillars, and its sockets. … Where … Rav Ḥisda says … Avimi says: Beneath the tunnels of the Sanctuary.

The Sages taught … sota placed her eyes, … on one who is unfit for her, … That which she desired, … is not given to her, … And that which she had, … was taken away from her, … that anyone who places his eyes on that which is not his is not given what he desires, and that which he had is taken from him.

And, so too, we found with regard to the primeval snake … for he placed his eyes on that which was unfit for him, … that which he desired was not given to him, and that which was in his possession was taken from him. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: I … said … will be king over every domesticated animal and non-domesticated animal, but now he is cursed more than all the domesticated animals and all the non-domesticated animals of the field,

I said … will walk upright, … now he shall go on his belly; I said … his food will be … food … a person, … now he shall eat dust. … said: I will kill Adam and marry Eve, … now: “I will put enmity between you and the woman and between your seed and her seed”

And so we found with regard to Cain, … and Korah, … and Balaam, … and Doeg, … and Ahithophel, … and Gehazi, … and Absalom, … and Adonijah, … and Uzziah, … and Haman, … who placed their eyes on that which is unfit for them, and … what they desired was not given to them, and what they had was taken from them.

She began her transgression with … thigh … From where are these matters … If we say … because it is written … when the Lord does make your thigh to fall away, and your belly to swell” … but isn’t … written … “And her belly shall swell, and her thigh shall fall away”

Abaye said … When … curses … he first curses the thigh and then he curses the stomach, but when the … water evaluates … it evaluates … along its way … first … stomach and then … thigh. … in … curse it is also written: … and will cause your belly to swell, and your thigh to fall away” … That … that the priest notifies her that … stomach … first and then … thigh, so that … not cast aspersions on the bitter water.
MISHNA: … Samson followed his eyes, therefore … the Philistines gouged out his eyes, as it is stated: “And the Philistines laid hold on him, and put out his eyes”

Absalom was … proud of his hair, … therefore he was hanged by his hair. And … because he engaged in sexual intercourse with ten of his father’s concubines … therefore ten spears [loneviyyot] were put, … into him, as it is stated: “And ten young men that bore Joab’s armor compassed about … And because he stole … three thefts … The heart of his father, … the heart of the court, … and the heart of the Jewish people, as it is stated: “So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel” … therefore three spears were embedded into … as it is stated: … And he took three spears in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom,

And the same … with regard to the … good … Miriam waited for … Moses … one hour … as it is stated: “And his sister stood afar off, … Therefore the Jewish people delayed … seven days … for her … as it is stated: … and the people journeyed not until Miriam was brought in again”

Joseph merited to bury his father, … and there was none among his brothers greater than he … as it is stated: “And Joseph went up to bury his father; … And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen; … Who, to us, … a greater … than Joseph, as it was none … Moses who involved … his

Moses merited … in … Joseph’s bones … and there was none among the Jewish people greater than he, as it is stated: “And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him” … Who … a greater … than Moses, as no one involved himself in his … other than the Omnipresent … as it is stated: “And He buried him in the valley … Not only with regard to Moses did … say … but … with regard to all the righteous individuals, as it is stated: “Your righteousness shall go before you and the glory of the Lord shall gather you in”

GEMARA: The Sages taught … Samson rebelled with his eyes, as it is stated: … And Samson said to his father: Get her for me; for she is pleasant in my eyes” … Therefore, the Philistines gouged out his eyes, as it is stated: “And the Philistines laid hold on him, and put out his eyes”
Is that so? But isn’t it written: “But his father and his mother knew not that it was from the Lord; … in any event when he went, he followed his inclination

It is taught … Rabbi … says: His initial wrongdoing was in Gaza, … therefore he was smitten in Gaza. … His initial wrongdoing was in Gaza, as it is written: “And Samson went to Gaza, and saw there a harlot, … Therefore, he was smitten in Gaza, as it is written: … and they brought him down to Gaza,
But isn’t it written … “And Samson went down to Timnah, … Gemara answers: In any event, his initial wrongdoing was in Gaza,

“And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah” … It is taught … Rabbi … says: … if she had not been called … name Delilah, it would have been fitting that she be called Delilah, … she weakened [dildela] his strength, she weakened his heart, … she weakened his deeds,

She weakened his strength, as it is written: … and his strength went from him” … She weakened his heart, as it is written: “And when Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, … She weakened his deeds, … as the Divine Presence left him, as it is written: … But he knew not that the Lord was departed from him”

“And when Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart” … From where did she know … Rabbi Ḥanin says … Rav says: Words of truth are recognizable, … Abaye says … She knew about … a righteous individual, that he would not express the name of Heaven in vain. Once he said: … I have been a nazirite unto God … she said: Now he is certainly saying the truth.

“And it came to pass, when she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, … What … “and urged him”? … Rabbi Yitzḥak of the school of Rabbi Ami says: At the moment … completion of … intercourse, she slipped away from beneath him.

“Now therefore beware, I pray of you, and drink no wine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing” … what … “any unclean thing”? … And … more, until now was she eating unclean things, … Rabbi Yitzḥak of the school of Rabbi Ami says: … items that are forbidden to a nazirite.
“But God cleaved the hollow place that is in Lehi, … Rabbi Yitzḥak of the school of Rabbi Ami says: He desired something unclean, … Therefore, … his life was dependent on something unclean,

“And the spirit of the Lord began [vataḥel] … Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: The prophecy of Jacob our forefather … took effect [ḥaleta] … as it is written: “Dan shall be a serpent in the way,

“To move him [lefa’amo] in Mahaneh Dan.” Rabbi Yitzḥak of the school of Rabbi Ami says: … teaches that the Divine Presence jangled before him, … like a bell [zog], … it is written here: “To move him [lefa’amo] in Mahaneh Dan,” and it is written there … “A bell [pa’amon] and a pomegranate”
“Between Zorah and Eshtaol.” Rabbi Asi says: Zorah and Eshtaol were two large mountains, and Samson uprooted them and ground them one against the other.
and he shall begin to save Israel … Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says:
the oath of Abimelech, … was negated, as it is written … that you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my son’s son;

and the child grew, and the Lord blessed him” … With what did He bless him? Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: … that He blessed him with regard to his penis, … his penis … like … men, and … his seed … like an overflowing river.

“And Samson called unto the Lord, and said: Lord God, remember me, I pray to You, and strengthen me, I pray to You, only this once, … that I may be this once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes” … Rav said … Samson said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, remember … my … twenty-two years that I judged the Jewish people … and I did not … say to any one of them: Move a stick for me from … place to … place.

“And Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, … What is different … foxes … Rabbi Aivu bar Nagdi says … Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says: Samson said: Let … that goes in reverse … come and exact punishment from the Philistines, who reneged on their oath

It is taught … Rabbi Shimon the Pious said: … between the shoulders of Samson was sixty cubits, as it is stated: “And Samson lay till midnight, and arose at midnight, and grabbed hold of the doors of the gate of the city, and the two posts, and plucked them up, bar and all, and put them upon his shoulders, … and it is learned … that doors … of Gaza were no less than sixty cubits

and he did grind in the prison-house” … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Grinding is nothing other … a language of a transgression … and so … says: “Then let my wife grind unto another man” … teaches that each and every … brought his wife to the prison in order that she should be impregnated by … Rav Pappa said: This … that people say: Before a wine drinker, … wine; before one who digs in the ground, … figs.

And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … anyone who commits adultery, his wife commits adultery against him, as it is stated: “If my heart has been enticed unto a woman, and I have lain in wait at my neighbor’s door” … and it is written: “Then let my wife grind unto another man and may strangers kneel over her” … And this … that people say: He is … among the pumpkins [karei] and his wife among the zucchinis [butzinei],

And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Samson judged the Jewish people as their Father in Heaven … as it is stated: “Dan shall judge his people, as one … And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Samson [Shimshon] is called by the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is stated: “For the Lord God is a sun [shemesh] and a shield” … If that is so, … should not be erased … Rather, … is akin to the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, … just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, protects the entire world, so too Samson, in his generation, protected all the Jewish people.

And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Balaam was lame in one of his legs, as it is stated … “And he went, limping [shefi]” … Samson was lame in … his two legs, as it is stated … a horned snake [shefifon] in the path”

The Sages taught … Five … were created … akin to a representation of the … High, and they were all stricken by that … Samson … in his strength, Saul in his neck … Absalom in his hair, Zedekiah in his eyes, … Asa in his feet.
Samson … by his strength, … as it is written: … and his strength went from him”
Saul … in his neck, as it is written: … Therefore, Saul took his sword and fell upon it”
Absalom … in his hair, as we will state later. Zedekiah … in his eyes, as it is written: … and put out the eyes of Zedekiah,

Asa … in his feet, as it is written: … But in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet” … And Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: … that gout [padagra] grabbed hold of him. Mar Zutra, son of Rav Naḥman, said to Rav Naḥman: What are the circumstances … gout? … He said to him: … like a needle … into living flesh. … From where did he know this? … Some say … suffered from this … and some say … he heard it from his teacher, and some say … “The secret of the Lord is with them that fear Him; and His covenant, to make them know it”

Rava taught: For what … Asa punished … Because he made Torah scholars perform forced labor [angarya], as it is stated: “Then King Asa made a proclamation unto all Judah; none was exempted; … everyone, including … What … “None was exempted [ein naki]”? Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: … even a bridegroom from his chamber and a bride from her canopy,

It is written … “And Samson went down to Timnah, … and it is written … Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah … Rabbi Elazar says: … Samson, who was disgraced there … descent is written with regard to his … Judah, who was elevated there, … ascent is written with regard to his
Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says … There were two … Timnah, one … by descent … and one … by ascent.
Rav Pappa said … There was one Timnah, … who came from this side … descent, and … who came from that side … ascent. … For example: Vardonia, and Bei Varei, and the market of Neresh.

and sat in the entrance of Enaim [befetaḥ einayim], … Rabbi Alexandri says: … teaches that she went and she sat at the entrance … of Abraham our forefather, a place that all eyes hope to see it, … Rabbi Ḥanin … Rav says: … a place called Enaim, and similarly … states … “Tappuah and Enam”

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says: She provided eyes [einayim] for her statements, … When … solicited her … he … said to her: … you perhaps are a gentile? She said to him: I am a convert. … Perhaps you are a married woman? She said to him: I am an unmarried woman. … Perhaps your father accepted betrothal for you … She said to him: I am an orphan. … Maybe you are impure? She said to him: I am pure.
“And he planted an eshel in Beersheba, … Reish Lakish says: … teaches that … made an orchard and planted in it all kinds of sweet things.

Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya … One said … an orchard [pardes], and one said … an inn [pundak]. … Granted, according to the one who said … an orchard, this is what is written: “And he planted,” … But according to the one who said … an inn, what is … “and he planted”? … As it is written: “And he shall plant [vayitta] the tents of his palace
and called there [vayyikra] on the name of the Lord, the Everlasting God” … Reish Lakish said: Do not read … “vayyikra,”

rather … vayyakri, and he caused … to call. … teaches that Abraham our forefather caused the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, to be called … in the mouth of all passersby. How so? After … ate and drank, they arose to bless him. He said to them: But did you eat from … mine? … you ate from … the God of the world. … you … thank and praise and bless the One Who spoke and the world was
“When Judah saw her, he thought her to be a prostitute, for she had covered her face” … Because she had covered her face he thought her to be a prostitute?

Rabbi Elazar says: … that … covered her face in the home of her father-in-law, … As Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says … Rabbi Yonatan says: Any daughter-in-law who is modest in the house of her father-in-law merits that kings and prophets emerge from her. From where do we … From Tamar. Prophets … as it is written: “The vision of Isaiah, the son of Amoz” … Kings … from David. And Rabbi Levi says: This matter is a tradition … we … from our ancestors: Amoz, … and Amaziah, … were brothers.

“When she was brought forth [mutzet], … It should have … When she was mitutzet. … Rabbi Elazar says: After her signs, … were brought out, … Samael came and distanced them … Gabriel … came and moved … closer

This is as it is written: “For the leader, upon yonat eilem reḥokim, a psalm [mikhtam] of David” … Rabbi Yoḥanan says … From the moment that her signs were distanced [reḥokim], she became like a mute dove [yona illemet]. … “a psalm [mikhtam] of David” … from whom David emerged, as he was modest [makh] and flawless [tam] with everyone. Alternatively, mikhtam … that makkato, … was complete [tama], … that … was born circumcised. Alternatively, mikhtam … just as in his youth … made himself small in front of one who was greater than him … to learn Torah … so too, when he became great

“She sent to her father-in-law, saying: By the man whose these are, am I with child” … And let her say to him … Rav Zutra bar Tuviyya says … Rav says, and some say Rav Ḥana bar Bizna says … Rabbi Shimon Ḥasida says, and some say … Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: It is more amenable for a person to throw himself into a fiery furnace … and not humiliate another in public. From where do we … From Tamar,

Discern, please, … Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: With … discern … informed his father … with … discern they informed … With … discern he informed … Discern now whether it is your son’s coat … With … discern they informed him: … Discern, please, whose are
please [na].” … na … nothing other … a language of request. … She said to him: I request of you: Discern the image of your Creator … and do not avert your eyes from me.

“And Judah acknowledged them, and said: She is more righteous than I; … This is … as Rav Ḥanin bar Bizna says … Rabbi Shimon Ḥasida says: Joseph, who sanctified the name of Heaven in private … merited that one letter from the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, was added to his … as it is written: “He appointed it in Joseph [bihosef ] for a testimony in his name,

Judah, who sanctified the name of Heaven in public, merited that his entire … is called by the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, … When he confessed and said: “She is more righteous than I,” a Divine Voice went forth and said: You saved Tamar and her two children … from … the fire. … your life, … in your merit, I will save three of your children from the fire. … who are they? Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah
“She is more righteous than I [mimmenni].” … From where did he know … A Divine Voice went forth and said: From Me these hidden … emerged,

“And he knew her [leda’atah] again no more [velo yasaf],” … Shmuel the Elder, father-in-law of Rav Shmuel bar Ami, says in the name of Rav Shmuel bar Ami: … once he knew … her … he did not desist from … her again, … it is written here: “Velo yasaf od leda’atah,” and it is written there … with a great voice and it went on no more [velo yasaf]”

Absalom was … proud of his hair, … The Sages taught … Absalom rebelled … due to his hair, as it is stated: … there was none … as Absalom for his beauty; … And when he shaved his head, as it was at every year’s end that he shaved it; because the hair was heavy on him, therefore he shaved it, and he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels, by the king’s stone” … taught: A stone with which the people of Tiberias and the people of Tzippori weigh

therefore, he was hung by his hair, as it is stated … “And Absalom chanced to meet the servants of David. And Absalom was riding upon his mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great terebinth, and his head caught hold of the terebinth, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was under him went on” … took a sword [safseira] and wanted to cut his hair … The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught: At that moment, … the netherworld opened beneath him

“And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept; and as he went about he said: O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Would I had died in your place, O Absalom, my son, my son” … “And the king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice: O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son” … Why … these eight … “my son” … Seven … which he raised him up from the seven chambers of Gehenna. And … the other, … some say that … brought … head … close to … body, and some say that … brought … to the World-to-Come.

“Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself … What did … take? Reish Lakish says: He engaged in a bad transaction for himself … “The pillar, which is in the king’s valley [be’emek hammelekh].” Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa says: … in the deep [amukka] counsel of the King [melekh] of the universe,

as it is written … Behold, I will raise up evil against you out of your own house” … Similarly, you can say … “And he sent him from the valley [emek] of Hebron” … Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa says: From the deep [amukka] counsel of that righteous individual who is interred in Hebron, … as it is written: … Know that your seed shall be a stranger

“For he said: I have no son … And did … not have sons? But isn’t it written: “And to Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter” … Rav Yitzḥak bar Avdimi says: … that he did not have a son worthy for royalty. Rav Ḥisda said: It is learned … Anyone who burns the produce of another does not leave a son to inherit … him, and he, … burned … of Joab, as it is written: “Therefore he said to his servants: See, Joab’s field is near mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire”
And the same … with regard to the … good … Miriam … Are … comparable? There, … one hour, … here, … seven days. Abaye said: Say … And with regard to … good it is not so,

Rava said to him: But … taught … And the same … with regard to the … good … Rather, Rava said: This is what … is teaching: And the same … with regard to the … good … with the same measure, … but the measure of good is always greater than the measure of punishment.

“And his sister stood afar off, … Rabbi Yitzḥak says: This entire verse is stated in reference to the Divine Presence, … “And … stood”; as it is written: “And the Lord came, and stood” … “His sister”; as it is written: “Say to wisdom: You are my sister” … “Afar off”; as it is written: “From afar the Lord appeared to me” … “To know”; as it is written: “For the Lord is a God of knowledge” … “What”; as it is written: “What does the Lord God require of you” … “Would be done”; as it is written: “For the Lord God will do nothing” … “To him”; as it is written: “And the Lord said to him: Peace

“And there arose a new king … Rav and Shmuel … One says … actually a new … and one says … that his decrees were transformed … The one who says … actually a new … because it is written “new.” And the one who says that his decrees were transformed … because it is not written: “And … died and … reigned.” … “Who knew not Joseph” … that he was like someone who did not know him at all.

“And he said to his people: Behold, the people of the children of Israel … taught … He, … initiated the proposal. Therefore, … he was stricken first. He initiated the proposal, as it is written: “And he said to his people.” Therefore, he was stricken first, as it is written: … both upon you, and upon your people, and upon all your servants”
“Come, let us deal wisely with him [lo], … He should have … With them [lahem], … Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says … Come, let us deal wisely with regard to the savior of Israel,

With what … shall we judge … them? … we shall judge them with fire, … it is written: “For behold, the Lord will come in fire” … it is written … “For by fire will the Lord contend” … with the sword, … it is written … “And by His sword with all flesh”

Rather, let us come and judge them with water, … for the Holy One, Blessed be He, already took an oath that He will not bring a flood upon the world, as it is stated: “For this is as the waters of Noah unto Me; … And … did not know that He will not bring a flood upon all the world, but He … bring … upon one nation.

Alternatively, … He does not bring … but they … come and fall into … and so it says: … and the Egyptians fled toward it; … And this is what Rabbi Elazar says: What is the … which is written: … for in that which they conspired [zadu] against them” … In the pot in which they cooked, they … were cooked, … From where may … be inferred that this … “zadu” is a term … a pot? … As it is written: “And Jacob simmered a pot [vayyazed Ya’akov nazid]”
Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says … Rabbi Simai says: Three … were … in that counsel … Balaam, and Job, and Yitro.

Balaam, who advised … was … killed … Job, who was silent … was punished by suffering, … Yitro, who ran away … merited that … of his children’s children sat … in the Chamber of Hewn Stone, as it is stated: “And the families of scribes who dwelt at Jabez, Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Sucathites, these were the Kenites who descended from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab” … And it is written: “The children of the Kenite, Moses’ father-in-law”
and fight against us, and get him up out of the land” … He should have … And get us up, … Rabbi Abba bar Kahana says: … is like a person who curses himself … applies his curse to another.

“Therefore they did set over him taskmasters … It should have … Over them, … The school of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, taught: … teaches … they brought a brick mold and they hung it on the neck of Pharaoh … And … each and every Jew who said to … I am a delicate person [istenis] … they said to him: Are you at all more of a delicate person than Pharaoh,
“Taskmasters [sarei missim]” … A matter that compels [shemesim] … bricks,
“In order to afflict him with their burdens” … It should have … “In order to afflict them,” … in order to afflict Pharaoh, with … the burdens of the Jewish people.

“And they built for Pharaoh storage cities [miskenot], … Rav and Shmuel … One says … that endanger [mesakenot] their owners, … And one says … that impoverishes [memaskenot] their owners, as the Master said: All who engage in construction become poor.

“Pithom and Raamses” … Rav and Shmuel … One says … Pithom … its … name, and why was it called Raamses? … that … they collapsed [mitroses] one by one … And one says … Raamses … its … name, and why was it called Pithom? … the opening of the abyss [pi tehom] swallowed … one by one, and it sunk into the ground.

“But the more they afflicted him, the more he would multiply and the more he would spread about” … It should have … The more they multiplied and the more they spread about, … Reish Lakish says: Divine inspiration proclaimed to … the more he will multiply and the more he will spread about. … “And they became disgusted [vayyakutzu] due to the children of Israel.” … teaches that … appeared in their eyes like thorns [kotzim].
“And the Egyptians made the children of Israel work
with rigor [befarekh]” … Rabbi Elazar says: … With a soft mouth [bifeh rakh], … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says: … With crushing [bifrikha],
“And they made their lives bitter through hard service, with mortar and brick, … Rava says: … initially … with mortar and bricks, and ultimately … “and with every laborious service in the field.”

“In all their service, wherein they made them serve with rigor” … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says … Rabbi Yonatan says: … would exchange … men’s work to women and women’s work to men, … And even according to the one who says … there, … with a soft mouth, here, … certainly … with crushing

Rav Avira taught: In the merit of … righteous women that were in that generation, the Jewish people were redeemed from Egypt. … At the time … would go … to draw water, the Holy One, Blessed be He, would materialize for them small fish … into their pitchers, and they would … draw … half … water and half … fish. And they would … come and place two pots on the fire, one … of hot … and one … of fish

And they would … take … to their husbands, to the field, and would bathe … and anoint them … and feed them … and give them to drink and bond with them … between the sheepfolds, … as it is stated: “When you lie among the sheepfolds, … as a reward … lie among the sheepfolds,” the Jewish people merited to … the plunder of Egypt, as it is stated … “The wings of the dove are covered with silver, and her pinions with the shimmer of gold”

And when … become pregnant, they would come … to their homes, and when the time for them to give birth … they would go and give birth in the field under the apple tree, as it is stated: “Under the apple tree I awakened you;

And the Holy One, Blessed be He, would send from the heavens above … who would clean and prepare … just as a midwife prepares the newborn, as it is stated: “And as for your birth, on the day you were born, your navel was not cut nor were you washed with water for cleansing; … And … would gather for them two round … One of … oil and one of … honey, as it is stated: “And He would suckle them with honey from a crag and oil

And once the Egyptians would notice them, … they would come to kill them. But a miracle would occur for them and they would be absorbed by the earth. And … would … bring oxen and would plow upon them, as it is stated: “The plowers plowed upon my back; … After … would leave, … would emerge and exit … like grass of the field, as it is stated: “I caused you to increase even as the growth of the field”

And once … would grow, they would come like many flocks … to their homes, as it is stated … “And you did increase and grow up and you came with excellent beauty [ba’adi adayim]” … Do not read … “Ba’adi adayim,” … Rather, … Be’edrei adarim,
And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, revealed Himself at the … Sea, … recognized Him first, as it is stated: “This is my God, and I will glorify Him”

“And the king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, … Rav and Shmuel … One says … a woman and her daughter, and one says … a daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law. … one who says … a woman and her daughter, … Jochebed, … and … Miriam. And … one who says … a daughter-in-law and her mother-in-law, … Jochebed and … Elisheba,

is taught … according to the one who says … a woman and her daughter, because it … taught … Shiphrah, … this … Jochebed. And why was she called Shiphrah? Because she would prepare [mishapperet] the newborn. Alternatively, … Shiphrah because the Jewish people increased and multiplied [shepparu verabbu] in her days,

Puah, … this … Miriam. And why was she called Puah? Because she would make a comforting sound [po’a] as she would remove the child … Alternatively, … Puah … as she would speak [po’a] through divine inspiration and say: In the future, my mother will give birth to a son who will save the Jewish people.

“And he said: When you deliver the Hebrew women, … What … “stones”? Rabbi Ḥanan says: … transmitted a great sign to them. He said to them: At the time … crouches to give birth, her thighs become as cold as stones,

And there are those who say … As it is written: “So I went down to the potter’s shop, and behold, he was at his work on the wheels [ovnayim]” … Just as this potter … thigh … here and … thigh … there and the block … is in the middle, so too, a woman … thigh here and … thigh there and the newborn is in the middle.
“If it be a son, then you shall kill him; … Rabbi Ḥanina says: … transmitted to them a great sign … A boy … his face downward; a girl … her face upward.

“But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt spoke about them [aleihen], … It should have … to them [lahen].” Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: … teaches that … proposed to them to … a sinful act, … but they did not accept
“But they kept the male children alive” … teaches: … not only that they did not kill … but that they would … provide for them water and food,

“And the midwives said to Pharaoh: Because … are not as the … women, … What … “ḥayot”? If we say … actual midwives … is that to say … a midwife does not need … another midwife … to help her give birth?

Rather, … said to … This nation is compared to an animal [ḥayya], … Judah … a lion’s whelp” … Dan … “Dan shall be a serpent … Naphtali … “A hind let loose” … Issachar … “A large-boned donkey” … Joseph … first bullock” … Benjamin … “A ravenous wolf”
where … is written with regard to him, … is … written with regard to him. And … where no … written with regard to him … is written about … “How your mother was a lioness; among lions she crouched,

“And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that He made them houses” … Rav and Shmuel … One says … the houses of … priesthood and … Levites … and one says … houses of royalty … The one who says … houses of … priesthood and … Levites … Aaron and Moses, … And the one who says … houses of royalty … David, … also comes from Miriam, as it is written: “And Azubah,” the wife of Caleb, “died, and Caleb took to him Ephrath, who bore him Hur” … And it is written: “David was the son of that Ephrathite

“And Caleb, the son of Hezron, begot children of Azubah his wife, and of Jerioth, and these were her sons: Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon” … son of Hezron? Wasn’t he … son of Jephunneh, … a son who turned away [sheppana] from the counsel of the spies.
But … still … was … son of Kenaz, as it is written: “And Othniel, the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s … brother, took it” … Rava said: … was the stepson of Kenaz,
is also precise … as it is written: … the Kenizzite … Conclude from it

Azubah. … this … Miriam. And why is she called Azubah? As everyone initially abandoned her [azavuha] … begot children [holid] … But … he married her? Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … anyone who marries a woman for the sake of Heaven, … the verse ascribes him … as if he gave birth to her.
Jerioth, … for her face was like … curtains [yeriot].

“And these were her sons [vaneha].” … Do not read … vaneha, her sons; rather, … boneha, her builders. … “Jesher,” … as he set himself straight [yisher] … “Shobab,” … that he broke [sibbev] his … inclination … “and Ardon [veArdon],” … that he ruled [rada] … his … inclination. And some say: Because the face … like a rose [vered]

“And Ashhur the father of Tekoa had two wives, Helah and Naarah” … Ashhur is Caleb. And why was he called Ashhur? Because his face became blackened [husheḥaru] from … fasts … “The father of” … as he became like a father to … “Tekoa,” … as he attached [taka] his heart to his Father in Heaven.
“had two wives” … Miriam became like two wives, … “Helah and Naarah,” were not … Helah and Naarah. Rather, initially … sickly [ḥela] … and ultimately … a young woman [na’ara].

“And the children of Helah were Zereth [Tzeret] and Zohar and Ethnan” … “Tzeret,” for she became … a rival [tzara] to other … “Zohar,” as her face … like … noon [tzohorayim]. … “Ethnan,” as any … that saw her … would bring a gift [etnan] to his wife

“And Pharaoh charged all his people, … Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: … he decreed even on his own nation … And Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says … He decreed three decrees. Initially, … If it be a son, then you shall kill him; … And afterward, … “Every son that is born you shall cast into the river” … And ultimately, he decreed even on his own nation
“And there went a man of the house of Levi, … To where did he go? Rav Yehuda bar Zevina says: He went according to the advice of his daughter

teaches: Amram, … was the great man of his generation. Once he saw that the wicked Pharaoh said: “Every son that is born you shall cast into the river, … he said: We are laboring for nothing … he arose and divorced his wife. All … arose and divorced their wives.

His daughter, … said to him: Father, your decree is more harsh … than that of Pharaoh, as Pharaoh decreed only with regard to the males, but you decreed … on the males and on the females. … Pharaoh decreed … only in this world, but you … in this world and in the World-to-Come,

Pharaoh the wicked, … uncertain … his decree … fulfilled, … uncertain … not … fulfilled. You are a righteous person, … your decrees … certainly … fulfilled, as it is stated … “You shall also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto you” … arose and brought back, … his wife, … all … arose and brought back their wives.

“And took … it should have … “And returned … Rav Yehuda bar Zevina says: He performed an act of marriage … He sat her on a palanquin [appiryon], and Aaron and Miriam danced before her, and the ministering angels said: “A joyful mother of children”

“a daughter of Levi” … possible … was … 130 years old and … calls her a daughter? … as Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: … is Jochebed, whose conception was on the road, … and she was born between the walls, … as it is stated: … who was born to Levi in Egypt”
Her birth … in Egypt, but her conception was not in Egypt. … Rabbi Yehuda says: The signs of a young woman were born in her

“And the woman conceived, and bore a son; … But … was pregnant with … for three months at the outset, … Rav Yehuda bar Zevina said: … juxtapose her … birth to her becoming pregnant. Just as her becoming pregnant was without pain, so too, her … birth was without pain. From here … concerning righteous women that they were not included in the verdict [pitkah] of Eve

and when she saw him that he was a goodly [tov] child, … is taught … Rabbi Meir says: “Tov” is his, … name, … Rabbi Yehuda says: His name was Toviya. Rabbi Neḥemya says: … fit for prophecy. Others say: … born when he was … circumcised. And the Rabbis say: At the time when Moses was born, the entire house was filled with light, … it is written here: “And when she saw him that he was a goodly [tov] child,” and it is written there: “And God saw the light, that it was good [tov]”
“And she hid him three months” … because the Egyptians counted … only from the time … took her back, but she was pregnant with … for three months from the outset

“And when she could no longer hide him” … Why … Let her continue to hide him. Rather, anywhere that the Egyptians heard that a baby was born … they would bring … baby there in order that it could be heard … and … would cry together, as it is written: “Take us the foxes, the little foxes,

she took for him an ark of bulrushes, … What is different … bulrushes … Rabbi Elazar says: From here … concerning righteous people that their money is more precious to them than their bodies, … And why … so much … Because they do not stretch out their hands to … stolen property.
Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says … a soft material … which is able to withstand … before a soft item and before a hard item.
“And daubed it with bitumen and with pitch” … teaches: … bitumen on the interior and pitch on the exterior, so that righteous person, … would not smell a foul odor,
“And she put the child therein, and laid it in the willows [bassuf]” … Rabbi Elazar says: … in the Suf Sea, … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says:
a marsh, as it is written: “The reeds and willows [suf] shall wither”

“And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe [lirḥotz] in the river” … Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: … teaches that she came down … to cleanse … from … her father’s idols, … And similarly it states: “When the Lord shall have washed [raḥatz] away the filth of the daughters of Zion,
“And her maidens walked … [holekhot] … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: This walking … nothing other … terminology of … death, and similarly it states: “Behold, I am going [holekh] to die”

“And she saw the ark among the willows” … Once … saw that … was intending to save Moses, they said to her: Our mistress, the custom of the world … a king of flesh and blood decrees a decree, … if all the world does not fulfill it, … his children and members of his household fulfill it, and … you are violating the decree of your father. … Gabriel came and beat them to the ground

“And she sent amatah to take it” … Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Neḥemya … One says … her arm, and one says … her maidservant. … The one who says … her arm … as it is written “amatah,” … And the one who says … her maidservant … because it does not … write … Her hand [yadah].
And according to the one who says … her maidservant, didn’t you say … Gabriel came and beat them to the ground … that … left her one … as it is not proper that a princess should stand alone.

And according to the one who says … her hand, let … write … Her hand [yadah]. … This … teaches us that her arm extended [ishtarbav] … As the Master said … And similarly you find with regard to the hand of Pharaoh’s daughter … and similarly you find with regard to the teeth of evildoers, as it is written: “You have broken [shibbarta] the teeth of the wicked” … and Reish Lakish said: Do not read … shibbarta, rather … sheribbavta,
“And she opened it and saw it [vatirehu], even the child” … it should have … And she saw. Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: … she saw the Divine Presence with him.

and behold a lad [na’ar] that wept” … calls him “a child [yeled],” and … calls him “a lad [na’ar].” … teaches: He is … a child but his voice … as a lad; … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Neḥemya said to him: If … so, you made Moses our teacher blemished, … Rather, … teaches that his mother made a canopy of youth, … for him in the ark, … she said: Perhaps I will not merit to … his … canopy.
“And she had compassion on him, and said: This [zeh] is one of the Hebrews’ children” … From where did she know … Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: As she saw … he was circumcised.
“This [zeh] … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … teaches that she prophesied unknowingly, … This … falls, … but no other … fall

And this is what Rabbi Elazar said: What is … which is written: “And when they shall say to you: Seek unto the necromancers and the diviners, that chirp [metzaftzefim] and that mutter [mahggim]” … They see [tzofin], but they do not know what they are seeing; they enunciate [mahggim], but they do not know what they are enunciating.

saw that the savior of the Jewish people would be stricken by water. … they arose and decreed: “Every son that is born you shall cast into the river” … Once … cast Moses … said: We no longer see … like that sign … they canceled their decree. But they did not know that … would be stricken on account of the waters of Meribah.

And this is what Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: What is … which is written: “These [hemma] are the waters of Meribah, where … strove … these are … that the astrologers of Pharaoh saw and … erred. And this is what Moses said: … are six hundred thousand men on foot [ragli]; … Moses said to the Jewish people: On account of me, … all of you were saved,

Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa says: That day … was the twenty-first … of Nisan. The ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, … one who in the future will say … Song at the … Sea on this day be stricken on this day?

Rabbi Aḥa bar Ḥanina says: That day was … the sixth … of Sivan. The ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, … one who in the future will receive … Torah on Mount Sinai on this day be stricken on this day?

Granted, according to the one who says … on the sixth of Sivan, you find … three months … as the Master said … died on the seventh of Adar, and Moses was born on the seventh of Adar. And … from the seventh of Adar until the sixth of Sivan … three months, … But according to the one who says … on the twenty-first of Nisan, how can you find
That year was a leap year … most of the first … and most of the last … and the entire middle one.
“Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter: Shall I go and call you a nurse of the Hebrew women, … And what is different … of the Hebrew women?

teaches that … they took Moses around to all the Egyptian … and he did not … nurse … he said: … a mouth that in the future … speak with the Divine Presence … nurse something impure? And this is as it is written: “Whom shall one teach knowledge? … To whom shall … teach … knowledge … and to whom shall … make to understand the message … “Them that are weaned from the milk, them that are drawn from the breasts”
“And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her: Go. … Rabbi Elazar says: … teaches that she went quickly like a maiden, … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says: … ha’alma … for she hid her words

“And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her: Take this [heilikhi] child away, … Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: … is prophesying and she does not know what she is prophesying, … heilikhi … This is yours [ha shellikhi], … “And I will give you your wages.” Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: … with regard to righteous people, not only … that … that their lost items are returned to them, but … also … that they get their wages,

“And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took … “the sister of Aaron,” and not the sister of Moses? Rav Amram says … Rav says, and some say … Rav Naḥman says … Rav says: … teaches that … prophesied when she was … the sister of … Aaron,

And … would say: In the future, my mother will give birth to a son who will save the Jewish people. And once Moses was born, the entire house was filled with light. Her father arose and kissed her on her head. He said to her: My daughter, your prophecy has been fulfilled. And once they put him into the river, her father arose and hit her on her head. He said to her: My daughter, where is your prophecy? And this is as it is written: “And his sister stood afar off, to know what would be done to him” … to know what will be the ultimate … of her prophecy.

Joseph merited … What is different initially that it is written: “And Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, … and afterward … “And all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and his father’s house; … And what is different at the end that it is written: “And Joseph returned into Egypt, he, and his brethren,” and afterward … “And all that went up with him to bury his father,
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Initially, before … saw the honor of the Jewish people, … they did not treat them … honor, … And in the end, when they saw their honor, they treated … honor.

As it is written: “And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, … And does a boxthorn … have a threshing floor? … Rabbi Abbahu says: … teaches that they surrounded the casket of Jacob with crowns, like this threshing floor that is surrounded with boxthorns, because the children of Esau and the children of Ishmael and the children of Keturah … came

taught: … they all came to … war … once they saw the crown of Joseph, … hanging on the casket of Jacob, they all took their crowns and hung them on the casket of Jacob. … taught: Thirty-six crowns were hung on the casket of Jacob.
“And there they wailed with a very great and sore wailing” … taught: Even horses and even donkeys

Once they reached the Cave of Machpelah, Esau came and was preventing them … He said to them: … Mamre, to Kiryat Arba, the same is Hebron, … And Rabbi Yitzḥak says: … Kiryat Arba … were four couples … Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebecca, Jacob and Leah. … buried Leah in his … and the … that is remaining is mine.

said to … You sold … to … said to them: Though I sold the birthright, did I … sell … an ordinary … said to him: Yes, … as it is written … in my grave that I have dug [kariti] for me … And Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak: … kira … is nothing other … a term of a sale [mekhira] … because in the cities overseas they call a sale kira.

said to them: Bring the bill … to me, … They said to him: The bill … is in the land of Egypt. … And who will go … Naphtali will go, for he is as fast as a doe, as it is written: “Naphtali is a doe let loose, he gives goodly words” … Rabbi Abbahu says: Do not read … goodly words [imrei shafer]”; rather, … imrei sefer,

Hushim, the son of Dan, was there and his ears were heavy, … He said to them: What … this … And they said to him: This one, … is preventing … until Naphtali comes … from the land of Egypt … He said to them: And until Naphtali comes … from the land of Egypt will … father’s father lie in degradation? He took a club [kulepa] and hit … on the head, … eyes fell out and they fell on the legs of Jacob. Jacob opened his eyes and smiled. And this is that which is written: “The righteous shall rejoice when he sees the vengeance; he shall wash his feet in the blood of the wicked”

At that moment the prophecy of Rebecca was fulfilled, as it is written … “Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?” … And although their deaths were not on the same day, in any event their burials were on the same day,

And if Joseph would not have dealt with … would his brothers not have dealt with it? But isn’t it written: “For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, … They said: Allow … more honor … by royalty than by common … [hedyotot].

Who, to us, … a greater … than Joseph, … The Sages taught … Come and see how beloved mitzvot are to Moses our teacher. As, … all the Jewish people were involved in … the plunder … and he was involved in … mitzvot, as it is stated: “The wise in heart will take mitzvot”

And from where did Moses our teacher know where Joseph was buried? … said: Serah, the daughter of Asher, remained from that generation … Moses went to her … said to her: Do you know anything … where Joseph is buried? She said to him: The Egyptians fashioned a metal casket for him and set it in the Nile [Nilus] River … so that its water would be blessed. Moses went and stood on the bank of the Nile. … said to … Joseph, Joseph, the time has arrived … which the Holy One, Blessed be He, took an oath … that I, … will redeem you. And … the oath that you administered to the Jewish people … has arrived. If you show yourself, … good, … if not, we are clear from your oath. Immediately, the casket of Joseph floated

And do not wonder how iron … float, as it is written … “But as one was felling a beam, the ax head fell into the water; … Alas, my master! For it was borrowed. And the man of God said: Where did it fall? And he showed him the place. And he cut down a stick, and cast it in there, and the iron floated up” … And are … matters not … a fortiori: And just as Elisha, … student of Elijah, and Elijah … student of Moses, … iron … float before him, all the more so … before Moses our teacher

Rabbi Natan says: … was buried in the crypt [kabbarnit] of kings. Moses went and stood by the crypt of kings … said: Joseph, the time has arrived … which the Holy One, Blessed be He, took an oath … that: I will redeem you. And … the oath that you administered to the Jewish people … has arrived. If you show yourself, … good, but if not, we are clear from your oath. At that moment, the casket of Joseph shook … Moses took it and brought it … to himself.

And all those years that the Jewish people were in the wilderness, these two arks, one … of a dead man, … and one … of the Divine Presence, … were traveling together, and passersby would say: What is the nature of these two arks? They said … One … of a dead person and one … of the Divine Presence. … And … what … the manner of a dead person to travel with the Divine Presence? They said
This … fulfilled all that is written in this.

And if Moses had not dealt with … would the Jewish people not have dealt with it? But isn’t it written … “And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, they buried in Shechem” … And furthermore, if the Jewish people had not dealt with … would his children not have dealt with it? But isn’t it written … “And they became the inheritance of the children of Joseph,”

What is … For its cedar work shall be its city? … Rabbi Yitzḥak … said: Is a house interlaced with cedars … a city, … Rather, … even a house interlaced with cedars will become unstable [mitroe’a] … Rav Ashi said: Learn from it that when the destruction starts … starts with the threshold, as it is stated: “Desolation shall be in the posts.” And if you wish, say … from here: … and the gate is smitten unto ruin [she’iyya]” … Mar bar Rav Ashi said: I saw it, … and it was goring … like an ox.

Rav Huna said: … song of those who pull ships and lead the herd is permitted, … of weavers is forbidden, … Rav Huna nullified … song, … one hundred ducks stood at a dinar, and one hundred se’a of wheat at a dinar, and there was no desire … Rav Ḥisda came and belittled … wanted … duck for … dinar and it could not be found.
Rav Yosef said: … men sing and women respond, … licentiousness. … women sing and men respond, … as if … fire to chips … What difference is there? … To nullify one before the other,

Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Anyone who drinks … with … four types of instruments brings five … retribution to the world, as it is stated: “Woe to them who rise early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; who tarry late into the night, until wine inflames them. And the harp and the psaltery, the drum and the pipe and wine, are at their feasts, but they do not regard the work of the Lord”

What is written afterward? “Therefore, My people have gone into captivity, for want of knowledge” … that they cause exile to the world; “and their honorable men are famished” … as they bring famine to the world; “and their multitude are parched with thirst” … that they cause the Torah, … to be forgotten by those who learn it. “And mankind is bowed down, and man is humbled” … that they cause the enemy of the Holy One, Blessed be He, … to be brought down, as “man” … nothing other … the Holy One, Blessed be He, as … is stated: “The Lord is a man of war” … “And the eyes of the lofty are humbled” … that they cause the Jewish people to be brought down.
And what … is written afterward … “Therefore,
the netherworld has enlarged her desire, and opened her mouth without measure, and down goes their glory and their tumult and their uproar, and he who rejoices among them”

From … when the early prophets died, … Who … the early prophets? Rav Huna says: This is … David, and Samuel, and Solomon, … Rav Naḥman said: In the days of David … times … rose up … and … times … did not rise up, … that Tzadok, … asked … and … rose up for him, … Abiathar asked and … did not rise up for him, as … is stated: “And Abiathar went up”

Rabba bar Shmuel raises an objection: … “And he set himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had an understanding of the vision of God” … What, is … not … of … Urim VeTummim, … No, … of … prophets,
Come … hear … From … when the First Temple was destroyed, the cities with fields … were nullified, and the Urim VeTummim ceased, and the monarchy ceased from the house of David.

And if a person would whisper to you saying … “And the Tirshatha said to them that they should not eat of the most sacred things, until there stood a priest with the Urim VeTummim” … say to him … like a person who says to his friend, … Until the dead live and the Messiah, … son of David, comes.

Rather, Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: Who … the early prophets, … to exclude Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi, … are … latter prophets. … As the Sages taught … From … when Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi died the Divine Spirit departed from the Jewish people, … And … nevertheless … make use of a Divine Voice

For on one occasion … were reclining in the upper story of the house of Gurya in Jericho. A Divine Voice from Heaven was issued to them, and it said: There is one person among you … whom it is fitting that the Divine Presence should rest upon him … but his generation is not fit for it; … directed their gaze to Hillel the Elder. And when he died, they eulogized him … Alas pious one, alas humble one, student of Ezra.

And again, on another occasion … were reclining in an upper story … in Yavne, … a Divine Voice from Heaven was issued to them, and said: There is one person among you … whom it is fitting that the Divine Presence should rest upon him, but his generation is not fit for it. … directed their gaze to Shmuel HaKatan. And when he died, they eulogized him … Alas humble one, alas pious one, student of Hillel.

And he too, … said … at the time of his death: Shimon, … and Yishmael, … for the sword, and their colleagues for killing, and the rest of the people for plunder, and great troubles are destined to befall the people. … And they also sought to say about Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava, … Alas pious one, alas humble one, but the moment was disturbed … eulogies are not given for those killed by the monarchy,

From … when the … Temple was destroyed the shamir ceased … The Sages taught: … shamir … with which Solomon built the Temple, as it is stated: “For the house, when it was built, was built of whole stone from the quarry” … these words … as they are written, … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

Rabbi Neḥemya said to him: And is it possible to say so? But isn’t it already stated: “All these were costly stones, … sawed with saws” … If so, what … the verse states: … were not heard in the house when it was being built” … that he would prepare … outside … and bring … inside … Rabbi … said: The statement of Rabbi Yehuda … appears … with regard to the Temple stones, and the statement of Rabbi Neḥemya … with regard to the stones of the … house.

And … Rabbi Neḥemya, … for what … did the shamir come? … It … necessary for that which is taught … These stones … they may not be written on with ink, because it is stated: “Like the engravings of a signet” … And they may not be scratched on with a scalpel [izemel], because it is stated: “In their full settings”

Rather, … writes … on them in ink, and shows them, … shamir … from outside, … and they split … of their own accord, like this fig that splits in the summer without losing anything … and like this … a valley that cracks in the rainy season without losing anything

The Sages taught: This shamir, its size is that of a barleycorn, and it was created in the six days of creation, and nothing hard can withstand it. In what is it kept, … They wrap it in tufts [sefogin] of wool and place it in a leaden vessel [itenei], full of barley bran,

Rabbi Ami says: From … when the First Temple was destroyed, shiny [peranda] silk [shira] and white glass ceased … This is also taught … From … when the First Temple was destroyed, shiny silk, white glass, and iron chariots ceased; and some say … even congealed wine that comes from Senir, … which is similar to round fig cakes

And … sweetness of the honeycomb [nofet tzufim] … What … nofet tzufim? Rav says: Fine flour that floats … on the top of the sieve [nafa], which is similar … to dough kneaded with honey and oil. And Levi says … two loaves stuck together in an oven, which keep swelling until they reach each other. And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: This is honey that comes from elevated areas [tzipiyya]. … From where may … be inferred … As Rav Sheshet would translate … Like the bees spread out and fly all over the world and bring honey from mountainous plants.

We learned … there … Anything that is poured … ritually pure. … apart from zifim honey and wafer … What … zifim? Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Honey … they … falsify [mezayyefin] it, … And Reish Lakish says: … after its place, as it is written: “Ziph and Telem and Bealoth”

Similarly, you … say … “When the zifim came and said to Saul, does not David … What is … zifim, … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … people who … falsify [hamzayyefin] their words. And Rabbi Elazar says: … after their place, as it is written: “Ziph and Telem and Bealoth.”

men of faith ceased. Rabbi Yitzḥak says: These are people who believe in the Holy One, Blessed be He, … As it is taught … Rabbi Eliezer the Great says … whoever has bread in his basket … and says: What shall I eat tomorrow, … he is nothing other … from those of little faith.

And this is what Rabbi Elazar said: What is … which is written: “For who plunders the day of small things” … What caused the table, … of the righteous to be plundered, … in the future? … the … they possessed. … That they did not believe in the Holy One, Blessed be He, … Rava said: … These are the small children of the wicked ones of the Jewish people,
who plunder, … their fathers’ future judgment. … say before Him: Master of the Universe, because You were destined to exact punishment from … why did You blunt their teeth with

Rabbi Ile’a bar Yeverekhya says: If it were not for the prayer of David … all Israel would be sellers of fat [revav], … as it is stated: “Place for them mastery, O Lord” … And Rabbi Ile’a bar Yeverekhya … says: If it were not for the prayer of Habakkuk, two Torah scholars would have to cover themselves with a single cloak … and engage in Torah study … as it is stated: “Lord, I heard Your report and was afraid; O Lord, revive Your work in the midst of the years” … Do not read: “In the midst [bekerev] of the years [shanim],” but in the closeness [bikrov] of two [shenayim].

And Rabbi Ile’a bar Yeverekhya says: … two Torah scholars who are walking along the way and there are no words of Torah between them, … they are deserving of being burned in fire. As it is stated … “And it was as they walked along, talking, that behold, there appeared a chariot of fire … The reason … that there was speech … but if there had been no speech, they … deserving of being burned

And Rabbi Ile’a bar Yeverekhya says: … two Torah scholars who reside in the same city and they are not pleasant to each other with regard to halakha, … one … die and … one … exiled. As … is stated: “That the manslayer might flee there, who slays his neighbor without knowledge” … and “knowledge” … nothing other … Torah, as it is stated: “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge”

Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya, says: … any Torah scholar who engages in Torah … while experiencing the pressure … his prayer is listened to, as it is stated: “For, O people that dwells in Zion at Jerusalem, you shall weep no more; He will surely be gracious to you at the voice of your cry. When He shall hear, He will answer you” … and after it is written: “And the Lord shall give you sparse bread and scant water”

Rabbi Abbahu says: … is satiated with the glory of the Divine Presence, as it is stated … “And your eyes shall behold your Teacher.” Rabbi Aḥa, son of Ḥanina, said: Even the … partition … pargod … is not locked before him, as it is stated: “And your Teacher shall not hide Himself anymore”

Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua: From the day that the Temple was destroyed, there is no … Rava says: Each and every day is more cursed than the previous one, as it is stated … “In the morning you will say, would that it were evening, and in the evening you will say, would that it were morning” … which morning … If we say … the following morning, does he know what will be … Rather, … that has passed;

But … why does the world … exist? … By the sanctification that … order … and … Let His great name … of aggada. As it is stated: “A land of thick darkness, as darkness itself; a land of the shadow of death, without any order” … Therefore, … there are orders … shall appear from … the darkness.

dew has not descended for a blessing, and the taste has been removed from fruit. It is taught … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: … purity has removed the taste and the aroma; … tithes … have removed the fat of grain.

Rav Huna found a fragrant date. He took it and wrapped it in his shawl. Rabba, his son, came … said to him: I smell the aroma of a fragrant … said to him: My son, there is … purity in you, … He gave it to him. Meanwhile, Abba, … son, arrived. … took … gave it to … said to … My son, you have made my heart rejoice … and you have blunted my teeth, … This … that people say: The love of a father is for the sons; the love of the sons is for their own sons,

Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov took care of Rav Ya’akov, the son of his daughter, … When … grew up, … said to him: Give me water to drink. He said to him: I am not your son, … And this … that people say: Raise, raise … I am the son of your daughter,
MISHNA: In the war [pulemus] of Vespasian … decreed upon the crowns of bridegrooms, … and upon the drums,
In the war of Titus they … decreed upon the crowns of brides, and … that a person should not teach his son Greek.
In the last war, … they decreed that a bride may not go out in a palanquin inside the city, but our Sages permitted a bride to go out in a palanquin inside the city,

From … when Rabbi Meir died, those who relate parables ceased; from … when ben Azzai died, the diligent ceased; from … when ben Zoma died, the exegetists ceased; from … when Rabbi Akiva died, the honor of the Torah ceased; from … when Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa died, the men of … action ceased; from … when Rabbi Yosei the Small died, the pious were no more. And why was he called the Small? Because he was the smallest of the pious,

From … when Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai died, the glory of wisdom ceased; from … when Rabban Gamliel the Elder died, the honor of the Torah ceased, and purity and asceticism died. From … when Rabbi Yishmael ben Pavi died, the glory of the priesthood ceased; from … when Rabbi … died, humility and fear of sin ceased.

GEMARA: The Sages taught: Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya’ir says: From … when the … Temple was destroyed, the ḥaverim and free men … were ashamed, and their heads were covered … and men of action dwindled, and violent and smooth-talking men gained the upper hand, and none seek, and none ask, and none inquire
Upon whom … for us to rely? … upon our Father in Heaven.

Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: From the day the … Temple was destroyed, … Scholars have begun to become like scribes … and scribes have become like beadles, and beadles have become like ignoramuses, and ignoramuses
are increasingly diminished, and none ask and none seek. Upon whom is there to rely? … upon our Father in Heaven.

In the … approach of the Messiah, impudence will increase and high costs will pile up. … the vine shall bring forth its fruit, wine will … be expensive. And … monarchy shall turn to heresy, and … no … reproof … The meeting place … will become … promiscuity, and the Galilee shall be destroyed, and the Gavlan will be desolate, and the men of the border shall go round from city to city … but they will find no mercy.

And the wisdom of scribes will putrefy, and people who fear sin will be held in disgust, and the truth will be absent. The youth will shame the face of elders, elders will stand before minors. … A son will disgrace a father; a daughter will rise up against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A man’s enemies … the members of his household. The face of the generation … like the face of a dog; a son will no … be ashamed before his father. And upon what is there for us to rely? … upon our Father in heaven.

Rav says … they taught … only … of salt and sulfur, but … of myrtle and rose are permitted. And Shmuel says … even … of myrtle and rose are prohibited, … of reeds and bulrush are permitted. And Levi says: Even … of reeds and bulrush are prohibited. And likewise Levi teaches in his baraita: Even … of reeds and bulrush are prohibited.

and upon the drums. … What is … drum [irus]? Rabbi Elazar says: A drum with one mouth. … Rabba bar Rav Huna made a tambourine for his son. His father, … came … broke it. He said to him: … confused for a drum with one mouth, … go and make for him … on the mouth of an earthen jug [ḥatzava], or on the mouth of … a kefiza,

in the war of Titus … decreed upon the crowns of brides. … What are … crowns of brides? Rabba bar bar Ḥana says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: A city of gold, … This is also taught … Which are … crowns of brides … a city of gold. However, one may make it as a cap of fine wool [meilat].

taught: … even decreed upon the canopy of grooms. … What is … canopy of grooms … the golden crimson [zehorit] … This is also taught … These are the canopy of grooms … The golden crimson … But he may make a papyrus [papirit] … and hang upon it whatever he wants,

that a person should not teach his son Greek. The Sages taught … When the kings of the Hasmonean monarchy besieged each other … Hyrcanus was outside of … and Aristoblus was inside. On each and every day they would lower dinars in a box … and … would send up … daily offerings

A certain Elder was there, … who was familiar with Greek wisdom. He communicated to … by … Greek wisdom, … He said to them: As long as they are engaged in the … service, they will not be delivered into your hands. … on the following day, … they lowered dinars in a box, they sent up a pig to them. Once … reached halfway … wall, it inserted its hooves … Eretz Yisrael shuddered four hundred parasangs.

they said … that time: Cursed is the person who raises pigs, and cursed is the person who teaches his son Greek wisdom. And with regard to that year … we learned … An incident … in which the omer, … came from Gaggot Tzerifim, and the two loaves … from the valley of Ein Sokher.

Is that so? But didn’t Rabbi … say: In Eretz Yisrael, why … the tongue of Syriac [Sursi], … Rather, … either … the sacred tongue, … or … the … tongue of Greek. And Rav Yosef … said: In Babylonia, why … the … tongue of Aramaic? Rather, … either … the sacred tongue, … or … the tongue of Persian,
Greek tongue is discrete and Greek wisdom is discrete,

And is Greek wisdom prohibited? But didn’t Rav Yehuda say … Shmuel said in the name of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: What is … which is written: “My eye affected my soul, due to all the daughters of my city” … There were a thousand children in … father’s house, … Five hundred … learned Torah, and … five hundred learned Greek wisdom, and there only remained of them, … me, here … and the son of … father’s brother, … in Asia Minor [Asya].

of the house of Rabban Gamliel are different, … they were close to the monarchy, … As it is taught … cuts … komi … is … ways of the Amorites, … they permitted Avtolos ben Reuven to cut … komi … as he is close to the monarchy, … they permitted the house of Rabban Gamliel … Greek wisdom, because they are close to the monarchy.
In the last war … decreed that a bride may not go out in a palanquin … What is the reason … Due to modesty,

from … when Rabban Yoḥanan … died, wisdom ceased. The Sages taught: From … when Rabbi Eliezer died, … the Torah scroll had been interred, … From … when Rabbi Yehoshua died, council and … thought ceased, … From … when Rabbi Akiva died, the … arm of Torah, … ceased, and the fountains of wisdom were sealed.

From … when Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya died, the crowns of wisdom ceased, as “the crown of the wise is their riches” … From … when Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa died, the men of … deeds ceased. From … when Abba Yosei ben Katonta died, the pious men ceased. And why was he called Abba Yosei ben Katonta? Because he was among the diminished [miktanei] of the pious people,

From … when ben Azzai died, the diligent ceased; from … when ben Zoma died, the exegetists ceased. From … when Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel died, locusts ascended … and troubles proliferated. From … when Rabbi … died, … troubles multiplied.

from … when Rabbi … died, humility and fear of sin ceased. Rav Yosef said to the tanna … Do not teach … humility … for there is … me. Rav Naḥman … said to the tanna … Do not teach … fear of sin … for there is … me.

And the Rabbis say … one is required to say: It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence, only … brings … from a country overseas … and … one who delivers … And … who brings … from … region to … region within … overseas countries is … required to say: It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence. Rabbi Yehuda says: … from Rekem eastward … and Rekem … is like east … From Ashkelon southward … and Ashkelon … is like south … from Akko northward … and Akko … is like north … Rabbi Meir says: Akko is like Eretz Yisrael with regard to … bills of divorce.

One who brings a bill of divorce … within Eretz Yisrael is not required to say: It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence. And if there are those who contest it, … it should be ratified through its signatories.

It was stated … Rav says … Babylonia … like Eretz Yisrael with regard to bills of divorce, and Shmuel says … like outside of Eretz

on his left, to the west of the road, … pure with regard to … the land of the nations, … and obligated in the … tithe … and in … the Sabbatical … until … where it is known to you that it is exempt. And the Rabbis, what do they do with this … “And for the border”? … They require it to … islands … And Rabbi Yehuda … verse is not required … islands,
Rabbi Meir says: Akko is like Eretz Yisrael … raised a dilemma before Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba: One who sells his slave to … Syria, … he considered like one who sells … outside of Eretz … or not?

said to them: You learned … Rabbi Meir says … Akko … like Eretz Yisrael with regard to bills of divorce, … With regard to bills of divorce, yes, … with regard to slaves, no, … and all the more so Syria, which is far more distant

a certain man who sent a bill of divorce to his wife … The agent said: I do not know her. … said to him: Go give … to Abba bar Minyumi, as he knows her, and he will go and give it to her. … came and did not find Abba bar Minyumi, … He found Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa and Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa, and Rav Safra was sitting among them. … said to him: Transfer your words, … before us, as when Abba bar Minyumi comes, we will give … to him, and he will go and give it to her.
