There are … who say … Rava said: Rav Safra struck three ordained Sages mistakenly. Rav Ashi … said: What … the mistake? … what did … say to … Abba bar Minyumi … and not you
a certain man who sent a bill of divorce to his wife … He said to the agent: Do not give … to her until thirty days … Circumstances … within … thirty days that were beyond … control,

was embarrassed … Ultimately, the matter was revealed that … was … betrothed … Rava said: If they said … with regard to a married woman … would they say … with regard to a betrothed woman,
Rava said: We certainly raise this dilemma:

is obvious that … disagree … lest you say … what … retroactive … from the time … until the … time … teaches us

so-and-so and so-and-so the judges, in such and such a place,

orphans who came to divide their father’s property, the court appoints a steward … apotropos … for them, and they select for them, … a fine portion. … have grown up, … can protest … And Rav Naḥman said his own … When they have grown up, they cannot protest, for if so, what advantage … the court have?

You … even say … Rabbi Yehuda, … Rabbi Yehuda states … only with regard to a single mention … But … entire Torah scroll … not … Because … it would look speckled,

a certain … who came before Rabbi Abbahu … said to him: … the Torah scroll that I wrote for so-and-so, I did not process its parchment with the proper intention. … said to him: The Torah scroll is … in whose possession? … said to him: … in the possession of the buyer. … said to him: Since you are deemed credible to cause the loss of your wage, … you are deemed credible to cause a loss … the Torah scroll.

And … what … is … different from … Rabbi Ami … There it can be said … he made the mistake of Rabbi Yirmeya. … Here, … since … that … he causes the loss of his entire wage, and … comes and says … say … he speaks … truth

And … about a stolen beam that was … built into a large building [bira], … receives … the value … due to an ordinance … for the penitent.

GEMARA: Rava says: … from the testimony of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda … says to witnesses: See this bill of divorce that I … give to … and then he says … Take this promissory note, … she is divorced … Didn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda say … we do not require … consent … Here too, … we do not require … consent.

Isn’t … obvious? … Lest you say: Since he said … Take this promissory note, … cancel … teaches us: If it is so that … cancel … he would have told … witnesses … And the reason he said … due to embarrassment,
about the … a minor daughter of a non-priest … while … a deaf-mute woman … may not partake … What is the reason … decreed … lest a deaf-mute … feed teruma to … deaf-mute
And let him feed … a minor … eats … animal carcasses?
decreed … lest a deaf-mute … feed teruma to … competent

about a stolen beam that was … built … the Sages taught … one robbed … a beam and built it into a building, Beit Shammai say: … destroy the entire building and return the beam to its owners. about a sin-offering … through robbery, … Ulla says: By Torah law, … Whether it is known or … it is not known … it does not effect atonement
What is the reason … despair … does not by itself … acquire … And what is the reason … said … it was not … known … it effects atonement? … so that the priests not be distraught
The Rabbis said to Ulla: … But didn’t we learn … for the benefit of the altar, … said to them: When the priests are distraught, the altar is found idle.
but Rav Yehuda says: By Torah law, whether it is known or it is not known … it effects atonement … What is the reason … despair … by itself … acquire
And what is the reason … said … it is known … it does not effect atonement? … not say … the altar consumes stolen property.
Granted, … Ulla, … this is the reason that … teaches … a sin-offering: … But according to … Rav Yehuda, … why … specifically … a sin-offering; … a burnt-offering, as well,

is speaking … It is not necessary, … It is not necessary … a burnt-offering, which is entirely … But even … a sin-offering, where … the fat and the blood go up … on the altar and the rest is consumed by the priests, even so they issued a decree … so … should not say … the altar consumes stolen property.

We learned … about a sin-offering that … through robbery … that is not publicly known … that it effects atonement … for the benefit of the altar. Granted, according to … Ulla, … works out well, … But according to … Rav Yehuda, it should have … the opposite,
That is also what … is saying: … it is not known … it effects atonement, … is known, it does not effect atonement, for the benefit of the altar.

Rava raises an objection … one stole … and consecrated … and afterward he slaughtered or sold … he pays double payment … but he does not pay fourfold or fivefold payment, … And it is taught … with regard to … outside … in a case like this, … punishable by karet … And if you say … despair … does not by itself … acquire … what is the relevance of … karet?

Rav Sheizevi said: … karet by rabbinic law. … laughed at him. Is there … karet by rabbinic law? Rava said to them: A great man has spoken, do not laugh at him. … karet that comes to him through the words … the Sages … placed … in his possession, so that he would become liable for it.

Rava said: … this … is certainly a dilemma for me. When the Sages placed … in his possession, … from the time of the theft or from the time of the consecration? What is the difference … with regard to its wool and with regard to its offspring. … What … Rava then said, … It stands to reason … from the time of the consecration. … so that the sinner not profit

MISHNA: … Sicarii [Sikarikon] did not … in Judea in the … people were being killed in the war. From … people were being killed in the war and onward, … Sicarii did … there. What … one … purchased … from a Sicarius, … and … returned and purchased … from the … landowner, his purchase is void. … from the … owner and … he returned and purchased … from a Sicarius, his purchase stands.

one … purchased from the husband … and … he returned and purchased … from the wife, … his purchase is void. … from the wife, and … he returned and purchased … from the husband, his purchase stands. This … initial … mishna.

the court of those … after … said: … one who purchased … from a Sicarius, he must give the … owner one-fourth … When … At a time when … is unable to purchase … But if he is able to purchase … he precedes anyone
Rabbi … convened a court, and they counted … that if … remained before, … the Sicarius … twelve months, whoever first purchases … acquires possession … but he must give the … owner one-fourth
GEMARA: … Now … in … people were being killed in the war, there were no Sicarii … from … people were being killed in the war and onward there were Sicarii?

Rav Yehuda said: … is saying … they did not apply the law of Sicarii, … Rabbi Asi said: … issued three decrees … first decree … anyone who does not kill … should … be killed. … second … anyone who kills … should pay four dinars … last … anyone who kills … should … be killed. Therefore, … first and second … since … would kill … owing to the danger … would fully transfer ownership
the last … say … Now let him take … tomorrow I will claim it from him in court.

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: What … which is written: “Happy is the man who fears always, but he who hardens his heart shall fall into mischief” … Jerusalem was destroyed on account of Kamtza and bar Kamtza. … the King’s Mountain was destroyed on account of a rooster and a hen. … Beitar was destroyed on account of a shaft from a chariot [rispak].

Jerusalem was destroyed on account of Kamtza and bar Kamtza. … as … a certain man whose friend … Kamtza and whose enemy … bar Kamtza. He … made … feast … said to his servant: Go bring me … Kamtza. … went … brought him … bar Kamtza.

came and found … sitting … said to … That man is the enemy [ba’al devava] of that man, … What … do you want here? Arise … leave. … said to him: Since I have … come, let me stay and I will give you money … whatever I eat and drink.

said to him: No, … said to him: I will give you money for half of the feast; … said to him: No, … said to him: I will give you money for the entire feast; … said to him: No, … took … by his hand, stood him up, and took him out.

said … Since the Sages were sitting … and did not protest … learn from it that they were content … I will … go and inform [eikhul kurtza] against them to the king. He went … said to the emperor: The Jews have rebelled against you. … said to him: Who says … said to him: … send them an offering … see whether they … sacrifice it.

went and sent with him … three-year-old calf. While … was coming … he made a blemish on … upper lip. And some say … on … eyelids, a place where according to us, … is a blemish, but according to them, … is not a blemish.

the Sages thought to sacrifice … due to … peace … government. Rabbi Zekharya ben Avkolas said to them: … will say … blemished … may be sacrificed … on the altar. … thought to kill him so that he would not go and speak … Rabbi Zekharya said to them: … will say … one who makes a blemish on sacrificial … is to be killed.
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The … humility of Rabbi Zekharya ben Avkolas destroyed our Temple, burned our Sanctuary, and exiled us from our land.
sent Nero Caesar against … When he came … He shot an arrow to the east … came … fell in Jerusalem. … to the west … it … fell in Jerusalem. … in … four directions of the heavens, … fell in Jerusalem.

He said to a child: Tell me a verse … He said to him … “And I will lay My vengeance upon Edom by the hand of My people Israel” … said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, wishes to destroy His Temple, and He wishes to wipe his hands with that man, … he fled … became a convert, and … Rabbi Meir descended from him.

sent Vespasian Caesar against … He came … laid siege … three years. There were … in … these three wealthy people: Nakdimon ben Guryon, ben Kalba Savua, and ben Tzitzit HaKesat. … Nakdimon ben Guryon … because the sun shined [nakad] on his behalf, … Ben Kalba Savua … because anyone who entered his house when he was hungry as a dog [kelev] would leave satiated [save’a]. Ben Tzitzit HaKesat … his ritual fringes [tzitzit] dragged … on blankets [keset], … There are … who say that his seat [kiseh] was found among the nobles of Rome,

One … said to … I will feed … with wheat and barley. And one … said to … with wine, salt, and oil. And one … said to … with wood. … And the Sages gave … praise to he … wood, … As Rav Ḥisda would give all of the keys [aklidei] to his servant, except … to … for … wood, … As Rav Ḥisda said: One storehouse [akhleva] of wheat requires sixty storehouses of wood … had … to sustain … for twenty-one years.

There were certain zealots among … The Sages said to them: Let us go out and make peace with … did not allow them … said to … Let us go out and engage in battle against … the Sages said to them: You will not be successful. … arose and burned … these storehouses [ambarei] of wheat and barley, and there was … famine.

Marta bat Baitos was … wealthy women of Jerusalem. She sent … her agent and said to him: Go bring me fine flour [semida]. By the time he went, … was … sold. He came … said to her: There is no fine flour, … there is … flour. She said to him: Go … bring me … By the time he went, … was … sold. He came and said to her: There is no … flour, … there is coarse flour [gushkera]. She said to him: Go … bring me … By the time he went, … was … sold. He came and said to her: There is no coarse flour, … there is barley flour. She said to him: Go … bring me … by the time he went, … was … sold.
She had … removed her shoes, … she said: I will go out … and see if I can find something to eat. … dung, … stuck to her foot, and, … she died.

Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai read concerning her … “The tender and delicate woman among you who would not adventure to set the sole of her foot … There are … who say … she ate a fig of Rabbi Tzadok, and became disgusted and died. … Rabbi Tzadok observed fasts … forty years, … that Jerusalem would not be destroyed. … that when he would eat something it was visible from the outside … And when he would eat … they would bring him figs … he would suck out their liquid and cast … away.
as she was dying, she took out all of … gold and silver … threw it in the marketplace. She said: Why do I need this? And this is as it is written: “They shall cast their silver in the streets

Abba Sikkara was the leader of the zealots [biryonei] of Jerusalem … the son of the sister of Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai. … sent … to him: Come to me in secret. He came, … said to him: Until when will you do this and kill everyone through starvation? … said to him: What can I do, for if I say something to them they will kill me. … said to him: Show me a method … that I will … leave … possible that … there will be … small salvation.

said to him: … Pretend to be sick, and have everyone come and ask … bring something putrid and place it near you, so that … will say that you have died … And … have your students enter … and let no one else come in so that … not notice that you are … light. As … know that a living … is lighter than a dead

did this. Rabbi Eliezer entered from one side and Rabbi Yehoshua from the other side … When they arrived at the entrance … wanted to pierce him … said to them: … will say … they pierce … their teacher. … wanted … to push him … said to them: They will say … they push … their teacher. … opened the gate … he was taken out.

When … reached there, … he said: Greetings to you, the king; greetings to you, the king. … said to him: You are liable for two death penalties, one … I am not a king and … you call me king, and furthermore, if I am a king, why didn’t you come to me until now? … said to him: … what you said … I am not a king,

in truth, you are a king, … As if you are not a king, Jerusalem will not be handed over into your hand, as it is written: “And the Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one” … And “mighty one” … only a king, as it is written: “And their mighty one shall be of themselves, … And “Lebanon” … only the Temple, as it is stated: “That good mountain and the Lebanon” … And … what you said … If I am a king why didn’t you come to me until now, there are zealots among us … did not allow us

said to him: If … a barrel of honey and a snake [derakon] is wrapped around it, wouldn’t they break the barrel in order to … the snake? … was silent … Rav Yosef … read … about him, and some say … Rabbi Akiva … Who turns wise men backward and makes their knowledge foolish” … should have said … to … we take tongs, remove the snake, and kill it, and … we leave the barrel

In the meantime, … a messenger [feristaka] arrived from Rome, … said to him: Rise, for the emperor has died, and the noblemen of Rome plan to appoint you as … leader … was wearing … one shoe, … he tried to put on the other one, it would not go on … He … tried to remove the other … it would not come off. He said: What is this?

said to him: Be not distressed … good tidings have reached you, as it is written: “Good tidings make the bone fat” … But what is the remedy? … said to him: Have someone with whom you are displeased come and pass before you, as it is written: “A broken spirit dries the bones” … He did this, and … went on … said to him: Since you are so wise, why didn’t you come to … me until now? … said to him: But didn’t I … tell you? … said to him: I also told you

said to … I will be going … and I will send someone else … But … ask something of me that I … give you. … said to him: Give me Yavne and its Sages … and … the dynasty of Rabban Gamliel … and … doctors to heal Rabbi Tzadok. Rav Yosef read … about him, and some say … Rabbi Akiva … Who turns wise men backward and makes their knowledge foolish” … he should have said to him to leave … this time.
And … He maintained … might not do that much … and there would not be even a small … salvation.

What … doctors to heal Rabbi Tzadok? … The first day they gave him water to drink … bran [parei]. The next … water … flour mixed with bran [sipuka]. The following day … water … flour. … his stomach to broaden little by little.
went … sent Titus … “And he shall say: Where is their God, their rock in whom they trusted?” … This is the wicked Titus, who insulted and blasphemed God on High.

What did … do … He took a prostitute with his hand, and entered the Holy of Holies … He … spread out a Torah scroll … and committed a sin, … on it. … he took a sword and cut into the curtain … And a miracle was performed and blood spurted forth. … he … thought … he had killed himself. … As it is stated: “Your enemies roar in the midst of Your meeting place; they have set up their own signs for signs”

Abba Ḥanan says: … “Who is strong like You, O Lord?” … Who is strong and indurate like You, as You hear the abuse and the blasphemy of that wicked man and remain silent. … the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught … “Who is like You, O Lord, among the gods [elim]” … Who is like You among the mute [ilmim],

What … do? He took the curtain and formed it like a large basket, and brought all of the … vessels of the Temple and placed them in it. And he put them on a ship to go and be praised in his city … as it is stated: “And so I saw the wicked buried, and come to their rest; but those that had done right were gone from the holy place, and were forgotten in the city; … ” … Do not read … as “buried [kevurim].” Rather, … collected [kevutzim]. … do not read … as “and were forgotten [veyishtakeḥu].” Rather, … And they were praised [veyishtabeḥu].
There are … who say … actually buried. … even items that had been buried were revealed to them,

at sea … a wave rose up against him … to drown him. … said: It seems to me that their God, … has power only in water. Pharaoh rose … He drowned him in water. Sisera rose … He drowned him in water. … too, He has risen up against me to drown me in water. If He is … mighty, let Him go up on dry land and … wage war against me. A Divine Voice issued forth and said to him: Wicked one, son of a wicked one, grandson of Esau the wicked, … I have a lowly creature in My world and it is called a gnat.
Why is it called a lowly creature? … because it has an entrance … but it does not have an exit

Go up on dry land and make war with it. He went up on dry land, … a gnat came, entered his nostril, and picked at his brain for seven years. … one day he passed by the gate of a blacksmith’s shop. … heard the sound of a hammer … was silent … said: … there is a remedy … Every day they would bring a blacksmith who hammered before him. He would give four dinars … to a gentile … to a Jew he would … say: It is enough for you that you see your enemy … He did this for thirty days … From that … forward, since … became accustomed … it became accustomed

It is taught … Rabbi Pineḥas ben Arova said: I was … among the noblemen of Rome, and when … died they split open his head and found … the size of a sparrow weighing two sela. It was taught in … baraita: … like … year-old pigeon weighing two litra.

Abaye said: We have a tradition … its mouth … of copper and its claws were … iron. When … was dying, he said to … Burn that man, … and scatter his ashes across the seven seas, so that the God of the Jews should not find me and stand me for judgment.

Onkelos bar Kalonikos, the son of Titus’s sister, wanted to convert … He went … raised Titus … through necromancy, … said to him: Who is … important in that world … said to him: The Jewish people. … Should I … attach … to them … said to him: Their commandments are numerous, and you will not be able to fulfill them. … Go … battle against them in that world, and you will become the chief, as it is written: “Her adversaries [tzareha] have become the chief” … Anyone who distresses [meitzer] Israel will become the chief. … said to him: What is the punishment of that man, … said to him:
That which he decreed against himself, … Every day his ashes are gathered, and they judge him, and they burn him, and they scatter him over the seven seas.

went and raised Balaam … through necromancy. He said to him: Who is … important in that world … said to him: The Jewish people. … Should I … attach … to them … said to him: You shall not seek their peace or their welfare all the days … said to him: What is the punishment of that man, … said to him: … in boiling semen,

went … raised Jesus the Nazarene … through necromancy. … said to him: Who is … important in that world … said to him: The Jewish people. … Should I … attach … to them … said to him: Their welfare you shall seek, their misfortune you shall not seek, … anyone who touches them is … as if he were touching the apple of his eye

said to him: What is the punishment of that man, … said to him: … with boiling excrement. As the Master said: Anyone who mocks the words of the Sages will be sentenced to boiling excrement. … Come … see the difference between the sinners of Israel and the prophets of the nations of the world.
is taught: Rabbi Elazar says: Come and see how great is the power of shame, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, assisted bar Kamtza, … and … He destroyed His Temple and burned His Sanctuary.

the King’s Mountain [Tur Malka] was destroyed on account of a rooster and a hen. … It was customary … that when they would lead a bride and groom … they would take out a rooster and a hen before them, … to say … Be fruitful and multiply like chickens.

One day a troop [gunda] of Roman … passed by … and took … from them. … fell upon them and beat them. … came and said to the emperor: The Jews have rebelled against you. … came against them … there was a certain man … bar Deroma who could jump … a mil, and he killed … The emperor … took his crown and set it on the ground … He said: Master of the Universe, if it is pleasing to You, do not give over that man, … and his kingdom into the hands of … one man.
his … mouth … caused bar Deroma to stumble, as he uttered … “Have You not rejected us, O God, so that You go not forth, O God, with our hosts?” … David also say this? … David uttered … as a question,

He entered an outhouse, a snake came … eviscerated him, and he died. … said: Since a miracle was performed for me, … I will let … be this time … He let them be and went … They leapt … ate, drank, and lit … candles … that the image [bilyona] … on a seal [gushpanka] was visible from a distance of a mil. … said: The Jews are rejoicing over me. … he went back … came against them.

Rav Asi says: Three hundred thousand men with drawn swords entered the King’s Mountain and massacred … for three days and three nights. And … on … side … weddings and … festivities … and they did not know about each other,

“The Lord has swallowed up without pity all the habitations of Jacob” … when Ravin came … he … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: This … six hundred thousand cities … King Yannai had in the King’s Mountain. … Rav Yehuda says … Rav Asi says: King Yannai had six hundred thousand cities in the King’s Mountain, and each of them … as … those who left Egypt, except for three … was double … those who left Egypt.

These … those … Kefar Bish, Kefar Shiḥalayim, and Kefar Dikhrayya. … Kefar Bish, … would not open … houses to guests. Kefar Shiḥalayim … their livelihood was … from … cress [shaḥalayim]. … Kefar Dikhrayya, … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Their women would first give birth to boys, and afterward give birth to girls, and … they would stop

Ulla said: I myself saw that place, and it could not hold even six hundred thousand reeds, … A certain heretic said to Rabbi Ḥanina: You lie … said to him: With regard to … it is written: Land of the deer … Just as the skin of a deer cannot hold its flesh, … so too, … Eretz Yisrael, when it is settled, it expands, but when it is not settled, it contracts.
Rav Minyumi bar Ḥilkiya, Rav Ḥilkiya bar Toviya, and Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya were … sitting together. They said: If there is someone who has heard anything about Kefar Sekhanya of Egypt, … let him relate

One of them began … and said: … an incident involving a betrothed man and woman … who were taken captive by gentiles and … married them off to each other. … said to … Please do not touch me, as I do not have a marriage contract from you, … And until … his death … did not touch

And when he died … said to … Eulogize this … who conquered [shepitpet] his passion [beyitzro] more than Joseph. As … Joseph it was only for a short time … whereas this … each and every day. … Joseph … not in one bed … whereas this … in one bed … Joseph … not his wife, whereas … this … his wife,

Another … began … and said: It once happened that … forty se’a … stood at one dinar. … the rate went down one se’a [modeya], … And they checked … and they found a father and son who had engaged in sexual intercourse with a betrothed young woman on Yom Kippur. They brought … to court and stoned them, and the rate returned to its … level.

another … began … and said: … an incident … involving a man who set his eyes upon his wife to divorce her, but her marriage contract was large … What did he do? He went and invited his friends, gave them food and drink, made them drunk, and lay … in one bed. He … brought the white of an egg, … and placed it … between them. He … stood witnesses over them … and went to court

A certain Elder of the disciples of Shammai the Elder was there, and Bava ben Buta … his name. He said to them: This is … I received from Shammai the Elder: Egg white … contracts … by fire, whereas semen is absorbed … by the fire. They checked … and found in accordance with his statement … They … brought … to court, administered lashes to him, and made him pay … marriage contract

Abaye said to Rav Yosef: But since … were so righteous, what is the reason that they were punished … said to him: … because they did not mourn for Jerusalem, as it is written: “Rejoice with Jerusalem, and be glad with her, all you that love her, rejoice with joy with her, all you that did mourn for her”

Beitar was destroyed on account of a shaft from a carriage. … it was customary … when a boy was born they would plant a cedar … a girl … would plant a cypress [tornita]. And when they would … marry … they would cut … and construct … canopy … One day the emperor’s daughter passed by … the shaft of the carriage … broke. … chopped down a cedar … and brought it to her. … came … fell upon them and beat them. … came … said to the emperor: The Jews have rebelled against you. … came against them

“He has cut off in His fierce anger all the horn of Israel” … Rabbi Zeira says … Rabbi Abbahu says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: These are the eighty thousand … battle trumpets … who entered the city of Beitar when … took it and killed men, women, and children until their blood flowed into the Great Sea. Lest you say … was close … it was a mil away.

It is … taught … Rabbi Eliezer the Great says: There are two rivers in the Yadayim Valley … one flowing one way and one flowing the other way. And the Sages estimated … two parts water to one part blood. … it was taught in a baraita: For seven years the gentiles harvested their vineyards … with the blood of Israel without … fertilizer.

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin says … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa says: An old man from … the inhabitants of Jerusalem related to me: In this valley … Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard … killed 2,110,000 … And in Jerusalem … he killed 940,000 … on one stone, until the blood … flowed and touched the blood of Zechariah to fulfill what is stated: “And blood touches blood”
found the blood of Zechariah, … that it was bubbling up … he said: What is this? … said to him: … sacrificial blood that had been poured … He brought … blood, … and … it was not similar

said to … If you tell me … well … But if not, I will comb your flesh with iron combs. They said to him: What shall we say to you? He was a prophet among us, who used to rebuke us about heavenly matters, … we rose up against him, and killed him … and for many years … his blood has not settled.

said to them: I will appease … He brought … the Great Sanhedrin and … a lesser Sanhedrin … killed them alongside … but … did not settle. … young men and virgins and killed them alongside it, but … did not settle. He … brought schoolchildren and killed them alongside it, but … did not settle. … said to him: Zechariah, Zechariah, I have killed the best of them. … please you if I destroyed them all? When he said this, … settled.

At that moment … contemplated … repentance … said … If, for … one soul, … this … that man, … who has killed all of those souls, all the more so … He fled, sent to his house a document detailing … and converted
taught … Naaman, … was a ger toshav, … Nebuzaradan, … was a convert,

of Haman’s descendants studied Torah in Bnei Brak, … of Sisera’s descendants taught children … in Jerusalem, … of Sennacherib’s descendants taught Torah in public. Who are they? … Shemaya and Avtalyon,
this is … that which is written: “I have set her blood upon the bare rock that it should not be covered”

“The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau” … “The voice”; this … the emperor Hadrian, who … killed six hundred thousand on six hundred thousand in Alexandria of Egypt, twice … who left Egypt. “The voice of Jacob”; this is … the emperor Vespasian, who killed four million … in the city of Beitar. And some say: … forty million … “And the hands are the hands of Esau”; this is the wicked kingdom … that destroyed our Temple, burned our Sanctuary, and exiled us from our land.

As it is taught … All pure items whose … had been performed in it, … retroactive … whether … in the private domain or in the public domain, are impure. And Rabbi Shimon says … in the public domain, they are pure, … in the private domain, … is suspended,

Reish Lakish said:
taught … only with regard to the consecrated … the border, … But with regard to lineage, … not … And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … even with regard to lineage.

flogs … on the … presumptive status, in accordance with … Rav Yehuda. As Rav Yehuda says: … had … her neighbors the presumptive status of a menstruating woman, … her husband … is flogged due to … a menstruating woman,

stones or burns … on the … presumptive status, in accordance with … of Rabba bar Rav Huna. As Rabba bar Rav Huna says: … a man and a woman … a boy and a girl who grew up … in … home … they are stoned due to … each other … And they are burned due to … each other

Reish Lakish says in the name of Rabbi Oshaya: This … is … that one burns teruma based on it, … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: This is not the presumption that one burns teruma based on it.

But … according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, what is the presumption that one burns teruma based on it? … As we learned … started dough is in the house, and creeping animals, … and frogs, … are … present there, and pieces … were found in the started dough, if the majority … are creeping animals, … is impure, … If the majority are frogs, it is pure.

is taught … in accordance with … Rabbi Yoḥanan: … Two things do not have the capacity to be questioned, … the Sages deemed them as things that have the capacity to be questioned … a child and an additional

GEMARA: What is the reason … The school of Eliyahu taught: Since women are of light mind

From where are these matters, … Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Yishmael: From where … an allusion from the … Torah to … seclusion? As it is stated … “If your brother, the son of your mother, entices you”

With regard to what is the plain … of the verse written, … Abaye said: … is speaking … It is not necessary. It is not necessary … the son of a father, who hates him … and … gives him bad advice. Rather, … even … the son of a mother, … does not hate him, … say … he should listen to him … teaches us

we say the mishna is not in accordance with … Abba Shaul, as it is taught … any … thirty days … is carried out … in … bosom, … and buried by one woman and two men. But … may not … by one man and two women, … Abba Shaul says: … even … by one man and two women.
You … even say … Abba Shaul, … at the time of acute mourning, … inclination … is broken,

And the Rabbis, … hold in accordance with … Rabbi Yitzḥak, as Rabbi Yitzḥak says … “Why does a living man complain, a powerful man due to his sins?” … Even at the time of a person’s acute mourning, his inclination … overpowers him. … And … Abba Shaul … When that was written, it was written … to one who complains about … ways. we say … supports him: … they provide him with two Torah scholars … lest he engage in sexual intercourse with her along the way, … Torah scholars, yes; … Regular men, no; … Torah scholars are different, in that they know

Peleimu had the habit to say every day: An arrow in the eye of Satan, … One day, it was the eve of Yom Kippur, … appeared to him as a pauper … came and called … to the door, … brought out bread to him. … said to him: On a day like today, everyone is inside … and … I … outside … brought him inside and gave him bread. He was sitting … covered himself with boils and pus, and he was doing repulsive things … said to

Sit properly … said to him: Give me a cup. They gave him a cup. He coughed up his phlegm and spat it into … They berated him … sink … and die. They heard … saying: Peleimu killed a man! Peleimu killed a man! … fled and hid himself in the bathroom. … followed him … fell before him. One day, … he was studying in his garden, she adorned herself and repeatedly walked past him. He said: Who are you? She said: I am Ḥaruta, … returning from my day … He propositioned her. She said to him: Give me that pomegranate from the top of the tree … He leapt up, went, … brought it to her,

When he came home, his wife was lighting … oven. He went and sat inside it. She said to him: What is this? He said to her: Such and such an incident … She said to him: It was I. He paid no attention to her, … until she gave him signs … He said to her: I, in any event, intended to transgress. … All the days of that righteous man he would fast … until he died by that death

As it is taught … “Her husband has made them null; and the Lord will forgive her” … With regard to what … is the verse speaking? … to a woman who vowed … be a nazirite, and her husband heard and nullified her … And she did not know that her husband had nullified her … and she drank wine and contracted impurity from a corpse,

When Rabbi Akiva came to this verse he would cry. He said: And if … one who intended to eat pork, and … lamb came up in his hand, … the Torah … says: She requires atonement and forgiveness, all the more so … one who intended to eat pork and pork came up in his hand

a man may be secluded with his mother. even with an animal. … Abaye removed … from the entire field … Rav Sheshet transferred … of the fence. Rav Ḥanan from Neharde’a happened … to Rav Kahana in Pum Nahara. when … have grown up, this one sleeps in his garment … And how … Rav Adda bar Rav Azza says … Rav Asi says: A girl … age … nine years and one day; a boy … age … twelve years and one day. Rabbi Elazar says: Even one who does not have … A dilemma was raised before … one who does not have a wife at all, or perhaps … in … where she is not residing with him? Come … hear: Even one who has … but she is not residing with him may not act as a teacher of children.
Rabbi Yehuda says: … may not herd … It is taught … They said to Rabbi Yehuda: Jews are not suspected of … homosexual intercourse nor of … an animal.

MISHNA: Anyone who has professional dealings … with women may not be secluded with women. … And a person may not teach his son a trade … women, … Rabbi Meir says: A person should always teach his son a clean and easy trade and pray … to the One to Whom wealth and property belong, as … there is no trade that does not include … poverty and wealth, … Poverty does not … from a … trade, nor does wealth … from a … trade, … rather, all is in accordance with … merit.

Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Have you ever seen a beast or a bird that has a trade? And … they earn their livelihood without anguish. But … were created only to serve me, and I, … was created to serve … formed me. Is it not right that I should earn my livelihood without anguish? But I, … have … evil actions and have lost my livelihood.

Abba Guryan of Tzadyan says in the name of Abba Gurya: A person may not teach his son … a donkey driver, a camel driver, a pot maker, a sailor, a shepherd, or a storekeeper. … as their trades are the trades of robbers; … Rabbi Yehuda says in … name: Most donkey drivers are wicked, … and most camel drivers, … are … fit … Most sailors are pious, … The best of doctors is to Gehenna, and … the fittest of butchers is a partner of Amalek.

we do not say … since … is suspect with regard to financial … he is suspect with regard to … an oath. … As if you do not say so, … that which the Merciful One states, … one who admits to part of the claim must take an oath, let us … say … since he is suspect with regard to financial … he is suspect with regard to … an oath.
There, … evading … in accordance with … of Rabba
Know … as Rav Idi bar Avin says … Rav Ḥisda says: One who denies … a loan … is fit to bear witness … a deposit … disqualified from bearing witness

But … that … that Rami bar Ḥama teaches: … four … bailees … require denial of part … and admission of part … an unpaid bailee, and a borrower; a paid bailee, and a renter. … let us say … since he is suspect with regard to financial … he is suspect with regard to … an oath

But … that which Rav Huna says … administer an oath to him that … is not in his possession. Let us say … since he is suspected of financial … he is suspect with regard to … an oath

Rav Aḥa of Difti said to Ravina: But … doesn’t … violate the prohibition of: “You shall not covet

But … that … Rav Naḥman says, … administer an oath of inducement to him, … Let us say … since he is suspect with regard to financial … he is suspect with regard to … an oath.

And furthermore, that which Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches … both … take an oath and take … from the employer, … Let us say … since he is suspect with regard to financial … he is suspect with regard to … an oath.

And furthermore, … that which Rav Sheshet says: … administer three oaths to … an oath that I was not negligent in … it; … an oath that I did not misappropriate … an oath that it is no … in my possession, … let us say … since he is suspected of financial … he is suspected with regard to … an oath.
Rather, … we do not say … since one is suspected of financial … he is suspected with regard to … an oath.
Abaye said: … we suspect … perhaps … has an old loan … to
If so, … Let him take … without … an oath,
Rather, … We suspect … perhaps … uncertain … he has an old loan … to
But … don’t we say … seizing … property due to an uncertain … he may also take an oath … due to … uncertainty?

Rav Sheshet, son of Rav Idi, said: People refrain from … an oath … uncertain but do not refrain from … property … uncertain. What is the reason … property can be returned, … an oath cannot be retracted.
Rabbi Zeira raises a dilemma: … one … seized it … in our presence, … what is
What are the circumstances? If … remained silent, … he admits to … And if he shouted … what … should he have done?

No, … necessary … where he was silent initially, … and … later shouted. What … since he was … silent, he admitted to … Or perhaps, since he is shouting now … the matter is revealed that … that he was silent initially … he thought: The Rabbis … saw him

Rav Naḥman says: Come … hear … In what … is this statement said … where both of them are … holding … But … garment was in the possession of … one of them, the burden of proof rests upon the claimant, … What are the circumstances … If we say … as it is taught, … obvious … Rather, … where one of them seized it in our presence,

No, … here we are dealing with … where they came before us, … while both were holding … and we said to them: Go divide … and they left … and afterward came … while one of them was holding it. This … said: … admitted to me … And that … said: I rented … to him for money … as we say to him: Until now you suspected him of … a robber, … and now you rented … to him without witnesses?

And if you wish, say … as it is taught, … they came before us while … one of them was holding … but the other was hanging on … And … even according to Sumakhos, who says … property of uncertain ownership … divide … without an oath, … Sumakhos concedes that hanging … is … nothing.

If you say … one seizes … in our presence … removes it from his possession, … consecrated … consecration … not … if you say … one seizes … in our presence … does not remove it from his possession, … consecrated … without seizing it, what is
Since the Master said … a declaration to the Most High is equivalent to a transfer to an ordinary … considered like one who seized it,

Or perhaps … now, in any event, he did not … seize … it … And it is written: “And when a man shall sanctify his house to be sacred … Just as his house is in his possession, so too, anything … in his possession, to the exclusion of this … which is not in his possession,
Come … hear … as … a certain

bathhouse over which two … were arguing, … This … said: It is mine, and that … said: It is mine. One of them arose … consecrated … Rav Ḥananya and Rav Oshaya and all the Rabbis kept away from … And Rav Oshaya said to Rabba: When you go … before Rav Ḥisda in … Kafrei, ask him

When … came to … Sura … Rav Hamnuna said to him: … is … mishna … uncertainty … firstborns, whether a human firstborn or an animal firstborn, whether … kosher … or non-kosher … the burden of proof rests upon the claimant. … And it is taught in that regard … prohibited from shearing and from working

And here, where … says … a priest … seized … does not remove it from his possession, as it teaches … the burden of proof rests upon the claimant, … when … did not seize it, … prohibited from shearing and working

Rabba said to him: … You say … the sanctity of a firstborn. Actually, I will say to you … a priest seized it, … removes it from his possession, … And nevertheless, … prohibited from shearing and from working … as sanctity that emerges by itself is different.
Rav Ḥananya said to Rabba: … is taught … that supports your … The … uncertain enter the pen to be tithed.
And if it enters your mind … seized by a priest, … does not remove it from his possession, why do … enter the pen? … this … exempting his property … with the property of a priest?

Abaye said to him: If … due to that … does not support the Master. Here, we are dealing with … where … has only nine … and it, … Since whichever way you … If … subject to the obligation … tithes properly. And if … not subject to the obligation … nine … not subject to tithing.
Abaye then said: That which I said is not correct, as, … uncertain is not subject to tithing, as we learned … one of … counted jumped … into … among … all those … are exempt

And if it enters your mind … uncertain requires tithing, let him tithe … whichever way you … Because if … obligated … he is tithing properly. And if it … not … obligated … is exempt … due to … a tally fit
as Rava says: A tally fit … exempts
Rather, what have you to say … The Merciful One states: … a certain tenth … but not an uncertain tenth, … Here too, … the Merciful One states … a certain tenth … and not an uncertain tenth,
Rav Aḥa of Difti said to Ravina: What are … uncertain … If we say … firstborns … uncertain, the Merciful One states: … shall be sacred … But not … that is already sacred

Rather, … an uncertain redemption of a firstborn donkey, … And … in accordance with … of Rav Naḥman, as Rav Naḥman says … Rabba bar Avuh says: An Israelite who has ten donkeys … firstborn … uncertain in his home separates ten lambs … and tithes … and they … belong to him,

What … was … about … of the bathhouse? Come … hear … as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin said: There was … incident … the school of Rav Ḥisda, and Rav Ḥisda … the school of Rav Huna, and … resolved … based on that which Rav Naḥman says: … any property that … cannot recover … by legal process, … he consecrated it … consecration is not

one can recover … by legal process, … he consecrated it, … consecration … although he has not … recovered it? But doesn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan say: … robbed … and the owner did not despair … neither … can consecrate it; this … because it is not his, and that … because it is not in his possession?
Did you think … we are dealing with a movable bath? … we are dealing with a bath … ground, … once … can recover it by legal process … exists in his possession.

Rav Taḥalifa from the West, … taught … before Rabbi Abbahu: … two … grasping a garment, this … takes up to where his hand reaches, and that … takes up to where his hand reaches, and they divide the remainder, … equally. Rabbi Abbahu indicated … And … with … an oath.

But … how can you find … the mishna … As … teaches that they divide … between them, and does not teach that this … takes up to where his hand reaches … Rav Pappa said: … where … they are holding onto the fringes [bekarkashta]
Rav Mesharshiyya said: Learn … a cloth … from … once … has grasped three by three … of … we consider … and gave it to his neighbor;
because … as though it were severed … and … effects the acquisition,

But … what … is … different from … of Rav Ḥisda? As Rav Ḥisda said: … a bill of divorce in … hand, and a string … in his hand, if … can … pull … and bring it to him, she is not divorced; and if … not … she is divorced.
There, … we require … severance … and … there is no … here, … we require … giving, and there is
Rava says: … if … garment was … with gold … they divide … obvious? … No, … necessary … where the gold is in the middle
This too … obvious; … No, … necessary … where … closer to one … Lest you say that … say to … Divide … this … teaches us that … say to him … What did you see that … you … divide … that … Divide … this

The Sages taught … two … are grasping … note, … creditor says: … is mine, … and I … dropped it and I … found it, and … debtor says: … was … yours, … but I … repaid you, … the … note must be ratified through its signatories … the statement of Rabbi
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: … divide
fell into the possession of a judge … it may never be removed … Rabbi Yosei says: … retains its presumptive status
The Master said … the … note must be ratified through its signatories. And … creditor collects the entire … But doesn’t … hold … the mishna … two people holding
Rava says … Rav Naḥman says: In … ratified … everyone agrees … divide … They disagree … where … not ratified.
Rabbi … holds … admits that he wrote … note, … must ratify it … And … if he ratifies … he divides … and if he does not ratify it he does not divide

And Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel holds … admits that he wrote … note, … is not required to ratify it … And … even if … does not ratify it, … they divide
fell into the possession of a judge it may never be removed

And … it is not necessary … no ratification written in … as it can be said … wrote … to borrow … but he … did not borrow … Rather, … even … a ratification written in … as … a ratified … should not return … as we suspect that … repayment,
And Rabbi Yosei says: … retains its presumptive status. … And we do not suspect that … repayment; … But does Rabbi Yosei not suspect that … repayment?
But isn’t it taught … found a marriage contract in the marketplace, … when the husband admits … must return … to the wife. … the husband does not admit … should not return it to this … or to that
Rabbi Yosei says … is still under … her husband, … must return … to the wife … was widowed or divorced, he should not return it to this … or to that
Reverse … fell into the possession of a judge, it may never be removed; … the statement of Rabbi Yosei. And the Rabbis say: It retains its presumptive status.
If so, … of the Rabbis … and … of the Rabbis … difficult.

the marriage contract is entirely … Rabbi Yosei; … And … is incomplete, and this … it is teaching: … the husband does not admit … should not return it to this … or to that … In what … is this statement said? … where … was widowed or divorced. But … she is still under … her husband, … must return … to the wife. As Rabbi Yosei says: … she is still under … her husband, … must return … to the wife. … was widowed or divorced, he should not return … to this … or to that
Rav Pappa said: Actually, do not reverse … Rabbi Yosei was telling the Rabbis … according to their statement,

In my … even if she was widowed or divorced we do not suspect … payment. … according to your … concede to me, in any event, … while she is still under … her husband … return … to the wife, as … is not … subject to payment.
And the Rabbis said to him … say … he gave her bundles

Ravina said: Actually, reverse … the first … and … The reason … of the Rabbis here, … is that we suspect that … two marriage contracts; … And Rabbi Yosei … he does not suspect that … two marriage contracts;

Rabbi Elazar says: … dispute … in … where both are grasping the standard … or both … the essential … But … one … is grasping the standard … and … one is grasping the essential … this … takes … standard … and that … takes … essential … And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Actually, they divide
And … even … one is grasping the standard … and one the essential … But isn’t it taught … This … takes up to where his hand reaches … No, … necessary … where … essential … is located in the middle.

If so, what … of stating … No, … necessary … where … is closer to one … Lest you say … say to … Divide … this … teaches us that … say to him … What did you see that … you … divide … that … Divide … this
Rav Aḥa of Difti said to Ravina: According to … Rabbi Elazar, who says this … takes … standard … and that … takes … essential … why do … Does he need … to cover the opening of his flask?
said to him: … of … monetary

can say this: … note that has … date … on it; how much … worth? And … that does not have … date … on it; how much … worth? … of … note that has … date … on it, … can collect … from liened … But … the other … cannot collect … from liened … the other … gives him
And … also … where we said … divide … to … monetary … As, if you do not say so, … two … holding a garment, … also divide … But … ruin it. … This … not difficult,
as it is fit … for small
But … which Rava said, … if … garment was … with gold … they divide … also … that they divide … ruin it. … That … not difficult, as … it is fit … for the children of kings

But … that which we learned … two … were sitting on an animal … also … that they divide … ruin it. Granted, … a kosher … fit … for … meat. But … a non-kosher … ruin it … Rather, … monetary … Here too, … monetary
Rami bar Ḥama says: That is to say: … one who … lifting a found item on behalf of another, the other … acquires

As, if it enters your mind … the other does not acquire … this … would be considered as though … lying on the ground, and that … as though … lying on the ground, and neither this … nor that … acquires … Rather, isn’t it … conclude from … one who … lifting a found item on behalf of another, the other … acquires

Rava said: … actually I … say to you … one who … lifting a found item … on behalf of another, the other … does not acquire … And here … this is the reason … Since … acquires … for himself, he also acquires … for the other

Know … as, if … says to his agent: Go out and steal … for me, and … stole … exempt … but partners who stole … liable … What is the reason … not because we say … since … who … acquires … for himself, he also acquires … for the other … Learn from it
Rava said … Now that you said … we say: Since [miggo] … a deaf-mute and … competent … who lifted a found item … since … deaf-mute acquires … competent … acquires
Granted, … deaf-mute acquires … as … mentally competent … lifted it for him; … But how does … mentally competent … acquire
Rather, say … deaf-mute acquires … competent … does not acquire … And what … miggo … Since [miggo] in general two deaf-mutes … acquire … this … too, … acquires

What … this … if you say … one who … lifting a found item on behalf of another, the other … acquires … this statement … where he lifts it with the intention of … the other person … this … lifted … with the intention of … himself; … he does not acquire … does he acquire … for others?
Rather, say … since … competent … does not acquire … deaf-mute does not acquire

And if you would say: … what … is … different from … general … two deaf-mutes, … there, … the Sages instituted … for them … so that they will not come to quarrel … Here, … says … competent … does not acquire … can I acquire

Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Adda, said to Rav Ashi: From where … is Rami bar Ḥama’s inference … If we say … from the first clause … two … holding a garment, … there … this … says: All of it is mine, and I lifted the entire … and that … says: All of it is mine, and I lifted the entire

Rather, … from that which is taught … This … says all of it is mine and that … says all of it is mine. Why do I … this … as well? … Rather, learn from … superfluous … mishna … one who … lifting a found item on behalf of another, the other … acquires
But … didn’t we … establish … the first clause … to … a found item, and the latter clause … to … buying and selling,

Rather, … from the latter clause … this … says all of it is mine and that … says half of it is mine. Why do I … this … as well? … Rather, learn from … superfluous … mishna … one who … lifting a found item on behalf of another, the other … acquires
And from where … that … to … a found item? Perhaps … to … buying and selling.

And if you would say: If … to … buying and selling, what … of stating … was necessary … enter your mind to say … the one who says: Half of it is mine, should be considered the equivalent of one returning a lost item; … and … he should be exempt … teaches us that … this … is employing artifice. … thinking: If I say … all of it is mine I will need to take an oath. I will state this … as I will … be considered the equivalent of one returning a lost item, and I will be exempt

Rather, … from this … two … were sitting on an animal, … Why do I … this … as well? … Rather, learn from … superfluous … mishna … one who … lifting a found item on behalf of another, the other … acquires
But perhaps this … teaches us that … who sits … also acquires

Rather, … from the last clause … When they … admit … or when they have witnesses … they divide … without … an oath. To what … If … to … buying and selling, … need to be said? Rather, is it not … to a found item? … And learn from it … one who … lifting a found item on behalf of another, the other … acquires
And Rava said to you … since he acquires … for himself he can also acquire … for another
two … were sitting … Rav Yosef said: Rav Yehuda said to me:
I heard two … from Master Shmuel, … who sits … and … who leads … one … he … acquires … and … one … he does not acquire … But I do not know … which of them.

What are the circumstances? If we say … who sits … alone and … leads alone, is there anyone who says that … who leads … alone does not acquire … Rather, if … it could be said that … does not acquire … it is … sits … that it could be said.
Rather, his dilemma … sits … while … leads … What … sitting … take precedence, as … is in his grasp, … or perhaps … leading … takes precedence, as it walks because of him?

Rav Yosef said: Rav Yehuda said to me: … let us see … ourselves, as we learned … the one leading … incurs the forty … and the one sitting in the wagon [bakaron] … incurs the forty … Rabbi Meir deems the one sitting in the wagon exempt,

And from … that … Shmuel reversed … and taught: And the Rabbis deem the one sitting in the wagon exempt, … Conclude from it … sits … alone does not acquire … and all the more so … sits … while … leads
Abaye said to Rav Yosef: Didn’t you say to us many times … Let us see … ourselves, … And you did not say to us … in the name of Rav Yehuda.

said to him: Indeed [ivra], … and I also remember that I said to him … How can the Master resolve … sits … from … sits … sits … does not hold the reins, … sits … holds the reins. And … said to me … Rav and Shmuel both say … reins … does not effect acquisition

There are … who say … Abaye said to Rav Yosef: How can the Master resolve … sits … from … sits … sits … does not hold the reins, … sits … holds the reins. … said to him: Idi taught … like this: … reins … does not effect acquisition
was also stated … Rabbi Ḥelbo says … Rav Huna says: … reins … from another … acquires … with regard to … a found … or with regard to … the property of a convert … does not effect acquisition.

What … the term reins [moseira]? Rava said: Idi explained to me … like a person who transmits [moser] an item to another, … Granted, … from another, … effects acquisition … as the other … hands … to him. But … of a found … or of … the property of a convert, who is handing him … to acquire

raises an objection … two … were sitting … on an animal, … whose … If we say … Rabbi Meir, now, … sits … acquires … Is it necessary … sits … Rather, is it not … the Rabbis? And learn from it … sits … acquires

With what are we dealing here? … where … leads, … with his legs. … If so, this is … leading … two types of leading, … Lest you say … is sitting … takes precedence, as he is … leading … and … holding it … teaches us
Come … hear … two … who were pulling a camel or driving a donkey … or one who was pulling … and one … driving
they … acquired … in that manner. Rabbi Yehuda says: Actually, … acquires … only … pulling in … a camel or driving in … a donkey,
In any event, it is taught … Or one who was pulling and one … driving, … pulling and driving … indeed … but sitting … not.

The same is true … even sitting … And … that … teaches … pulling and driving … to exclude … of Rabbi Yehuda, who says … only … pulling in … a camel or driving in … a donkey. … teaches us that even … the opposite … acquires
If that is so, … let … combine … and teach them … two … who were pulling or driving either a camel or a donkey,
There is one manner … that … does not acquire … Some say … pulling a donkey … and some say … driving a camel
And … there are those who raise an objection … from the latter clause … acquire … in that manner. … in that manner … to exclude what? Is it not to exclude … sits … No, … to exclude the opposite
If so, that is … Rabbi Yehuda. … There is … between them … one manner … which … does not acquire … Some say … pulling a donkey … and some say … driving a camel
Come … hear … one … is sitting … a donkey and one … is holding the reins, this … acquires … donkey, and that … acquires the reins. Learn from it … sits … acquires
Here too, … to … driving … with his feet … If so, … one who is sitting should acquire … of the reins too. … say: This … acquires … donkey and half of … reins, and that … acquires half of … reins.
Granted, … sitting … acquires … because a mentally competent … has lifted it for him, but in what … does the one holding the reins acquire
say: This … acquires the donkey and … the entire reins, and that … acquires … that … held in his hand.

Rav Ashi said: … This … acquires … donkey and its halter, … and that … acquires … that is held in his hand. And … the rest, … neither this … nor that … acquired

If that is so, what is the reason … sits … in the city does not acquire … Rav Kahana said: … because people do not normally ride in the city,

Rather, … we are dealing with … buying and selling … where … said to … Acquire … the way that people … acquire

MISHNA: … was riding on an animal and saw a found item, and said to another … Give … to me, … took it and said: I have acquired it … he has acquired it … if, after giving it to … he said: I acquired it … at the outset, he has said nothing

GEMARA: We learned … there … one who gleaned the produce in the corner of the field, which is given to the poor [pe’a], and said: This … is for so-and-so, a poor person, Rabbi Eliezer says: He … acquired … on … behalf. As Rabbi Eliezer holds … since [miggo], if he … desires, he can renounce ownership of his property and … be poor, and … suitable for him, now too, … suitable for him … And since [miggo] he can acquire … for himself, he can acquire … on behalf of another … as well. And the Rabbis hold … we say miggo once, … we do not say miggo twice.
But … by a poor person on behalf of … poor person, everyone agrees … he acquires … on behalf of … as since [miggo] he can acquire … for himself, he can acquire … on behalf of another … as well.

Granted, if you say … dispute … by a poor person on behalf of a poor person,

whose … the mishna? It is … the Rabbis, … But if you say … dispute … in … a rich person and a poor person but … by a poor person on behalf of a poor person everyone agrees … he acquired … on … behalf, … whose … is this … neither … the Rabbis nor … Rabbi Eliezer.
said to … The mishna … where … said: … at the outset;

So too, it is reasonable … as it teaches in the last clause: … if, after giving it to … he said: I acquired it … at the outset, he has said nothing … Why do I need … At the outset, … in the last clause? It is obvious … even if he did not … say: At the outset, he meant … at the outset, … Rather, isn’t … teach us this: The first clause … where he said: … at the outset?
And the other … taught … the last clause … to shed light on the first clause. The last clause … where he said … at the outset … the first clause, … where he did not say … at the outset.
Rav Naḥman and Rav Ḥisda, who both say: … one who … lifting a found item on behalf of another, the other … does not acquire

What is the reason … it is … one who seizes … for a creditor in a situation that … a disadvantage for others, … and one who seizes … for a creditor in a situation that … a disadvantage for others does not acquire
Rava raised an objection to … Rav Naḥman … The found item of a laborer, … to him
In what … is this statement, … said? … when the employer … said to him: Weed for me today, … Till for me today. … But … said to … Work for me today, … found item is the employer’s,

Rabbi Yehuda says: … unless there is … in it … nine half-kav … for this one and nine half-kav … for that one.
