not … a hall [hateraklin], a drawing room, a dovecote, a cloak, a bathhouse, an olive press, and an irrigated field unless there is enough for this one … and enough for that one … This is the principle: Anything … which … is divided, … retain the name … divides … But if … not … does not divide
When … when … do not both wish … But when both of them wish … they may divide … even … less than … But … sacred writings, … they may not divide … even if both of them wish

GEMARA: Rabbi Asi says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The four cubits … which they said … in addition to … the entrances … That … is also taught … does not divide a courtyard unless … there will be in it eight cubits for this one and eight cubits for that one. … But didn’t we learn … four cubits for this one and four cubits for that one? Rather, conclude from it … in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Asi. … Conclude from it

And there are … who raise … We learned … does not divide a courtyard … unless there will be … four cubits for this one and … four cubits for that one. But isn’t it taught … eight cubits for this one and eight cubits for that one? … Rabbi Asi said … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The four cubits … which they said … in addition to … the entrances
Rav Huna says: A courtyard is divided according to its entrances. … And Rav Ḥisda says: Four cubits are allotted … for each and every entrance, and the rest … is … divided equally

It is taught … in accordance with … of Rav Ḥisda: … the entrances … to a courtyard … four cubits. … this one has one entrance and that one has two entrances, the one who has one entrance takes four cubits, and the one who has two entrances takes eight cubits, and they divide the rest … equally … this one had an entrance eight cubits wide, … takes eight cubits adjacent to the entrance and four cubits in the courtyard. … What are … four cubits in the courtyard doing here? … Abaye said: This … is saying: … he takes eight cubits along the length of the courtyard and four cubits along the width of the courtyard.
Ameimar says: A pit for … animal food [peira desuflei] has four cubits on each and every side … And we said … only when … has no special entrance
But … he designates an entrance … he has four cubits only in front of his entrance.

Rav Huna says: A portico [akhsadra] … does not have … four cubits. … What is the reason … for unloading … its burden. Here he can go inside … and unload. Rav Sheshet raises an objection … Both gates of houses and gates of porticos have … four cubits … When that … is taught, it is … with regard to the portico of a study hall, … obvious that … the portico of a study hall, … it is a proper room. Rather, … a Roman portico,

The Sages taught … A gatehouse, a portico, and a balcony … have … four cubits … five houses open onto the balcony, they only have four cubits … Rabbi Yoḥanan asked Rabbi Yannai: … a chicken coop … have four cubits or does it not have four cubits? … said to him: What is the reason … for unloading … burden … his … Here … climb up … and climb down

Rava asked Rav Naḥman: … a house … half roofed and half unroofed, does it have … four cubits or does it not have … four cubits? … said to him: It does not have … four cubits. … not necessary … roofing is … the inside … since it is possible … to go inside and unload … Rather, even … roofing is … the outside … it is possible … to go inside and unload

Rav Huna asked Rabbi Ami: … one of the residents of an alleyway … wishes to alter his entrance to a different alleyway, … the residents of the … alleyway prevent him … or can they not prevent him … said to him: The residents of … alleyway can prevent him

a billeting … divided according to … people … or … divided according to … entrances … said to him: It is divided according to the … people … That … is also taught … The dung in a courtyard … is divided … according to … entrances … billeting … according to … people
Rav Huna says: … one of the residents of an alleyway wishes to close off … adjacent to his entrance, … the residents of the alleyway can prevent him … it will increase the way for them,

raises an objection … five courtyards open onto an alleyway, all … use … the outermost … and … the outermost … use … its own … And … the other … use … the second … and … the second … use … its own … and … use … the outermost
outcome … the innermost … use … its own … and … use … each and every

is … tanna’im, as it is taught … one of the residents of an alleyway wishes to alter his entrance to a different alleyway, the residents of the … alleyway can prevent him … there had been … sealed and he wishes to open it, the residents of the … alleyway cannot prevent him … the statement of Rabbi … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: … five courtyards which open onto an alleyway, … may all use the alleyway with each other.

Courtyards, who mentioned anything about them? … is incomplete and this … it is teaching: Additionally, … five courtyards which open onto an alleyway, … may all use … the outermost … and the … outermost one … use … own … the statement of Rabbi … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: … five courtyards which open onto an alleyway, … may all use the alleyway.

The Master said: … there had been … sealed and he wishes to open it, the residents of the … alleyway cannot prevent him … Rava says: This was taught only when he did not break its doorposts, … But if he … broke its doorposts, … the residents of the … alleyway can prevent him … Abaye said to Rava: … is taught which supports you:
A house … a sealed … has … four cubits … one broke its doorposts … it does not have … four cubits

A grave whose entrance is sealed does not render all its surroundings ritually impure; … one broke its doorposts and sealed it, … renders all its surroundings ritually impure, … a house … a sealed … does not render all its surroundings ritually impure. … one broke its doorposts, … renders all of its surroundings ritually impure.

Rabba bar bar Ḥana says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … alleyways that are open to another city, … the residents of the city … wished to block them … the residents of the city … can prevent them … It is not necessary … that they can prevent … when there is no alternative route … but they can prevent … even when there is an alternative route.

due to … Rav Yehuda … Rav says. As Rav says: … prohibited from ruining a path that the public has established … of Rav Giddel, as Rav Giddel says: … the public has chosen a route for itself … what they have chosen is chosen,
Rav Anan says … Shmuel says: … alleyways that open onto a public thoroughfare, … the residents of the alleyways wished to put up doors … the people … the public thoroughfare can prevent them

understood from this … this statement … within four cubits … in accordance with … that Rabbi Zeira … Rav Naḥman says, as Rabbi Zeira says … Rav Naḥman says: The four cubits … that are adjacent to the public thoroughfare are considered like the public thoroughfare … But … is not so. There, … with regard to the issue of ritual impurity, … But here, … sometimes the public thoroughfare becomes crowded with people and they enter far

And … not … field unless there is … in it … nine kav … for this one and nine kav … for that one. … And … do not disagree … Sage … in accordance with … his locale, and … Sage … in accordance with … his locale.
what … in Babylonia? Rav Yosef said: … the area of a day’s plowing
What … the area of a day’s plowing? If … a day’s … the planting … not … two … days … the plowing … if … a day’s … plowing … not … day … planting
If you wish, say … a day’s … plowing … since he plows … and … repeats … And if you wish, say … a day’s … planting … rocky ground,
a cistern, … Rav Naḥman said: … the volume of … a day’s irrigation … an orchard, Shmuel’s father says: … an area … three kav,

That … is also taught … one who says to another: I am selling you part of a vineyard, … Sumakhos says: He may not … less than an area … three kav. Rabbi Yosei said: These are nothing other than words of prophecy, … What … in Babylonia? Rava bar Kisna said: Three rows [atzyata] of twelve vines, which is … a person can hoe in … day.

Rabbi Avdimi from Haifa says: From the day that the Temple was destroyed prophecy was taken from the prophets and given to the Sages. … Is that to say … a Sage is not … a prophet? … This is what … is saying: Even though … was taken from the prophets, it was not taken from the Sages.
Ameimar said: And a Sage is greater than a prophet, as it is stated: “And a prophet has a heart of wisdom” … who is compared to whom? You must say … the lesser is compared to the greater.

Abaye said: Know … as a great man makes a statement … and … is … cited in the name of a different great man in accordance with his … Rava … said: And what is the difficulty … Perhaps they were born under the same constellation, … Rather, Rava said: Know … as a great man makes a statement and … is … cited
in the name of … Rabbi Akiva bar Yosef in accordance with his … Rav Ashi said: And what is the difficulty … Perhaps … the same constellation, … with regard to this issue

Rather, Rav Ashi said: Know … as a great man makes a statement and … is … cited as a halakha … to Moses from Sinai in accordance with his … But perhaps … like a blind man … through a skylight. … But does … not offer a reason

Rabbi Yoḥanan said: From the day that the Temple was destroyed, prophecy was taken from the prophets and given to imbeciles and children. … what … to imbeciles? … like this … Mar bar Rav Ashi, who was standing in the street [beristeka] of Meḥoza … he heard a certain imbecile say: The head of the yeshiva who will be appointed in Mata Meḥasya signs … Tavyumei. … said … Who among the Sages signs … Tavyumei? … me. Conclude from … that my hour has arrived, … He arose and went … By the time he arrived, the Sages … decided to appoint Rav Aḥa of Difti as the head

As soon as … heard that … had arrived, … They sent a pair of Sages to him to consult with him, … he detained them. They again sent a pair of Sages … he detained them … until they completed … of ten … Once they reached ten … opened … taught, and expounded. … because one should not open a lecture during kalla, … less than ten
Rav Aḥa … read about himself … Anyone who is treated poorly will not soon be treated well; and anyone who is treated well will not soon be treated poorly.

what … to children? … like this … daughter of Rav Ḥisda, … was sitting on her father’s lap … Rava and Rami bar Ḥama were sitting before him. … said to … Which of them would you want … She said: … both of them. Rava said: And I … last.

Rabbi Avdimi from Haifa says: Before a person eats and drinks he has two hearts, … after he eats and drinks he has only one heart, as it is stated: “A hollow [nevuv] man is two-hearted” … As it is written … “Nevuv luḥot” … which we translate … Hollow with planks,
Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, says: … one who is accustomed to wine, although his heart, … is closed like a virgin, wine opens it, as it is stated: “And new wine opens [yenovev] the virgins”
Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, says: … obvious … a portion … firstborn, and … a portion … an ordinary … he is given … along one boundary, … What … a yavam,

Abaye said: This … is … that … What is the reason … The Merciful One calls … “firstborn” … Rava said: The verse states: “And it shall be, the firstborn” … his being, … is like a firstborn; but … the distribution … is not like a firstborn,

a certain person bought land along the boundary of his father’s property. … When they … divide … said to … Give me my portion … along my boundary. Rabba said: In … such as this, … compels … conduct … of Sodom.
Rav Yosef objects to this, … The brothers … say to him: We assess this … as … valuable, like the property of the house of bar Maryon. … And the halakha … in accordance with … Rav Yosef,

two … land next to two … channels [nigrei], … Rabba says: In … such as this, … compels … conduct … of Sodom … Rav Yosef objects to this, … Sometimes this … continues running … while this … does not continue running … And the halakha … in accordance with … Rav Yosef.

two … next to one channel … Rav Yosef said: In … such as this, … compels … conduct … of Sodom … Abaye objects to this, … can say … I want … sharecroppers to increase. … And the halakha … in accordance with … Rav Yosef … the increase … is … nothing,
channel … one side … and a river … the other side, … is divided diagonally [bekarna zol]

a hall, … not … What is … there is not enough for this one and that one? … Rav Yehuda said: There is a halakha … you set … or I will set … Rav Naḥman said: There is no halakha … you set … or I will set

Rava said to Rav Naḥman: According to you who say … there is no halakha … you set … or I will set … what should they do … a firstborn … and … ordinary … whose father left them a slave and a non-kosher animal … said to him: I say that they work for this one, … one day, and for the other one, … two days.

raises an objection … One who is half-slave half-freeman, … serves his master one day and himself one day; … the statement of Beit Hillel. Beit Shammai say: You have remedied … his master, … you have not remedied his own … He cannot marry a maidservant, … He is … not able to marry a free woman, … he should be idle … but is it not … the world was created only for procreation, as it is stated: “He did not create it to be a waste; He formed it to be inhabited”
Rather, … forces his master to make him a freeman … and … writes a bill … half his value … And Beit Hillel retracted … ruled in accordance with the statement of Beit Shammai.
It is different here, because … I will set … not … You set

Come … hear … two brothers, one poor and one rich, and their father left them a bathhouse or an olive press … built … for profit, … the profit … shared equally … built them for himself … the rich … say to the poor
take servants for yourself, and they will bathe in the bathhouse. … take olives for yourself and come and transform … in the olive press. … There too … You set … not … I will set

Come … hear … Anything which, … is divided, … retains the name … may be divided. … if … not … its monetary … is assessed, … is … tanna’im, as it is taught … You take … measure … and I … less, … listens to him. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: They do not listen to him.

What are the circumstances … If we say it is … as it is taught, what is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel’s reasoning? … Rather, is it not that … is incomplete and this … is saying: … You take … measure … and I … less, … listens to him. … And … you set … or I will set … they also listen to him. And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel comes to say: … they do not listen to him

No, … actually … as it is taught. And with regard to what you said: What is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel’s reasoning? … because … can say to him: If … money … I have no money to give you. … a gift, I am not at ease … as it is written: “But he who hates gifts shall live”

Abaye said to Rav Yosef: That … of Rav Yehuda is … of Shmuel, … as we learned … But … sacred writings, … they may not divide … even if both of them wish … And Shmuel said: They taught … only … in one scroll; but … in two scrolls, they may be divided. And if it should enter your mind … that there is no halakha of: … you set … or I will set … why … specifically to one scroll? Even … in two scrolls, … also
Rav Shalman interpreted … where they both want

Ameimar said: The halakha … there is a halakha of: … you set … or I will set … Rav Ashi said to Ameimar: What … that … of Rav Naḥman, … said to him: I do not know … that is to say, I do not maintain … And … not … But … the father of Ravin bar Ḥinnana and Rav Dimi bar Ḥinnana … left them two maidservants, one … knew how to bake and to cook, and the other … knew how to spin and to weave. … They came before Rava and he said to them: There is no halakha of: … you set … or I will set

different there, since this master wanted both of them and the other master wanted both of them. … when … said to … You take one and I … one, it is not … you set … or I will set … And can we not say so? But … sacred writings, which both of them … want, and Shmuel said: They taught … only … in one scroll; but … in two scrolls, they may be divided. … Rav Shalman interpreted … where they … want

The Sages taught: A person may attach the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings together as one … the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda says: The Torah … by itself, … Prophets … by themselves, and … Writings … by themselves. And the Sages say: Each one … by itself.

And Rabbi Yehuda said: … an incident involving Baitos ben Zunin, who had eight … of the Prophets attached together as one … with the approval of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya. And others say that each and every one … by itself, … Rabbi … said: … an incident where they brought before us the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings attached together as one … and we … deemed them fit.
four … lines … between each book of the Torah, and similarly between one … the Prophets and another. But … the Twelve Prophets … three … lines … And … finish … at the bottom … and begin … at the top

The Sages taught … One who wishes to attach the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings together as one … may attach … He should leave enough … at the beginning … for winding around the pole … And at the end … for winding around the … circumference … And he may finish … at the bottom … and begin … at the top
And if he wishes to cut … he may cut … What is … saying? … This is what … is saying: … so that if he wishes to cut … he may cut

raises a contradiction … Enough … the beginning of the scroll and at its end for winding. … For winding … what? If … for winding around the pole … difficult … circumference … if … for winding around … circumference, … difficult … pole.
Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: … teaches … disjunctively,

Rav Ashi said: When that … is taught, … to a Torah scroll, as it is taught … All … scrolls are wound from the beginning to the end … but a Torah scroll is wound … to the middle … poles, … he attaches at this … and … at the other … Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, said: This is how the scribes in Jerusalem made their scrolls,

The Sages taught: A Torah scroll should not be made … that its length, … is greater than its circumference … nor … its circumference be greater than its length. They asked Rabbi … What should the size of a Torah scroll be? … said to them: … on a hide that was treated with gallnuts [gevil ] … six … How much … on … parchment [kelaf ]? … I do not know.
Rav Huna wrote seventy Torah scrolls … and it happened for him … once … Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov wrote one … on calf hide and it happened … The Sages looked at him … and he died

The Sages said to Rav Hamnuna: Rabbi Ami wrote four hundred Torah scrolls. … said to them: Perhaps he wrote … “Moses commanded us the Torah” … Rava said to Rabbi Zeira: Rabbi Yannai planted four hundred vineyards. … said to him: Perhaps … two … facing … two … one protruding … a tail,

raises an objection … the Ark … that Moses fashioned, its length was two and one-half cubits, its width was one and one-half cubits, and its height was one and one-half cubits … the cubit … being six handbreadths.

And … the tablets, their length was six … their width was six … and their thickness was three … were placed along the length of the Ark, … how much … the tablets occupy … of the Ark? Twelve handbreadths, … Three handbreadths were left there … Deduct a handbreadth from them: One-half … for this wall, … and one-half … for the other wall. … two handbreadths were left there, in which the Torah scroll … lay.

As it is stated: “There was nothing in the Ark except the two tablets of stone which Moses put there” … What … “there was nothing in the Ark except” … a restriction following a restriction, … And … a restriction following a restriction serv … only to amplify … to include a Torah scroll that lies in the Ark.

you have accounted for the … length of the Ark; go … and account for the width of the Ark, … How much … the tablets occupy … of the Ark, … Six handbreadths; … three handbreadths were left there … Deduct a handbreadth from them: One-half … for … this wall and one-half … for … the other wall. … two handbreadths were left there. … so that the Torah scroll would be able to go in and out without being pressed; … the statement of Rabbi Meir.

Rabbi Yehuda … says: … cubit … was five handbreadths … And … the tablets, their length was six … their width was six … and their thickness was three … they were placed along the length of the Ark, … how much … the tablets occupy … of the Ark? Twelve handbreadths, … one-half a handbreadth was left there, … One fingerbreadth … for … this wall and one fingerbreadth … for … the other wall.

you have accounted … the … length of the Ark; go … and account for the width of the Ark, … How much … the tablets occupy in the Ark? Six handbreadths, … one and one-half handbreadths were left there … Deduct one-half a handbreadth, one and one-half fingerbreadths for … this wall, and one and one-half fingerbreadths for … the other wall. … one handbreadth was left there in which the … columns were placed … as it is stated: “King Solomon made himself a palanquin of the timbers of Lebanon; he made its columns of silver, its back of gold, its seat of purple”

And the chest in which the Philistines sent the gift to the God of Israel was placed alongside … as it is stated: “And put the golden devices which you are restoring to Him for a guilt-offering in a chest by the side of it, and send it away that it may go” … And upon … lay the Torah scroll, as it is stated: “Take this Torah scroll and put it at the side of the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord” … it was placed at the side … and not inside
And … how do I realize … “There was nothing in the Ark except … to include

the broken pieces of the … tablets, which were placed in the Ark. … And if it should enter your mind … the circumference of a Torah scroll is six handbreadths, now since any … having a circumference of three handbreadths has a diameter of one handbreadth, … And since … is wound to the middle, … it … more than two handbreadths … the space between … how did … fit in … two handbreadths [pushkei]

Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov said: The scroll of the … courtyard, … was wound to its beginning, … But still, how does … that is two … fit into … two … Rav Ashi said: A small section … was wound … and … placed on top

And … Rabbi Yehuda, … where was the Torah scroll placed before the chest arrived? … A shelf protruded from … and the Torah scroll rested on it. … And … Rabbi Meir, … what does he do with this … at the side of the Ark” … He requires … that … was placed at the side … and that it was not placed between … tablets, but … actually … inside … at the side

And … Rabbi Meir, where were the … columns placed? … Outside … And from where does Rabbi Meir … the broken pieces of the … tablets were placed in the Ark, … He derives … from what Rav Huna … as Rav Huna says: What … which is written: … whereupon is called the Name, the name of the Lord of hosts that sits upon the cherubs” … teaches that … the … tablets and the broken pieces of the … tablets were placed in the Ark.
And … the other … He requires … for … which Rabbi Yoḥanan … as Rabbi Yoḥanan says … Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says: … teaches that the … name … and all of His appellations were placed in the Ark.

And … the other … also require it for that? … Yes, … is indeed so. Rather, from where does he … the broken pieces of the … tablets were placed in the Ark? … He derives … from … which Rav Yosef taught, as Rav Yosef taught … which you broke, and you shall put them … This teaches that … the … tablets and the broken pieces of the … tablets were placed in the Ark.

And … the other … He requires it for … which Reish Lakish … as Reish Lakish says: … which you broke [asher shibbarta]”? … the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses: May your strength be straight [yishar koḥakha] because you broke

The Sages taught: The order of the … Prophets … Joshua and Judges, Samuel and Kings, Jeremiah and Ezekiel, … Isaiah and the Twelve … Consider: Hosea preceded … as it is written: “The Lord spoke first to Hosea” … But did God speak first with Hosea, … Weren’t there many prophets between Moses and Hosea? And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: He was the first of four prophets who prophesied in that period, and they were: Hosea and Isaiah, Amos and Micah. … and … Hosea … should precede

Since his prophecy is written together with … Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi … and Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi were the last of the prophets, he is counted with them. … But let … be written separately and let it precede … since it is small it would be lost.

Consider: Isaiah preceded Jeremiah and Ezekiel; let … Isaiah precede … Since … Kings ends with the destruction … and … Jeremiah … entirely with … the destruction, and … Ezekiel begins with the destruction … but ends with consolation … and Isaiah … entirely with consolation, … we juxtapose destruction to destruction and consolation to consolation.

The order of the Writings … Ruth and the book of Psalms, and Job and Proverbs; Ecclesiastes, Song of Songs, and Lamentations; Daniel and the Scroll of Esther; … Ezra and Chronicles. … And according to the one who says … Job … in the time of Moses, let … Job precede … We do not begin with suffering, … Ruth, … is also … suffering, … suffering which has a future … As Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Why was she named Ruth, … descended from her David who sated, … the Holy One, Blessed be He, with songs and praises.

And who wrote … Moses wrote his own book, … and the portion of Balaam … and … Job. Joshua wrote his own book and eight verses in the Torah, … Samuel wrote his own book, … Judges, and … Ruth. David wrote the book of Psalms by means of ten elders … by Adam the first … by Melchizedek … and by Abraham, and by Moses, and by Heman, and by Jeduthun, and by Asaph,
and by the three sons of Korah.

Jeremiah wrote his own book, and the book of Kings, and Lamentations. Hezekiah and his colleagues wrote … a mnemonic … yod, mem, shin, kuf: Isaiah [Yeshaya], Proverbs [Mishlei], Song of Songs [Shir HaShirim], and Ecclesiastes [Kohelet]. The members of the Great Assembly wrote … a mnemonic … kuf, nun, dalet, gimmel: Ezekiel [Yeḥezkel ], and the Twelve Prophets [Sheneim Asar], Daniel … Daniel … and the Scroll of Esther [Megillat Ester]. Ezra wrote his own book and the genealogy of … Chronicles until his
supports Rav, as Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: Ezra did not ascend from Babylonia … until he established his own genealogy, and … ascended. … And who completed … Nehemiah, son of Hacaliah.

The Master said … Joshua wrote his own book and eight verses of the Torah. … is taught in accordance with the one who says that … Joshua … wrote the … eight verses in the Torah. … as it is taught … “And Moses the servant of the Lord died there” … is it possible that … Moses died, he … wrote “And Moses died there”? Rather, Moses wrote … until this point, … Joshua wrote from this … forward; … the statement of Rabbi Yehuda. And some say … Rabbi Neḥemya

Rabbi Shimon said to him: Is it possible … Torah scroll was missing a single letter? But it is written: “Take this Torah scroll” … Rather, until this point the Holy One, Blessed be He, dictated and Moses repeated … and wrote … From this … forward, … the Holy One, Blessed be He, dictated and Moses wrote with tears. … later, as it is stated … “And Baruch said to them: He dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them with ink in the scroll”

In accordance with whose … is that which Rabbi Yehoshua bar Abba says … Rav Giddel says … Rav says: … one … reads the … eight verses in the Torah, … Shall we say … this is … Rabbi Yehuda and not in accordance with … Rabbi Shimon, … Even … you say … Rabbi Shimon, since they differ … they differ

Joshua wrote his own book. … But isn’t it written … “And Joshua, son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died” … Eleazar completed it. … But isn’t it … written: “And Eleazar, son of Aaron, died” … Pinehas completed it.
Samuel wrote his own book. … But isn’t it written: “And Samuel died” … Gad the seer and Nathan the prophet finished it.

David wrote the book of Psalms by means of ten elders, … But … let it also count Ethan the Ezrahite … Rav says: Ethan the Ezrahite is … Abraham. … it is written here: … Ethan the Ezrahite” … and it is written there: “Who raised up one from the east [mizraḥ], whom righteousness

counts Moses … and it … counts Heman. But doesn’t Rav say: … Heman … is … Moses? … it is written here: “Heman” … and it is written there … “For he is the trusted one in all My house” … There were two Hemans,

Moses wrote his own book, … the portion of Balaam, and … Job. This supports Rabbi Levi bar Laḥma, as Rabbi Levi bar Laḥma says: Job … in the time of Moses. It is written here … “Oh, that my words were written now [eifo]” … and it is written there … “For in what shall it be known here [eifo]”

But … say … in the time of Isaac, as it is written … “Who then [eifo] is he that has taken venison” … Or say … in the time of Jacob, as it is written … “If it must be so now [eifo], do this” … Or say … in the time of Joseph, as it is written … where [eifo] are they feeding their flocks?”

not enter your mind … as it is written … “Oh, that … were inscribed [veyuḥaku] in a book” … and it is Moses who is called the inscriber, as it is written … “And he provided the first part for himself, for there was the inscriber’s [meḥokek] portion reserved”

Rava says: Job … at the time of the spies … it is written here: “There was a man in the land of Utz, whose name was Job” … and it is written there … “Whether there are trees [eitz] in it” … Is it comparable? Here … Utz, … there … eitz. … This is what Moses said to Israel, … Is that man … he whose years are as long as … of a tree and who protects his generation like a tree?

one of the Sages sat before Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani and he sat and said: Job never existed and was never created; … Rather, … was a parable. … said to him: … to you, the verse states: “There was a man in the Land of Utz whose name was Job”

But if that is so, … but the poor man had nothing except one little lamb, which he had bought and reared” … Was there … Rather, it was merely a parable; here too it is merely a parable. … If so, … why … his name and the name of his city?

Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar both say: Job was among those who ascended from the exile … and his house of study was in Tiberias. … raises an objection … The days of Job’s life … from when Israel entered Egypt until they left,
Say … as from when Israel entered Egypt until when they left,

raises an objection … Seven prophets prophesied to the nations of the world, and they are: Balaam and his father … and Job, Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite, and Elihu ben Barachel the Buzite, … He said to him: And according to your reasoning … was Elihu ben Barachel not a Jew? Is it … written: “Of the family of Ram”

Rather, … he prophesied to the nations of the world; … so too … Job … prophesied to the nations of the world. … But did not all the … prophets … prophesy to the nations of the world? … There, … their main prophecies were … to Israel, … here, … their main prophecies were … to the nations of the world.

raises an objection … There was a … pious man among the nations of the world and his name was Job, and he came into the world only to receive his reward. The Holy One, Blessed be He, brought afflictions upon him, … he began to blaspheme and curse. The Holy One, Blessed be He, doubled his reward in this world in order to expel him from the World-to-Come.

is … tanna’im, as it is taught … Rabbi Elazar says: Job … in the days of the judging of the Judges, as it is stated … “Behold, all you yourselves have seen it; why then have you become altogether vain?” … Which generation was completely vain? You must say it was the generation of the judging of the Judges,

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa says: Job … in the days of Ahasuerus, as it is stated: “And in all the world were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job” … which generation were beautiful women sought? You must say it was the generation of Ahasuerus … But … say … in the days of David, as it is written: “And they sought a beautiful maiden” … There, … “throughout the territory of Israel” … here, … Ahasuerus, … throughout the world,

Rabbi Natan says: Job … in the days of the kingdom of Sheba, as it is stated: “And Sheba fell upon them, and took them away” … And the Rabbis say: Job … in the days of … the Chaldeans … as it is stated: “The Chaldeans formed three bands” … And some say … Job … in the days of Jacob and … he married Dina, the daughter of Jacob. … it is written here: “You speak as one of the loathsome women speaks” … and it is written there … “He has done a loathsome act in Israel” … And all … tanna’im hold that Job was a Jew except for … And some say,

As if it should enter your mind … from the nations of the world, … After Moses died, did the Divine Presence rest … on the nations of the world? But doesn’t the Master say: Moses requested that the Divine Presence not rest … on the nations of the world, and … was granted to him, as it is stated: “That we shall be differentiated, I and Your people,

Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The generation of Job was awash in licentiousness, as it is stated: “Behold, all of you yourselves have seen [ḥazitem] it; why then have you become altogether vain?” … and it is written: “Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look [veneḥeze] upon you” … say … prophecy, as it is written: “The vision [ḥazon] of Isaiah ben Amoz” … If so, why do I … “Why then have you become altogether vain”?

And … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: What … which is written: “And it happened in the days of the judging of the Judges” … a generation that judged its judges. … say to … Remove the splinter from between your eyes, … say to him: Remove the beam from between your eyes, … say to him: “Your silver is become dross” … say to him: “Your wine is mixed with water”

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says … Rabbi Yonatan says: Anyone who says that the queen of Sheba [malkat Sheva] … was a woman is nothing other than mistaken. What … malkat Sheba? The kingdom [malkhuta] of Sheba,

“Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and the Satan came also among them. And the Lord said to the Satan: From where do you come? And the Satan answered … said to … Master of the Universe, I have gone to and fro throughout the entire world and I have not found anyone as faithful as Your servant Abraham, to whom You said: “Arise, walk through the land in the length of it and in the breadth of it; for I will give it to you” … And even so, when he did not find a place to bury Sarah before he purchased … for four hundred silver shekels, he did not find fault with Your ways

“And the Lord said to the Satan: Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on earth, … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: That … is stated about Job is greater than that … is stated about Abraham. As with regard to Abraham it is written: “For now I know that you fear God” … with regard to Job it is written: “A perfect and an upright man, one who fears God and turns away from evil”
What … “and turns away from evil”? Rabbi Abba bar Shmuel says: Job was forgiving with his money. … the way of the world … one pays the storekeeper … half-peruta … Job, … would forgive him

“Then the Satan answered the Lord, and said: Does Job fear God for naught? Have You not made a hedge about him, and about his house, … What … “You have blessed the work of his hands”? Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak says: Anyone who took a peruta from Job was blessed.

What … “And his livestock is increased [paratz] in the land” … Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina says: Job’s livestock breached [paretzu] the order of the world. … the way of the world … wolves kill goats, … Job’s livestock, the goats killed the wolves.

“But now put forth Your hand, and touch all that he has, and he will curse You to Your face. And the Lord said to the Satan: Behold, all that he has is in your power; only upon himself do not put forth your hand. … “Now there was a day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house, and there came a messenger to Job, and said: The oxen were plowing, … What … “The oxen were plowing and the asses were feeding beside them”? Rabbi Yoḥanan says: This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave Job a taste
of the World-to-Come,

“While he was yet speaking, there came also another and said: The fire of God … While he was yet speaking, there came also another and said: The Chaldeans formed three bands, and fell among the camels, and have carried them away, … While he was yet speaking, there came also another and said: Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house; and, behold, there came a great wind from across the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, … Then Job arose, and rent his coat, and shaved his head, … And he said: I came naked out of my mother’s womb, and naked I shall return there; the Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away, blessed be the name of the Lord. In all this Job sinned not, nor did he lay reproach on God”

“Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves … And the Lord said to the Satan: From where do you come? And the Satan answered the Lord, and said: From going to and fro in the earth … said before … Master of the Universe, I have gone to and fro across the entire world and have not found anyone as faithful as your servant Abraham, to whom you said: “Arise, walk through the land in the length of it and in the breadth of it; for I will give it to you” … And when he wanted to bury Sarah, he could not find a place to bury her, and … he did not criticize Your ways,

“And the Lord said to the Satan: Have you considered My servant Job, that there is none like him on earth, … And still he holds fast to his integrity, although you moved Me against him, to destroy him without cause”
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Were it not … written in the verse, it would be impossible to say this, … like a person whom others persuade and … persuaded,
It was taught in a baraita … descends … and misleads … ascends … and inflames … anger … receives permission … and takes away the … soul

“And the Satan answered the Lord, and said: Skin for skin, for all that a man has he will give for his life. But put forth Your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse You to Your face. And the Lord said to the Satan: Behold, he is in your hand; only spare his life. So the Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job … Rabbi Yitzḥak says: Satan’s suffering was more difficult than that of Job. … a parable involving a servant whose master said to him: Break the barrel but save its wine.

Reish Lakish says: Satan, the evil inclination, and the Angel of Death are one, … He is the Satan … as it is written: “So the Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord, … He is … the evil inclination, … it is written there: … was only evil continuously” … and it is written here: “Only upon himself do not put forth your hand” … He is … the Angel of Death, as it is written: “Only spare his life” … apparently … depends upon him,

Rabbi Levi says: … Satan, … and Peninnah, … intent … for the sake of Heaven. … Satan, when he saw that the Holy One, Blessed be He, inclined to … Job … he said: Heaven forbid that He should forget the love of Abraham. … Peninnah, as it is written: “And her rival wife also provoked her sore, to make her fret” … Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov taught … in Paphunya, … Satan came and kissed his feet

“In all this Job did not sin with his lips” … Rava says: … he did not sin with his lips, … he sinned in his heart. What did he say … “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked, he covers the faces of its judges; if not he, then who is it?” … Rava says: Job sought to turn the bowl upside down, … Abaye said to him: Job was referring … only to the Satan,

parallel to … tanna’im, … “The earth is given into the hand of the wicked.” Rabbi Eliezer says: Job sought to turn the bowl upside down; Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: Job was referring … only to the Satan.

“Although You know that I am not wicked, and there is none that can deliver out of Your hand” … Rava says: Job sought to exempt the whole world from judgment, … said before … Master of the Universe, You created the ox with split hooves, … You created the donkey with closed hooves, … You created the Garden of Eden, … You created Gehenna; … You created righteous people … You created wicked people; who can restrain You?
And how did Job’s friends answer him? “You do away with fear, and impair devotion before God” … the Holy One, Blessed be He, created the evil inclination, … He … created the Torah … an antidote

Rava interpreted … homiletically: What … which is written, … “The blessing of him that was lost came upon me, and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy” … “The blessing of him that was lost came upon me” teaches that … used to steal a field from orphans, … improve it, and … return it to them; … “I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy” … anywhere that there was a widow whom no one would marry, he would go … cast his name upon her, … and … somebody would … marry her.

“O that my vexation were thoroughly weighed, and my calamity laid in the balances” … Rav says: Dust … in the mouth of Job, … a friendship with Heaven? … “There is no arbiter between us, who may lay his hand upon us both” … Rav says: Dust … in the mouth of Job … is there a servant who rebukes his master? … “I have made a covenant with my eyes; why then should I look upon a virgin?” … Rava says: Dust … in the mouth … Job … he … at other … Abraham did not even look at his own … as it is written: “Now I know that you are a beautiful woman” … by inference that initially he did not know

“As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, so he who goes down to the grave shall come up no more” … Rava says: From here … that Job denied the resurrection of the dead, … “He crushes me with a tempest, and multiplies my wounds without cause” … Rabba says: Job blasphemed with … a tempest and he was answered with … a tempest.

He blasphemed with … a tempest [bise’ara], as it is written: “He crushes me with a tempest.” … said before … Master of the Universe, perhaps a tempest passed before You and You confused Iyov, … with oyev, … He was answered with … a tempest, as it is written: “Then the Lord answered Job out of the tempest, and said: … Gird up now your loins like a man, for I will demand of you and let me know your answer”

said to him: I have created many hairs [nimin] on a person, and for each hair I created its own follicle … so that two … should not draw from one follicle. As were two … to draw from one follicle, they would impair a man’s vision. … I do not confuse one follicle with another, would I confuse Iyov with oyev?

“Who has divided a channel [te’ala] for the torrent … I have created many drops … in the clouds, and for each drop I created its own channel, so that two drops should not emerge from the same channel. As were two drops to emerge from the same channel they would destroy the earth and it would not yield produce. … I do not confuse one drop with another, would I confuse Iyov with oyev? … From where may … be inferred that this … te’ala … a channel? Rabba bar Sheila said: As it is written … “And he fashioned a channel [te’ala] … as … two se’a of seed”

“Or a path for the lightning of thunder,” … I have created many thunderclaps in the clouds, and for each and every thunderclap I created its own path, so that two thunderclaps should not issue forth from the same path. As were two thunderclaps to issue from the same path, they would destroy the world. … if I do not confuse one thunderclap with another, would I confuse Iyov with oyev?
“Do you know when the wild goats of the rock give birth? Can you mark when the hinds do calve?” … This goat is cruel to her young … when she squats

to give birth she ascends to the top of a mountain so that … should fall down from her and die. And I summon her an eagle that receives it with his wings and places it before her; and if … reached … one moment early or was one moment late, … would immediately die. … I do not confuse one moment with another moment, would I confuse Iyov with oyev?

“Can you mark when the hinds do calve?” … The womb of this hind is narrow, … When she squats to give birth, I summon her a snake [derakon] that bites her at the opening of the womb, which … becomes loose, and she gives birth, and if … reached … one moment early or was one moment late, she would immediately die. … do not confuse one moment with another moment, would I confuse Iyov with oyev?

“Job has spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom” … But … it is written … “You have not spoken of Me the thing that is right, like my servant Job” … Rava said: From here … that a person is not held responsible … when he is in distress.

“And Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place, Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him” … What … “they had made an appointment together” … Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: This … teaches that they all entered … one gate … And … taught … three hundred parasangs between each and every one

How did they … know … There are … who say … they … had a crown … And there are … who say they … had trees and when … withered they knew … Rava said … this … that people say: Either a friend like the friends of Job or death.

“And it came to pass, when men began to multiply [larov] on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them” … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … propagation [reviyya] came to the world … Reish Lakish says: Strife [meriva] came to the world. … Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yoḥanan: According to you who say … propagation came to the world, for what … were … Job’s daughters not doubled,

said to him: Granted, … were not doubled in name, … but they were doubled in beauty, as it is written: “He had also seven sons and three daughters. And he called the name of the first Jemimah, and the name of the second was Keziah, and the name of the third one was Keren-happuch”

Jemimah [Yemima]; … she was similar to the day [yom]. Keziah; her scent wafted like … cassia [ketzia] … Keren-happuch; in the school of Rav Sheila they say: She was similar to the horn [keren] of a keresh, … They laughed at this in the West, … a blemish … the horn of a keresh. Rather, Rav Ḥisda said: … like garden saffron [kekurkema derishka], … of its kind. … as it is stated: “Though you enlarge … with paint [pukh],

a daughter was born to Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi … he was upset … His father said to him: Propagation has come to the world … Bar Kappara said to … Your father has consoled you with meaningless consolation, as it is taught … The world cannot endure without males and females, … But fortunate is he whose children are males and woe to him whose children are females. … the world cannot endure without either a spice dealer … or a tanner [bursi], … Fortunate is he whose occupation is a spice seller, … woe to him whose occupation is a tanner.

parallel to … tanna’im: … “And the Lord blessed Abraham with everything [bakkol]” … what bakkol … Rabbi Meir says: … that he did not have a daughter. Rabbi Yehuda says: … that he had a daughter. Others say: Abraham had a daughter and her name was Bakkol. Rabbi Elazar HaModa’i says: Abraham our forefather was so knowledgeable in astrology [itztagninut] that all the kings of the East and the West would come early to his door … Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says: A precious stone hung around the neck of Abraham our forefather; any sick person who looked at it would immediately be healed. When Abraham our forefather died, the Holy One, Blessed be He, hung … from the sphere of the sun, … Abaye said: This … that people say: As the day progresses, sickness is lifted.

Alternatively, … That Esau did not rebel in … lifetime, … Alternatively, … that Ishmael repented in … lifetime. … From where do we … Esau did not rebel in … lifetime? As it is written: … and Esau came in from the field and he was faint” … and … taught: On that day Abraham our forefather passed away, and Jacob our forefather prepared a lentil stew to comfort Isaac, his father,

And what is different about lentils … They say in the West, … in the name of Rabba bar Mari: Just as this lentil has no mouth, … so too a mourner has no mouth, … Alternatively, just as this lentil is … round, so too mourning comes around to the inhabitants of the world. … What is … between … There is … between them … to console … with eggs,

Rabbi Yoḥanan says: That wicked … committed five transgressions on that day … He engaged in sexual intercourse with a betrothed maiden, he killed a person, he denied the principle … he denied resurrection of the dead, and he despised the birthright.

He engaged in sexual intercourse with a betrothed maiden, … it is written here: “And Esau came in from the field”; and it is written there … “For he found her in a field” … He killed a person, … it is written here: … faint”; and it is written there: “Woe is me, for my soul faints before the slayers” … And he denied the principle … it is written here: “What profit is this to me” … and it is written there: “This is my God and I will glorify Him” … And he denied resurrection of the dead, as it is written: “Behold, I am at the point of death” … And he despised the birthright, as it is written: “And Esau despised the birthright”

And from where do we … that Ishmael repented in … lifetime? From … Ravina and Rav Ḥama bar Buzi, … were sitting before Rava, and Rava was dozing … Ravina said to Rav Ḥama bar Buzi: Is it true that you say … any death with regard to which … gevia, … is the death of the righteous? … said to him: Yes. … But … the generation of the flood … said to him: We say … gevia and asifa,

But isn’t there Ishmael, about whom gevia and asifa are written, … Meanwhile Rava, … awoke … said to them: Children [dardekei], this is what Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Ishmael repented in the lifetime of his father, as it is stated: “And Isaac and Ishmael, his sons, buried him”

But perhaps … listed them in the order of their wisdom; … But if that is so, … “And Esau and Jacob, his sons, buried him” … What is the reason … did not list them in the order of their wisdom? Rather, since … allowed … to precede him, … made … his leader, and since he made him his leader, learn from it that he repented in … lifetime.
the Sages taught: … three … to whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave … in this world

a taste of the World-to-Come. They are: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Abraham, as it is written with regard to him: … with everything” … Isaac, as it is written with regard to him: … from everything” … Jacob, as it is written with regard to him: … everything”

three … over whom the evil inclination had no sway. They are: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as it is written … to them, … “With everything,” “from everything,” “everything.” … And some say … even David … as it is written: “And my heart has died within me” … And … the other … He is mentioning his travails.

The Sages taught: … six … over whom the Angel of Death had no sway … and they are: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as it is written … to them, … “With everything,” “from everything,” “everything”; … Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, as it is written … to them … “by the mouth of the Lord”

But with regard to Miriam it is not written: “By the mouth of the Lord.” Rabbi Elazar says: Miriam also died with a kiss, as this is learned … “there” … “there” … to Moses: … And for what … is “by the mouth of the Lord” not stated with … her? It is unseemly to mention

The Sages taught: … seven … over whom the worm and the maggot had no sway, and they are: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Moses, Aaron and Miriam, and Benjamin, son of Jacob. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as it is written with regard to them, … “With everything,” “from everything,” “everything.” Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, as it is written with regard to them: “By the mouth of the Lord”; Benjamin, son of Jacob, as it is written: “And to Benjamin he said: The beloved of the Lord, he shall dwell in safety by Him” … And some say … even David … as it is written: “My flesh also dwells secure” … And … the other … He is asking for mercy,

The Sages taught … four … who died … because of the counsel of the … snake, … And they are: Benjamin, son of Jacob; Amram, father of Moses; Yishai, father of David; and Chileab, son of David. And all of these are known through tradition except for Yishai, father of David, with regard to … it is written explicitly: “And Absalom placed Amasa over the army instead of Joab, and Amasa was the son of a man whose name was Ithra the Israelite, who engaged in intercourse with Abigail, daughter of Nahash, the sister of Zeruiah, mother of Joab” … But was … the daughter of Nahash? Was she not the daughter of Yishai, as it is written: “And their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail” … Rather, … she was the daughter of one who died … because of the counsel of the snake.

MISHNA: A person may not dig a pit close to the pit of another, … And … may not … a ditch, nor a cave, … nor a water channel, nor a launderer’s pond, … unless he distanced … three handbreadths from the wall of another and he plasters lime

And one must distance the solid residue … and … manure, and salt, and lime, and rocks three handbreadths from the wall of another, … Or, alternatively, he … plaster … with lime … One must … distance seeds, … and … the plow, and … urine, three handbreadths from the wall

And one must distance a mill … three … from the lower stone … which is four … from the … upper stone … And … three … from the … base [hakalya] … an oven … which is four … from the … upper rim [hassafa]
GEMARA: … opens by … a pit: … and … he ends with … a wall: … Let … teach: Unless he distanced … three handbreadths from the pit of another,
Abaye said, and some say it was Rav Yehuda … We learned … From the wall of his pit.

But … let it teach: Unless he distanced … three handbreadths from the pit of another, … this teaches us … that the wall of a pit … three handbreadths … difference … with regard to buying and selling, as it is taught … one who says to another: I am selling you a pit and its walls, the wall … must be … three handbreadths

It was stated: … one who comes to … place … close to the boundary … Abaye says: He may … place … close … and Rava says: He may not … place … close … All agree that he may not … place … close … a field … that … is designated for … pits, … When they disagree … with regard to a field that is not designated for … pits.
Abaye says: He may … place … close … as … is not designated for pits, … Rava says: He may not … place … close … as … say to him: Just as you changed your mind and dug … I too … change my mind and dig

There are … who say … All agree … one may … place … close … a field that is not designated for … pits. When they disagree … with regard to a field that is designated for … pits. Abaye says: One may … place … close … even according to … the Rabbis, who say … One must distance a tree twenty-five cubits from a cistern, … there it … as when he plants … there is … a cistern. But here, … when he digs … there is … no cistern

And Rava says: … may not … place … close … even according to … Rabbi Yosei, who says … This one may dig in his … and that one may plant in his … this matter … there, as when he plants … its roots, which … damage the cistern, are not … But here, … say to him: Each and every strike of yours with the hoe loosens my earth,

We learned … a person may not dig a pit close to the pit of another, … reason … is that there is a pit … there is no pit he … close … Granted, according to that … version … in which you said: All agree … one may … place … close … a field that is not designated for … pits, … the mishna … to a field that is not designated for … pits.

But … to that … version … in which you said … they disagree with regard to a field that is not designated for … pits, … Granted, … works out well according to … Abaye, … But according to … Rava, … difficult.
Rava … said to you: Wasn’t it stated with regard to that … Abaye says, and some say it was Rav Yehuda … We learned … From the wall of his pit?

There are … who say … and it was stated with regard to that … Abaye says, and some say it was Rav Yehuda … We learned … From the wall of his pit. … Granted, according to that … version … in which you said: All agree that he may not … place … close … a field … that … is designated for … pits, … the mishna … to a field that is designated for … pits.

But according to that … version … in which you said … they disagree with regard to a field that is designated for … pits, … Granted, … works out well according to … Rava, … But according to … Abaye, … difficult,
Abaye … said to you: The mishna … where … came to … pits at the same time.

Come … hear … rock that … crumbles in … hands, … this one may dig his pit from here, and that one may dig his pit from there. This one distances … three handbreadths and plasters with lime, and that one distances … three handbreadths and plasters with lime. … crumbles in … hands is different.
And he who asked it, why did he ask it? … it was necessary for … crumbles in … hands, … enter your mind to say that since … crumbles in … hands he is required … greater distance. … teaches us
Come … hear … One must distance the solid residue … and … manure, and
salt, and lime, and rocks three handbreadths from the wall of another, or he … plaster … with lime. … reason … is that there is a wall … there is no wall … one may place … close
No, … if there is no wall one may also not place … close … Rather, what does … teach us? … This teaches us that … these … are damaging to a wall.

Come … hear … One must distance seeds, and the plow, and urine three handbreadths from the wall … reason … is that there is a wall, … there is no wall, one may place … close … No, … if there is no wall, one may also not place … close … But rather, what does … teach us? … This teaches us that dampness [dimtunta] is damaging to a wall.

Come … hear … And … a mill … three … from the lower stone … which is four … from the upper stone. … reason … is that there is a wall, … there is no wall, one may place … close … No, … if there is no wall, one may also not place … close … But rather, what does … teach us? … This teaches us that vibrations are damaging to a wall.

Come … hear … And the oven … three … from the base, which is four … from the upper rim … reason … is that there is a wall, … there is no wall, one may place … close … No, … if there is no wall, one may also not place … close … Rather, what does … teach us? … This teaches us that heat is damaging to a wall.
