And the wave raised its voice … to another … My friend, did you leave anything in the world that you did not wash away, that I may come and destroy it? … said to it: Go out … see the greatness of your Master, … as much as a string of sand … I cannot pass, as it is stated: “Will you not fear Me, said the Lord; will you not tremble at My presence? Who has placed the sand for the bound of the sea, an everlasting ordinance, which it cannot pass?”

Rabba said: I have seen … Hurmin, son of Lilith, when he was running on the pinnacles of the wall of … Meḥoza, and a horseman was riding an animal below him but was unable … him. Once, they saddled for him two mules and they stood

on the two bridges of … Rognag, and he jumped from this one to that one, and from that one to this one. And he was holding two cups of wine in his hands and was pouring from this one to that one, and from that one to this one, and not … drop fell to the ground. And that day was … “They mounted up to the heavens, they went down to the deeps; … until … was heard in the house of the king, and they killed him.

Rabba said: I have seen a day-old antelope [urzila] that was … as Mount Tabor. And how … is Mount Tabor? … four parasangs. And the length of its neck … three parasangs, and the place where his head rests … a parasang and a half. It cast feces [kufta] and … dammed up the Jordan.

And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: I have seen a certain frog [akrokta] that was … as the fort [akra] of Hagronya. And how … is the fort of Hagronya? … sixty houses. A snake came and swallowed … A raven came and swallowed the snake, and … up and sat in a tree. Come … see how great is the strength of the tree, … Rav Pappa bar Shmuel said: If I had not been there … I would not believe

And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: Once we were traveling in a ship and we saw a certain fish in … nostril [be’usyeih] a mud eater [akhla tina], … had sat … And the waters thrust … and threw it upon the shore. And sixty districts were destroyed by … and sixty districts ate from it, and … sixty districts salted its … And they filled from one of its eyeballs three hundred flasks of oil. And when we returned … after … twelve months … the year … we saw that they were cutting beams from its bones, and they had set out to build those districts

And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: Once we were traveling on a ship and we saw a certain fish upon which sand had settled, and grass grew on it. We assumed … it was dry land and went up and baked and cooked on the back … but when its back … hot it turned over. And were it not for … that … ship was close … we would have drowned.

And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: Once we were traveling in a ship and the ship traveled between … fin [shitza] and … fin of a fish … three days and three nights. … it … upward … and we were … downward. And if you would say … the ship did not travel very fast, when Rav Dimi came … he said: … heat a kettle of water, … travel sixty parasangs. And … a horseman shot an arrow, and … outraced it. And Rav Ashi said: That … was a sea gildana, which has two … fins.

And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: Once we were traveling in a ship and we saw a certain bird that was standing with water up to its ankles [kartzuleih] and its head … in the sky. And we said … there is no … water … and we wanted to go down to cool ourselves off. And a Divine Voice emerged and said to us: Do not go down here, as the ax of a carpenter fell … seven years … and … not reached the bottom. And … not because the water is so large … Rather, … because the water is turbulent. Rav Ashi said: And that … is … ziz sadai, … as it is written: … and the ziz sadai is Mine”

And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: Once we were traveling in the desert and we saw these geese whose wings were sloping because they were so fat, and streams of oil flowed beneath them. I said to them: Shall we have a portion of you in the World-to-Come? One raised a wing, and one raised a leg, … When I came before Rabbi Elazar, he said to me: The Jewish people will … be held accountable for … of
a mnemonic … Like the dust of the sky-blue; the scorpion stung the basket.

And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: Once we were traveling in the desert and we were accompanied by a certain Arab who would take dust and smell it and say: This is the road to such and such a place, and that is the road to such and such a place. We said to him: How far are we from water? And he said to us: Bring me dust. We brought … to him, and he said: Eight parasangs. … a second time, and gave him … he said to us that we are at a distance of three parasangs. I switched … but I could not … him,
said to me: Come, I will show you the dead of the wilderness, … I went … saw them; and they had the appearance of one who is intoxicated,

and they were lying on their backs. And the knee of one of them was elevated, and … Arab entered under his knee while riding a camel and with his spear upright, and he did not touch him. I cut one corner of the sky-blue … of one of them, and we were unable to walk. … said to me: Perhaps you took something from them? Return it, as we know … that one who takes something from them cannot walk. I then returned … and then we were able to walk.

When I came before the Sages, they said to me … Every Abba … a donkey, and every bar bar Ḥana … an idiot. For … what halakha did you do that? … to know whether … is in accordance with … Beit Shammai or in accordance with … Beit Hillel, … you should have … counted the threads and counted the joints.

said to me: Come, I will show you Mount Sinai. I went … saw that scorpions were encircling it, and they were standing … as white donkeys. I heard a Divine Voice saying: Woe is Me that I took an oath; and now that I took the oath, who will nullify it for me?

When I came before the Sages, they said to me … Every Abba … a donkey, and every bar bar Ḥana … an idiot. You should have said: Your … is nullified. … And … he reasoned: Perhaps … is … oath that … flood … But the Sages … if … so, why … Woe is Me?

said to me: Come, I will show you those who were swallowed … of Korah. I saw two rifts … that were issuing smoke. … took a shearing of wool, and dipped it in water, and inserted it on the head of a spear, and placed it … there. And when he removed … was scorched. He said to me: Listen … what you hear; and I heard that they were saying: Moses and his Torah are true, and they, … are liars. … said to me: Every thirty days Gehenna returns them to here, like meat in a pot … And … they say this: Moses and his Torah are true, and they, … are liars.

said to me: Come, I will show you … where the earth and the heavens touch each other. I took my basket … placed it in a window of the heavens. After I … praying, I searched for it but did not find it. I said to him: Are there thieves here? He said to me: This is the heavenly sphere that is turning around; wait here until tomorrow and you will find it.

Rabbi Yoḥanan relates: Once we were traveling on a ship and we saw a certain fish that took its head out of the sea, and its eyes had the appearance of two moons, and water scattered from its two gills like the two rivers of Sura. Rav Safra relates: Once we were traveling on a ship and we saw a certain fish that took its head out of the sea, and it had horns, and … inscribed on them: I am a lowly creature of the sea and I am three hundred parasangs … and I am going into the mouth of the leviathan. Rav Ashi said: That is the goat of the sea, which searches … and has horns.

Rabbi Yoḥanan relates: Once we were traveling on a ship and we saw a certain crate [kartalita] in which precious stones and pearls were set, and a species of fish called sharks encircled it. … descended,

a diver [bar amoraei] … to bring … and … became angry and sought to sever his thigh, but … threw … a flask of vinegar and they descended … A Divine Voice emerged … said to us: What … do you have to … the crate of the wife of Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa, as she is destined to insert sky-blue … in it to … the righteous in the World-to-Come?

Rav Yehuda from India relates: Once we were traveling in a ship and we saw a certain precious stone that was encircled by a snake. A diver descended to bring it … snake came and sought to swallow the ship. A raven came … cut off its head, … the water turned into blood … Another snake came, took … and hung it … and it recovered. It returned … sought to swallow the ship, … a bird came and cut off its head, took that precious stone, … threw it onto the ship. We had with us these salted birds; we placed … on them, … they took … and flew away with it.

The Sages taught: … an incident involving Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, who were traveling on a ship, and Rabbi Eliezer was sleeping and Rabbi Yehoshua was awake. Rabbi Yehoshua trembled, and Rabbi Eliezer awoke. … said to him: What is this, Yehoshua; for what … did you tremble? … said to him: I saw a great light in the sea. … said to him: Perhaps you saw the eyes of the leviathan, as it is written: “And his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning”

Rav Ashi said: Huna bar Natan said to me: Once we were traveling in the desert, and we had a thigh of meat with us. We cut open … and tore … and put it on the grass. By … that we brought wood, the thigh had repaired … and we roasted it. When we returned … after twelve months … the year … we saw that those coals were still glowing. When I came before Ameimar, he said to me: That grass was a drug of life [samterei], … those coals were of broom.

“And God created the great sea monsters” … Here, … they interpreted … sea oryx. Rabbi Yoḥanan says: This is leviathan the slant serpent, and leviathan the tortuous serpent, as it is stated: “In that day the Lord with His sore … sword

a mnemonic … Everything; time; Jordan. Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: Everything that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created in His world, He created male and female. Even leviathan the slant serpent and leviathan the tortuous serpent He created male and female. And if they would have coupled … destroyed the entire world. What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? He castrated the male and killed the female, and salted … for the righteous in the future. As it is stated: “And He will slay the serpent that is in the sea”

And He created even the beasts on the thousand hills … male and female. And … if they would have coupled … they would have destroyed the entire world. What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do? He castrated the male and cooled … the female and preserved it for the righteous in the future. As it is stated … “Lo now, his strength is in his loins” … this … male. … “And his force is in the stays of his body”; this … female,

There too, … let Him castrate the male and cool the female; … Fish are unrestrained, … And let Him do the opposite, … If you wish, say … salted female is better; if you wish, say … that … it is written: “There is leviathan, whom You have formed to sport with” … not proper conduct … with a female. … Here too, … let Him … female in salt, … Salted fish is good, … salted meat is not good.

And Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: At the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to create the world, He said to the minister of the sea: Open your mouth and swallow all the waters of the world, … said before Him: Master of the Universe, … enough that I will stay within my own … immediately struck him and killed him; as it is stated: “He stirs up the sea with His power, and by His understanding He smites through Rahab”

Rabbi Yitzḥak said: Conclude from here … the name of the minister of the sea is Rahab, and were it not for waters … cover him, no creature could withstand his smell, … As it is stated: “They shall not hurt nor destroy in all My holy mountain; … as the waters cover the sea” … Do not read … “cover the sea”; rather … Cover the minister of the sea,

And Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: The Jordan issues forth from the cave of Pamyas. That is also taught … The Jordan issues forth from the cave of Pamyas, and travels in the Sea of Sivkhi, … and in the Sea of Tiberias, … and rolls down to the Great Sea, and rolls down until it reaches the mouth of the leviathan. As it is stated: “He is confident, though the Jordan rush forth to his mouth” … Rava bar Ulla strongly objects to this … this … is written about the beasts on the thousand hills. Rather, Rava bar Ulla said … When are the beasts on the thousand hills confident? When the Jordan rushes forth into the mouth of the leviathan.

a mnemonic … Seas; Gabriel; hungry. When Rav Dimi came … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: What … which is written: “For He has founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the floods” … These are … seven seas and four rivers that surround Eretz Yisrael. And these are … seven seas: The Sea of Tiberias, the Sea of Sodom, … the Sea of Ḥeilat, the Sea of Ḥeilata, the Sea of Sivkhi, the Sea of Aspamya, and the Great Sea, … And these are the four rivers: The Jordan, the Jarmuth, and the Keiromyon, and the Piga,
When Rav Dimi came … Rabbi Yonatan says: In the future, Gabriel will perform

a hunt of the leviathan, as it is stated: “Can you draw out leviathan with a fish hook? Or press down his tongue with a cord?” … And were the Holy One, Blessed be He, not assisting … he would not be able to … it, as it is stated: “Only He Who made him can use His sword to approach him”

When Rav Dimi came … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: When … leviathan is hungry, he produces breath from his mouth and … boils all of the waters in the depths … As it is stated: “He makes the deep boil like a pot” … And if … did not place its head in the Garden of Eden, no creature could withstand his … smell, as it is stated: “He makes the sea like a seething mixture [merkaḥa]”

And when he is thirsty, he makes many furrows in the sea, as it is stated: “He makes a path to shine after him” … Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov says: … the depth … not return to its normal condition until seventy years … as it is stated: “One would think the deep to be hoary” … and hoary … no less than seventy

Rabba says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will make a feast for the righteous from the flesh of the leviathan, as it is stated: “The ḥabbarim will make a feast [yikhru] of him” … And kera … nothing other than a feast, as it is stated: “And he prepared [va’yikhreh] for them a great feast [kera]; and they ate and drank” … And ḥabbarim … nothing other than Torah scholars, as it is stated: “You that dwell in the gardens, the companions [ḥaverim] hearken for your voice: Cause me to hear it”

And … the remainder … divide it and use it for commerce in the markets of Jerusalem, as it is stated: “They will part him among the kena’anim” … And kena’anim … nothing other than merchants, as it is stated: “As for the merchant [kena’an], the balances of deceit are in his hand. He loves to oppress” … And if you wish, say … from here: “Whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers [kinaneha] are the honorable of the earth”

And Rabba says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will prepare a sukka for the righteous from the skin of … leviathan, as it is stated: “Can you fill his skin with barbed irons [besukkot]” … is deserving … sukka is prepared for him … not deserving … a covering is prepared for his … as it is stated: “Or his head with fish-spears”

deserving … a covering is prepared for him, … not deserving, a necklace is prepared for him, as it is stated: “And necklaces about your neck” … deserving, a necklace is prepared for him, … not deserving … an amulet is prepared for him … as it is stated: “Or will you bind him for your maidens”

And … the remaining … the Holy One, Blessed be He, spreads it on the walls of Jerusalem, and its glory radiates from … end of the world until the … end. As it is stated: “And nations shall walk in your light, and kings at the brightness of your rising”

“And I will make your pinnacles of kadkhod” … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said: Two angels in heaven, Gabriel and Michael, disagree … And some say … two amora’im in the West, … And who are they? … Yehuda and Ḥizkiyya, the sons of Rabbi Ḥiyya. One said … onyx, and one said … jasper. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them: Let it be like this [kedein] and like that [ukhedein],

“And your gates of precious stones” … in … that … where Rabbi Yoḥanan sat and taught: … future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will bring precious stones and pearls that are thirty by thirty … and He will hollow out in them … ten by twenty … and set them in the gates of Jerusalem. A certain … student sneered at him, … Now we do not find … of … an egg of a dove, … all of this we will find?

After … time … ship went to sea, … he saw ministering angels sitting and sawing precious stones and pearls that were thirty by thirty … and hollowed out in them … ten by twenty … He said to … For whom are these? They said to him that … future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will place them in the gates of Jerusalem. … came before Rabbi Yoḥanan … said to him: … interpret, my teacher, it is fitting for you to interpret, … I saw … as you said. … said to him: Worthless … if you had not seen, you would not have believed; … you are mocking the statement of the Sages. … set his eyes upon him, and … and turned into a pile of bones.
raises an objection … “And I will make you go upright [komemiyyut]” … Rabbi Meir says: … two hundred cubits, equivalent to two … height [komot] of Adam the first

Rabbi Yehuda says: … one hundred cubits, corresponding to the Sanctuary and its walls, as it is stated: “We whose sons are as plants grown up in their youth; whose daughters are as corner-pillars carved after the fashion of the Sanctuary” … When Rabbi Yoḥanan stated … to … windows that … wind

And Rabba says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will fashion seven canopies for each and every righteous … as it is stated: “And the Lord will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion, and over those who are invited to it, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory shall be a canopy” … teaches that … each and every … the Holy One, Blessed be He, fashions for him a canopy … in accordance with his honor,

Why … smoke in a canopy? Rabbi Ḥanina said: … because anyone whose eyes are narrow, … toward Torah scholars in this world, his eyes fill with smoke in the World-to-Come. And why … fire in a canopy? Rabbi Ḥanina said: … teaches that each and every one is burned from … the canopy of the other, … Woe for this embarrassment, woe for this disgrace,

In a similar manner, you … say … “And you shall put of your honor upon him” … but not all of your honor. The elders of that generation said: The face of Moses … as the face of the sun; the face of Joshua … like the face of the moon. Woe for this embarrassment, woe for this disgrace,

Rabbi Ḥama bar Ḥanina says: The Holy One, Blessed be He, fashioned ten canopies for Adam the first … in the Garden of Eden; as it is stated … “You were in Eden the garden of God; every precious stone … Mar Zutra said: … eleven … as it states: “Every precious stone,” … Rabbi Yoḥanan said: And the worst of all of them … gold, as it is counted last,

What … “The workmanship of your drums and of your holes [nekavekha]” … Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Hiram, king of Tyre: … I looked at you, … and created many orifices [nekavim] in man, … And there are … who say … this … said … I looked at you
and I decreed death on Adam the first

What … “And over those who are invited to it”? Rabba says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Jerusalem of the World-to-Come is not like Jerusalem of this world. … Jerusalem of this world, anyone who wants to ascend … ascend. … of the World-to-Come, only those who are invited to it … ascend.

And Rabba says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … future, the righteous will be called by the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He; as it is stated: “Every one that is called by My name, and whom I have created for My glory, I have formed him, yea, I have made him” … And Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Three were called by the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He, and they are: The righteous, and the Messiah, and Jerusalem.

the righteous, this … as we … said. … the Messiah, … as it is written: “And this is his name whereby he shall be called, the Lord is our righteousness” … Jerusalem, … as it is written: “It shall be eighteen thousand reeds round about. And the name of the city from that day shall be, the Lord is there [shamma]” … Do not read … “there” [shamma]; rather, … its name [shemah]. Rabbi Elazar says: … future, the righteous will … Holy, recited before them, as one recites before the Holy One, Blessed be He; as it is stated: “And it shall come to pass, that he who is left in Zion, and he who remains in Jerusalem, shall be called holy”

And Rabba says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will raise Jerusalem three parasangs upward; as it is stated: “And it shall be lifted up and inhabited in its place” … What … “in its place”? … equivalent to its place, … And from where … that the place … was … three … parasangs? Rabba said … a certain elder said to me: I saw the initial Jerusalem, … and … was three … parasangs.

And lest you say … there is discomfort in ascending … the verse states … “Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their cotes” … Rav Pappa said: … learn from … this cloud … is three parasangs high,

Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa says: The Holy One, Blessed be He, wished to give … measure for Jerusalem, as it is stated … Then I said: Where are you going? And he said to me: To measure Jerusalem, to see what is its breadth, and what is its length”

The ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, You have created many cities in Your world for the nations of the world, and You did not give the measure of their length or the measure of their width, … Jerusalem, which has Your name in it, and Your Temple in it, and righteous people in it, … You give it a measure? Immediately: … and said to him: Run, speak to this young man, saying: Jerusalem shall be inhabited without walls for the multitude of men and cattle within it”

Reish Lakish says: … future, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will add to Jerusalem one thousand … tefaf … gardens; one thousand … kefel … towers; one thousand … litzoy … fortifications; … one thousand and two … shilo … small houses [totpera’ot]. And each and every one … will be like … Tzippori in its prosperity.
It is taught … Rabbi Yosei said: I saw Tzippori in its prosperity, and there were one hundred and eighty thousand markets of sellers of … sauces in it.

“And the side-chambers were one over another, three and thirty times” … What … “Three and thirty times”? Rabbi Levi says … Rav Pappi says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnei: If … Jerusalem … three … each and every … contain thirty stories upward. If … Jerusalem … thirty, each and every … contain three stories above
It was stated … a ship … Rav says: Once … has pulled … any amount, … acquired … And Shmuel says: … not acquire … until he pulls the entire

Let us say … is parallel to … tanna’im, … How … through passing? … grasped it by its hoof, … by its hair, … by the saddle that is on it, … by the load that is on it, … by the bit [perumbiyya] in its mouth, … by the bell on its neck, … acquired it. How … through pulling? … he calls it and it comes, or … he hits it with a stick and it runs before him, once it lifts a foreleg and a hind leg … acquired it. Rabbi Aḥai, and some say Rabbi Aḥa, says: … until it walks its full length,

Shall we say … Rav, who … states … in accordance with … the first tanna … and Shmuel, who … states … in accordance … Rabbi Aḥa … Rav … said to you: I state … even … Rabbi Aḥa, … Rabbi Aḥa states … only with regard to animals, as although it lifted a foreleg and a hind leg, it stands in its place. But … a ship, once a bit of it moves, all of it moves,

And Shmuel … say: I stated … even in accordance with … the first tanna. The first tanna states … only with regard to animals, as once … lifted a foreleg and a hind leg, the other … stand … to be lifted. But … a ship, if he pulls the entire … yes, … if … not … not
Let us say … parallel to … these tanna’im, as it is taught … A ship is acquired by pulling. Rabbi Natan says: A ship and letters, … are acquired by pulling
and by … a bill

Letters … who mentioned … them? … is incomplete, and this … it is teaching: A ship is acquired by pulling, and letters, … are acquired by … transferring … Rabbi Natan says: A ship and letters are acquired by pulling and … by … a bill

Why do I … a bill … for a ship? … is movable property, … Rather, is it not … this … is teaching: A ship is acquired by pulling, and letters … by passing. Rabbi Natan says: A ship … by pulling, and letters, … by … a bill

a ship … by pulling, … is … the first tanna. Rather, … between … of Rav and Shmuel. … No, everyone, … either in accordance with … Rav, or in accordance with … Shmuel. And with regard to a ship, everyone agrees

When they disagree, … with regard to … letters, … And this … Rabbi Natan is saying to the first tanna: With regard to a ship, I certainly concede to you … with regard to letters, … if … there is a bill … yes, … if not, … not

And … with regard to the dispute … these tanna’im. As it is taught … Letters, … are acquired by … transferring … the statement of Rabbi … And the Rabbis say: Whether one wrote … but did not transfer … whether he transferred … but did not write … does not acquire … until … writes … and transfers

In accordance with which … did you interpret … in accordance with … Rabbi … let a ship be acquired also by passing, … As it is taught … A ship is acquired by passing; … the statement of Rabbi … And the Rabbis say: … does not acquire
until he pulls it, or until he rents its place.
not difficult; here, … in the public domain. … there, … in an alleyway [simta],

To what … did you interpret that last … to the public domain. … say the latter clause … And the Rabbis say … does not acquire … until he pulls it … But if … in the public domain, from whom can he rent … And furthermore, does pulling in the public domain effect acquisition? But don’t Abaye and Rava both say … Passing effects acquisition in the public domain or in a courtyard that does not belong to either of … pulling effects acquisition in an alleyway or in a courtyard that belongs to both of … and lifting effects acquisition in every place,

What … when it says: Until he pulls it, and what … when it says: Until he rents its place? This … is saying: … until he pulls it from the public domain into an alleyway. And if … is … the domain … owner, … does not acquire … until he rents its place
Shall we say … Abaye and Rava state … in accordance with … Rabbi
Rav Ashi said: … if … where … says to him: Go take possession and … effect acquisition, so too … Here … we are dealing with … where … says to him: Go pull and … effect acquisition
Sage, … holds … particular … And … Sage, … holds … indicating the manner to him,

Rav Pappa says: One who sells … note to another must write to him: Acquire it and all liens on property that are … within it. Rav Ashi said: I stated … halakha before Rav Kahana, and I said to him … The reason … that … wrote this for him. … he did not write this for him, … does not acquire
But does he require … to tie around the mouth of his flask … said to me: Yes, … to tie

Ameimar says: The halakha … letters are acquired by … transferring … in accordance with … Rabbi … Rav Ashi said to Ameimar: … a tradition or … logical reasoning? … said to him: … a tradition. Rav Ashi said: It also … reason … as letters, … are words, … and words cannot be acquired through … words.

And … cannot … But doesn’t Rabba bar Yitzḥak say … Rav says: There are two … documents. … Take possession of this field for so-and-so and write the document for him … he may renege with regard to the document, … But he may not renege with regard to the field,
on the condition that you write him a document. … he can retract … both with regard to the document and with regard to the field,
And Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin … Rav Huna says: There are … three … documents. Two … those that we stated … the other … if … seller wrote the document in advance.

like that which we learned … may write a bill … for the seller even if the buyer is not with him … once this … takes possession of the land the deed is acquired wherever it is. And this is that which we learned … Property that does not serve as a guarantee, … acquired … with property that serves as a guarantee, … by … money, or … a document, or … possession.
by means of … is different, … that money, which cannot be acquired through … exchange, … can be acquired by means of land.

like that … where Rav Pappa had … twelve thousand dinars … in Bei Ḥozai. He transferred … to … Rav Shmuel bar Aḥa by means of the threshold of his house. … When … came … went out … until Tavakh to … him.
but he has not sold the slaves, nor the packing bags, nor the antikei. … What … antikei? Rav Pappa said: … the merchandise that is on

MISHNA: … sold a wagon [hakkaron] has not sold the mules … sold the mules, he has not sold the wagon. … sold a yoke [hatzemed] has not sold the oxen, … sold the oxen has not sold the yoke. Rabbi Yehuda says: The … money indicates … How so? … said to … Sell me your yoke for two hundred dinars, … it is a known matter that a yoke is not … for two hundred dinars … And the Rabbis say: The … money is not proof.

its weaving on its inside, … a bed … its weaving on its outside,

parallel to … tanna’im, … Rabbi Yosei says: … all … that are stated in the … passage about … king, … is permitted … a king to … them. Rabbi Yehuda says: This … passage was stated only … to threaten … as it is stated: “You shall set a king over you” … that his fear should be upon you.

prophet … said to … if that were too little, then I would add to you like these and like those” … “Like these”; … six. “And like those”; … six, … that … are eighteen

reason … that the Merciful One writes: … for himself,” … consequently, … not … this, I would say … even … for his chariot and riders … not … No, … necessary … to add

reason … that the Merciful One writes: … for himself,” … consequently, … not … this, I would say … is not … even enough … to provide … soldiers’ sustenance; … No, … necessary … to … a liberal appropriation

from the Prophets … as it is written: “Your dead shall live, my corpse shall arise. Awake and sing, you that dwell in the dust, for your dew is as the dew of vegetation, and the land shall cast out the dead” … But perhaps … the dead that Ezekiel revived.

from Writings … as it is written: “And your palate is like the best wine that glides down smoothly for my beloved, moving gently the lips of those that sleep” … But perhaps merely their lips will move, in accordance with … Rabbi Yoḥanan, as Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak: Anyone in whose name a halakha is stated in this world, his lips move in the grave … as it is stated: “Moving gently the lips of those that sleep.”

until … stated to them this verse: … that the Lord took an oath to your forefathers to give them” … To … you, is not stated; rather, … “To … them,” … From here resurrection of the dead … from the Torah.

And there are those who say … from this … verse … he said to them … “But you who cleave to the Lord your God every one of you is alive this day” … obvious … “every one of you is alive this day”? Rather, … Even on the day when everyone is dead you will live; just as today every one of you is alive, so too, in the World-to-Come every one of you … alive.

The Romans asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya: From where … that the Holy One, Blessed be He, revives the dead, and … He knows what is destined to be? … said to them: Both of those … from this verse, as it is stated: “And the Lord said to Moses, Behold, you shall lie with your fathers and arise; this people will go astray”

But perhaps … and this people will arise and go astray … said to them: Take at least … half … in your hands … that … knows what is destined to be. … It was also stated … Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: From where … that the Holy One, Blessed be He, revives the dead, and … He knows what is destined to be? … as it is stated: “Behold, you shall lie with your fathers and arise.”

It is taught … Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei, says: With this … matter, I refuted the books of the Samaritans, as they would say … there is no … the resurrection of the dead from the Torah. I said to them: You falsified your torah and you accomplished nothing, as you say there is no … the resurrection of the dead from the Torah, … states: “That soul shall be excised; his iniquity shall be upon him” … shall be excised” … in this world. … “his iniquity shall be upon him,” for when … not for the World-to-Come,
Rav Pappa said to Abaye: And let … say to … both of those … from … “shall be excised [hikkaret tikkaret].” … would say: The Torah spoke in the language of people,

parallel … tanna’im … “hikkaret tikkaret,” … “Hikkaret” … in this world, … “tikkaret” … in the World-to-Come; … the statement of Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Yishmael said to him: Isn’t it already stated … “That person that blasphemes the Lord, that soul shall be excised [venikhreta]” … and are there three worlds … Rather, … “venikhreta” … in this world, … “hikkaret” … in the World-to-Come, … “hikkaret tikkaret” … the Torah spoke in the language of people.

both Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva, what do they do with, … “His iniquity shall be upon him”? … for that … which is taught … might … even … he repented. … the verse states: “His iniquity shall be upon him.” … I said … only when his iniquity … upon him.

Queen Cleopatra asked Rabbi Meir … She said: I know that the dead will live, as it is written: “And may they blossom out of the city like grass of the earth” … But when they arise, … arise naked or … they arise with their garments? … said to her: … a fortiori from wheat. If wheat, which is buried naked, … emerges with several garments … all the more so … the righteous, who are buried with their garments,
emperor said to Rabban Gamliel: You say that the dead will live. Aren’t they dust? And does dust come to life?

The daughter of … said … Leave him, and I will respond to him … There are two craftsmen in our city; one fashions … from water, and one fashions … from mortar. Which is more noteworthy? … said to her: … that … that fashions … from water. … said to him: … he fashions … from the water, all the more so … not … from mortar?

The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught … a fortiori from glass vessels: If … glass vessels, which are fashioned by the breath of … flesh and blood, … they break they can be repaired, … flesh and blood, whose … the breath of the Holy One, Blessed be He, all the more so

a certain heretic said to Rabbi Ami: You say that the dead will live. Aren’t they dust? And does dust come to life? … said to him: I will tell you a parable. To what is this matter comparable? … to a flesh-and-blood king who said to his servants: Go and construct for me a great palace [palterin] in a place where there is no water and earth … They went and constructed it. Sometime … collapsed. … said to them: Return … and construct … in a place where there is earth and water … They said to him: We are unable

became angry at them and said to them: … in a place where there is no water and earth … you constructed … now that there is water and earth … all the more so … And if you do not believe … go out to the valley and see an akhbar, … that today is half flesh and half earth, … tomorrow … develop and all of it will become flesh. Lest you say … over an extended period, ascend a mountain and see that today there is only one snail there; … tomorrow, … rain … have fallen, and … it … entirely filled with snails.

a certain heretic said to Geviha ben Pesisa: Woe unto you, the wicked, as you say: The dead will come to life. … those … alive die. … that the dead will come to life? … said to him: Woe unto you, the wicked, as you say: The dead will not come to life. … those who were not … come to life, is it not … all the more so … those who were … alive … said to … You called me wicked? If I stand, I will kick you and flatten your hump, … said to him … If you do so, you will be called an expert doctor and will take high wages

The Sages taught … On the twenty-fourth … in Nisan … usurpers [dimusana’ei] were expelled from Judea and Jerusalem. When the people of Afrikiya came to judgment with the Jewish people before … Alexander of Macedon, they said to him: The land of Canaan is ours, as it is written: … the land of Canaan according to its borders” … And … Canaan is the forefather of these people.

Geviha ben Pesisa said to the Sages: Give me permission and I will go and deliberate with them before Alexander of Macedon. If they will defeat me, say … You have defeated an ordinary … from among us, … And if I will defeat them, say to them: The Torah of Moses defeated you, … gave him permission, and he went and deliberated with them.

said to them: From where are you citing proof … They said to him: From the Torah. … said to them: I too will cite proof to you only from the Torah, as it is stated: “And he said: Cursed will be Canaan; a slave of slaves shall he be to his brethren” … a slave who acquired property, … slave … to whom … property … to whom? … And moreover, … several years … that you have not served us.

Alexander the king said to … Provide … a response … They said to … Give us time; … three days … gave them … time … they examined … and did not find a response … Immediately, they fled and abandoned their fields when they … sown and their vineyards when they … planted. … And … that year was a Sabbatical

another occasion, the people of Egypt came to judgment with the Jewish people before Alexander of Macedon. … said to … It says … “And the Lord gave the people favor in the eyes of Egypt, and they lent them” … Give us the silver and gold that you took from us;

Geviha ben Pesisa said to the Sages: Give me permission and I will go and deliberate with them before Alexander … If they will defeat me, say … You have defeated an ordinary … from among us, … And if I will defeat them, say to them: The Torah of Moses, our teacher, defeated you, … gave him permission, and he went and deliberated with them.

said to them: From where are you citing proof … They said to him: From the Torah. … said to them: I too will cite proof to you only from the Torah, as it is stated: “And the sojourning of the children of Israel, who dwelt in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years” … Give us the wages for the work … by … 600,000 … whom you enslaved in Egypt … four hundred and thirty years.

Alexander of Macedon said to … Provide … a response … They said to him: Give us time; … three days … gave them … time … they examined … and did not find a response … Immediately, they abandoned their fields when they … sown and their vineyards when they … planted, and fled. … And that year was a Sabbatical

And … another occasion, the descendants of Ishmael and the descendants of Keturah came to judgment with the Jewish people before Alexander of Macedon. They said to … The land of Canaan is … ours and yours, as it is written: “And these are the generations of Ishmael, son of Abraham, … and it is written: “And these are the generations of Isaac, son of Abraham”

Geviha ben Pesisa said to the Sages: Give me permission and I will go and deliberate with them before Alexander of Macedon. If they will defeat me, say … You have defeated an ordinary … from among us, … And if I will defeat them, say to them: The Torah of Moses, our teacher, defeated you, … gave him permission, and he went and deliberated with them.

said to … From where are you citing proof … They said to him: From the Torah. … said to them: I too will cite proof to you only from the Torah, as it is stated: “And Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac. But to the sons of the concubines that Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, … a father who gave a document of bequest [agatin] to his sons during his lifetime and sent one … away from the other, does … have any claim against the other? … What … gifts … Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says: … teaches that … provided them … name … impurity,

Antoninos, … said to Rabbi … The body and the soul are able to exempt themselves from judgment … How so? The body says: The soul sinned, as from the day … when it departed from me, I am cast like a silent stone in the grave, … And the soul says: The body sinned, as from the day that I departed from it, I am flying in the air like a bird, … said to him: I will tell you a parable. To what is this matter comparable? … to a king of flesh and blood who had a fine orchard, and in it there were

fine first fruits … and he stationed two guards in … one lame, … and one blind. … The lame … said to the blind … I see fine first fruits … in the orchard; come and place me … and we will bring … to eat them. The lame … rode upon … the blind … and they brought … and ate them.

Sometime … the owner of the orchard came … He said to … The fine first fruits … where are they? The lame … said: Do I have any legs with which … to walk … The blind … said: Do I have any eyes … to see … What did … do? He placed the lame … upon … the blind … and he judged them as one.

So too, the Holy One, Blessed be He, brings the soul … and casts it … into the body, … and He judges them as one, as it is stated: “He calls to the heavens above and to the earth that He may judge His people” … “He calls to the heavens above”; this is the soul, … “And to the earth that He may judge His people”; this is the body,

Antoninos said to Rabbi … For what … does the sun emerge in the east and set in the west? … said to him: If it were the reverse, you would have also said that to me, … said to him: This is what I am saying to you: For what … does … set in the west

said to him: … in order to greet its Creator, as it is stated: “And the hosts of heaven worship You” … said to him: … let … come until the midpoint of the sky, … and greet … and enter … due to workers and due to travelers,

And Antoninos said to Rabbi … From when is … soul placed in a person? … from the moment of conception or from the moment of … formation … said to him: … from the moment of … formation … said to him: … possible … a piece of meat … stand … three days without salt … and … not rot? … Rather, … from the moment of conception. Rabbi … said: Antoninos taught me this matter, and … a verse … supports him, as it is stated: “And Your Providence [pekudatekha] has preserved my spirit”

And Antoninos said to Rabbi … From when does the evil inclination dominate a person? … from the moment of … formation … or from the moment of emergence … said to him: … from the moment of … formation … said to him: If so, … kick his mother’s innards and emerge … Rather, the evil inclination dominates a person from the moment of emergence … Rabbi … said: Antoninos taught me this matter, and … a verse … supports him, as it is stated: “Sin crouches at the entrance”

Reish Lakish raises a contradiction … It is written: … and with them the blind and the lame, the woman with child and the woman giving birth together” … And it is written: “Then shall the lame man leap as a deer and the tongue of the mute sing; for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert” … How so? … will arise … with their defects, and … will … be healed.

Ulla raises a contradiction. It is written: “He will swallow death forever; and the Lord … will wipe tears from all faces” … And it is written: “There shall be no more an infant a few days old then…for the youngest shall die one hundred years old” … not difficult. … here, … with regard to the Jewish people, … there, … with regard to gentiles, … And what do gentiles seek, … that … those … about whom it is written: “And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and aliens shall be your plowmen and vinedressers”

Rav Ḥisda raises a contradiction. It is written: “Then the moon shall be confounded and the sun ashamed, when the Lord of hosts will reign … And it is written: “And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days” … not difficult. … here, … to the days of the Messiah, … there, … to the World-to-Come,

And according to Shmuel, who says: The difference between this world and the messianic era is only subjugation of the exiles, … not difficult. … here, … in the camp of the righteous; … there, … to the camp of the Divine Presence,

Rava raises a contradiction. It is written: “I will kill and I will bring to life” … And it is written … “I wounded and I will heal,” … The Holy One, Blessed be He, is saying: What I kill, I bring to life, … And then what I wounded, I will heal.

The Sages taught … “I will kill and I will bring to life.” … might … that there will be death … one … and life … one … person, in the … manner that the world operates. … the verse states: “I wounded and I will heal.” Just as wounding and healing … in one … so too, death and … life … in one … From here … a response to … say … there is no resurrection of the dead … from the Torah.

It is taught … Rabbi Meir said: From where … resurrection of the dead … from the Torah? … as it is stated: “Then Moses and the children of Israel will sing this song to the Lord” … is not stated: Sang, … rather, … “they will sing” … From here … resurrection of the dead … from the Torah. On a similar note, you … say: “Then Joshua will build an altar to the Lord … is not stated: Built, … rather, … “will build” … From here, resurrection of the dead … from the Torah.
If that is so, … “Then Solomon will build an altar for Chemosh the abomination of Moab” … also … will build … rather, … the verse ascribes him … as though he built it,

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: From where … resurrection of the dead … from the Torah? … as it is stated: “Happy are they who dwell in Your house; they will yet praise You, Selah” … is not stated: They praised you, … rather, … “they will praise you” … From here, resurrection of the dead … from the Torah. And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: Anyone who recites song … in this world is privileged and recites it in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: “Happy are they who dwell in Your house; they will yet praise You, Selah.”

Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: From where … resurrection of the dead … from the Torah? … as it is stated: “Your watchmen, they raise the voice; together shall they sing, … is not stated: They sang, … rather, … shall they sing” … From here resurrection of the dead … from the Torah. And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: All the prophets are all destined to recite song in one voice, as it is stated: “Your watchmen, they raise the voice; together shall they sing.”

Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: … anyone who withholds halakha from … the mouth of a student … it is as though he robs him of the inheritance of his ancestors, as it is stated: “Moses commanded us the Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob” … is an inheritance for all of the Jewish people from the six days of Creation. Rav Ḥana bar Bizna says … Rabbi Shimon Ḥasida says: … anyone who withholds halakha from … the mouth of a student … even fetuses in their mother’s womb curse him, as it is stated: “He who withholds bar,

the people [leom] shall curse him [yikkevuhu], … And … leom … nothing other than fetuses, as it is stated: … and the one leom shall overcome the other leom” … And kabbo … nothing other than curse, as it is stated … “How can I curse one who is not cursed [kabbo] by God?” … And bar … nothing other than Torah, as it is stated: “Pay homage to bar lest He be angry”

Ulla bar Yishmael says: One perforates like a sieve … It is written here: … the people yikkevuhu” … and it is written there: “And he bored [vayyikkov] a hole in its lid of it” … And Abaye says: … like a launderers’ utensil

And if one teaches … what is his reward? Rava says … Rav Sheshet says: He is privileged … blessings like Joseph, as it is stated … “But blessing shall be upon the head of one who provides [mashbir]” … And mashbir … no … other than Joseph, as it is stated: “And Joseph was the governor of the land, and he was the provider [hamashbir] to all the people of the land”

Rav Sheshet says: Anyone who teaches Torah in this world is privileged and teaches it in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: “And he who satisfies abundantly [umarveh] shall be satisfied himself [yoreh]”

Rava says: From where … resurrection of the dead … from the Torah? … as it is stated: “Let Reuben live and not die, … “Let Reuben live” in this world “and not die” in the World-to-Come. Ravina says … from here: “And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awaken, some to everlasting life, and some to reproaches and everlasting disgrace” … Rav Ashi says … from here: “But go you your way until the end be; and you shall rest, and arise to your lot at the end of days”

Rabbi Elazar says: Any communal leader who leads the community calmly, … is privileged and leads them in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: “For he that has compassion upon them will lead them, even by the springs of water shall he guide them”
And Rabbi Elazar says: Great is knowledge, as it was placed between two letters, … as it is stated: “For a God of knowledge is the Lord”

And Rabbi Elazar says: Great is the Holy Temple, as it … was placed between two letters, … as it is stated: … You have made, Lord, the Temple, Lord, which Your hands have prepared” … Rav Adda Karḥina’a objects to … If that is so, … Great … vengeance, as it was placed between two letters, as it is written: “God of vengeance, Lord, God of vengeance shine forth”
said to him: In its context, indeed, … in accordance with … of Ulla. As Ulla says … these two appearances: … why … One, … for the attribute of … good, … and one, … for the attribute of … punishment,
And Rabbi Elazar says: … any person in whom there is knowledge, … as though the Temple was built in his days, as this, … was placed between two letters and that, … was placed between two letters.
And Rabbi Elazar says: Any person in whom there is knowledge ultimately becomes wealthy, as it is stated: “And by knowledge are the chambers filled with all precious and pleasant riches”

And Rabbi Elazar says: … any person in whom there is no knowledge, it is prohibited to have mercy upon him, as it is stated: “For it is a people of no understanding; therefore its Maker will have no mercy on them, and its Creator will show them no favor”

And Rabbi Elazar says: … anyone who gives his bread to one without knowledge, afflictions befall him, as it is stated: “They who eat your bread will place mazor under you, in whom there is no discernment” … And mazor … nothing other than afflictions, … as it is stated: “And Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound [mezoro]”
And Rabbi Elazar says: Any person in whom there is no knowledge is ultimately exiled, as it is stated: “Therefore my people are exiled, for lack of knowledge”

And Rabbi Elazar says: … any house in which there are no matters of Torah heard at night, the fire … consumes it, as it is stated: “All darkness is laid up for his treasures, a fire not fanned shall consume him; it shall go ill with a sarid in his tent” … Sarid … no … but a Torah scholar, as it is stated: “And among the seridim, those whom the Lord shall call”

And Rabbi Elazar says: Anyone who does not benefit Torah scholars from his property never sees a sign of blessing, as it is stated: “None of his food shall remain [sarid]; therefore his prosperity shall not endure” … Sarid … no … but Torah scholars, as it is stated: “And among the seridim, those whom the Lord shall call.”
And Rabbi Elazar says: Anyone who does not leave bread on his table … never sees a sign of blessing, as it is stated: “None of his food shall remain; therefore his prosperity shall not endure.”

But doesn’t Rabbi Elazar say: … anyone who leaves pieces … on his table, it is as if he worships idols, as it is stated: “Who prepare a table for Fortune [Gad] and offer blended wine for Destiny” … not difficult: This … when there is a whole … with … that … when there is no whole … with

And Rabbi Elazar says: … anyone who amends … in his speech, it is as though he worships idols. … it is written here, … “And I shall seem to him a deceiver [metate’a]” … and it is written there … “They are vanity, the work of deception [tatuim]”
And Rabbi Elazar says: … anyone who looks at nakedness [erva], his bow is emptied, … as it is stated: “Your bow is stripped bare [erya]”
And Rabbi Elazar says: Forever be in the dark, … and … exist. Rabbi Zeira says: We learn … as well … a dark house, one does not open windows to … it … to see … its … leprosy, … Conclude from

Rabbi Tavi says … Rabbi Yoshiya says: What … which is written: … the grave, and the barren womb, and earth that does not receive sufficient water” … And what does a grave have to do with a womb? Rather, … to say to you: Just as a womb takes in and gives forth, so too a grave takes in and … gives forth,

And are … matters not … a fortiori: If … a womb, into which one introduces … in secret, one removes … from it … by … loud sounds … the grave, into which one introduces … with sounds … is it not right that one removes … by … loud sounds … From here … a response to … say: There is no resurrection of the dead … from the Torah.

The school of Eliyahu taught: The righteous whom the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to resurrect do not return to their dust, as it is stated: “And it shall come to pass, that he who remains in Zion and he who remains in Jerusalem shall be called holy, anyone who is written unto life in Jerusalem” … Just as … Holy One exists forever, so too will they exist forever.

And if you say: … those years when the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to renew His world, as it is stated: “And the Lord alone shall be exalted on that day” … what are the righteous … do? … The Holy One, Blessed be He, … make wings like eagles for them and … fly over the surface of the water, as it is stated: “Therefore, we will not fear when God changes the land, and when the mountains are moved in the midst of the sea” … And lest you say … suffering … the verse states: “But they who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; they shall walk, and not tire”
And let us derive from the dead that Ezekiel revived … holds in accordance with … the one who says: In truth, … was a parable,

as it is taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: The dead that Ezekiel revived stood on their feet and recited song … and died. And what song did they recite? The Lord kills with justice and gives life with mercy. Rabbi Yehoshua says … this song … they recited: “The Lord kills, and gives life; He lowers to the grave and elevates” … Rabbi Yehuda says: … truth … was a parable.

Rabbi Neḥemya said to … If … truth, why … a parable, and if … a parable, why … truth? Rather, … In truth, it was a parable. Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says: … dead that Ezekiel revived ascended to Eretz Yisrael and married wives and fathered sons and daughters. Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira stood on his feet and said: I am a descendant of their sons, and these are phylacteries that my father’s father left me from them.
And who are … dead that Ezekiel revived?

Rav says: These were the descendants of Ephraim who calculated … of the end … and erred … as it is stated: “And the sons of Ephraim; Shuthelah, and Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eleadah his son, and Tahath his son. And Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer and Elead whom the men of Gath that were born in the land slew, … and it is written: “And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him”

And Shmuel says: These … people who denied the resurrection of the dead, as it is stated: “Then He said to me: Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel; behold, they say: Our bones are dried and our hope is lost; we are cut off”
Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says: These … people in whom there … not … the moist … of a mitzva, as it is stated: “The dry bones, hear the word of the Lord”

Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa says: These are the people who covered the Sanctuary with repugnant creatures and creeping animals, as it is stated: “So I entered and saw and behold, every form of creeping animal and repugnant animal, and all the idols of the house of Israel, etched upon the wall around” … and it is written there … “And he passed me over them around and around”

Rabbi Yoḥanan says: These are the dead from the Dura Valley … And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … from the Eshel River to Rabat, … the Dura Valley. As, at the time that Nebuchadnezzar the wicked exiled the Jewish people … there were among them youths who overshadowed the sun with their beauty, and the Chaldean women would see them, and … and discharge the flow of a zava. … told their husbands, and their husbands … the king. The king ordered … and … executed them. And … were still discharging the flow of a zava. … The king ordered … and … trampled them

The Sages taught … At the moment that Nebuchadnezzar the wicked cast Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah into the fiery furnace, the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Ezekiel: Go and revive the dead in the Dura Valley. Once … revived them, the bones came and struck … that wicked … in his face. … said: What is the nature of these? … said to him: The friend of these … is reviving … dead in the Dura Valley. … began and said: “How great are His signs and how mighty are His wonders; His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom and His dominion is from generation to generation”

Rabbi Yitzḥak says: Molten gold should be poured into the mouth of that wicked … that if an angel had not come and struck him on his mouth … have sought to overshadow all the songs and praises that David recited in the book of Psalms.

The Sages taught … Six miracles were performed on that day … and they are: The furnace rose … and the furnace was breached; and its limestone dissipated; and the graven image … fell on its face; and four … monarchies, … were burned; and Ezekiel revived the dead in the Dura Valley.

And … all of … tradition. And the four … monarchies … a verse, as it is written: “Then Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to gather together the satraps, the prefects and the governors, the counselors, the treasurers, the justices, the magistrates and all the rulers of the provinces” … And it is written: “There are certain Jews … And it is written … “And the satraps, the prefects, the governors, and the king’s counselors gathered and saw these men”

The school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov teaches: Even during a period of danger, a person should not deviate from his prominence … as it is stated: “Then these men were bound in their mantles, their tunics, and their hats,
Rabbi Yoḥanan says:

The righteous are greater than the ministering angels, as it is stated: “He answered and said: I see four men unbound, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods”

Rabbi Tanḥum bar Ḥanilai says: At the moment that Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah emerged from the fiery furnace, all the nations of the world came and struck the enemies of Israel, … in the face … said to them: You have a God … like that and you bow to the graven image? Immediately … began and said: “Lord, righteousness is Yours, but we are shamefaced, as of this day”

Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says … Rabbi Yonatan says … What … which is written: “I said: I will climb into the palm tree; I will grasp its boughs” … “I said: I will climb into the palm tree”; this is … the Jewish people, … And now … I have succeeded … in My hand only … one bough of Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,

Rabbi Yoḥanan says: What … which is written: “I saw the night, and behold, a man riding upon a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle bushes that were in the depths” … What … “I saw the night”?
