said to him: If so, help me. That is … which is written: “And Abishai, son of Zeruiah, came to his aid, … Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: … that he came to his aid in prayer. Abishai recited … name … and caused … land

pursued them, … When they reached … Kuvi they said: … Stand … against him [kum beih]. When they reached … Bei Terei, … said: With two [bitrei] cubs they killed the lion, … They said to … Go find Orpah, your mother, in the grave. When they mentioned his mother’s name to him … his strength diminished, and they killed him. … It is … that it is written: “Then David’s men took an oath to him saying: You shall not go with us to war anymore and you will not douse the lamp of Israel”

The Sages taught … For three … the land contracted, … Eliezer, servant of Abraham, and Jacob our forefather, and Abishai, son of Zeruiah. … Abishai, son of Zeruiah, … that which we said. … Eliezer, servant of Abraham, … as it is written: “And I came that day to the well” … to say … that on that day he left … Jacob our forefather

as it is written: “And Jacob departed from Beersheba and went to Haran” … and it is written … “And he encountered [vayyifga] the place, and he slept there, for the sun had set” … when … arrived at Haran, he said: Is it possible that I bypassed a place where my forefathers prayed and I did not pray there? He sought to return … Once he contemplated in his mind to return, the land contracted for him, … immediately: “And he encountered the place,”

Alternatively, encounter … nothing other than prayer, as it is stated: “And you, do not pray on behalf of this nation, and do not raise on their behalf song and prayer, and do not encounter [tifga] Me,

“And he slept there because the sun had set” … After … prayed … he sought to return … the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: This righteous … came to My inn. Will … him to take leave without sleeping … Immediately the sun set, … and that is … which is written … “And the sun shone for him … And did … shine only for him? But didn’t … shine for the entire world? Rather, Rabbi Yitzḥak says: The sun that set … for him shone … for him

And from where do we … that David’s descendants ceased … as it is stated: “And Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, and she arose and destroyed all the royal descendants” … But didn’t Joash remain … There too, … Abiathar, … remained … as it is written: “And one of the sons of Ahimelech, son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped” … Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: Were it not for … Abiathar remained … for Ahimelech, son of Ahitub, there would have been no remnant or refugee remaining from the descendants of David.

Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: Sennacherib the wicked came upon them with forty-five thousand men, sons of kings, sitting in carriages of gold, and with them … consorts and prostitutes, and with eighty thousand warriors … wearing a coat of mail, and with sixty thousand sword-bearers running before him, and the rest were cavalry. And likewise, … came upon Abraham … And likewise, … are destined to come with Gog and Magog

was taught in a baraita: The length of the camp … was four hundred parasangs and the width of the necks of his horses … was forty parasangs. … total … his camp was 260 ten thousands, … minus one. Abaye asks: … minus one … ten thousand, or minus one … one thousand, or minus one … one hundred or minus one? … shall stand

taught: The first … crossed by swimming … as it is stated: “And he shall sweep through Judea; he shall overflow and pass” … the middle … passed while standing upright, as it is stated: “It shall reach even the neck” … The last … kicked up dust with their feet, and they did not find water in the river to drink, … until they brought water from another place and drank … as it is stated: “I dug and drank water”

But isn’t it written: “Then the angel of the Lord went forth and smote in the camp of the Assyrians one hundred and eighty-five thousand. And when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses” … Rabbi Abbahu says: These … are regiment leaders,

Rav Ashi says: It is also precise … as it is written: … among his fat ones leanness” … the fat, … among them … Ravina says: … is also precise … as it is written: “And the Lord sent an angel, who obliterated the mighty men-at-arms and the leaders and captains in the camp … And when he came into the house of his God, his own offspring slew him there with a sword” … Conclude from it

With what … strike them? Rabbi Eliezer says: He struck them by hand, as it is stated: “And Israel saw the great hand” … the hand that was destined to exact retribution from Sennacherib. Rabbi Yehoshua says: He struck them with … finger, as it is stated: “And the sorcerers said to Pharaoh: This is the finger of God” … indicating … it is … finger that was destined to exact retribution from Sennacherib. Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says … the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Gabriel: … your scythe honed? … said before Him: Master of the Universe, it is standing honed from the six days of Creation, as it is stated: “For they have fled from the swords,

Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says: That period was the season of the ripening of the fruit. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Gabriel: When you emerge to ripen … fruits, attend to … them, as it is stated: “As often as it passes through, it shall take you; for morning by morning shall it pass through, by day and by night; and the mere understanding of the report shall bring terror” … Rav Pappa says … this … that people say: While on your path, appear before your enemy

And there are those who say: … blew into … through their noses and they died, as it is stated: “When he blows upon them, and they wither” … Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says: … clapped his hands to them and they died, as it is stated: “I will also strike My hands together and I will assuage My anger” … Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa says: He revealed ears for them and they … hear the songs … from the mouths of the … creatures … and they died, as it is stated: “From Your exaltation the nations were scattered”

And how many of … remained … Rav says: Ten … as it is stated: “And the rest of the trees of his forest shall be few, that a child may write them” … And what number can a child … write? … ten, … And Shmuel says: Nine … as it is stated: “And gleanings shall be left of him, as in the beating of an olive tree, two or three berries in the top of the uppermost bough, four or five in the branches of a fruitful tree”

Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: Fourteen … as it is stated: “Two or three…four or five,” … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Five … Sennacherib, and his two sons, … Nebuchadnezzar, and Nebuzaradan, … Nebuzaradan … tradition. Nebuchadnezzar … as it is written … “And the appearance of the fourth is like that of an angel” … And if he had not seen … from where would he have known … Sennacherib and his two sons … as it is written … “And it came to pass as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god that Adrammelech and Sarezer, his sons, smote him with the sword”

Rabbi Abbahu says: Were the … verse not written, it … impossible to say it, … as it is written: “On that day shall the Lord shave with a hired razor in the parts beyond the river the king of Assyria, the head, and the hair of the legs, and it shall also sweep away the beard”

The Holy One, Blessed be He, came and appeared to … as an old man. … said to him: When you go to the kings of the east and the west whose children you brought and killed, what will you say to them? … said to … That man, … also sits … with the same fear, … said to … What should we do? … said to him: Go

and change your … With what shall I change … said to him: Go bring me scissors and I will shear you … From where should I bring … said to him: Go to that house and bring … He went … found ministering angels, … came and appeared to … as men; and … were grinding date pits.

said to them: Give me scissors. … said to him: Grind a se’a of pits and we will give … to you. He ground a se’a of pits and they gave him scissors. By … he came … it grew dark. … said to … Go … bring fire … went and brought fire. While he was fanning it, the fire ignited his beard … it spread … sheared his head and his beard. … said: This is … which is written: “And it shall also destroy the beard” … Rav Pappa says … this … that people say: If you scorch a gentile … it is pleasant for him, ignite a fire in his beard and you will never tire of ridiculing him.

went and found a beam from Noah’s ark, … He said: This … is the great god who delivered Noah from the flood. He said: If that man, … goes and succeeds, he will sacrifice his two sons before you. His sons heard … and killed him. This is … which is written: “And it came to pass as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god that Adrammelech and Sarezer, his sons, smote him with the sword,

And he divided himself against them by night [laila], he and his servants, and smote them” … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: That angel that happened to … Abraham … Laila is his name, as it is stated: “And Laila said: A man-child is brought forth” … And Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa says: … performed for him an act of night, … as it is stated: “They fought from heaven; the stars in their courses fought against Sisera” … Reish Lakish said: … the smith, is preferable to … of the son of the smith,

“And he pursued as far as Dan” … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Once that righteous … came to Dan, his strength weakened. He saw … that his descendants were destined to worship idols in Dan, as it is stated: … and he set one in Bethel, and the other one he placed in Dan” … And even that wicked … did not prevail until he reached Dan, as it is stated: “From Dan the snorting of his horses is heard”

Rabbi Zeira says: Even though Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira sent … from Netzivin: Be vigilant with regard to … an elder who forgot his studies due to circumstances beyond his control, and be vigilant with regard to … jugular veins … in accordance with … Rabbi Yehuda, and be vigilant with regard to … the children of ignoramuses, as from … them Torah will emerge, we inform them … like this matter.

“Right would you be, Lord, were I to contend with You; yet will I reason with You: Why does the path of the wicked prosper; why are all who deal treacherously secure? You have planted them, they have also taken root; they grow, they also bring forth fruit” … What did they respond to … “If you have run with the pedestrians, and they have wearied you, how can you contend with horses? And though in a land of peace you feel secure, how will you do in the wild country of the Jordan?”

a parable of a person who said: I can run three parasangs before the horses in the swamplands. He encountered a pedestrian … ran before him … three mil on dry land and wearied. … said to him: And if … before a pedestrian … so … before horses, all the more so … And if … three mil … so … three parasangs, … all the more so … And if … on dry land … so … in the swamplands, all the more so

So too, you, … And if with regard to … reward … four paces that I compensated that wicked person, … who ran in My honor, you are astonished … when I compensate Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who ran before Me like horses … all the more so … That is … which is written: “Concerning the prophets. My heart within me is broken; all my bones shake; I am like a drunken man and like a man whom wine has overcome, due to the Lord and due to His sacred words”

these four paces … what is … as it is written: “At that time Merodach-Baladan, son of Baladan, king of Babylonia, sent a letter … Due to … Hezekiah had been ill and was recovered, he sent him a letter and a gift? … Yes, … “to inquire of the wonder that was in the land” … As Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … that day that … Ahaz, died, … two hours,

And when Hezekiah fell ill and recovered, the Holy One, Blessed be He, restored those ten hours to … as it is written: “Behold, I will return the shadow of the dial, which descended on the sundial of Ahaz, ten degrees backward. So the sun returned ten degrees, by which it had gone down” … said to … What is this … They said to him: Hezekiah fell ill and recovered, … said: There is a man like that and I do not need to send him greetings? … wrote to … Greetings to King Hezekiah, greetings to the city of Jerusalem, … greetings to the great God.

Nebuchadnezzar was the scribe of Baladan, … at that time he was not there. When he came … he said to … How did you write … They said to him: We wrote this: … said to … You called him: The great God, and you wrote Him at the end … He said: Rather, write this: Greetings to the great God, greetings to the city of Jerusalem, … greetings to King Hezekiah. … said to … The one who reads the letter, let him be the messenger.
pursued … When he ran four paces, … Gabriel came and stopped his … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: If Gabriel had not come and stopped his … there would have been no remedy for the enemies of the Jewish people,

What is … Baladan, son of Baladan? … say: Baladan was a king, and his visage was transformed and became like that of a dog. His son was sitting on the throne … and when he would write … he would write his name and the name of his father, King Baladan. That is … which is written … “A son honors his father and a servant his master”

“A son honors his father” … that which we stated … “And a servant his master” … as it is written: “And in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, came Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, who stood before the king of Babylonia, into Jerusalem. And he burned the House of the Lord, and the house of the king”

And did Nebuchadnezzar ascend to Jerusalem? But isn’t it written … and brought him up to the king of Babylonia, to Riblah” … and Rabbi Abbahu says: This … Antioch. … Rav Ḥisda and Rav Yitzḥak bar Avudimi … One says: An image of … likeness was engraved on … chariot, … And one says: … was in extreme fear of … and it was as though … was … standing before

Rava says: Nebuchadnezzar sent to Nebuzaradan three hundred mules laden with iron axes that cut iron. All of them were incapacitated … one gate of Jerusalem, as it is stated: “And now they pound its carved work together with hatchet and with hammers” … sought to return … said: I am afraid. … that they will not do to me just as they did to Sennacherib,

Voice emerged and said: Leaper, son of a leaper; Nebuzaradan, take … leap, as the time has arrived for the Temple to be destroyed and the Sanctuary to burn. One ax remained for him … He went and struck … with the dull end … and it opened, as it is stated: “He became known as the wielder of axes upward in a thicket of trees”

He was proceeding and killing until he reached the Sanctuary. … he ignited a fire in it. The Sanctuary rose, … They trod upon it from Heaven … as it is stated: “The Lord has trodden the virgin, the daughter of Judah, as in a winepress” … became haughty, … A Divine Voice emerged and said to him: … you killed a nation … dead, you burned a Sanctuary … burned, … you ground flour … ground, as it is stated … “Take millstones and grind flour; uncover your locks, tuck up the train, uncover the leg, pass over rivers” … It was not stated: … wheat, but … flour,”

he saw the blood of Zechariah … boiling. … said to … What is this? They said to him: It is the blood of offerings that was spilled. … said to them: Bring … and I will test … if … is similar … He slaughtered … and … was not similar … said to … Reveal … to me, and if not I will comb your flesh with an iron comb.

said to … This … is … a priest and a prophet who prophesied for the Jewish people with regard to the destruction of Jerusalem and whom they killed. He said to … I will pacify … He brought the Sages … killed them over … and … did not cease. He brought schoolchildren … killed them over … and … did not cease. He brought young priests … killed them over … and … did not cease. … until he killed 940,000 … over … and … did not cease.

approached … said: Zechariah, Zechariah, the worthy among them I killed … Is it satisfactory for you that I kill them all? Immediately … ceased. … contemplated repentance. He said: If they, who caused only one person to perish, … this … that man, … what will be … for him … He deserted … dispatched … will to his house and converted.

The Sages taught … Naaman … was a ger toshav, … Nebuzaradan was … righteous convert. Among the descendants of Sisera … studied Torah in Jerusalem. Among the descendants of Sennacherib … taught Torah in public. … And who are they? … Shemaya and Avtalyon.

Among the descendants of Haman … studied Torah in Bnei Brak. And even among the descendants of that wicked … the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought to bring beneath the wings of the Divine Presence … The ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe: … one who destroyed Your House and burned Your Sanctuary, … You introduce … beneath the wings of the Divine Presence? … That is … which is written: “We have healed Babylonia, but she is not healed” … Ulla says: This … is … Nebuchadnezzar, … Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says: … these are the rivers of Babylonia, and interpret it … the bitter saltwater rivers of Babylonia.

Ulla says: Ammon and Moab were bad neighbors of Jerusalem. Once they heard the prophets who prophesied about the destruction of the Jerusalem, they sent to Nebuchadnezzar: Emerge … and come … said … I am afraid. … that they will not do to me just as they did to … predecessors.

sent to him … “For the ish is not at home; he is gone on a long journey” … and ish … no … but the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is stated: “The Lord is an ish of war” … sent to them … He is in a nearby … and He will come. … sent to … “He has gone on a journey from afar” … said to them: They have righteous … who will pray for mercy and bring Him

sent to … “He has taken a bundle of kesef with him” … and kesef … nothing other than the righteous, as it is stated: “So I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of kesef and for a kor of barley and a half-kor of barley”

sent to them: … the wicked will repent … and they will pray for mercy and they will bring Him … sent to … God already designated the time of their … as it is stated: “On the day of the keseh, He will come home” … keseh … nothing other than … time, as it is stated: … at the keseh on the day of our feast” … sent to them: It is winter … and I cannot come … due to the snow and the rain.

sent to him: Come on the peaks of mountains, … as it is stated: “Send the lamb to the ruler of the land from the peaks of the wilderness to the mount of the daughter of Zion” … sent to them: If I come … I … have no place to dwell … sent to him: Their burial caves are superior to your palaces, … as it is written: “At that time, says the Lord, they shall remove the bones of the kings of Judea, and the bones of his princes, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem from their graves; and they shall spread them before the sun and the moon and all of the hosts of heaven, whom they have loved, and whom they have served, and after whom they have walked”

Rav Naḥman said to Rabbi Yitzḥak: Have you heard when the son of giants [bar niflei] will come? … said to him: Who … the son of giants? … said to him: … Messiah. … you call the Messiah son of giants? … said to him: Yes, as it is written: “On that day I will establish

the Tabernacle of David that is fallen [hanofelet]” … said to him … this … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … the generation in which … son of David, comes, Torah scholars decrease; and … the rest … their eyes fail with sorrow and grief, and troubles increase. And the harsh decrees will be introduced; before the first passes the second quickly comes.

The Sages taught … the seven-year … during which … son of David, comes: … the first year, this verse will be fulfilled: “And I will cause it to rain upon one city and cause it not to rain upon another city” … second … arrows of famine will be shot, … third … there will be a great famine, and men, women, children, the pious, and men of action will die, and the Torah is forgotten by those who study it. During the fourth … plenty but not … plenty. During the fifth … great plenty and they will eat, and drink, and rejoice, and the Torah will return to those who study it. During the sixth … voices … During the Sabbatical … wars, … During … the conclusion of the Sabbatical … the son of David will come.

Rav Yosef said: Haven’t there been several Sabbatical … which … transpired … that … and … did not come? Abaye said: Have … During the sixth … voices, … during the Sabbatical … wars, transpired? And furthermore, have … transpired in … order

“That Your enemies taunted, Lord, that they have taunted the footsteps of Your anointed” … It is taught … Rabbi Yehuda says: During the generation that the son of David comes, the hall of the assembly … will be … for prostitution, and the Galilee will be destroyed, and the Gavlan, … will be desolate, and the residents of the border … will circulate from city to city and will receive no sympathy. The wisdom of scholars will diminish, and sin-fearing … will be despised. And the face of the generation will be like the face of a dog

And the truth will be lacking, as it is stated: “And the truth is lacking [ne’ederet], and he who departs from evil is negated” … What … And the truth is lacking [ne’ederet]? … the study hall of Rav said: … teaches that … will become like … flocks [adarim] and walk … What … “And he that departs from evil is negated”? … the study hall of Rabbi Sheila said: Anyone who deviates from evil is deemed insane by the people.

Rava says: Initially I would say … there is no truth … in the world. … a certain one of the Sages, and Rav Tavut is his name, and some say Rav Tavyomei is his name, … that if they were … give him the entire world, he would not deviate … in his statement. He said to me: One time I happened … to a certain place, and Truth is its name, and … would not deviate … in their statements, and no person from there would die prematurely. I married a woman from … them, and I had two sons from her.

One day his wife was sitting and washing the … head. Her neighbor came … knocked on the door. He thought: … not proper conduct … He said to her: She is not here. … his two sons died. The people … in … place came before him … said to him: What … this? He said to them: This was … incident, … They said to him: Please leave our place and do not provoke … death upon these people.

It is taught … Rabbi Nehorai says: During the generation … which the son of David comes, youths will humiliate elders and elders will stand … before youths, and a daughter will rebel against her mother, and a bride against her mother-in-law, and the face of the generation will be like the face of a dog, and a son will not be ashamed before his father.

It is taught … Rabbi Neḥemya says: During the generation that the son of David comes, arrogance will proliferate and the cost … will corrupt … The vine will produce its fruit, and … the wine … costly. And the entire … monarchy will be converted to … heresy … and there will be no … rebuke. … supports … Rabbi Yitzḥak, as Rabbi Yitzḥak says: The son of David will not come until the entire kingdom will be converted to heresy. Rava says: What is the verse … “It is all turned white; he is ritually pure”

The Sages taught … “For the Lord shall judge His people … when He sees that their power is gone and there is none shut up or left” … the son of David will not come until informers will proliferate. Alternatively, … until the … students … diminishes. Alternatively, … until … peruta will cease from the purse. Alternatively, … until they despair from the redemption, as it is stated: “And there is none shut up or left,” as though there were no supporter or helper for the Jewish people.

as … that … of Rabbi Zeira, … when he would find Sages who were engaging in … said to them: Please, I ask of you, do not delay … As we learn … three … come … by means of diversion of attention … and these are they: … Messiah, a lost item, and a scorpion.

Rav Ketina says: Six thousand years is … the world, … it is in ruins … one … as it is stated: “And the Lord alone shall be exalted on that day” … Abaye says: It is in ruins … two … as it is stated: “After two days He will revive us; in the third day He will revive us, and we shall live in His presence”

It is taught … in accordance with … of Rav Ketina: Just as the Sabbatical … abrogates … once in seven years, so too, the world abrogates … one thousand years in … seven thousand years, as it is stated: “And the Lord alone shall be exalted on that day,” and it states: “A psalm, a song for the Shabbat day” … a day, … that is entirely Shabbat. And it says … “For a thousand years in Your eyes are but like yesterday when it is past,
The school of Eliyahu taught: Six thousand years is … the world. Two thousand … chaos; two thousand … Torah, … two thousand years … the period of … the Messiah.
but due to our many sins, … that elapsed since … have elapsed.

Elijah … said to Rav Yehuda, brother of Rav Sala Ḥasida: The world will … no fewer than eighty-five Jubilee … And during the final Jubilee, the son of David … come. … said to … during the beginning of … or during its end? … said to … I do not know. … end … or … not … end … said to him: I do not know. Rav Ashi says: This … Elijah said to him: Until that time do not anticipate his … from this … forward anticipate his

Rav Ḥanan bar Taḥlifa sent … to Rav Yosef: I found one man, and in his hand … one scroll written … Ashurit … and … the sacred tongue, … I said to him: From where … this … into your … He said to me: I was hired to … the Roman army and I found … among the Roman archives. … And it is written in … After 4,291 years … from the creation of the world, the world will end; during … the wars of the sea monsters … among … the wars of Gog and Magog and the remaining … messianic period. … And the Holy One, Blessed be He, will renew His world only after … seven thousand years. Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, says … it was stated: After … five thousand years.

It is taught … Rabbi Natan says: This verse penetrates and descends until the depths; … “For the vision is yet for the appointed time; and it declares of the end, and does not lie; though it tarry, wait for it, because it will surely come; it will not delay”
not in accordance with … our Rabbis, who would interpret … “For a period and periods and a half period”
And … not in accordance with … Rabbi Simlai, who would interpret … “You have fed them with the bread of tears and have given them tears to drink in great measure [shalish]”
And … not in accordance with … Rabbi Akiva, who would interpret … “Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens and the earth”
Rather, the first, … monarchy … seventy years. The second kingdom, … fifty-two … and … the monarchy of bar Koziva, … two and a half years.

What … “And it declares [veyafe’aḥ] of the end, and does not lie”? Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says … Rabbi Yonatan says: May those who calculate the end of days be cursed [tippaḥ], as they would say once the end … arrived and … did not come, … he will no longer come … Rather, … wait for his … as it is stated: “Though it tarry, wait for it.” Lest you say we are … awaiting … and … is not awaiting … the verse states: “And therefore will the Lord wait, to be gracious to you; and therefore will He be exalted, to have mercy upon you;

since we are awaiting … and … is … awaiting … who is preventing … the … attribute of judgment … prevents … And since the attribute of judgment prevents … why do we await … to receive a reward … as it is stated: “Happy are all they who wait for Him.”

Abaye said: The world … no fewer than thirty-six righteous … in each generation who greet the Divine Presence, as it is stated: “Happy are all they who wait for Him [lo]” … The numerical value of lo, … is thirty-six. … Is that so? But doesn’t Rava say: The row … before the Holy One, Blessed be He, … eighteen thousand parasangs, as it is stated … “It shall be eighteen thousand reeds round about, … not difficult; this … who view … through a luminous crystal [be’ispaklarya], … that … who view … through a crystal that is not luminous.

And are … so numerous? But doesn’t Ḥizkiyya say … Rabbi Yirmeya says in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai: I have seen members … of … prominent, … and they are few. If they … one thousand, I and my son are among them. If they … one hundred, I and my son are among them; … if they … two, I and my son are they.
not difficult. This … who … enter … by … permission [bar] … That … who … enter … without … permission,

Rav says: All the ends … passed, and the matter depends only upon repentance and good deeds. … And Shmuel says: It is sufficient for the mourner to endure in his mourning … parallel to … tanna’im: Rabbi Eliezer says: If the Jewish people repent they are redeemed, and if not they are not redeemed. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: If they do not repent, will they not be redeemed … Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, will establish a king for them whose decrees are as harsh as … Haman, and the Jewish people … repent, and … restore them to … right

raises an objection … “And I made you go upright [komemiyyut]” … Rabbi Meir says … two hundred cubits … the equivalent of twice the height of Adam the first … Rabbi Yehuda says: … one hundred cubits … corresponding to … Sanctuary and its walls, as it is stated: “For our sons are as plants grown up in their youth; our daughters as cornerstones, carved in the fashion of a palace”
When Rabbi Yoḥanan says … to the windows … wind enters.
What … And its leaf for medicine [literufa]? Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avudimi and Rav Ḥisda … One says: … To unlock the mouth [lehattir peh] … above, … And one says: … to unlock the mouth … below,

It was also stated … Ḥizkiyya says … To unlock the mouth of mutes, … bar Kappara says … To unlock the mouth of barren women. Rabbi Yoḥanan says: … to actual medicine. … what is … For medicine [literufa]? Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says: … to … the countenance [letoar panim] of the keepers of the mouth [peh],

Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Simon, taught: … anyone who blackens his face … over matters of Torah in this world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, shines his brightness in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: … “His countenance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars”

Rabbi Tanḥum, son of Rabbi Ḥanilai, says: … anyone who starves himself over matters of Torah in this world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, satisfies him in the World-to-Come, as it is stated: … “They are abundantly satisfied with the plenty of Your house, and You feed them drink of the river of Your pleasures”

When Rav Dimi came … he said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, will give each and every righteous person His handful, as it is stated: “Blessed be the Lord, Who day by day bears our burden; God is our salvation, Selah” … Abaye said to him: And is it possible to say so, … But wasn’t it already stated: “Who has measured the waters in the hollow of His hand, and meted out heaven with the span,

said: What is the reason … you are not familiar with … aggada? As they say in the West, … in the name of Rava bar Mari: The Holy One, Blessed be He, will give every righteous person 310 worlds as it is stated: “To bequeath to those who love Me substance [yesh]; and I will fill their treasuries” … In … numerical value, … yesh, … is 310,
it is taught … Rabbi Meir says: In accordance with the measure that a person metes … metes … for him, … as it is written: “In full measure [besasse’a] when You send her away do You contend with her”

Rabbi Yehoshua said … And is it possible to say that … a person gives his handful to a pauper in this world, the Holy One, Blessed be He, gives him His handful in the World-to-Come? But isn’t it written: “And meted out heaven with the span” … And you do not say so? Which … attributes is greater? … the attribute of reward greater or … the attribute of punishment

You must say that the attribute of reward is greater than the attribute of punishment, … with regard to the attribute of reward it is written: “He commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, and rained upon them manna to eat” … And with regard to the attribute of punishment … says: “And the windows of the heavens were opened”

With regard to the attribute of punishment it is written: “And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcasses of the men who have rebelled against Me; for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh” … Is it not so … a person extends his finger into the fire in this world, he is immediately burned? … Rather, just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, provides strength to the wicked to receive their punishment, so too, the Holy One, Blessed be He, provides strength to the righteous to receive their reward,

Rabbi Akiva says: Also one who reads external literature … taught … books of heretics. Rav Yosef says: It is also prohibited to read the book of ben Sira, … Abaye said to … What is the reason … If we say … due to … that … wrote in it: Do not flay the skin of the fish from its ear, so that its skin does not go to ruin, but roast it on the fire and eat with it two loaves of bread,

If … from its literal … in the Torah, … also wrote: “You shall not destroy its trees” … If … from … homiletic interpretation … is teaching us proper conduct: … should not engage in sexual intercourse in an atypical manner,

Rather, … because it is written … A daughter is for her father false treasure; due to fear for her he will not sleep at night: During her minority, lest she be seduced; during her young womanhood lest she engage in licentiousness; once she has reached her majority, lest she not marry; once she marries, lest she have no children; once she grows old, lest she engage in witchcraft … Didn’t the Sages also say it … impossible for the world … without males and without females; … happy is one whose children are males and woe unto him whose children are females.

Rather, … because it is written … Do not introduce anxiety into your heart, as anxiety has killed mighty men … Didn’t Solomon … say it … “Anxiety in a man’s heart dejects him [yashḥena]” … Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi … One says … He shall remove it [yesiḥenna] from his mind, … And one says: He shall tell it [yesiḥenna] to others,

Rather, … because it is written … Prevent the multitudes from inside your house, and do not bring everyone into your house … But didn’t Rabbi … also say it, as it is taught … Rabbi … says: A person should never have many friends inside his house, as it is stated: “There are friends that one has to his own detriment”

Rather, … because it is written … A sparse-bearded man is clever; a thick-bearded man is a fool. One who blows on his cup is not thirsty. One who said: With what will I eat bread, take the bread from him. One who has a passage in his beard, the entire world is unable to overcome him.

Rav Yosef says: … we teach the superior matters that are in it … A good wife is a good gift; she will be given into the bosom of a God-fearing man … A bad wife is leprosy for her husband. What is his remedy? He shall chase her from his house and will be healed from his leprosy … A beautiful wife, happy is her husband; the number of his days is doubled

Avert your eyes from a woman of grace, lest you be trapped in her snare. Turn not to her husband to mix wine and strong drink with him, as many have been corrupted by the beauty of the beautiful woman, and mighty are all her fatalities … Many are the wounds of a peddler … who accustom … to matters of forbidden sexual relations. Like a spark ignites a coal … like a cage full of birds, so too, their houses are filled with deceit … Prevent the multitudes from inside your house, and do not bring everyone into your house … Let many be those who greet you; reveal your secrets to one in a thousand. From she who lies in your bosom guard the openings of your mouth, … Grieve not about tomorrow’s trouble, because you know not what a day may bring; perhaps tomorrow you will no longer be, and one will have worried about a world that is not his.

“All the days of the poor are terrible” … ben Sira says: Also the nights … roof is among the lowest roofs … and in the elevation of the hills is his vineyard, … From the rain on the roofs … to his roof … and the soil of his vineyard … to … vineyards.
a mnemonic … Zeira; Rava; Mesharshiyya; Ḥanina toviyya, … Yannai yafe, … Yoḥanan meraḥem, … Yehoshua mekatzer,

Rabbi Zeira says … Rav says: What … which is written: … “All the days of the poor are terrible”; these are masters of the Talmud, … “And for the good-hearted it is always a feast”; these are masters of the Mishna,

Rava says … the opposite … and this is … which Rav Mesharshiyya said in the name of Rava: What … which is written: “One who quarries stones shall be saddened by them … these are masters of the Mishna, … “And he who chops wood shall be warmed by it”; these are masters of the Talmud,

Rabbi Ḥanina says: “All the days of the poor are terrible”; this … one who has a bad wife. “And for the good-hearted it is always a feast”; this … one who has a good wife. Rabbi Yannai says: “All the days of the poor are terrible”; this … delicate [istenis], … “And for the good-hearted it is always a feast”; this … broad-minded [da’ato yafe], … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: “All the days of the poor are terrible”; this … compassionate [meraḥem], … “And for the good-hearted it is always a feast”; this … cruel … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: “All the days of the poor are terrible”; this

who is intolerant [da’ato ketzara] … “And for the good-hearted it is always a feast”; this … who is tolerant … And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says … “All the days of the poor are terrible”: But aren’t there Shabbatot and Festivals, … in accordance with that … of Shmuel, as Shmuel says: A change in routine … the onset of an intestinal ailment.

The Sages taught: One who reads a verse from Song of Songs and renders it a form of … song, … and one who reads … verse at a banquet house, not at its … time, … introduces evil to the world, as the Torah girds … sackcloth and stands before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and says before Him: Master of the Universe, Your children have rendered me like a harp on which clowns play.

says to … My daughter, during the time that they are eating and drinking, in what should they be engaged? … says before Him: Master of the Universe, if they are masters of the Bible, let them engage in … Torah, Prophets, and Writings. If they are masters of the Mishna, let them engage in … the Mishna, in … halakha, and in … aggada. And if they are masters of the Talmud, let them engage in … the halakhot of Passover on Passover, in … the halakhot of Shavuot on Shavuot, … in … the halakhot of Sukkot on Sukkot. … Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar testified in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Ḥananya: Anyone who reads a verse at its … time … introduces good into the world, as it is stated: “And a word in its season, how good is it”

And … one who whispers … over a wound. Rabbi Yoḥanan says: And … where he spits into … as one does not mention the name of Heaven over spittle, … It was stated … Rav says: Even … a leprous mark … Rabbi Ḥanina says: Even … “And He called to Moses”

The Sages taught … One may smear oil … and rub … intestinal … on Shabbat … One may whisper incantations of snakes and scorpions on Shabbat … And one may pass … vessel upon … eye on Shabbat, … Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: In what … are these matters stated? … in … a vessel that … be moved … But … a vessel that … not be moved, … prohibited … And one may not consult the words of demons on Shabbat. Rabbi Yosei says: Even during the week … prohibited

Rav Huna said: … halakha … in accordance with … Rabbi Yosei. … And even Rabbi Yosei did not say … rather, … due to danger, … as … that … concerning Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef, who … was swallowed into a cedar … and a miracle was performed for him and the cedar split and expelled him.

The Sages taught … One may smear oil … and rub … intestinal … on Shabbat, … provided that he does not do … in the manner in which he does during the week. … How … does one do … Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: One … smears oil and afterward rubs … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: One smears oil and rubs … simultaneously.

The Sages taught … demons of oil and demons of eggs, … it is permitted to consult them; but … due to … that they deceive. One may whisper … over oil that is in a vessel and one may not whisper … over oil that is in … hand. Therefore, one may smear oil … from oil that … in … hand, … and one may not smear oil that … in a vessel,

Rav Yitzḥak bar Shmuel bar Marta happened … to a certain inn, … they brought him oil in a vessel. He rubbed it … and boils developed on his face. He went out to the marketplace, and a certain woman saw him … said: I see here the … spirit … Ḥamat … She performed an action, … for him, and he was healed.

Rabbi Abba said to Rabba bar Mari … It is written: “All the disease that I placed in Egypt I shall not place upon you, for I am the Lord, your Healer” … And since … does not place … why is healing … said to him … this … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: This verse can be interpreted … from … itself, as it is stated: “And He said: If you will diligently hearken to the voice of the Lord, your God” … If you hearken … I will not place … and if you do not hearken … I will place … Nevertheless, … “for I am the Lord, your Healer.”

Rabba bar bar Ḥana says: When Rabbi Eliezer fell ill, his students entered to visit him. … said to them: There is intense wrath in the world, … began to cry … and Rabbi Akiva was laughing. They said to him: Why are you laughing? … said to them: And for what … are you crying? They said to him: … possible … a Torah scroll, is afflicted with pain and we will not cry?

said to them: … for that … I am laughing. As long as I would see … my teacher that neither does his wine ferment … nor is his flax stricken, nor does his oil spoil, nor does his honey turn rancid, I would say … Perhaps, Heaven forfend, my teacher … received his world … But now that I see my teacher … with suffering, I am happy. … said to him: Akiva, have I failed … of the entire Torah? … said to him, you taught us, our teacher: “For there is not a righteous man upon earth who does good and sins not”
The Sages taught … When Rabbi Eliezer fell ill, four Sages entered to visit him: Rabbi Tarfon, and Rabbi Yehoshua, and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, and Rabbi Akiva.
Rabbi Tarfon responded … and said: You are better for the Jewish people than a drop of rain, as a drop of rain … in this world, and my teacher … in this world and in the World-to-Come.
Rabbi Yehoshua responded and said: You are better for the Jewish people than the sphere of the sun, as the sphere of the sun … in this world, and my teacher … in this world and in the World-to-Come.

Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya responded and said: You are better for the Jewish people than a father and mother, as a father and mother … in this world, … my teacher … in this world and in the World-to-Come.

Rabbi Akiva responded and said: Afflictions are cherished. … he said to … Support me … and hear the statement of Akiva my student, who said: Afflictions are cherished. … said to him: Akiva, from where do you … this? … said: I interpret a verse … “Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem…And he performed that which was evil in the eyes of the Lord” … And it is written:

“These too are the proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah, king of Judea, copied” … And … Hezekiah, king of Judea, taught Torah to the entire world and to Manasseh his son he did not teach Torah? Rather, … from all his exertion to … him and from all his toil to … him, … only afflictions … elevated him to … good, as it is stated: “And the Lord spoke to Manasseh and to his people but they would not heed. And the Lord brought upon them the captains of the army of the king of Assyria, who took Manasseh with hooks, and bound him with chains, and carried him to Babylonia”

And it is written … “And when he was in distress, he sought the Lord his God, and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers, and he prayed to Him and He was entreated of him, and He heard his supplication, and brought him back to Jerusalem into his kingdom; then Manasseh knew that the Lord He was God” … You learned … this that afflictions are cherished.

the Sages taught … Three came with a demand, … these are they: Cain, Esau, and Manasseh. Cain … as it is written: “My sin is too great to bear” … said before … Master of the Universe, is my transgression greater than … the 600,000 who are destined to sin before You … and You … forgive them? … Esau … as it is stated: “Have you but one blessing, my father?” … initially he called to multiple gods, … and ultimately he called to the God of his forefathers
Abba Shaul says: Also … one who pronounces the … name … with its letters. … taught … in the outlying areas … and in colloquial [aga] language,

three kings and four commoners … The Sages taught … Jeroboam [Yorovam] … who debased … people [riba am]. Alternatively, Yorovam … who engendered strife among the people [meriva ba’am], … Alternatively, Yorovam … who engendered strife between the Jewish people [meriva bein ha’am] and their Heavenly Father, … son of Nebat … son who looked [nibat] … but did not see

taught … He is … Nebat, he is … Micah, … he is … Sheba, son of Bichri. Nebat, who looked [nibat] but did not see, … Micah, who was crushed [nitmakhmekh] in the building … And what is his … name? His name is Sheba, son of Bichri.
The Sages taught … Three looked but did not see … And these are they: Nebat, and Ahithophel, and the astrologers of Pharaoh.
Nebat saw fire that emerges from his penis. He thought … he … rule. But that is not … would be Jeroboam who … emerge from him
Ahithophel saw leprosy that glowed on his penis … he thought … he … rule. But it is not so. … from Bathsheba his daughter, … came Solomon

The astrologers of Pharaoh … as Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says: What … which is written: “These are the waters of contention” … These are … that the astrologers of Pharaoh saw, and they erred … they saw … that the savior of Israel would be stricken by water, … said: “Every son that is born you shall cast into the river” … And they did not know that … over matters … the waters of Meribah … stricken

And from where do we … that … does not enter into the World-to-Come? … as it is written: “And by this matter there was a sin to the house of Jeroboam, and to eradicate it and to destroy it from off the face of the earth” … To eradicate it in this world, and to destroy it for the World-to-Come.

Rabbi Yoḥanan says: For what … was Jeroboam privileged … to monarchy? … due to … that he rebuked Solomon … And for what … was he punished … due to … that he rebuked … in public, as it is stated: “And this was the cause that he lifted his hand against the king: Solomon built the Millo, and repaired the breaches of the city of David his father” … said to … David, your father, created breaches in the wall so that the Jewish people could ascend for the pilgrimage Festival, and you sealed them in order to marshal forced labor [angarya] for the daughter of Pharaoh,

And what … “and this was the cause that he lifted his hand against the king”? Rav Naḥman says: He removed his phylacteries before … Rav Naḥman says: The arrogance that existed in Jeroboam drove him from the … as it is stated: “And Jeroboam said in his heart: Now shall the kingdom return to the house of David. If this people go up to offer sacrifices in the House of the Lord in Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again to their lord, even to Rehoboam, king of Judea, and they shall kill me and return to Rehoboam, king of Judea”

said: It is learned … that sitting in the Temple courtyard … only for kings of the house of Judah alone. Once they see Rehoboam, who is sitting, and … me standing, they will think: This, … is king, and that, … is the servant. And if I sit … I will be … a traitor against the throne, and they will kill me and follow him. Immediately, … “And the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said to them: It is too much for you to ascend to Jerusalem; behold your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. And he placed the one in Bethel and the other he placed in Dan”

What … “and … took counsel”? Rabbi Yehuda says: … that … seated a wicked … alongside a righteous … He said … Do you sign … for all that I am doing? They said to him: Yes. He said to them: I want to be the king. They said to him: Yes. … Will you do everything I tell you to do? They said to him: Yes. … Even to worship idols? A righteous … said: Heaven forfend; … wicked … said to the righteous … Does it enter your mind that a man like Jeroboam … worship idols? Rather, he … seeks to test … if they accept … his pronouncements.

And even Ahijah the Shilonite erred … and signed … As Jehu was an extremely righteous person. As it is stated: “And the Lord said to Jehu: Because you have done well, to perform what is right in My eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab according to all that was in My heart, your children of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel” … And it is written: “But Jehu took no care to walk in the Torah of the Lord, God of Israel, with all his heart; he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, who made Israel sin”

What caused … Abaye says: A covenant is made with the lips, as it is stated … “Ahab worshipped Baal a little, but Jehu shall serve him much” … Rava says: He saw the seal of Ahijah the Shilonite … and he erred

which is written: “And the apostates are deep in slaughter and I am rejected by them all” … Rabbi Yoḥanan says … the Holy One, Blessed be He, says: They … more profound … than my own. I said: Anyone who does not ascend … for the pilgrimage Festival violates a positive mitzva, and they said: Anyone who ascends … for the pilgrimage Festival will be stabbed with the sword.

“And it came to pass at that time, and Jeroboam left Jerusalem, and the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the way, and he was clad in a new garment, … taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei: … it is a time ordained for calamity.

“At the time of their punishment, they shall perish” … taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei: … a time ordained for calamity. … “In an acceptable time have I answered you” … taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei: … a time ordained for good. … “On the day when I punish, I will punish their sin upon them” … taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei: … it is a time ordained for calamity. … “And it came to pass at that time, and Judah descended from his brothers” … taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei: … a time ordained for calamity.

“And Rehoboam went to Shechem; for all Israel came to Shechem, to make him king” … taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei: … a place ordained for calamity. In Shechem, they tormented … Dinah, in … Shechem the brothers sold Joseph, in Shechem the kingdom of the house of David was divided.
“And Jeroboam left Jerusalem” … Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa says: … that he left the destiny of Jerusalem,

“And the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the way, and he was clad in a new [ḥadasha] garment, and the two were alone in the field.” What … “in a new garment”? Rav Naḥman says: … like a new garment; just as a new garment has no imperfection, so too, the Torah … of Jeroboam … had no imperfection. Alternatively, “a new garment” … that they introduced [sheḥideshu] matters that … ear had ever heard.

What … “and the two were alone in the field”? Rav Yehuda says … Rav says: … that all … Torah scholars … seemed, … to them, like grass of the field, … And there are … who say: … that all the rationales of the Torah were revealed to them like a field

“Therefore shall you give parting gifts to Moresheth Gath; the houses of Achzib are a deceitful thing for the kings of Israel” … Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa says: … a Divine Voice emerged and said to … He who killed the Philistine and bequeathed … Gath to you, … will you give parting gifts to his sons … the houses of Achzib are a deceitful thing for the kings of Israel,

Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa says: … anyone who derives benefit from this world without … a blessing, it is as though he stole from the Holy One, Blessed be He, and the congregation of Israel, as it is stated: “Whoever robs his father and his mother and says: It is no transgression, he is the companion of a corrupter” … And … “his father” … none other than the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is stated: “Is He not your Father Who created you, … And … “his mother” … none other than the congregation of Israel, as it is stated: “Hear, my son, the discipline of your father, and do not forsake the Torah of your mother”
What … “He is the companion of a corrupter”? … he is a companion of Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who corrupted … Israel before their Father in Heaven
“And Jeroboam drove Israel from following the Lord, and caused them to sin a great sin” … Rabbi Ḥanin says: … like two sticks … cause each other to carom,

“And Di Zahav” … The school of Rabbi Yannai said: Moses said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, because of the gold and silver that You lavished upon the Jewish people … until they said enough [dai], … caused the Jewish people to fashion for themselves gods of gold. … a parable … A lion does not maul and roar over a basket of straw … rather, … over a basket of meat,

Rabbi Oshaya says: Until Jeroboam, Israel was suckling, … from … one calf … From that … forward, … from two and three calves, … Rabbi Yitzḥak says: You have no punishment that comes to the world in which there is not one twenty-fourth of the surplus of a litra of the first calf. … as it is stated: “On the day when I punish, I will punish their sin upon them”

Rabbi Ḥanina says: After twenty-four generations … this verse was collected, as it is stated: “And he cried in my ears with a loud voice, saying: Those who have charge over the city draw near, every man with his deadly weapon in his hand”

“And after this matter, Jeroboam returned not from his evil way” … what … “After … Rabbi Abba says: … after the Holy One, Blessed be He, grabbed Jeroboam by his garment, … and said to him: Repent, and you and I and … son of Yishai will stroll … in the Garden of Eden. … said to Him: Who … in the lead? … said to … son of Yishai … in the lead. … If so, I do not wish
Rabbi Abbahu was accustomed to lecture … about the three kings … He fell ill, and he undertook that he would not lecture … Once
he recovered, he then lectured … said to him: Did you not undertake that you will not lecture about them? … said: Did they repent, that I will reconsider

Rav Ashi ended … of the three kings. He said … Tomorrow we will begin … with our colleagues … Manasseh, … came and appeared to him in his dream. … said … You called us your colleague and the colleagues of your father?

from where are you required to begin … Who brings forth … said to him: I do not know. … said to him: … from where you are required to begin … Who brings forth … you did not learn, and … you call us your colleague? … said to … Teach me … and tomorrow I will lecture … it in your name during … lecture … said to him: … from where it crusts … baking.

said to him: Since you were so wise, what is the reason you engaged in idol worship? … said to him: Had you been there … you would have taken … the hem of your cloak and run after me … The next day … said to the Sages … We will begin with … our teachers,

Ahab [Aḥav], … a brother [aḥ] to Heaven, … a father [av] for idol worship. … a brother to Heaven, as it is written: “And a brother is born for adversity” … a father for idolatry. … as it is written: “As a father has compassion for his children”

“And it came to pass, the most minor of his transgressions was his walking in the sins of Jeroboam, son of Nebat” … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The minor … that Ahab performed … on par with the major … that Jeroboam performed, … And for what … did the verse attribute … to Jeroboam, … due to … that he was first to … iniquity. … “Their altars shall also be like droppings in the furrows of the field” … Rabbi Yoḥanan says: You do not have even one furrow in Eretz Yisrael upon which Ahab did not place … idol worship and bow to it.

And from where do we … that … does not enter into the World-to-Come? … as it is written: “And I will excise from Ahab every man, and him that is shut up and him that is abandoned in Israel” … “Him that is shut up” … in this world, … “and him that is abandoned” … in the World-to-Come.

Rabbi Yoḥanan says: For what … was Omri, … privileged … to … monarchy? … due to … that he added one city in Eretz Yisrael, as it is stated: “And he bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, and built on the hill, and called the name of the city that he built after Shemer, the owner of the hill, Samaria”
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: For what … was Ahab privileged … to … monarchy … twenty-two years?

due to … that he respected the Torah, which was given with twenty-two letters, as it is stated: “And he sent messengers to Ahab, king of Israel, into the city, and said to him: So says Ben-Hadad: Your silver and your gold are mine; your wives and also your good children, are mine. … Yet I will send my servants to you tomorrow about this time, and they shall search your house, and the houses of your servants, and it shall be, that they shall put in their hand all the delight of your eyes and take it…And he said to the messengers of Ben-Hadad, tell my lord the king: All that you did send for to your servant at the first I will do; but this thing I may not do”
What … “the delight of your eyes” … Is it not a Torah scroll?

Perhaps … idol worship. … not enter your mind, as it is written … “And all the elders and all the people said to him: Do not consent and heed not” … But perhaps they were wicked elders, … Isn’t it written: “And the saying pleased Absalom well and all the elders of Israel” … and Rav Yosef says: … wicked elders.

There, … it is not written: “And all the people,” … here, … it is written: “And all the people.” As it is impossible that there were not among them righteous … And it is written: “And I will leave seven thousand in Israel; all the knees that have not bent to the Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed it”

Rav Naḥman says: Ahab was balanced … as it is stated: “And the Lord said, who shall entice Ahab that he may ascend and fall at Ramoth Gilead? And this one said in this manner, and that one said in that manner” … Rav Yosef objects to this … about whom … wrote: “But there was none like Ahab who devoted himself to do evil in the eyes of the Lord, whom Jezebel his wife had incited” … And we learn … Every day she would weigh gold shekels … for idol worship. And you say he was balanced? Rather, Ahab was generous with his money … and since he … benefited Torah scholars with his property, … expiated half … for him.
