supports … Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: All … acts of Creation were created with their … stature, … they were created with their … capacities; they were created with their … form. As it is stated: “And the heaven and the earth were finished, and all the host of them” … Do not read … “The host of them [tzeva’am]”; rather, … Their form [tzivyonam].

Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa taught: “May the glory of the Lord endure forever; let the Lord rejoice in His works” … This verse was stated by the minister of the world, … When the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: … after its kind” … the grasses drew an a fortiori … with regard to themselves.

If the Holy One, Blessed be He, wishes … mixing … why did he say: After its kind, with regard to the trees? And furthermore, … an a fortiori … If … trees, which do not naturally grow mixed, … the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: “After its kind,” all the more so … us,
Immediately, every … emerged after its kind, … The minister of the world began … and said: “May the glory of the Lord endure forever; let the Lord rejoice in His works,”
Ravina raises a dilemma: … grafted two … grass onto one another,

what is … according to Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa? … since … “after its kind” is not written … with regard to them, … not liable … Or perhaps, since … agreed with them … it is as if … “after its kind” is written with regard to them. … shall stand

Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi raises a contradiction … is written: “And God made the two great lights” … and … is … written … “The greater light … and the lesser light … the moon said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, … possible for two kings to serve with one crown? … said to her, … go and diminish yourself.

She said before Him: Master of the Universe, since I said a correct … before You, … I diminish myself? … said to her: … go and rule … during the day … and during the night. She said to Him: What is the greatness of … What use is a candle in the middle of the day? … said to her: Go; let the Jewish people count the days and years with you, … She said to Him: But … the sun as well, … it is impossible that they will not count seasons with it, as it is written: “And let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years” … Go; let righteous men be named after you. … Ya’akov HaKatan, … Shmuel HaKatan … David HaKatan,

saw that … was not comforted. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: Bring atonement for me, since I diminished the moon. … And this is what Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: What is different … goat … of … New Moon, that … is stated with regard to it: “For the Lord” … The Holy One, Blessed be He, said: This goat shall be an atonement … for having diminished … the moon.

Rav Asi raises a contradiction … is written: “And the earth brought forth grass” … on the third day of the week … And … is … written: “No shrub of the field was yet in the earth” … on Shabbat eve, … teaches that the grasses emerged … and stood at the opening of the ground, … until Adam, the first … came and prayed for mercy upon them, and rain came, and they sprouted. … to teach you that the Holy One, Blessed be He, desires the prayers of the righteous.
Rav Naḥman bar Pappa had a certain garden. He planted seeds but they did not sprout. He prayed for mercy, … rain came, and … sprouted. He said: This is … of Rav Asi,

Rav Ḥanan bar Rava said: “Hashesua” … a distinct creature, which has two backs and two spines … But was Moses our teacher a hunter, or was he an archer, … from here … a refutation to those who say that the Torah is not from Heaven,
Rav Ḥisda said to Rav Taḥlifa bar Avina: Go write … hunter [kinnigi] and … archer [ballisteri] in your … aggada, and explain

“The five lords of the Philistines: The Gazite, and the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite, and the Ekronite; also the Avvim” … said … five … but it … lists six. Rabbi Yonatan said: … the greatest of them … five. Rav Ḥisda said to Rav Taḥlifa bar Avina: Write … the greatest [arunekei] in your … aggada, and explain … And … disagrees … of Rav, as Rav says: … Avvim … came from Teiman.

This is also taught … Avvim came from Teiman. And why were they called Avvim … Because they corrupted [ivvetu] … their place … Alternatively, … Avvim since they desired [ivvu] many deities. Alternatively, … Avvim since … all who saw them were seized by convulsions [avit]. Rav Yosef said: And each one of them has sixteen rows of teeth.

Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: … many verses that … fit to be burned as books of the heretics, … and … they are themselves the essence of Torah. … “And the Avvim, that dwelt in villages as far as Gaza, … What … difference … for us?

Since Abimelech, … administered an oath to Abraham: “That you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my grandson” … the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: Let … Caphtorim come … remove … from … Avvim, who are … Philistines, and let Israel come … remove … from the Caphtorim,

Similarly, you say … “For Heshbon was the city of Sihon, the king of the Amorites, who had fought against the … king of Moab, … What is the … difference … that … the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel: “Be not at enmity with Moab” … the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: Let Sihon come … remove … from Moab, and let Israel come … remove … from Sihon. … And this is what Rav Pappa says: … Ammon and Moab were purified by Sihon,

“Which Hermon the Sidonians call Sirion, … taught: Senir and Sirion are mountains of Eretz Yisrael. … teaches that every one of the nations of the world went and built itself a great city … and named it after … the mountains of Eretz Yisrael, teaching you that even the mountains of Eretz Yisrael are beloved by the nations of the world.
Similarly, … “And as for the people, he removed them city by city” … What is the … difference … so that they would not call his brothers exiles.
The signs of the … bird were not … stated … And … not … But isn’t it taught … “The nesher”

Just as a nesher … unique … that it has no extra digit or crop, and its gizzard cannot be peeled, and it claws … and eats … non-kosher, so too, all like … non-kosher. … doves … which have an extra digit and a crop, and whose gizzard can be peeled, and do not claw … and eat … kosher, … so too, all like … kosher. … Abaye said: … the explanation of … was not stated in the Torah. Rather, … from the statements of the Sages,

Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches: A bird that comes … with one sign … is kosher, since it is unlike a nesher. … it is … a nesher, which has none … that you shall not eat. But … there is … that has … one … you may eat
But … Let one derive … from … doves: Just as doves, which … have all four … so too here, … unless it has all four
If … so … why do I … the rest of the non-kosher birds that the Merciful One wrote?
But let us derive … from them, … Just as there, … three … and we … do not eat … so too, all … three signs … and we will not eat … And all the more so … two … or one.
If so, why do I … the crow that the Merciful One wrote … Now … that we do not eat … that has three … is … necessary … which has … two?

But one should derive … from a crow: Just as there, … two … not … so too any … two … not … If so, why do I … peres and … ozniyya that the Merciful One wrote … Now … that we do not eat … that has two … is … necessary … which have … one?

But let us learn … from … peres and ozniyya … If so, why do I … nesher that the Merciful One wrote? Now … that we do not eat … that has one … is … necessary … which has none? Rather, … it is a nesher, which has none … that you shall not eat. But … that has … one … eat

But … the reason … that the Merciful One wrote: “Nesher.” … then, … not … this, I would say: Derive from … peres and ozniyya … peres and ozniyya are two verses that come as one, … and … two verses that come as one do not teach
It is learned … that … present in this, … is absent in that, … and that … present in that is absent in this.
Now, there are twenty-four non-kosher birds … It is impossible that … one … present in these, … is absent in … those … constitutes two verses that come as one.

It is learned … there are twenty-four non-kosher birds, and four signs … three … can be found in all of them, … Twenty of them … three … and two … in a crow. One … in a peres and one in an ozniyya, … present in this is absent in that, … Lest you say: Derive from it … the Merciful One wrote … nesher … It is a nesher, which has none … that you shall not eat. But … there is … that has … one … eat
But … why do I … doves that the Merciful One wrote … Rav Ukva bar Ḥama said: … to … an offering. Rav Naḥman says:

one is familiar with … and their names, … bird that comes … with … one sign is kosher, … he is not familiar with them and their names, … with one sign is non-kosher, … with … two signs, … kosher, provided that he … recognize a crow,

crow and nothing more? But isn’t it taught … orev, this is the … crow; … “after its kinds,” Rabbi Eliezer says: … to include the zarzir, … said to Rabbi Eliezer: But wouldn’t the people of Kefar Temarta in Judea eat … because it has a crop? … said to them: They too will be judged in the future

Alternatively, … “after its kinds” … to include … white senunit … the statement of Rabbi Eliezer. … said to him: But don’t the people of the upper Galilee eat it, because its gizzard can be peeled? … said to them: They too will be judged in the future … Rather, … crow and all … species of crow.

Ameimar said: The halakha … bird that comes … with one sign is kosher, provided that it does not claw … Rav Ashi said to Ameimar: What … that which Rav Naḥman … said to him: I did not hear … that is to say: I do not hold … What … is there? … because … the peres and ozniyya, … They are not … in settled areas,
Rav Yehuda says: … the scratching bird is fit for … the purification of a leper, … And this is the white senunit about which Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis disagreed

Ameimar said: … With regard to … with a white belly, everyone agrees that it is permitted … They disagree when … with a yellow belly. Rabbi Eliezer prohibits it, and the Rabbis permit it. And the halakha … in accordance with … Rabbi Eliezer.

Mar Zutra teaches … this … With regard to … with a yellow belly, everyone agrees that it is prohibited. They disagree when … with a white belly. Rabbi Eliezer deems … prohibited, and the Rabbis deem … permitted. And the halakha … in accordance with … the Rabbis, who deem … permitted.

Granted, according to the one who says … they disagree with regard to … with a white belly, this … that which … teaches: This is the white senunit … But according to the one who says … they disagree with regard to … with a yellow … what … This is the white senunit? … to exclude … house … which is black.

Raḥava says … Rabbi Yehuda says: … tasil, … unfit … as a dove, … but … fit … as a pigeon, … datzifi … and … doves of Reḥava, are fit as doves, but are unfit as pigeons, … Rav Daniel bar Rav Ketina raises an objection … All birds

disqualify … water of purification, … except for the pigeon, because it sips … But if it is so … let … teach: Except for … pigeon and … tasil. Rabbi Zeira said: … this, … sips … and spits … and that, … sips but does not spit.

Rav Yehuda says: The tzutzeyanei doves are fit for … on the altar, and they are the doves of Reḥava … raises an objection … hyssop, and neither a hyssop of Greece, nor stibium hyssop, nor Roman hyssop, nor desert … nor any … hyssop whose … a modifier.

Abaye said: Any … whose name was modified before the giving of the Torah, and … the Torah was particular … it, is unfit … its … a modifier, … But the name of these … was not modified, … before the giving of the Torah. … Rava said: The tzutzeyanei doves are called simply … in their place

Rav Yehuda says: These grasshoppers … among the shrubs … permitted … And … among the cabbages are forbidden. Ravina said: And we flog … on their account, due to … winged swarming things … And Rav Yehuda says: … tzarda is permitted … and … barda is prohibited. And your mnemonic … except [bar] for it. … the marda, it is uncertain

Rav Asi says: There are eight uncertain … ḥuva, ḥuga, suga, and harnuga, tushelemi, and marda, kuḥilna, and bar nappaḥa. … What is their uncertainty? The gizzard of kosher birds can be peeled, … and the gizzard of non-kosher … cannot be peeled, but the gizzard of these … can be peeled … with a knife.

But … a certain duck in the house of Mar Shmuel whose gizzard could not be peeled, and they set … in the sun, and once it softened it could be peeled? … There, when it softened it could be peeled by hand. Here, … even when it softened it could be peeled only with a knife.

Abaye says: The swamp rooster is one of the eight uncertain … and this is … mardu, … Rav Pappa says: The swamp rooster is forbidden, but the swamphen is permitted. And your mnemonic … an Ammonite man … but not an Ammonite woman. Mareimar taught: The swamphen is forbidden, … saw that it claws … and eats … And this is … giruta,

Rav says: … shavor anderafta is permitted, … piruz anderafta is forbidden. And your mnemonic … Piruz the Evil. Rav Huna says: … bunya is permitted. … parva is forbidden. And your mnemonic … Parva’a the Sorcerer.

Rav Pappa says: … reclining and eating mardu is permitted, … bowing and eating … is forbidden. And your mnemonic … “You shall bow down to no other god” … Shmuel says: … wine drinker is forbidden. And your mnemonic … Those who drank wine are unfit for service … And Shmuel says: … wine pourer is forbidden.
little wine pourer is permitted. And your mnemonic … The power of the son is greater than the power of the father,

Rav Yehuda says: … shekitena. … long-shanked red … permitted. And your mnemonic … murzema … little red … forbidden, and your mnemonic … a dwarf … unfit … long-shanked green, … forbidden, and your mnemonic … green … unfit

Rav Yehuda says: … shalakh, … this is … that scoops [sholeh] fish out of the sea. … dukhifat … whose comb … bent [hodo kafut] … This is also taught … dukhifat … whose comb … bent, and this is … that brought the shamir to the Temple.
When Rabbi Yoḥanan would see a shalakh, he … say: “Your judgments are like the great deep” … When he would see an ant, he … say … “Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains,”

Ameimar says: … laknei and batnei … permitted. … sakna’ei and batna’ei … place that it is customary to eat … one may eat … place that it is customary not to eat … one may not eat … Is that to say that the matter … depends on custom? … Yes, but … not difficult: This … a place where the peres and ozniyya are found. … That … a place where the peres and ozniyya are not found.
Abaye says: … kevai and kakvai are forbidden, … kakvata is permitted. … in the West, … they flog … on its … and they call it taḥveta.

The Sages taught … tinshemet, … ba’ut among birds. … Do you say … the ba’ut among birds, or is it only the ba’ut among creeping animals? … Say: Go out and learn from the thirteen hermeneutical principles, … A matter derived from its context. What are the … verses speaking about? … about birds. So too here, … to birds.

It is also taught … in this way with regard to … creeping animals: … tinshemet … ba’ut among creeping animals. … Do you say … ba’ut among creeping animals, or it is only … ba’ut among birds? Say: Go out and learn from the thirteen hermeneutical principles, … A matter derived from its context. What are the … verses speaking about? … about creeping animals. So too here, … to creeping animals.
Abaye says: … ba’ut among birds … kifof. … ba’ut among creeping animals … kurpedai. Rav Yehuda says: … ka’at … this is the … a kuk. … raḥam, this is … sherakrak.

Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Why is it called the raḥam? … when the raḥam comes … mercy [raḥamim] comes to the world, … Rav Beivai bar Abaye said: And it is … when it sits on something and makes a sherakrak … is learned … that if it sits on the ground and hisses [veshareik], … the Messiah is coming, as it is stated: “I will hiss [eshreka] for them, and gather them”
Rav Adda bar Shimi said to Mar bar Rav Idai: But … a certain … that sat on a plowed field and hissed, and a stone came and broke its head? … said to him: That … was a liar
the Sages taught … orev, this is the crow. … “Every orev,” … to include the valley crow … “After its kinds,” to include the crow that comes at the heads of pigeons.

The Master said: … orev, this is the crow. Is that to say … stands before us, … Rather, say: … orev, this is the black crow, and so … states: “His locks are curled, and black as a crow” … The valley … [ha’amaki] … white … And so … states … “If the appearance thereof be deeper [amok] than the skin” … As the appearance of … sun, which … deeper than the shade,
And … the crow that comes at the heads of pigeons, Rav Pappa said: Do not say … that it comes at the head of pigeons, … rather, … head resembles that of a pigeon.
the Sages taught: … the netz, this is the hawk. … “After its kinds,” to include … bar ḥireya. … What is the bar ḥireya? Abaye said: … shurineka.

Rav Yehuda says: … the ḥasida, this is the white dayya. And why is it called ḥasida? Since it performs charity [ḥasidut] for its fellows, … the anafa, this is the irritable dayya. And why is it called anafa? Since it quarrels [mena’efet] with its fellows.

Rav Ḥanan bar Rav Ḥisda says … Rav Ḥisda says … Rav Ḥanan, son of Rava, says … Rav says: There are twenty-four non-kosher birds. Rav Ḥanan bar Rav Ḥisda said to Rav Ḥisda, … From where … If … of Leviticus … there are … twenty … If … of Deuteronomy … there are … twenty-one … And if you would say: Add … da’a, which is written in Leviticus but is not written in Deuteronomy, to … still there are … twenty-two.

said to him: This … your mother’s father, … said in the name of Rav: … “after its kinds,” “after its kinds,” “after its kinds,” … “after its kinds,” … Here, … are four … If so, there are twenty-six, … Abaye said: … da’a … and … ra’a … are one … As, if it enters your mind that they are two

Since … Deuteronomy comes to add … what is different here, … that it is written: “Da’a,” … what is different here, … that it is written: “Ra’a,” and da’a is not written? Rather, conclude from … ra’a and da’a are one species.

But still, there are twenty-five … Abaye said: Just as … ra’a and da’a are one … so … ayya and … dayya, … are one … As, if it enters your mind that they are two … Since … Deuteronomy comes to add … what is different here, … that it is written: “After its kinds,” about … ayya, … and what is different there, … that it is written: “After its kinds,” about … dayya? … Rather, learn from … ayya and dayya … are one

And now that … ayya and dayya are one … why did … to write … ayya and dayya … As it is taught … Rabbi … says: … I will read ayya … Why is dayya stated? … so as not to give a claim to a litigant to disagree, … it should not occur … you call … an ayya and he calls … a dayya … you call … a dayya and he calls … an ayya … Therefore, … writes in Deuteronomy: “And the ra’a, and the ayya, and the dayya after its kinds”

raises an objection … Why … of … animals … repeated? … due to … the shesua … And … of … birds … due to the ra’a. What, is it not … from … that … animals there, … to add … birds … also … to add … No, there, … to add, … here, … to explain.

And … differs from … Rabbi Abbahu, as Rabbi Abbahu says: … ra’a is … ayya. And why is it called … ra’a? Since it sees [ro’ah] most … And so … states: “That path no bird of prey knows, neither has the eye of the ayya seen it” … taught: … stand in Babylonia and see a carcass in Eretz Yisrael.

Since … ra’a is … ayya, by inference, … that … da’a is not the … ra’a; … since … Deuteronomy comes to add … what is different here, … that it is written: “Da’a,” … what is different there, … that da’a is not written? Rather, … not conclude from … da’a and ra’a and ayya are … one

And … from … ra’a is … ayya, by inference, … dayya is not … ayya. … What is different there, … that it is written: “After its kinds,” about … ayya, and what is different here, … that it is not written: “After its kinds,” about … ayya but about … dayya? Rather, … learn from … da’a and ra’a, dayya and ayya are … one

it is taught … Isi ben Yehuda says: There are one hundred non-kosher birds in the East, and they are all species of ayya. Avimi, son of Rabbi Abbahu, taught: There are seven hundred types of … fish, and eight hundred types of … grasshopper, and there are countless birds. … birds? … there are … twenty-four … Rather, … And there are countless kosher birds.

It is taught … Rabbi … says: It is revealed and known before the One Who spoke and the world came into being that … non-kosher animals are more numerous than the kosher … Therefore, the Torah lists the kosher … it is revealed and known before the One Who spoke and the world came into being that … kosher birds are more numerous than the non-kosher … Therefore, the Torah lists the non-kosher
What is … teaching us? … As Rav Huna says … Rav … and some say … Rav Huna says … Rav says in the name of Rabbi Meir: A person should always teach his student in a concise manner,

Rabbi Yitzḥak says: A kosher bird may be eaten on … a tradition … the hunter is deemed credible to say: My teacher conveyed to me … this bird is kosher. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: And this … when … is familiar with … and with their names.

Rabbi Zeira raises a dilemma: … teacher the Sage, or … his teacher the hunter, … Come … hear … which Rabbi Yoḥanan said: And this … when … is familiar with them and with their names. Granted, if you say … his teacher the hunter, … well. But if you say … his teacher the Sage, granted, … their names, … he has learned them, but does he recognize … themselves? Rather, … not conclude from it … his teacher the hunter? … conclude from it
The Sages taught … One may buy eggs from the gentiles anywhere, and one … not … concerned, neither with regard to carcasses, … nor with regard to … tereifot,
But perhaps they … a non-kosher bird. Shmuel’s father said: … to … says … of such and such bird, … kosher. … But … let him say … of a kosher bird. … If so, … he has … deflect

But … Let him inspect … for signs, as it is taught … Like the signs of … eggs, so … the signs of fish. … enter your mind … the signs of fish? The Merciful One states … “Fins and scales” … Rather, say: So … the signs of
fish embryos,

And it is taught … about eggs … these are the signs of … eggs: Any … that narrows … and is rounded, … one of its ends is rounded and … one of its ends is pointed, is kosher. … both of its ends are rounded or both of its ends are pointed, … non-kosher. … albumen … on the outside and … yolk on the inside, … kosher. … yolk … on the outside and … albumen on the inside, … non-kosher. … yolk and albumen are mixed with each other, it is certainly the egg of a creeping animal.
No, … necessary … cut … But let him inspect the yolk and the albumen, … with … mixed in a bowl,

But in a case like this, … may we buy … from them? Isn’t it taught … One may sell the egg of a tereifa … to a gentile only if it is mixed in a bowl; therefore, one may not buy eggs mixed in a bowl from them,

Rather, Rabbi Zeira said: … signs … are not … by Torah law. As, if you do not say so, … that which Rav Asi says: There are eight … uncertain. … Let one inspect their eggs … Rather, learn from it … signs are not … by Torah law

But … with regard to what halakha is … teaching … This … is saying: … both of its ends are rounded, or both its ends are pointed, or … yolk … on the outside and … albumen … on the inside, … certainly non-kosher. … one of its ends is pointed … one of its ends is rounded, and … albumen … on the outside and … yolk on the inside, and … says to you … from such and such bird, and … is kosher, rely on … no specification … do not rely on them, since there are crow’s … that resemble those of a pigeon.

The Master said: … albumen and yolk are mixed with each other, it is certainly the egg of a creeping animal … For what halakha … Rav Ukva bar Ḥama said: … to say that if tissue … developed [rikema] … and it was perforated, … it transmits ritual impurity … that … of a lentil-bulk,

Ravina objects to this: But perhaps it is … of a snake, … Rather, Rava said: … that if tissue … developed … and one ate it, he is flogged on its account, due to … swarming thing that swarms upon the earth
If so, why specifically … of a non-kosher … even … of a kosher … as well. … as it is taught … “Every swarming thing that swarms upon the earth,”
to include chicks … whose eyes have not … opened … by rabbinic … and the verse … a mere support
The Sages taught … eggs … boiled … permitted. Unfertilized eggs … strong constitution may eat them, … a drop [koret] of blood is found on it, … discards the blood, … and eats the rest.

Rabbi Yirmeya said: And this … when … is found on its knot, … taught Dostai, father of Rabbi Aptoriki: … taught … only when … is found on its albumen, … but … it is found on its yolk, even … the egg is forbidden. What is the reason … that the decay has spread through all of it. Rav Geviha from Bei Ketil said to Rav Ashi: A tanna taught the opposite before Abaye, … and it is Abaye that corrected it … this

Ḥizkiyya says: From where … that the egg of a non-kosher … is prohibited by Torah … As it is stated: “And the daughter [bat] of the ya’ana” … But does the ya’ana have a daughter … Rather, which … This is a non-kosher egg. … But perhaps this is their name, … should not enter your mind, as it is written: “The daughter of my people has become cruel, like the ye’enim in the wilderness”

And … not … But isn’t it written: “I will make a wailing like the jackals, and a mourning like the daughters [benot] of the ya’ana” … like this ya’ana that mourns for its children. … But isn’t it written: “And benot ya’ana shall dwell there” … like this ya’ana that dwells with its children.

But isn’t it written: “The animals of the field shall honor Me, the jackals and the benot ya’ana” … And if it enters your mind … an egg, can an egg sing a song … Rather, … The ya’ana is written, and the bat ya’ana is … written,
And … here is different … that the scribe splits … into two words: … And from … that the scribe splits it
into two words, conclude from it … they are two names,

If that is so, … “Chedorlaomer” … which the scribe splits in two … also … that they are two names? … They say … There, … splits … into two words, … may not split it into two lines … But here, he may split … even into two lines,

But the Sages stated … any bird … It is taught … Rabban Gamliel says: … claws … and eats … is certainly non-kosher. … it has an extra digit and a crop, and its gizzard can be peeled, it is certainly kosher. Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says: One stretches a line, … If it splits its feet … two … here and two there, … non-kosher. … three … here and one there, … kosher. Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: Any bird that catches … out of the air is non-kosher.
tziparta also catches … Abaye said: We say … catches and eats
Others say: … dwells with non-kosher … non-kosher; … with kosher … kosher.

In accordance with whose … in accordance with … Rabbi Eliezer, as it is taught … Rabbi Eliezer says: … not for naught … zarzir went … with the crow, but because it is … species. … You … even say … the Rabbis, … We say … dwells … and resembles

And with regard to grasshoppers, any … that has … What … most of its … Rav Yehuda said … Rav said: Most of its length. And some say … Most of its circumference. Rav Pappa said: Therefore, … We require … most of its length, and we … require … most of its circumference.
